IsraAID expects the successful consultant/firm to field a multidisciplinary team with a balance of quantitative, qualitative, and GESI expertise, complemented by strong in-country presence across ICNMP priority geographies where possible. The indicative team composition below is provided as guidance; consulting firms may propose an alternative structure provided all required competencies are demonstrated and justified.

· Team Leader / Baseline Study Lead: Advanced degree in public health, social sciences, statistics, international development, or related field; minimum 10 years’ experience leading baseline/endline evaluations for complex, multi-country development programs; demonstrated experience with forced displacement, refugee, or migration programming; strong track record managing mixed-methods research teams across multiple African countries. Excellent interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with the IsraAID team.

· Quantitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in statistics, economics, or related field; expertise in survey design, sampling methodology, and quantitative data analysis (e.g., STATA, R, SPSS); experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK).

· Qualitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in social sciences; expertise in qualitative methods including KIIs, FGDs, and complexity-aware approaches (e.g., Outcome

· Data Management / MEL Support: Experience in data cleaning, database management, and dashboard/data visualization; familiarity with data protection standards applicable to work with protected persons.

GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING LINES

The consulting firm will report to IsraAID’s ICNMP MEAL Coordinator, who holds day-to-day responsibility for the MEAL leadership of the ICNMP programme, and will work closely with the ICNMP program teams in both Uganda and Kenya Country Offices on tool design, data quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. The ICNMP MEAL Coordinator retains overall accountability for the assignment and will review and approve the inception report and final baseline report.

PAYMENT PLAN

50% after the approval of the inception report, 50% after the approval of the final report.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested candidates should submit the following:

· Technical proposal outlining approach and methodology

· A financial proposal in US Dollars (USD), detailing all consultancy-related costs (operational, and logistical costs for conducting the assignment in Kenya and Uganda).

· CVs of the Lead Consultant and the entire team

· At least three relevant samples of previous similar work

· At least two (2) recommendation letters from recent clients for similar assignments.

· Copy of the company registration, Memorandum, and Articles of Association if a company/ firm is applying.

· Copy of tax compliance Certificate

· TIN Number

· VAT Number

· Any other relevant information supporting the application.

EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR SELECTION OF THE CONSULTANT/CONSULTING FIRM

Proposals from the interested bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1\. Technical Approach & Understanding of the Assignment (30%): Understanding of the programme, evaluation objectives and scope; quality and appropriateness of the proposed methodology; sampling approach; quantitative and qualitative

methods; data analysis, triangulation and validation; and ethical/safeguarding considerations.

2\. Relevant Experience & Technical Capacity (25%): Demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, evaluations or similar assignments, particularly in humanitarian, refugee, displacement and development contexts. Experience working with refugee and host communities in Uganda and/or Kenya will be an advantage. Qualifications and expertise of the proposed consultant/team will also be considered.

3\. Workplan, Fieldwork & Data Quality Approach (20%): Feasibility of the proposed workplan within the 10-week period; capacity to undertake fieldwork sequentially in Uganda and Kenya; approach to data quality assurance, data management, safeguarding and secure access to data on a rolling basis during data collection.

4\. Financial Proposal & Value for Money (25%): Completeness, clarity and reasonableness of the financial proposal, including professional fees and all logistical and operational costs required to conduct the assignment in Uganda and Kenya.

ANNEXES

1\. Program Document

2\. Program LogFrame

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing contained in this RFP/TOR shall be construed as creating any obligation on the part of IsraAID to enter into a contract with any bidder. IsraAID reserves the unrestricted right to determine the evaluation criteria, request additional documentation, waive minor irregularities, seek clarifications, reject any or all proposals, and terminate the procurement process at its sole discretion and without prior notice.

jobs.title: 23451 Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA) (P)
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director for Operations (DRD-O), and in close coordination with the Department of Mobility, Pathways and Inclusion (DMPI) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer (RPLO), the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs), and Country Offices (COs) along the region’s priority migration routes, the Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will be responsible and accountable for leading, at the technical level, the regional operationalisation and implementation of the IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and providing strategic and programmatic advice on its implementation across the region.

The Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will ensure alignment with IOM’s global approach, lead regional and inter-agency coordination at the technical and operational levels, and oversee the application of Route-Based Approach (RteBA) tools and instruments within and across countries and along migration routes.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

jobs.title: 22954 Programme Officer (Immigration and Border Governance (IBG) (P)
Training Officer, Cultural Orientation
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers. This staff member is responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective cultural orientation resources such as curricula, training materials, and learning tools, and facilitating learning experiences that improve outcomes for newcomer children, adults, and families. This role requires hands-on experience working directly with clients, subject matter experts, and partners, along with prior experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Design and deliver versatile cultural orientation training to service providers and cultural orientation delivery staff.
- Provide responsive and cross-disciplinary technical assistance to refugee service providers in response to cultural orientation TTAs, adapting content to meet varied organizational needs and learning styles.
- In collaboration with colleagues across teams, develop written and multimedia learning resources (e.g., toolkits, videos, podcasts) that reflect trauma-informed, client-centered, and strength-based approaches.
- Adapt materials for different literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts
- Integrate feedback from internal and external reviewers to continuously improve training and resource contents and delivery methods.
- Facilitate communities of practice and peer learning groups to promote knowledge exchange and cross-training across service areas.

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage internal and external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

- Other duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably in a related field such as Education, International Development, Social Work, Public Administration, Cross-Cultural Studies, Migration/Refugee Studies, or a related social science (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience in supporting newcomers' access and gaining self-sufficiency for services and resources i.e. financial, medical, social, vocational etc.

**Preferred:**

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Strong understanding of cultural orientation frameworks, refugee/newcomer integration principles, and adult learning principles
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Programme Manager, Slovenia (Europe and Asia)
source: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.body:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

DCAF Ljubljana is a permanent DCAF regional office, based in Slovenia. The office is responsible for two main programs: implementation of the Police Cooperation Convention for Southeast Europe (PCC SEE) and Western Balkans Border Security Programme (BSP). With funding from the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), DCAF Ljubljana is implementing the project “CHAIN BiH”, a project strengthening sub-national case-building and inter-agency coordination against organised immigration crime (OIC) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on Una-Sana Canton, and is looking to employ an experienced, high-performing and positive individual to be our next **Programme Manager (Europe and Asia).**

**Location: DCAF Ljubljana, Slovenia, with frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina \***

**Starting date: November 2026 or upon agreement**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: Fixed-term employment until 31 March 2029, with the possibility of extension \*\***

**The role**

Join DCAF Ljubljana as a Programme Manager, tasked with implementation and management of the project “CHAIN BiH”. Reporting directly to the Director of DCAF Ljubljana office and supported by the Project Officer, you will be responsible for the overall coordination and oversight of a unique evidence-led project.

**Key areas of operation**

**Project leadership**

- Lead the overall implementation and day-to-day management of the project across its inception, field-testing, design and implementation phases, ensuring timely delivery of activities and achievement of project objectives.
- Develop and maintain detailed implementation plans, monitor progress, and proactively address implementation challenges, applying adaptive management as evidence from the field emerges.
- Lead the evidence-gathering and diagnostic work of the project.
- Coordinate project resources, supervise the Project Officer and external experts, and ensure effective collaboration across all project stakeholders.

**Partnership management**

- Maintain close working relationships with the donor and other relevant national and international stakeholders.
- Coordinate the participation of various participants in project activities.
- Facilitate the project’s Practice Review Forum, as well as regular communication, coordination meetings and consultations to support effective project implementation.
- Represent DCAF Ljubljana at project meetings, workshops and other relevant events.

**Monitoring and compliance**

- Monitor project progress against the adaptive results framework, agreed indicators and deliverables using results-based management principles, and ensure that lessons learned inform project decisions.
- Identify implementation risks, maintain the project risk register and develop appropriate mitigation measures.
- Ensure that gender equality and social inclusion, human rights, safeguarding and conflict-sensitivity standards are integrated throughout project implementation.
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements, DCAF policies and applicable project management procedures.
- Monitor project finances in close cooperation with the Project Officer and the DCAF finance and administration team, ensuring sound financial management, value for money and efficient use of project resources.

**Reporting and visibility**

- Prepare high-quality narrative and financial reports for the donor and DCAF management.
- Ensure appropriate project visibility and communication in accordance with donor requirements.
- Maintain accurate project documentation and support internal and external monitoring, evaluation and audit processes.

**Your experience**

We are looking for a motivated and experienced project management professional who combines strong organisational skills with the ability to build trusted partnerships across diverse institutional environments.

You bring

- University degree (Bachelor’s or higher) in a relevant field (e.g., security studies, law, criminology, social studies, international relations or related disciplines)
- 7 years of professional experience, including a minimum of 5 years of experience with international project management/implementation
- Proven experience in the planning, implementation and coordination of international projects;
- Experience with project monitoring, evaluation and results-based management, adaptive management and risk management
- Experience preparing high-quality narrative and financial reports for international donors;
- Proven experience in stakeholder coordination, building of partnerships and partnership management
- Demonstrated expertise in one or more of the following areas: organised crime, migrant smuggling and/or trafficking in human beings, criminal investigations, border policing or international police and judicial cooperation
- Experience in designing and delivering capacity-building activities for law enforcement and/or criminal justice institutions
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in multi-cultural environments
- Professional working proficiency in English and Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian

**Desirable assets**

The following would be considered an advantage:

- Previous experience as law enforcement officer or border police
- Familiarity with the institutional structure and operational aspects of law enforcement and prosecution services in Bosnia and Herzegovina, including at cantonal level
- Experience in working with the Border Police of Bosnia and Herzegovina, SIPA, the Service for Foreigners’ Affairs, the Ministry of Security of Bosnia and Herzegovina and/or cantonal police and prosecutors
- Knowledge of the migration context in Una-Sana Canton
- Familiarity with UK Government (FCDO)-funded programmes or other bilateral donor-funded projects
- Experience in integrating gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) and human rights considerations in security sector projects
- Experience working with international organisations or EU-funded programmes
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office tools, particularly Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook

**We offer**

At DCAF Ljubljana, you will have the opportunity to contribute to a project that supports more effective, rights-based responses to organised immigration crime and stronger security sector governance in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

We offer:

- an opportunity to work on a high-impact international project with tangible regional impact
- a rewarding, dynamic and meaningful work experience
- the chance to be part of a diverse team of collaborative, respectful, hardworking and values-driven people
- opportunity for professional growth, international networking and continuous learning
- the chance to contribute to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices

***\* The post holder is expected to undertake frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular to Una-Sana Canton.***

***\*\* The post remains subject to continued project funding.***

jobs.title: Country Director - JRS Thailand
jobs.body:
**Position Title: Country Director, JRS Thailand**  
**Location: Bangkok, Thailand with possibility to move Chiang Mai**  
**Reports to: Regional Director, JRS Asia Pacific**  
**Starting date: January 2027**  
**Type of Employment: Localised position open for all nationalities**  
**Local salary package, individual medical insurance, and visa support.**

(Note on family status: This is typically structured as an individual/non-family posting given the inclusion of "individual insurance" and local contract terms, but we need to explicitly add "Non-family posting" or "Family posting" at the top of the ad for absolute clarity.)

**Contract duration: 2 years (possibility of renewal)**  
**Starting Salary: THB88,495-THB102,141 (depending qualification)**

Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS) is an international Catholic organization, with a mission to accompany, serve, and advocate for refugees. Our advocacy flows from a service that is direct, pastoral, human and exposed to the sufferings and limitations of refugee life. Through our presence we help to sustain the goodness and hope in people who live in situations of evil and who have reason to despair. To support such an approach, JRS welcomes people who are able to contribute to and draw from the mission of JRS and the desire to share in the lives of the people we serve.

In Thailand, JRS serves refugees, asylum seekers and other forcibly displaced persons in urban Bangkok Metropolitan Area (BMA) and in two camps in Mae Hong Son. The field offices are located in Bangkok and Mae Hong Son, while the country office in Bangkok with a possibility to move to Chiang Mai. The main areas of work include education, psychosocial services, livelihoods, and advocacy.

**Overall Position Purpose:**

As the leader of JRS operations in Thailand, the Country Director oversees the overall management and success of country programmes, personnel, and offices to fulfill the JRS mission and humanitarian sector standards. Reporting directly to the Regional Director, the role provides strategic management support to project directors and teams while driving country-level operations. Key responsibilities include exploring emerging needs of refugees as well as emerging opportunities, developing and implementing project proposals as participatory as possible, overseeing country finances, evaluating projects, managing staff recruitment and care, managing partnerships especially critical for JRS Thailand’s work in Thailand, and maintaining vital external relations with the local Church, the Society of Jesus, government authorities, and international organizations.

**Responsibilities**

**Provision of Strategic Direction**

- Safeguard and promote the mission, vision, identity, values, and unity of JRS across all programmes in Thailand.
- Monitor political, social, economic, and migration trends to formulate proposals for new initiatives, project designs, and advocacies responding to the greatest needs of refugees and displaced persons.
- Lead the development and implementation of country strategic plans that is translated into annual programming, financial budgets, and in-country policies with participation and consultation of the staff.
- Facilitate critical reflection, monitoring, and evaluation of JRS projects to continuously improve program quality and services.
- Provide direction and guidance for JRS Thailand advocacy in country, in collaboration with JRS Asia Pacific and Global Offices.
- Identify capacity development/strengthening needed by the staff to do their roles
- Act as the gatekeeper of the JRS communication strategy and products to ensure. risk management, submitting required reports to Regional Director.

**People Management & Care**

- Review HR needs against available resources to ensure effective and efficient service delivery.
- Provide leadership, inspiration, and holistic care for staff well-being, fostering a supportive, multicultural, and professional working environment.
- Guide and support field teams through regular visits and listening sessions to maintain high standards of quality and accountability.
- Oversee staff recruitment, contracts, appraisals, and terminations in collaboration with HR and Project Directors.
- Lead regular reviews and updates of JRS Thailand’s Personnel, Travel, and Child Protection and Safeguarding policies.

**Programming**

- Guide the programming strategy to adapt to dynamic contexts for urban and in-camp refugees, as well as other emerging displacement issues aligned with the JRS mission.
- Collaborate with the Country Programme Officer, Project Directors, and Finance Manager to design proposals addressing the evolving needs of displaced populations.
- Ensure all projects comply with donor partnership agreements and humanitarian sector standards.
- Oversee timely and accurate reporting on project progress, challenges, and field updates through six-month and annual reports.
- Maintain regular communication with field teams to share critical updates regarding government policies, refugee situations, and organizational developments.
- Oversee database development and management to ensure data used for program development and reporting is accurate, while maintaining strict protection for sensitive information.

**Operations (Finance, Administration & Procurement)**

- Ensure financial administration and procurement strictly adhere to JRS policies to maintain full accountability.
- Lead the annual country planning and budgeting process collaboratively alongside the Finance Manager, Project Directors, and key staff.
- Oversee annual project and institutional audits, implementing corrective actions based on auditor recommendations in consultation with the Finance Manager and relevant team members.
- Monitor project budgets and financial reports, actively overseeing funding status and managing re-budgeting processes as needed.

**Partnership Management & Representation**

- Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with the local Jesuit Provincial, diocesan Church, local Jesuit communities, government authorities, key NGOs, and UNHCR.
- Sustain existing partnerships and forge new ones to ensure JRS Thailand's mission remains context-driven and responsive to the evolving needs of the communities we serve.
- Works closely with CCSDPT representatives and other NGOs in Thailand, UNHCR and the Royal Thai government at national level. JRS together with other organizations and networks also advocate changes to government policy/practice as needed for the benefit of the refugees.
- Represent JRS at national-level meetings with NGOs, UNHCR, government bodies, and stakeholder forums.
- Ensure prominent representation in donor forums while strictly complying with Thai government and donor requirements.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

- Education: Degree in Development Studies, Social Work, International Development, or a related field.
- Experience: Minimum of five years in a senior management role, overseeing complex programs, diverse multi-cultural teams, and strategic partnerships (experience in Asia is an advantage).
- Financial & Technical Skills: Strong background in project cycle management, budgeting, financial monitoring, and accounting, alongside high computer literacy (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with a proven track record in report writing and proposal development (knowledge of Thai is an advantage).
- Values & Mindset: Deep empathy for refugees, a strong grasp of local cultural sensitivities, and a service-minded, patient, and self-motivated approach.
- Personal Attributes: Exceptional diplomatic, leadership, and stress-management skills, with the ability to thrive under pressure in a multicultural, multi-faith, and resource-constrained environment.

jobs.title: Medical Coordinator (F/M) - Afghanistan
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

## About the role

You will join the mission at a pivotal moment. Beyond ensuring the quality and relevance of medical activities, you will play a key role in strengthening the mission’s medical leadership, supporting teams, reinforcing SRHR priorities and helping to structure programmes, partnerships and ways of working in line with Médecins du Monde’s values and standards. Working closely with the General Coordinator, HQ Health Advisor and programme teams, you will contribute directly to improving access to quality healthcare for vulnerable populations across Afghanistan.

## What you'll do

? Define, drive and monitor the mission's medical strategy and ensure its alignment with MdM's global priorities, with a particular focus on SRHR.

? Ensure the quality, relevance and effectiveness of health, nutrition, MHPSS and SRHR activities across all programmes.

? Lead, support and develop medical teams through coaching, capacity-building and performance management.

? Analyse programme performance and medical data to guide decision-making and continuous improvement.

? Design new projects, contribute to donor proposals and support the mission's strategic development.

? Represent MdM with health authorities, humanitarian actors, partners and community stakeholders.

? Adapt programmes and priorities in response to contextual changes, population needs and humanitarian emergencies.

## Who you'll work with

You will report directly to the General Coordinator and maintain a strong functional relationship with the Health Advisor based at headquarters. You will supervise a technical medical team of two to three people and work closely with programme managers, medical supervisors, support departments and local partners across the mission. The position also requires regular interaction with health authorities, UN agencies, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and community representatives.

## What you'll gain

- Develop advanced leadership skills in one of the world's most complex humanitarian contexts.
- Strengthen your expertise in SRHR programming, community-based health approaches and health system strengthening.Gain significant experience in humanitarian negotiation, representation and stakeholder engagement
- Contribute to meaningful, high-impact programmes supporting vulnerable communities while helping shape the future strategic direction of the mission.
- Propose and develop projects relating to women’s rights and health, in collaboration with local organisations.

### REQUIREMENTS

## You are the right match if you:

- Demonstrate a strong commitment to human rights, non-discrimination and respectful engagement, even in sensitive contexts where values, beliefs or lifestyles differ significantly from your own.
- Can provide strategic medical leadership and bring structure, clarity and direction to complex health programmes.
- Lead teams through trust, listening, accountability and collaboration while fostering a healthy and inclusive work environment.
- Have successfully strengthened the quality, relevance and impact of SRHR or public health programmes.
- Build productive relationships and negotiate effectively with authorities, partners and diverse stakeholders in challenging environments.
- Remain calm, analytical and decisive when responding to emergencies, operational constraints or rapidly changing contexts.

## This role may not suit you if:

- You favour directive or individualistic approaches over collaboration, dialogue and collective problem-solving.
- You struggle to provide constructive management, clear communication and respectful feedback.
- You are uncomfortable representing humanitarian principles and advocating for vulnerable populations in sensitive environments.
- You prefer highly structured and predictable settings over complex and evolving humanitarian contexts.
- You are not aligned with Médecins du Monde's values, principles and activist approach.

## Recruitment process

Apply soon! If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

## Ready to apply?

We only need your CV and a cover letter.

If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we'd love to hear from you!

### **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: € 3,664
- Fixed-term contract (6 months), starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: in a guesthouse with other expatriates initially, with the possibility of individual housing later on
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Coordinateur logistique voltigeur - Worldwide (F/H)
jobs.body:
Vous souhaitez intégrer une association militante et agir concrètement pour plus de justice sociale ?

Médecins du Monde agit depuis plus de 40 ans pour soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, dénoncer les entraves à l’accès aux soins et faire évoluer durablement les politiques de santé.

En France et dans près de 30 pays, nos actions s’articulent autour de six combats politiques :

- droits et santé sexuels et reproductifs (dont le droit à l’avortement)
- migration, exil, droits et santé
- réduction des risques
- santé environnement
- droits et système de santé
- espaces humanitaires

## **Pourquoi nous avons besoin de vous**

Les interventions d’urgence face aux crises, conflits, catastrophes naturelles, sont l’un des axes prioritaires d’intervention pour Médecins du Monde. Notre indépendance financière, la force de nos partenariats, l'implication et la flexibilité de nos équipes sont autant d’éléments clés pour apporter une réponse efficace à ces catastrophes.

Le mandat de la Cellule Urgence est d’intervenir en priorité sur les urgences et crises qui surviennent dans les pays où MdM est déjà opérationnel (30 pays). La réponse d’urgence dans les pays où MdM n’est pas présent est systématiquement considéré si l’accès au continuum de soins est interrompu et si les capacités du pays et des acteurs sur place sont dépassées.

MdM fournit également un appui et une expertise opérationnelle et technique aux missions des pôles géographiques sur leurs réponses d’urgences.

Vous faites partie de l’équipe voltigeur.euse.s de la Cellule Urgence qui est donc déployée dans les contextes d’urgence pour lancer de nouvelles interventions et/ou renforcer les équipes existantes. Vous pouvez également être déployé.e pour participer à des missions exploratoires, participer à l’ouverture de nouvelles missions et/ou de nouvelles bases, appuyer les opérations/missions existantes MdM à travers du « gap-filling » ou appuyer la mise en œuvre d’activités spécifiques liées aux activités logistiques (ex : formation, préparation, etc.).

## **Vos missions**

Vos principales responsabilités sont :

- Piloter la stratégie logistique de la mission et en assurer la mise en œuvre
- Coordonner et superviser l’ensemble des activités logistiques : chaîne d’approvisionnement, parc de véhicules, gestion des stocks, équipements, bâtiments, infrastructures informatiques, moyens de communication et énergie
- Animer et renforcer les capacités de l’équipe
- Appuyer également le/la coordinateur·rice général·e dans le suivi des procédures de sécurité
- Veiller au respect et à la bonne application des procédures MdM et bailleurs, et contribuer à garantir la qualité, l’efficacité et la conformité des services logistiques au sein de la mission, tout en œuvrant à la prévention et à la lutte contre la fraude et la corruption

Le partage du temps de travail entre le terrain et le siège est évaluée à 80%-20%.

La durée d’un déploiement sur le terrain est de trois 3 mois maximum, et est suivie par un temps de récupération.

## **Vos collègues**

Vous travaillez sous la responsabilité du responsable de la Cellule urgences basé au siège. Lorsque vous êtes déployé.e sur le terrain, vous reportez directement au/à la coordinateur.rice général.e de la mission. Vous avez un lien fonctionnel avec le/la référent.e logistique basé.e au siège. Vous collaborez avec les coordinateur.rice.s support ainsi qu'avec le/la chargé.e d'accès humanitaire & risques et les équipes programme.

## PROFIL

**Vous êtes la bonne personne si :**

- Vous avez une formation supérieure bac+2 type achat ou logistique
- Vous justifiez d'une expérience professionnelle de 5 ans (dont minimum 1 an sur un poste en coordination logistique dans le milieu humanitaire ou de minimum 2 ans d'expérience en tant que logisticien)
- Vous avez une solide résistance au stress et une capacité à vous adapter dans des contextes sécuritaires complexes
- Vous maitrisez le Pack Office
- Vous maitrisez l’anglais et le français couramment à l’écrit comme à l’oral

**Ce poste n'est pas pour vous si :**

- La flexibilité et l’adaptabilité ne comptent pas parmi vos principales qualités ; les déplacements fréquents ainsi que les changements réguliers d’équipe vous posent des difficultés
- Vous craignez de ne pas vous retrouver dans les valeurs et le positionnement militant de Médecins du Monde.

## Les prochaines étapes

Si votre candidature est sélectionnée, nous vous contacterons pour vous proposer un entretien RH avec notre chargée de recrutement. Puis viendront l'entretien technique et managérial (auquel des cas pratiques pourront éventuellement être intégrés).

Dans le cadre de la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, des vérifications d’antécédents sur listes internationales pourront être effectuées. Les données sont traitées de façon confidentielle et sécurisée. Plus d’infos : [http://bit.ly/3CSThBs](http://bit.ly/3CSThBs)

Un extrait de casier judiciaire (B3) sera demandé à toute personne recrutée.

## Nous attendons votre candidature

Nous n’avons besoin que de votre CV et de votre lettre de motivation.

Si vous pensez correspondre à ce poste, n’attendez plus, postulez !

## VOS CONDITIONS D'EMPLOI

**Contrat & statut :**

- CDD à pourvoir dès que possible et jusqu'au 31/12/2026
- Salaire brut mensuel de 3 392 €
- Statut : agent de maitrise
- Poste à temps plein

**Les avantages :**

- Télétravail ponctuel
- 13e mois (pour les salarié.e.s ayant plus de 6 mois d’ancienneté)
- Prime de déplacement terrain de 198,18€ brut/mois au prorata du temps de présence sur le terrain
- Au siège, tickets restaurants d’une valeur unitaire de 10€ (participation à hauteur de 60% de MdM, 40% salarié.e) et sur le terrain via une allocation forfaitaire de restauration fixée en fonction du pays
- Au siège, remboursement du titre de transport en commun à 50% (abonnement mensuel) et prise en charge à 100% des allers-retours siège-terrain
- Logement pris en charge sur le terrain à 100%
- Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%
- MdM favorise la formation et la mobilité interne

**Les indispensables :**

- 5 semaines de congés + 22,5 RTT par an
- Engagement fort en faveur de l’inclusion et de la lutte contre toutes les discriminations
- Plus d’infos : [https://bit.ly/3x5MezL](https://bit.ly/3x5MezL)

**Cadre de travail :**

- Poste basé au siège à Saint-Denis (20% du temps) et sur les terrains internationaux (80% du temps)
- Déploiement sur le terrain pas avant 1 mois d’intégration
- Travail sur écran, en open space
- Communication orale et téléphonique
- Posture assise prolongée

**Diversité et inclusion**

MdM s’engage pour l’insertion des personnes en situation de handicap et lutte contre toutes les discriminations.

Si vous bénéficiez d’une reconnaissance de la qualité de travailleur.se handicapé.e et/ou si vous avez besoin d’un aménagement de poste, n’hésitez pas à nous en faire part.

jobs.title: Caseworker (Dari speaking)
jobs.body:
**IRC Background:** The mission of the International Rescue Committee (IRC) is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933, the IRC has a presence in over 40 countries and 27 offices in the United States; the IRC leads the way from harm to home. Domestically, our offices across the U.S. ensure new arrivals have food, shelter, and clothing, and work with refugees to help them gain self-sufficiency.

**Job Overview:** The UHP Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The UHP Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has living essentials such as housing, food, medical care, and access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Provide comprehensive, client-centered case management services including but not limited to accessing public benefits, housing, mental health services, medical care, school and ESL enrollment, referrals to community service providers, and assistance with booking appointments and scheduling transportation and interpretation.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Work cross different programs as needed
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position reports to:** OIRS Casework Supervisor

**Position directly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect Reporting: Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:***IRC Employees and program departments across Sacramento

***External:***IRC partners and other community agencies

jobs.title: Expression of Interest - Research Consultant/Research Firm: Falepili Mobility Pathway Economic Impact and Policy Research
jobs.body:
**About the Australia-Pacific Partnerships Platform**

The Australia-Pacific Partnerships Platform program is an Australian Government initiative funded by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and managed by DT Global. It provides Pacific Island Countries with a suite of flexible, fit-for-purpose options that support broad governance and stability development outcomes. Services provided by the Partnerships Platform can include recruitment, procurement, grants, monitoring and evaluation, research and training, advisory support, and program design and management. Our partners identify the areas in which this support is required, and these can include climate change, strengthening public financial management systems, infrastructure, governance, economic growth and social inclusion.

**About DT Global**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [**www.dt-global.com**](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**About the Opportunity**

This research seeks to generate robust evidence on the sustainability and economic challenges of the Falepili Mobility Pathway, how to maximise the economic benefits of the Falepili Mobility Pathway and circular migration, the financial challenges faced by Falepili visa holders, and the potential for a small loan facility for visa holders. The findings will support evidence-based policy development and contribute to a stronger understanding of how migration pathways can support Tuvalu's development priorities, resilience objectives and future planning.

**Selection Criteria**

Applicants should demonstrate:

- Advanced qualifications and a strong publication or applied-research record in economics, migration, labour mobility, development policy, public policy, finance or a closely related field;
- Demonstrated experience undertaking Pacific research, preferably relating to migration, mobility, remittances, labour markets or small island states;
- Strong mixed-methods research design and quantitative and qualitative analysis capability;
- Experience with feasibility studies, inclusive finance, loan facilities or financial-product design;
- Knowledge of Tuvaluan context, institutions and culturally appropriate engagement practices;
- Experience conducting research with geographically dispersed participants, including online data collection;
- Strong research ethics, safeguarding and data-protection practice;
- The ability to communicate complex findings clearly to Government and non-technical audiences; and
- Capacity to complete the assignment within the required timeframe.

**HOW TO APPLY**  
We welcome your interest in joining the Australia-Pacific Partnerships Platform. Interested consultants, research firms, universities, research institutes, individual researchers, or consortia should submit:

- A brief technical proposal outlining their understanding of the assignment, proposed approach and methodology.
- Details of the proposed team, including relevant expertise, roles and key personnel CVs.
- A summary of relevant experience, including examples of similar research or evaluation assignments.
- An outline of the proposed approach to ethics, data protection and culturally appropriate engagement.
- A detailed financial proposal with budget assumptions and indicative costs.
- Any declarations, including conflicts of interest and proposed subcontracting arrangements.
- Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate how Tuvaluan and Pacific expertise and participation will be incorporated into the assignment.

jobs.title: Head of support services (F/M) - Lebanon
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Lebanon**

MdM has been working in Lebanon for 30 years and actively contributed to respond to needs of the most vulnerable communities as the context unfolded (2011 Syrian crisis, 2019 severe economic crisis, 2020 Beirut Blast) and the current period since October 7th, 2023 – especially as the war resumed in Lebanon since March 2nd, 2026.

MdM’s intervention in Lebanon aims to strengthen the national health system and increase access to quality healthcare.

MdM is recognized in Lebanon as a major actor in the areas of mental health (MHPSS) and sexual and reproductive health (SRH). MdM supports several health centers and mobile clinics in the South, Beirut Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and Baalbek Hermel; and works with other partners.

Despite the June 2026 ceasefire, the situation remains highly volatile and high needs remain, particularly in the South of the country. MdM continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure an appropriate, timely and flexible intervention, always in line with the needs of the various conflict-affected populations.

## **About the role**

You are responsible for the overall strategy and compliance, through the management of logistics, human resources and finance departments in the MdM Lebanon mission.

You ensure support services are fully compliant with MdM policies, donor requirements, national authorities' regulations, and applicable legislation.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the line management of the General coordinator, and the technical management of the Desk manager, you work in close collaboration with the other departments: Program, Medical/MHPSS, Grants, Security-Safety-Access, MEAL.

## **What you’ll do**

**Support services leadership & strategic planning**

- Provide strategic leadership and guidance to the General Coordinator and Country Management Team on all support-related matters
- Contribute to country strategy development, annual planning and financial planning processes
- Lead support services planning and ensure alignment between operational and programme priorities
- Anticipate operational challenges and oversee contingency planning to ensure humanitarian response continuity

**Development & reporting**

- Ensure support functions contribute effectively to proposal development, reporting and donor-related processes
- Coordinate the timely provision of analyses and support inputs required for programme development and decision-making

**Support services management & quality**

- Oversee the quality, compliance and performance of all support functions in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements and local regulations
- Ensure sound resource management, accountability and legal compliance across the mission
- Monitor support systems, identify risks and corrective actions, and strengthen tools and procedures to support informed decision-making
- Promote effective integration and collaboration between Finance, HR, Logistics and programme teams

**Risk management, compliance & internal control**

- Strengthen internal control systems and ensure appropriate management of mission resources
- Identify and mitigate financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding, fraud and corruption risks
- Lead or coordinate audits, investigations and follow up on recommendations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
- Promote adherence to anti-fraud, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies across the mission

**Team management & capacity building**

- Recruit, manage and develop the support services team through coaching, performance management and capacity-building initiatives
- Foster effective coordination, communication and information sharing across teams
- Identify learning and development needs and ensure access to appropriate technical support and resources

**Coordination & representation**

- Ensure strong coordination between support, programme, field and headquarters teams
- Facilitate effective information sharing and contribute to organizational reporting
- Represent the organization with authorities, partners and donors, alongside the General Coordinator, when required.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Have significant experience in humanitarian operations, including in complex contexts, and have held a senior support coordination role within an international NGO
- Have strong expertise across HR, Finance, Logistics and Administration, ideally supporting health programmes and donor-funded projects
- Are a strategic and analytical leader, able to drive operational performance, manage risks and support decision-making
- Have a proven ability to lead, coach and develop teams while fostering collaboration across departments
- Are organized, adaptable and solution-oriented, with the confidence to make decisions and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Are an excellent communicator and relationship builder, comfortable engaging with partners, authorities, donors and diverse teams
- Are comfortable using Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel
- Are fluent in English; knowledge of French and/or Arabic and experience in the Middle East are strong assets.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer a specialist role rather than overseeing multiple support functions and leading cross-department coordination
- Are uncomfortable working in complex, evolving humanitarian environments where priorities can shift rapidly
- Are not motivated by team leadership, capacity building and stakeholder engagement responsibilities

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info:  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3392€
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Beirut, Lebanon
- Field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Outreach Officer
jobs.body:
**Job overview**

The Outreach Officer leads participant recruitment and outreach for the “Razem na Rynku Pracy” (RMW) project financed from the Labor Fund under the Sectoral Activation Program for Foreigners for 2026., driving the multi-channel sourcing effort that feeds Individual Support for Project Participants in Professional Activation and, through it, the project’s language, vocational, and labour-rights components (P1–P3). The role is responsible for reaching, informing, and registering foreign nationals across the project’s target regions so that the project’s headline target of 1,500 participants is met, and for ensuring a smooth handover of registered participants into the diagnosis and Individual Action Plan (IPD) process, with confirmation of activities completed and services delivered.

**Key responsibilities**

***1. Multi-channel outreach & recruitment***

- Plan and deliver outreach across the project’s multi-channel recruitment model: online registration, field activities and information sessions, local events, workshops, and community activities.
- Represent the project at community events, job fairs, and information sessions to raise awareness and reach eligible participants across target regions.
- Coordinate with partners infoline and first-contact function to keep outreach channels complementary and avoid duplicating first-contact responsibilities.

***2. Registration, screening & referral***

- Handle inbound enquiries by phone and other channels, providing accurate project information and screening candidates against eligibility criteria (legal residence in Poland, age, target-group definition).
- Register participants using the project’s common registration form, capturing information on professional situation, Polish language level, residency status, and barriers to employment, always with informed consent and respect for participants’ privacy.

- Fluency in Polish required; fluency in Ukrainian and/or Russian required given the project’s target population; English is an asset.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust quickly with people from diverse backgrounds, including people with experience of forced migration or displacement.
- Comfortable with proactive, target-driven outreach: field visits, community events, and sustained phone-based engagement.
- Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, particularly for data entry and maintaining accurate records.
- Cultural sensitivity and a strong commitment to treating all participants with dignity, respect, and confidentiality.
- Familiarity with the Polish labour market, residency/legalization procedures, or local labour-market institutions (PUP, MOPS, JST) is an asset.
- Willingness to travel regularly within the project’s target regions.

**Key success indicators**

- Minimum 1,500 participants recruited and registered over the project period, in line with Projects target.
- Complete, accurate participant data entered into KOBO/CommCare with minimal errors or missing fields.
- Confirmed, disaggregated data covering IAP development, completed activities and support received of all registered project participants.
