jobs.title: Technical Mentor - Consultancy
jobs.body:
**Strengthening Media Capacity and Civil Oversight for Accountability in Lebanon**

## **Project Background**

Lebanon's governance environment is heavily impacted by systemic crises and erosion of the national integrity system. This project aims to strengthen the organizational capacity of six Lebanese media and civil society organizations (CSOs) to evaluate public data sources, apply advanced analytical workflows, and execute evidence-based accountability work.

The project integrates cutting-edge technology, AI-assisted research routines, and automated data monitoring workflows to enhance the analytical capacity of independent media and CSOs scrutinizing public procurement, registries, and financial data in Lebanon.

This project is implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH in partnership with Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT). It is funded by Germany through the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

- **Duration:** 10 months
- **Level of Effort:** 5 days per month per mentor (across 6 mentors)

**Role Objective**

Technical Mentors work directly with assigned organizations to build, refine, document, and embed custom data tools, AI workflows, and monitoring routines into regular organizational operations until complete operational independence is achieved.

## **Key Responsibilities & Scope of Work**

- **Hackathon Support & Working Sprint:** Guide assigned teams during the Beirut Hackathon event. Provide at least two structured technical check-ins per week during the 4-week working sprint to unblock obstacles in coding, data fetching, and prototyping.
- **Mentorship Opening & Workplan:** Conduct an opening 1-day in-person session in Beirut. Co-draft a binding mentorship workplan with assigned organization specifying technical tasks, staff training targets, and output timelines.
- **Fortnightly Mentorship & Site Visits:** Hold bi-weekly remote sessions and at least two in-person site visits per organization. Train at least two designated staff members to independently operate and maintain the tool/agent.
- **Technical Log & Verification:** Maintain running technical logs documenting software architecture, code repositories, user manuals, digital safety protocols, and editorial integration.

## **Key Deliverables**

1. Approved Mentorship Workplan and baseline technical diagnosis for assigned organization.
2. Fortnightly mentorship meeting notes and technical progress updates.
3. Completed Technical Log, source code documentation, and User Manual for the custom tool/workflow.
4. Final assessment report confirming that at least two staff members can independently operate the tool without external support.

## **Qualifications & Requirements**

- Degree or equivalent professional experience in Data Journalism, Software Development, OSINT, Data Analysis, or Computational Media.
- 5 to 7 years of demonstrated experience in mentoring, capacity building, or training non-technical staff in digital tools.
- Expertise in tools such as Python, SQL, web scraping, LLM APIs, visualization platforms, or security protocols.
- Fluency in Arabic and English.

jobs.title: Cash and Markets Project Manager Sudan Khartoum (Open for Sudanese only)
jobs.body:
**Background:**

The Cash Project Manager sits in the Country Office Cash & Markets team, reports to the Cash & Markets Programme Manager, and works at middle-management level. The role leads the day-to-day management of a portfolio of CVA grants across several Area Offices. It supervises the Cash & Markets Project Coordinator(s) and is the technical reference point for Area Office cash and market staff. It is the main link between the Country Office, Area Office teams, partners and support functions, turning strategy and donor commitments into on-time, compliant, quality delivery.

**What you will do:**

The Cash Project Manager leads the oversea of NRC's cash and markets projects from start to close-out. The role owns project cycle management across multiple grants and Area Offices: planning, budget follow-up, quality assurance, reconciliation of reach figures, and timely donor reporting. It ensures cash reaches people most in need safely and in line with NRC standards, and that market functionality and risk inform every modality decision.

The position sits in the Country Office Cash & Markets team and is a key link between the Programme Manager, Area Office teams, partners, the Sudan Collective technical unit and support functions.

General Responsibilities:

1. Line management responsibilities for directly reporting staff. This includes the
    - Performance management process; setting clear goals aligned to country strategy and priorities, and to follow up and support staff’s achievement.
    - Responsible for key processes as workforce planning, recruitment, staff induction and development and ensure Duty of Care for own staff
    - Manage cash projects (activities, budgets, procurement, partners, documentation) in line with proposals, strategy and donor requirements.
2. Report on progress regularly and on an ad-hoc basis, meeting all internal and donor deadlines.
3. Coordinate across NRC departments and Area Offices involved in delivery

**Specific responsibilities**

1. Project cycle management
    - Engage with AO teams to develop and maintain work plans, spending plans, MEAL plans and procurement plans for each CVA grant.
    - Lead grant opening, project review and grant closing meetings with Grants, Finance and Area Offices.
2. Cash and voucher delivery – Field based.
    - Oversee MPCA, sectoral cash, voucher delivery, both direct and partner led.
    - Ensure Area Office teams apply NRC Sudan SOPs: targeting, registration, verification, payment and complaints handling.
3. Markets and feasibility
    - Lead or support cash feasibility, market and risk assessments ahead of each response.
    - Identify opportunities for market-support interventions and integration with other Core Competencies.
4. Grants, budgets and reporting
    - Oversee CVA project budgets with AO teams and Finance: forecasting, BvA follow-up, and timely reallocation requests.
    - Reconcile reach and distribution figures across Area Offices, NRC systems, in close collaboration with the Information Management Coordinator.
5. MEAL, quality and learning
    - Work with MEAL on baseline, post-distribution monitoring and market monitoring, and act on findings.
    - Ensure complaints and feedback are tracked, referred and closed on time.
6. Partnership and coordination
    - Support partner capacity assessments and capacity building for local partners on CVA.
    - Represent NRC in the Cash Working Group and CCS technical meetings as delegated.
7. People management
    - Line-manage the Cash & Markets Project Coordinator(s) and provide functional guidance to Area Office cash staff.
    - Identify capacity gaps and deliver or arrange CVA training for NRC staff.

**Please refer to the** [**Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQC6dQo7nbPSR5_U1Cn2kmuxAZK1nDO9GHQDXompx5lhLDk?e=DxdFER) **for detailed information as the above responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

1. **Generic professional competencies:**

- Bachelor's degree in economics, business administration, social sciences, development studies or a related field. A Master's degree is an asset.
- At least 4 years of humanitarian experience, including a minimum of 3 years of experience managing Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) projects or similar interventions.
- Proven project cycle management: planning, budget management, risk management and reporting on multiple grants at once.
- Experience working in complex, insecure and fast-changing contexts.
- Line management experience, including recruitment and performance management.
- Documented results related to the position's responsibilities.
- Fluency in Arabic and English, written and spoken. Able to draft donor-quality reports in English.
- Advanced Excel skills. Experience with KoBo/ODK, Power BI or beneficiary data systems (e.g. LMMS, RedRose) is an asset.

**2. Context related skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Strong knowledge of the Sudan context, including displacement dynamics, the economic situation and access constraints.
- Knowledge of Sudanese markets, financial service providers and digital payment options (e.g. mobile money, bank apps).
- Experience with cash consortia or the Sudan Cash Working Group.
- Experience with institutional donor requirements, especially ECHO, BHA, SHF/CBPF and GFFO.
- Experience with partner-led delivery, including local NGOs and ERRs. Experience with group cash transfers is an asset.
- Familiarity with CALP, Sphere and MSMS market assessment tools\*.\*
- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: Al-Geniena, Darfur/**Update to the advert on 19th October: the duty station is changed from Al-Geniena, Darfur to Khartoum.**
- Contract: 12 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: 40% to Area Offices and field locations
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s **national** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
    - **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
    - **Your most updated Cover Letter**
    - **Do not attach certificates or any other documents apart from the two mentioned above.**
    - **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- **This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Sudan. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency.**
- We receive many applications for each vacant position. Therefore, only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)
- [Learn more about Sudan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/sudan/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Consultancy Services of Graphic designer in shift asia learning session
jobs.body:
## TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR CONSULTANCY SERVICES

### Graphic designer in shift asia learning session

***Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.***

**Shaping a stronger Oxfam for people living in poverty.**

**BACKGROUND**

The Supporting Humanitarian Initiatives for Transformation in Asia (SHIFT Asia) Project is a critical regional initiative building upon the success of the first phase of Women’s Local Humanitarian Leadership (WLHL) implemented in 2022–2023. SHIFT Asia now operates across Indonesia, Bangladesh, the Philippines, and Myanmar, and is focused on advancing women’s leadership by positioning their organizations at the center of humanitarian decision-making.

The project operates based on the reality that women and girls are disproportionately affected by crises yet remain severely underrepresented in leadership. By applying a feminist and participatory approach that fosters regional networks and solidarity, SHIFT Asia aims to transform humanitarian systems to be more inclusive, representative, and effective in achieving gender-transformative disaster preparedness and response.

Central to this second phase is the SHIFT Asia Learning Agenda (2025–2027). This agenda promotes feminist learning spaces, peer-to-peer exchanges, and collective capacity enhancement in key areas such as program design (Theory of Change - TOC) and robust Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems. Grounded in Oxfam’s Common Approach to MEAL, the Learning Agenda is designed to generate evidence, capture lessons, and drive accountability and social change across local, national, and regional levels. To effectively communicate these lessons, we require a professional Graphic Designer to transform technical content into engaging visual assets.

**PURPOSE**

The primary purpose of this assignment is to secure a professional Graphic Designer to produce high-quality visual learning materials for **eight (8) design packages**. The goal is to ensure complex humanitarian and feminist concepts are accessible and shareable across regional networks.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

The selected graphic designer shall be responsible for:

- **Visual Design:** Creating cohesive and culturally sensitive designs that align with Oxfam’s branding and the feminist principles of the SHIFT Asia project.
- **Layout & Illustration**: Developing infographics and layouts that simplify technical MEAL and program design concepts.
- **Revision:** Incorporating feedback from the SHIFT Asia team to ensure technical accuracy and visual clarity.
- **Technical Compliance:** Ensuring all files are delivered in high-resolution print-ready and web-optimized formats.

**EXPECTED RESULTS**

*It must be noted that the copyright for all the plans and reports and other intellectual property created as a part of this project shall vest exclusively to Oxfam which would be free to use all such material, without restrictions.*

For each of the **eight (8) design packages**, the consultant will provide:

1. **One (1) Learning Paper Design:** A detailed A4-sized document of 5–6 pages summarizing the key findings and technical data of the topic.
2. **Two (2) Social Media Designs:** Two separate carousels (4–6 slides each) designed for platforms like LinkedIn, Instagram, or Facebook to promote the learning highlights.
3. **Posting the social media design via Oxfam Asia social media platform**

**DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE**

The implementation period will be for **approximately 6 months** starting from **19 November 2026**.

***Deliverable - Description - Quantity***

1. ***Learning Papers -*** 5-6 page A4 Infographic/Learning Paper per package - 8 Total
2. ***Social Media Assets -*** Carousel (4-6 slides) per package (2 versions each) - 16 Total

**DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The intended start date is 19 November 2026 and the period of implementation will be for approximately 6 monthsfrom this date.

Note: Specific session dates will be confirmed upon contracting.

**CONTRACT SUPERVISION**

The consultant will work closely with and under day-to day supervision of the of the SHIFT Asia MEAL Coordinator to fulfil the objectives of this consultancy.

**REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS**

The consultant’s proposal shall demonstrate the following refined capabilities to ensure alignment with the visual and technical needs of the SHIFT Asia project:

- **Language Proficiency:** Near-native or native fluency in English and professional working proficiency in either Indonesian (Bahasa) or Bengali (Bangla).
- **Technical Experience:** A minimum of 3 years of professional experience providing graphic design services for international development or humanitarian organizations.
- **Portfolio:** A strong portfolio demonstrating a proven ability to create similar tasks, specifically transforming technical data and concepts into digestible 5-6 page learning papers and social media carousels.
- **Software Proficiency:** Proven ability to use **Canva** or other professional design and conferencing platforms (e.g., Adobe Creative Suite, Zoom, MS Teams) with access to reliable high-speed internet.
- **Oxfam Branding:** Prior experience working with **Oxfam branding guidelines** and visual identity is highly preferable to ensure seamless integration with existing project materials.

**KEY ATTRIBUTES**

- Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to cultural differences and gender issues, as well as the commitment to equal opportunities.
- Ability to demonstrate an openness and willingness to learn about the application of gender/gender mainstreaming, women’s rights, and diversity for all aspects of development work.
- Commitment to Oxfam’s safeguarding policies to ensure all people who come into contact with Oxfam are as safe as possible.

**ORGANISATIONAL VALUES**

- Accountability – Our purpose-driven, results-focused approach means we take responsibility for our actions and hold ourselves accountable. We believe that others should also be held accountable for their actions.
- Empowerment – Our approach means that everyone involved with Oxfam, from our staff and supporters to people living in poverty, should feel they can make change happen.
- Inclusiveness – We are open to everyone and embrace diversity. We believe everyone has a contribution to make, regardless of visible and invisible differences.

jobs.title: Global Communication Coordinator
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified and enthusiastic Global Communication Coordinator.

**About the job**

You will be working with a diverse and dynamic team at the Mixed Migration Centre (MMC), which is an intrinsic part of DRC. MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based protection responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move.  
Reporting to the director of MMC, the Global Communication Coordinator leads and oversees the implementation of all MMC activities in relation to internal and external communication and visibility, finalization of MMC publications for release, report launches, organization of events and MMC’s online (social media, website, etc.) presence

  
Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

***Communications strategy***

- Lead the implementation of MMC's external communication strategy across the global team and regional hubs.

***Publications, events, online presence and campaigns***

- Oversee the updating and maintenance of the MMC website.
- Be responsible for all MMC social media output, including the MMC X, LinkedIn and YouTube accounts and channels.
- Oversee the finalisation of all MMC research outputs in line with MMC editorial and brand guidelines, and act as guardian of MMC's global publication calendar.
- Lead the release of all publications, including the Quarterly Mixed Migration Updates, and develop and execute the associated communication plans and toolkits, including social media launches.
- Oversee the release of MMC's regional and global newsletters.
- Lead the implementation of the extensive communication campaign around the annual Mixed Migration Review (MMR).
- Prepare and deliver virtual and in-person events (registrations, social media promotion, hosting of online conference platforms, etc.).

***External engagement and identification of opportunities***

- Work closely with MMC regional hub staff to proactively identify and develop new communication tools, such as podcasts, videos on key research findings and human-interest stories.
- Track events calendars, and signal and organise speaking opportunities for MMC.
- Draft press releases, maintain an up-to-date list of MMC media contacts and strengthen media outreach.
- Engage with global and regional partners to disseminate MMC research products.
- Liaise with DRC Communication and Press offices at HQ (Copenhagen), Geneva, Brussels and in the regions.

***Coordination, reporting and management***

- Report on MMC's external visibility (e.g. monthly and annual website and social media statistics, event attendance and post-event surveys, external references to MMC) as input into MMC's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning.
- Manage the work of MMC's communication officers/specialists (currently two).

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to be able to take the lead on your tasks and be able to oversee all internal and external communication and visibility activities across the global MMC network. Attention to detail while capable of keeping the big picture in sight is key in this role. Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- 5+ years of professional experience in external communication, ideally in the NGO, UN, research or humanitarian/development sector.
- Proven experience planning and running social media campaigns and managing social media output.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an excellent eye for detail.
- Strong organisational and multitasking skills, and flexibility to manage many tasks of varying size at the same time.
- Full proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); proficiency in WordPress, InDesign and Canva.
- Ability to develop data visualisations using different visualisation software.
- Ability to work effectively with a team based remotely across several countries.
- University degree within relevant field of study

*Desirable*

- Strong affinity with matters relating to (mixed) migration, forced displacement and humanitarian/development work.
- Previous work with NGOs or UN in the development or humanitarian sector
- Fluency in French and/or Spanish
- Academic background in migration studies, including some experience in research (field-level research is a strong asset)

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Work location: Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station

Start date: 1st December 2026

End date: 31 June 2027

The position is temporary as it is currently funded until the end of June, but likely to be extended, upon donor funding confirmation.

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC The position is at “fuldmægtig” level. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

Please note that you need to have the right to work in Denmark (through nationality or existing work visa) in order to be considered for this role.

**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Gretel Ana Martin Araya by email gretel.araya@mixedmigration.org. We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/javascript:void(0)).

*Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.*

jobs.title: Senior Advisor - Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Senior Advisor - Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)**, you will provide strategic and technical leadership to advance gender equality, disability inclusion, and social inclusion across the East Asia region. You will develop and deliver a regional GEDSI roadmap, strengthen organizational practices and staff and partner capabilities, embed GEDSI across strategy, programme and proposal design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning, and position World Vision with donors, governments, UN agencies, civil society, and representative organizations.

**Core Areas of Focus**

You will develop and execute an East Asia regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organizational policies and child well-being priorities. You will lead GEDSI mainstreaming and quality assurance across regional and national office programming, grants, and organizational systems. You will strengthen the capabilities of GEDSI focal points, technical teams, leaders, partners, and representative organizations. You will generate evidence, learning, and innovation and strengthen World Vision’s external positioning on GEDSI across development, humanitarian, and fragile contexts. You will also manage and coordinate GEDSI-related consultancies, technical assistance engagements, and partnerships, including developing scopes of work, providing procurement inputs, ensuring quality assurance, overseeing delivery, and disseminating outputs aligned with global and regional priorities and standards.

**Lead regional GEDSI strategy, policy implementation and organizational change.**

You will develop and monitor a regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organizational priorities and policies. You will engage regional and national leadership, People & Culture, operations, programmes, grants, advocacy, and communications teams to embed GEDSI in programming, organizational practices, advocacy, external engagement, and communications in accordance with World Vision’s GEDSI Policy. You will guide organizational GEDSI self-assessments and action plans, promote inclusive language, accessible workplaces, non-discrimination, and reasonable accommodation, and ensure GEDSI is reflected in organizational priorities, programme strategies and design, key messages, and resource allocation.

**Lead GEDSI mainstreaming in programs, implementation and proposals across funding streams.**

You will provide technical leadership for GEDSI-responsive and transformative programme and proposal design across sectors and contexts. You will ensure designs are informed by GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, barriers, disparities, harmful norms, root causes, and intersectional risks. You will advise teams on GEDSI objectives, theories of change, indicators, budgets, risk mitigation, Do No Harm, safeguarding, and donor requirements. You will contextualize and promote GEDSI tools, approaches, minimum standards, domains of change, the continuum, and markers. You will strengthen the identification and use of disaggregated data, including the appropriate use of Washington Group Questions or other approved tools, to inform programme and project design. You will coach teams to monitor emerging barriers and adapt implementation to improve equitable access, participation, decision-making, systems, and well-being. You will promote rights-based and social-model approaches that address attitudinal, environmental, communication, and institutional barriers. You will also develop, manage, and monitor the Disability Consultant’s workplan and project deliverables, communicate progress, and ensure alignment with EAS GEDSI priorities and agreed objectives.

**Build GEDSI capability, networks and communities of practice.**

You will assess competency and capacity gaps and develop regional capacity-strengthening plans for staff, focal points, partners, and leaders. You will deliver and coordinate contextualized training, coaching, mentoring, and peer learning on gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, and related frameworks. You will equip GEDSI focal points and technical teams with tools, models, resources, and quality-assurance support. You will also strengthen regional collaboration networks and communities of practice, including linkages with gender equality and disability inclusion leadership networks.

**Lead evidence, learning, innovation and knowledge management.**

You will develop and implement a regional GEDSI learning agenda linked to child well-being outcomes. You will initiate and oversee research, pilots, and testing of new or adapted GEDSI approaches and programming models. You will support the analysis and use of data, evaluations, learning reviews, impact stories, case studies, and promising practices. You will facilitate knowledge sharing across national offices, the wider World Vision Partnership, and external audiences.

**Build strategic partnerships, external positioning and thought leadership.**

You will represent and position World Vision with governments, donors, UN agencies, clusters, working groups, NGOs, faith actors, academia, and regional networks. You will build or strengthen the capacity to establish strategic and equitable partnerships with women-led organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities, and minority groups as part of social inclusion, including children, to ensure their meaningful participation in assessment, design, implementation, monitoring, learning, and advocacy. You will identify opportunities for shared learning, advocacy, policy influence, resource mobilization, and thought leadership. You will also support communications and external engagement colleagues in using inclusive, rights-based, and evidence-informed GEDSI language and narratives.

**Requirements include:**

- A bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience may be considered.
- Master’s degree or equivalent in gender studies, disability studies, social or political sciences, social work, international development, economics, public policy, programme management or a related field highly preferred
- Relevant professional development in gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, safeguarding, programme design, MEAL or humanitarian programming.
- Minimum 5 years of demonstrated experience providing strategic and technical leadership on gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion in international development and/or humanitarian programming.
- Experience supporting GEDSI-responsive and transformative designs, mainstreaming strategies and activities across multiple sectors and funding streams.
- Experience leading GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, and integrating findings into design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning.
- Strong facilitation, coaching, relationship-building, partnership, influencing, writing and presentation skills.
- Experience working in or across the East Asia region and adapting global approaches to diverse national and local contexts.
- Substantial experience in disability-inclusive programming, accessibility, disability-disaggregated data, partnership with organisations of persons with disabilities, and rights-based approaches.
- Experience in organisational change, policy implementation, advocacy, research, knowledge management, external engagement and donor positioning.
- Experience leading or supporting organisational GEDSI self-assessments, audits or action plans and building the capability of staff and partners.
- Experience applying Do No Harm, safeguarding and ethical approaches to gender-based violence and other GEDSI-related risks.

**Required Language(s):**

- English, both written and verbal

**Required travel and/or work environment accommodations:**

- The position requires approximately 20% travel, subject to field office needs.
- The successful candidate will be based in their home country and will work remotely, with travel to field locations, regional offices, and partner meetings as required.

jobs.title: Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)
jobs.body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, proudly supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are renowned for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME) Division** is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the 165 plus staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)** will support the Coastal Fisheries Science Team with providing advice to governments, stakeholders and the private sector in planning and implementing coastal fisheries science activities, focusing on coastal finfish and/or invertebrate resources and their supporting habitats.

**The key responsibilities of the role include the following:**

**Assist the CFAP Science team in providing support and training to PICT members to enhance science capacity and capability in coastal living resources data collection, entry, quality control, analysis, interpretation and reporting in support of sustainable management.**

- Assists in the development of coastal fisheries survey (independent and dependent) training materials for countries through needs-based stakeholder consultations, taking into account gender, culture and human rights in the country or territory.
- Assists in the training of local staff in-country and/or online in all areas of data collection, data management, analysis and reporting for coastal fisheries and associated habitats.
- Ensure there are no gender or social inclusion barriers to training activities.

**Contribute to the design and implementation of assessments of coastal living resources, the development and application of innovative tools and approaches for data collection, data management and reporting to inform coastal fisheries management.**

- Participates in the design of surveys based on standardised methodologies and lessons learned.
- Assists in the promotion of the standardisation of data collection and assists with the expansion of standardised data collection and/or monitoring systems for coastal fisheries (finfish, invertebrates, habitat and catch and effort) and programmes at the national level
- Assists in the development and implementation of data systems, tools and approaches that will improve data collection and monitoring of coastal fisheries at the national and regional levels.
- Assists in the collection of biological samples to help inform coastal fisheries assessments.
- Support PICTs to analyse available scientific data on coastal finfish and invertebrate fisheries and associated habitats to provide updates on the status of coastal fishery resources.

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration with partners in coastal fisheries and aquaculture science in support of evidence-based management**

- Liaises, encourages collaboration and works with national, regional and international organisations, research institutes and NGOs on coastal finfish and invertebrate fishery issues.
- Assists in collaboration with other sections/programmes/Divisions within SPC on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.

**Contribute to Section administration and communication**

- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures including training data for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, Programme reports to RTMCFA and HoF.
- Contributes to peer-reviewed scientific publications that highlight results and/or developments of international interest.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Pacific Islands**

- Only applicants from Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply.
- Applicants must be employed in a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment department or a recognised NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Qualifications**

- A recognised degree in a discipline relevant to coastal fisheries science (finfish and/or invertebrates), or related field or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least two years’ direct relevant experience in PICT coastal fisheries, particularly applied field research for coastal finfish and/or invertebrates
- Demonstrated experience in undertaking surveys for coastal finfish and/or invertebrates using a range of methodologies
- Understanding of current Pacific Island regional coastal fisheries management and science issues, and experience of working with gender issues relating to fisheries
- Strong PC based computer skills (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) with knowledge of software programmes for data entry and analysis

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written) in English

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in a team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and communicate with people from various ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries, sometimes under difficult physical conditions.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Requirements:** Only applicants who are nationals and residents of Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply. Applicants must be employed in or contracted by a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment agency, or a recognized NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Letter of endorsement –** A signed letter from the employer, stating they agree to release the applicant for the attachment and that the position will be held for the applicant to return to at the end of the attachment with SPC must be provided before an appointment can be finalized.

**Contract duration –** This appointment will last for a duration of 364 days and will not be renewable.

**Remuneration –** The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)** is a Band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a salary of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,038 per month, which currently converts to approximately XPF 438,381 (USD 4,071; EUR 3,674). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea –** SPC provides housing support in Noumea and an establishment grant, return airfare, and will reimburse excess accompanied luggage of up to two additional bags. Employees are entitled to: 25 days annual leave and 30 days sick leave per annum; medical and life insurance; and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

We encourage all eligible candidates to apply but please note that as this is a special short-term contract, the full list of benefits included in other international contract types are not available. Appointees may bring their families, but all extra costs for travel, insurance, education, housing and other additional expenses will be their own responsibility.

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Finance and Support Services Director
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Finance and Support Services Director**, you will provide overall leadership, oversight, and management support for all aspects of financial management in the Field Office (FO).

You will serve as a strategic partner and member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) of WV Mauritania, focusing on accountability, stewardship, planning and budgeting, accurate financial data and analysis, and financial advice. You will develop a financial strategy that supports the Field Office’s strategic and programme objectives. You will also strengthen finance staff capacity, develop and implement effective internal controls and risk management practices, and ensure the proper utilization and safeguarding of assets in accordance with World Vision-approved policies and procedures.

**(a) Leadership, Capacity Development, and Strategic Partnering**

You will provide strong and positive leadership to the Finance Department, ensuring competent and motivated staff are recruited and retained to deliver efficient services. You will coordinate the professional and personal development of Finance, ICT, Fleet, and Administration staff through orientation, on-the-job coaching, training, and succession planning. You will model Christ-centred servant leadership and support your team’s spiritual development. You will actively participate in Field Office Senior Leadership Team meetings and strategic regional meetings, help the National Director (ND), Operations, and other non-finance staff understand financial statements, and ensure relevant stakeholders understand partnership finance policies and procedures. You will strengthen collaboration and communication between the Field Office and Regional Office, develop internal and external networks, promote shared resources across the region and partnership, and adhere to WVI’s mission, core values, and Covenant of Partnership.

**(b) Stewardship**

You will ensure that appropriate cost-efficiency and effectiveness measures are implemented and followed. You will provide cost analyses, promote benchmarking, and make recommendations to improve resource utilization at all levels. In collaboration with the Supply Chain team, you will contribute to developing appropriate policies and procedures for procuring goods and services.

**(c) Financial Planning and Budgeting**

In collaboration with the Regional Finance Director, you will advise the National Director on strategic resource acquisition and allocation in line with Partnership Resource Allocation Committee (PRAC) guidelines. You will coordinate planning and budgeting processes, provide technical support to ensure compliance with global and regional guidelines, and develop and implement financial strategies in response to changing constraints and circumstances. You will review budget alignment across the Field Office, projects, grants, MyPBAS, and Support Offices, ensuring effective cost recovery practices. In collaboration with the Integrated Programs Director (IPD), you will monitor and manage the WV Mauritania budget, cash flow, and project funding, providing timely and relevant information to budget managers. You will closely monitor budgets and expenditures at Area Development Program (ADP), Cluster, and Field Office levels to ensure funds are used for their intended purposes, including monitoring field expenses. You will also contribute to developing WV Mauritania’s strategic direction and priorities.

**(d) Fiscal Accounting, Compliance, Monitoring, and Reporting**

You will design and manage systems, policies, and procedures that provide appropriate security and control over WV assets, resources, and operations. You will establish effective internal controls and ensure timely, accurate, and complete reporting to the partnership and internal stakeholders. You will comply with partnership policies, procedures, and guidelines outlined in the WVI Financial Manual and related documents, including grant compliance, planning and budgeting, year-end closing, carryforward, accounting, and reporting. You will coordinate the timely and accurate submission of financial reports through the Field Financial Reporting database on SharePoint, review monthly MyPBAS-to-FFR reconciliations, and develop action plans to address outstanding items. You will provide monthly analyses of ADP and grant financial reports, giving timely feedback to ADP and grant managers to support decision-making. You will also ensure that Finance, ICT, Fleet, and Administration staff visit programmes and projects to monitor accountability, follow up on audit findings, and provide necessary support.

**(e) Financial Risk Management and Controls**

You will manage appropriate financial systems and controls to minimize significant finance audit risks at both Field Office and project levels. You will coordinate management responses to financial audits, ensure timely submission to the Audit Department, and oversee the timely implementation of audit recommendations. You will coordinate adequate preparation for Global Centre (GC) and external audits, manage financial risks and integrity, and implement anti-corruption and fraud prevention strategies.

**(f) Support to Supply Chain Processes**

You will coordinate and maintain an effective interface between the Supply Chain and Finance teams. You will review Purchase Requests and Purchase Orders to ensure compliance with Supply Chain Management (SCM) policies, budget availability, and appropriate controls against fraudulent activities. You will also review procurement activities to ensure purchases contribute to ministry objectives and align with donor budget line items.

**(g) Improve ICT Infrastructure and Provide Quality Service**

You will ensure improved connectivity across the office and programmes and facilitate the development and implementation of computer usage policies. You will oversee ICT security and integrity, ensuring office disaster preparedness measures and policies are regularly updated to address new technologies, trends, and threats.

**(h) Administration and Fleet Management**

You will ensure that WV staff and assets remain secure, safe, and well-maintained, while overseeing logistics coordination and providing quality hospitality services to staff and visitors. You will implement fleet management policies covering vehicle tracking, fuel management, and vehicle and motorcycle maintenance. You will also manage asset disposals in compliance with WVI and WV Mauritania policies.

**(i) Talent Management and Capacity Building**

You will contribute to capacity assessment, development, and implementation as part of the overall Talent Management Plan, ensuring an integrated WV Mauritania capacity-building plan informed by finance priorities and strategy. You will identify Finance staff development needs, including grant financial management, and facilitate relevant training opportunities while developing diverse leadership. In collaboration with the People and Culture (P&C) Team Leader, you will co-lead the recruitment of Field Office Finance staff. You will advise and support the induction of new functional directors, grant managers, and project team leaders. You will also coach, advise, and mentor Finance staff to identify their strengths and development gaps and address them effectively.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or Economics or a related field
- Minimum 5 years of experience in a finance position with a medium business/medium NGO/government agency
- Minimum 3 years of experience in a senior finance management position
- Experience with financial planning and forecasting
- Solid knowledge of accounting principles, financial systems, budget/cash flow monitoring, and internal accounting controls.
- Highly flexible and agile in style, with the ability to produce creative and pragmatic solutions to complex problems.
- Good working knowledge of computerized accounting systems, preferably Sun Systems & ProVision.
- Demonstrates systems thinking and is a high champion and Manages Innovation.
- Able to work in a cross-cultural environment with a multi-national staff.
- Ability to travel within the country, regionally, and internationally.
- French is non-negotiable (both written and spoken)
- Proficiency in written and spoken English
- Excellent oral/written and interpersonal skills

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Human Resource Administrative Specialist
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Summary**

Under the direct supervision of the HR Manager, the HR Administrative Specialist supports the HR administration affairs for the IRC New Jersey and New York offices. They will assist in the human resources administrative tasks including recruitment and onboarding, personnel files, time attendance management, and orientation. They serve as a knowledgeable resource for staff and management, coordinate employee lifecycle processes, and support special project and initiatives.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Serve as the offices’ first point of contact on employee lifecycle matters, including but not limited to recruitment, new hire setup and orientation, benefits, payroll, on-boarding, leaves of absence, status changes, and separations.
- Assists with HR administrative activities including new hire and hire change paperwork processing, managing background checks for staff.
- Administer the organization’s applicant tracking system, posting and closing locally managed requisitions, and providing related coordination.
- Support compliance with HR-related IRC policies and procedures and state-specific labor laws.
- Coordinate HQ initiatives related to the IRC Way, Duty of Care, Safeguarding, and related content.
- Liaise with HR Manager to escalate issues and connect staff with appropriate HR-related training and other resources.
- Support special projects and initiatives.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for interns throughout the program, providing guidance, support, and direction
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Undergraduate degree in related field preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- At least 2 years of relevant work experience in office administration; human resources, or related field, preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and oral.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.

IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Job Overview:**   
The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency. jobs.title: Design of ISF stations works
jobs.body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/201**
- **Position Title**: Design of ISF stations works
- **Duty Station:** ISF stations of Nabatieh, Jdeideh and Saida, with occasional meetings at UNDP offices if needed
- **Duration:** 2 Months (without exceeding 11 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 14 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 21 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/13OZio4hY1jbm00VR4cGnblnmaiXX8XiP/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/13OZio4hY1jbm00VR4cGnblnmaiXX8XiP/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

UNDP Lebanon supports the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities (MoIM) and the Internal Security Forces (ISF) in improving the operating conditions of ISF stations and enhancing the delivery of security services to the population, as part of UNDP’s ongoing stabilization support to ISF facilities in the south of Lebanon and the Beirut area, and in line with the ISF Strategy.

As part of this support, UNDP is preparing the design of upgrading/rehabilitation works for three ISF stations: the Emergency Department in Nabatieh, the Judicial Police Station in Jdeideh, and the Judicial Police Station in Saida (hereinafter referred to as the three Lots). The proposed design is informed by lessons learned from previous UNDP-supported ISF station rehabilitation works and by guidelines produced by the ISF Directorate.

Therefore, the project is looking to hire an architect/engineer to design the upgrading/rehabilitation works of the above three ISF stations (three Lots) and to ensure that the proposed design accommodates and responds to the needs of the population and the operational requirements of the ISF.

jobs.title: Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert - CDR
jobs.body:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/200**
- **Position Title**: Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert - CDR
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 14 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 21 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JFJvvMi0X1CMbBMR4IhA-Zv5eASVx6wv/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1JFJvvMi0X1CMbBMR4IhA-Zv5eASVx6wv/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Council for Development and Reconstruction (CDR), operating under the Council of Ministers, plays a central role in Lebanon’s development planning, infrastructure projects, coordination with development partners, and reconstruction efforts. The prolonged crisis has placed pressure on its human resources and operational capacity, highlighting the need to strengthen its institutional arrangements, organizational structure, and business processes to respond effectively to evolving priorities.

In response, a comprehensive Functional and Business Process Review of CDR was undertaken to assess the institution’s existing functions, organizational arrangements, business processes, governance mechanisms, and staffing requirements, and to identify measures to improve its efficiency and effectiveness. The findings and recommendations of the review have been consolidated in an implementation roadmap. The roadmap distinguishes between measures that can be implemented within the existing legal and regulatory framework, referred to as the Interim Arrangements, and reforms that require amendments to Decree No. 10941 of 2003 and Decree No. 10942 of 2003, referred to as the Target Roadmap. The implementation of these reforms is structured in stages, with the present assignment supporting measures identified for implementation under Stage 1.

The successful implementation of CDR’s digital transformation requires the establishment of a clear governance and implementation foundation before major technology investments and platform deployments can proceed. This includes defining ownership and decision-making arrangements, validating the target structure and functions of the Information Technology Department, establishing an enterprise architecture and data governance framework, and ensuring that core business processes are appropriately re-baselined to reflect the future operating model. It also requires a clear understanding of CDR’s existing technology, systems, data, infrastructure, and security environment, together with a structured approach to prioritizing investments and addressing critical gaps.

Therefore, a set of foundational measures have been identified to be undertaken during Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Roadmap. These measures are intended to establish the rules, governance arrangements, technical and organizational architecture, inventories, and implementation baseline required to guide subsequent phases of digital transformation. They include the establishment of programme governance arrangements, validation of the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, definition of data governance principles, risk-based re-baselining of core processes, and preparation of the inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budgets required to move from planning to implementation. Immediate actions have also been identified to strengthen CDR’s existing backup, recovery, and cybersecurity arrangements using available tools and resources, alongside urgent remediation measures that need to be initiated.

Accordingly, UNDP seeks to recruit a Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert to support CDR in delivering Stage 1 of the Digital Transformation Program. The Expert will establish the programme governance arrangements and implementation baseline, validate the target IT Department structure and enterprise architecture, define the foundations for data governance, and validate the priority use cases of the document management system and the shared workflow system. The Expert will also prepare the key inventories, procurement strategy, terms of reference, and multi-year budget requirements needed to enable subsequent digital investments and implementation.

Through this assignment, the Expert will support CDR in moving from the recommendations of the Functional and Business Process Review to a structured and implementable digital transformation programme, ensuring that the institutional, governance, process, technical, procurement, and financial foundations are in place before major digital platforms and systems proceed to implementation.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the initiative’s team leads from UNDP and CDR, the Senior Information Management and Digital Transformation Expert will be responsible for the following:

**Workstream 1. Program Governance and Mobilization**

- Within two weeks of mobilization, agree with CDR the process scope, the technical changes, the available working days and the resources required for this assignment, and prepare a work plan that schedules the remaining work with its owners, dependencies and costs.
- Support CDR in establishing the governance bodies of the Digital Transformation Program, comprising the ICT Steering Committee, the Data Governance Committee and the Technical Review Committee, and prepare their terms of reference, their decision rights and the responsibility matrix that assigns each decision to a named body. The terms of reference of the ICT Steering Committee cover its decisions, escalation arrangements, meeting frequency and progress reporting. Support CDR management in formally designating the interim ICT Transformation Lead and the business and technical owners of critical systems and services.
- Support the establishment of the Digital Transformation Program Office function, comprising the integrated roadmap, the dependency register, the risk register, the benefits plan, the procurement plan, the architecture decision log and the reporting calendar, and hand the instruments over in working order.
- Assist in validation of the target structure and staffing of the Information Technology Department against the functions the program requires, the existing staff and their workload, and coordinate the resulting job descriptions with the human resources workstream so that a single set of descriptions is produced. Prepare the responsibility matrix of the Department, identify staffing and skills gaps, and recommend interim assignments, training and specialist support. Formal appointments and organizational decisions remain with CDR.

**Workstream 2. Architecture and Data Governance**

- Develop and validate the enterprise architecture and the digital building blocks against the baseline covering the business, data, application, integration, technology and governance domains. Produce an updated high-level application and integration diagram, confirm the roles of JDE, the document management system, ArcGIS and the planned systems, and record the compatibility issues, dependencies and decisions required before procurement.
- Support in establishing the standing coordination arrangement with the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform and, where relevant, with the national digital acceleration program, with a designated focal point, a defined agenda covering hosting, interoperability, digital identity and electronic signature, and a reporting line to the ICT Steering Committee.
- Prepare the initial data governance principles, covering named business data owners, authoritative systems, shared project and contract identifiers, minimum metadata, access and classification, data quality, retention and controlled sharing. Submit the principles, with the validated enterprise architecture, to the ICT Steering Committee for endorsement.

**Workstream 3. Process Re-baselining and Technical Readiness**

- With the business service owners, review the process maps to identify the common requirements for the document management system and the shared workflow system. Validate representative use cases, bottlenecks, document types and control needs to the level required for the terms of reference. Validate the approval thresholds and segregation of duties for these use cases, and record unresolved decisions and required authorizations. Produce a prioritized catalogue of business flows for later implementation. Full process redesign and configuration follow in later stages.
- Prepare the system, application, asset and workload inventories, including hardware, software licenses, contracts and support arrangements, and record the baseline performance indicators, or the method for collecting them where data are not yet available, against which the benefits of the program are later measured. The inventories record quantities, condition, capacity, hosted workloads, owners, dependencies, support status and renewal dates. They also assess workstation upgrade readiness and the priority server, storage, backup, scanner and power-protection needs. The workload inventory of the hosts designated for retirement, prepared by the firm contracted for the server refresh, is incorporated rather than repeated.

**Workstream 4. Procurement and Funding Readiness**

- Prepare the phased procurement strategy. The strategy specifies the document management system and the shared workflow system during this assignment, establishes and accepts the platform in a later stage, and configures the priority business flows in successive releases. Identify the packages, dependencies, lead times and owners, and define separate deliverables and acceptance gates for the platform foundation and for each business-flow release.
- Prepare the technical specifications, quantities and supplier pricing schedule for the justified priority hardware, infrastructure and services. Compare reuse, support renewal, repair and replacement, and include capacity, compatibility, migration, warranty, support response, acceptance testing and staff handover requirements.
- Reconcile the installed software and its use with entitlements and contracts. Verify the current vendor lifecycle and upgrade terms for operating systems, productivity tools, server and database licenses, electronic mail, endpoint protection, backup, firewalls and core applications. Identify renewals, unused entitlements and license gaps, and prepare a costed renewal and upgrade schedule.
- Prepare the terms of reference for the document management system and the shared workflow system, assessing the modernization of the existing SharePoint environment against its replacement. Define document capture, metadata, search, versioning, retention, permissions and audit trails; reusable forms, routing, approvals, notifications and monitoring; configurable roles, approval rules and audit controls; integration with JDE and identity services; and migration, hosting, licensing, training and support. Specify the platform acceptance tests and the later releases of priority business flows. The requirements preserve CDR data ownership, editable documentation, interoperability, portability and exit rights, with brand-neutral specifications where feasible.
- Prepare the indicative multi-year budget for the three-year horizon of the roadmap, separating implementation costs from recurring costs, and covering operations, maintenance, staffing, training, security reviews, licensing, hosting, support, hardware refresh, integration maintenance and contingency, and confirm the institutional and budget owner of each system before procurement.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 3 months (without exceeding 16 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant shall perform tasks with day-to-day management and the direct supervision of the designated project manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will be also responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months without exceeding 16 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by the 31st of January 2027.

Any continuation of the services beyond this period, including the second phase of support described in the Background, is subject to a separate contract or a formal amendment of this contract. Continuation depends on satisfactory performance under this contract, the continued requirement for the services and the availability of funds.

The time needed to review/complete/approve deliverables and output is (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The consultant will work from home with regular visits to CDR - Beirut, Republic of Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** Master’s degree or equivalent in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Digital Transformation, Information Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Public Administration or a related field. Specialized focus on enterprise architecture, information systems, digital transformation, data governance, cybersecurity, or ICT management is highly preferred.
- **Experience:** At least 10 years of combined professional experience in: (i) designing, managing, or implementing digital transformation and information management programmes, including ICT governance, enterprise architecture, systems integration, data governance, and business-process digitization; and (ii) providing strategic and technical advice on ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity, information systems, technology procurement, and digital transformation planning, preferably in public-sector or institutional environments.
- **Language:** Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis.
