Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**What we are looking for**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been supporting people affected by displacement in Lebanon for 20 years. As we embark on an important period of strategic and operational change, we are seeking an **experienced** **Finance Manager** to provide **strategic financial leadership**, **strengthen financial systems**, and ensure the effective and accountable use of resources to deliver humanitarian assistance.

We are looking for **a strategic, analytical, and solutions-oriented finance leader** who can navigate change, translate financial data into actionable insights, and balance strong financial controls with the operational flexibility required in a dynamic humanitarian context.

This is an exciting opportunity to shape NRC Lebanon’s financial direction, support organisational transformation, and strengthen collaboration with local partners and actors.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Finance Manager is responsible for effective financial management, budgeting, reporting, compliance and internal controls across NRC Lebanon.

This role provides strategic financial leadership by delivering accurate, reliable, and timely financial information, enabling senior management to make informed decisions and ensure the efficient use of organisational resources.

The position holder will ensure that NRC Lebanon is well positioned to respond to current and future needs and shall demonstrate strong engagement and leadership in all major Finance actions, while ensuring capacity building for Finance team members and budget holders across the entire country.

Key responsibilities:

- **Provide strategic financial leadership** across NRC Lebanon, ensuring robust financial systems, policies, internal controls, and compliance with NRC, donor, and local regulatory requirements.
- **Lead budgeting, financial reporting, and analysis**, delivering timely, accurate insights to inform senior management decisions and support effective resource allocation.
- **Oversee accounting, cash flow, and liquidity management**, ensuring operational continuity, accurate financial records, and effective audit preparation and follow-up.
- **Manage financial risks and compliance**, strengthening accountability, implementing anti-corruption measures, and addressing audit findings and financial control gaps.
- **Advise and support budget holders and programme teams** throughout the project cycle, from proposal development and budgeting to expenditure monitoring and reporting.
- **Strengthen financial capacity and team performance** through effective leadership, staff development, and technical support to Finance colleagues and budget holders nationwide.
- **Advance NRC’s localisation agenda** by strengthening financial systems, tools, and capacity to support local partners and actors in delivering compliant, effective, and sustainable humanitarian responses.

**What you will bring**

- A bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, or a relevant field.
- **At least four years of finance experience**, including **three years in a managerial or equivalent role** **within a humanitarian or recovery context.**
- **Experience working with local partners** and **institutional humanitarian donors.**
- **Strong financial analysis**, **budgeting, reporting**, and risk management skills, with proficiency in MS Excel and accounting systems.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Experience **developing financial systems during organisational change** is highly desirable; **emergency finance leadership experience** and previous work in the Middle East are an advantage.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDykXJd7GUEQZVDhD3vlo8xAUtc9vURiJeSfCAscQg3el0?e=oaBMOR) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 10-20%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

**Join NRC Lebanon and help shape the financial leadership, systems, and partnerships that will enable us to respond effectively to humanitarian needs and deliver greater impact.**

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Lebanon](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/lebanon)

jobs.title: Nigeria Regional Warehouse Coordinator (Fixed-term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

We started working in Nigeria in 2018, serving just 150 farmers. That figure grew year on year, and we now serve more than 300,000 farmers across three regions in Niger State: Minna, Mokwa, and Iseyin.  
  
Between our tree program and a diverse staple crop program, xx staff are supporting farmers in Nigeria to grow their way to prosperity.

## About the Role

Seeking a supply chain professional with 2-5 years' experience to coordinate warehouse and inventory operations, team supervision, and space optimization to support efficient and scalable program delivery.

## Responsibilities

Regional Warehouse Operations & Performance

- Coordinate day-to-day warehouse operations across assigned regional facilities.
- Ensure warehouses consistently follow approved OAF warehouse processes, and SOPs.
- Monitor warehouse performance against agreed KPIs for inventory accuracy, shrinkage, service, productivity, safety and compliance.
- Identify and share best practices across warehouses to improve consistency and performance.
- Plan ahead for peak periods and ensure warehouses are ready to support field and farmer needs.
- Regularly Go to Gemba to understand operational challenges and drive practical improvements.

Inventory Management & Control

- Lead regular physical stock counts, reconciliations and inventory reviews across assigned warehouses.
- Ensure physical stock is accurately reflected in the relevant inventory management system.
- Investigate inventory variances, identify root causes and ensure corrective actions are completed.
- Monitor inventory ageing, stock movements, transfers and potential losses.
- Strengthen controls that prevent shrinkage, stock errors and unauthorized stock movements.
- Ensure inventory records and supporting documentation are complete and audit-ready.

Warehouse Systems, Documentation & Compliance

- Ensure receiving, dispatch and inter-warehouse movements are properly documented and recorded on time.
- Maintain accurate warehouse records, including stock count sheets, waybills, delivery notes, GRNs, transfer documents and quality records.
- Conduct regular compliance checks and follow up on identified gaps.
- Support internal and external audits by ensuring warehouse records and physical stock are readily available.
- Escalate suspected theft, fraud, significant loss or other serious compliance concerns through the appropriate channels.

Warehouse Layout, Quality & Process Improvement

- Ensure effective warehouse layout, product segregation, palletization, labelling and storage practices.
- Work closely with QA/QC to maintain appropriate product handling, storage and release standards.
- Identify bottlenecks and opportunities to improve warehouse flow, space utilization and productivity.
- Lead practical improvement initiatives using data, root-cause analysis and feedback from warehouse teams.
- Standardize successful improvements across other regional warehouses where appropriate.

Health, Safety & Environment

- Promote a strong safety culture across all assigned warehouses.
- Conduct regular warehouse Gemba walks and safety checks to identify and address hazards.
- Ensure appropriate use of PPE and compliance with warehouse safety standards.
- Maintain clean, organized and safe working environments for employees, casual workers and visitors.
- Ensure incidents, near misses and safety concerns are reported, investigated and followed through to closure.
- Encourage team members to speak up and take ownership of safety.

Distribution & Supply Chain Coordination

- Coordinate with Logistics, Procurement, QA/QC and field teams to ensure smooth warehouse operations and timely movement of inputs.
- Support efficient loading, dispatch and inter-warehouse transfer activities.
- Ensure warehouse capacity and dispatch plans are aligned with operational demand.
- Work with Logistics teams to resolve delivery and dispatch challenges quickly.
- Support efficient use of warehouse and transport resources to reduce avoidable operational costs.

Team Leadership & Development

- Provide day-to-day leadership and support to Warehouse Supervisors and warehouse teams.
- Set clear expectations, priorities and performance standards.
- Coach team members to improve warehouse practices, inventory controls, safety and customer service.
- Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, feedback and continuous improvement.
- Support performance reviews, recruitment, onboarding and development of warehouse staff.
- Lead by example and create an environment where people can take ownership and grow.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's degree or HND in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Agribusiness, Science & Engineering or a related discipline. (A Masters degree with relevant professional certificate in supply chain would be an added advantage)
- At least 2 - 5 years of relevant experience in warehouse, inventory, logistics operations including supervising, managing or coordinating
- Strong leadership skills to effectively lead and motivate a team.
- Organizational skills to efficiently plan, prioritize and delegate tasks.
- Warehouse operations; inventory management and reconciliation; warehouse systems/WMS; stock control; warehouse layout and capacity planning; HSE; basic data analysis; process improvement; documentation and compliance.
- Makes day-to-day operational decisions within approved policies, SOPs and budgets; escalates significant operational, financial, safety and compliance risks appropriately.
- Quick problem-solving abilities to anticipate, identify and resolve issues with deliveries and transport operations.
- High attention to detail to accurately plan, schedule and track all deliveries.
- Excellent communication skills to effectively interact with clients, colleagues and stakeholders.
- Computer literacy to efficiently use software and systems for planning, managing and tracking deliverables.
- Efficient time management capabilities to ensure timely execution of deliveries and transport operations.
- Flexibility to adapt to evolving customer needs and requirements.
- Commercial awareness to identify cost-saving opportunities and make profitable decisions.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bida, Niger State, Nigeria

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Nigeria.

## Application Deadline

08 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Protection Analyst—Research and Advocacy
jobs.body:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Head of Protection, the Junior Protection Analyst – Research, and Advocacy supports the Mobility Pathways and Inclusion (MPI) Unit in donor reporting, analysis and advocacy of programmatic interventions in Iraq.

The scope of this consultancy relates to MPI’s protection monitoring and research activities, as well as reporting. IOM contributes to evidence-based protection advocacy through protection monitoring. Protection monitoring is carried out to identify the protection risks and needs of affected populations to support evidence-based programming and advocacy. Research is conducted using a mixed-method approach and feeds into advocacy with key stakeholders, including government, development actors, and donor communities. The consultant contributes to this work by supporting the production of protection monitoring reports and any other protection monitoring products and activities.

The Junior Protection Analyst also supports MPI with its donor reporting portfolio. The consultant will support the Protection Analyst for MPI donor reports to be submitted to the Programme Support Unit (PSU) for final clearance.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

  
Mobility Pathways and Inclusion (MPI) Unit

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

- Provide support to the Al-Amal Protection Monitoring work, including proofreading, copy-editing, fact-checking, and assisting with qualitative and quantitative analysis; coordinate with team members to keep products accurate and up to date.
- Contribute to thematic work on environmental migration, gender-based violence, disability and inclusion, migration, and protracted displacement by conducting desk research, organising literature, and assisting with data analysis for reports and briefs.
- Help maintain knowledge-sharing products, such as thematic notes, policy briefs, and dashboards, by compiling data, verifying consistency, and providing analysis.
- Support the MPI donor reporting portfolio. Analyze data from field reports and monitoring tools to support comprehensive donor reports, ensuring alignment with reporting requirements; support proposals by incorporating key findings from protection monitoring activities and advocacy efforts.
- Work closely with the Programme, IMS, and M&E teams to ensure reporting inputs remain consistent, clarify indicator definitions, and support routine data management tasks.
- Assist with additional tasks that help the MPI Unit deliver its regular monitoring, reporting, and research activities.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- 6 protection monitoring reports and 5 donor reports

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education, Experience and/or skills required**

- Master’s Degree in Forced Migration, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related discipline
- At least 2-year experience in research, data analysis, protection monitoring, and advocacy within the humanitarian or development sector; experience designing data collection tools and methodologies.
- Proven track record of producing high-quality analytical and written outputs, including concise reports and publications.
- Familiarity with protection challenges faced by displaced populations in Iraq or similar crisis-affected contexts.
- Experience in donor reporting, including data analysis and report writing.
- Experience working effectively and independently in remote or virtual environments.

Experience communicating effectively with a variety of stakeholders, including diverse audiences

**Languages**

For this consultancy,Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required (Yes/NO)**

Yes

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

jobs.title: Senior Marine Ecology Officer - Southeast Asia
jobs.body:
**Location**: Bali, Indonesia

**Closing date for applications:** November 1st, 2026

**Start date:** As soon as possible

**Contract duration:** Permanent

**Remuneration:** IDR 255,498,264 to IDR 305,344,256 per Annum

**We rebuild tropical fisheries with coastal communities**

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

**Summary job description**

We are currently recruiting a Senior Marine Ecology Officer - Southeast Asia, technical support to Blue Ventures’ marine ecology operations across Southeast Asia. Reporting directly to the Data Science Manager - Asia and based full-time in Denpasar, Indonesia (with regular regional travel), the role will support community-based ecology monitoring, management, and governance, working closely with teams in Indonesia, Timor-Leste, and the Philippines as well as regional partners across Southeast Asia. Working closely with the global Spatial Ecology team, you will execute the technical development, workflow standardization, field-level rollout of mobile data technologies, and tailored learning resources that bridge science and community-led conservation.

The Senior Officer will be in charge of capacity-building initiatives—including hands-on workshops, technical mentoring, and peer exchanges—to translate ecological theory into practical, community-level action. We are seeking a dynamic technical person with proven expertise in mangrove, seagrass and coral reef, participatory monitoring, and ecosystem-based fisheries governance in Southeast Asia. You will bring a strong track record in community-led natural resource management, multi-stakeholder partnership building, and optional familiarity with coastal carbon markets. If you thrive in complex environments, work independently across disciplines, and share our commitment to human rights-based marine conservation, this role offers an exciting opportunity to drive regional impact.

jobs.title: Field Researcher / Field Monitor (Researchers Pool)
jobs.body:
**Organization:** Jouri Research and Consulting (JRC)  
**Location:** Whole of Syria  
**Engagement Type:** Roster-based, assignment by assignment (full-time or part-time depending on project needs)  
**Reporting to:** Jouri Field Coordinator

**About JOURI**  
Jouri is an international development consultancy with presence and offices in Geneva, Turkey, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon and Syria with a team based across Europe and the Middle East. We support humanitarian and development actors to increase the relevance, effectiveness, efficiency, sustainability and impact of their work. Our key services include Research and Analysis, Third-Party Monitoring and Evaluation in Conflict Contexts, and Capacity Building. Jouri is pleased to announce an opportunity for Field Researcher / Field Monitor.

**About the Role**  
Jouri is updating its pool of field researchers in Syria. Selected candidates will join our roster and be engaged on upcoming assignments, including third-party monitoring (TPM), needs assessments, baseline and endline studies, post-distribution monitoring, and programme evaluations. Assignments cover sectors such as food security and livelihoods, health, education, WASH, shelter, and protection.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Conduct field data collection using quantitative tools (household surveys, PDM, KAP surveys) on digital platforms such as KoboToolbox or ODK.
- Conduct qualitative data collection, including key informant interviews (KIIs) and focus group discussions (FGDs), and produce clear, accurate notes or transcripts in Arabic.
- Carry out site visits and direct observation at distribution points, schools, health facilities, markets, and project sites to verify implementation against agreed criteria.
- Collect market price data on essential food and non-food items when required.
- Obtain informed consent and apply research ethics, do-no-harm principles, and data protection standards in every interaction.
- Identify, document, and promptly report protection concerns, safeguarding issues, or serious gaps observed in the field, following JRC's referral and reporting procedures.
- Take photographs as evidence where appropriate and permitted, respecting the privacy and dignity of participants.
- Ensure data quality by checking submissions for completeness and accuracy and responding to supervisor feedback.
- Participate in training, piloting of tools, and team debriefs, and share field observations that inform analysis.
- Maintain professional and respectful relationships with communities, partners, and local authorities in line with humanitarian principles.

**Qualifications and Experience**

- **Education:** Bachelor's degree in social sciences, sociology, economics, development studies, public health, or a related field. An intermediate institute diploma combined with strong relevant experience may be considered.
- **Experience:**
    - At least three years of relevant professional experience.
    - Proven experience in field data collection, monitoring, or research (quantitative and/or qualitative).
    - Experience with UN agencies, international NGOs, or research firms in a humanitarian or development context is highly desirable.
    - Experience facilitating KIIs and FGDs, or using KoboToolbox/ODK, is a strong asset.
- **Skills and Competencies:**
    - Fluency in Arabic (spoken and written) is required; working knowledge of English is an asset.
    - Strong communication and interviewing skills, including with vulnerable groups.
    - Attention to detail and commitment to accurate, unbiased data.
    - Ability to work under pressure, manage multiple tasks, and meet deadlines.
    - Cultural sensitivity and strong commitment to ethical conduct, confidentiality, and safeguarding.
    - Willingness and ability to travel frequently to remote and sometimes challenging locations.

**Additional Requirements**

- Good knowledge of, and access to, the local community in the governorate(s) where the applicant is based.
- Comfortable using a smartphone or tablet for data collection.
- Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Compensation:** Determined per assignment based on scope, duration, and location.

jobs.title: Programme Associate VAM
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE APPOINTMENT:**

WFP Jordan works with national institutions and partners to strengthen food security, social protection and evidence-based programming. The Vulnerability, Assessment and Mapping (VAM) function generates and manages evidence to support programme design, targeting, market analysis, monitoring and operational decision-making.

The post is based in the WFP Jordan Country Office in Amman. Under the guidance and supervision of the Senior VAM Officer, the VAM Associate will contribute to market analysis, assessment design and implementation, household profiling, targeting analysis, evidence generation and capacity strengthening activities.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Market Analysis and Price Monitoring**

- Lead the planning, coordination, collection, management and analysis of market price data in collaboration with relevant units, including Supply Chain and Field Offices, and prepare monthly, quarterly and ad hoc market monitoring reports and bulletins to support programme and country office decision-making.
- Serve as a focal point for the resolution of technical and operational queries and problems related to market analysis, price monitoring and economic trends.
- Lead assessments and analysis related to the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), affordability and household purchasing power.
- Monitor market trends, inflation and economic risks and support Country Office risk management, including the formulation, updating and monitoring of key economic and market-price risk indicators in the CO risk register.
- Support the generation of evidence on market conditions and economic factors affecting food security and programme implementation.

**Assessment, Targeting and Evidence Generation**

- support the design and implementation of quantitative and qualitative assessments, including periodical vulnerability assessments, surveys and regular monitoring activities, under the guidance of the VAM Officer, covering methodology, sampling, tool development, oversight of enumerator training and field data collection, and quality assurance.
- Conduct data cleaning, validation and analysis using SPSS, R, Excel or similar tools.
- Conduct household profiling, vulnerability and targeting analyses, including regression analysis where appropriate, to identify factors influencing food security and programme outcomes, assess targeting effectiveness, and inform beneficiary selection, prioritization and programme decision-making.
- Analyze indicators related to food security, nutrition, markets, vulnerability, resilience and livelihoods, applying gender, accountability to affected populations (AAP) and protection perspectives, and prepare clear reports and evidence products.
- Support the dissemination of evidence products in accordance with WFP protocols, compile lessons learned and best practices, and contribute to the preparation of external VAM products.
- Contribute analytical evidence to discussions and implementation of WFP assistance, including general food assistance, school feeding and resilience-based programmes.
- Support coordination with government institutions, UN agencies, NGOs and other partners to support assessments, analysis and evidence generation.
- Maintain clear documentation of business processes, methodologies, datasets and analytical processes, and contribute to effective information management and sharing.

**Capacity Building and Partnerships**

- in Coordination with the VAM officer, technically support analytical initiatives between WFP, government institutions and other partners in line with WFP corporate policies and data protection and privacy requirements.
- Support the establishment and implementation of technical agreements and joint analytical activities with national counterparts, including the Department of Statistics of Jordan, as relevant.
- Support capacity strengthening activities for WFP staff, partners and government counterparts in market monitoring, targeting, household analysis and food security analysis.
- Provide technical support to government institutions and other partners to strengthen national capacities in food security information, market analysis, early warning systems and evidence-based decision-making, including but not limited to the Food Security Information Management System, administered by the Higher Food Security Council.
- Perform other related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:**

**Education:** Completion of secondary school education. A post-secondary certificate in a related functional area is desirable.

**Experience:** At least six years of progressively responsible experience, including relevant experience in assessments, data analysis, market monitoring, targeting or food security analysis.

**Knowledge & Skills:**

- Experience in conducting surveys, assessments and quantitative data analysis.
- Good understanding of household vulnerability analysis and targeting approaches.
- Proficiency in SPSS, R, STATA, Excel or other data analysis software.
- Ability to conduct and interpret statistical analysis, including regression analysis, and translate findings into clear recommendations.
- Strong report writing, data presentation and communication skills.
- Experience working with government counterparts and humanitarian or development partners.

**Other Post Requirements**

- Previous experience in humanitarian or development contexts.
- Previous experience in conducting assessments, surveys or research.
- Experience in household-level data analysis, targeting, market monitoring or food security analysis.
- Good report writing and communication skills.

**Languages:** Fluency in oral and written Arabic and English

jobs.title: Grant Management and Learning Coordinator - International
jobs.body:
**Job profile**

The Grant Management and Learning Coordinator fulfils a key function within the Department of Programme Development, Impact and Learning, sitting in the Grant Management Unit. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Director of Programme Performance and Monitoring, the Grant Management and Learning Coordinator is responsible for ensuring compliance with donor grants, coordinating consolidation of coherent and accurate project data, supporting timely development and submission of high-quality donor reports, building and maintaining relationships with partners and donors, and proactively identifying the need for contract changes. In addition, the role coordinates the production of high-quality research on the organisation's Climate Adaptation work and other programming, translating findings into articles, reports and other documents for donors, the NGO community, and other external audiences.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The position covers the following key areas of responsibility:

- For assigned grants, serve as the focal point for Afghanaid’s policies and donor contract terms and conditions, maintaining comprehensive knowledge and ensuring that all grant documentation (including proposals, reports, and budgets) is properly stored and available to relevant staff, and that key reporting requirements and other compliance obligations are clearly communicated to finance and project teams.
- Upon the signing of a new grant agreement, facilitate a smooth handover of the project to the Grant Management Unit, following up on outstanding project partnership agreement (PPA) tasks, and confirming reporting responsibilities and processes with relevant parties at the project kickoff meeting.
- Maintain internal and external tracking of reporting timelines, including working with relevant departments to coordinate appropriate data collection, analysis and financial and narrative reporting by Afghanaid and its partners.
- Review and refine high-quality financial and narrative project reports, survey and evaluation reports, and other associated donor communications, ensuring timely submission and compliance with Afghanaid, donor and partner requirements.
- Independently troubleshoot issues raised by project and operational teams, serving as liaison between the project team and donor to address and resolve challenges.
- Facilitate and contribute to regular project review processes, and pre-emptively raise concerns where contractual obligations, quality standards or deadlines are at risk of not being met, especially identifying risks of donor ‘clawback’ and reputational damage.
- In coordination with project teams, partners and the finance team, lead on revisions to project budgets, logical frameworks and other project documents for assigned grants, ensuring timely submission to the donor and follow up on approvals, and communicating updates to relevant departments.
- Support the Consortium Manager in strengthening partner performance and report quality by reviewing and providing input on partner organisations’ annual and semi-annual narrative reports.
- Initiate learning exchanges and facilitate reflection and adaptive management sessions with Afghanaid staff and partners.
- Lead organisational research initiatives, including establishing and managing partnerships with research organisations, individual researchers (including PhD candidates/Masters’ students), universities and institutes, and consultants to facilitate the production of research outputs for Afghanaid. Adapt research findings into policy and practitioner briefs tailored to different audiences, including donors and external stakeholders; and producing reports drawing on the organisational database of past reports and data.
- Lead and contribute to the design of impact evaluations and internal studies, including initiating Terms of Reference, to inform the evolution of Afghanaid’s programming and implementation of the organisation’s strategy.
- Represent the organisation at external fora and in meetings with partners and donors to promote the organisation, strengthen external relations and identify opportunities for new and repeat funding and partnerships that contribute to Afghanaid’s funding pipeline.
- Support organisational learning initiatives where possible, for instance through documenting institutional knowledge and expertise and participating in lessons learned workshops.
- Contribute to organisational capacity through developing and facilitating training and workshops for Afghanaid staff, including in provincial offices, on subjects including effective reporting and impact analysis.
- Lead and support on the development of project reporting, analysis and evaluation templates and tools.
- Facilitate field visits with donor organisations, and virtual visits as required.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Requirements**

**Essential**

**Education**

- A Master’s degree in Development Studies, International Relations, Social Sciences or another relevant programme of study

**Experience**

- 3-4 years of experience of working in a development or humanitarian context, in project support, grant management, programme development or a similar role
- Proven experience of synthesising data and input from various sources into clear and cohesive narrative reports
- Strong experience with logical frameworks and/or theories of change
- Experience working in high-risk or volatile contexts, including humanitarian or emergency settings.

**Knowledge and Skills**

- Native English proficiency and demonstrated ability to write high quality, polished documents and reports that are consistent with a set brand and style
- Experience turning data and research into clear reports for a variety of audiences
- Strong data entry skills, familiarity with use of a databases, and office tools (Excel, Word)
- Experience in contract management
- Experience in donor/client relationship management in the humanitarian / development sector
- Experience in humanitarian project design or management, and/or budget development or management
- Strong organisational skills, able to plan effectively, set priorities, and meet tight deadlines under pressure
- Strong people and coalition-building skills and proven ability to form good working relations, both internally within the organisation and externally with people at all levels

**Personal Attributes**

- Intellectually curious and able to question assumptions
- Ability to work independently and as a team member, including in a coordinating capacity with other departments
- Initiative and drive to achieve results, working quickly and accurately with attention to detail
- An outgoing and engaging personality and strong sense of humour, able to build trust and manage relationships with a variety of stakeholders
- Cultural sensitivity and ability to work in diverse multi-cultural environment
- Ability and willingness to travel for work

**Desirable**

- Experience working on Climate Adaptation projects
- Experience working with, or knowledge of, key institutional donors for development and humanitarian programming in Afghanistan
- Experience with EU/INTPA grants
- Training in and/or exposure to M&E
- Understanding of the cultural, security and operating environment in Afghanistan (or in a similar context)
- Understanding of Dari and/or Pashto

jobs.title: Staff Auditor
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is currently seeking a talented professional for the role of a Staff Auditor. The Staff Auditor will help evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal controls of various departments at HFHI's headquarters, HFHI's international area offices, and selected programs of Habitat's U.S. and international organizations.

This position will be remotely based within the US and will require 40-60% domestic and/or international travel.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Assist with the planning, execution, and reporting on operational, financial and compliance audits in the designated areas. (20%)
- Assist in the preparation of the audit planning memo, risk-based audit programs and test plans which defines specific procedures to be performed during an audit. (5%)
- Conduct audit fieldwork work papers, findings, and recommendations for compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditor International Professional Standards and HFHI Internal Audit Department (IAD) Standards. (20%)
- Conduct peer reviews of other audit staff's audit documentation and working papers to ensure consistency, quality and compliance with internal audit standards. Provide constructive feedback to support continuous improvement. (5%)
- Draft finding and recommendations audit report in accordance with and monitor the quality of audit reports to ensure compliance with International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) and HFHI IAD Standards. (15%)
- Document processes, procedures, and test results. (5%)
- Coordinate the monitoring of outstanding audit recommendations. (5%)
- Plan, coordinate and performing consulting and advisory services as appropriate for the organization. (5%)
- Assist in the development of the IAD annual risk-based internal audit plan. (5%)
- Lead auditor assigned to the audit projects under his/her responsibility, will provide guidance and overall review of deliverables. (10%)
- Assists the VP/Director/Manager of Internal Audit on any other duties as assigned by management of Internal Audit as needed. The above duties could include supporting other internal audit units and audit activities, such as the SOAR process, audit committee package and risk assessment process. (5%)

**Key Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, or a related field.
- 3-5 years of professional experience with external and internal audits, forensic accounting investigations, preferably with a public accounting firm.
- Experience with international travel and/or cross-cultural communications.
- Expert level skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as a good understanding of the COSO - International Control Integrated Framework.
- Excellent English, verbal and written, communication skills.
- Strong critical thinking and project management skills.

**Preferred:**

- 3 years of domestic and international experience in internal or external audit management, preferably with a large international non-profit government, corporate organizations, or Big 4 Accounting Firm.
- Experience auditing construction activities and Micro-Finance operations.
- Proficiency with auditing software such as Galvanize HighBond or others.
- Experience using data analytics tools to create queries and trend analysis reports.
- Experience in non-profit Internal Audits, particularly executing audits of controls and transactions related to government and corporate grant requirements.
- Spanish, verbal and written, communication skills would be beneficial.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$55,600.00 USD

$82,675 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

**Habitat for Humanity International is an E-Verify employer.**

jobs.title: Senior Finance Associate (Fiji Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23549**  
Position Title: **Senior Finance Associate**  
Duty Station City: **Suva**  
Duty Station Country: **Fiji Islands**  
Grade: **G-6**  
Contract Type: **One-Year Fixed Term**  
Recruiting Type: **General Service**  
Vacancy Type: **Vacancy Notice**  
Initial duration: **12 months**  
Closing date:  **27 October 2026**

**Context:**

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Fiji and direct supervision of the Head of Resources Management; and, in collaboration with relevant units at Headquarters, Regional Office and the Global Shared Services Centre, the Senior Finance Associate will be responsible and accountable for managing or supporting the financial operations, budget monitoring, accounting processes, and financial reporting in accordance with IOM policies and procedures to countries in the South Pacific.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

1. Provide procedural guidance to managers and staff; supervise, guide and train other finance support staff;
2. Manage financial resources through monitoring and controlling assets, reserves, funds, supplies, etc. in accordance with IOM rules and regulations;
3. Provide specialized advice and support to Project Managers and/or Chief of Missions/Head of Office/ on financial and administrative matters;
4. Provide specialized support preparing annual budget submission and revisions including estimating the cost of staff as well as rental and utilities, office equipment and supplies, printing, and other contracts, services or running expenses;
5. Assist in monitoring compliance with financial policies, procedures, rules and regulations;
6. Consolidate data into financial statements and assist in monitoring expenditures to ensure they remain within authorized levels;
7. Provide regular and ad hoc financial information to support informed financial decision making;
8. Assist monitoring that bank reconciliations for IOM accounts are regularly performed and reviewed by designated stakeholders;
9. Manage and prepare the payroll by executing validity checks on monthly payroll results;
10. Ensure that disbursements are made based on proper authorizations and supported by legitimate and sufficient documentation;
11. Provide assistance responding to audit queries and follow up on audit recommendations;
12. Review the status and monitor the proper maintenance of Vendor Accounts in accounting system;
13. Verify vendor claims for accuracy and conformance with IOM finance policies and instructions;
14. Assist in the preparation of budget, accounting, financial, statistical reports and other reports as required; and,
15. Perform other related duties as required.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- High School diploma with six years of relevant experience; or,
- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finances, or related field with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, E-mail, Outlook; previous experience in SAP is a distinct advantage;
- Attention to detail, ability to organize paperwork in a methodical way;
- Discreet, details and clients-oriented, patient and willingness to learn new things; and,
- Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM/UN finance procedures and rules;
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, especially Excel;
- Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS); and,
- Knowledge of Oracle/SAP is highly desirable..

**Languages**

- Required for this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).
- IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this [link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Location**: Global

**Closing date for applications:** Monday**,** 26 October 2026

**Start date:** As soon as Possible

**Consultancy duration:** Three to Four Months

## We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities, restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

## **Summary job description**

We seek a consultant or team with strong experience in service design, customer experience (CX), user experience (UX) or human-centred service transformation to bring an independent partner-experience perspective and organisational critique to this work.

The consultancy will examine the end-to-end experience of working with Blue Ventures and connect it to the organisational choices shaping that experience. This includes how functions such as training and learning, partnerships, programme performance, data science and advocacy engage partners and coordinate their work.

Direct partner research will inform the assignment. The consultant must also bring the expertise to interpret and challenge existing arrangements, develop alternative approaches and demonstrate how support could be designed and delivered differently.

The work should introduce a shared framework that Blue Ventures can continue using beyond the consultancy. By applying this framework to selected priority areas, the consultant should demonstrate its value and help teams develop the understanding and practices needed to maintain it. The assignment is not expected to identify or design every change the organisation may need.

The primary focus will be partners funded through the Frontline Community Fund (FCF) and their interactions across Blue Ventures. The consultancy will complement our wider Partnership Strategy and internal operating model review, informing both without taking responsibility for the overall strategy, a comprehensive internal efficiency review or full implementation of recommendations.

### To download the full Terms of Reference, please click [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kceKwGi3lGg4hhkxuyB6Byv9lQWPV6Kp/view?usp=drive_link).

jobs.title: Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm.

**Job Summary**

You will provide strategic technical leadership, advice, guidance, and support across program design, business development, implementation, learning, and evidence generation in the areas of Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration. Working in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices, you will support Country Office(CO) teams to develop, implement, and scale innovative, high-quality programming that advances resilience, environmental stewardship, and sustainable livelihoods for poor and vulnerable communities. Your technical knowledge, advice and guidance will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming is across Uganda.

Your technical expertise, strategic vision, and leadership will contribute to the growth and positioning of CRS Uganda's Climate Change and Landscape Restoration portfolio. You will help identify and pursue new funding opportunities, lead technical design for priority investments and proposals, build relationships and partnerships, and support the effective implementation of strategic initiatives that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, and inform future programming. Through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will strengthen CRS' reputation as a trusted partner and technical leader in climate resilience, nature-based solutions, and landscape restoration across Uganda.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Contribute to the development and implementation of CRS Uganda strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration that effectively engage partners, donors and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction, while promoting innovation, learning, and evidence-based programming.
- Provide technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply program design and implementation standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools, and M&E, ensuring high-quality implementation. Support adaptive management and the use of evidence and learning to strengthen program quality and impact.
- Lead CRS Uganda's technical efforts to position and grow its Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration portfolio by identifying emerging opportunities, strengthening strategic partnerships, and shaping innovative, evidence-based programming approaches. Lead or contribute to the technical design of large and/or complex proposals, including the development of technical strategies, theories of change, and appropriate monitoring, evaluation, and learning frameworks in collaboration with business development, MEAL, and other cross-functional teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities, and technical requirements into CRS' approach and support the development of programming that strengthens CRS' competitiveness, impact, and thought leadership.
- Lead the design, implementation, and technical oversight of strategic initiatives and discretionary-funded investments in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, strengthen partnerships, and inform future programming and resource mobilization efforts.
- Contribute to technical communications, visibility, and thought leadership efforts by supporting the development of success stories, case studies, presentations, publications, learning products, and other materials that showcase CRS' experience, evidence, and impact in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration.
- Contribute to capacity strengthening initiatives in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and mentoring and coaching.
- Contribute to knowledge management and learning through collecting and analyzing program data, evaluating strategic projects, assisting with measuring program impact, capturing and sharing lessons learned and best practices, and research and internal reports.
- Establish and maintain relationships with donors, peer organizations, research and other institutions. Participate in forums in Climate Change and Landscape Restoration to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work, support organizational positioning, and identify opportunities for collaboration and resource mobilization.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s Degree in Climate Change, Forestry, Agroforestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Environmental Management, Agriculture, or a related field required.
- Minimum of eight years relevant international working experience in an advisory or management role with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of three years working for programming interventions in climate change adaptation and mitigation and/or landscape restoration
- Previous experience providing technical assistance and developing successful proposals for external donor funding is required.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master's Degree in Climate Change, Forestry, Agroforestry, Environmental Science, Natural Resource Management, Ecology, Environmental Management, Agriculture, or a related field is an advantage
- Demonstrated ability to convene, coordinate, and facilitate complex multi-stakeholder consultations and partnerships involving government, development partners, technical agencies, academia, and community stakeholders.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Demonstrated application of technical principles and concepts in climate change adaptation and mitigation and landscape restoration. General knowledge of other related disciplines to ensure a proper cross-sectoral approach.
- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks.
- Experience in business development, project design and proposal development in, including technical writing.
- Experience in mentoring, coaching, facilitation and training applying adult learning principles and practices.
- Experience with program monitoring and evaluation, including applying data collection tools and methodologies, data analysis, and data presentation.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.
- Excellent relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings.

jobs.title: Middle East Head of Operations
jobs.body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 6 months with very good prospects for an extension. Employment location will be Amman, Jordan (JO) .The position is paid according to SG8 of WHH's salary grid in Jordan.

As a member of the hub, your duty will be to lead procurement, IT and relevant legal matters of its work in Jordan and beyond, with your technical expertise, your problem-solving skills and onsite presence where necessary. You’ll lead the logistic and operations team, work closely with other members of the hub, closely liaise with legal counsellors, and provide solutions to operational issues. As the Middle East Head of Operations, your main task would be to oversee procurement, handle IT issues, manage facilities, oversee visa/permit issues for WHH staff, support in relations with the authorities and legal matters. You’ll work in close collaboration with the Logistics Coordinator and support the Head of Mission.

## Your responsibilities

**Tasks**

**Facilities**

- Identification, setup, and establishment of premises (offices, warehouses, guesthouses) across countries under WHH Amman hub’s responsibility. The role will involve overseeing the leasing processes, including due diligence, contract negotiation and compliance with WHH and local regulations.
- Close coordination with office, warehouse, and guesthouse focal points to assess facility needs, resolve issues, and ensure functionality, safety, and alignment with operational requirements.
- Supervise facility operations including utilities, services, maintenance, health and safety compliance, and security measures.
- Ensure proper management of facility-related assets and inventories, maintain accurate documentation (e.g., contracts), and promote sustainable facility practices such as energy efficiency and waste reduction.
- Support contingency planning for facility-related disruptions, and coordinate space planning to ensure effective use of premises in line with evolving programmatic needs.

**Fleet & Transportation**

- Establish or actively support the establishment of WHH’s fleet management systems in operational areas.
- Supervise and ensure proper use of vehicle logbooks (or apps), fuel tracking systems, and maintenance records. Conduct regular reviews and audits to ensure accuracy, accountability, and compliance with WHH and donor regulations.
- Provide technical supervision and capacity building for fleet personnel to maintain safe, cost-effective, and reliable transport operations.

**Inventory and Asset**

- Establish & implement standardized asset and inventory management software for WHH hub in Amman and its operational areas and ensure alignment with WHH procedures and donor requirements.
- Monitor the availability of supplies (inventory, stationery etc.) and establish a system for their replenishment for each operational area tailored to the needs of each operational area.
- Support stock management and warehousing and maintain updated inventory list for all locations with accurate data in collaboration with field logisticians, office responsible, and ensure accurate documentation and proper storage conditions
- Collaborate closely with field logisticians and office responsible to maintain up-to-date inventory and asset records across all locations, ensuring data accuracy and traceability.

**Procurement**

- Establish a sound procurement system for Amman hub, capable of adapting to changing operational needs and donor requirements across diverse contexts.
- Launch and manage framework agreements for commonly used items in each operational area, while ensuring market assessments and supplier prequalification remain up to date for rapid response in volatile environments.
- Closely follow up on digitalization processes lead by Head Office and make sure that the hub countries are well adopting new solutions and systems.
- Organize and oversee cross-border shipments through multiple supply corridors, proactively addressing access constraints, border procedures (custom clearance), and documentation to ensure timely delivery in dynamic settings.
- Ensure procurement documentation is collected and archiving practices are in place, maintaining full traceability and audit compliance.

**IT**

- Ensure that IT systems of the hub are up to standard with WHH systems
- Ensure that IT support personnel of the hub are well coordinated and that they are working closely with the regional IT.
- Ensure that all personnel have access to necessary equipment and systems and are not facing IT related challenges in conducting their tasks.
- Be aware and advice on digital solutions that would increase efficiency and effectives of WHH’s work.

**Partnerships**

- Provide active technical support to local partner organizations in conducting transparent and compliant procurement processes, aligned with WHH and donor regulations.
- Strengthen partner logistics capacity through training, mentoring, and support in the development or improvement of logistics manuals, tools, and procedures for sustainable operational management.
- Provide support to partners on other operations topics as needed.

**Legal & Admin Matters**

- Support the Head of Mission in legal & admin related matters for the hub such as (Registration process, renewal of required licenses, permits, visa & work permits for International staff) in Iraq, Yemen, Palestine, Jordan and other countries, if necessary,
- Give advice on legal matters to head of mission in ensuring compliance with national laws and regulations in each country.
- Act as focal point for legal advisors in each country, follow up on requests/permits/approvals, lead the preparation of necessary documentation, and keep the head of mission and the legal counsellors in head office up to date on these.
- Ensure that international staff and visitors receive necessary legal support for their travels to Jordan and other countries.
- Support registration related processes in all countries.

**Other**

- Take overall ownership establishing, standardizing and continuously improving all operations related processes in the hub countries, ensuring efficiency, compliance, digitalization, and adaptability to changing operational contexts.
- Proactively identify capacity building needs of WHH staff, by identifying development opportunities, delivering practical training, and fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement in operation practices.
- In coordination, with the other logistics personnel, represent the organization in forums such as logistics clusters, meetings amongst partners, authorities and different local actors involved in operations.

## Your profile

- University degree in humanitarian logistics, supply chain or similar
- Minimum 5 years of experience in operations of which **at least 2 years as head of logistics or operations department**
- Experience in working in conflict zones would be an asset
- Demonstrated experience in supporting local organizations in their capacity strengthening is required
- **Previous international experience in similar roles beyond Jordan is a must**
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, experience with logistic and operations software would be an asset
- Excellent inter-personal, communication, advisory and facilitation skills
- Fluency in verbal and written Arabic and English is a must
- **Willingness and ability to travel to OPT, Syria, Yemen, Iraq and Lebanon** (Ideally not blacklisted or barred from entering to any of the countries)

## Our offer

We offer you the opportunity to work in a responsible and interesting field as part of an extremely dedicated team. Welthungerhilfe attaches great importance to the personal and professional development of its employees. Remuneration is based on our gender-independent salary scale.

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

jobs.title: Online Training Facilitator for African Mental Health CSOs and OPDs: Project Management, Resource Mobilization, Financial Management, and M&E
jobs.body:
## Background

The Africa Mental Health Leadership Programme (MHLP) is funded by the Wellcome Trust through the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and is implemented by Africa CDC in collaboration with CBM Global, the Mental Health Innovation Network (MHIN), the Pan-African Network of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (PANPPD), and other key stakeholders. The programme aims to build a new generation of mental health leaders across Africa who are equipped to advance mental health policy, advocacy, and service delivery.

As the lead partner for Pillar Four: Civil Society Engagement and Networks, CBM Global works in collaboration with MHIN and PANPPD to strengthen civil society engagement, networking, and collective action within the mental health sector. Through this pillar, the programme seeks to strengthen the capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs), including organisations of persons with lived experience of psychosocial disabilities (OPDs), to advocate for quality, rights-based mental health services and to hold service providers and policymakers accountable. A key focus of CBM Global's role is to ensure the meaningful participation of people with lived experience at all stages of programme implementation, while supporting the institutional strengthening of representative organisations.

To inform these efforts, a Mental Health Organizations Needs Survey was conducted under Pillar Four across Africa to identify the needs, aims and priorities of the organizations among other key areas. The survey findings revealed significant capacity gaps in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation (M&E). In response to these identified needs, this Terms of Reference (ToR) proposes the development and delivery of an accessible online training initiative focused on these key capacity areas. The initiative aims to strengthen the organizational capacity, sustainability, and effectiveness of mental health CSOs and OPDs across the continent by equipping them with practical knowledge, skills, and tools in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and Monitoring &Evaluation (M&E). Furthermore, the initiative emphasizes a shift from one-off training workshops towards practical application, ongoing mentorship, and follow-up support to enable participating organisations to strengthen internal systems, improve funding readiness, and enhance accountability and organizational performance.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The purpose of this consultancy is to engage a qualified facilitator to design, facilitate, and provide a post training technical support for an accessible online capacity strengthening programme for mental health CSOs and OPDs across Africa.

The facilitator will develop and deliver practical, interactive and accessible training in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and in M&E, equipping participants with practical tools and templates. The Facilitator will also provide follow-up mentorship and technical support to strengthen organizational capacity, sustainability and accountability

## Overall Objective

To strengthen the institutional capacity of mental health CSOs and OPDs across Africa to sustainably mobilize resources, effectively manage programmes and finances, and generate evidence to improve accountability advocacy, and mental health outcomes in their communities.

## 4. Specific Objectives of the Assignment

- Design and deliver an accessible online capacity strengthening programme that starts with the project management cycle and progressively covers fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and M&E.
- Develop practical tools, templates, and learning assignments that participants can adapt and apply within their organizations.
- Provide structured mentorship and technical assistance to support participants in applying learning to real organizational priorities and strengthening institutional practices.
- Support the programme team in participant onboarding, baseline and endline assessments, and reporting on the training process and outcomes.
- Facilitate the development of organizational action plans and provide follow-up support to enable participating organizations to implement improvements in project management, fundraising, financial management, and M&E systems.

## Scope of Work

The Facilitator will be responsible for the full design, delivery, mentorship, and reporting of an online capacity strengthening programme for CSOs and OPDs across Africa. The assignment will include the development and adaptation of training content for a fully online, accessible, and low bandwidth. Deliver interactive training sessions; provide practical assignments and post-training mentorship; and documentation of programme outcomes and recommendations. to reinforce institution learning uptake.

## Key Tasks and Responsibilities

- Review the approved concept notes and other relevant background documents. Develop an inception report outlining the understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, delivery plan, work plan, and timeline.
- Support the refinement of participant application, selection and onboarding criteria, taking into account the concept note’s indication that small, emerging, and mid-sized organizations with clear institutional strengthening needs should be prioritized and that, where feasible, at least two representatives per organization should participate.
- Develop and administer baseline assessment to identify capacities, needs and priorities expectations, and institutional priorities in project design.
- Design a structured online curriculum covering project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and M&E.
- Develop training materials, facilitator guides, presentations, practical exercises, assignments and participants' resources.
