jobs.title: Country Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**Position**: Country Finance Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Representative (Line Management) and Regional Finance Manager (Functional Management)

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 07/11/2026

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Country Finance Manager** is responsible for all the administrative and accounting processes, including financial reporting, budget planning, development and monitoring. They manage staff within the Finance Department in country.

**MAIN FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES**

**General Administration**

- Track and manage deliverables and timelines related to grants, contracts, vendors, and partners
- Monitor grant administration to ensure compliance with reporting and expenditure requirements
- Supervise compliance of administrative documents and their proper filing
- Ensure the smooth flow of administrative information and data to the HQ
- Supervise flow of administrative information from project partners and the compliance with MoU
- Ensure smooth and punctual communications and reporting with local banks

**Accounting**

- Supervise and approve regular accounting, including monthly reconciliations, monthly and yearly closing of accounts, monthly journal entries
- Supervise cash and bank balance checking process when closing the monthly accounts

**Financial Reporting**

- Responsible for the preparation of financial reports, in coordination with Regional Finance Manager, and administrative team
- Ensure the compliance of financial reports with donors’ and internal rules and procedures

**Budget & Planning**

- Prepare and regularly monitor/updateWeWorld’s core budget for the Lebanon operation and provide an analysis to the Country Representativefocusing on gaps and risks
- Collaborate with the Country Representative, Head of Programmes and Project Managers to develop project budgets with quality, on time, in line with the operation’s core budget and according to donors’ regulations;
- Review administrative/financial terms of grant contracts before signature (payment & financial reporting schedule, etc.)
- Collaborate with the Head of Programmes, Project Managers and Procurement & Logistics Managers to regularly monitor actual and forecasted expenses against budget to avoid under and overspending on the projects in compliance withdonor flexibility rules
- Monitor financial flows of ongoing projects
- Anticipate financial risks, present budget updates and mitigation plans and report them to the Country Representative;
- Participate with the Country Management Team in reflecting on the evolution of the mission, and the programming of new projects and/or reorientation

**Audit Process**

- Collaborate to the management of financial audit performed on the projects
- Supervise yearly financial audit on general accounting for local authorities
- Prepare information and is directly responsible for any assessment/audit performed by donor on WeWorld administrative procedure

**Procedure**

- Design and implement administrative routines, procedures, and systems to increase efficiencies within the finance department, in particular relating to better structuring Budget Follow Ups, Forecasts, Payment Follow Ups and optimizing staff roles and responsibilities within the team
- Update the Local Operational Manual based on WeWorld procedures to implement organizational policies related to the Finance Department

**Operational**

- At Country level, liaise with the Human Resources and Procurement and Logistic departments for a fluid and collaborative collaboration
- Follow-up payments from donors and financial project close-out

**Human Resources**

- Participate in analyzing staffing needs & costs, compensation & benefits
- Supervise administrative and finance local personnel to complete routine tasks
- Capacity building of local finance staff and partner organizations in areas such as financial management, administration, good governance and management of accountability and transparency
- Support the Country Representative and the HR Manager to monitor and revise salary scale, if necessary

**Representation**

- Participate in inter-admin meetings with other INGOs and NGOs
- Ensure official representation for the administrative management of the Mission to the competent authorities

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) month collaboration contract subject to verification of the achievement of specific objectives (these objectives will be agreed together with the Line Manager upon arrival on assignment); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first months of contract and availability of funds.

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2950€ - 3550€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience in Financial/Accounting management
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluent in English both written and verbal

**Professional experience**

- At least 5 years of specific experience in finance/administrative positions in the international cooperation sector, in similar roles and levels or responsibility
- Experience of representation to institutions and participation in coordination meetings
- Experience in budget design and management and monitoring of logistics procedures
- Experience in using accounting software
- Experience in managing teams

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong flexibility and capacity to adapt behavior to the needs of the situation
- Capacity to work autonomously and in problems prevention/resolution
- Proven organizational skills and ability to effectively manage multiple tasks while fostering quality, team spirit and positive working relationships with colleagues
- Ability to identify, initiate and maintain good relationships with partner organizations, donors and national authorities including building professional relationships with senior decision-makers and influencers / leaders
- Good communication, negotiation skills and sensitivity in dealing with local institutions on critical issues
- Cultural, gender, religion, and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest for international cooperation development topics

**Desirable Requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous experience in the Middle East Region is an asset

jobs.title: Country Representative
jobs.body:
Habitat for Humanity is looking for “**Country Representative**” that serves as primary country focal point of Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) and external representative in Jordan and is a key member of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) leadership structure.

**1.Introduction and background:**

**Habitat for Humanity (HFH)** is an international nonprofit organization founded in 1976 as the world’s leader in addressing the housing challenges faced by vulnerable communities. Currently it operates in more than 60 countries around the world and brings people together to build more prosperous and vibrant communities by making sure everyone has a safe, affordable place to call home. Since its founding in 1976, it has helped more than 62 million people globally build their futures on their own terms through access to decent housing. HFH works alongside people of all walks of life to build, repair and finance their homes, by innovating new ways of building and financing, and by advocating for policies that make constructing and accessing housing easier for everyone.

HFHI works through a broad network of national Habitat organizations and other strategic partners, such as corporations, financial service providers, individuals, non-governmental organizations, foundations, local governments, as well as the private sector actors. HFHI supports program and project implementation by national HFH organizations and directly implements some projects and programs regionally. HFH started operating in Jordan in 1989 and has supported more than 48,000 households in 6 governorates across Jordan to improve their housing conditions in partnership with strategic local partners and community members.

**2. Position Description:**

The Country Representative (CR) reports to MENA Hub Director and supports the Director in identifying and nurturing relationships with country-based donors, local authorities, development partners, and target communities, all within the framework of HFHI’s regional and global strategies. Under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director, the CR is also responsible for leading country-level fundraising and resource mobilization efforts, while positioning HFHI as a housing thought leader in national dialogues and debates.

While the CR is also expected to deliver on standard country management tasks such as operational planning, financial and risk management, compliance, and safeguarding, our newly integrated model and structure require daily collaboration with MENA Hub staff on all the above.

The CR collaborates closely with thematic leads enabling and facilitating their technical leadership, and supports program managers in delivering against agreed objectives, embracing a people-centric approach.

**3.Scope of work and deliverables:**

**Strategic Alignment and Country Planning:**

1. Support overall strategic leadership for HFHI’s engagement in Jordan aligning country goals and plans with the MENA Strategy and HFHI global priorities.
2. Working closely with thematic leads to incorporating strategies and priorities into the overall country strategy, ensuring country plans reflect and operationalize agreed thematic approaches.
3. Support the annual country planning and budgeting process (for HFHI-funded work in-country), under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director and relevant Hub teams and monitor performance against approved plans.
4. Conduct regular country-level risk reviews, maintain a country risk register, develop mitigation plans, and escalate high/ “red” risks to the MENA Hub Director.

**Operation, Finance, Governance and Compliance:**

1. Oversee HFHI’s operational footprint in Jordan (offices, staff, contracts, and major activities), ensuring effective and efficient use of resources and compliance with HFHI standards, donor requirements and local legislation.
2. Ensure day-to-day operational compliance, local registration, and risk monitoring.
3. Provide day-to-day administrative line management for country-based staff, including leave approvals, budget oversight related to country operations, and coordination of operational support in line with HFH policies and procedures.
4. Ensure HFHI complies with all relevant registration, licensing, tax, and regulatory requirements in Jordan, working closely with the MENA Hub, Legal and Finance teams.
5. Enforce the Code of Conduct, Conflict of Interest, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies, ensuring they are understood and applied in day-to-day operations and partnerships.
6. Oversee basic financial management and internal controls for HFHI operations in-country, including oversight of budgets, expenditures, and financial reporting to the MENA Hub
7. Ensure procurement, contracting and vendor management for HFHI activities in Jordan comply with HFHI and donor policies, and that value for money, transparency and fairness are upheld.
8. Implement and oversee HFHI global safety and security standards for all HFHI staff, consultants, and visitors in-country, including maintaining country security plans, contact trees and incident protocols.
9. Ensure prompt reporting, investigation and follow-up of safeguarding and security incidents in line with HFHI policies and national law.
10. Coordinate external and internal audits related to HFHI’s country presence and support the timely closure of audit findings and implementation of management actions.

**Program Implementation Oversight, Resources mobilization and Partnership:**

1. Support local funding opportunities relevant to Jordan (institutional donors, multilaterals, private sector, foundations, etc.) and share intelligence with the MENA Hub.
2. Network and coalition building.
3. Support the development of country-level concept notes and project proposals, and support HFHI’s participation in multi-country or regional proposals that include Jordan.
4. Support the identification, scoping and design of quality projects in Jordan, aligned with HFHI’s priorities and in collaboration with the MENA Hub Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
5. Map and engage potential donors, partners, and stakeholders in Jordan (government, private sector, financial service providers, civil society, faith organizations, academia, UN and other international actors)
6. Maintain a country partnership mapping and engagement tracker, including pipelines, contacts and agreed follow-up actions.
7. Facilitate the negotiation of country-level Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and partnership agreements, in coordination with the MENA Hub, Legal Programs and Finance.

**Advocacy, Policy Engagement & External Representation:**

1. In coordination with the MENA Hub Director and HFHI Advocacy teams, support the development and implementation of a national advocacy and policy engagement plan aligned with regional advocacy priorities (e.g. housing policy, housing finance, urban development, resilience).
2. From an advocacy perspective, supports building and maintaining relationships with government counterparts, donors, United Nations (UN) agencies, European Union (EU) delegations, financial institutions, sector networks, civil society organizations, and other policy stakeholders at country level.
3. Represent HFHI in national forums, sector working groups, donor coordination platforms and, where appropriate, media opportunities, positioning HFHI as a credible housing and urban development actor in Jordan.
4. Support the development and implementation of a country communications approach that promotes HFHI’s brand, programs and advocacy messaging, and provides content for regional and global communications.
5. Ensuring advocacy and communication efforts are evidence-based, reflecting learning and impact from HFHI-supported programs and partnerships in Jordan.

**People Leadership, Culture and Volunteer Engagement:**

1. Provide direction, support to any HFH staff and consultants based in Jordan, fostering a culture of accountability, inclusion, learning and safeguarding.
2. In collaboration with Regional Human Resources (HR), support recruitment, onboarding, performance management and development of country-based staff and key consultants, as applicable.
3. Model and promote HFHI’s values and commitments to safeguarding, diversity, equity and inclusion in all country-level interactions and decisions.
4. Where applicable, support planning and hosting of HFHI-associated volunteer builds and events in Jordan, ensuring that they are safe, ethical, and aligned with HFHI standards and community priorities.
5. Ensure volunteer activities comply with safeguarding and duty-of-care standards, and that relevant stories and data are captured for visibility and fundraising purposes.

**4.Required Skills & Competencies:**

1. Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, combined with substantial professional experience in international development, organizational leadership, or a related area. An advanced degree is an asset.
2. Experience:
    - 7-10 years of progressively responsible experience in international development, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or management role.
    - Experience with traditional and emerging institutional donors including the Gulf countries.
    - Proven experience in resource mobilization including donor engagement and proposal development.
    - Experience managing diverse teams remotely.
    - A proven track record of both winning and executing multimillion projects.
    - Extensive experience working in Jordan's international development sector, with a strong understanding of the local operating environment, stakeholder landscape, and partnership networks.
    - Ability to adapt a changing environment and navigating market turbulences.
    - Management of teams and experience operating in a matrix structure.
    - Excellent written and spoken English and Arabic language.
    - Experience working with private philanthropy is an asset.
    - Previous experience in a hub structure is a plus.
3. Active support for **HFHI Values**:

**Humility** – We are part of something bigger than ourselves,

**Courage** – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular,

**Accountability** – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission),

***Safeguarding:***

*HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work*

*Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct).*

jobs.title: CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director
jobs.body:
## Candidates must currently reside in Indonesia.

**Position Title**: CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director

**Hiring Organization:** CORE, Inc. to be paid from the US

**Type of Employment:** Full-time consultancy.

**Duration of Contract:** November 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027 (with the possibility of extension)

**Duty Station:** Jakarta, Indonesia (with frequent travel to project-supported regions)

**Reports to:** CGPP Global Deputy Director

## **Background**

The CORE Group Partners Project (CGPP) is a multi-country, multi-partner initiative that provides on-the-ground technical assistance and guidance to support host country efforts to strengthen immunization systems, disease surveillance, and essential community-based health services. Globally, CGPP works across five technical areas (polio, maternal and child health, nutrition, malaria, and global health security) through existing networks of international and local NGOs operating in hard-to-reach areas with low immunization coverage. At the country level, a Secretariat coordinates the work of CGPP partner organizations in a manner that complements the efforts of all implementing partners. In Indonesia, CGPP supports national health strategies by strengthening routine immunization and polio eradication efforts while promoting maternal and child health through integrated community-based interventions.

## Consultancy Purpose

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director will be based in Jakarta, Indonesia and support CGPP National Program Manager and Provincial Team Leaders in operations in Indonesia to improve maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes in the selected districts of Papua and East Java provinces or any other selected CGPP work areas in Indonesia.

Serving as CGPP’s senior in-country representative, the CGPP Secretariat Director will maintain close coordination with government and the US Department of State (DOS) Foreign Assistance team.

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director will provide leadership across all aspects of project planning and implementation and will maintain and strengthen CGPP's relationship with key partners and stakeholders. These include the Government of Indonesia’s Ministry of Health (and other relevant government ministries) the US Department of State (US DOS), UNICEF, STRIDES implemented by FHI 360, other Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) partners, and Wahana Visi/ World Vision (WV) Indonesia.

In fulfilling this role, the Secretariat Director will ensure that:

- CGPP activities address stated project objectives, support national MCH and polio priorities, and are aligned with global MCH and polio objectives; and
- The needs and concerns of CGPP field teams and the communities they serve for all program related needs are effectively communicated to decisionmakers at all levels.

## Key Responsibilities

The Secretariat Director will be responsible for the following:

- **Strategic Leadership**  
    Provide strategic leadership for CGPP programming in Indonesia, in coordination with the CGPP global headquarters team, and CGPP National Program Manager including guiding the development of technical priorities and strategic plans that expand access to lifesaving services, strengthen routine immunization systems, and improve maternal and child health outcomes through integrated and sustainable approaches aligned with national and global priorities.
- **Government and Donor Engagement**  
    Lead institutional engagement with the Ministry of Health and relevant national and subnational structures, as well as with US DOS-Foreign Assistance.
- **Secretariat Leadership and Capacity Strengthening**  
    Provide leadership, mentorship, and oversight performance management for the CGPP National Program Manager; ensure the adequacy and quality of capacity strengthening for field-level teams and guide continuous improvement of implementation approaches.
- **Program Oversight, Quality, and Integration**  
    Provide oversight to the CGPP National Program Manager to effectively track progress toward CGPP MCH and polio goals, ensuring high-quality, coordinated implementation across program areas, and guide adjustments to strategies and approaches based on performance, risk analysis, and evolving context.
- **Planning, Budgeting, and Accountability**  
    Review, approve, and oversee implementation of the activities as per approved annual work plans and budgets, ensuring coherence, feasibility, alignment with agreed priorities, and adherence to approved budgets, with proactive identification of risks and timely course correction as needed.
- **Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning**  
    Oversee monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities, including planned CGPP assessments/ evaluations; ensure data quality and validation processes; guide the interpretation and use of data and evidence to inform strategic, technical, and operational decision-making; and work closely with the CGPP MEAL Officer to align workflows, strengthen MEAL capacity across secretariat and partner teams, coordinate partner support, and maintain MEAL standards in data quality and reporting across all partners.
- **Partner Coordination and Representation**  
    Serve as the focal point for strategic coordination and engagement with national and international stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, and peer organizations; represent CGPP in relevant technical, policy, and coordination platforms; and sustain informal engagements with government counterparts and peer organizations, including cultivating ongoing informal communication channels to strengthen relationships, identify emerging issues, and foster trust and collaboration across stakeholders.
- **Reporting and Knowledge Management**  
    Ensure timely preparation and submission of required CGPP reports and briefings; validate monthly data updates, performance indicators, and partner-reported results; and oversee systematic documentation, timely synthesis, and dissemination of policy developments, coordination outcomes, and lessons learned as well as key discussions, decisions, action points, and follow-up items arising from all secretariat engagements – including technical coordination meetings, internal secretariat discussions, partner consultations, stakeholder engagements, and informal coordination touchpoints – to strengthen transparency, institutional memory, and accountability.

## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

- **Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership** for complex, multi-partner initiatives, with strong analytical judgment and systems thinking to navigate ambiguity, risk, and competing priorities.
- **Exceptional relationship management and diplomatic skills**, with the ability to build trust, influence outcomes, and manage alignment across diverse stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, implementing partners, and civil society organizations.
- **Proven ability to lead, mentor, and hold accountable senior and multidisciplinary teams**, fostering a culture of collaboration, performance, learning, and results in complex operating environments.
- **Strong executive communication and representation skills**, with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information, brief senior decisionmakers and donors, and represent the Secretariat credibly in high-level national and international forums.
- **Demonstrated capacity to convene, align, and harmonize partners** around shared lifesaving priorities, ensuring integrated approaches and avoiding fragmentation or vertical implementation.
- **Sound judgment and decision-making capacity**, including the ability to make timely, evidence-informed decisions with significant organizational, financial, and reputational implications.

## Preferred Qualifications

- **Experience leading or supporting a secretariat or partnership platform**, including stewardship of collective decision-making processes across multiple institutions.
- **Demonstrated experience navigating complex political or institutional environments**, including managing sensitivities across government, donors, and implementing organizations.
- **Experience leading programs during periods of transition or uncertainty**, such as scale-up, funding shifts, public health emergencies, or changes in government or donor priorities.

## Required Languages

- **English** (Required): Advanced professional proficiency required, with ability to communicate effectively in meetings, presentations, and written reports with international stakeholders.
- **Bahasa Indonesia** (Required): Professional proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing.

## Travel

- Must be willing and able to travel approximately 30% to 50% of the time.

## Supervisory Responsibilities

- Will supervise staff as assigned.

## Working Relationships

- Within CGPP Indonesia (e.g., National Program Manager, MEAL Officer, Provincial Team Leaders), Wahana Visi leadership, and finance, procurement, and grants teams.
- External: Ministry of Health and relevant provincial, district, and local MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, and others.
- CGPP Global Secretariat Team: Coordinate with the global secretariat team and Asia regional team and obtain technical guidance as needed.

## Qualifications

- Master's degree in public health or a related technical field.
- At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience, including at least five years in a senior management or leadership role, overseeing multidisciplinary teams in international and/or multicultural settings.
- Demonstrated experience providing strategic leadership and operational oversight for complex programs or initiatives.
- Demonstrated experience working with or supporting governance structures and engaging effectively with government counterparts and institutional partners.
- Proven experience in managing donor-funded programs, including compliance with donor regulations, financial accountability, audits, and high-quality reporting.
- Strong knowledge and experience in budget management and financial oversight.
- Technical expertise and demonstrated experience in maternal and child health (MCH), combined with strong familiarity with the Indonesian health system and context.
- Ability to use data, evidence, and learning to inform strategic decision-making and program improvement.
- Proficiency in standard office and data analysis software.
- Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with demonstrated ability to represent organizations at senior national and international levels and to build effective partnerships with donors, government, and implementing partners.

## Disclaimer

- This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.

jobs.title: Technical Advisor I, Cash & Markets
jobs.body:
**NOTE: The Pay Range referenced in this job announcement only applies to applicants who perform the job within the US and to applicants classified by CRS as International Assignees. Staff hired on local payroll would follow the respective Country pay range. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your anticipated work location during the candidate selection process.**

**Pay Range**  
$71,349 - $88,085 Annually

**NOTE: This is a remote position, with a preference for candidates based in the LACRO and EMEA regions; CRS will also give preference to candidates who are based in countries where we have existing offices. CRS does not sponsor visas for remote employees.**

Catholic Relief Services is implementing a global emergency response initiative designed to deliver timely, lifesaving humanitarian assistance in rapidly evolving crises worldwide. Over 18 months, the program enables fast, flexible action to address urgent needs arising from sudden shocks and protracted emergencies. It supports critical humanitarian sectors through context-appropriate assistance while emphasizing operational readiness, locally led implementation, accountability to affected communities, and safe, dignified programming. The initiative strengthens the organization’s ability to respond at speed and scale in complex and resource-constrained environments, ensuring help reaches people most in need when it matters most. This role will support cash readiness efforts of Country Programs and partners, as well as provide technical support for ongoing programming, and new emergency programs, related to cash, market-based programming, and emergency food security and livelihoods.

**Job Summary:**

This position is embedded in the Humanitarian Response Department (HRD) Market-based Rapid Response and Recovery (MBRRR) Team. The HRD MBRRR Team is the agency lead for Cash & Market-based Programming and the emergency Food Security & Livelihoods Sectors. As part of this team, you will provide technical advice and support to a range of program design and implementation issues in Cash & Markets as well as Food Security & Livelihoods, in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices to Country Program (CP) teams and partners to advance the delivery of high-quality humanitarian assistance programming to the poor and vulnerable impacted by crises. Your advice, knowledge, and support will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive, and innovative CRS’ Cash and Market-based programming is across the agency.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Support the development and contribute to the implementation of agency-wide strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in relation to Cash and Market Based Programming that effectively engage partners, donors, and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction.
- Provide programmatic and operational (including administrative and finance) technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools and M&E, helping to ensure high-quality implementation.
- Contribute to, and in some cases lead, the development of the technical design for proposals. Support the process of preparation, design, submission and approval of project concepts and full-fledged proposals. As needed, act as a technical writer on proposal development teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technical requirements into CRS’ approach.
- Support capacity strengthening initiatives in relation to Cash and Market based programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and coaching.
- Collect and analyze program data, capture, and share lessons learned and best practices for specific projects to facilitate improvements in decision-making and contribute to the Cash and Market Based Programming learning agenda.
- Contribute to maintaining relationships with donors, peer organizations, research, and other institutions, participate in forums in the area of Cash and Market Based Programming to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work.
- Support Country Programs and partners in strengthening their cash readiness through targeted technical support, particularly in relation to developing capacities, identifying suitable cash delivery mechanisms and Financial Service Providers (FSPs), developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and tools, and supporting the design and implementation of pilot cash programs.

***Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

- Strong relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings
- Good strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Good technical writing skills
- Presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented

***Required Languages*** – English and Spanish required. French, Portuguese and Arabic highly desired.

***Travel*** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 50%, including at short notice and to emergency situations.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's Degree in humanitarian assistance, social policy, economics or related field required.
- Minimum of five-eight years relevant work experience with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of two years relevant emergency response and field-based experience in cash and market-based programming, including in protracted and rapid onset crisis contexts.
- Experienced trainer in CVA Programming. Knowledge of technical principles and concepts in cash and market-based programming, including experience with multiple CVA delivery mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience in designing CVA Programs, particularly for US Government funding, and designing and implementing Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) or sectoral cash and voucher programs related to Food Security, Livelihoods, Shelter or WASH sectors. Experience in other sectoral cash programming, such as Nutrition, DRR, and/or Protection, desirable. Experience with e-voucher platforms highly desirable.
- Knowledge of, and experience in, conducting market assessments and response analysis to inform modality decisions across different areas of programming, particularly in emergency rapid-onset humanitarian contexts.
- Experience in innovative project design for rapid response with market-based programming in a diversity of contexts.
- Experience in proposal development, for government and/or private donors.
- Knowledge of capacity strengthening and technical accompaniment best practices, with a focus on collaboration and supporting partner-led responses.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based and civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), data analytics and PowerBi.
- Master's Degree in humanitarian assistance, social policy, economics or related field is an advantage.

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

**What we offer**

CRS offers U.S. based staff a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, life insurance, vision, and a generous retirement savings plan. Benefits packages for successful candidates employed outside the U.S. are based on the country of employment/in-country office where the candidate will perform the role. CRS´ work culture is a collaborative, mission-driven culture committed to improving the lives of the poor throughout the world.

jobs.title: Project Director, Chad
jobs.body:
**Role:** Full Time

**Contract Duration**: 2 Years

**Deadline for submission:** 30th October 2026

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**About Us**

Founded in 1992, Nutrition International is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into broader development programs. In more than 60 countries, primarily in Asia and Africa, Nutrition International nourishes people to nourish life.

For more than 30 years now, Nutrition International has focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Nutrition International’s work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

**About the role**

Nutrition International is supporting the Ministry of Health in Chad to implement Child Survival programming including to maintain coverage and ensure that all eligible children receive two doses of vitamin A supplementation (VAS) every six months and to preposition zinc & low-osmolarity oral rehydration salts (LO-ORS) to treat childhood diarrhea in line with WHO -recommended treatment protocols.

To ensure the supported rounds are successful, and program data is available for decision-making, Nutrition International will conduct regular post-event coverage survey (PECS) after campaigns. Doing so will ensure review data is available quickly post-event to allow course corrections in time for the next round of the vitamin A supplementation implementation. The program will also produce data and guidance that is needed to curb child deaths and maximize every dollar invested.

Nutrition International will scale up its technical assistance and advisory services to reinforce government capability and programming. Nutrition International will ensure campaigns are designed and delivered effectively and with attention paid to gender equity. This includes the application of best practices and the adaptation of global guidance to the country’s context.

The Project Director is the lead focal person for Nutrition International’s programming in Chad. The job holder will be responsible for external relationships and accountable for program delivery in Chad, in line with NI’s vision, mission and values and the VAS program design. The Job holder will also provide high-level representation of Nutrition International and oversee support to the Government at national and sub-national levels.

The Project Director will provide overall leadership of the Nutrition International Country Team and Child Survival programming in Chad, will lead the management of relations with the Government of Chad and with other key local stakeholders and oversee the work of a country team in developing, managing, monitoring and reporting on Nutrition International Child Survival programming in Chad. The Project Director will be accountable for programmatic and financial delivery and reporting against Nutrition International requirements and will also manage Nutrition International’s country operations including ongoing compliance with legal and financial regulations in the country.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. External Relations and Representation**

- Lead Nutrition International’s representation in Chad, building strong relationships with national and sub-national government, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, the private sector, academia and communities.
- Position Nutrition International as a key actor in nutrition and public health, including through national task forces, alliances and conferences.
- Engage in advocacy, directly and with partners, to influence government policy and partner investment in nutrition.
- Harmonise Nutrition International’s work with other partners and actively support government leadership and ownership.
- Identify opportunities to leverage and mobilise additional resources to expand Nutrition International’s work in Chad.

**2. Programme Management and Delivery**

- Be accountable for achieving agreed results, programme quality and disbursement targets within agreed timelines.
- Manage the performance of partners and sub-contractors against agreements, negotiating corrective action where needed and assessing value for money.
- Monitor progress against workplans and performance frameworks, account for variances and prepare reports for donors and stakeholders.
- Convene and participate in programme review and steering meetings with government and partners and negotiate adjustments to plans and budgets.
- Ensure vitamin A programming mainstreams gender equality in line with Nutrition International’s global strategy, including Sex and Gender Based Analysis.

**3. Financial Management**

- Working with the administrative support partner, ensure country resources are managed in line with Nutrition International policies and within approved budgets.
- Guide the team in costing, budgeting, expenditure forecasting, variance analysis and value-for-money reporting for donor purposes.

**4. Team Leadership and Country Operations**

- Lead and develop the country team of three Senior Programme Officers and a Project Officer.
- Manage country operations, including ongoing compliance with legal and financial regulations in Chad.
- Keep Nutrition International staff informed of progress and ensure contributions are recognised.

**5. Focal Point for Nutrition International Child Survival programming in Chad**

- Be the primary focal point and lead for Nutrition International Child Survival programming in the country.
- Build strong relationships with and engage regularly with senior government officials to ensure programming gaps. and needs are clearly articulated and coordinated with other partner support.
- Ensure visibility of Nutrition International’s support to national and sub-national authorities.

## **Requirements**

**Education/Professional Designations/Experience:**

- Master’s degree from a recognized university in management, international development, public health, nutrition or related area;

\- Additional post graduate certification in project or general management is desirable.

\- Certificate in research and/or monitoring and evaluation an added advantage.

- At least 10 years of experience in the management of programs in public health, nutrition, international development or a related field;
- Significant experience managing complex budgets and diverse teams in progressively more senior leadership roles;
- At least 5 years’ experience in networking at a high level with international partners and country government, desirable;
- At least 5 years’ experience of working in Chad; regional and/or global experience highly desirable;
- Previous experience as a Country Manager or Director or equivalent role in scope and responsibility for an international organization/NGO highly desirable.

**Languages Skills**

- Fluent in English and French required.
- Fluency in local Chad languages would be an asset.

## **Benefits**

Competitive market pay, comprehensive medical benefits, flexible working hours, generous annual leave, support for professional learning and development, and dedicated health and wellness allowance.

Nutrition International is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and accessible work environment. Applicants with special needs who require adjustments or support are encouraged to reach out during the recruitment process.

**Our Commitment to Safeguarding**

Nutrition International has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), or any other form of safeguarding misconduct. We incorporate safeguarding-related questions throughout the recruitment process, including during interviews and reference checks, to ensure a safe and respectful working environment. In accordance with the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, reference checks will include safeguarding verifications with previous employers.

**Candidate Consent**

By applying for this position, you consent to professional reference checks and appropriate background screening as part of the selection process. Any offer of employment is conditional on satisfactory completion of these checks.

jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY  
Habitat for Humanity International seeks a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) Specialist to support and advance the Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter's work with small and growing businesses. The purpose of the Terwilliger Center is and always has been to influence market actors – i.e., private companies, public officials, civil society, consumers, and households – to change attitudes, behaviors, policies, business models, and products and services in ways that lead to scalable affordable housing solutions. This is the essence of the Terwilliger Center's contribution to the HFHI mission of ensuring that everyone has a decent place to live.

The Terwilliger Center supports enterprises expanding innovative and client-responsive services, products and financing so that low-income households can improve their housing more effectively and efficiently. The Terwilliger Center operates in a dynamic environment where projects are often executed using a matrix structure, leveraging cross-functional teams within the center and, at times, across the wider Habitat network to achieve success.

The MEAL Specialist will play a key role in supporting the implementation, learning, and continuous improvement of the Small and Growing Businesses (SGB) Framework, the Terwilliger Center's global approach to identifying, supporting, and learning from enterprises with solutions for affordable housing via direct support and capital mobilization. This position strengthens the systems, evidence, and coordination needed to align global strategy with regional implementation. The role will also contribute to MEAL and learning efforts connected to the Shelter Venture Fund (SVF), the Center's mechanism for deploying investment into housing SGBs, ensuring coherence between the SGB framework and investment-related evidence. The MEAL Specialist will help advance learning, insights, and network engagement that elevate the Center's ability to support SGBs, influence entrepreneurial ecosystems, and inform future program design. Specifically this role designs and implements MEAL systems for impact investment portfolios and SGB programs, ensuring evidence-based decision-making and will contribute to global learning agendas, donor reporting, and impact measurement frameworks aligned with GIIN/IRIS+ standards.

**Key Responsibilities:**

ESSENTIAL DUTIES 1) Design and implement the MEARL framework for the SGB framework.  
Develop results chains/frameworks for SGB framework and Shelter Venture Fund investments.  
Ensure alignment with global impact measurement standards (IRIS+, SDG indicators).  
Supports SGB team in target setting for annual and multi-year projections and puts a rigorous but realistic plan in place to track and monitor against these targets.

2)Ensure Data Quality and Insight Generation to support the SGB framework and strengthen evidence of uptake.

Working with global MEARL, geographic MEARL and SGB leads, lead rigorous data collection, validation, and analysis using mixed methods. Lead stakeholder reporting requirements and ensure integrity of reporting. Produce dashboards and learning briefs for internal strategy and external stakeholders.

3)Learning and Knowledge Management.

Facilitate learning loops across regions; synthesize cross-portfolio insights. Translate evidence into actionable recommendations for the SGB framework, including investment insights and program design. Promote adaptive management. Use evidence and real-time insights to inform strategic pivots and improve program effectiveness.

4\) Capacity Building and Systems Strengthening.  
Develop and maintain digital data systems (such as CRM, Airtable, PowerBI) for real-time monitoring and data visualization.  
Keep up to date on industry trends and build insights into continuous improvement of MEAL systems.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Master’s in Monitoring & Evaluation, Development Economics, Statistics, Impact Measurement, or related field.

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS

Minimum 5 years in MEAL roles, including impact investing or enterprise development contexts.

Proven ability to design and implement MEAL systems.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance.

For work locations in Slovakia, the minimum monthly gross pay starts at:

€3,060.00 EUR

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Protection Officer
jobs.body:
TEAM PURPOSE:  
To identify, analyse and address risks affecting the safety, dignity, rights and wellbeing of individuals and communities affected by conflict, displacement and other crises, in Rural Damascus, Daraa and Assweida governorates. The team designs, implements and oversees protection interventions through direct implementation and partner-led modalities, while strengthening community capacities, local protection systems, social cohesion, and community-based protection mechanisms. The team contributes to the prevention, mitigation and response to protection risks through individual assistance, community-based protection, protection monitoring, evidence generation, advocacy, social cohesion and other protection programming in line with Oxfam Syria's strategy and humanitarian principles.  
  
JOB PURPOSE:  
The Protection Officer in the Southern hub is responsible for the technical leadership and operational management of Oxfam's protection portfolio within the hub, ensuring that all protection activities are implemented in accordance with Oxfam Safe Programming standards and Oxfam Syria's endorsed SOPs, methodologies and guidance. This responsibility applies to both directly implemented and partner-led interventions. The Team Leader leads the identification, analysis and monitoring of protection risks affecting individuals and communities and oversees the design and implementation of appropriate protection responses, including Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion activities, and other protection interventions. The role is responsible for determining the most appropriate implementation modality for each intervention, including direct implementation, partner-led implementation, or phased transition approaches. This role establishes and maintains collaboration with affected communities, local authorities, community leaders, community-based organizations (CBOs), implementing partners and other humanitarian and development actors.  
Where activities are implemented through partners, the Protection Team Leader remains responsible for technical oversight, partner capacity strengthening, mentoring, accompaniment, quality assurance, compliance and risk management. This includes supporting partners to progressively assume leadership of protection activities while ensuring adherence to Oxfam standards and protection outcomes.  
  
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:  
Assessments, analysis and evidence generation  
•Lead and supervise protection staff, and/or support protection partners, in the planning and implementation of Community Gendered Protection and Social Cohesion Analyses, protection monitoring exercises, stakeholder mapping, service mapping, and other assessments required to inform programme design and advocacy priorities.  
•Ensure timely consolidation, dissemination and utilization of assessment findings to inform protection responses, programme adaptation, advocacy efforts and strategic decision-making across Oxfam sectors and external stakeholders.  
•Contribute to research, learning and evidence-generation initiatives informing protection and social cohesion programming, advocacy and policy development.  
Programme and project development  
•Contribute to the development, implementation and adaptation of Oxfam Syria's protection and social cohesion strategy and operational plans based on field evidence, protection trends, emerging risks and organizational priorities.  
•Lead the identification and design of protection and social cohesion interventions, including community-based protection, IPA, protection monitoring, social cohesion, and other protection approaches implemented through direct and/or partner-led modalities.  
•Contribute to concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports, ensuring technical quality and alignment with Oxfam standards, Protection and social cohesion priorities and contextual needs.  
•Identify opportunities for protection and social cohesion integration across sectors and support the design of protection-sensitive as well as conflict-sensitive interventions, in coordination with relevant technical teams.  
Programme implementation and oversight  
•Lead and supervise the implementation of protection and social cohesion activities within the hub, ensuring compliance with Oxfam standards, donor requirements and endorsed SOPs and methodologies.  
•Directly supervise Protection staff and/or support protection partner, and provide technical guidance, coaching and performance management under their responsibility.  
•Oversee the delivery of IPA, community-based protection activities, social cohesion programming, distributions, protection monitoring activities and other protection programming implemented directly by Oxfam.  
•Ensure effective collaboration with case management and other specialized strategic partners to strengthen referrals, complementarity of services and protection outcomes for individuals facing protection risks.  
•Ensure that referral pathways, service mapping mechanisms and coordination arrangements remain functional, updated and accessible to affected populations. Monitoring, reporting, learning and accountability  
•Ensure interventions' outputs, outcomes and impact are monitored and evaluated, in line with methodologies and tools, and in coordination with MEAL staff at hub level  
•Supervise programme quality, protection outcomes, risks and implementation progress through regular field visits, partner monitoring systems, data review and engagement with affected communities.  
•Ensure timely and accurate programme reporting to enable timely contribution to donor, management and sector reporting requirements, including for both direct and partner-led implementation.  
•Work closely with MEAL teams to ensure data quality and the collection and analysis of sex-, age- and diversity, including disability-disaggregated data.  
•Promote learning, adaptive management and continuous improvement based on monitoring findings, community feedback and lessons learned.

  
Representation and coordination  
• Represent Oxfam in Protection Sector and other relevant coordination platforms.  
•Coordinate with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, community leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen protection and social cohesion outcomes and facilitate implementation.

  
Partnership Management Responsibilities  
•Lead and oversee the planning and quality assurance, as well as support the implementation and monitoring when needed and requested, of protection and social cohesion programmes implemented through partners.  
•Manage strategic protection partnerships to ensure the timely, effective, and accountable delivery of project activities, outputs, and outcomes.  
•Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and capacity strengthening to partners, in line with partner priorities, on protection programming, including community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion, individual protection assistance (IPA), referrals, safeguarding, and protection mainstreaming.  
•Support partners in developing, maintaining, and regularly updating service mapping and safe, confidential, and survivor-centred referral pathways in line with agreed protocols.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable the delivery of survivor-centred, timely, and quality protection services, including appropriate referrals to specialized service providers.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable timely and quality monitoring of the quality and effectiveness of partner-led protection interventions.  
•Support partners in identifying and designing high-quality protection and social cohesion interventions that respond to evolving humanitarian needs.  
•Promote integrated, protection-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive programming by facilitating coordination between partners and relevant technical sectors i.e. WASH and FES.  
•Together with protection partners, monitor partner-led project implementation against agreed work plans, indicators, budget& burn rates, deliverables, and implementation timelines, and support timely corrective actions where needed.  
•Conduct regular partner review meetings, field monitoring visits, and joint supervision missions to assess programme quality, identify challenges, and strengthen implementation.  
•Review partner reports and ensure timely, accurate reporting on progress, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and best practices.  
•Identify implementation risks and operational bottlenecks and work collaboratively with partners to develop and implement corrective action plans.  
•Promote continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and partner capacity development through joint learning moments.  
•Build and maintain strong working relationships with partners, promoting accountability, mutual learning, and high-quality programme delivery.

jobs.title: 23451 Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA) (P)
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director for Operations (DRD-O), and in close coordination with the Department of Mobility, Pathways and Inclusion (DMPI) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer (RPLO), the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs), and Country Offices (COs) along the region’s priority migration routes, the Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will be responsible and accountable for leading, at the technical level, the regional operationalisation and implementation of the IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and providing strategic and programmatic advice on its implementation across the region.

The Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will ensure alignment with IOM’s global approach, lead regional and inter-agency coordination at the technical and operational levels, and oversee the application of Route-Based Approach (RteBA) tools and instruments within and across countries and along migration routes.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.
