jobs.title: Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Contract duration:** 4 months' probation period with prolongation upon successful probation period end

**About PIN Ukraine:**

People in Need (PIN) has been active in Ukraine since early August 2014. Currently, PIN is one of the major humanitarian actors in Ukraine responding to the recent military escalation, providing humanitarian aid to conflict-affected people across Ukraine. Since 2014, PIN has implemented emergency food and cash assistance, NFI, shelter, protection, livelihoods and WASH interventions supporting 5 million vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in urban and rural areas.

PIN is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic. PIN encourages applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds and values diversity.

**General information about the role of the person:**

Under the supervision of the Economic and Green Recovery Technical Lead, the Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator will provide technical and analytical support to the design, quality assurance, monitoring, and continuous improvement of PIN's economic recovery programs in Ukraine.

The position involves:

• supporting the development and adaptation of economic recovery methodologies, tools, and technical guidance;

• providing technical support to program teams without taking over the management of their implementation;

• supporting the development of proposals, concept notes, needs assessments, studies, and program frameworks;

• documenting lessons learned, best practices, and evidence generated within economic recovery programs;

• supporting capacity development of teams on relevant technical approaches and tools;

• participating in coordination and technical exchange with relevant internal and external stakeholders;

• supporting the Technical Lead in ensuring coherence and quality across the economic recovery program portfolio.

• conducting and supporting field-based technical work, including field visits, assessments, consultations, data collection, and technical follow-up, either jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead;

• engaging with external stakeholders and representing PIN’s interests in relevant technical discussions, meetings, consultations, and coordination forums, as needed

**Description of general duties:**

**1. Technical Quality and Methodology**

• Facilitate the development, analysis, and adaptation of technical approaches, methodologies, tools, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and recommendations for economic recovery programs. Maintain a clear record of methodological revisions, consolidate feedback from teams, and submit proposed changes to the Technical Lead for review before wider use.

• Analyze the technical quality, relevance, and consistency of programmatic approaches and provide recommendations for their improvement.

• Provide support to teams in adapting and aligning technical approaches across different projects and contexts.

**2. Technical Support to Program Implementation Teams**

• Participate in grant committees and conduct application assessments. Review applications and business plans against agreed eligibility and scoring criteria, assess technical feasibility and market assumptions, and document recommendations and clarification requests for committee consideration.

• Provide program teams with technical advice on the application of economic recovery methodologies and tools. Respond to technical questions during implementation, review practical examples with staff, and escalate unresolved methodological issues to the Technical Lead. Keep programme delivery decisions with the responsible implementation teams.

• Support teams in interpreting and applying technical guidance, targeting approaches and selection criteria, monitoring requirements, and program methodologies.

**3. Technical Monitoring and Quality Assurance**

• Conduct regular technical monitoring visits to program implementation regions and activity sites. Agree visit objectives with the Technical Lead and implementation teams; prepare checklists, review available project records, and consult participants, businesses, partners, and staff as relevant. Conduct visits jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead as agreed.

• Assess the technical quality of implementation against approved methodologies, SOPs, program frameworks, and relevant standards.

• Identify technical, methodological, and quality issues and prepare recommendations for corrective actions.

• Coordinate monitoring work with MEAL, Protection, Grants, Partnerships, and Programme Implementation as needed.

• Prepare technical monitoring reports, action lists, and recommendations for follow-up. Record findings, supporting evidence, recommended actions, responsible colleagues, and agreed timeframes. Follow up on technical improvements with the relevant teams and flag recurring or unresolved quality issues to the Technical Lead.

**4. Program Analysis, Evidence, and Learning**

• Support the development and interpretation of economic recovery indicators and monitoring tools. Work with MEAL on indicator definitions, data sources, collection methods, and interpretation of baseline, monitoring, and endline findings. Identify data gaps and limitations before drawing conclusions about results.

• Contribute to the analysis of program results, including economic impact and changes in livelihoods, income, employment, business performance indicators, and resilience, as relevant. Compare results across locations and participant groups where the data allow; examine barriers to economic recovery and explain the practical implications for programme adjustments.

• Support the identification of needs within the economic recovery sector.

**5. Program Development and Proposal Preparation**

• Support the Technical Lead and relevant program teams in developing new economic recovery concepts and project proposals.

• Participate in technical discussions during program design and implementation where specialized economic recovery expertise is required.

• Collect and analyze information needed for program design.

• Conduct stakeholder mapping in the economic recovery sector.

• Support the development of intervention logic, targeting approaches, selection criteria, technical methodologies, and monitoring systems. Prepare technical inputs on activities, expected outputs and outcomes, assumptions, risks, and resource needs. Check that proposed approaches are feasible, evidence-based, and consistent with the agreed programme framework.

• Support the development of new economic recovery initiatives in line with PIN's strategic priorities and identified needs.

**6. Needs Assessments, Research, and Analytical Work**

• Support needs assessments, market and sector analyses, and other economic recovery research to contribute to PIN’s evidence base on economic recovery in Ukraine. Help define research questions, assessment tools, stakeholder consultations, and field data collection plans. Analyse market demand, employment opportunities, business constraints, access to services, and recovery needs as relevant; validate findings with teams and stakeholders and prepare practical recommendations.

**Coordination with Programme Implementation and Livelihood Functions**

The Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator works closely with the Livelihood Coordinator and relevant Programme Implementation teams.

The Coordinator does not:

• manage the day-to-day implementation of program activities;

• replace the Livelihood Coordinator in coordination with operational departments;

• take on responsibility for logistics, procurement, finance, or administrative support to implementation;

• take on Programme Implementation's responsibility for delivering program activities;

• duplicate the operational reporting and control mechanisms of the Programme Implementation structure.

**Internal Coordination**

• Maintain regular coordination with Programme Implementation, MEAL, Grants, Partnerships, and other relevant departments. Agree technical priorities and follow-up actions, share findings that affect programme quality or reporting, and clarify responsibilities where technical and implementation functions intersect.

• Coordinate with technical colleagues in Protection, WASH, Shelter, and Education when economic recovery activities involve cross-sectoral approaches.

**External Technical Engagement**

Under the guidance of the Technical Lead:

• participate in relevant technical working groups, coordination meetings, workshops, and consultations;

• support technical communication with relevant CSOs, private sector representatives, service providers, research institutions, and other stakeholders;

• support stakeholder mapping and identification of relevant technical resources and partnerships;

• represent PIN at selected technical meetings as needed. Prepare agreed technical inputs and briefing points, document discussion outcomes, and share relevant opportunities and follow-up actions with the Technical Lead and programme teams.

**Functional Relationship with the Livelihood Coordinator**

The two positions are complementary:

**Livelihood Coordinator > Programme Implementation**

• oversight of implementation;

• coordination with operational departments;

• implementation planning and follow-up;

• resolution of operational issues;

• ensuring delivery of program activities.

**Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator > Programme Quality / Technical Function**

• technical quality;

• methodology and tools;

• technical monitoring;

• analysis and learning;

• technical capacity development;

• program improvement;

• technical input into program design.

**Development of the Role**

The position of Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator is being created to strengthen PIN Ukraine's technical capacity in the field of economic recovery.

As the economic recovery program portfolio expands, the position may gradually take on responsibility for specific technical areas or thematic components, including coordination of particular technical strands across multiple projects.

The role may also evolve toward greater responsibility for technical coordination, quality assurance, program development, and technical representation, depending on program needs and demonstrated performance.

**Team and Partner Capacity Development**

• Identify technical capacity needs of teams and partners and agree development activities with the Technical Lead.

• Deliver technical onboarding, refresher training, and mentoring on economic recovery methodologies and tools. Use practical exercises and programme examples, gather participant feedback, and provide follow-up support to help staff apply the tools consistently.

• When requested, support technical recruitment, preparation of terms of reference, and assessment of candidates’ technical skills; this does not imply line management.

• Provide technical guidance to PIN partners, support monitoring of their programme quality, and facilitate knowledge sharing.

**Documentation and Application of Learning**

• Document lessons learned, good practices, and research findings; prepare technical materials, recommendations, and internal updates.

• With MEAL, support review of baseline and endline tools and use evidence to improve programmes.

**Inclusion, Environmental Sustainability, and Accountability**

• Integrate age, gender, diversity, equality, non-discrimination, and do-no-harm principles into technical approaches and selection criteria.

• Under the Technical Lead’s guidance, support environmental sustainability and climate resilience in relevant economic recovery activities.

• Ensure accountability through appropriate communication and information sharing within PIN and with partners and communities.

• Comply with PIN policies and procedures, including Finance, Logistics, HR, and Security; report identified technical risks to the relevant responsible staff.

**Qualification Criteria:**

**Education and Speciality:**

Higher education in economics, development studies, business administration, agriculture, social sciences, or a related field.

**Required Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong analytical and methodological skills. Ability to conduct field visits, assessments, and technical monitoring. Skills in preparing technical recommendations, reports, tools, and training materials. Ability to advise teams without taking over implementation management functions. Strong communication and coordination skills. Fluency in Ukrainian and working proficiency in English.

**PIN OFFERS**:

- A competitive salary according to the People in Need salary scale in amount of **1882 EUR Gross (Based on qualifications) + 3% after probation period.**
- Opportunities for professional development through various capacity-building activities, including trainings, workshops, and seminars.
- 28 calendar days of annual leave, plus 3 additional New Year bonus leave days.
- Health insurance — becomes effective after completion of the first month of the probationary period.
- Life insurance — effective from the first day of employment, 24/7, providing additional financial protection for employees and their families.
- Possibility to work one day per week remotely for office-based staff.
- Coverage of accommodation and per diem costs for work-related travel outside the assigned office region and/or in cases of excessive travel distance or time, in accordance with People in Need travel policy.
- Provision of a laptop, mobile phone (including prepaid SIM cards), and People in Need branded items (backpack, thermal mug, notebook, portable power bank).
- People in Need offices are equipped with all necessary security and energy-resilience measures, ensuring uninterrupted internet access.
- Free coffee, tea, milk, and water available in all offices.
- A multicultural and friendly working environment, with approximately 400 staff members in the Ukraine programme.

**Application procedure:**

Please send clearly marked CV and Motivation letter in English. Please note, only the shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Written test and interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis and the vacancy will be closed when filled.

Please note that PIN does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process.

*We support the principles of inclusiveness and non-discrimination in the selection process. You can submit an anonymized resume - without specifying your name, age, gender, photo or other personal data. Such resumes will be reviewed on a general basis in accordance with professional experience and qualifications.*

jobs.title: Training Officer, Cultural Orientation
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Training Officer, Cultural Orientation for Switchboard, an Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded program. Switchboard is a one-stop resource hub for refugee service providers in the United States. Switchboard provides training and capacity-building services to service providers in the United States, including resettlement agencies and affiliates, state agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others. More information about Switchboard can be found at [www.SwitchboardTA.org](https://reliefweb.int/file:///C:UsersTigestCoAppDataLocalMicrosoftOlkAttachmentsooa-fefcb179-4b91-4707-b044-59e9496f57fe69780562696ebcadf2340c5c93711aeb96e9493d8b84ea912d714b7dd9c61fdbwww.SwitchboardTA.org).

Settle In is Switchboard's digital information service for newcomers taking the knowledge and resources Switchboard offers to service providers and adapting and delivering it directly to newcomers**,** in multiple languages, through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on https://www.settleinus.org/.

Cultural orientation is a core service in refugee resettlement in the United States, helping newcomers build the knowledge and skills to navigate life in their new communities. The Training Officer, Cultural Orientation, leads the development and delivery of capacity-building initiatives for these programs. This includes training and technical assistance (TTA) to service providers, helping them build strong cultural orientation programs and apply best practices when working with newcomers. This staff member is responsible for producing and maintaining high-quality performance by collaborating with experts, designing effective cultural orientation resources such as curricula, training materials, and learning tools, and facilitating learning experiences that improve outcomes for newcomer children, adults, and families. This role requires hands-on experience working directly with clients, subject matter experts, and partners, along with prior experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Training and Technical Assistance**

- Design and deliver versatile cultural orientation training to service providers and cultural orientation delivery staff.
- Provide responsive and cross-disciplinary technical assistance to refugee service providers in response to cultural orientation TTAs, adapting content to meet varied organizational needs and learning styles.
- In collaboration with colleagues across teams, develop written and multimedia learning resources (e.g., toolkits, videos, podcasts) that reflect trauma-informed, client-centered, and strength-based approaches.
- Adapt materials for different literacy levels, languages, and cultural contexts
- Integrate feedback from internal and external reviewers to continuously improve training and resource contents and delivery methods.
- Facilitate communities of practice and peer learning groups to promote knowledge exchange and cross-training across service areas.

**Project Management**

- Contribute to the creation of Switchboard’s annual training and technical assistance (TTA) workplan.
- Ensure related trainings and learning resources are developed and delivered on time and on budget.
- Use effective communication and collaborative skills with a wide range of stakeholders
- Manage internal and external subject matter expert/consultant relationships and project plans as they contribute to the development of related TTA.

**Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E)**

- Oversee tracking of related TTA outputs and outcomes against targets (materials developed, trainings delivered, individuals participating, etc.)
- Together with Training Officers and Switchboard’s M&E team, review and analyze feedback data from related TTA participants
- Oversee provision of inputs into Switchboard reports, including monthly activity updates and semi-annual Performance Progress Reports.

- Other duties as assigned

**Job Requirements:**

**Required:**

- Bachelor's degree required, preferably in a related field such as Education, International Development, Social Work, Public Administration, Cross-Cultural Studies, Migration/Refugee Studies, or a related social science (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum 6 years of direct service experience with refugees and/or other ORR-eligible populations
- Experience delivering cultural orientation to newcomers
- Experience providing training and/or technical assistance to build the capacity of refugee service providers
- Experience providing client-centered, trauma-informed, and strength-based services for refugees
- Experience in supporting newcomers' access and gaining self-sufficiency for services and resources i.e. financial, medical, social, vocational etc.

**Preferred:**

- Lived experience with forced displacement or shared background with newcomer populations
- Experience managing external subject matter experts and/or consultants
- Experience contributing to project M&E (data collection, management, and reporting)
- Experience with evidence-based programming

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

- Working knowledge of programs and services related to client-centered services for refugees and newcomer families
- Strong understanding of cultural orientation frameworks, refugee/newcomer integration principles, and adult learning principles
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with fluency in English; including engaging public speaking abilities
- Self-starter with ability to work both independently and collaboratively as a part of a team
- Capacity to give and receive constructive feedback
- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines and efficient time management
- Adequate technology literacy including intermediate knowledge of MS Office Suite (Teams, Word, PowerPoint, Excel), and Zoom, with adaptability to learning new and innovative technology.
- Strong attention to detail

***Language Skills:*** Fluent in written and spoken English***.***

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $80,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: P&C Compliance Sr Specialist
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:**

The P&C Employment Compliance Manager is the organization's designated subject matter expert and primary focal point for U.S. employment compliance — spanning Form I-9/E-Verify, background screening, EEO/EEOC compliance, and Employee Handbook and HR policy governance. This role exists to move IRC from a reactive, administrative approach to employment compliance toward a proactive, audit-ready one — particularly given IRC's workforce naturally includes a significantly higher proportion of employees with non-native immigration backgrounds than a typical U.S. employer, which elevates both the stakes and the complexity of getting this right.

This role is designed to make the jobs of P&C Partners easier, not to displace or duplicate them. By owning the standards, tools, training, audit processes, and regulatory tracking that P&C Partners currently have to navigate on their own, this role frees them to focus on people-centered, relationship-driven work, while giving them a dedicated expert to call on for complex or gray-area compliance questions — and appropriately escalating matters that require legal interpretation or advice.

The right candidate moves fluidly between hands-on execution — personally completing I-9 reverifications and audits, and serving as the final checkpoint before Tier 1 submits new-hire verifications — and enterprise-level program leadership: building the compliance frameworks, quality controls, vendor relationships, reporting structures, and training curricula that keep the organization audit-ready at all times. This is a deep practitioner role for someone interested in a career in this space, not a legal role — a law degree is not required.

While the role's deepest ownership sits with U.S. compliance given the concentration of legal complexity here, it also maintains lightweight visibility into policy currently across IRC's global operations.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Employment Eligibility, I-9 & Background Screening Compliance**

- Own the organization's I-9 program end-to-end: set policy, standards, and process, and serve as the final review and confirmation point before Tier 1 submits new-hire I-9 verifications
- Personally complete all I-9 reverifications (e.g., work authorization renewals) and manage reverification timelines and tracking
- Design and deliver training and certification for everyone completing new-hire I-9 verifications (currently Tier 1 HR Operations), and serve as their go-to point of confirmation before submission when questions arise
- Conduct regular internal I-9 audits — including audits of Tier 1's completed verifications — and prepare the organization to respond to any government inspection or Notice of Inspection with confidence
- Own and oversee the U.S. background screening program, including process governance, vendor management, and continuous improvement, ensuring compliance with applicable federal, state, and local requirements, including the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA)
- Own the Workday ↔ HireRight integration, coordinating with HR Technology, Talent Acquisition, and the vendor to ensure the integration meets compliance and operational requirements, and manage any future changes or new requirements as they arise

**Multistate Compliance & Regulatory Tracking**

- Maintain a living compliance matrix of federal, state, and local employment law obligations across all U.S. operating locations, including state-specific holidays, paid family leave requirements, and other jurisdiction-specific nuances
- Maintain clear visibility into where employees are located by state, so compliance obligations can be mapped accurately as the distributed workforce evolves
- Partner with Payroll to monitor wage-and-hour compliance — including meal and rest break requirements and timekeeping accuracy — in high-risk states such as California, proactively closing gaps before they become costly
- Monitor regulatory changes and proactively update policies, handbooks, and practices before deadlines take effect

**EEO / EEOC Compliance**

- Serve as the HR Operations focal point for EEO/EEOC-related compliance and reporting, including EEO-1/Affirmative Action Plan obligations and applicable state-level equivalents (e.g., New Jersey), monitoring where federal requirements have lapsed but state requirements may still apply
- Own California Pay Data Reporting (SB 1162) — coordinating with Payroll and People Analytics to compile accurate pay band, race/ethnicity, and sex data by job category, and managing the annual submission to California's Civil Rights Department ahead of the required deadline
- Coordinate EEO-1 reporting — data collection, validation, and submission — in partnership with People Analytics, HR Technology, and Payroll to ensure data integrity and reporting readiness
- Coordinate responses to EEOC-related requests, inquiries, or audits in partnership with Legal

**Audit, Quality Control & Vendor Management**

- Establish and execute a regular internal audit cadence across all compliance domains, identifying gaps and remediating errors before they escalate
- Manage relevant HR compliance vendors (background screening, I-9/E-Verify, and related third-party providers), monitoring performance and ensuring consistent application of compliance processes
- Identify opportunities to automate, streamline, and standardize compliance-related processes in partnership with HR Technology

**Policy and Handbook Currency**

- Own the review and update cycle for U.S. employment policies and the employee handbook, ensuring alignment with current federal, state, and local law across all jurisdictions, including state-specific and local addenda and the NY State/NYC regulatory environment
- Own a central repository for all P&C policies, driving a regular review cadence with each policy's subject-matter owner (Compensation, Benefits, Recruitment, etc.) to confirm currency and surface any conflicts between policies for resolution by the relevant owners — this role owns the system and process, not the content of policies outside employment law
- Partner with HR Communications to effectively communicate policy and handbook changes to employees and managers
- Maintain a lightweight annual review cycle for handbooks across IRC's non-U.S. operations — collecting the most current version from each country and flagging any that are overdue for update — without taking on deep ownership of non-U.S. policy content

**P&C Partner Enablement & Reporting**

- Act as a standing SME resource for P&C Partners, fielding compliance questions and providing guidance on complex or gray-area cases, and identifying the appropriate process, policy, resource, or escalation path
- Develop FAQs, guidance materials, tools, and job aids that enable P&C Partners to independently navigate common compliance questions
- Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting for HR leadership and General Counsel on compliance status, open items, training completion rates, and emerging regulatory risk

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience); law degree not required
- 5–8+ years of experience in U.S. employment and labor law compliance, with demonstrated expertise in Form I-9, E-Verify, and multistate regulatory environments
- Demonstrated experience managing background screening programs and working knowledge of FCRA requirements
- Experience supporting EEO/EEOC compliance and reporting, including EEO-1 reporting; experience with state-level pay data or pay equity reporting (e.g., California SB 1162) is a plus
- Proven experience working with employees across diverse immigration statuses, including refugees, SIV holders, parolees, green card holders, visa holders, and naturalized citizens
- Track record of building or significantly maturing a compliance program, not just maintaining one
- Experience designing and delivering compliance training for non-legal audiences, including certifying frontline staff to perform compliance-sensitive tasks
- Experience with HRIS platforms and HR technology; Workday experience strongly preferred
- Experience managing HR compliance vendors and third-party providers
- SHRM-CP/SCP, PHR/SPHR, or a specialist certification in immigration or I-9 compliance is a plus

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Strong working knowledge of FLSA, Title VII, FMLA, ADA, PWFA, OSHA, WARN Act, and applicable state and local equivalents, particularly New York State and NYC
- Ability to work independently, exercise sound judgment, and operate with credibility across all levels of the organization
- Strong diplomatic and relationship-building skills, able to guide and influence without formal authority over the teams they support
- Comfortable moving between hands-on casework and enterprise-level program building

**Working Environment:**

Standard office working environment with the ability to work remote 2-3 days per week.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $95,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Communications Officer
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
Communications Officer

Full-time: 37.5 hours per week

Line managed by: Communications Manager

Salary: starting at £29,000

Location: London, UK – hybrid with at least 2 days in GISF’s London office

## About GISF

The Global Interagency Security Forum (GISF) is a member-led NGO network working to strengthen security risk management across the humanitarian and development sectors. With over 150 member organisations, GISF provides resources, convening spaces, and expertise to help keep aid workers safe.

GISF also leads communications for several strategic initiatives and delivers a programme of events, campaigns, and resources that strengthen NGO security risk management.

## About the role

We’re looking for an enthusiastic and organised Communications Officer to join our friendly team. This is a varied and hands-on role that would suit someone who enjoys working with people, is confident communicating with different audiences, and is keen to strengthen their skills across digital communications, content, and events.

The Communications Officer is responsible for the day-to-day delivery of GISF’s digital communications and content. Working closely with the Communications Manager and colleagues across GISF, the postholder will manage GISF’s digital channels, produce, and publish engaging content, and support communications for GISF’s programmes, events, publications, and campaigns.

A key focus of the role is strengthening GISF’s use of digital communications and data. The postholder will monitor performance across GISF’s website, social media, and email channels, using analytics and audience insights to understand what is working and inform continuous improvements to content and channel delivery.

As part of a small Secretariat, the postholder will work across multiple projects and priorities and will need to be organised, proactive, and comfortable taking ownership of day-to-day communications delivery. The postholder will work closely with colleagues across GISF to help deliver engaging communications and to ensure our members, supporters and stakeholders stay informed and connected.

## Key responsibilities

### Digital communication and content creation

- Manage the day-to-day delivery of GISF’s digital communications across its website, social media, newsletters, and member-only community platform.
- Plan, produce, schedule, and publish digital content, adapting messaging, format, and presentation for different audiences and channels.
- Gather stories, case studies, and updates from colleagues, members, and community partners, and explore creative and multimedia approaches to communicating GISF’s work.
- Help maintain GISF’s social media channels, creating simple graphics and promotional materials using Canva and existing templates.
- Keep up to date with social media trends, platform developments, and best-practice techniques, applying learning to strengthen content and drive audience engagement.
- Manage the production and delivery of GISF’s newsletters and other email communications, including building and scheduling campaigns and maintaining mailing lists and audience segments.
- Deliver engaging communications to GISF members, working closely with the Membership/Engagement team to ensure members receive timely and relevant information about GISF activities, opportunities, and resources.

### Analytics and digital performance

- Monitor and analyse performance across GISF’s website, social media and email channels, producing regular reporting against agreed objectives and KPIs.
- Use analytics and audience insights to understand audience behaviour and inform improvements to content, formats, targeting, timing and channel delivery.
- Support the Communications Manager to evaluate communications activities and strengthen GISF’s approach to measuring communications performance and impact.
- Keep abreast of developments in digital communications, platforms and tools, identifying opportunities to strengthen GISF’s digital communications.

### Events and communications delivery

- Support the planning and delivery of events, workshops, and community engagement activities, helping with registrations, event materials, presentations, signage, and promotional resources.
- Help coordinate practical arrangements with venues, suppliers, digital agencies, and colleagues.
- Gather feedback from participants to inform future events and communications.
- Support the delivery and dissemination of GISF research and publications, including coordinating copyediting, design, and other production processes where required
- Ensure communications outputs consistently meet GISF’s editorial, brand and accessibility standards.
- Work collaboratively with colleagues across GISF to coordinate communications requirements, deadlines, and inputs.
- Help keep communications templates and shared documents organised and up to date, and support consistent ways of working.
- Respond to, or route, general communications queries received through GISF’s shared inboxes.
- Undertake other duties as may reasonably be required, consistent with the level and purpose of the role.

## Person specification

### Essential experience and skills

- Experience creating digital communications, gained through employment, internships, volunteering, freelance work or other relevant settings.
- Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear and engaging content for different audiences and digital channels.
- Strong visual communication and design skills, with experience creating engaging graphics and digital content using tools such as Canva or Adobe Creative Suite.
- Creativity and a strong visual eye, with the ability to develop engaging content ideas and present information in accessible ways.
- An understanding of digital communications and how websites, social media, and email can be used to reach and engage different audiences
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
- Ability to work collaboratively and communicate effectively with colleagues and external stakeholders.
- Enthusiastic, with a can-do attitude and a willingness to learn, and an ability to build positive relationships with a wide range of people, including members, partners and colleagues.
- Confidence and technical know-how for using digital tools and learning new systems.

### Desirable experience and skills

- A degree in Communications or related qualifications
- Experience working in, or an interest in, the humanitarian, development, charity or NGO sector.
- Experience using website content management systems, email marketing platforms, or digital analytics tools
- Experience producing or editing video, photography, or other multimedia content.
- Experience creating content for social media, websites or newsletters, or supporting events and community activities.
- Familiarity with website CMS systems, social media scheduling tools, CRM systems, newsletter platforms and event platforms such as Eventbrite.

### What we offer

- 25 days of annual leave increasing annually after 2 years, up to a maximum 30 days (plus bank holidays)
- Office shutdown between Christmas and New Year
- Employer Pension contributions
- A focus on professional development, including access to overseas events, workshops; and CharityComms membership for training and development opportunities, mentoring, events, resources and networking with communications professionals across the charity sector.

jobs.title: Human Resources Payroll Associate (G.5)
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
## Purpose of the Post

Under the supervision of the Senior Human Resources Officer and close coordination with the HR Officer (Entitlements and Information Management), the incumbent supports the accurate, timely, and compliant administration of payroll, compensation, benefits, and staff entitlements, contributing to the effective delivery of high-quality human resources services.

### Required Competencies

- Ability to plan, organize and prioritize a high volume of tasks/transactions and manage time efficiently to meet deadlines.
- Thoroughness and meticulous attention to detail, ensuring accuracy of output.
- Ability to work effectively under pressure with a hands-on and solutions-oriented approach.
- Effective oral and written communication skills, with the ability to provide clear guidance and explain complex payroll concepts and processes in a concise and understandable manner to diverse audiences.
- Ability to work harmoniously, build and maintain effective working relationships with staff at all levels in a multicultural team.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and to deal tactfully in all situations and interactions.

### Professional Experience

A minimum of six years of relevant experience in payroll, HR, and social security/pension administration, or related areas are essential. Experience with an international Organization, especially within the United Nations Common System, would be an asset.

### Education

A minimum of completed secondary education is required for this role. A qualification in finance or human resources (payroll) would be an added advantage.

### Language Skills

Complete proficiency in English (oral and written), including ability to draft clearly and concisely. Working knowledge of any other UN languages would be an asset.

### Other Skills

Ability to effectively use MS Office tools (Windows, Word, Power Point, Excel and standard database software). Working knowledge of SharePoint, and an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system such as SAP, Umoja, PeopleSoft or similar Payroll/HR ERP is desirable.

## Main Duties and Responsibilities

The successful candidate would provide a broad range of administrative, HR (including payroll), and financial support to the team. The incumbent will:

- Create, maintain staff appointments and related personnel data in SAP, applying the appropriate salary, benefits and entitlements for different staff categories in accordance with applicable rules and procedures.
- Liaise with the Workforce Planning team to ensure the timely transmission of all required documentation for the smooth appointment and onboarding of staff.
- Respond to staff queries on all payroll-related matters and escalate to appropriate officers in cases of complex queries.
- Prepare staff cost estimates for incoming Junior Professional Officers (JPOs) and Senior Professional Officers (SPOs) based on Member States’ requirements and their Memorandum of Understanding (MoU).
- Administer and monitor compensation and benefits actions, ensuring timely and accurate payroll processing of staff status changes, including within-grade increases, promotions, and seasonal ticket loans as applicable.
- Create and administer health insurance-related-payroll records and process related changes for newly appointed, serving and retired staff members.
- Ensure all entitlements changes are processed before the payroll cutoff date and create entries for all payroll actions in the SAP log.
- Administer staff separations and end-of-service benefits, including separation processing, repatriation-related entitlements, payment of unused annual leave and recovery or referral of outstanding obligations, as applicable.
- Conduct thorough reviews of supporting documentation to determine staff entitlement and eligibility in accordance with the Staff Regulations and Staff Rules and escalate complex cases as required.
- Coordinate with the external pension administrators and other relevant stakeholders on pension-related notifications, deductions, separations and staff queries, within established procedures.
- Maintain accurate, secure and confidential payroll and personnel records in accordance with applicable information-management and data-protection requirements.
- Assist in the onboarding of newly recruited staff members.
- Contribute to initiatives, projects, and activities of Human Resources Services.
- Perform other duties, as may be required

## **Contract Information**

\*Local status requires applicants to have unhindered permission to live and work in the UK.

jobs.title: Project Officer, Slovenia (Europe and Asia)
source: Geneva Centre for Security Sector Governance
jobs.body:
At DCAF, we envision a world where democratic sector governance advances sustainable peace and development and human dignity for all.

Our mission is to advance the security of all people through nationally owned, inclusive, and participatory security sector reforms based on international norms and good practices.

DCAF contributes to making peace and development more sustainable by assisting partner states and international actors supporting these states, to improve the governance of their security sector through inclusive and participatory reforms. It creates innovative knowledge products, promotes norms and good practices, provides legal and policy advice and supports capacity‐building of both state and non‐state security sector stakeholders.

DCAF Ljubljana is a permanent DCAF regional office, based in Slovenia. The office is responsible for two main programmes: implementation of the Police Cooperation Convention for Southeast Europe (PCC SEE) and the Western Balkans Border Security Programme (BSP). With funding from the United Kingdom Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO), DCAF Ljubljana is implementing the “CHAIN BiH” project, which aims to strengthen sub-national case-building and inter-agency coordination against organised immigration crime (OIC) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a focus on Una-Sana Canton. DCAF Ljubljana is looking to employ a motivated, well-organised and positive individual to be our next **Project Officer (Europe and Asia).**

**Location: DCAF Ljubljana, Slovenia, with frequent travel to Bosnia and Herzegovina \***

**Starting date: November 2026 or upon agreement**

**Work rate: 100%**

**Duration: Fixed-term employment until 31 March 2029, with the possibility of extension \*\***

**The role**

Join DCAF Ljubljana as a Project Officer, supporting the implementation of the project “CHAIN BiH”. Reporting to the Project Manager, you will be responsible for the operational, logistical, administrative and financial support of project activities, and will contribute to monitoring, evaluation and learning, reporting and coordination with national and cantonal partners in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

**Key areas of operation**

**Project implementation support**

- Support the Project Manager in the planning, organisation and day-to-day implementation of project activities, including workshops, trainings, field visits, working meetings and meetings of the Practice Review Forum.
- Manage the logistical and administrative preparation of activities, including travel, venues, interpretation and translation, participant lists and procurement of goods and services, in line with DCAF procedures.
- Prepare background materials, agendas, presentations, minutes and summary notes of meetings and activities.
- Support the evidence-gathering and diagnostic work of the project, including the collection, organisation and basic analysis of information from the field.

**Coordination and communication**

- Maintain regular contact with focal points in partner institutions, external experts and service providers.
- Support the organisation of the participation of officers from EU Member States within the framework of the PCC SEE.

**Financial and administrative management**

- Monitor project expenditure against the approved budget in close cooperation with the Project Manager and the DCAF finance and administration team.
- Prepare, verify and file financial documentation, contracts, invoices and supporting documents in compliance with donor and DCAF requirements.
- Keep project documentation and records complete, accurate and audit-ready.

**Monitoring, reporting and visibility**

- Collect and maintain monitoring data against project indicators, including sex- and age-disaggregated data, and support the documentation of lessons learned.
- Contribute to the preparation of narrative and financial reports for the donor and DCAF management.

The Europe and Asia Entity at DCAF works across Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus, Central Asia and other parts of Europe and Asia, providing policy advice, capacity-building, technical assistance and support to institutional reforms. Its work covers areas such as democratic oversight, accountability, integrity and anti-corruption, human rights, defence and security governance, and institutional resilience, working closely with governments, parliaments, security institutions, civil society and international partners. For our country office in Kyiv, Ukraine, we are looking for a highly-motivated and dynamic individual to be our next **Project Officer – MEAL (Europe and Asia).**

The position strengthens evidence-based programme management by ensuring that implementation progress, results and expenditure are consistently tracked against approved objectives, outputs and activities.

The main objective of the position is to support the effective implementation of DCAF’s MEAL framework across the Ukraine programme, with a particular focus on results-based management and programme performance. jobs.title: Head of Support Services
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Head of Support Services

Location : Remote

Job Type: Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Head of Support Services provides strategic leadership and oversight of INARA’s global finance and operational support systems across all country operations and legal entities. The role ensures strong financial management, compliance, internal controls, budgeting coherence, donor financial accountability, and organizational financial sustainability.

The post-holder serves as the central finance oversight function between Headquarters and Country Offices, ensuring that financial systems, reporting processes, fund management, and accounting practices operate in alignment with donor requirements, organizational policies, and applicable regulatory frameworks.

The role also supervises finance staff across country operations, supports organizational audits and compliance obligations, oversees financial systems optimization, and strengthens institutional financial management capacity across the organization.

**Key Responsibilities**

Key responsibilities include and may not be limited to:

1. **Financial Planning and Budget Oversight**

The Head of Support Services leads organizational budgeting processes and ensures financial planning aligns with operational realities and strategic priorities.

Tasks:

- Review and consolidate annual organizational budgets and donor project budgets from all country operations
- Ensure consistency between programmatic plans, operational priorities, and financial forecasts
- Validate budget assumptions including exchange rates, inflation projections, staffing costs, and operational estimates
- Review cost allocations across grants, shared costs, and general organizational operations
- Support Country Offices and program teams in developing realistic and compliant donor budgets
- Ensure budget structures align with donor regulations and internal financial controls
- Monitor overall organizational financial sustainability and resource allocation

Key Competencies:

- Strong financial planning and budgeting expertise
- Advanced analytical and forecasting skills
- Understanding of donor budgeting requirements
- Strategic financial oversight capacity

1. **Fund Management and Financial Oversight**

The role oversees organizational fund management processes and ensures financial liquidity and accountability across all operations.

Tasks:

- Oversee inter-office fund transfers and HQ financial allocations
- Review and approve fund requests from Country Offices
- Monitor cash flow, liquidity, and financial reserve levels
- Monitor foreign exchange exposure and associated financial risks
- Ensure donor funds are utilized in accordance with approved budgets and restrictions
- Track organizational spending thresholds and authorization compliance
- Support the CEO on high-level financial decision-making and risk management

Key Competencies:

- Strong treasury and cash-flow management skills
- Financial risk management expertise
- Understanding of multi-country fund management
- Strong attention to accountability and financial control

1. **Expenditure Management and Internal Controls**

The Head of Support Services ensures organizational expenditures comply with internal policies, donor regulations, and approval frameworks.

Tasks:

- Review expenditures above approved authorization thresholds and submit to the CEO for final approval where required
- Review complex procurement packages including competitive bidding documentation and vendor justifications
- Ensure expenditures comply with donor restrictions and organizational policies
- Monitor implementation of internal control procedures across all country operations
- Identify and address financial control weaknesses and operational risks
- Ensure procurement and expenditure documentation is audit-ready and properly archived

Key Competencies:

- Strong internal control and compliance knowledge
- Procurement and donor compliance understanding
- Risk identification and mitigation skills
- Attention to detail and accountability

1. **Accounting, Reconciliation, and Financial Systems Oversight**

The role ensures the accuracy, integrity, and efficiency of organizational accounting systems and financial records.

Tasks:

- Oversee organizational accounting and bookkeeping processes across all country operations
- Ensure financial entries, reconciliations, and classifications are accurate and completed on time
- Review month-end and year-end closing processes
- Conduct periodic spot checks of financial records and supporting documentation
- Ensure bank reconciliations and petty cash reconciliations are completed accurately and on schedule
- Supervise organizational use of QuickBooks Online (QBO)
- Coordinate with system consultants on QBO structure optimization and reporting systems
- Maintain oversight of chart of accounts, donor classes, and financial coding structures

Key Competencies:

- Advanced accounting and bookkeeping knowledge
- Strong financial systems management skills
- QBO proficiency and oversight experience
- Strong reconciliation and audit trail management skills

1. **Financial Reporting and Donor Compliance**

The role oversees organizational financial reporting processes and ensures compliance with donor and regulatory requirements.

Tasks:

- Consolidate financial data from all country operations into organizational financial reports
- Review and validate donor financial reports prior to submission to the CEO and donors
- Ensure financial reports meet donor formatting, compliance, and deadline requirements
- Review budget versus actual (BvA) reports and variance explanations
- Provide structured feedback to Country Offices on reporting quality and compliance gaps
- Ensure consistency between programmatic implementation and financial reporting
- Support donor financial reviews and due diligence processes

Key Competencies:

- Strong donor financial reporting expertise
- Financial analysis and variance interpretation skills
- Understanding of humanitarian donor compliance frameworks
- Strong organizational and coordination skills

1. **Audit, Compliance, and Organizational Risk Management**

The Head of Support Services leads financial compliance and audit coordination processes across all INARA operations.

Tasks:

- Maintain and update financial policies, SOPs, and internal control frameworks
- Coordinate external audits including donor audits, IRS filings, and independent organizational audits
- Ensure implementation and follow-up of audit recommendations
- Oversee submission of IRS Form 990 and other compliance-related financial filings
- Support compliance across INARA’s legal entities and jurisdictions
- Identify organizational financial risks and recommend mitigation measures
- Ensure compliance with donor regulations, anti-fraud standards, and applicable legal requirements

Key Competencies:

- Strong audit and compliance management experience
- Knowledge of nonprofit regulatory frameworks
- Risk management and governance expertise
- Strong policy development and implementation skills

1. **Systems Strengthening and Capacity Building**

The role strengthens organizational financial systems and supports finance staff development across all operations.

Tasks:

- Supervise and support Country Finance Leads and finance staff across all country operations
- Conduct finance staff performance evaluations and capacity development planning
- Organize training workshops and refresher sessions on financial procedures and systems
- Identify inefficiencies within financial systems and recommend improvements
- Support automation and financial process optimization initiatives
- Strengthen organizational financial documentation and reporting systems
- Promote standardization of financial practices across all country operations

Key Competencies:

- Leadership and staff management skills
- Capacity building and mentoring experience
- Systems improvement and problem-solving skills
- Strong coordination and communication abilities

**Key working relationships**

- CEO: Primary line manager and final financial approval authority
- Country Directors: Coordination on budgets, expenditures, and operational finance oversight
- Country Finance Leads: Technical supervision and financial management oversight
- Partnerships & Development Department: Coordination on proposal budgets and donor financial reporting
- Program Teams: Budget planning and financial monitoring support
- Auditors and External Consultants: Compliance, audit, and systems coordination
- SMT: Strategic financial planning and organizational decision-making

**THE POST-HOLDER WILL BE EXPECTED TO DEMONSTRATE MEASURABLE PROGRESS AGAINST THE FOLLOWING WITHIN THE FIRST SIX MONTHS:**

The post-holder will be expected to demonstrate measurable progress against the following within the first six MONTHS:

- Reporting validation process fully established and adhered to across all active country operations
- Zero reports submitted to Partnerships & Development without completed quality review
- SMT action tracker operational and actively maintained, with no overdue items going unescalated
- Entity documentation archive created and populated for all INARA legal entities
- Coordination gaps between Country Offices, Finance, and Partnerships & Development visibly reduced
- Positive feedback from Country Directors, Finance, and the CEO on coordination quality and turnaround times

**Requirements & Qualifications**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or related field
- Professional accounting qualification preferred

**Experience**

- Minimum 7 years of progressive finance and operational management experience
- Experience in humanitarian or nonprofit sector finance management
- Experience managing multi-country financial operations
- Strong knowledge of donor compliance and nonprofit financial systems
- Experience with QuickBooks Online and financial reporting systems

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

**Location: Amsterdam, Barcelona, Brussels, Geneva, Paris** (the candidates must hold a valid work authorisation in one of these locations)

**Starting date**: 01st of January 2027

**Deadline to apply:** 20th of October 2026

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract.

**I. MSF INTERNATIONAL**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation.

MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and other offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information, and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**II. CONTEXT**

The role of Travel Administrator involves managing the travel arrangements for MSF International staff based in various MSF entities. The role replaces that of the Travel Referent for all staff travel, liaising with the finance and procurement departments, MSF partner sections, decentralized hubs, the Global Procurement Unit, as well as external suppliers such as the AMEX travel agency and accommodation providers.

**III. PURPOSE OF THE JOB**

The Travel Administrator is responsible for booking and coordinating travel arrangements for MSF International staff, ensuring that travel services are delivered accurately, efficiently and in compliance with the Travel Policy. The role provides operational and administrative support to travellers and contributes to the smooth delivery of travel services across MSF International.

**IV. ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**Coordinate travel bookings and related travel services for MSF International staff, ensuring compliance with the Travel Policy and operational requirements.**

- Review travel requests for completeness and compliance.
- Book flights, trains, buses, accommodation and related travel services.
- Ensure travel arrangements meet traveller and organisational needs.

**Provide travel administration and traveller support throughout the travel process.**

- Advise travellers on travel procedures and documentation requirements.
- Support visa and travel preparation processes.
- Respond to travel-related queries and provide accurate travel information.

**Contribute to efficient and sustainable travel management.**

- Identify travel options that balance cost, duration, comfort and environmental impact.
- Apply the most appropriate booking channels according to organisational requirements.
- Promote responsible travel practices among travellers.

**Maintain travel records and support travel monitoring and reporting.**

- Update and maintain travel-related data and records.
- Consolidate information required for travel reporting and monitoring.
- Escalate irregularities or non-compliance with the Travel Policy

**V. AUTONOMY, COMPLEXITY**

**Autonomy**

Works within established procedures and the Travel Policy, organising travel bookings and managing competing priorities while referring exceptional situations to the Travel Referent

**Complexity**

Operates in an international and multicultural environment, coordinating with multiple stakeholders while balancing operational, administrative, budgetary and data protection requirements.

**VI. SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS FOR THE ROLE**

The incumbent is committed to contributing to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse, including those detailed in MSF’s Typologies of Abuse, and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it (without investigating it) to protect others.

**VII. REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Secondary education and relevant administrative training or equivalent professional experience.

Asset: Training in travel, tourism, business administration or a related field.

**Experience**

- Minimum 2 years' experience in travel administration, travel coordination, travel agency services or a similar role.
- Experience organising international travel arrangements.
- Experience working with multiple stakeholders and service providers.

Asset: Experience in an international and multicultural environment and/or the humanitarian sector.

**Knowledge**

- Knowledge of travel booking processes and travel administration.
- Understanding of international travel requirements, visas and travel documentation.
- Proficiency in travel booking systems, databases and standard IT applications.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Ability to prioritise workload and manage multiple requests.
- Effective written and verbal communication skills.

**Languages**

- Fluency in English; French is an advantage.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

**We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.**

**Note: All offers of employment will be subject to reference checks and to appropriate screening checks. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her/their understanding of these recruitment procedures.**

We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**
