jobs.title: Middle School Alliance Site Coordinator
jobs.body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:**

The Middle School Alliance (MSA) Site Coordinator provides day-to-day operational and administrative coordination for Out-of-School Time (OST) programming at assigned middle school sites, working within clearly defined procedures and under the general direction of MSA leadership. The coordinator carries out established site operations, logistics coordination, family engagement, and data-accountability tasks -- coordinating schedules and communication with program providers, volunteers, and site-based staff on clearly defined tasks, without formal responsibility for supervising their work -- and escalates unusual or non-routine issues to MSA leadership for resolution.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Site Operations & Program Coordination***

- Serve as the primary on-site coordinator responsible for overseeing daily MSA operations and implementation, including coordination of related logistics, schedules, and communication with program providers and site-based staff on clearly defined tasks.
- Coordinate daily program logistics including scheduling, room allocation, meal distribution, transportation coordination, dismissal procedures, and site transitions.
- Support scheduling and coordination of program providers to ensure alignment with site needs, school schedules, and MSA priorities.
- Monitor daily site operations to ensure programming is implemented with consistency, efficiency, and fidelity.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for site-based operational communication between school staff, providers, transportation, security, and MSA leadership.
- Troubleshoot routine operational challenges within established procedures and proactively communicate concerns and solutions, escalating unusual or non-routine issues to MSA leadership.
- Assist with coordination of site calendars, events, special activities, and school-based initiatives.
- Ensure site implementation aligns with MSA operational expectations, procedures, and standards.

***Student Recruitment & Family Engagement***

- Collaborate with the Manager of Partnerships & Community Engagement to support student recruitment and enrollment efforts.
- Support outreach and engagement efforts for students, families, teachers, and school personnel.
- Assist with family communication regarding programming schedules, attendance expectations, transportation updates, and special events.
- Promote inclusive access to OST opportunities and support student participation across diverse student populations.
- Build and maintain positive relationships with youth and families to encourage consistent engagement and participation.
- Support implementation of student and family engagement activities throughout the school year.

***Data Management & Reporting***

- Work closely with the Data & Evaluation Manager to support accurate and timely attendance tracking, data collection, and reporting.
- Monitor registration, attendance, participation trends, and Average Daily Attendance (ADA) data.
- Support implementation of evaluation tools, surveys, assessments, and data collection processes, including SAYO-Y and other program quality measures.
- Ensure site-based data systems and reporting procedures are completed accurately and consistently, following established formats and deadlines.
- Use data insights to identify operational challenges and support continuous improvement, in consultation with the Data & Evaluation Manager.
- Maintain organized and accurate records related to attendance, participation, case management, schedules, and operational documentation.

***Program Quality & Continuous Improvement***

- Collaborate with the Network Quality Manager to support implementation of NextUp quality standards and Youth Program Quality Initiative (YPQI) practices.
- Participate in professional development, coaching, training, and quality improvement activities.
- Support program providers in creating safe, engaging, and youth-centered learning environments.
- Monitor program implementation and communicate concerns related to quality, consistency, youth engagement, or operational effectiveness to MSA leadership.
- Gather and communicate feedback from youth, families, providers, and school staff to support continuous improvement.

***Relationship Management & Communication***

- Build and maintain collaborative relationships with school administrators, teachers, providers, families, community partners, and youth.
- Facilitate clear, timely, and professional communication between all stakeholders.
- Attend and support school-based meetings, provider meetings, site leadership meetings, trainings, and MSA planning meetings.
- Represent NextUp and the MSA professionally within school communities and partner spaces.

***Safety, Supervision & Risk Management***

- Support implementation and monitoring of established safety and supervision procedures during OST programming.
- Ensure students are properly supervised during transitions, programming, transportation, and dismissal.
- Maintain awareness of site safety concerns and communicate incidents promptly to MSA leadership.
- Assist with incident reporting, documentation, and follow-up procedures, per established protocols.
- Assist with emergency response coordination and communication when necessary, following established emergency procedures.

***Administrative & Organizational Support***

- Maintain organized operational records and documentation.
- Assist with inventory management, supply coordination, and site preparation.
- Support preparation of operational updates, reports, and presentations.
- Monitor implementation timelines, deadlines, and deliverables related to site operations.
- Follow site-based operational procedures and systems established by MSA leadership.

**Job Requirements:**

- Bachelor's degree is preferred in education, youth development, nonprofit management, public administration, social work, or a related field.
- Minimum of 2–3 years of related experience in youth development, education, afterschool programming, or community-based programming.
- Proficient in English and Spanish, both spoken and written.
- Experience working with middle school youth, school communities, or after-school programming strongly preferred.
- Experience with attendance tracking, data systems, and reporting processes preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Strong organizational, time management, and project coordination skills.
- Ability to manage day-to-day operational responsibilities and site-based priorities within clearly defined procedures, escalating exceptions to MSA leadership.
- Demonstrated ability to build collaborative relationships and function effectively within a team environment.
- Strong communication skills, both written and verbal in Spanish and English.
- Ability to solve problems, adapt, and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
- Knowledge of positive youth development and youth engagement practices preferred.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to high-quality implementation.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and database/data management systems preferred.
- Ability to exercise sound judgment and maintain professionalism in school and community settings.

**Working Environment:**

- Primarily an in-person, school-based environment across assigned middle school sites, with standard office/administrative time for planning and reporting.
- Hours during programming are 11am-7pm. Biweekly staff meetings are held at IRC office.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $28.94-$29.90/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

jobs.title: Business Development and Grants Manager
jobs.body:
**Country Programme:** Moldova

**Contract Length:** 1 year

**Base:** Chisinau

**Starting date**: September 2026

**Line Manager**: Deputy Head of Programmes

**People in Need (PIN)** is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has been providing humanitarian and development assistance worldwide since 1992. Today, PIN operates in more than 40 countries, responding to humanitarian crises and supporting long-term development through programmes in education, human rights, climate resilience, and social inclusion. As one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, PIN works across Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe to support vulnerable communities, strengthen civil society, and promote democratic values and human dignity.

## **About the Moldovan Programme of People in Need:**

People in Need (PIN) has been operating in Moldova since 2003, delivering development and humanitarian assistance across social protection and inclusion, civil society empowerment, agriculture and economic development. Following the escalation of the war in Ukraine in February 2022, PIN significantly scaled up emergency programming, including protection, cash assistance, education, winterization, and livelihoods support for refugees and host communities.

PIN Moldova currently manages a large and diverse portfolio of emergency and development projects implemented nationwide and funded by a range of institutional donors, while increasingly shifting toward long-term development assistance, particularly in the context of Moldova’s EU integration and the need to support local CSOs and line ministries in meeting EU accession commitments.

## **About the role:**

The Business Development and Grants Manager works closely with Programme, Grants, and Partnership teams to secure funding and build sustainable donor relations. The role drives strategic resource mobilization for the Country Programme – identifying, mapping, and pursuing donor opportunities aligned with the Country Programme’s strategic direction.

The position collaborates with Programme Leads in Moldova and HQ Technical Advisors and partners to co-create high-quality concept notes, pitches, and funding proposals, including leading complex multi-stakeholder proposals, and ensures that all concept notes and pitches reflect dignified, non-paternalistic narratives that respect local knowledge and partner expertise.

The role also ensures communication, with donors and maintains strong donor relationships through high-quality reporting and proactive relationship management, including with the Czech Embassy and the Czech Development Agency (CzDA), the European Union Delegation, and other current and prospective donors (e.g. GCF, U.S. Government donors, FCDO, and Swiss Cooperation, etc.). Additional responsibilities include supporting visits of international experts and study visits to countries outside Moldova, conducting institutional funding and proposal design, development and writing mentorship sessions for local team and local partners, and providing broader support to the Programme and Grants functions.

The Business Development and Grants Manager reports to the Deputy Head of Programmes and works in close cooperation with senior CP management (HoP/CD/HoSo/Head of MEAL) and relevant HQ departments.

The Business Development and Grants Manager supports the Grants and Reporting Team on grants health review and oversight, particularly on compliance and donor communications, and may also act as a secondary focal point for external liaison, including representing PIN vis-à-vis donors and in other coordination forums (clusters, working groups, etc.).

## **Main Duties and Responsibilities:**

**1. Strategic Pipeline Management and Donor Intelligence**

- Maintains and regularly updates the donor mapping and funding strategy, tracking funding trends and donor priorities, with particular attention to diversifying the portfolio into development sector in line with PIN’s Country Programme Strategy; keeps management informed of opportunities and strategic trends.
- Continuously monitors emerging and anticipated funding opportunities through donor websites, humanitarian assistance portals, clusters, and bilateral scoping with existing and potential donors; leads funding opportunity review (Go/No-Go) meetings.
- In coordination with the line manager and/or HoP, engages with donors during field visits to build and nurture relationships and promote PIN’s work in its strategic domains; documents donor intelligence and engagement efforts.
- Liaises with HQ funding advisors to strengthen donor knowledge and support proactive fundraising for the Country Programme.
- Maintains up-to-date grant files, donor guidelines, and resource materials, coordinating with relevant HQ desk colleagues.

**2. Proposal Development and Co-Creation**

- Collaborates with Programme Leads in Moldova and HQ Technical Advisors and partners to design high-quality concept notes, pitches, and funding proposals, facilitating a collaborative proposal-design process.
- Leads complex, multi-stakeholder proposals, coordinating the development process across all relevant departments — including supporting the design of logical frameworks, setting realistic and measurable targets, and supporting the development of narrative proposals and budgets.
- Ensures concept notes and proposals reflect dignified, non-paternalistic narratives that respect local knowledge and partner expertise.
- Supports proofreading and translation of proposals and budgets ahead of submission.

**3. Grants Compliance and Reporting Oversight**

- Supports the Grants and Reporting Team on grants health review and oversight, with particular focus on compliance and donor communications.
- Ensures reports meet donor requirements in structure and content, including mainstreaming issues (protection, gender, do-no-harm, conflict sensitivity), and that programme staff receive timely guidelines, templates, and examples to develop quality reporting contributions.
- Oversees compliance with donor guidelines on programme implementation, information collection and storage, and project deliverables.
- Maintains standardized reporting formats and an internal tracking database of reporting timelines by donor/grant, coordinating with the Deputy Head of Programmes, Programme/Project Managers, and MEAL to ensure timely, quality data collection and compilation.
- Drafts, proofreads and compiles interim and final donor reports.
- Prepares documentation and collects inputs from finance and programme teams to facilitate regular project review meetings, using standardized tools provided by PIN.
- Supports administration of project documentation in ELO and Navision (IRPs and other project documentation).

**4. Donor and Stakeholder Relations**

- Ensures communication, with donors and maintains strong donor relationships through high-quality reporting and proactive relationship management, including with the Czech Embassy and the Czech Development Agency (CzDA), the European Union Delegation, and other current and prospective donors (e.g. GCF, U.S. Government donors, FCDO, and Swiss Cooperation, etc.)
- Acts as a focal point for selected donors and grant contracts, both in external representation and in internal coordination with programme and operations teams on programme development and reporting matters.
- May act as secondary focal point for external liaison, representing PIN with donors and in other coordination forums (clusters, working groups, etc.).
- Supports visits of international experts to Moldova and study visits to countries outside Moldova, and coordinates and finalizes related documentation with the regional desk and CP senior management.

**5. FSTP Schemes, Subgranting and Partners Management**

- Oversees the design and set-up of Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP) schemes, ensuring the scheme’s objectives, eligibility criteria, and financial ceilings comply with EU and other donors’ grant agreement requirements.
- Leads or supports the launch of calls for proposals to sub-grantees (e.g., local CSOs, community structures), including drafting guidelines for applicants, organizing information sessions, and managing the selection and evaluation process.
- Coordinates capacity and due diligence assessments of prospective sub-grantees, ensuring findings inform award decisions, tailored support plans, and risk mitigation measures.
- Ensures sub-grant agreements are properly contracted, with clear deliverables, budgets, and reporting obligations, in line with PIN’s internal grant management policy and donor rules.
- Maintains a subgrant tracking system/database recording contract values, disbursement schedules, reporting deadlines, and compliance; flags, and provides regular updates to the line manager and relevant donors.
- Identifies and flags subgranting risks (financial, reputational, safeguarding) in a timely manner and proposes mitigation measures, including site visits and spot-checks as needed.
- Ensures proper close-out of sub-grants, including final financial and narrative reporting, asset verification/transfer where applicable, and archiving of documentation for audit purposes.

**6. Capacity Strengthening and Partner/Programme Support**

- Conducts institutional funding and proposal design, development and writing mentorship sessions for local team members and local partners.
- Provides general support, direction, and advice to staff as workload and time permit.
- Supports internal coordination of meetings and events.
- Updates the grants management tools provided by PIN and liaises with other departments (Finance, MEAL, etc.).
- Supports proofreading and translation of project documents during implementation.
- Compiles documentation and supports related administrative tasks as needed.

## **Main requirements:**

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in development and/or humanitarian programming, with demonstrated involvement in program and project implementation in Eastern Partnership or comparable contexts.
- At least 2 years of experience in senior or middle management roles, such as Program Manager, Portfolio Manager, or similar positions with responsibility for overseeing and supporting project teams.
- Proven experience in program and project design, program development, and preparation of project proposals for institutional donors.
- Solid experience in humanitarian and development sectors relevant to PIN Moldova's portfolio, such as civil society support, including governance, protection, social inclusion, livelihoods, education, agriculture, or climate resilience programming.
- Proven experience managing and coordinating multi-partner or consortium-based initiatives.
- Experience engaging and collaborating with governmental stakeholders, including representatives of central and local government institutions, and representing programs in institutional and policy dialogue.
- Experience supporting Project Managers across the full Project Cycle Management, including planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and project closure.
- Strong leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to guide, support, and coordinate Program Managers and Project Managers and engage effectively with donors, partners, and internal teams.
- Good contextual understanding of the Moldovan operating environment, including humanitarian needs, development challenges, and coordination mechanisms.
- Strong program planning and coordination skills, ensuring coherence between project objectives, donor requirements, work plans, and budgets.
- Proven ability to operate effectively in complex, high-pressure, and evolving environments, including emergency and politically sensitive contexts.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, enabling timely identification of implementation risks and support to practical, solutions-oriented responses.
- High commitment to quality programming, accountability, and continuous improvement, including the use of monitoring data to inform decision-making.
- Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, and accountability to affected populations, in line with PIN policies and humanitarian
- Languages – English - Fluent in all aspects

## **We Offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- **Salary & Benefits**: Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2900 - 3350 EURsuper gross (based on the assessment of the candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities and previous experience)
- **Additional allowances include**:
- - Monthly Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR; - Accommodation provided by PIN/Monthly Housing Allowance of up to 750 EUR;
- **Time off and Rest:**
- - 25 days of holiday annually; - 10 sick days
- **Travel benefits:**
- - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work; - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure; - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment; - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation;
- **Health and Well-being:**
- - 24/7 Medical Support available online; - Free psychological consultations available online;
- **Professional Development:** Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities;
- This positions is unaccompanied.

**Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Candidates will be assessed as applications are received, and the recruitment process may be closed before the stated deadline if a suitable candidate is identified.**

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager, Safety, Health & Wellness
jobs.body:
**Background:**

IRC Arizona operates Health, Safety, and Wellness programming across both the Phoenix and Tucson offices, addressing the health, safety, and stabilization needs of refugees, asylees, survivors of trafficking and torture, and other vulnerable populations. The Health Program addresses vulnerable populations' health needs through medical case management, health education, and public health interventions, working in collaboration with the healthcare sector, public health authorities, medical providers, facilities, universities, and community agencies. The Safety & Wellness Department provides therapeutic services, asylum casework, survivor support, anti-trafficking and victim services, and case management for individuals with acute safety and stabilization needs.

As IRC Arizona continues to rebuild and adapt to changing refugee arrivals, an uncertain federal funding environment, and evolving community needs, there is a growing need for statewide coordination across these programs. Rather than operating independently across Phoenix and Tucson, IRC Arizona can strengthen its statewide impact through a unified Safety, Health, and Wellness strategy that aligns resources, expands partnerships, builds staff capacity, and improves outcomes for clients and communities in both offices.

**Job Overview:**

The Senior Program Manager for Safety, Health & Wellness provides unified, statewide program oversight, staff supervision, partnership development, and grant maintenance for IRC Arizona's Health and Safety & Wellness programs across both Phoenix and Tucson. This position maintains service provision and contract compliance for Therapeutic Services, Asylum Casework, Survivors of Torture, Anti-Trafficking and Victim Services, the Arizona Asylum Network, Preferred Communities, medical case management (Program Initial Resettlement, Matching Grant, and Refugee Support Services), and public health and health literacy programming. This position builds a shared statewide strategy that strengthens program quality, expands partnerships and diversified funding, and coordinates growth and shared learning across both offices, while preserving the ability of each office to respond to its community's distinct needs.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Statewide Strategy & Coordination**

- Serve as IRC Arizona's statewide point of coordination for Health and Safety & Wellness programming, aligning strategy, tools, and resources across Phoenix and Tucson without centralizing day-to-day office operations.
- Identify statewide and office-specific program priorities and support leadership in decisions about program investment, expansion, consolidation, or redesign.
- Create a shared framework for collaboration and shared program standards that promote consistency and quality while preserving local flexibility.
- Build and disseminate knowledge and analysis of local and national public health, safety, and wellness trends that affect IRC clients; act as IRC Arizona's subject matter expert on these issues.

**Program Oversight & Quality**

- Oversee Health and Safety & Wellness program staff in a manner that supports the exchange of ideas, encourages camaraderie and collaboration, and fosters professional development.
- Design strategies and frameworks to effectively operate programs and coordinate logistics for grant implementation, program subcontracts, and monitoring of grant activities across both offices.
- Implement, monitor, and provide ongoing training on a trauma-informed service model for Health and Safety & Wellness staff.
- Provide appropriate supervision and case coordination to ensure acute client needs are met in a timely and culturally appropriate manner across all programs.
- Monitor provision of services through regular and systematic file reviews, client interviews, and field visits to ensure compliance with donor requirements and delivery of quality services.
- Track budgets, program expenditures, and activities across programs; ensure donor deliverables are met; compile data and draft reports as required by donor and agency specifications.

**Program Development & Community Expansion**

- Support the development of new and expanded programming, including intensive case management, anti-human trafficking and survivor support services, behavioral health and psychosocial support, chronic disease prevention, maternal and child health, healthcare navigation, community health worker initiatives, and health education.
- Identify key stakeholders, partners, resources, donors, and volunteers to support program growth.
- Assess opportunities to responsibly adapt or expand select services to broader underserved populations whose needs overlap with those of IRC's existing clients, consistent with IRC's mission, policies, and operational capacity.
- Coordinate with other IRC teams to create multi-disciplinary approaches to services that facilitate the best possible client outcomes.

**Partnership & Funding Development**

- Build and maintain statewide relationships with state and local health agencies, FQHCs, hospital systems, universities, Medicaid health plans, behavioral health providers, law enforcement, community organizations, and philanthropic partners.
- Develop strategies to enhance community outreach and engage new stakeholders.
- Review, recommend, and write new grant opportunities in alignment with the office strategic action plan and in partnership with the Grants Manager, identifying federal, state, county, municipal, foundation, healthcare, and victim-services funding opportunities.
- Support diversification of funding to reduce dependence on refugee arrival levels or any single government funding stream.

**Staff Supervision & Development**

- Provide direct supervision to program supervisors and staff across the Health and Safety & Wellness departments (see Key Working Relationships).
- Provide coaching, leadership development, technical assistance, and opportunities for cross-office collaboration to strengthen local leadership and staff capacity.
- Provide supervision to AmeriCorps members, MSW interns, and volunteers associated with each program.

**Compliance & Organizational Commitment**

- Ensure coordination with the development and implementation of outreach and training activities to meet program outcomes.
- Participate in senior management meetings and staff development activities as requested.
- Role model IRC values and commitment to mission and clients.
- Comply with all IRC policies, procedures, and protocols, including the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Site Director, Tucson

**Position directly supervises:** TBD

**Position indirectly supervises:** N/A

**Indirect Reporting:** N/A

**Other Internal and/or external contacts:**

***Internal:** IRC staff, interns, and volunteers across Phoenix and Tucson*

***External:** Community partners, stakeholder partners, DES, law enforcement, medical providers, employers*

**Job Requirements:**

- Graduate degree in social work, public health, or a related field strongly preferred; undergraduate degree in social work or equivalent work experience required.
- At least 5 years of related professional experience, including proven skills supervising case management staff, grant reporting, and program development; multi-site or cross-program management experience preferred.
- Demonstrated experience with trauma-informed, victim-centered, and/or public health service models.
- Excellent written and spoken English skills; bilingual ability preferred.
- Strong organizational skills and detail oriented; excellent writing and analytical skills.
- Case management, victim's assistance, and/or workforce development experience preferred.
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Computer literacy; database experience preferred.
- Ability to work independently across multiple sites and be a flexible team player.
- Must have a valid driver's license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation to travel regularly between Phoenix and Tucson offices.
- Must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time within the service delivery area to perform the responsibilities outlined above.
- Regular travel between Phoenix and Tucson required; occasional domestic (non-local) travel required, up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $69,939 - $92,500/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Job Overview**

The Deputy Director, Supply Chain Business Development and Program Delivery is a senior global role responsible for making IRC's supply chains fit for scale across its most ambitious health and humanitarian programming commitments. The role is designed to translate strategic program targets into operational supply chain solutions that work at country level and ensuring country realities shape global supply chain strategy in return.

The role has three integrated areas of responsibility.

It serves as a primary GSC lead and contributor to business development: identifying, designing, and positioning supply chain funding opportunities with institutional and non-traditional donors, and leading supply chain sections of competitive proposals.

It provides support across IRC's Impact at Scale (I@S) thematic supply chains, driving end-to-end performance from demand planning and forecasting through sourcing, pre-positioning, and last-mile delivery.

It builds country and regional capacity to sustain health supply chain improvements over time, providing direct technical support, deploying to high-priority contexts, and harmonizing tools and SOPs across country programs in collaboration with Regional Supply Chain Directors (RSCDs) and other relevant Global Supply Chain (GSC) units and IRC stakeholder departments.

Reporting to the Director of Emergency and Health Supply Chain, the Deputy Director works in close collaboration with the Health Technical Unit, Global Procurement, Regional Supply Chain Directors, Country Programs, IT, Finance, and external partners including UNICEF, WHO, ECHO, and peer INGOs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Leadership for Program Delivery**

- The Deputy Director plays an active role in GSC’s business development (BD) function. Supply chain is an increasingly fundable programming area, with institutional donors such as ECHO, SIDA, Gates and non-traditional donors explicitly framing requirements around operational efficiency, commodity management, and supply chain innovation. Additionally, private and corporate donors have expressed specific interest in funding the optimization of health and emergency supply chains.
- Act as the primary GSC focal point within I@S agile working groups and cross-functional scaling teams, ensuring supply chain planning is embedded in program design from the outset and not treated as a downstream implementation task.
- Implement the strategic direction for cross-cutting supply chain enablers including pooled procurement, global pre-positioning frameworks, harmonized delivery models, and digital systems and oversee their development and rollout across priority country programs.
- Provide supply chain leadership and oversight for the addition of any new I@S Ready to Scale thematic areas, ensuring new commodities and delivery models are integrated into IRC's global supply chain architecture without creating fragmentation or duplication.
- Serve as GSC's coordinating focal point with the Research and Innovation Department, contributing to supply chain innovations including AI-enabled solutions.

**2. Business Development & Resource Mobilization**

- Is responsible for operationalizing the BD strategy, assembling inputs to create compelling bids, gap filling in the BD process as needed/relevant, and driving ultimate bid success through correct donor intel and positioning, strong bid submission, and effective cross-functional collaboration.
- Flag, track and route relevant funding opportunities to GSC Leadership and work closely with internal stakeholders to plan for staff needs and business development capacity requirements to successfully write and budget for winning bids based on the pipeline
- Lead or co-lead the technical design of supply chain sections for proposals where GSC has a primary role, including narrative writing, logical framework development, and supply chain costing.
- Collaborating with program and business development leads to embedding supply chain considerations into program design, with specific attention paid to Impact at Scale initiatives
- Contribute to bid assessment, probability-of-winning analysis, and positioning strategy for supply chain funding opportunities with specific focus on I@S thematic areas
- Develop and maintain GSC supply chain capability statements and value propositions relevant to I@S programming areas, for use in capture and proposal development.
- Participate in the BD review cycle for proposals with significant supply chain components, ensuring technical quality and alignment with IRC’s global supply chain strategy.
- Mobilize opportunities with non-traditional partners such as Airlink to improve program delivery and increase cost savings
- Take the lead with External relations and other fundraising teams to enable increased use of GIK goods and services, enabling program delivery whilst making IRC more cost effective.
- Build and maintain donor intelligence on supply chain funding streams
- Support pre-award activities including donor engagement, capture visits, and key personnel recruitment where relevant to I@S supply chain opportunities.
- Coordinate with Regional Supply Chain Directors and country programs to ensure country-level supply chain needs and evidence are reflected in proposals.
- Contribute to after-action reviews following award decisions to capture lessons and improve future supply chain BD submissions.
- Identify and evaluate opportunities for business development & partnerships with academic or research centers, with Research & Innovation colleagues as appropriate.

**3. Implementation of Strategic Initiatives Supporting Impact @ Scale**

- Strengthening global forecasting and demand planning systems for key health commodities.
- Collaborate with Global Procurement to define sourcing strategies, monitor supplier performance, and ensure security of supply.
- Lead global visibility efforts by consolidating country-level data on demand, pipeline status, consumption, and stock risks. Collaborate with GSC Systems and Data to digitalize as many aspects of this as possible in a timely manner.
- Work with country teams to improve quantification, storage, distribution planning, and last-mile delivery.
- Translate I@S targets into actionable supply chain plans with milestones, KPIs, and risk controls.
- Design and support the rollout of cross-country improvements (e.g., pooled procurement feasibility, centralized pre-positioning, LMIS integration, preferred vendor strategies, emergency surge mechanisms, harmonized delivery models).
- Support the implementation of the supply chain I@S bodies of work.
- Escalate and advise GSC Leadership on global priorities, risks, and mitigation strategies impacting success of I@S activity plans.

**4. Capacity Building, Country Support & Operational Strengthening**

- Provide specialized technical support to country supply chain and health teams.
- Strengthening country practices in forecasting, contingency planning, supplier management, and stock-out prevention.
- Support countries facing pipeline risks or operational bottlenecks; deploy to high-priority locations as needed.
- Promote best practices and harmonize tools, guidance, and SOPs across all countries, regions and departments.
- Train country and departmental staff as required. Develop e-training as funding permits.

**5. Monitoring, KPIs, Reporting & Knowledge Management**

- Develop supply chain KPIs aligned to IRC’s LMIS, BD and I@S objectives.
- Produce timely reports on global health supply chain performance, risks, and mitigation actions.
- Document lessons learned and drive continuous improvement.
- Maintain updated knowledge of global markets, procurement trends, supplier landscapes, regulatory shifts, and donor funding priorities relevant to supply chain programming.

**Qualifications**

**Education**

- Master's degree in public health, pharmacy, supply chain management, strategy development, , international development, international relations, or relevant field or equivalent combination of education and work experience background is required or related field.

**Work Experience**

- Experience in supply chain management in humanitarian settings, preferably with demonstrable experience in health supply chains, especially immunization, nutrition and sexual and reproductive health (SRH).
- Proven experience in departmental or organizational strategy development in operations / supply chain in humanitarian organizations.
- Expertise in forecasting, strategic sourcing, procurement, quality assurance, and distribution of health commodities including in the context of vaccine storage and distribution.
- Experience in conducting assessments and evaluations of supply chain systems.
- Experience engaging in business development processes, including writing and project design, proposal development, donor positioning, or capture for supply chain or health programming is strongly preferred.
- Experience in developing and managing project concepts and funding proposals for humanitarian / development work with the ability to turn concepts and strategy into measurable action
- Strong capacity to understand the humanitarian system and operating context and coordinate the relevant technical inputs from within and outside GSC
- Familiarity with donor landscapes for supply chain programming (e.g., ECHO, SIDA, USAID, Gates) and ability to contribute to donor engagement and positioning.
- Familiarity with managing large-scale, complex portfolio and experience using strategic insights and data from varied sources to support portfolio management, pivoting and alignment to organizational and sectoral goals
- Experience in building partnerships for development and humanitarian funding as well as negotiation of programmatic and financial contractual arrangements with donors and partners
- Experience and comfort interrogating partnership practices and familiarity with emerging developments including growing attention to power-shifting, localization and technical assistance models for INGOs

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Proficiency in data analysis, visualization tools (Power BI), and performance monitoring.
- Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills and ability to analyses trends based on a diverse set of data and insights
- Digital supply chain literacy: familiarity with LMIS platforms, supply chain technology ecosystems, and data interoperability standards in humanitarian or low-resource settings. Experience with using AI-enabled solutions preferred.
- Ability to identify fundable supply chain programming opportunities and experience in business development writing and proposal design
- Ability to translate operational supply chain experience into compelling proposal narratives and capability statements.
- Demonstrated ability to work with stakeholders at multiple levels and influence decision making
- Knowledge of public and private fundraising - appetite and curiosity about building collaborative pathways with philanthropy and private sector
- Fluent in English (required); proficiency in French, Spanish or Arabic.

**Competencies**

- Strong project management and coordination skills.
- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in supply chain optimization.
- Good organizational skills and ability to prioritize competing priorities effectively.
- Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities; skills; ability to work cross-functionally and across cultures.
- A sense of curiosity about how things can be done, and a willingness to get creative on solutioning.
- Attention to detail and ability to identify and address potential risks proactively.
- Commitment to ethical standards and accountability.

**Key Relationships**

**Reports to:**

Director, Emergency & Health Supply Chain

**Directly Supervises:** N/A

**Internal:** Global Supply Chain, Health Technical Unit, IT, Regional Supply Chain Directors, Health Coordinators/teams and Supply Chain Coordinators/Teams; Pharmacists; GOAT BD Coordinator; GSC BD pipeline monitoring

**External:** Peer INGOs, UN agencies (UNICEF, WHO), institutional donors (ECHO, SIDA, Unitaid, USAID), implementing partners, HLGSC members

**Additional Information**

- Frequent travel to program countries will be required up to 20%.
- This position may involve collaboration with government agencies, international NGOs, private-sector partners, and institutional donors.
- The role actively participates in IRC’s BD process, including pipeline monitoring, capture, and proposal development for supply chain funding opportunities.

**Working Environment**

- Remote work / standard office (location dependent)

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United Kingdom, Kenya, and Lebanon.***

**Compensation:** (UK Pay Rate: £58,476-£69,440/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

jobs.title: Finance/Ops Lead - FCDO-funded Technical Assistance
jobs.body:
**Background and Objectives of the FCDO-funded Technical Assistance Programme in Pakistan**

IRC is preparing to bid for an upcoming long-term FCDO-funded Technical Assistance programme in Pakistan. The programme will provide sustained technical and advisory support to strengthen the capacity of government counterparts and partners, with delivery structured against agreed results and milestones in line with FCDO's payment-by-results (PBR) requirements. The Finance/Ops Lead will play a central role in ensuring the programme's financial management, operations and PBR-linked reporting are robust, compliant and responsive to the needs of the technical team throughout the life of the contract.

The Finance/Ops Lead will be responsible for overseeing financial management, operations and financial reporting for the FCDO-funded Technical Assistance programme in Pakistan. Acting as the principal finance and operations business partner to the Project Director and other Senior Management team, the Finance/Ops Lead provides the leadership and management necessary to ensure the project has the appropriate financial and operational infrastructure and systems in place to support smooth project implementation, including robust tracking and reporting against payment-by-results (PBR) milestones. The Finance/Ops Lead will ensure the assistance complies with FCDO rules and regulations and host country labor, tax, and other relevant laws. S/he will contribute to the development of the Project’s strategic and operational plans and be accountable for ensuring and monitoring delivery against the financial and PBR plans through targeted and comprehensive financial analytical review. Additionally, the Finance/Ops Lead will coordinate their work with IRC Finance Unit to enforce internal controls over the programme.

**Job Responsibilities:**

- Ensures that all policies and procedures are in compliance with IRC and FCDO policies, procedures, and requirements.
- Establishes project’s finance and supporting function policies, systems and procedures, and directs or performs their development, documentation, and implementation.
- Manages project finance activities and schedules to meet the financial reporting requirements and deadlines specified by IRC HQ and FCDO. Prepares quarterly accrual reports, expenditure reporting, and burn rate projections.
- Provides project management and program staff with monthly actual-to-budget expenditure reports and analysis for project funds and facilitate the review and discussion.
- Ensures balance sheet reconciliations are completed monthly and on a timely basis and review final reconciliations and trial balances with the Project Director.
- Closely monitors all financial activities, and keeps the Project Director advised of all situations which have the potential for a negative impact on internal controls or financial performance.
- Directs the preparation of and approval of all FCDO financial reports in respect to accounting, legal and contractual requirements and ensures the review of such reports by the Project Director and HQ prior to submission.
- Enforces internal control policies and procedures.
- Maintains current knowledge of local government requirements related to financial matters and ensures compliance with tax regulations and other legal requirements.
- Establishes project finance roles and responsibilities matrix; ensures job descriptions are current; recruits and maintains qualified staff to perform finance functions.
- Develops and implements a training program for the project’s finance staff.
- Ensures constructive performance reviews are completed on a timely basis and facilitates discussion of performance and career options with project finance staff.
- Supervises all project office bank relations and bank account activities including negotiation of fees, interest and currency exchange rates.
- In compliance with IRC policy, establishes policies regarding cash holding limits, cash movements and foreign currency holdings of the project.
- Oversees the timely preparation, review and approval of all monthly bank account and cash reconciliations.
- Designs, implements, and monitors systems, procedures and reporting necessary to maintain on current basis accurate forecasts of cash requirements for meeting future spending, including commitments entered into and which obligate IRC to future spending.
- Supervises the preparation of Cash Transfer Requests to IRC HQ and ensures that appropriate cash balances are maintained to facilitate project implementation.
- Assists with the preparation and revision of project budgets.
- Prepares the annual and monthly cash budgets based on approved funding.
- Prepares monthly pipeline analysis (spending forecast) on the project in coordination with the technical team.
- Coordinates and reconciles spending forecasts with Project Director to reflect realistic data.
- Leads on operational management of the project office, including logistics, procurement, and administrative/HR coordination, ensuring operations are efficient and compliant with FCDO and IRC requirements.
- Leads on the financial tracking, verification, and reporting of Payment by Results (PBR) milestones and disbursement-linked indicators, ensuring accurate and timely submissions to FCDO.

**Requirements:**

- A bachelor’s degree from an accredited university in Accounting, Business Administration, Commerce or Finance with a recognized professional certificate in accounting such as CPA, or a master’s degree in Accounting.
- Minimum of 10 years in similar financial, compliance, or operational role in managing and supporting $7 million or larger FCDO funded projects and other Institutional Donor projects in similar contexts;
- Experience with budgeting and financial reporting requirements on $7 million or larger FCDO, or other Institutional Donor funded projects;
- Experience with financial management and reporting on projects with substantial subaward components;
- Strong knowledge of generally accepted accounting practices, financial reporting standards, financial management processes and procedures
- Familiarity with FCDO rules and regulations including applicable laws.
- Prior experience working on FCDO Technical Assistance programmes and/or with commercial contractors delivering FCDO/ODA-funded assistance, with a solid understanding of the associated compliance, procurement and reporting requirements.
- Strong background in the Payment by Results (PBR) approach, including designing and tracking results-based milestones and disbursement-linked indicators, and financial reporting against PBR schedules.
- Extensive experience in working with computerized accounting systems (ERP), standard spreadsheet and database programs, and advanced and demonstrated/practical skills in Microsoft Excel.
- Must have a proven track record of proactively identifying and communicating potential problems and proposing solutions.
- Excellent interpersonal communication skills and professional patience and be able to interact, partner and thrive in a diverse environment.
- Strong negotiation skills and the ability to develop relations with diverse teams.
- Good written and verbal skills in English.

***Recruitment for this role is contingent upon the successful award of the project to the IRC. The final applicant's selection is subject to FCDO approval.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. jobs.title: Regional Research and Learning Coordinator, PlayMatters
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee’s mission is to help people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded over 90 years ago, the IRC is a leading humanitarian and development organization with presence in more than 40 countries. Across contexts, the IRC is committed to delivering innovative, high-impact programs tailored to the needs of communities affected by crisis.

The IRC has been working in Uganda since 1998 supporting refugees, vulnerable host communities, and various institutions in the country notably the government, community-based organizations, civil society, and the private sector. Currently, the IRC in Uganda has a presence across five sub-regions and six refugee settlements, implementing programming in the sectors of health, protection and rule of law (PRoL), women’s protection and empowerment (WPE), economic recovery and development (ERD), and education. IRC Uganda also implements cross-cutting programming focused on systems strengthening and accountability to affected persons.

**Job Overview/ Summary:**

PlayMatters 3.0 is a 4-year education initiative (2026-2030) with a goal of improving the well-being and holistic learning outcomes of pre-primary and primary school aged children (ages 3-12+), including those who are affected by conflict and crisis, in Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Uganda by strengthening education systems to deliver quality education services using active teaching and learning through play. The PlayMatters consortium is made up of the IRC, Plan International, and War Child Alliance, in collaboration with national partners and the LEGO foundation. PM prioritizes strengthening education systems to be resilient and scaling impact by working with and through existing systems rather than establishing parallel systems. PM has three main outcomes: Outcome 1: Education systems have increased capacity, uptake, and coordination of Learning through Play (LtP) as a teaching method; Outcome 2: School-aged children in refugee hosting and post-crisis recovery zones have increased access to quality learning opportunities in safe environments; Outcome 3: School-aged children's holistic development is protected in times of acute crisis.

Research and learning are core to PlayMatters, which emphasizes evidence generation and use. The Regional Research and Learning Coordinator will directly support the PlayMatters regional research team to coordinate, design, implement, and disseminate IRC-led PlayMatters research, and support the regional PlayMatters MEL teams to collect, store, analyze, use, and disseminate learning internal and external to the Consortium in Ethiopia, South Sudan, and Uganda. He/she will work closely with the regional team and country-based teams in support of quality evidence-building and actionable learning activities in support of moving PlayMatters forward on the Path to Scale. This role also serves as a key coordination point between the PlayMatters Consortium and its internal (Airbel) and external (the PlayMatters External Evaluator) research partners, ensuring alignment across technical design, implementation timelines, and evidence dissemination.

**Major Responsibilities:**

The Regional Research and Learning Coordinator will lead and support a broad range of PlayMatters research and learning activities, including the following:

**Coordinate and Manage the Operationalization of the Research Agenda and Plan:**

- Coordination and implementation of IRC-led qualitative and quantitative research studies, including a range of formative and implementation research studies that utilize a range of methods and analytical strategies, including:
    - Coordinate with Airbel's research team on study design, data management, budget/level-of-effort alignment, and quality assurance of research outputs;
    - Instrument adaptation and validation, including cognitive pretesting of tools across languages and cultures and the calibration of classroom observation tools across cultural contexts.
    - Programming of tools as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities, using CommCare and Tangerine primarily.
    - Enumerator trainings as needed for the different studies, in preparation for data collection activities.
    - Data cleaning and analysis, including both quantitative and qualitative analysis as needed.
    - Capacity building for research teams across PlayMatters.
- Coordination and support to WCA-led research studies, including reporting and dissemination of findings;
- In collaboration with the External evaluator and the donor, RCT preparation and support across the three countries, including support with path to scale planning, RCT design, timelines, data collection strategies, logistics, etc.

**Lead Learning Activities, including integrating learning into adaptive management and the PlayMatters Learning Agenda:**

- Co-design and lead the actualization of the PlayMatters Learning Agenda, including a range of learning studies utilizing a range of quantitative and qualitative methods
- Serve as Consortium lead and focal point for learning, providing strategic thinking and design to establish a Consortium culture of learning and viable learning products and opportunities
- Support the collection, storage, analysis, use, and dissemination of learning across a spectrum of systematic collection
- Conduct evidence reviews, including desk reviews and literature reviews to support the design and implementation of PlayMatters interventions.
- Facilitate a broad range of learning activities for the consortium and beyond, including workshops, presentations, written products including reports and academic papers for peer-reviewed journals, stakeholder engagement, and dissemination.
- Provide high quality connections with HQ to connect PlayMatters with broader organizational and Education sector learning and strategy.

**Coordinate Research Across the PM Consortium, with Airbel and with External Evaluation Partners:**

- Serve as a key point of contact and coordination lead between IRC/Airbel's internal research team and PlayMatters country and regional teams.
- Liaise with the PlayMatters External Evaluator (EE), including reconciling EE technical design with realistic implementation plans, and engaging the EE in relevant working groups (e.g., the Research Management Group).
- Support communication and coordination mechanisms between the EE, PMCs, National Partners, and the PlayMatters Consortium.
- Support convening and coordination of PM research governance structures (e.g., Research Management Group, RMEAL Reference Group), including quality assurance review of research products.
- Ensure coordination between Research and MEAL workstreams across the Consortium.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- Position Reports to: Deputy Project Director - Technical, PlayMatters
- Position directly supervises: N/A
- Indirect Reporting: N/A
- Other Internal and/or external contacts:
    - Internal: RMEAL Advisor, PlayMatters; RMEAL Advisor, LF Framework; Engaged researchers from Airbel Impact LaB.
    - External: External Evaluator

**Education and Technical Competencies:**

- Degree in Education, Psychology, International Development, International Relations, Peace and Conflict Studies, Policy Studies, or other related Social Sciences-Related discipline.

**Skills and Competencies**

- At least three years of experience working in education in low-resource environments,
- A background in education research, including training in both quantitative and qualitative research methods,
- At least one year of experience doing research on education in emergencies;
- At least one year of experience supporting the implementation of mixed-methods research studies focused on education, psychosocial support, or other areas related to Learning through Play;
- At least one year of experience supporting the implementation of measurement and learning systems in complex programs
- Strong writing skills (in English) and significant writing experience;
- Experience coordinating research activities across multiple institutional partners (e.g., research organizations, academic institutions, or external evaluators) is a plus.
- Experience publishing in peer-reviewed journals is a plus.
- Experience analyzing qualitative data using Dedoose, nVivo or other qualitative data analysis software is a plus;
- Experience analyzing quantitative data using SPSS, Stata, or other statistical analysis packages is a plus;
- Experience working in East Africa is a plus.
- Fluent in written and oral English; knowledge of other regional language preferred

**Working Environment:**

- Standard office working environment
- Travel required 25%
- The position may be based in any IRC country program or IRC office

***This position is open to candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United States of America, United Kingdom, and Uganda.***

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $70,000-$88,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £41,767-£49,599/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Education and Early Childhood Development (ECD) Technical Advisor – MENAU
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Background**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world’s largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions.

The IRC’s Technical Excellence department helps achieve that aim by generating evidence, sharing learning, and providing technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff. Technical Excellence is comprised of Technical Units (TUs) – Health; Economic Recovery and Development (ERD); Education; and Violence Prevention and Response (VPR) – including Global Practice Teams, regionally aligned technical teams, and supporting units for MEAL, policy and advocacy, and partnerships and program development.

In 2025, the IRC reached over 600,000 children and youth in 20 countries with early childhood development and education programs, ensuring that even the hardest to reach children in the most challenging places are able to go learn, develop and thrive. The Middle East, North Africa & Ukraine (MENAU) region is one of IRC’s largest and most complex areas of operation, encompassing protracted conflict, displacement, and recovery contexts across multiple country programs. Regional TU teams provide dedicated, context-relevant technical assistance to these country programs across the program cycle, aligned with the IRC Technical Assistance model and service charter.

**Position Overview**

The IRC is seeking an Education & Early Childhood Development (ECD) Technical Advisor to provide temporary coverage during a period of parental leave. This is a fixed-term, 6-month assignment (September 1, 2026 – March 1, 2027) focused exclusively on the Middle East, North Africa & Ukraine (MENAU) region. IRC’s MENAU region includes Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, occupied Palestinian Territory, Syria, Ukraine and Yemen.

The role is focused on education and early childhood development (pre-natal through age 8), which is closely aligned with the Nurturing Care Framework and has key interlinkages across multiple sectors. The Education & ECD TA will provide direct technical support to MENAU country programs identified as strategic priorities for Education and ECD innovation, growth, and research, in close collaboration and coordination with the regional Education TA and other sector-specific TAs relevant to ECD (Child Protection, Nutrition, Primary Health, Mental Health, Economic Recovery and Development, Women’s Protection, Governance, etc.).

To ensure quality programming and impact for young children and families affected by conflict and crisis, the Education & ECD TA will: support country program staff to design programs and projects aligned to IRC’s outcomes and evidence framework / theories of change / core indicators; review technical quality of proposals; input into proposal go/no-go decisions; analyze data to inform course correction; conduct technical trainings and ongoing technical coaching; share cross-context learning with country program staff; design, review, and share program-level tools (e.g., assessment frameworks, M&E templates, proposal materials); and support senior technical country program recruitment and capacity-building. Development, adaptation, and quality assurance of Education and ECD content and curricula sit with the ECD Content Specialist, and the ECD TA is expected to route any content-related country requests accordingly rather than duplicate that work.

As the Education and ECD Technical Advisor for MENAU, you will be responsible for ensuring high-quality technical assistance to Education and ECD projects across the MENAU region, including collaboration with counterparts from other sectors to ensure holistic support to clients. You will promote and collaborate with relevant stakeholders to achieve high-quality, high-impact interventions that are informed by evidence and best practice, contextually appropriate, driven by client and partner voices, and widely inclusive.

**Key Duties and Responsibilities**

**Program Design & Business Development**

Support designated MENAU country and regional programs to design winning submissions and generally position IRC for continued success in our Education and ECD technical domains:

- Support designated country programs’ proposal technical lead through participation in and/or facilitation of program design meetings
- Promote and support design collaboration with partners and clients
- Advise on program modalities and strategic partnership development based on how we can best support, complement, and reinforce local systems
- Advise on and/or provide hands-on support on assessments, including application and contextualization of technical standards
- Review technical design quality, including alignment of narratives, log-frames, and budgets to IRC standards and outcomes

**Implementation Support**

Support MENAU country program staff and other key stakeholders in implementing technical interventions:

- Support country and regional programs and other stakeholders with the recruitment and training of technical coordinators
- Assess program quality and inform improvements, providing follow-up support to country programs as needed
- Collaborate with country and regional program colleagues to monitor and analyze key indicators to inform periodic review, program adaptation, and course-correction as needed
- Provide technical capacity strengthening through ongoing mentoring, coaching, and trainings with country program focal points

**Knowledge & Learning**

Support continuous sectoral learning and IRC technical leadership within the MENAU region:

- Document learnings from program activities and share takeaways and opportunities
- Share cross-contextual learnings with country program staff across the MENAU region
- Refresh the sectoral evidence base in collaboration with global and regional staff to influence approaches
- Collaborate with other technical advisors within the region to promote integrated programming leadership
- Contribute to the delivery of education strategic priorities
- Maintain currency with sectoral best practices through continual learning and development
- Coordinate closely and maintain a regular check-in with the ECD Content Specialist and relevant Regional ECD Portfolio Team to align on country requests, agree on division of labor between program-level technical assistance and content/curricula work, and avoid duplicative deliverables

**Professional Profile**

Success in this position requires an individual with expertise in designing and delivering Education and ECD technical assistance and with a keen ability to work across the range of cultural, societal, and political contexts found across the MENAU region.

**Work Experience**

- A minimum of 10 years of relevant experience in implementing and/or managing ECD education programs, preferably with on-the-ground programmatic experience in humanitarian or crisis-affected contexts
- Experience and familiarity with related donors, peer agencies, and national contexts required, preferably in humanitarian and transitional, post-crisis contexts within the MENAU region
- Demonstrated expertise in technical program design, monitoring and evaluation, research methods, and data analysis, with the ability to turn concepts and strategy into measurable action

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies**

- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- Strong organizational and time-management skills; proven ability to prioritize and deliver projects on time and independently
- Demonstrated ability to navigate a dynamic, cross-functional, global team structure in a large multi-national organization
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with internal and external stakeholders at all levels
- Strong analytic problem-solving skills, data analysis, and data visualization skills
- Highly proficient in Microsoft Office suite
- Ability to manage and work through change in a proactive and positive manner
- Strong cross-cultural communication skills and familiarity with the MENAU region’s humanitarian context

**Education**

Bachelor’s degree in Education or a relevant field required; Master’s degree preferred.

**Language Skills**

Fluency in Arabic (spoken and written) is required. Excellent spoken and written English is also required.

**Key Working Relationships**

This position reports to the Global Practice Lead and Director of Research, Early Childhood Development, in close coordination with the Education Technical Advisor for MENAU, based in Amman for the duration of the parental leave cover. This role is expected to play an active role in the Education Technical Unit and regularly engage with other Technical Advisors and colleagues through meetings and virtual events. Communication and coordination with other technical unit staff, MENAU regional and country program teams, awards management and grants management staff, and other internal stakeholders is expected.

**Working Environment**

This is a remote, fixed-term position and may be based within the MENAU region or relevant timezone. This role may require some travel within the MENAU region (up to approximately 40% of the time), conditions permitting.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. **Job Overview**

The Kansas Office for Refugees (KSOR) serves as a “Replacement Designee” for the state of Kansas, administering the Refugee Cash and Medical Assistance (CMA) program and Refugee Support Services (RSS) program in accordance with the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR) regulations, through the KSOR office, based in Wichita.

Beginning in FY2026, ORR awarded RSS grants directly to the State of Kansas government. The Community Engagement Prom Manager (CEPM) will support the KSOR Director and Deputy Director (DD) in planning, implementing, and managing changes to a state-centric model of refugee resettlement. In addition, KSOR responds to community needs by coordinating and supporting various events, including stakeholder meetings, quarterly consultation meetings, community forums, partner coordination meetings, and training sessions with guest speakers. As part of the KSOR team, the CEPM is responsible for helping plan and/or support stakeholders in executing these events. jobs.title: Nigeria Tech Specialist (Fixed-term)
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

The Tech Specialist will own the end-to-end technical delivery of our field and internal solutions. You will use approved AI coding tools and development agents to accelerate architecture, coding, testing, debugging, and documentation.

## **Responsibilities**

Product & Software Development — 40%

- Design, build, and maintain mobile, web, backend, and data solutions.
- Develop reliable digital workflows that support both online and offline use.
- Build scalable, maintainable features that support operational and business requirements.
- Integrate systems, data, and services to deliver a seamless user experience.

Architecture & Data — 20%

- Integrate systems, data, and services to deliver a seamless user experience.
- Contribute to the technical architecture and ongoing evolution of the platform.
- Design secure and scalable data models, APIs, and integration patterns.
