jobs.title: Early Refugee School Impact Specialist
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:**

Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. The IRC is on the ground in more than 40 countries, providing emergency relief, relocating refugees, and rebuilding lives in the wake of disaster. Through 29 regional offices in cities across the United States, the IRC helps refugees resettle and become self-sufficient. Our programs are designed to ensure refugees thrive in America--whether ensuring children are enrolled in school, adults become self-reliant through employment or starting businesses, or families receive acute medical care they need to recover from trauma or illness. IRC Wichita has been assisting refugees since 2011. The Wichita office offers a range of services including trauma-informed family support, economic empowerment, education for youth and adults, and immigration services. The IRC helps those in need to rebuild their lives and regain control of their future in their new home.

**SCOPE OF WORK:**

The Early Refugee School Impact (ERSI) Specialist engages in the implementation, coordination, and support of IRC’s early childhood programming in alignment with organizational goals. Program coordination includes conducting program intakes, presenting, and explaining information on childcare options, preschool services, and connecting caregivers to relevant resources. This position will serve caregivers of children ages 0-5. The ERSI Specialist reports directly to the Education Manager.

**MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES:**

 **Client Services**

- Develop resources and expand partnerships that promote the success of refugee families through material design and partner engagement.
- Nurture partnerships with childcare centers and preschool service providers to advocate and provide support for the caregivers.
- Assess that quality practices are implemented and program outcomes are met; maintain data and reports indicating such.
- Serve as a focal point in the community for referrals to educational programs and services.
- Design and implement activities, workshops, and services which directly contribute to positive outcomes for refugee families.
- Identify and connect with licensed childcare providers and preschools who may partner with IRC.
- Perform outreach and educate caregivers on the benefits of enrolling children in childcare and preschool.
- Liaise between childcare providers, preschools, parents, caseworkers, employment specialists, and other relevant colleagues.
- Conduct intakes with qualified program participants to assess the needs of each individual/family.
- Assist interested caregivers with applications for childcare and financial resources (through childcare provider or government assistance).
- Lead and facilitate educational workshops, meetings, and events to promote healthy parenting skills.
- Provide follow-up with providers and families to assess the effectiveness of childcare plans.
- Other duties as assigned.

 **Administration, Monitoring and Evaluation**

- Conduct assessments of caregivers’ understanding of age-appropriate resources, activities, and childcare options.
- Ensure required intake documents are fully completed and service plan updated as appropriate.
- Comply with all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.

**Team/Office Participation**

- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and other duties as assigned.
- Work as part of a team to provide comprehensive strength-based services to IRC clients through coordination of cases and effective communication between team members and departments.
- Comply with all policies, procedures, and protocols of the agency, placing importance on client confidentiality.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS:**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work, early childhood education, or a related field of study is preferred.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills, strong attention to detail, and the proven ability to prioritize duties and manage time effectively.
- Strong written, oral, and interpersonal communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively with colleagues and partners in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment, and the ability to present to a varied public.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; Bilingual a plus but not required.
- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook). Proven experience in web-based data entry systems.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time efficiently.
- Strategic, creative, problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.
- Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area for home visits, agency visits, and service provider visits.
- Well organized and enthusiastic about working in a multi-cultural and client-centered setting.

**WORKING ENVIRONMENT:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional evenings and weekends may be required.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23.50/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: eLearning Proposal Writer (Remote)
jobs.body:
Altamont Group is a mission-driven advisory and impact investment organization, working across advisory, consulting, digital, and investment services to help clients deliver meaningful impact. We are hiring an **eLearning Proposal Writer** to lead the development of complete, targeted, and compelling responses to RFPs for digital learning solutions, articulating Altamont Group's value and winning new business across our learning and development service lines.

**Description**

Altamont Group is hiring an **eLearning Proposal Writer** to respond to complex RFPs spanning **custom eLearning development, instructional design, learning management systems, mobile and blended learning, multimedia production, and learning analytics**, working with clients across government, enterprise, education, and non-profit/NGO sectors.

- The eLearning Proposal Writer will create complete and compelling responses to requests for proposals (RFPs) that communicate Altamont Group's learning expertise, solution approach, and value with the aim of winning new business
- The ideal candidate has a strong learning and development background with a solid understanding of instructional design, custom eLearning production, LMS platforms, and digital learning standards, along with three or more years of experience responding to RFPs from government, enterprise, education, and non-profit organizations, coupled with strong writing skills
- We need an energetic, motivated, and persistent person who can write winning proposals

**Responsibilities**

- Read incoming RFPs/TORs and develop the proposal development plan
- Develop bid development strategy and proposal project planning
- Complete the research and discovery needed to develop instructional, technical, implementation, and cost proposal documents
- Ensure content matches the RFP/TOR and includes approved proposal language according to company policy
- Ensure responses follow corporate brand style and tone guidelines
- Review and customize RFP responses
- Serve as a liaison between learning solution teams and proposal content, clearly articulating instructional approaches, learner journeys, content formats, platform requirements, accessibility considerations, and implementation plans
- Verify that responses address key client priorities, evaluation criteria, learner needs, measurable outcomes, and win themes
- Write all required and additional RFP response documents and attachments, including cover letters, executive summaries, needs-analysis narratives, instructional design approaches, development methodologies, implementation plans, quality-assurance plans, and project schedules
- Incorporate feedback from proposal review sessions
- Assist with proposal knowledge management and retention of content for future use
- Provide the proposal submission package, including accompanying documents and cover email
- Develop pitch and clarification-meeting materials, including presentations, solution overviews, learning journey summaries, briefing notes, demonstrations, and speaking points
- Support in other areas as requested
- Ensure:
    - Our unique value proposition is clear and evident in every part of the proposal
    - Our cover letter and executive summary clearly address what the client is looking for
    - Thoroughly yet concisely respond to all areas of the proposal
    - By the end of the proposal, the reader is left with no questions as to why they should choose Altamont Group
    - A complete, client-ready, proofread, and edited proposal is provided

**Required Skills and Experience**

- Bachelor's Degree from an accredited University; Master's preferred
- Learning and development background and experience across eLearning service areas, particularly in:
- Instructional design; custom eLearning and microlearning; virtual instructor-led and blended learning; learning management systems; storyboarding and multimedia production; assessments and learning evaluation; accessibility; and standards such as SCORM, xAPI, and LTI
- Expertise in developing evidence-based, well-researched learning solution methodologies in response to RFPs, including needs analysis, learner and audience analysis, instructional strategy, content development, implementation, quality assurance, and evaluation
- Three or more years of experience responding to eLearning, training, education technology, or learning management system RFPs
- Excellent writing, organizational, communication, and planning skills
- Previous experience writing successful bids/proposals
- Demonstrated history of winning bids
- Enhanced research and data analysis skills
- Able to articulate the linkage between client needs, learner profiles, instructional strategies, technology choices, deliverables, implementation plans, and measurable learning or performance outcomes
- Strong attention to detail
- Proven track record of timely and high-quality completion of assignments
- Ability to manage deadlines efficiently
- Strong critical thinking ability
- Ability to work independently
- Highly organized with strong time management skills, and an ability to learn quickly and produce high-quality work under tight deadlines
- Flexible attitude toward receiving feedback
- Proficient with MS Office and SharePoint; familiarity with common eLearning authoring tools, LMS platforms, and proposal collaboration systems is preferred

- Act as the core mechanical technical intervention specialist for Soko factory machinery repairs and maintenance. Ensure all soko machinery is in a good performance state.
- Conduct technical repairs on industrial dehydrators, macadamia processing systems, and industrial-level biochar production equipment.
- Verify and list precise mechanical specifications for machines, spare parts, and consumables requested by factory teams.

Workforce Mentorship & TPM Support

- Mentor and model best-practice mechanical repair techniques during direct interaction with factory staff to elevate technical standards
- Assist in delivering TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) maintenance training for machine operators specifically regarding mechanical checks, cleaning, and precision lubrication
- Coach operators on identifying early mechanical warning signs like abnormal vibrations, heat, or noise

Safety, Food Safety, and Regulation

- Ensure all maintenance activities comply with safe systems of work: permit to work, LOTO, confined space, and relevant Kenyan regulatory requirements (KEBS, DOSH, NEMA)
- Maintain HACCP-required equipment records for food-contact assets; lead the maintenance function's contribution to food safety audits
- Champion a zero-harm safety culture on the shop floor; report hazards and quickly close out structural or machine risk issues

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You'll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You'll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Technical skills:

- Degree or Higher Diploma in Mechanical Engineering or appropriate engineering field
- Active registration/membership as an engineer or technical practitioner in Kenya
- Preventive/predictive maintenance programme design and implementation
- Experience with avocado oil machinery repairs and maintenance preferred
- Experience with industrial dehydrators, macadamia processing, and industrial level biochar production preferred
- Ability to utilize CMMS software (SAP PM, Maximo, Limble, etc.) to close work orders and log technical data
- Deep mechanical fault-finding and root cause analysis on industrial plant equipment
- Proficiency in mechanical drawings, pneumatics, hydraulics, and welding/fabrication techniques

Knowledge:

- Food safety management systems and HACCP requirements as applied to plant maintenance
- Kenyan occupational health and safety legislation (OSHA, DOSH requirements)
- TPM (Total Productive Maintenance) or World Class Manufacturing principles
- Kenyan regulatory environment for food manufacturing (KEBS, relevant standards)

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Rukanga, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, paid time off

## **Contract Duration**

2 years

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

20 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization's mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR-eligible immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. This position delivers individualized case management services, develops self-sufficiency plans in partnership with clients, and connects households to essential resources in the community. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external service providers to ensure timely access to benefits, housing, healthcare, employment, and other supports necessary for successful resettlement.

**Major Responsibilities:**  
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intakes and needs assessments to identify strengths, barriers, and goals for enrolled clients.
- Develop Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs) with clients, ensuring alignment with program and donor requirements.
- Provide trauma-informed case management services, including direct support, referrals, and advocacy with service providers.
- Coordinate access to housing, benefits, healthcare, education, and employment services.
- Monitor client progress toward goals, adjusting plans as needed, and ensure documentation is timely and accurate in case files and data systems.
- Maintain strong relationships with community partners and service providers to expand available resources for clients.
- Participate in case conferences, team meetings, and trainings to promote quality service delivery and professional development.
- Follow all IRC policies and procedures, including safeguarding, data protection, and confidentiality protocols.

**Job Requirements**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work or related field strongly preferred; comparable work experience may be substituted.

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum 2 years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or underserved populations preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong organizational and time-management skills; detail-oriented.
- Ability to work effectively as part of a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary team.
- Problem-solver with ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams).
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills; public speaking experience preferred.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in English required; bilingual ability in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French, or other refugee/immigrant language preferred.

**Certificates or Licenses:**

- Valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, and access to reliable transportation.
- Must possess or be eligible for a fingerprint clearance card per Arizona state law.

**Working Environment**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional evening or weekend work may be required.
- Must be able to lift 35–50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, food boxes).

**Compensation:** ($20.97/hr). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

jobs.title: Victim Services Caseworker
jobs.body:
**IRC Background:**

Founded in 1933, the IRC is a leading nonsectarian, voluntary organization providing relief, protection and resettlement services for refugees and victims of oppression or violent conflict. One aspect of the IRC is to provide assistance to refugees resettling in the United States. The IRC opened an office in Phoenix, Arizona in 1994 to provide reception and placement services to newly arrived refugees. The office resettles refugees and provides numerous program services to assist refugees from their arrival through citizenship.

**Job Overview:**

The primary role of the Victim Services Caseworker is to provide comprehensive, victim-centered case management services for victims of crime. Responsibilities will include completing eligibility screening and enrollment paperwork, developing service plans, educating about community services, resources, and legal rights, and helping problem solve barriers to access. This position is also responsible for assisting with programmatic and administrative tasks including case notes, case file management, and data collection.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with accessing community resources through local partners, making appropriate referrals to legal providers, and help identify and arrange social activities in-line with service plans
- Provide crisis intervention to victims and their family members suffering from crime related trauma (through provision of information on victimization, crime prevention, victim’s legal rights and protections, criminal justice process; providing emotional support to victims; safety planning; assistance with compensation applications; interventions with creditors, landlords and employers; creation and monitoring of client service plan and self-sufficiency matrix and on-going tracking)
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referrals and enrollment paperwork for all eligible program participants
- Assessing and evaluating the needs of victims while providing appropriate services and maintaining appropriate documentation
- Build and maintain relationships with various local, state, and federal stakeholders including law enforcement agencies
- Develop strategies to further assist in the identification and referral of victims of crime in Arizona
- Ensure acute needs are met in a timely and client-centered manner for each program participant
- Provide assistance with the development and implementation of all outreach and training activities to ensure program outcomes and activities are met
- Track program activities, compile data and draft reports as required by donor and agency specifications
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities and generally be an engaged team member
- Comply with all policies, procedures and protocols of the agency
- Other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Survivor Services Supervisor  
**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers  
**Other Internal and/or external contacts:** The Victim Services Caseworker will be responsible for developing relationships within the IRC network and external relations with social service agencies and government entities

***Internal:** IRC Victim Services and Anti-Trafficking Programs*

***External:** Arizona domestic violence coalitions, other OVC grantees, attorney offices providing pro-bono legal services, law enforcement, social service agencies, community education presentations, community outreach*

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree in Human Services or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of related work experience; 1-year minimum working with victims of crime or other vulnerable populations.
- Case management and/or victims assistance experience preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent written and spoken English skills
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Excellent writing and analytical skills
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment
- Computer literacy, data base experience preferred
- Ability to work independently and be a flexible team player

***Language Skills:***

- Fluency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Dari, Spanish, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $23.50/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Research Associate
jobs.body:
**Background/IRC Summary:**

The International Rescue Committee helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities that support them, as well as with those who remain within their homes and communities. At work today in over 40 countries and 22 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.

IRC reaches over a million children annually with education and child protection programs in 25 countries around the world. The Education technical unit defines the vision and strategic priorities for all of IRC’s education a programs. The team provides evidence-based and contextually-relevant technical support to programs, with the goal of ensuring they are technically sound and achieving the outcomes we seek.

The IRC’s Airbel Impact Lab designs, tests, and scales life-changing, cost-effective solutions for people affected by conflict and disaster. By applying the IRC’s deep technical expertise and field experience with a range of skills from the behavioral sciences, human-centered design, rigorous research, and multi-disciplinary problem-solving in humanitarian contexts, we work to develop breakthrough solutions that combine creativity and rigor, openness and expertise, and a desire to think afresh with the experience of a large-scale implementing organization.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

This Junior Researcher position sits within the Airbel Impact Lab and supports the Education Unit across multiple research projects. The role focuses primarily on data management and analysis — including cleaning and processing both quantitative and qualitative datasets — as well as synthesizing findings into clear, accessible reports for varied audiences. This is an excellent opportunity for an early-career researcher to build hands-on experience in humanitarian education research.

The role reports to the Senior Researcher for Education in the Airbel Impact Lab and works closely with the Education Technical Unit.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Conduct quantitative and qualitative research activities across multiple education research projects, including cleaning, organizing, managing, and analyzing data; , ensuring data quality and integrity; and producing high-quality reports for diverse audiences.
    - Support implementation research studies to identify whether education interventions are being delivered as intended, with appropriate quality and fidelity, and potential for cost-effectiveness.
    - Support randomized control trials; to identify the impact of interventions on children´s foundational learning and wellbeing.
- Support an internal education research team by contributing to the advancement of research priorities under the supervision of senior researchers
- Contribute to the dissemination of research findings by drafting reports, briefs, and blog posts for practitioner and policy audiences.
- Collaborate with colleagues within the Education team, Research team and R&D team, and other IRC departments in support of research activities
- Perform other related duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

- MA required in Education, Economics, Statistics, or related field.
- Excellent knowledge of quantitative research methods, including inferential statistics and qualitative approaches; exposure to implementation research and causal inference.
- Demonstrated experience in data cleaning, management and analysis; with proficiency in at least one statistical or data analysis tool (e.g. Stata, R, Python).
- Familiarity with qualitative data methods (e.g. thematic analysis, content analysis) is desirable .
- Up to three years of experience in research, data analysis, or a related field; relevant internship, academic research, or volunteer experience will be considered.
- Strong written communication skills, including the ability to present research findings clearly and accessibly for non-specialist audiences; experience drafting reports, summaries, or briefs is an asset

jobs.title: Subnational Shelter & NFI Cluster Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Country Programme**: Ukraine  
**Base**: Kharkiv, Kharkivska Oblast / Kharkiv Hub, Ukraine  
**Cluster Lead Agency**: UNHCR (Shelter/NFI Cluster Lead at national level)  
**Line Manager**:  
• Technical Supervision within the Shelter Cluster structure: Reports to the National Shelter/NFI Cluster Coordinator (UNHCR) for guidance, supervision on deliverables, and oversight.  
• Administrative: Reports to the PIN Shelter & Housing Technical Lead, including for administrative and contractual matters as per PIN policies and procedures

## **About the Ukrainian Programme of People in Need:**

PIN has been working in Ukraine since 2014, providing emergency relief and early recovery support to conflict-affected communities in Government Controlled Areas (GCA) and Non-government control areas (NGCA). Due to the escalation of the war and in 2022, programmes for war-affected communities focus mainly on WASH, Shelter, Protection, including recovery, among other pressing needs. PIN’s contribution to the Ukrainian humanitarian response is amongst the largest, with an annual turnover of close to $100 million, engaging full-time staff members across Ukraine.

**About the role:**

**Background and Context**  
Ukraine continues to face a large-scale humanitarian crisis, with heavy destruction of housing and infrastructure due to ongoing conflict. In eastern Ukraine, including Kharkivska Oblast, the needs for shelter and non-food items (NFI) are among the most acute – an estimated 2.5 million homes have been damaged or destroyed nationwide, with Kharkivska among the oblasts suffering the heaviest damage from shelling and fighting. In 2025, approximately 6.9 million people in Ukraine were projected to need shelter assistance, with a significant portion in eastern regions such as Kharkiv. This high level of need necessitates strong coordination of the shelter response at both national and sub-national levels.  
The humanitarian Shelter/NFI Cluster in Ukraine is led by UNHCR under the Inter-Agency Standing Committee cluster approach, coordinating the efforts of UN agencies, NGOs, and other partners to ensure effective shelter and NFI assistance. People in Need (PIN), a humanitarian NGO active in Ukraine, has been co-chairing shelter coordination in Ukraine since 2015 and led coordination in the East previously, to strengthen the cluster’s reach and effectiveness. Until recently, Kharkivska Oblast was coordinated as part of a larger eastern hub (based in Dnipro) that covered multiple oblasts. As needs evolved, and as part of the Humanitarian reset and move towards area-based coordination, a dedicated **Kharkiv Hub** has been established in May 2025 to focus on Kharkivska Oblast exclusively, improving localized coordination and partner engagement. This ToR outlines the role of the **Subnational Shelter/NFI Cluster Coordinator for the Kharkiv Hub**, which has been created to ensure continuity of coordination in Kharkiv Oblast after its separation from the broader East hub. In continuation of PIN’s contributions to shelter coordination, PIN takes responsibility for this new position.

**Purpose of the Role**: The Subnational Cluster Coordinator in Kharkiv will lead and facilitate the inter-agency coordination of shelter and NFI activities in Kharkivska Oblast. The overall goal is to ensure a **consistent, effective, and well-coordinated humanitarian shelter/NFI response** at the oblast level, in alignment with national cluster strategies and standards. By convening partners, assessing needs and gaps, and liaising with the national cluster, the Coordinator helps avoid duplication of efforts and ensures that vulnerable populations in Kharkiv receive timely and appropriate shelter assistance. Importantly, this position will maintain the momentum and continuity of cluster functions in Kharkiv during and after the transition from the former regional hub structure.

**Coordination Structure and Reporting Lines**  
The Subnational Shelter/NFI Cluster Coordinator for Kharkiv Hub will operate within the framework of the Ukraine Shelter/NFI Cluster’s coordination structure.

**UNHCR**, as the Cluster Lead Agency, provides strategic oversight and support through the national coordination team in Kyiv. The Kharkiv Coordinator will work under the guidance of the National Cluster Coordinator (UNHCR) and closely collaborate with the national Shelter Cluster support staff (e.g. Information Management, Technical Coordinators) to ensure two-way communication and consistency in strategy implementation. The coordinator is considered an integral part of the national cluster coordination team and will participate in national cluster coordination calls/meetings as needed to represent Kharkiv hub issues.

The coordinator is also expected to work closely and provide technical guidance and functional support to the incoming Shelter Associate in the Kharkiv Hub. While formal supervisory and administrative responsibilities are not foreseen due to differing administrative frameworks, the coordinator will offer technical oversight and direction as needed to ensure effective cluster operations.

**People in Need (PIN)** serves as the employer and host agency for this role, reflecting the collaborative leadership model of the cluster, and the importance of leveraging civil society and NGO actors for a more effective and efficient shelter response. The coordinator will be formally employed by PIN, which handles administrative matters like contracting, line management, and logistics support. Whilst contractual line management sits with PIN as per PIN terms and conditions and policies, primary technical direction comes from UNHCR’s cluster coordination leadership, with the National Cluster Coordinator (UNHCR) providing supervision. This dual reporting arrangement ensures strong linkages to both the cluster lead agency and to PIN.  
It is critical to note that the Cluster Coordinator position is a **neutral, inter-agency role**. In line with the principles of the cluster approach, the coordinator represents all Shelter/NFI Cluster partners collectively and not any single organization’s interests. The post holder will focus exclusively on coordination tasks (not direct implementation), serving as an honest broker and facilitator among humanitarian actors. Hershel must uphold the principles of partnership, collaboration, and impartiality, ensuring that the cluster coordination platform remains inclusive and benefits all members and affected communities. The coordinator will also liaise with relevant local coordination bodies in Kharkiv including the soon to be established Humanitarian Operational Coordination Group for Kharkiv, in addition to other relevant coordination bodies (e.g. OCHA’s field coordination and authorities and government-led coordination forums) to represent the Shelter/NFI Cluster and promote cohesive action.

**Main Duties & Responsibilities:**

The Subnational Shelter/NFI Cluster Coordinator – Kharkiv Hub is responsible for the following core duties, aligned with the cluster’s six core functions and the specific needs of the Kharkiv operational context:

1. **Coordination of Humanitarian Shelter/NFI Partners at Hub Level**  
    o **Cluster Meetings:** Organize and facilitate regular coordination meetings in Kharkiv (at least monthly) with all Shelter/NFI cluster partners operating in the oblast. Prepare meeting agendas (in consultation with partners), ensure that minutes are documented, and follow up on action points. These meetings will serve as a platform for information sharing, planning, and addressing operational issues.  
    o **Partner Inclusion & Engagement:** Ensure the cluster coordination forum is inclusive of all relevant stakeholders – UN agencies, international and national NGOs, local NGOs and civil society, Red Cross/Red Crescent, and local authorities involved in shelter/NFI activities. Conduct periodic mapping of all current and potential actors (including government and local organizations) in Kharkiv Oblast, maintain an updated contact list, and actively invite/encourage new or local actors to participate. Support and mentor local organizations to engage in the cluster, strengthening localized response capacity.  
    o **Avoiding Gaps & Overlaps:** Act as a focal point for partners to coordinate their activities, helping to identify and prevent duplication of aid and to highlight gaps in coverage. Through cluster meetings and bilateral contacts, gather information on who is doing what, where, and when (5W matrix) and facilitate collaborative planning so that assistance is provided to all areas of need without redundancy.  
    o **Inter-Cluster Coordination**: Collaborate with other cluster/sectors at the sub-national level to promote an integrated response. This includes maintaining an effective network with coordinators of related clusters (e.g. CCCM, Protection, WASH, etc.) in Kharkiv to address cross-cutting issues and ensure synergy. Represent the Shelter/NFI Cluster to the newly established Humanitarian Operational Coordination Group (Kharkiv) or OCHA-led coordination meetings in Kharkiv and liaise with OCHA’s Kharkiv field office to align cluster activities with overall humanitarian efforts in the oblast.  
    o **Liaison with Local Authorities**: In coordination with UNHCR and cluster partners, engage relevant local authorities (such as the Kharkiv Oblast authorities, housing and infrastructure departments, etc.) to ensure government involvement and endorsement of shelter/NFI interventions. The coordinator will represent the cluster in sub-national coordination meetings with local government and regional administration as needed or as requested by the national cluster lead, advocating for humanitarian shelter priorities and maintaining a two-way information exchange with authorities.  
    o **Phased Transition of CCCM Functions**: Ensure effective support for the phased transition of CCCM functions, with the transfer of ‘hard components’ (e.g., essential items, winterization, repairs) to the Shelter Cluster and ‘soft components’ (e.g., site management, community engagement, support for solutions) to the Protection Cluster. This includes maintaining continuity of services, ensuring active partner engagement, and fostering linkages to recovery and development actors to support sustainable solutions in collective sites.
2. **Planning, Strategy & Standards Implementation**  
    o **Strategic Planning:** Support the development and implementation of the Shelter/NFI Cluster’s strategies and plans in Kharkiv Oblast in line with the national cluster strategy and the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) for Ukraine. This includes contributing local inputs and context to any cluster planning documents, and guiding partners in Kharkiv to align their projects with the agreed cluster strategic objectives and priority activities.  
    o **Needs Assessment & Gap Analysis:** Facilitate joint needs assessments and analysis at the oblast level. Coordinate with cluster partners to collect and analyze data on shelter damage, NFI needs, and population movements in Kharkiv, to identify unmet needs and inform evidence-based decision making. Ensure that assessment findings and gap analyses from Kharkiv are communicated to the national cluster team to shape broader response strategies.  
    o **Technical Standards and Guidelines:** Promote the application of agreed technical standards and best practices among Shelter/NFI actors in Kharkiv. Ensure that all partners are aware of the cluster’s policies, guidelines, and technical guidance (e.g. specifications for emergency shelter kits, insulation materials for winterization, activity handbook, Sphere minimum standards) and that their interventions are consistent with these standards. Where necessary, work with cluster Technical Working Groups (TWGs) to develop or adapt guidelines to the local context and encourage partners to use them.  
    o **Cross-Cutting Issues:** Mainstream cross-cutting issues and humanitarian principles in the shelter response. The coordinator will encourage and monitor that cluster members integrate protection principles, gender considerations, age/disability inclusion, and accountability to affected populations (AAP) in their shelter/NFI programs. For example, ensure partners collect sex- and age-disaggregated data, involve women in shelter decision-making, and establish feedback mechanisms for communities. Any concerns on these fronts should be escalated and addressed through cluster guidance or support from specialists (e.g. Protection Cluster or Gender Advisor).  
    o **Emergency Preparedness & Contingency Planning:** Under the guidance of the national cluster coordination team, lead contingency planning and preparedness measures for potential emergencies in Kharkiv Oblast. This includes scenario planning for possible new displacement waves or sudden onset disasters (e.g. escalation of conflict in certain districts or severe winter conditions), updating preparedness plans, and coordinating with partners to pre-position or mobilize shelter/NFI stocks if feasible. The coordinator will ensure that the cluster has an agreed plan to respond swiftly to localized crises in the oblast and will activate emergency coordination mechanisms (e.g. more frequent meetings, rapid assessments) if such events occur. Additionally, capture and disseminate any lessons learned from past responses in Kharkiv to refine future preparedness and response plans.  
    o **Subnational Transition Planning under the Humanitarian Reset:** Contribute to the implementation of the Global Humanitarian Reset endorsed by the HCT in Ukraine, which aims to adapt the humanitarian setup to better deliver on strategic priorities in the fourth year of the response. This position will lead subnational consultations and transition planning for the Shelter Cluster in Kharkiv Hub, focusing on:
    1. Sustaining life-saving coordination and technical functions during the transition.
    2. Identifying and engaging with national and oblast-level counterparts.
    3. Facilitating capacity-building and technical support.
    4. Aligning shelter interventions with national recovery frameworks.
    5. Supporting the phased handover of coordination roles to local and national actors based on readiness and capacity.
3. **Information Management and Reporting**  
    o **Information Sharing and 5W Reporting**: Work with the cluster’s Information Management Officer (IMO) to manage information at the hub level. Collect, compile, and regularly update who-is-doing-what-where (5W) data from all shelter/NFI partners in Kharkiv. Validate the data for accuracy and use it to produce maps or tables showing coverage and gaps. Share consolidated information products with cluster partners and with the national cluster IMO to feed into the overall Ukraine Shelter Cluster information system. Ensure that partners in Kharkiv are reporting their activities timely and that this information is channeled upward for national situational analysis.  
    o **Progress Monitoring**: Monitor the implementation of the shelter/NFI response in Kharkiv against cluster plans and targets. Track key indicators (e.g. number of households assisted with emergency shelter, number of NFI kits distributed, repairs completed, etc.) and analyze the data to gauge progress. If certain targets are lagging or specific areas/populations are not being reached, identify these gaps and work with partners to address them. Ensure that the sub-national cluster response is contributing to the overall cluster objectives in the Humanitarian Response Plan and is on track to meet agreed outcomes.  
    o **Reporting to National Cluster**: Provide regular situational updates and reports to the National Shelter/NFI Cluster coordination team about the Kharkiv hub. This includes preparing concise written inputs for national cluster reports, situation reports, dashboards, or presentations, highlighting the key developments, achievements, challenges, and support needs in Kharkiv. Critical issues that require higher-level advocacy or decision (e.g. severe gaps, resource shortfalls, access problems) should be promptly raised to the national Cluster Coordinator and cluster lead agency for action. The coordinator may be asked to contribute to periodic cluster products such as the 3/4W matrix, humanitarian bulletins, and cluster meeting updates at national level.  
    o **Maintaining Information Flow**: Serve as the essential link between the Kharkiv hub and the national cluster. The coordinator must ensure effective two-way communication: conveying national cluster guidance, policies, and requests to the partners in Kharkiv, and conversely channeling local partner feedback, concerns, and field realities to the national cluster leadership. This guarantees that the Kharkiv response is consistent with national strategies and that the national plans are informed by ground-level evidence. The coordinator should also verify that any cluster referral or escalation mechanisms (for issues that cannot be solved at hub level) are functional and utilized properly. All relevant information (e.g. minutes, assessments, guidelines) should be disseminated to Kharkiv partners so they remain informed and engaged.
4. **Capacity Building and Local Partner Support**  
    o **Identify Capacity Gaps**: Working closely with cluster members, identify any technical or coordination capacity gaps among organizations responding in Kharkiv. This could include gaps in technical shelter expertise, cluster coordination know-how (especially for local NGOs), or general project management skills. Bring these capacity issues to the attention of the national cluster team and lead agency and contribute to developing a plan to address them.  
    o **Training & Workshops**: Support and coordinate capacity-building initiatives for Shelter/NFI cluster partners and relevant local authorities in Kharkiv. In collaboration with the national cluster, organize trainings or workshops to strengthen partners’ abilities in areas such as emergency shelter construction, safe housing repairs, cluster coordination and reporting, SIDAR, RAIS+, etc.. Facilitate the logistical arrangements for such trainings (venues, participants invitations, materials) and encourage attendance by a broad range of actors, including local NGOs and government counterparts. The aim is to empower local responders to take on greater roles and improve the overall quality of the shelter response.o **Mentoring and Technical Support**: Provide day-to-day guidance to cluster partners in Kharkiv as needed. This may involve mentoring new partners on how to engage with the cluster system, advising NGOs on technical standards for their shelter projects, or linking partners to technical expertise (e.g. structural engineers or architects via the cluster’s technical working groups). Where specialized support is required, coordinate with the national cluster to deploy technical experts to the field or develop remote guidance. Strengthen the capacity of local authorities by involving them in cluster trainings and information sharing, so that they too can better coordinate and plan in the shelter sector.  
    o **Local Coordination Structures**: Work to reinforce local coordination structures and avoid creating parallel systems. If there are existing local government or inter-agency coordination forums in Kharkiv related to shelter or housing (for example, an oblast emergency housing task force), collaborate with and support these structures. The cluster coordinator should aim to integrate humanitarian coordination with any government-led efforts for reconstruction or winterization, aligning humanitarian relief with early recovery where appropriate. By doing so, the cluster helps build local ownership and continuity beyond the immediate emergency phase.
5. **Advocacy, Resource Mobilization and External Representation**  
    o **Advocacy for Needs**: Serve as an advocate for the shelter and NFI needs of conflict-affected populations in Kharkiv Oblast. Using evidence from assessments and partner reports, articulate the priority needs and gaps in forums with donors, UN leadership, or government, in coordination with the cluster lead agency. Ensure that Kharkiv’s needs are duly reflected in national appeals and strategic documents (e.g. the HRP, flash appeals) so that adequate resources are allocated. The coordinator will also collaborate with the Communications/Advocacy focal points to highlight critical shelter issues (such as winterization needs in Kharkiv’s cold climate, or housing repairs in newly accessible areas) in humanitarian advocacy initiatives.  
    o **Mobilizing Resources**: Support efforts to mobilize additional resources (funding, supplies, technical expertise) for the shelter/NFI response in Kharkiv. Work with cluster partners to identify funding opportunities and encourage them to submit proposals that fill the gaps identified. Ensure cluster members are aware of relevant funding mechanisms – for instance, the Ukraine Humanitarian Fund (UHF) or other pooled funds, and any cluster-led funding allocations – and assist them as needed in accessing these opportunities. The coordinator may provide inputs or endorsements for partner funding proposals if required under cluster processes, in a transparent and equitable manner.  
    o **Representation and Relationship Management**: As the subnational cluster focal point, represent the Shelter/NFI Cluster in external engagements at the oblast level. This includes maintaining productive relationships with donors and visiting delegations in Kharkiv by providing briefing updates on the shelter response, escorting them to project sites with partners, etc., in coordination with UNHCR/PIN management. Additionally, coordinate with other clusters’ coordinators to present a unified inter-sectoral picture to local stakeholders. The coordinator should always represent the collective cluster interests and agreed positions when dealing with external actors, consistent with the guidance from the national cluster lead.  
    o **Communication & Media**: In coordination with UNHCR and PIN, serve as a spokesperson for shelter/NFI coordination in Kharkiv if media interaction is needed (ensuring messages align with cluster-wide communications). Any sensitive or high-level advocacy messages should be harmonized with the national cluster (and UNHCR as lead) before public release.
6. **Accountability and Other Responsibilities**  
    o **Accountability to Affected Populations**: Encourage cluster partners to set up complaints and feedback mechanisms for their shelter programs in Kharkiv, and to use community feedback to adjust their interventions. Periodically, gather feedback from community consultations (via partners or directly) about the adequacy of shelter/NFI assistance and present these findings in cluster meetings to inform the collective response.  
    o **Monitoring and Evaluation**: In conjunction with the national cluster, participate in monitoring visits or evaluations of shelter projects in Kharkiv when possible. Help identify best practices and lessons learned from the field. Disseminate lessons learned and success stories among cluster members and to the national level, to improve future programming. If required, assist the national cluster coordinator in conducting Cluster Coordination Performance Monitoring (CCPM) or other evaluations for the subnational cluster.  
    o **Uphold Humanitarian Principles**: Ensure that humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence are adhered to in the Shelter/NFI response in Kharkiv. The coordinator should be vigilant that aid is delivered based on needs and without discrimination. Any issues of concern (e.g. obstruction of aid, politicization, or exclusion of vulnerable groups) should be reported and addressed through appropriate channels.  
    o **Administrative Cluster Support**: Handle essential administrative tasks for cluster coordination at hub level. This includes maintaining the Kharkiv Shelter/NFI mailing lists, sharing relevant documents (meeting minutes, assessment reports, guidelines) with partners in a timely manner, and coordinating any joint field missions. If the cluster has common supply pipelines or stockpiles, coordinate with logistics focal points to manage requests from Kharkiv partners. Ensure that cluster documents and data from Kharkiv are properly archived and accessible to the national cluster team.  
    o **Other Duties**: Carry out any other related tasks as required to fulfill the cluster’s coordination mandate in Kharkiv, as assigned by the National Shelter Cluster Coordination Team or cluster lead agency. This may include supporting the cluster coordination in neighboring oblasts on an interim basis if needed, contributing to the development of funding proposals for cluster coordination, etc. Flexibility and adaptability to emerging demands will be expected

**Working conditions & Support**

As an employee of PIN, the Sub-national Coordinator’s working conditions are according to PIN contract and policies, including working hours, public holidays, Annual Leave, and R&R cycle.The coordinator will inform UNHCR technical supervisor and other relevant team members in advance of plans, to aid coordination across the team. Approval of leave remains with the PIN line manager.  
As agreed between UNHCR and PIN, the Coordinator will work between UNHCR and PIN offices in Kharkiv, with working space provided and supported. Translation and administrative support will be provided by the P6 UNHCR officer.

**Policies/ Duty of care**

The Coordinator must comply with the rules and comply with all applicable terms and conditions specified therein: PIN Code of Conduct, PIN Safety and Security Policy, PIN Anti-Corruption Policy, PIN Safeguarding Policy, PIN Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Policy, PIN Child Protection Policy, PIN Conflicts of Interest Policy, PIN Whistleblowing Policy and other policies governing the organizational work.  
(Through all the above responsibilities, the Subnational Coordinator must maintain an impartial stance, facilitate collaborative decision-making, and work towards the collective outcomes of the Shelter/NFI Cluster.)

**Security situation in Ukraine**

Humanitarian workers continue to operate throughout Ukraine, although the front line areas are being shelled almost constantly, and main cities are being targeted with missiles and UAVs quite regularly. PIN security SOPs require PIN staff to proceed to shelter should the risk level be assessed by the Security Department as the highest (launch of missiles or drones) and remain there until the air raid siren is cancelled, which cumulatively can be several times a week, occasionally for several hours at a time (although shorter periods are as well occurring). While air strikes that were targeting energy infrastructure have finished after winter, they have succeeded in reaching their goals and are likely to resume in late autumn/winter. At the moment military and civilian objects are being targeted, including the west of Ukraine. While Kyiv enjoys relatively strong air defence systems that are intercepting most of the missiles and UAVs, other regions are covered much less significantly which results in bigger damage. Outside of the areas in the vicinity to the contact line, services such as medical care, shops, public transportation as well as restaurants or leisure facilities remain operational.

People in Need is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behavior at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct and is committed to promoting the welfare of children and adults with whom People in Need involves. People in Need expects all staff to perform job duties and responsibilities in accordance with People in Need code of conduct and key policies (available at: [https://www.peopleinneed.net/pin-code-of-conduct-key-policies-4142gp)](https://www.peopleinneed.net/pin-code-of-conduct-key-policies-4142gp)). People in Need Staff will undertake the appropriate level of training.

All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks.

We are committed to ensuring diversity and gender equality within our organization and encourage applicants from diverse backgrounds to apply.

**Main requirements:**

**Education:** A minimum of a BA International relations, Humanitarian assistance, Social/political science, Sociology or similar, knowledge or experience in Architecture, Civil Engineering or other Shelter-related fields will be an asset.  
**Relevant Job Experience:**  
Three years of relevant work experience.  
Knowledge of the Humanitarian reform process and the role of the humanitarian community (UN System, Red Cross Red Crescent Movement, and NGO), preferably in Shelter/NFI sector.  
Knowledge of current humanitarian issues. Good knowledge of shelter-related technical guidelines and standards is considered an asset  
**Required languages (expected overall ability is at least B2 level):** English and Ukrainian

## **We offer:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organization in a challenging context;
- Strategic role with direct contribution to PIN’s funding diversification;
- Close collaboration with senior leadership in a country programme;
- **Salary & Benefits**:
    - Salary based on PIN’s salary scale and HR policies; expected salary range between 2 500 - 3 000 EUR super gross based on experience,
    - Subsistence Allowance of 1440 EUR/month;
    - Hardship of 400 EUR/month;
    - Housing Allowance up to 1000 EUR/month;
    - RnR allowance of 350 EUR/cycle.
- **Time off and Rest:**  
    25 days of holiday annually;  
    10 sick days  
    5 days of RnR up to three cycles per calendar year
- **Travel benefits:**
    - Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
    - Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
    - Reimbursement for the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
    - Travel health insurance covering medical care, incl. the repatriation.
- **Health and Well-being:**  
    24/7 Medical Support available online;  
    Free psychological consultations available online
- **Professional Development:**
    - Free access to e-learning platforms and PIN Learning Hub; PIN’s global Induction Training, and tailored capacity-building opportunities, including Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT).

jobs.title: Uganda Finance Associate
jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

## **About the Role**

You will support the Uganda program with financial analysis, budgeting, and reporting to inform decision-making. In addition, you will collaborate with the Grants Finance team in overseeing the financial aspects of specific Uganda-focused grants, including budgeting, reporting, compliance, and stakeholder engagement.

## **Responsibilities**

**Financial Planning and Analysis**

- You’ll lead the development and continuous update of 5-year rolling forecasts and financial models. You will ensure alignment on financial, operational, and impact assumptions between the Country Director and Global Finance to drive informed, long-term strategic decisions.
- You’ll act as the primary financial advisor for all strategic initiatives, providing rigorous recommendations backed by sensitivity analyses. You will ensure every decision with financial consequences is grounded in Global Finance’s best practices and a deep understanding of potential fiscal outcomes.
- You’ll direct the monthly financial reporting and Budget vs. Actual (BVA) processes in collaboration with department heads. By providing senior leadership with targeted analysis and performance updates, you will serve as a key partner in managing the Uganda program’s fiscal health and communicating results to stakeholders.

**Grants Management**

- You’ll direct the lifecycle of grants by ensuring compliance with donor requirements, overseeing accurate reporting, and continuously enhancing tracking systems and databases for efficiency.
- You’ll lead the development of donor budget reports and forecasts, monitoring grant spending against budgets to ensure fiscal alignment and proactive performance management.
- You’ll manage comprehensive fund flow models to guarantee operational liquidity for restricted activities, while acting as the strategic liaison between Finance, Field, and Fundraising teams to synchronize fund transfers and grant progress.

**Compliance and Control**

- You’ll lead the preparation and timely filing of all Uganda-specific tax returns and statutory obligations in strict alignment with local regulatory frameworks. You will serve as the primary point of contact for internal and external audits, ensuring seamless reviews through meticulous data organization and documentation.
- You’ll strengthen the organization’s financial integrity by proactively identifying control weaknesses and risk exposures. You will partner with country leadership and department heads to drive process improvements, seal compliance gaps, and implement robust governance frameworks.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- A Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or Business Administration, underpinned by a rigorous command of accounting fundamentals and financial reporting standards.
- Over 4 years of progressive experience in finance, consulting, or strategic advisory.
- Full professional qualification in ACCA or CPA (U)
- Experience managing multi-currency grants from major donors.
- Fluency in Power BI and Google Sheets with intermediate Microsoft Excel modeling capabilities. Proven ability to architect complex financial models and leverage data visualization to drive executive-level decision-making.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Jinja, Kampala. Uganda

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Contract Duration**

2 years (renewable to a permanent role based on performance)

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Uganda, Rwanda and Kenya.

## **Application Deadline**

07 September 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.body:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

Owns the facility's Compliance function, combining leadership of the Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) programme with responsibility for facility Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) programme design and oversight. Designs and runs the data system that captures feedstock, production, quality, and end-use data to the standard required by the external verifier. Owns HSE programme design, training, documentation, and audit readiness. Serves as the primary interface with external verifiers, auditors, and regulators (NEMA, DOSH, third-party carbon verifiers). Reports to the Biochar Lead.

## **Responsibilities**

Health, Safety, and Environment (HSE) Leadership

- Design and maintain the facility's HSE programme, including risk registers, emergency response plans, and safety-critical procedures
- Design and deliver HSE training for all facility staff, including inductions, toolbox talks, and emergency drills
- Ensure PPE distribution, safety signage, and site safety infrastructure are in place and maintained
- Support the Production Shift Supervisors, who carry shift-level safety accountability, with the programme, tools, and training they need to enforce safety on shift.
- Coordinate scheduled third-party HSE testing and audits (fire safety, emissions, occupational health)

Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Leadership

- Design, implement, and manage the facility's MRV system covering feedstock inputs, production outputs, quality measurements, and carbon removal calculations.
- Ensure data collection processes across all shifts are accurate, consistent, and traceable to the carbon standards the facility reports against
- Oversee and support the Lab and Quality Technicians in their data recording responsibilities to ensure the standard required for verification
- Develop and maintain data management systems, dashboards, and reporting templates for MRV purposes
- Stay current on evolving carbon standards, methodology requirements, and MRV best practices in the biochar sector

Audit Readiness

- Serve as the primary point of contact with external verifiers, auditors, and certification bodies during verification and audit cycles (carbon, HSE, environmental)
- Prepare and submit monthly and quarterly reports required for carbon credit verification
- Prepare the facility for audits, including documents, site walkthroughs, and evidence for the verifier
- When auditors flag issues, own the corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) through to closure
- Maintain audit-ready documentation across MRV, HSE, and environmental compliance streams at all times

Staff Training

- Train all relevant staff at the facility on MRV data recording requirements, HSE procedures, and the importance of data and safety discipline
- Coordinate cross-functionally with Production, Quality, and Administration on the completeness and accuracy of the data they record for MRV and safety reporting

Farmer Engagement

- Develop and maintain training materials for field staff on correct biochar application methods and how to collect data at the point of delivery
- Deliver refresher training to field teams before the start of each season

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You'll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You'll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Degree in Health and Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, Data Science, Agronomy, or a related field
- Minimum 3 years of experience in HSE, compliance, audit, or environmental data management roles
- Strong background in HSE, OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Act, Kenya, 2007), ISO (International Organization for Standardization), or comparable regulatory environments is a strong advantage
- Comfort engaging with third-party auditors and external verifiers, and comfort designing and running audit-facing programmes
- Familiarity with carbon standards (e.g., Isometric, Puro.earth, EBC, IBI) or carbon credit methodologies is a plus but not required. Successful candidates will build this expertise on the job, supported by Tupande's carbon partners
- Strong data management, reporting, and analytical skills
- Experience with data management platforms, spreadsheets, or environmental monitoring software
- High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data integrity, traceability, and safety discipline
- Willingness to learn on the job across both MRV and HSE domains; the role's success depends on translating a strong compliance foundation across both areas
- Fluent in English; experience working in an East African context is an advantage

Rukanga, Kenya.

Health insurance, paid time off

6 months
