jobs.title: Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Title**

Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator

**Reports To**

Programmes Manager

**Status**

FTE 0.8 - 4 days per week

**Location**

Remote working, based in **The Netherlands, Germany or the United Kingdom**.

*You must have the right to work in the country for which you apply. IDC is unable to support work visa applications or relocation.*

**Languages**

Excellent communication skills in oral and written English

**Compensation**

Per annum depending on skills and experience:

- €36,000 to €42,400 gross annually for 0.8 FTE (based on a full-time equivalent of €45,000 to €53,000)

**Background**

[International Detention Coalition (IDC)](https://idcoalition.org/) is a unique global network of over 200 civil society organisations and individuals in more than 75 countries, which coordinates with members and partners on advocacy, research, coalition and capacity building, to eliminate immigration detention and advance rights-based alternatives to detention. IDC is a highly recognised, impact-driven organisation, offering a stimulating workplace committed to local, national, regional and global change.

**Role Purpose**

The Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator supports the development and implementation of IDC’s fundraising and resource mobilisation efforts, helping to strengthen and diversify the organisation’s funding base, with a focus on mobilising private capital and securing funding from donors and sectors that IDC has not yet reached.

**Role Summary**

The Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator combines strategic thinking with hands-on implementation, and works to identify and pursue funding opportunities, develop high-quality pitches, support donor communications, coordinate with relevant team members, and maintain strong relationships between IDC and its funders, and prospective funders. Working closely with the Executive Director, Programmes Manager, Chief Communications Officer, as well as the finance and regional programme teams, the Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator will help ensure that fundraising is proactive, coordinated, innovative and aligned with IDC’s organisational strategy and programme priorities.

The Partnership and Resource Mobilisation Coordinator will help strengthen IDC’s long-term financial sustainability by building a proactive, relationship-driven and diversified fundraising function. The role will focus on mobilising private philanthropic capital, engaging philanthropic and entrepreneurial networks, and developing strategic relationships with prospective supporters, particularly from sectors that IDC has not yet reached. In parallel, the Coordinator will explore innovative funding approaches and emerging giving channels, translating promising opportunities into meaningful, long-term partnerships that expand and diversify IDC’s funding base.

**Role Responsibilities**

**Strategic Relationship Development & Engagement**

- Support the development and implementation of IDC’s organisational fundraising and resource mobilisation strategy, ensuring that all activities align with IDC’s ethical guidelines and policies.
- Maintain an overview of IDC’s funding priorities, funding needs and development pipeline.
- Support forward planning of fundraising opportunities, including prospecting, cultivation, proposal development and renewal timelines.
- Monitor developments in the funding environment, particularly related to the mobilisation of private capital and identify emerging opportunities, trends and risks relevant to IDC.
- Contribute to organisational discussions about funding priorities, positioning and sustainability.
- Identify opportunities to strengthen and diversify IDC’s funding base, in particular:
    - ***Mobilise private philanthropic capital*** Identify and develop opportunities with corporates, philanthropists, family offices, donor-advised funds (DAFs) and other private funding partners to broaden and diversify IDC’s funding base.
    - ***Explore innovative funding approaches*** Identify and assess emerging funding channels and mechanisms, for example, digital giving and crypto philanthropy, that could unlock new sources of support for IDC.
    - ***Develop impact-oriented partnerships*** Build relationships with funders and partners who share IDC’s mission and are interested in supporting measurable, long-term social change through strategic, mission-aligned partnerships.

**Donor Cultivation and Communication**

- Champion networking and relationship-building opportunities that strengthen the organisation’s profile, partnerships and reach.
- Coordinate follow-up, such as thank you letters and other stewardship communications, with funders and prospective funders, ensuring actions and opportunities are appropriately tracked.
- Prepare background research, briefing materials and correspondence for donor meetings.
- Liaise with the Executive Director, Programmes Manager and relevant team members on potential opportunities related to target funders.
- Coordinate relevant IDC impact stories and social media activities in cooperation with the Chief Communications Officer.

**Development Research and Prospecting**

- Conduct research into new prospective funders as described above, from sectors we have not yet reached, that match IDC’s strategy and priorities, while respecting IDC’s ethical guidelines and policies.
- Oversee and maintain a comprehensive funder database and assess prospective opportunities against IDC’s strategic priorities, programmes, and organisational capacity in consultation with relevant personnel.
- Update IDC’s Executive Director, Programmes Manager and relevant personnel regularly by preparing concise prospect profiles and recommendations for internal consideration.
- Develop and maintain a pipeline of prospective funding opportunities.

**Funding Cultivation**

- Coordinate and contribute to the development of high-quality concept notes, proposals, pitch decks, and tailored partnership propositions for different types of prospective supporters, in collaboration with IDC’s Executive Director and relevant personnel.
- Work with IDC colleagues, including the Chief Communications Officer to translate IDC’s mission, strategic priorities, programmes and approach into compelling and impact-oriented funding propositions, incorporating outcomes from impact monitoring and assessment, such as impact stories that resonate with funders’ interests and priorities.
- Coordinate proposal development processes related to the mobilisation of private capital, including timelines, inputs, review and submission.
- Maintain a forward-looking calendar of funding opportunities, applications, pitches and renewals.

**Development Systems and MEL**

- Maintain and improve systems for tracking prospects, opportunities, applications, funder relationships and development activity.
- Contribute to regular development reporting and pipeline reviews.
- Track fundraising progress against agreed objectives and priorities.
- Capture and share learning from successful and unsuccessful funding approaches.
- Contribute to improving organisational fundraising tools, templates, processes and resources.

**Collaboration and Teamwork**

- Work with relevant team members to develop and maintain a system for grant administration and acquisition, including development of resources and capacity building for IDC team members.
- Work collaboratively with relevant team members, including the Executive Director, Programmes Manager, Chief Communications Officer, as well as the finance and regional programme teams to achieve fundraising goals and objectives.
- Participate in team meetings, training sessions and other organisational activities as needed.

**Core Responsibilities**

- Actively contribute to a culture of agile learning, collaboration, teamwork and support within the IDC team.
- Demonstrate passion and alignment with IDC’s mission, vision and core values of innovation, collaboration, respect, inclusion, representation and being solutions-focused.
- Demonstrate an understanding of IDC policies to ensure a positive and safe working environment for all.
- Actively engage with organisational systems, processes and infrastructure to ensure sustainability and appropriate safeguarding of institutional knowledge, assets and core activities over time.
- Test and use AI tools across relevant areas of work, where appropriate, to enhance efficiency, effectiveness and innovation.

**Essential Qualifications**

- Relevant degree in management, business administration, economics, social sciences, communications, marketing or related field or equivalent professional experience.
- Proven experience and a successful track record in fundraising or development and mobilisation of private capital for the non-profit sector.
- Strategic and entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to recognise opportunities, think creatively, work proactively and develop new approaches to building partnerships and diversifying income.
- Experience maintaining funding pipelines, donor information or similar relationship-management systems.
- Knowledge of fundraising best practices and grant regulations
- Ability to understand complex organisational or programme information and translate it into clear, compelling pitches.
- Demonstrated understanding of the issues faced by refugees, people seeking asylum and migrants, particularly those affected by immigration detention.
- Strong research, analytical and writing skills in English.
- Excellent networking and relationship-building skills.
- Excellent organisational skills including attention to detail, with the ability to multitask and prioritise effectively and work within time constraints and competing deadlines.
- Ability to work independently and proactively in a remote and internationally distributed team.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, donor management software, online research tools and relevant AI technologies.
- Commitment to the mission and values of IDC.
- Ability to travel if needed.

**Desireable**

- Experience engaging with private philanthropists, corporate giving, family foundations, family offices, major donors, donor-advised funds (DAFs), philanthropic advisers or other private funding networks.
- Familiarity with entrepreneurial networks, business angels or other intermediaries who can facilitate access to philanthropic capital.
- Experience exploring alternative funding channels, such as digital giving, crypto philanthropy or other emerging approaches to resource mobilisation.
- An established professional network in philanthropy, private giving, business development or related fields, or the ability to build such networks proactively.
- Understanding of impact-oriented philanthropy and the ability to communicate the social impact of an organisation in ways that resonate with prospective supporters.
- Knowledge of the Spanish language.
- Knowledge of project management/fundraising software such as Salesforce, Sales Navigator, etc.

jobs.title: Training on Practical Business Skills, Market Systems and Cross-Cutting Capacity Building Training for Livelihoods Groups
jobs.body:
## 1. Background and Context

Somali Lifeline Organization (SOLO), in partnership with the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) and with funding from the IKEA Foundation, implements a Livelihoods Programme in the Dadaab Refugee Complex, Garissa County. The programme supports refugee and host-community households to build sustainable, market-oriented livelihoods, with a particular focus on agriculture and allied sectors such as poultry, honey value chain, livestock (meat and milk), and textiles.

Through a rigorous identification process, the programme has organized 350 participants into 10 livelihoods groups of 35 members each (aggregate unit), distributed equally between refugee and host communities (50% / 50%), and drawn from Ifo1, and Dagahaley camps and neighbouring host-community villages including Bulla Kheir and Dadaab Host. Members have self-selected livelihoods sectors and are now ready to move from basic registration into structured capacity building that equips them to run their enterprises profitably and sustainably.

SOLO/NRC now seeks to engage a qualified training consultant or firm to design and deliver a practical, hands-on training package covering two complementary thematic areas: (a) core business skills, and (b) market participation and cross-cutting skills including gender and social inclusion, leadership, life skills, legal awareness, and quality and branding.

## 2. Rationale

Many group members currently operate small-scale production activities with limited exposure to formal business practice: informal or absent record keeping, ad hoc pricing that does not reliably cover costs, weak customer care and marketing practice, and limited experience negotiating with buyers or honouring contracts. Refugee members in particular face additional barriers to market participation, including restricted movement, limited legal and regulatory awareness, and constrained access to formal markets, while women across both communities often face compounded barriers linked to time poverty, decision-making power, and access to leadership roles within groups.

A structured, practical training package is therefore required to convert production-focused groups into viable, market-oriented enterprises; to strengthen group governance and inclusion so that gains are equitably shared; and to build the confidence, negotiation ability, and legal literacy members need to participate safely and profitably in local markets.

## 3. Purpose and Objectives

### 3.1 Overall Objective

To strengthen the business, market participation, governance, and life-skills capacities of 350 members of 10 SOLO/NRC-supported livelihoods groups in Dadaab, enabling them to operate viable, market-oriented, and gender-inclusive enterprises.

### 3.2 Specific Objectives

1. Equip participants with practical entrepreneurship, record keeping, costing and pricing, customer care, and marketing skills applicable to their specific livelihoods sector.
2. Build participants' understanding of local market dynamics and demand, and strengthen their negotiation and contract management skills.
3. Strengthen gender and social inclusion practice, and leadership and governance capacity, within the 10 groups.
4. Build participants' life skills and soft skills to support individual and collective decision-making, resilience, and cooperation.
5. Raise awareness of the legal and regulatory environment relevant to trading and group enterprise in and around Dadaab.
6. Strengthen participants' understanding and practice of product quality and branding to improve market competitiveness.

## 4. Scope of Work

The assignment covers two complementary training components, to be delivered to each of the 10 groups. The consultant/firm is expected to develop a detailed curriculum against the indicative content below, adapt it to the specific sectors and literacy levels of each group, and translate/deliver in Somali and/or Kiswahili as appropriate.

### 4.1 Component A. Practical Business Skills

**Sub-topic, indicative content, and indicative duration**

Entrepreneurship; entrepreneurial mindset; opportunity identification; business planning basics tailored to the participant's sector (poultry, kitchen gardening, crop farming, livestock) for 0.5 day

Record keeping: Simple, low-literacy-friendly tools for recording sales, expenses, stock, and savings; separating business and household finances for 1 day

Costing and pricing: Calculating production/unit costs, setting profitable prices, break-even basics, responding to competitor and seasonal price changes, for 1 day

Customer care: building customer relationships and trust, handling complaints, and repeat-business practices for 0.5 day

Marketing strategies: identifying customers and market channels, low-cost promotion, and group/collective marketing approaches for 1 day

### 4.2 Component B. Market Participation, Governance, and Crosscutting Skills

**Sub-topic, Indicative content and Indicative duration**

Market dynamics and demand: Understanding local/Dadaab market structures, seasonality, demand assessment, and identifying viable market opportunities for 1 day

Negotiation skills: Practical negotiation techniques with buyers, suppliers, and off-takers, including role-play practice for 0.5 day

Contract management: understanding, negotiating, and honoring simple supply/off-take agreements; managing disputes for 0.5 day

Gender and social inclusion, leadership and governance, GESI awareness, equitable participation in group decision-making, group leadership roles, and transparent and accountable group governance structures for 1 day

Life skills and soft skills: communication, teamwork, problem-solving, conflict resolution, stress management, and goal setting for 0.5 day

Legal and regulatory awareness; relevant national and county trading regulations; business registration basics; rights and obligations of refugee and host traders for 0.5 day.

Quality and branding; basic quality control/assurance for produce and simple branding and packaging to strengthen market competitiveness for 1 day.

*Total indicative contact time is 4 days for Component A and 5 days for Component B per group (9 training days), plus follow-up coaching described in Section 7. The consultant/firm may propose an alternative sequencing or balance of days, with justification, in their technical proposal.*

## 5. Target Participants

Livelihoods groups formed under the SOLO/NRC registration exercise - 10

Members per group, standard group size - 35

Total participants: 10 groups × 35 members = 350

Community distribution: Refugee community / Host community (50% / 50%)

Camp locations include Ifo1 and Dagahaley camps (5 groups) and Host-community locations - Bulla Kheir, Dadaab (5 groups)

Participants include both male and female members across a wide age range, with varying levels of literacy. The consultant/firm must design and facilitate sessions that are accessible to low-literacy adult learners and give equal opportunity for participation to women, men, youth and persons with disabilities. SOLO/NRC will share group-level lists (anonymized) confirming exact composition by sex, age, camp/village, and sector at contract signing.

## 6. Training Methodology

The training must be practical and participatory and should draw on adult-learning principles. At minimum, the consultants/firm are expected to:

- Use experiential, hands-on methods: role play, simulations, group work, case studies, and, where feasible, market/field visits rather than lecture-based delivery.
- Adapt materials for low-literacy participants, using pictorial, oral, and demonstration-based tools alongside written materials.
- Deliver in Somali, with facilitators fluent in the languages spoken by participants.
- Apply gender-sensitive facilitation, ensuring equal voice and participation for women and men and reasonable accommodation for persons with disabilities.
- Conduct a pre-training assessment to establish baseline knowledge/skills and a post-training assessment to measure learning gains.
- Support each group to produce a simple, practical output from the training (e.g., a basic costing sheet, record-keeping template, or group action plan) rather than knowledge alone.
- Provide at least two follow-up coaching/mentoring visits per group after the classroom training to reinforce learning and support application (see Section 7).

## 7. Duration and Indicative Schedule

The assignment is expected to run over approximately 8–10 weeks from contract signing, inclusive of inception, delivery to all 10 groups, follow-up coaching, and reporting. This is an indicative timeframe; the consultants/firm should propose a detailed work plan and team composition (e.g., number of parallel facilitation teams) in their technical proposal, with justification for any variation from the indicative schedule below.

**Phase**

**Activity**

**Indicative duration**

Phase 1

Inception: desk review, curriculum design/adaptation, translation of materials, submission of inception report and training plan - 1 week

Phase 2

Delivery of Component A and Component B classroom training to all 10 groups (9 contact days per group; groups may be trained in parallel by a facilitation team or sequentially) - 4–6 weeks

Phase 3

Follow-up coaching/mentoring visits (minimum two per group) and post-training assessment- 2–3 weeks

Phase 4

Consolidation, final reporting and handover of materials and datasets - 1 week

*Exact start and end dates will be confirmed at contract signing.*

## 8. Deliverables

**Deliverable**

Inception report, including finalized curriculum, session plans, and translated/localized training materials— Within 1 week of contract signing

Pre- and post-training assessment tools and completed assessment data/report

Tools before delivery; report after each group's training

Signed attendance registers for all 10 groups, disaggregated by sex, age, camp/host village, and group—throughout delivery

Group-level practical outputs (e.g., costing sheets, record-keeping templates, group action plans)

By end of classroom training per group; follow-up coaching/mentoring visit reports (minimum 2 per group) throughout Phase 3

Final training report, including methodology, participation data, assessment results, challenges, lessons learned and recommendations within 2 weeks of assignment completion

Provide full set of training materials/manuals and a facilitator's guide handed over to SOLO/NRC for future use with final report.

## 9. Roles and Responsibilities

**SOLO / NRC will**

Mobilize and confirm participants and group schedules

Arrange venues, seating and any required camp access/movement permissions

Provide available baseline/registration data on groups (sector, camp/village, sex, age)

Provide a technical focal point for oversight, quality assurance and approvals

Cover participant transport/refreshments if budgeted separately from this contract

**The Consultant / Firm will**

Design and adapt the curriculum and all training materials

Provide qualified, experienced facilitators for all sessions

Deliver all training, assessments and coaching visits per the agreed schedule

Prepare and submit all deliverables in Section 8 to agreed quality and timelines

Comply with SOLO/NRC and donor safeguarding, PSEA and code-of-conduct requirements

## 10. Duty Station and Reporting

The assignment will be delivered in Dadaab and Bula Kheir, with sessions held in Ifo 1 and Dagahley camps and in the listed host-community villages. The consultants/firm is responsible for its own travel, accommodation and logistics within Dadaab unless otherwise agreed in the contract.

The consultant/firm will report to the SOLO Livelihoods Project Manager, in coordination with the NRC livelihoods focal point, and will provide brief progress updates after each group's training in addition to the formal deliverables listed above.

## 11. Required Qualifications and Experience

The firm (or team) should demonstrate:

- Registration as a training consultant, firm or institution, with a valid business registration and tax compliance certificate.
- A minimum of 3–5 years' experience designing and delivering business/entrepreneurship or market systems development (MSD) training, preferably with refugee, IDP or host-community populations.
- Demonstrated experience working in Dadaab, Garissa County, or comparable arid/semi-arid and displacement-affected contexts.
- A facilitation team with combined expertise across all thematic areas in Section 4, including at least one facilitator experienced in gender and social inclusion (GESI) programming.
- Facilitators fluent in Somali, with experience adapting training for low-literacy adult audiences.
- A track record of participatory, practical training methodology (not purely lecture-based), supported by references or sample materials.
- Familiarity with humanitarian/NGO safeguarding standards, including PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) and child safeguarding.
- Logistical capacity to mobilize a facilitation team to deliver training across 10 groups within the proposed timeframe.

## 12. Safeguarding, Ethics and Data Protection

The consultant/firm and all facilitators must sign and comply with SOLO’s Code of Conduct, Child Safeguarding Policy, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) policy prior to engagement. Any incidents or concerns arising during training must be reported immediately through SOLO's safeguarding reporting channels.

All participant data (names, ID/phone numbers, attendance and assessment records) collected during the assignment is confidential and remains the property of SOLO. The firm may not share, publish or reuse participant data for any purpose outside this assignment without prior written consent, and must securely store and, on request, delete or return all such data at the end of the assignment.

## 13. Budget and Payment Terms

Interested consultants/firms must submit a detailed, itemized financial proposal in Kenya Shillings (KES) covering facilitator fees, training materials, travel/logistics within Dadaab, and any other costs required to deliver the scope of work.

Payment will be made in instalments linked to approved deliverables, indicatively: 30% on submission and approval of the inception report; 40% on completion of training and coaching for all 10 groups; 30% on submission and approval of the final report and materials. Exact terms will be confirmed in the signed contract, subject to applicable taxes.

## 14. Evaluation Criteria

Technical proposals meeting a minimum qualifying score of 70% will have their financial proposals opened and scored. Overall award will be based on the combined technical and financial score below.

**Criteria**

Technical proposal: understanding of the assignment, methodology, work plan, and curriculum outline- 30%

Team composition and qualifications, including thematic coverage and language capacity- 20%

Relevant experience in Dadaab/refugee or comparable contexts, with references- 20%

Financial proposal (cost-effectiveness and value for money)- 30%

**Total - 100%**

## ABOUT US

**Desired start date: ASAP**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**  
**Location: CABO DELGADO**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.

Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.

At the beginning of 2025, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganisation of operations to maintain essential activities. This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement and unpredictable access since mid-2024.

In early 2026, the mission entered a new phase with the confirmation of significant short-term emergency funding, alongside the launch of a major 3-year development-oriented WASH/FSL/Education project in Consortium. This shift requires strengthened programmatic oversight to manage simultaneous emergency and longer-term interventions within a rapidly evolving operational context.

Despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, IFSAN, UNICEF and WFP.

Projects and activities include:

\- Rapid Response Mechanism to shocks (conflict, natural disasters, epidemics): multisectoral WASH / Food / Shelter-NFI assistance through CVA or in-kind distributions

\- WASH: rehabilitation of large water networks, water points construction/rehabilitation, WASH in schools and health facilities, rainwater harvesting systems, sanitation and hygiene promotion

\- FSL: seeds and equipment distributions, support to cooperatives, cash-for-work and income-generating activities

\- Shelter/NFI: mainly emergency shelter and NFI through RRM

Around 50 staff in total across the mission in April 2026, but it will increase in May/June with the new funding.

SI operates 3 bases:

• Pemba (Coordination / Operational Base): 27 staff

• Mueda (Operational Base): 19 staff

• Mocímboa da Praia (Operational Sub-base): 4 staff

• Chiure (Operational Sub-base) to be opened: 6 staff

The DCDP is based in Pemba and covers operations in all bases of SI in Mozambique.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The Deputy CD for Programs (DCDP) is responsible for the overall supervision, quality and strategic orientation of Solidarités International programmatic operations and MEAL systems in Cabo Delgado. S/he ensures effective, high-quality and compliant implementation of programmes in line with SI strategy and donor requirements. S/he supervises Program Managers and the MEAL Manager, supports adaptive programming, and works closely with the Area Coordinator and field teams to strengthen coordination, accountability and operational continuity.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

1- Major mission restructuring following BHA funding cuts in early 2025, with reduced staffing and evolving organisational set-up, followed by a rapid increase of funding in 2026, including short-term emergency grants and a multi-year development project  
2- Short implementation timelines for emergency projects (6 months) requiring strong planning, monitoring and adaptive management  
3- Volatile and unpredictable security context requiring continuous analysis and flexible programming  
4- Multi-base programme (Pemba, Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Chiure) with limited resources and high coordination needs  
5- High workload linked to simultaneous project closures, scale-up of emergency response and launch of new projects  
6- Strengthening and maintaining relationships with local authorities and coordination bodies in a sensitive operational environment

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

1- Ensure structured supervision of ongoing programmes across all bases and also the suppervision of the technicall departments (WASH, FSL, RRM Co, and MEAL)  
2- Strengthen MEAL systems and ensure effective use of monitoring data and accountability mechanisms for programmatic decision-making  
3- Ensure quality closure of ending projects and structured launch of new projects (Apri-May 2026)  
4- Reinforce program compliance with donor requirements and internal procedures  
5- Clarify roles, workflows and coordination mechanisms between Program, MEAL and Support departments  
6- Lead and coordinate proposal development with Project Managers, Technical Coordinators and the Grants Department  
7- Strengthen representation and collaboration with provincial and district authorities, clusters and key partners

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Security level 2 in Pemba with limited constraints.

Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia are security level 3, with more restrictions. Movements and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

The security situation remains volatile, with unpredictable insurgent attacks and evolving dynamics involving armed actors. Close monitoring of the context is required for daily movement validation. Travel to field bases is mainly via UNHAS flights.

## YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Master in humanitarian action, development, international law or any other technical area related to the humanitarian sector

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Strong Project Cycle Management skills
2. Solid background or experience in at least one technical
3. Strong understanding of MEAL systems and accountability mechanisms, with ability to ensure effective use of monitoring data for programmatic decision-making
4. Good knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong information management capacity and ability to coordinate multiple activities across bases
2. Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills
3. Ability to represent SI with authorities, partners and coordination bodies
4. Strong analytical capacity and ability to adapt programming to evolving contexts
5. Capacity to supervise and structure teams in a complex operational environment

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English (mandatory)
2. Portuguese (strong asset)
3. Spanish or Italian (asset)

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3300 gross per month (3000 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a coastal city with good living conditions for expatriates, including stable water and electricity and reliable 4G internet. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day. SI provides comfortable office and guesthouse facilities close to amenities.

The position is based in Pemba, with frequent visits to the bases. Field bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour. Living conditions in field locations are basic but functional.

jobs.title: Call for Expression of Interest – Pool of Expertise for Facility 1325
jobs.body:
**Project Description**  
As part of the project implemented by Expertise France, the 1325 Facility initiative, we are seeking to expand our pool of gender experts and practitioners in the Women, Peace, and Security agenda in the Syrian Arab Republic.

**Project/Context Description**  
In Syria, more than a decade of armed conflict has led to high levels of widespread violence, massive population displacement, territorial fragmentation, and a severe deterioration of essential public services. In this context, women and girls are disproportionately affected by violence, particularly sexual and gender-based violence, insecurity linked to forced displacement, increased economic precariousness, and the shrinking of civic space. At the same time, despite their central role in community resilience, humanitarian aid, local mediation, and the maintenance of the social fabric, their participation in formal peace, governance, and security processes remains limited, and they are underrepresented in decision-making spaces.  
Thus, in a context marked by still-fragile dynamics of transition and political realignment, as well as significant momentum surrounding prospects for stabilization, issues related to the protection of women’s and girls’ rights and their inclusion in decision-making processes are taking on increased importance. However, these opportunities remain hampered by persistent insecurity, institutional fragmentation, and protection and justice mechanisms, which contribute to maintaining their marginalization in political, security, and humanitarian responses.  
As part of the ongoing political transition in Syria, the transitional authorities have demonstrated a commitment to more inclusive governance and the country’s institutional reconstruction. This commitment, reflected in official statements and certain frameworks supported by the international community, emphasizes the promotion of human rights, national reconciliation, and broader participation by all segments of Syrian society, including women. Efforts have also been announced to strengthen the inclusivity of political processes and consolidate transitional institutions.  
Nevertheless, despite these stated intentions, women’s actual participation in decision-making bodies remains limited, and their representation in governance structures remains marginal. This persistent gap between commitments and concrete implementation highlights the structural challenges facing the transition, in a context where security, institutional, and humanitarian constraints continue to weigh heavily on its trajectory.

The 1325 Facility as a response to these challenges  
In the face of these structural challenges, the implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda remains fragile and insufficient. It is within this context that the 1325 Facility project, implemented by Expertise France and funded by the French Development Agency (AFD), is situated. The 1325 Facility is designed as a flexible and targeted support mechanism aimed at strengthening the implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda in fragile and conflict-affected contexts. The project supports national and local actors—particularly human’s right organizations, public institutions, and civil society partners—through technical and strategic support, capacity building, and the promotion of a more inclusive participation in peace, security, and governance processes.  
Drawing on a human rights-based approach, women’s leadership, and conflict-sensitive analysis, the 1325 Facility aims to contribute to more inclusive, sustainable, and effective responses to conflict prevention, the protection of populations, and peacebuilding in Syria.  
The 1325 Facility aims to support actors working on the Women, Peace, and Security agenda through enhanced technical, strategic, and operational support that is, above all, tailored to local realities. Mobilizing national experts with diverse backgrounds, connections, and experiences is a key lever in implementing this support. The essential requirement is that the mobilized experts possess a mastery of international, regional, and national normative frameworks—tailored to each country—and an in-depth understanding of local, institutional, and community dynamics to ensure maximum impact.  
Approach promoted by the 1325 Facility:  
Through the 1325 Facility, France promotes an ambitious, integrated, and context-sensitive approach aimed at strengthening the effective implementation of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda. This approach is implemented for the benefit of national and local actors, particularly civil society organizations, public institutions, and technical and financial partners. It is based on the following guiding principles:

1. Addressing the structural determinants of gender equality and women’s empowerment in crisis and post-crisis contexts by moving beyond ad hoc responses in favor of sustainable change,
2. Promoting an integrated territorial approach based on a detailed analysis of local dynamics of conflict, power, and gender.
3. Prioritize actions in support of girls and women, while involving boys and men (with a focus on adolescents and young adults)
4. Promote an approach focused on changing behaviors and social norms generally attributed to men and women, power relations, and institutional practices—particularly in terms of representation and at decision-making levels.
5. Sustainably strengthen the capacities of local actors by prioritizing forms of technical support that promote ownership, leadership, and sustainability.
6. Adopt a conflict-sensitive approach that is mindful of the risks of tension, exclusion, or political co-optation, and aims to contribute to the prevention of violence and social cohesion.

**An integrated intervention framework organized by sectoral areas:**

The intervention framework of the 1325 Facility is structured around thematic and sectoral areas that are mobilized in a complementary manner and in accordance with the needs expressed by local actors and national priorities, with the aim of strengthening the key levers of the 1325 Facility agenda. For example, these areas may include governance, peace and security, prevention of and response to sexual and gender-based violence, conflict-related violence, women’s participation and leadership in decision-making processes, particularly peace negotiation mechanisms, as well as strengthening the organizational, administrative, financial, and technical capacities of civil society organizations, particularly those working for women’s rights. They may also include knowledge generation, contextual analysis, and knowledge capitalization to improve the quality and impact of interventions.

Thus, the interventions of the 1325 Facility aim to contribute to:

- Promoting sustainable changes in social and institutional norms by supporting transformative gender approaches tailored to local dynamics.
- Supporting the leadership and organizational development of human’s rights organizations by strengthening their operational and structural capacities, as well as their ability to influence and engage in dialogue with national and international authorities.
- Preventing and responding to conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence by supporting public policies, coordination mechanisms, protection systems, and conflict-sensitive and inclusive community-based approaches
- The provision of sexual and reproductive health services through the maintenance of accessible, high-quality public SRH (sexual and reproductive health) services, as well as by strengthening the capacity of women and adolescent girls to make free, informed, and responsible choices regarding SRH. This capacity is a key factor in their empowerment and in the region’s demographic transition.
- The reduction of all forms of gender-based violence, such as early marriage and pregnancy, violence in schools and hospitals, as well as all forms of violence linked to crises and conflicts.
- Systematically integrate an inclusive approach into peace and security policies, strategies, and programs through gender-based analysis, operational tools, training, and institutional support.
- Inclusive participation in economic, political, and social decision-making bodies through support for quota policies in decision-making bodies and the strengthening of women’s leadership.

Through this approach, the 1325 Facility aims to achieve sustainable outcomes such as:

- greater national and local ownership of the Women, Peace, and Security agenda;
- strengthening the technical and strategic capacities of the actors involved;
- Increasing effective inclusive participation in peace and security processes

**Desired Qualifications**

- At least 7 years of experience in one of the following areas: Women, Peace, and Security; gender equality; prevention of and response to sexual and gender-based violence and/or conflict-related violence; women’s participation in peace, security, and governance processes; or social cohesion in crisis, conflict, or post-conflict contexts, as an individual consultant or trainer;
- Proven experience in supporting the integration of women’s and girls’ rights and the WPS agenda into international cooperation projects, working with the public sector (ministries and decentralized state agencies) and civil society organizations;
- Proven experience in designing and implementing capacity-building and training initiatives for public actors and civil society organizations, particularly those working on women’s rights, on topics related to the WPS agenda. These initiatives may address both WPS-related content and the administrative, financial, and technical capacity-building of the organizations being supported;
- Proven experience in the design, implementation, and monitoring and evaluation of international cooperation projects in fragile or conflict-affected contexts in the Middle East, including Syria;
- Proven ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder activities and represent Expertise France with institutional partners and civil society organizations within the scope of assigned missions.
- Strong writing skills: developing assessments and methodologies, drafting project design and initiation documents;
- Ability to produce practical tools: guides and educational materials, and experience in training trainers.
- Fluency in Arabic (required) and fluency in English or French (at least one of the two languages required) ;
- Knowledge of AFD tools and procedures is an asset;
- Experts must become familiar with the following tools and procedures:
- Tools for analyzing and integrating gender and the FPS agenda
- Gender toolkits produced by AFD
- The “Do No Harm” approach promoted by AFD
- The project cycle according to AFD procedures.

**Additional Information**  
We are primarily seeking Syrian national experts with in-depth knowledge of the local context and, if from the diaspora, who have already carried out missions in Syria. International candidates are not a priority for this mission.  
Experts may be called upon for short-term expert assignments of varying durations (ranging from one week to several months), either in person (primarily in Damascus, depending on access conditions) and/or remotely (working from home), depending on the needs of local partners.  
Please specify your areas of expertise and your availability for travel in your application.

jobs.title: Consultant.e Expert.e en gouvernance des données – Actualisation du cadre de gouvernance des données de la coopérative hulo
jobs.body:
**Titre :** Consultant.e Expert.e en gouvernance des données – Actualisation du cadre de gouvernance des données de la coopérative hulo

**Date :** 15/10/2026

**Référence : ​**HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-003​

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La Coopérative hulo, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur de l’humanitaire. En décembre 2025, hulo compte 16 organisations membres : ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, la Croix-Rouge française (CRF), Fleet Forum, Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross, International Rescue Committee (IRC), INTERSOS, Médecins du Monde (MDM), Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Solidarités International (SI), et Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement. Les « initiatives mutualisées » de hulo, sont déjà en cours dans 7 countries (Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, RDC, Liban, Jordanie pour la crise syrienne, Colombie, et Tchad). Les activités sur le terrain sont composées d'achats mutualisés, de ressources humaines partagées, d’une plateforme web permettant la mise en commun de ressources, et d’initiatives environnementales mutualisées. Ces initiatives permettent d'économiser du temps et de l'argent, d'améliorer la qualité des biens et des services fournis, et donc de fournir une aide plus efficace à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin.

Hulo développe actuellement son écosystème Data autour de Microsoft Fabric, avec l'objectif de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence.

Hulo a développé un cadre de gouvernance des données pour garantir l'exactitude, la sécurité, la conformité et l'exploitabilité des données tout au long de leur cycle de vie dans un cadre de gouvernance coopérative.

L’utilisation de services spécifiques liés à ces données se développant rapidement, hulo souhaite renforcer le cadre de gouvernance existant pour optimiser l’utilisation et la sécurisation des données de la coopérative.

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'accompagner hulo dans la revue, l’évolution et la préparation au déploiement d’un cadre actualisé de gouvernance des données composé de principes, de rôles, de processus, de normes et de contrôles qui garantit que les données hulo sont exactes, sécurisées, conformes et exploitables tout au long de leur cycle de vie.

Le.la consultant.e apportera une expertise indépendante en matière de :

- Data quality management
- Data stewardship and ownership
- Data privacy and security
- Data policies and standards
- Data integration and interoperability

La mission devra permettre à hulo de disposer d'un cadre de gouvernance des données actualisé et de recommandations spécifiques pour le déploiement et le suivi interne.

**Priorités et livrables :**

1\. Analyse de situation -

- Contexte et enjeux spécifiques à la coopérative hulo
    - Identification et prise de connaissance des politiques existantes
    - Identification des exigences éthiques, réglementaires et de gouvernance coopérative
    - Identification des données concernées, de leur qualité et de l’infrastructure technique de gestion des données.
    - Identification des perspectives futures à considérer (IA, privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs)…)
    - Collecte des besoins exprimés
- « Gap analysis » du cadre existant
    - Analyse comparative entre les enjeux identifiés et le cadre existant
    - Identification
    - Recensement et priorisation des points critiques d’amélioration
    - Validation de la proposition d’actualisation.

2\. Actualisation du cadre existant

- Echanges avec les postes impactés par les changements
- Actualisation du cadre existant à trois niveaux :
    - Principes (niveau stratégique) : engagements généraux applicables à l'ensemble de l'entreprise ;
    - Politiques (niveau tactique) : règles spécifiques régissant les activités de gestion des données ;
    - Normes et procédures (niveau opérationnel) : instructions détaillées de mise en œuvre.
    - Glossaire métier en impliquant activement les responsables des données, en tant que garants des définitions, qui les défendront et les maintiendront au fil du temps.
- Présentation et actualisation en fonction des retours.

3\. Mise en œuvre

- Recommandations sur les livrables, calendrier, budgétisation et responsabilités du déploiement
- Recommandations sur les solutions techniques associées à la mise en œuvre. Exemple - Catalogue de données (Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview ou similaire) pour la gestion du glossaire, la traçabilité et l’automatisation des workflows.
- Définition d’un cadre de suivi (Indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), notamment sur les domaines suivants - couverture du glossaire, scores de qualité des données par domaine, problèmes de gestion en suspens, taux de conformité aux politiques et indicateurs d’adoption du catalogue.
- Proposition d’un modèle personnalisé de maturité (inspiré de modèles comme le DCAM ou DAMA-DMBOK) pour évaluer la situation actuelle et définir la feuille de route permettant de passer au niveau de maturité supérieur.

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la data governance ;
- Expérience démontrée dans la création et la révision de cadre de gouvernance de données ;
- Bonne connaissance de la sécurité des données ;
- Expérience de l'écosystème Microsoft Azure ;
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaire contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles ;
- Capacité démontére à pouvoir travailler sur des documents en anglais.

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist et le Data Protection Officer.

**Calendrier**

Octobre – Décembre 2026

**Candidature et processus de contractualisation :**

Le.la Consultant.e séléctionné.e sera contractualisé.e par hulo pour une durée de 10 à 15jours, sans obligation de travailler à temps plein pour hulo durant cette période. Il.Elle devra mettre en avant les étapes clefs de la consultance dans sa candidature. Les taches décrites peuvent être menées à bien à 100% en distanciel.

Hulo appelle à candidater pour la provision des services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultant.e.s intéressé.e.s devront soumettre leurs candidatures avec propositions financières détaillées (taux journalier avec descriptifs des autres coûts, en plus d’une proposition de coût total), proposition pour répondre aux termes de référence, calendrier et CV renseignant sur les compétences et expériences qualifiant le.la candidat.e pour répondre au service détaillé ci-dessus.

**Critères de sélection:**

Les candidatures seront évaluées selon les critères suivants :

- Expertise en data governance
- Expertise sur la sécurité des données
- Expérience démontrée dans la création et la révision de cadre de gouvernance de données ;
- Compréhension des besoins métier et capacité à les traduire en exigences techniques
- Capacité d’analyse et d’écriture en anglais
- Communication, documentation et transfert de compétences
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaires et/ou de gestion coopérative contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles ;
- Capacité démontrée à pouvoir travailler sur des documents en anglais.

jobs.title: Consultant - Consolidation of Technical Guidance on Return, Readmission and Reintegration
jobs.body:
**Job Identification:** 23354

**Posting Date:** 16/10/2026 7:57 AM

**Apply Before:** 29/10/2026 11:59 PM

**Contract Type**: Consultancy (3 months with possibility of extension)

**Initial Contract Duration:** Three months

**Org Type:** Headquarters

**Vacancy Type:** Consultancy

**Recruiting Type:** Consultancy

**Grade:** UG

**Is this S/VN based in an L3 office or in support to an L3 emergency response?:** No

**Short Description**

IOM, UN Migration Agency in Geneva, Switzerland is looking for a consultant who will consolidate and harmonize existing guidance on return, readmission and reintegration including the readmission manual and the technical guidance on return and reintegration, into a single integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR).

**Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

To support rights-based migration governance, the consultant will consolidate and harmonize existing guidance on return, readmission and reintegration including the readmission manual and the technical guidance on return and reintegration, into a single integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR). The final document will be primarily targeted at government practitioners and authorities responsible for the development, implementation and management of return, readmission and reintegration processes, while also serving other relevant stakeholders. The guidance will aim to clarify the applicable standards and frameworks for rights-based RRR management and provide concrete operational recommendations to help practitioners establish or strengthen RRR systems including through effective inter-State cooperation.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Within the Department of Mobility Pathways and Inclusion, under the overall supervision of the Head of the Border Management, Returns and Readmission Division, and under technical management of the Head of the Return and Reintegration team and the Head of the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit, and in close coordination with Cooperation on Migration and Partnerships to Achieve Sustainable Solutions (COMPASS).

**Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

Produce a coherent and comprehensive integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR) based on the consolidation and harmonization of the existing draft of the Technical Guidance on Return and Reintegration, developed by IOM’s Regional Office in Vienna, and the draft Readmission Manual, developed by the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit in IOM’s Headquarters. More precisely the consultant will:

1. Identify overlaps and complementarities, and propose the appropriate structure and lay out of a coherent document for optimal user experience.
2. Consult appropriate teams and partners as needed.
3. Integrate the concepts and guidance from both documents into a single coherent narrative.
4. Ensure the final document is primarily targeted at government practitioners and authorities responsible for the development, implementation and management of return, readmission and reintegration processes, while also serving other relevant stakeholders.
5. Prepare dissemination material for external use.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

Timely Delivery:

- Adherence to the agreed-upon schedule for each deliverable, including meetings, reports, and final submission dates.

Quality of Output:

- The deliverables are of good quality, technically sound, with attention to coherent structure, flow, writing style, and user experience.

  
**Category B Consultants: Tangible and measurable outputs of the work assignment**

1. First deliverable – Inception meeting with the Return and Reintegration team and the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit. Proposed new structure for the document. First instalment payment - Deliverable by email.
2. Second deliverable – First draft of the consolidated guidance - Deliverable by email.
3. Third deliverable – Revised draft of the consolidated guidance based on comments received - Second instalment payment - Deliverable by email.
4. Final deliverable – Final guidance – Third and Final instalment payment (no less than 25% of overall contract value) - Deliverable by email.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Economics, Business Administration, Social Sciences, Law, Development Studies, International Affairs, or a related field.

**Experience**

- Experience in guidance development, policy and technical support to governments; and,
- Previous experience working with international organizations, NGOs, or government entities involved in migration and protection assistance is desirable.

**Skills**

- Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present findings in a clear and concise manner; and,
- Knowledge of return migration, readmission, reintegration and protection.

**Languages**

IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish. All staff members are required to be fluent in one of the three languages.

For this consultancy, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:
