jobs.title: Capacity Building Specialist (Public Health) – Philippines
jobs.body:
**A.** **About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific and Africa. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to serve scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs on the strategic themes of Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. Our strategic themes are complemented and underpinned by the cross-cutting themes of gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**B. Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Action Department (PCA) strengthens the capacities of governments, response organizations, civil society, private sector actors, and at‑risk communities to prepare for, respond to, recover from disasters and adapt to the increasing risks associated with disasters and climate change. PCA emphasizes locally led preparedness and adaptation, ensuring that resilience-building efforts are rooted in local systems, institutions, knowledge, and leadership.

PCA contributes to ADPC’s regional mandate by designing and implementing programs aligned with ADPC’s strategic priority areas, including Climate Services, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Health Risk Management, Nature‑based Solutions, Resilient Recovery, and Financing for Resilience, among others. These programs support countries in advancing the Sendai Framework, SDGs, and the Paris Agreement, while strengthening institutional, community, and system-wide resilience. The department also ensures that all interventions incorporate ADPC’s core cross‑cutting themes, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Disaster and Climate Innovations, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation, as foundational elements across program design, implementation, monitoring, and knowledge generation. PCA is structured into three functional units that work together to deliver integrated preparedness and climate action programming:

- **Climate Action and Impact (CAI) –** driving climate action strategies, impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation systems, and evidence generation.
- **Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR)** – strengthening preparedness capacities, emergency response planning, and health risk management.
- **Resilience Building and Localization (RBL)** – supporting resilient recovery, localization approaches, and capacity development at national and subnational levels.

Through multi‑country operations, technical advisory services, and strategic partnerships, PCA ensures coherent, evidence‑based, and impact‑driven delivery of ADPC’s mandate across Asia and the Pacific.

**C. Statement of Intent:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) seeks to strengthen its regional programming and technical capacity for public health emergency preparedness and response across the Asia-Pacific region. Building on its experience in disaster preparedness, emergency response, regional cooperation, and multi-country program implementation, ADPC aims to strengthen its support to countries and communities in preparing for and responding to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Effective public health emergency preparedness and response require timely and coordinated action, supported by strong technical and operational capacities, effective coordination mechanisms, and capable national and local response actors. Through partnerships with governments, regional institutions, UN agencies, civil society organizations, academic and research institutions, and technical networks, ADPC promotes nationally and locally led approaches that strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery capacities.

Within this broader commitment, ADPC is a consortium partner in the Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings, led by International Medical Corps (IMC). LEARN aims to strengthen Local First Responders (LFRs), particularly Local and National Non-Governmental Organizations (L/NNGOs), to improve their readiness and multisectoral response to infectious disease outbreaks of epidemic or pandemic potential in humanitarian settings.

As a consortium partner, ADPC will provide technical and implementation support for LEARN activities in South and Southeast Asia, including the Philippines. In the Philippines, ADPC will work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to provide technical support for capacity-strengthening activities, including contextualization of LEARN materials, training facilitation, organizational capacity strengthening, remote coaching and technical assistance to participating L/NNGOs. To support this work, ADPC seeks to engage a **Capacity Building Expert (Public Health) – Philippines**. The consultant will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point, working closely with the ADPC project team, the Health Emergency Management (HEM) Specialist, the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating L/NNGOs and relevant stakeholders to plan, deliver and follow up practical technical support within the agreed country implementation arrangements.

A key focus of the assignment will be to ensure that LEARN's capacity-strengthening approaches and resources are appropriately contextualized to the Philippine public health, humanitarian, disaster risk, and institutional context, and that participating L/NNGOs receive practical technical support to strengthen their readiness and capacity to respond to infectious disease outbreaks.

**Note:** *It is not the intent of the ToR to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**D. Duties and Responsibilities:**

Under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Emergency Preparedness and Response/LEARN Program Lead of ADPC, the Capacity Building Expert will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point for LEARN activities in the Philippines. The consultant will work closely with participating L/NNGOs, relevant stakeholders, the ADPC project team and the IMC Philippines Country Team on day-to-day planning, implementation coordination, organizational engagement and follow-up, and translation of LEARN technical approaches into practical, context-appropriate support responsive to identified organizational and operational needs. The consultant will undertake the following key responsibilities:

**1. Technical and Capacity-Building Support**

- Provide technical expertise in public health emergency preparedness and response to support ADPC's technical contribution to LEARN implementation in the Philippines.
- Jointly plan capacity-strengthening activities with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and undertake agreed technical preparation, contextualization, facilitation and follow-up of training, exercises and other capacity-development interventions for participating L/NNGOs and local first responders, in accordance with the approved workplan and country implementation arrangements.
- Adapt relevant LEARN training materials, tools and technical resources in consultation with the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating organizations and relevant stakeholders to reflect organizational capacities, priorities and Philippine realities; submit substantive technical products to the ADPC LEARN team for technical review and quality assurance before use, and incorporate agreed feedback.
- Support the review of English-to-Filipino/Tagalog and relevant local-language translations of LEARN training materials, tools and guidance for accuracy, clarity, consistency of public health terminology and suitability for participating organizations. Work with the IMC Philippines Country Team and qualified translators or language reviewers, drawing on the Consultant’s language competencies, and coordinate with project team to resolve technical ambiguities before use.
- Provide technical facilitation and resource support for agreed LEARN training and capacity-development activities, coordinating participant engagement, schedules, field access, event arrangements and logistical requirements with the IMC Philippines Country Team and ADPC according to their agreed responsibilities.
- Apply appropriate adult-learning, participatory and practical training methodologies to strengthen the application of knowledge and skills by participating organizations.
- Provide practical technical support according to assessed needs on infectious disease preparedness and response, including Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) or equivalent response mechanisms, health emergency management (HEM) systems, activation and escalation arrangements, emergency operations/incident coordination, community-based surveillance and reporting, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), referral pathways and multisectoral coordination.
- Apply the 7-1-7 framework as an additional ADPC technical framework, rather than an existing LEARN contractual requirement, with participating L/NNGOs and local first responders as appropriate to their roles and Philippine public health systems: detect a suspected infectious disease outbreak within seven days of emergence, notify the appropriate public health authority within one day of detection, and complete priority early response actions within seven days of notification.
- Integrate relevant 7-1-7 concepts into assessments, training, coaching and exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team to identify bottlenecks and enabling factors in detection, notification and early response, and strengthen reporting, activation and coordination pathways. Organizational support will contribute to wider system performance within each organization’s mandate; the Consultant will not be responsible for measuring national 7-1-7 performance.

**2. Organizational Capacity Strengthening and Technical Assistance**

- Work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to plan and conduct the agreed technical components of organizational and readiness assessments using agreed tools; document baseline capacities, strengths and gaps, validate findings with participating L/NNGOs, and submit findings to project team for technical review to inform capacity-strengthening support.
- Translate validated assessment findings into organization-specific capacity-strengthening action plans with participating L/NNGOs and the IMC Philippines Country Team, identifying priorities, responsible persons, timelines, training and coaching requirements, and evidence of progress. Align implementation with the Program’s approved workplan, country implementation arrangements and available resources.
- Provide ongoing technical assistance, mentoring, practical exercises and remote or in-person just-in-time coaching, as appropriate and authorized, to participating organizations to implement agreed capacity-strengthening priorities and apply learning in their preparedness and response arrangements, coordinating support and follow-up with the IMC Philippines Country Team.
- Support L/NNGOs in developing, testing and updating organizational preparedness arrangements and community response plans, including roles and responsibilities, activation triggers, reporting and referral pathways, coordination and resource needs, based on assessed priorities.
- Monitor progress against organization-specific action plans through documented follow-up, evidence of practical application and reassessment where appropriate; identify additional coaching needs, support problem-solving, and escalate unresolved technical issues and operational constraints to the Program Lead and IMC Philippines focal point, as appropriate.
- Promote approaches that build on existing national and local systems, structures and capacities and support locally led preparedness and response.

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Field Coordination**

- Coordinate regular technical engagement with participating L/NNGOs, local first responder networks, public health and humanitarian actors, community-based organizations and other relevant stakeholders in close collaboration with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, following agreed country engagement and communication arrangements.
- Jointly conduct participatory stakeholder mapping exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team, building on existing country mapping, and periodically update the mapping of L/NNGOs, local first responders, community-based organizations, public health authorities, health facilities, surveillance and laboratory actors, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and technical partners relevant to approved project locations.
- Analyze stakeholder roles, capacities, geographic and population coverage, coordination relationships, referral and reporting pathways, and gaps or duplication to inform organizational screening, selection and onboarding recommendations and capacity-strengthening priorities.
- Support participating organizations in establishing or strengthening linkages with relevant national and subnational public health preparedness and response mechanisms, as appropriate
- Maintain an updated stakeholder map/database in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team, applying appropriate data protection procedures and sharing relevant information with ADPC.
- Maintain regular technical communication with participating organizations to identify emerging capacity needs and provide appropriate follow-up support.
- Contribute to consultations, technical discussions, workshops and other LEARN engagements as required.
- Provide contextual and technical updates to the ADPC LEARN team on public health emergency preparedness, disaster-health risks and other developments affecting capacity strengthening and project implementation in the Philippines.
- Facilitate peer learning among participating organizations in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team and participate in cross-site technical exchanges with the Thailand–Myanmar Border Capacity Building Expert, HEM Specialist and relevant LEARN partners to share tools, lessons and practical solutions while maintaining context-specific implementation.
- Contribute Philippine experience and lessons to the refinement of LEARN capacity-strengthening resources and approaches.

**4. Outbreak Readiness and Response Support**

- Maintain awareness of emerging infectious disease events and public health threats relevant to participating organizations and project locations through coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team and appropriate public health information sources, and communicate significant developments and potential support needs to ADPC.
- Where an outbreak or other public health emergency creates a need for additional LEARN support, provide agreed technical and coordination assistance to participating L/NNGOs in close collaboration with the IMC Philippines Country Team, subject to ADPC/LEARN authorization, available resources, security considerations and defined project scope. Support will be coordinated with responsible public health authorities and relevant response mechanisms and remain within Consultant’s competencies and authorized role.
- Support rapid identification of organizational operational needs, capacities and gaps with IMC Philippines and participating organizations, and translate findings into priority actions. As authorized and appropriate, assist activation of RRTs or equivalent mechanisms, coordination, information management and reporting, community engagement, referral pathways, IPC/WASH and response planning; provide remote or field-based just-in-time coaching.
- Document operational bottlenecks, enabling factors and lessons from response support with IMC Philippines, applying 7-1-7 or Early Action Review principles where appropriate, and integrate agreed learning into organizational action plans, community response plans and subsequent preparedness activities.

**5. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting**

- Monitor capacity-strengthening activities and organizational progress against agreed workplan milestones, action plans and LEARN indicators in coordination with the ADPC project team and IMC Philippines Country Team, using agreed country monitoring systems and reporting schedules.
- Maintain training attendance and participant profiles, learning assessments, exercise findings, mentoring/coaching logs, stakeholder mapping records, organizational action trackers, technical review records and evidence of follow-up, using agreed formats and safe data-management procedures. Coordinate record collection and consolidation with the IMC Philippines Country Team to avoid duplication and disaggregate participation data by sex, age and disability where feasible, appropriate and safe.
- Provide regular technical and implementation updates to ADPC and share relevant updates with the IMC Philippines Country Team through agreed reporting arrangements, including achievements, action-plan progress, challenges, emerging needs, agreed corrective actions and responsibilities for follow-up.
- Contribute technical inputs and supporting information to ADPC's periodic LEARN progress reports, monitoring requirements and other project documentation.
- Document feedback, lessons learned, capacity-development results, good practices and emerging technical needs from participating organizations and field implementation.
- Propose improvements to technical tools, learning resources and guidance based on assessment findings, implementation experience and feedback from participating organizations and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and submit substantive technical revisions to the HEM Specialist for review and quality assurance.
- Support continuous improvement of LEARN capacity-strengthening approaches and contribute Philippine experiences and lessons to cross-country learning and refinement of technical resources.

**6. Cross-Cutting Responsibilities**

- Integrate Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), safeguarding, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm principles throughout stakeholder engagement, organizational assessments, training, coaching, community response planning and monitoring.
- Facilitate safe, inclusive and accessible participation, taking into account language, disability-related needs, displacement-related barriers and other relevant contextual considerations.
- Protect confidential organizational and community information, apply appropriate data protection and information-sharing procedures, and report safeguarding concerns through established ADPC and partner mechanisms.
- Undertake other related technical and capacity-strengthening responsibilities as may be reasonably required to support effective implementation of LEARN in the Philippines.

**E. Working Principles:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities outlined above, the Consultant will report directly to the LEARN Program Lead, who will provide overall programmatic, contractual and management oversight, including workplan and budget management, coordination with IMC, and approval of major implementation decisions. For country-level implementation, the Consultant will work in close coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team on activity planning, organizational engagement, implementation arrangements, technical delivery and follow-up, in accordance with agreed partner responsibilities and coordination mechanisms.

**F. Required Qualifications:**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

**Education:**

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree preferred) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Emergency/Disaster Management, Community Health, International Development, or another relevant field.
- A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline combined with substantial relevant professional experience may be considered.

**Professional Experience:**

- At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in public health, humanitarian health, infectious disease preparedness and response, health emergency management, community health, disaster preparedness or a closely related field.
- Demonstrated experience in capacity strengthening, training facilitation, mentoring and/or coaching of local organizations, health workers or community-based responders.
- Practical experience in infectious disease outbreak preparedness and/or response, public health emergency management or related programming.
- Proven experience working with government/public health institutions, health emergency coordination mechanisms, local government structures, NGOs and technical partners in the Philippines.
- Demonstrated experience working with local and national NGOs, civil society organizations and/or community-based organizations.
- Experience conducting or supporting organizational/capacity assessments and translating identified gaps into capacity-development interventions.
- Experience facilitating participatory, competency-based and/or scenario-based training is highly desirable.
- Experience with Rapid Response Teams (RRTs), emergency operations, community-based surveillance, risk communication and community engagement, IPC/WASH, community response planning or related technical areas would be an advantage.
- Knowledge of contemporary outbreak readiness and response frameworks, including 7-1-7, is highly desirable. Experience supporting real-time outbreak response, RRTs, emergency operations/incident coordination, Early Action Reviews, after-action reviews or comparable operational learning processes would be an advantage.
- Experience working across the disaster–health nexus, including preparedness and response in areas affected by natural hazards and concurrent public health emergencies, would be an advantage.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of the Philippine public health emergency preparedness and response context, including national and/or subnational systems, is strongly preferred.
- Experience working with organizations or stakeholders in Luzon/NCR and/or Mindanao/BARMM would be an advantage.

**Language**

- Excellent written and spoken English is required.
- Professional proficiency in Filipino/Tagalog is highly desirable.
- Knowledge of relevant local languages in project implementation areas would be an advantage.

**G. Performance Competency**

**Core competencies**

- **Integrity:** Demonstrates the highest level of commitment and demonstrates respect for persons of concern to ADPC, partners, and colleagues in all aspects of work. Ensures that personal and professional behavior is of the highest standard.
- **Diversity Awareness:** Able to embrace the uniqueness of all individuals along several dimensions such as race, religious beliefs, ethnicity, age, gender, physical abilities, political beliefs, socioeconomic status, disability, political conviction, or any other distinguishing features.
- **Equality Awareness:** Understands that each individual has an equal opportunity to make decisions, participate in social activities, perform any work at the organization, and make the most of her/ his life and talents.
- **Teamwork and Collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.

***H. Preparedness and Climate Action Department Functional Competencies:***

- **Teamwork and collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.
- **Results Orientation:** Focuses on delivering agreed-upon results through effectively managing internal and external resources to achieve results. Demonstrates a commitment to both personal and organizational excellence, with an emphasis on results.
- **Analytical Problem-Solving Skills:** Displays analytical thinking by identifying, defining, and analyzing information, situations, and problems. Arrives at viable solutions through a variety of approaches. Demonstrates critical thoughts, methodical review of implications, intuition, and rational conclusions.
- **Adaptability:** Demonstrates flexibility, both intellectually and behaviorally, to adapt to and work effectively in various situations, often under demanding conditions, and to cope with the unforeseen or unexpected. Looks for opportunities presented by change and is not "paralyzed" by new and unusual scenarios. Creates opportunities to improve how they work.

**I. Duty Station:**

Manila, Philippines. Technical support will cover participating L/NNGOs and approved LEARN project locations in the Philippines. Specific locations, remote support and field missions will be agreed through the approved workplan in close coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team; travel requires ADPC authorization, available resources, appropriate access and security arrangements, and alignment with project scope.

**J. Duration:**

November 2026 – September 2027 (11 months)

**K. Itinerary:**

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC financial policy.

**L. Condition of payment:**

The Consultant will receive a monthly payment upon submission of completed timesheets. In addition, the Consultant is eligible for reimbursement of any program-related expenses incurred in the implementation of project activities, subject to the prior approval of the Program Lead.

The Preparedness and Climate Action Department (PCA) strengthens the capacities of governments, response organizations, civil society, private sector actors, and at‑risk communities to prepare for, respond to, recover from disasters and adapt to the increasing risks associated with disasters and climate change. PCA emphasizes locally led preparedness and adaptation, ensuring that resilience-building efforts are rooted in local systems, institutions, knowledge, and leadership.

PCA contributes to ADPC’s regional mandate by designing and implementing programs aligned with ADPC’s strategic priority areas, including Climate Services, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Health Risk Management, Nature‑based Solutions, Resilient Recovery, and Financing for Resilience, among others. These programs support countries in advancing the Sendai Framework, SDGs, and the Paris Agreement, while strengthening institutional, community, and system-wide resilience.

The department also ensures that all interventions incorporate ADPC’s core cross‑cutting themes, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Disaster and Climate Innovations, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation, as foundational elements across program design, implementation, monitoring, and knowledge generation. PCA is structured into three functional units that work together to deliver integrated preparedness and climate action programming:

- **Climate Action and Impact (CAI) –** driving climate action strategies, impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation systems, and evidence generation.
- **Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR)** – strengthening preparedness capacities, emergency response planning, and health risk management.
- **Resilience Building and Localization (RBL)** – supporting resilient recovery, localization approaches, and capacity development at national and subnational levels.

Through multi‑country operations, technical advisory services, and strategic partnerships, PCA ensures coherent, evidence‑based, and impact‑driven delivery of ADPC’s mandate across Asia and the Pacific.

**C. Statement of Intent:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) seeks to strengthen its regional programming and technical capacity for public health emergency preparedness and response across the Asia-Pacific region. Building on its experience in disaster preparedness, emergency response, regional cooperation, and multi-country program implementation, ADPC aims to strengthen its support to countries and communities in preparing for and responding to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Effective public health emergency preparedness and response require timely and coordinated action, supported by strong technical and operational capacities, effective coordination mechanisms, and capable national and local response actors. Through partnerships with governments, regional institutions, UN agencies, civil society organizations, academic and research institutions, and technical networks, ADPC promotes nationally and locally led approaches that strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery capacities.

Within this broader commitment, ADPC is a consortium partner in the Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings, led by International Medical Corps (IMC). LEARN aims to strengthen Local First Responders (LFRs), particularly Local and National Non-Governmental Organizations (L/NNGOs), to improve their readiness and multisectoral response to infectious disease outbreaks of epidemic or pandemic potential in humanitarian settings.

As a consortium partner, ADPC will provide technical and implementation support for LEARN activities in South and Southeast Asia, including the Thailand–Myanmar border region. ADPC will lead field implementation in approved project locations on the Thai side of the border, including stakeholder engagement, organizational and capacity assessments, contextualization and delivery of capacity-strengthening activities, and ongoing technical assistance and mentoring for participating L/NNGOs. To support this role, ADPC seeks to engage a Capacity Building Expert (Public Health) based in Mae Sot. The consultant will serve as the field implementation focal point, working closely with the ADPC project team, IMC, participating L/NNGOs and relevant stakeholders.

A key focus of the assignment will be to ensure that LEARN's capacity-strengthening approaches and resources are practical, context-appropriate, and responsive to the humanitarian, public health, and operational realities of the Thailand–Myanmar border, while strengthening the capacity of local organizations and first responders to prepare for and respond effectively to infectious disease outbreaks.

**Note:**

It is not the intent of this TOR to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.

**D. Duties and Responsibilities:**

Under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Emergency Preparedness and Response/LEARN Program Lead of ADPC, the Capacity Building Expert will serve as ADPC’s field-based technical and implementation focal point for LEARN activities in approved locations on the Thai side of the Thailand–Myanmar border. The consultant will work closely with participating L/NNGOs, relevant stakeholders, the ADPC project team and IMC to translate LEARN technical approaches into practical, context-appropriate capacity-strengthening activities responsive to identified organizational and operational needs.

The consultant will undertake the following key responsibilities:

**1. Technical and Capacity-Building Support**

- Provide technical expertise in public health emergency preparedness and response to support the implementation of LEARN capacity-strengthening activities in the Thailand–Myanmar border context.
- Lead field planning, contextualization, preparation and delivery of training, exercises and other capacity-development interventions for participating L/NNGOs and local first responders, in accordance with the approved workplan and in coordination with the ADPC project team.
- Adapt relevant training materials, tools and technical resources in consultation with participating organizations and relevant stakeholders to reflect organizational capacities, priorities and border realities. submit substantive technical products to the ADPC LEARN team for technical review and quality assurance before use, and incorporate agreed feedback.
- Review English-to-Burmese translations of LEARN training materials, tools and guidance for accuracy, clarity, consistency of public health terminology and suitability for participating organizations. Coordinate with translators to resolve technical ambiguities before use.
- Apply adult-learning, participatory and practical training methodologies to strengthen the application of knowledge and skills by participating organizations.
- Provide technical support according to assessed needs on infectious disease preparedness and response, including Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) or equivalent response mechanisms, health emergency management (HEM) systems, activation and escalation arrangements, emergency operations/incident coordination, community-based surveillance and reporting, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), referral pathways and multisectoral coordination.
- Apply the 7-1-7 framework as an additional ADPC technical framework, rather than an existing LEARN contractual requirement, with participating L/NNGOs and local first responders as appropriate to their roles and public health systems: detect a suspected infectious disease outbreak within seven days of emergence, notify the appropriate public health authority within one day of detection, and complete priority early response actions within seven days of notification.
- Integrate relevant 7-1-7 concepts into assessments, training, coaching and exercises to identify bottlenecks and enabling factors in detection, notification and early response, and strengthen reporting, activation and coordination pathways. Organizational support will contribute to wider system performance within each organization’s mandate; the Consultant will not be responsible for measuring national 7-1-7 performance.

2\. Organizational Capacity Strengthening and Technical Assistance

- Lead field organizational and readiness assessments of participating L/NNGOs using agreed tools, documenting strengths, gaps and baseline capacities, validating findings with organizations.
- Translate validated assessment findings into organization-specific capacity-strengthening action plans with participating L/NNGOs, identifying priorities, responsible persons, timelines, training and coaching requirements, and evidence of progress. Align implementation with the Program’s approved workplan and available resources.
- Provide ongoing technical assistance, mentoring, practical exercises and just-in-time coaching to participating organizations to implement agreed capacity-strengthening priorities and apply learning in their preparedness and response arrangements.
- Support L/NNGOs to develop, test and update organizational preparedness arrangements and community response plans, including roles, activation triggers, reporting and referral pathways, coordination and resource needs, based on assessed priorities.
- Monitor progress against organization-specific action plans through documented follow-up, evidence of practical application and reassessment where appropriate; identify additional coaching needs, support problem-solving, and escalate unresolved technical issues and operational constraints to the Program Lead.
- Promote approaches that build on existing local systems, structures and capacities and support locally led preparedness and response.

3\. Stakeholder Engagement and Field Coordination

- Lead day-to-day field engagement and coordination with participating L/NNGOs, local first responder networks, public health and humanitarian actors, community-based organizations and other relevant stakeholders in approved Thai-side project locations, under the overall direction of the ADPC LEARN team.
- Support technical screening, organizational selection and onboarding using agreed criteria and stakeholder mapping and assessment findings; document recommendations for ADPC/LEARN decisions.
- Lead participatory stakeholder mapping exercises and periodically update the mapping of L/NNGOs, local first responders, community-based organizations, public health authorities, health facilities, surveillance and laboratory actors, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and technical partners relevant to approved project locations.
- Analyze stakeholder roles, capacities, geographic and population coverage, coordination relationships, referral and reporting pathways, and potential gaps or duplication to inform capacity-strengthening priorities and strengthen linkages with existing preparedness and response mechanisms.
- Maintain an updated stakeholder map/database using appropriate data protection procedures and share relevant information with the ADPC team.
- Maintain regular communication with participating organizations to support effective implementation of capacity-strengthening activities and identify emerging technical and operational needs.
- Facilitate consultations, technical discussions, workshops and other project engagements as required.
- Provide contextual updates to the ADPC LEARN team on developments in the humanitarian, public health and operational environment that may affect project implementation.
- Facilitate peer learning among participating organizations and cross-site technical exchanges with the relevant LEARN partners to share tools, lessons and practical solutions while maintaining context-specific implementation.

4\. **Outbreak Readiness and Response Support**

- Maintain awareness of emerging infectious disease events and public health threats relevant to participating organizations and project locations, and communicate significant developments and potential support needs to the ADPC LEARN team.
- Where an outbreak or other public health emergency creates a need for additional LEARN support, provide field-level technical and coordination assistance to participating L/NNGOs subject to ADPC/LEARN authorization, available resources, security considerations and defined project scope. Support will be coordinated with responsible public health authorities and relevant response mechanisms and remain within the Consultant’s competencies and authorized role.
- Support rapid identification of organizational operational needs, capacities and gaps, and translate findings into priority actions. As authorized and appropriate, assist activation of RRTs or equivalent mechanisms, coordination, information management and reporting, community engagement, referral pathways, IPC/WASH and response planning; provide just-in-time coaching.
- Document operational bottlenecks, enabling factors and lessons from response support, using 7-1-7 or Early Action Review principles where appropriate, and integrate agreed learning into organizational action plans, community response plans and subsequent preparedness activities.

5\. Monitoring, Documentation and Reporting

- Monitor capacity-strengthening activities and organizational progress against agreed workplan milestones, action plans and LEARN indicators in coordination with the ADPC project team; distinguish activity delivery from evidence of improved readiness and practical application.
- Maintain training attendance and participant profiles, learning assessments, exercise findings, coaching logs, stakeholder mapping records, organizational action trackers, technical review records and evidence of follow-up, using agreed formats and safe data-management procedures. Disaggregate participation data by sex, age and disability where feasible, appropriate and safe.
- Provide regular technical and implementation updates to the Program Lead and project team including achievements, action-plan progress, challenges, emerging needs, agreed corrective actions and responsibilities for follow-up.
- Contribute technical inputs and supporting information to ADPC's periodic LEARN progress reports, monitoring requirements and other project documentation.
- Document feedback, lessons learned, capacity-development results, good practices and emerging needs from participating organizations and field implementation.
- Propose improvements to technical tools, learning resources and guidance based on assessment findings, implementation experience and organizational feedback, and submit substantive technical revisions to project team for review and quality assurance.
- Support continuous improvement of capacity-strengthening approaches and facilitate the application of relevant lessons across participating organizations and project locations.

**6. Cross-Cutting Responsibilities**

- Integrate Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), safeguarding, conflict sensitivity and do-no-harm principles throughout stakeholder engagement, organizational assessments, training, coaching, community response planning and monitoring.
- Facilitate safe, inclusive and accessible participation, taking into account language, disability-related needs, displacement-related barriers and other relevant contextual considerations.
- Protect confidential organizational and community information, apply appropriate data protection and information-sharing procedures, and report safeguarding concerns through established ADPC and partner mechanisms.
- Undertake other related technical and capacity-strengthening responsibilities as may be reasonably required to support effective implementation of LEARN in the Thailand–Myanmar border area.

**Working Principles:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities outlined above, the Consultant will report directly to the LEARN Program Lead, who will provide overall programmatic, contractual and management oversight, including workplan and budget management, coordination with IMC, and approval of major implementation decisions. The Consultant will work closely with other project/program managers and technical specialists within ADPC’s Preparedness and Climate Actions (PCA) Department to ensure effective coordination and implementation of LEARN activities in accordance with agreed roles and responsibilities.

**E. Required Qualifications:**

***Required Qualifications and Specifications***

**Education:**

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree preferred) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Global Health, Health Emergency/Disaster Management, Community Health, International Development, or another relevant field.
- A Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline combined with substantial relevant professional experience may be considered.

**Professional Experience:**

- At least 8 years of relevant professional experience in public health, humanitarian health, infectious disease preparedness and response, health emergency management, community health, disaster preparedness or a closely related field.
- Demonstrated experience in capacity strengthening, training facilitation, mentoring and/or coaching of local organizations, health workers or community-based responders.
- Practical experience in infectious disease outbreak preparedness and/or response, public health emergency management or related programming.
- Proven experience working with government/public health institutions in Thai-Myanmar border, health emergency coordination mechanisms, local government structures, NGOs and technical partners in Thailand–Myanmar border.
- Demonstrated experience working with local and national NGOs, civil society organizations and/or community-based organizations.
- Experience conducting or supporting organizational/capacity assessments and translating identified gaps into capacity-development interventions.
- Experience adapting or contextualizing technical training materials for local implementation.
- Experience facilitating participatory, competency-based and/or scenario-based training is highly desirable.
- Experience with RRTs, emergency operations, community-based surveillance, risk communication and community engagement, IPC/WASH, community response planning or related technical areas would be an advantage.
- Knowledge of contemporary outbreak readiness and response frameworks, including 7-1-7, is highly desirable. Experience supporting real-time outbreak response, RRTs, emergency operations/incident coordination, Early Action Reviews, after-action reviews or comparable operational learning processes would be an advantage.
- Previous experience working in humanitarian, conflict-affected, displacement and/or cross-border settings is strongly preferred.
- Demonstrated knowledge and experience of the Thailand–Myanmar border operating context is highly desirable.

Language

- Professional proficiency in Burmese/Myanmar language is required, including the ability to facilitate discussions and capacity-strengthening activities with local organizations.
- Good written and spoken English is required.

**F. Performance Competency**

Core competencies

- **Integrity:** Demonstrates the highest level of commitment and demonstrates respect for persons of concern to ADPC, partners, and colleagues in all aspects of work. Ensures that personal and professional behavior is of the highest standard.
- **Diversity Awareness:** Able to embrace the uniqueness of all individuals along several dimensions such as race, religious beliefs, ethnicity, age, gender, physical abilities, political beliefs, socioeconomic status, disability, political conviction, or any other distinguishing features.
- **Equality Awareness:** Understands that each individual has an equal opportunity to make decisions, participate in social activities, perform any work at the organization, and make the most of her/ his life and talents.
- **Teamwork and Collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways tha tallow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.

***Preparedness and Climate Action Department Functional Competencies:***

- **Teamwork and collaboration:** Works constructively within and across teams in ways that allow shared objectives to be achieved. Works effectively with colleagues and partners. Fosters a positive and collaborative environment.
- **Results Orientation:** Focuses on delivering agreed-upon results through effectively managing internal and external resources to achieve results. Demonstrates a commitment to both personal and organizational excellence, with an emphasis on results.
- **Analytical Problem-Solving Skills:** Displays analytical thinking by identifying, defining, and analyzing information, situations, and problems. Arrives at viable solutions through a variety of approaches. Demonstrates critical thoughts, methodical review of implications, intuition, and rational conclusions.
- **Adaptability:** Demonstrates flexibility, both intellectually and behaviorally, to adapt to and work effectively in various situations, often under demanding conditions, and to cope with the unforeseen or unexpected. Looks for opportunities presented by change and is not "paralyzed" by new and unusual scenarios. Creates opportunities to improve how they work.

**Duty Station:**

Mae Sot, Tak Province, Thailand. Field activities will cover approved LEARN project locations on the Thai side of the Thailand–Myanmar border and relevant border-serving organizations. Specific locations and travel will be agreed through the approved workplan and ADPC authorization. Any mission into Myanmar requires separate authorization, access and security clearance, and must remain within project scope.

**Duration:** November 2026 – September 2027 (11 months)

**Itinerary:**

During official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC financial policy.

**Condition of payment:**

The Consultant will receive a monthly payment upon submission of completed timesheets. In addition, the Consultant is eligible for reimbursement of any program-related expenses incurred in the implementation of project activities, subject to the prior approval of the Program Lead.

jobs.title: Logistics Adviser Syria Damascus AO2
jobs.body:
**What we are looking for**

NRC Syria is in search of a **Logistics Adviser** who will oversee all **procurement** and operational procedures according to NRC standards and to support the program/project implementation. The position holder will ensure that NRC Syria is well positioned to respond to current and future needs and shall demonstrate strong engagement and leadership in all major logistics actions while ensuring capacity building of the logistics teams across the entire country.

If you are a passionate, seasoned leader with extensive experience in **Procurement in humanitarian settings, Capacity Building/ Training and Strategic planning** then this is the role for you!

**\*\*\*\*\*Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***

**What you will do**

**The role will have some of the following responsibilities:**

- Responsible for the mid value bid/tender reviews, endorsing, tracking the comments, and sharing analysis with managers.
- Conduct trainings and provide orientation on logistics matters to logistics teams in country and area offices and main stakeholders.
- Contribute to the country objective of improved efficiency mainly in procurement, by actively reviewing, updating and health checking of the existing systems.
- Identify and build-up the needed systems for improving the efficiency of the procedures considering the context (i.e. vendor database, establishing more framework agreements).
- Ensure that procurements in all offices are being handled efficiently and timely by supervising the processes, collaboration with budget holders and programme unit and capacity building of the teams.
- Ensure that procurement plans are compiled and analysed for possible optimizations, and that processes are compliant with donor regulations. Conduct regular meetings with Budget Holders for review and analysis of the procurement plans.
- Make strategic planning for efficient and transparent procurement processes by identifying the needs and the gaps and by engaging as logistics representative in proposal planning phases.
- Make analysis reports of procurement processes and challenges countrywide and share them with management.
- Maintain procurement monitoring reports and ensure they are in place regularly updated: procurement tracking sheet, E-contract management platform, procurement plans, vendor database, vendor evaluations, price list. Ensure appropriate measures are taken to address audit findings and recommendations related to procurement.

Please download the[ detailed job description ](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQASBwu-bAnWRZEQCh9OcfqwAXikQCfGoIugloT_b3gbAWs?e=8Gg5qA)to learn more about the position.

**What you will bring**

- **Minimum 3 years** of senior Logistics experience (Coordinator or above) in Humanitarian/ recovery contexts.
- **Bachelor’s degree** in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a relevant field.
- Experience from working in **complex and volatile contexts**.
- **Fluent in English and Arabic**, written and verbal.
- Knowledge of the **Syria context.**
- Knowledge of the Syrian context, **sanction programme and market is required.**
- Proven experience in **Supply Change Management and Compliance**.
- **Result oriented, proactive** in taking initiatives and passionate about the job.
- Experience of **logistics systems and structures development.**
- Proficient in **MS Excel and Word**.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: **Damascus.**
- **\*\*\*\*\*Please note for this role, applicants must be legally eligible to work in Syria. We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position. \*\***
- Travel: Approximately 20-30% to areas of operation.
- Salary/benefits: **Grade 8 on NRC’s National Syrian** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- For current NRC employees, please use your official email address when applying.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **mero.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

NRC currently has over 3,000 staff across the Middle East dedicated to assisting people affected by conflict in Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Libya and Palestine. Its humanitarian interventions are based upon its programming expertise in the Core Competencies of Shelter, Education, WASH, Livelihoods and Food Security, and Information Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA) to vulnerable displaced people that were forced to flee.

 [Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

Learn more about NRC's operations in Syria [here.](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/syria/)

jobs.title: Grants Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**Position**: Grants Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Head of Programmes

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 15/11/2026

**Contract Type**: Expatriate (International)

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Grants Manager** is responsible for leading and overseeing country-level grants management processes, from funding opportunity identification and proposal development to donor reporting, grant amendments and closeout, ensuring quality, timeliness and compliance with donor requirements and WeWorld procedures.

Reporting to the Country Head of Programmes, the Grants Manager operates with a high degree of autonomy within agreed priorities and delegated authority, while ensuring alignment with the country strategy and internal approval procedures.

The role provides functional coordination to Project Managers and relevant technical and support departments, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective collaboration and timely delivery of grants-related outputs. This coordination does not imply direct line management of Project Managers, who remain responsible for project implementation and the accuracy of their respective contributions.

The Grants Manager is also responsible for strengthening grants management systems, tools and procedures, identifying compliance risks and escalating issues requiring strategic or management decisions to the Country Head of Programmes.

**Main Tasks and Responsibilities**

**Proposal Development and Fundraising**

- Contribute to the development and regular review of the country fundraising strategy with the Country Head of Programmes and Senior Management Team, translating donor mapping, funding trends, programme priorities and pipeline analysis into recommendations on funding opportunities and donor engagement
- Build and maintain a donor database and an updated funding pipeline
- Proactively identify, assess and share opportunities aligned with WeWorld’s strategy and goals in Lebanon
- Lead and own proposal development processes, including grant writing, setting realistic calendars, allocating and agreeing contributions, functionally coordinating Project Managers and other contributors, and consolidating inputs. Be accountable for the quality, coherence, completeness and donor compliance of the final proposal package, ensuring appropriate technical and financial review, internal approval and timely submission. The Country Head of Programmes will provide strategic oversight and approval in line with WeWorld’s procedures
- Ensure learning from implementation and WeWorld’s programmatic strategy are duly taken into account when writing proposals
- Keep WeWorld’s profile up to date and adequately archive all proposal-related documents in WeWorld’s SharePoint files

**Compliance and Reporting**

- Own and regularly update the Grants Tracker and reporting calendar, ensuring clear responsibilities, internal deadlines and visibility of grant obligations, deliverables and compliance risks
- Develop, maintain and oversee the application of guidelines and workflows for proposal development, donor reporting, grant amendments and closeout
- Support the MEAL department and Project Managers with partner due diligence processes and implementation monitoring
- Lead the donor reporting process through functional coordination of Project Managers and relevant departments, setting internal deadlines, consolidating and reviewing inputs, and ensuring consistency between narrative and financial reports. Be accountable for the quality, completeness and donor compliance of report packages and their timely submission following the required internal reviews and approvals
- Provide guidance and build the capacity of Project Managers on grants management, reporting and donor requirements; monitor follow-up on agreed actions and escalate unresolved gaps or delays to the Country Head of Programmes

**Project Cycle Management**

- Coordinate grants-related preparation and follow-up for project kick-off, review and closeout meetings with Project Managers and relevant departments, ensuring grant conditions, reporting obligations, roles and deadlines are understood and tracked, under the strategic oversight of the Country Head of Programmes
- Coordinate guidance on donor compliance throughout implementation, maintain oversight of grants-related risks and corrective actions, and escalate significant issues to the Country Head of Programmes.
- Coordinate routine donor communication on grants matters within delegated authority, seeking approval for commitments or changes requiring management authorization
- Ensure the Project archiving system is up to date: conduct periodic reviews of project documentation, ensuring proper uploading and archiving by the Project Managers
- Coordinate the preparation, review and submission of grant amendment requests with Project Managers and Finance, ensuring their quality and compliance with donor procedures and obtaining the required internal approvals

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in International Cooperation or a related field
- Good computer skills are required
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluency in both written and verbal English is mandatory
- Fluency in both written and verbal Italian is mandatory

**Professional experiences**

- At least 4 years of specific experience in the field of international cooperation
- At least 3 years of specific experience in Grants management
- Proven experience in independently managing proposal development, donor reporting and compliance processes, including coordination of contributions from multiple stakeholders
- Experience working with institutional donors such as AICS, EU, OCHA and UN agencies

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong grant writing, donor compliance and functional coordination skills, with the ability to independently manage grants processes, coordinate contributors and ensure timely delivery and quality standards
- Excellent organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and tight deadlines
- Sound judgement, problem-solving and decision-making skills, including the ability to identify risks and escalate issues requiring management decisions
- Strong leadership, planning and teamwork skills, with the ability to influence and coordinate colleagues across different functions
- Proactive and dynamic attitude
- Ability to adapt and work under constraint, under pressure and in complex and multicultural contexts
- Interpersonal skills and intercultural approach
- Good listening and communication skills
- Good negotiation and conflict resolution skills
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest in international cooperation development topics
- Demonstrates integrity with regards to NGO values and ethical standards
- Displays cultural, gender, religion, nationality and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Treats all people fairly without favouritism

**Desirable requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous work experience in Lebanon would be considered an asset

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a 6 (six) month contract, renewable subject to funding availability

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2.840€ - 3.440€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Case Management Officer
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

## Vision

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

## Mission

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

## Purpose

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

Under the responsibility of the Country Director the Case Management Officer is responsible for overseeing and coordinating comprehensive care and support services for patients. This role involves assessing patients’ needs, developing care plans, and collaborating with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the delivery of high-quality and culturally competent services. The officer will be an integral part of a multidisciplinary team, working to enhance the overall well-being and outcome of target population.

## **Key Responsibilities**

Include and may not be limited to:

**Assessment and Planning:**

- Conduct comprehensive assessments of clients' physical, emotional, social, and financial needs.
- Develop tailored care plans in collaboration with clients, families, and relevant stakeholders.
- Regularly review and adjust care plans to ensure relevance and effectiveness.
- Work with a multidisciplinary team to integrate various perspectives into the assessment and planning process.
- Facilitate crisis intervention planning, anticipating potential emergencies.
- Demonstrate cultural sensitivity in the assessment and planning process.

**Coordination and Collaboration:**

- Establish effective communication channels with healthcare professionals, social services, and other relevant organizations.
- Coordinate and liaise with agencies, organizations, and external healthcare service providers to ensure a seamless continuum of care for clients.
- Facilitate collaboration among different stakeholders involved in the client's care journey.
- Act as a central point of contact for information exchange between relevant parties.
- Advocate for streamlined communication to enhance the efficiency of care coordination efforts to ensure accurate identification and addressing of the patient’s needs.
- Support and engage in regular team meetings to discuss patients’ progress, challenges, and adjustments to care plans.
- Ensure that all relevant parties are informed promptly of changes in care plans and patients' needs.
- Utilize effective communication strategies to address potential conflicts or challenges in the coordination process.
- Maintain up-to-date knowledge of local social services and healthcare resources to enhance collaboration efforts.
- Provide operational and administrative support across departments when needed to ensure seamless field and office execution.

**Patients Support and Education:**

- Provide emotional support and practical assistance to patients and their families throughout their care journey.
- Educate patients on available resources, services, and self-care strategies to empower them in decision-making.
- Foster a supportive environment for patients to actively participate in their care plans.
- Ensure patients are well-informed about their medical conditions, treatment options, and recovery expectations.
- Tailor supportive services to address the unique needs and preferences of each client.
- Collaborate with patients to set realistic goals and milestones within the care plan.
- Regularly assess clients' understanding of their health situation and adjust education efforts accordingly.
- Assist patients in accessing necessary services.
- Provide information on community support groups, workshops, or relevant events to enhance clients' well-being.
- Foster a compassionate and empathetic approach to patient support, recognizing the emotional challenges they may face.

**Cash Distribution- when needed**

- Cash distribution to the beneficiaries
- Documentation of receipts
- Confirmation of the bank details.
- Follow up if any payment hasn’t been received by the beneficiaries

**Program Development:**

- Participate in the development of educational materials and resources for patients and their families.
- Implementation of quality improvement initiatives to enhance patient care outcomes.
- Collect and analyze data to evaluate the effectiveness of case management interventions.
- Stay updated on current trends, best practices, and evidence-based approaches in physical health case management.

**Documentation and Reporting:**

- Maintain accurate and up-to-date patients’ records, ensuring confidentiality and compliance with regulations.
- Document interventions, assessments, and coordination efforts in a systematic and organized manner.
- Generate regular reports on patients’ progress, outcomes, and any changes to care plans.
- Ensure that all documentation aligns with INARA's standards and policies.
- Provide detailed and accurate information for internal and external reporting requirements.
- Collaborate with the administrative team to streamline documentation processes.
- Implement a robust filing system to retrieve and reference patients’ records as needed easily.
- Conduct regular audits of documentation to identify any discrepancies or areas for improvement.
- Prepare reports for supervisory review, ensuring clarity and completeness.
- Communicate effectively with the team regarding any updates or changes in documentation procedures.

## **Requirements & Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in social work, Psychology, Nursing, paramedical specialty or a related field. Master’s degree is a plus.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Ability to work collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of local social services and healthcare resources.
- Familiarity with relevant laws and regulations governing patient care.
- Proven experience in case management and care coordination
- Experience working with vulnerable and multicultural populations including refugees and children with medical needs.

jobs.title: Executive Director Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation
jobs.body:
Would you like to shape how one of the world’s leading humanitarian organisations builds partnerships, and mobilises resources needed to support people affected by displacement?

This is an opportunity to bring your leadership, external engagement and resource mobilisation experience to a mission with human impact. As Executive Director for Partnerships, Advocacy, Engagement & Resource Mobilisation (PAER) at the Danish Refugee Council (DRC), you will strengthen DRC’s voice, relationships and funding base - positioning DRC as a trusted partner and advocate for displaced people.

You will join DRC at an important time for the humanitarian sector, as needs continue to rise while funding and humanitarian space are under increasing pressure. As a member of the Executive Management Team, you will help set DRC’s strategic direction and lead a broad global portfolio spanning strategic partnerships, institutional and private fundraising, advocacy, external communications, press, international representations, and asylum and refugee rights.

**About the job**

Reporting to the Secretary General, you will set direction for DRC’s global partnerships, advocacy, engagement and resource mobilisation agenda. Working closely with the Executive Management Team, country leadership, and senior functional leaders, you will expand high-level relationships with institutional donors, global foundations, private contributors, private-sector partners to secure more sustainable and flexible funding.

You will harness DRC’s global advocacy, communications and press efforts across countries, regions, representations and headquarters, strengthening DRC’s position as a relevant influencing and dialogue partner for donors, political stakeholders, peers and the wider humanitarian system. You will also oversee DRC’s representations in Geneva, Brussels and Berlin, as well as our representative presence in London, and provide leadership for the Asylum & Refugee Rights department and its specialised expertise in asylum procedures, refugee rights and legal aid.

You will lead and develop leaders across the PAER portfolio, foster collaboration across the organisation, and ensure sound people planning, employee well-being and financial management. Based at DRC’s headquarters in Copenhagen, you will represent DRC internally and externally, communicate its priorities with clarity and build trusted relationships across cultures, sectors and geographies.

The impact you will make:

- Shape DRC’s global strategy and PAER agenda as a member of the Executive Management Team, helping translate organisational priorities into coordinated action.
- Expand institutional and private partnerships to secure more sustainable and flexible funding for DRC’s humanitarian mission.
- Strengthen DRC’s global advocacy, communications and influence on displacement-related agendas with donors, policymakers and humanitarian partners.
- Lead DRC’s international representations with a focus on external relations, and its asylum and refugee rights portfolio, connecting specialist expertise with global engagement.
- Develop senior leaders and promote effective collaboration, people management and financial stewardship across the PAER portfolio.

  
**About you**

You are a purpose-driven executive who combines political judgement, entrepreneurial energy and strong relationship-building skills. You understand the global humanitarian and development landscape and can translate opportunities into lasting partnerships, influence and income. You are an inclusive, inspiring and empowering leader with the ability to create momentum across a complex international organisation.

What you will bring: ​​​​​​​

- Senior-level experience building institutional and private partnerships in the international humanitarian or development sector.
- Deep knowledge of humanitarian funding to forced displacement and related global policy priorities.
- A proven record in resource mobilisation, high-level advocacy, external engagement and policy dialogue.
- Political acumen and credibility with senior government, donor, foundation and private-sector stakeholders.
- Executive leadership experience and an inclusive, entrepreneurial and high-integrity leadership style.

All employees in DRC should master DRC's core competencies: Communicating, Taking the lead, Collaborating, Striving for excellence and Demonstrating integrity.

  
**We offer**

Contract length: Permanent   
Work location: Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station   
Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and Lederaftalen between Dansk Arbejdsgiverforening and Lederne (agreement for managers), which can be found here: www.lederne.dk. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.   
We welcome all nationalities to apply for the role. If you do not have the existing right to work in Denmark, DRC will support with applying and paying for a work permit.   
  
**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact: Georgie Horn, Senior Associate Korn Ferry: **DRC\_PAER@KornFerry.com**

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [**drc.ngo**](https://drc.ngo/).

**Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.**

jobs.title: 22969 Protection Officer (P)
jobs.body:
The International Organization for Migration (IOM) in Liberia is working in close collaboration with the Government of Liberia, United Nations agencies, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), and international partners to address the complex migration, humanitarian, and development challenges exacerbated by decades of conflict, displacement, and instability.
