jobs.title: Protection Officer
jobs.body:
TEAM PURPOSE:  
To identify, analyse and address risks affecting the safety, dignity, rights and wellbeing of individuals and communities affected by conflict, displacement and other crises, in Rural Damascus, Daraa and Assweida governorates. The team designs, implements and oversees protection interventions through direct implementation and partner-led modalities, while strengthening community capacities, local protection systems, social cohesion, and community-based protection mechanisms. The team contributes to the prevention, mitigation and response to protection risks through individual assistance, community-based protection, protection monitoring, evidence generation, advocacy, social cohesion and other protection programming in line with Oxfam Syria's strategy and humanitarian principles.  
  
JOB PURPOSE:  
The Protection Officer in the Southern hub is responsible for the technical leadership and operational management of Oxfam's protection portfolio within the hub, ensuring that all protection activities are implemented in accordance with Oxfam Safe Programming standards and Oxfam Syria's endorsed SOPs, methodologies and guidance. This responsibility applies to both directly implemented and partner-led interventions. The Team Leader leads the identification, analysis and monitoring of protection risks affecting individuals and communities and oversees the design and implementation of appropriate protection responses, including Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion activities, and other protection interventions. The role is responsible for determining the most appropriate implementation modality for each intervention, including direct implementation, partner-led implementation, or phased transition approaches. This role establishes and maintains collaboration with affected communities, local authorities, community leaders, community-based organizations (CBOs), implementing partners and other humanitarian and development actors.  
Where activities are implemented through partners, the Protection Team Leader remains responsible for technical oversight, partner capacity strengthening, mentoring, accompaniment, quality assurance, compliance and risk management. This includes supporting partners to progressively assume leadership of protection activities while ensuring adherence to Oxfam standards and protection outcomes.  
  
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:  
Assessments, analysis and evidence generation  
•Lead and supervise protection staff, and/or support protection partners, in the planning and implementation of Community Gendered Protection and Social Cohesion Analyses, protection monitoring exercises, stakeholder mapping, service mapping, and other assessments required to inform programme design and advocacy priorities.  
•Ensure timely consolidation, dissemination and utilization of assessment findings to inform protection responses, programme adaptation, advocacy efforts and strategic decision-making across Oxfam sectors and external stakeholders.  
•Contribute to research, learning and evidence-generation initiatives informing protection and social cohesion programming, advocacy and policy development.  
Programme and project development  
•Contribute to the development, implementation and adaptation of Oxfam Syria's protection and social cohesion strategy and operational plans based on field evidence, protection trends, emerging risks and organizational priorities.  
•Lead the identification and design of protection and social cohesion interventions, including community-based protection, IPA, protection monitoring, social cohesion, and other protection approaches implemented through direct and/or partner-led modalities.  
•Contribute to concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports, ensuring technical quality and alignment with Oxfam standards, Protection and social cohesion priorities and contextual needs.  
•Identify opportunities for protection and social cohesion integration across sectors and support the design of protection-sensitive as well as conflict-sensitive interventions, in coordination with relevant technical teams.  
Programme implementation and oversight  
•Lead and supervise the implementation of protection and social cohesion activities within the hub, ensuring compliance with Oxfam standards, donor requirements and endorsed SOPs and methodologies.  
•Directly supervise Protection staff and/or support protection partner, and provide technical guidance, coaching and performance management under their responsibility.  
•Oversee the delivery of IPA, community-based protection activities, social cohesion programming, distributions, protection monitoring activities and other protection programming implemented directly by Oxfam.  
•Ensure effective collaboration with case management and other specialized strategic partners to strengthen referrals, complementarity of services and protection outcomes for individuals facing protection risks.  
•Ensure that referral pathways, service mapping mechanisms and coordination arrangements remain functional, updated and accessible to affected populations. Monitoring, reporting, learning and accountability  
•Ensure interventions' outputs, outcomes and impact are monitored and evaluated, in line with methodologies and tools, and in coordination with MEAL staff at hub level  
•Supervise programme quality, protection outcomes, risks and implementation progress through regular field visits, partner monitoring systems, data review and engagement with affected communities.  
•Ensure timely and accurate programme reporting to enable timely contribution to donor, management and sector reporting requirements, including for both direct and partner-led implementation.  
•Work closely with MEAL teams to ensure data quality and the collection and analysis of sex-, age- and diversity, including disability-disaggregated data.  
•Promote learning, adaptive management and continuous improvement based on monitoring findings, community feedback and lessons learned.

  
Representation and coordination  
• Represent Oxfam in Protection Sector and other relevant coordination platforms.  
•Coordinate with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, community leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen protection and social cohesion outcomes and facilitate implementation.

  
Partnership Management Responsibilities  
•Lead and oversee the planning and quality assurance, as well as support the implementation and monitoring when needed and requested, of protection and social cohesion programmes implemented through partners.  
•Manage strategic protection partnerships to ensure the timely, effective, and accountable delivery of project activities, outputs, and outcomes.  
•Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and capacity strengthening to partners, in line with partner priorities, on protection programming, including community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion, individual protection assistance (IPA), referrals, safeguarding, and protection mainstreaming.  
•Support partners in developing, maintaining, and regularly updating service mapping and safe, confidential, and survivor-centred referral pathways in line with agreed protocols.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable the delivery of survivor-centred, timely, and quality protection services, including appropriate referrals to specialized service providers.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable timely and quality monitoring of the quality and effectiveness of partner-led protection interventions.  
•Support partners in identifying and designing high-quality protection and social cohesion interventions that respond to evolving humanitarian needs.  
•Promote integrated, protection-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive programming by facilitating coordination between partners and relevant technical sectors i.e. WASH and FES.  
•Together with protection partners, monitor partner-led project implementation against agreed work plans, indicators, budget& burn rates, deliverables, and implementation timelines, and support timely corrective actions where needed.  
•Conduct regular partner review meetings, field monitoring visits, and joint supervision missions to assess programme quality, identify challenges, and strengthen implementation.  
•Review partner reports and ensure timely, accurate reporting on progress, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and best practices.  
•Identify implementation risks and operational bottlenecks and work collaboratively with partners to develop and implement corrective action plans.  
•Promote continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and partner capacity development through joint learning moments.  
•Build and maintain strong working relationships with partners, promoting accountability, mutual learning, and high-quality programme delivery.

jobs.title: 23451 Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA) (P)
jobs.body:
Under the overall supervision of the Regional Director and the direct supervision of the Deputy Regional Director for Operations (DRD-O), and in close coordination with the Department of Mobility, Pathways and Inclusion (DMPI) at Headquarters (HQ), the Regional Policy and Liaison Officer (RPLO), the Regional Project Development Officer (RPDO), Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs), and Country Offices (COs) along the region’s priority migration routes, the Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will be responsible and accountable for leading, at the technical level, the regional operationalisation and implementation of the IOM’s Route-Based Approach (RteBA) and providing strategic and programmatic advice on its implementation across the region.

The Regional Programme Coordinator (Route-Based Approach (RteBA)) will ensure alignment with IOM’s global approach, lead regional and inter-agency coordination at the technical and operational levels, and oversee the application of Route-Based Approach (RteBA) tools and instruments within and across countries and along migration routes.

**Responsibilities**

1. Provide technical and operational leadership for the regional and inter-regional operationalisation of IOM’s RteBA, in line with its institutional framework, and in coordination with relevant COs, Regional Offices (ROs), HQ divisions and global RteBA coordination structures; lead the development and implementation of multi-country, multi-partner operational plans for relevant routes; and ensure coherence with IOM’s institutional priorities, relevant regional strategies, and country-level operational realities.
2. Oversee the region’s RteBA Flexible Funding Mechanism allocation and other assigned RteBA projects, ensuring timely, high-quality delivery against approved results frameworks, workplans, budgets, indicators and donor requirements; monitor overall implementation and take or recommend corrective action to address delivery, quality and resource issues.
3. Serve as the RO’s RteBA focal point and lead the region’s engagement and participation in the global RteBA Task Force and, together with specific RTSs, its workstreams. Ensure that regional needs and priorities are reflected in global instruments, deliver agreed regional inputs on schedule, and lead the testing of operational guidance in the region.
4. In close coordination with RPLOs and relevant COs, lead government engagement on the RteBA to anchor route-based action in the priorities of States along relevant migration routes and reflect those priorities in regional cooperation processes. Provide route-level analysis, strategic advice and positioning to regional consultative processes, cross-regional discussions, and intergovernmental dialogues.
5. Support the Policy and Liaison Unit in providing substantive and coordination support to the Regional United Nations Network on Migration (RUNNM), including developing activities, promoting complementarity, and facilitating information exchange among regional RUNNM structures, the UNNM at the global level, IOM’s internal route-based coordination arrangements, and other relevant regional and inter-regional mechanisms.
6. In coordination with the Regional Director and Deputy Regional Director, lead the development and maintenance of strategic partnerships in support of the RteBA with United Nations (UN) agencies, international and national Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), civil society, migrant- and community-led organisations, academia, the private sector and other relevant actors. Provide substantive advice on partnership opportunities and approaches in support of regional RteBA priorities.
7. In close coordination with RPDOs and relevant RTSs, lead the coordination of coherent and integrated RteBA programming across global, regional and country levels, ensuring alignment of programme concepts, proposals and funding approaches through effective coordination with relevant technical and operational teams. Participate in the development of funding strategies and resource mobilisation initiatives, including through engagement with donors and strategic partners, and provide substantive inputs on regional funding priorities and opportunities.
8. In coordination with the relevant RTSs and the RPLOs, lead the translation of route-level analysis and operational experience into regional and inter-regional policy advice, practical guidance, capacity building priorities and coordinated support for Member States, UN Country Teams (UNCT) and country networks.
9. Lead efforts to strengthen institutional capacity and organisational learning for route-based programming by supporting the development, adaptation and institutionalisation of RteBA tools, guidance, methodologies, standard operating procedures, knowledge products and good practices within IOM.
10. Establish and maintain route-level coordination mechanisms among IOM COs and, where relevant, other ROs along migration routes; convene regular route coordination meetings; provide route-level guidance; and oversee the implementation of agreed multi-country, multi-partner operational plans.
11. In coordination with RPDOs and Regional Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation Officers (RPMEOs), coordinate the development and dissemination of route-level evidence, knowledge management products, diagnostic assessments, lessons learned and analytical outputs to support a shared understanding of priority migration routes, and formulate recommendations to inform regional programming and decision-making.
12. Contribute to institutional learning, results-based monitoring, donor engagement and strategic decision-making by leading the consolidation and communication of regional and route-level insights and providing substantive recommendations to inform programme priorities, implementation and policy development.
13. Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.

- Experience in engagement with regional economic communities, regional consultative processes, intergovernmental dialogue or the United Nations Network on Migration is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM’s Route-Based Approach and its institutional framing, and of IOM’s strategic and planning instruments, including the Strategic Results Framework and regional strategies;
- Knowledge of migration governance frameworks, including the Migration Governance Indicators (MGI) and the Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration;
- Knowledge of migration dynamics, actors and coordination structures along the region’s priority migration routes;
- Strong analytical, drafting and facilitation skills, with demonstrated ability to synthesise multi-country inputs into coherent products; and,
- Ability to work across reporting lines and to reconcile regional and Headquarters priorities.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: Communications, Advocacy and External Engagement Manager
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As Communications, Advocacy and External Engagement Manager, you will provide strategic communications leadership and support to World Vision CAR by developing and implementing communication strategies that will strengthen organizational trust, reputation, visibility, advocacy influence, and fundraising efforts.

You will ensure high-quality content production, stakeholder engagement, media relations, and advocacy support while promoting World Vision's impact on children and communities.

You will develop and implement integrated communications strategies, strengthen World Vision’s brand and reputation, produce high-quality multimedia and child-focused content, and ensure effective management of digital platforms and social media. You will lead emergency communication preparedness and response, manage media, donor, and high-profile visits, provide strategic communications advice to senior leadership, and lead advocacy communications related to World Vision’s sectors, conflict, displacement, and protection. You will also strengthen internal communications by building staff communications capacity, promoting engagement and organizational culture, establishing systems for content generation and information sharing, training organizational spokespersons, producing emergency reports, SitReps, alerts, and declarations, and ensuring compliance with World Vision communications policies and branding standards.

You will contribute to external engagement and influence strategies, support national advocacy initiatives, engage local and international media, and develop advocacy messaging for humanitarian and development issues. You will lead the development and implementation of an integrated advocacy agenda across humanitarian, development, and grant-funded programming, ensuring coordinated advocacy efforts and alignment of organizational positions, messaging, and external engagement with World Vision’s humanitarian advocacy priorities, including protection, humanitarian access, accountability to affected populations (AAP), and localization. You will ensure advocacy efforts are grounded in evidence and child and community participation, linking humanitarian response and grants programming into one coherent advocacy narrative.

You will develop and implement an external engagement strategy and build strong relationships with donors, UN agencies, INGOs, government authorities, and local partners. You will represent World Vision in coordination forums and ensure that proposals and concept notes reflect advocacy and communication priorities. You will also develop and implement campaign strategies aligned with the ENOUGH Campaign objectives, coordinate advocacy initiatives targeting policymakers and key institutions, engage children, youth, faith leaders, communities, and civil society organizations, and facilitate awareness campaigns on child hunger, nutrition, and food security. You will build partnerships to strengthen collective action against child hunger and malnutrition, monitor campaign progress, document achievements, support media and communication activities, and promote child participation so that children’s voices are reflected in advocacy actions.

You will monitor and manage reputational risks, support crisis communication and incident response, protect World Vision’s brand and stakeholder trust, and coordinate with regional teams on sensitive issues. You will also supervise communications and advocacy staff, provide performance management and coaching, identify capacity gaps and implement development plans, and support the recruitment and onboarding of new team members.

**Requirements include:**

- A degree in Communications, Journalism, Public Relations, Humanitarian Studies, or a related field (Master's preferred).
- At least 5 years of experience in advocacy, communications, donor engagement, and policy influence.
- A minimum of 3 years in a management role within the humanitarian or development sector, preferably with INGOs.
- Experience working with government institutions, multilateral agencies, and donors; strong leadership and team management skills; ability to work independently under pressure in multicultural environments.
- Excellent communication and writing skills, fluency in English, good French communication skills, and a solid understanding of humanitarian principles, standards, and disaster management.
- A strong alignment with World Vision's Christian values, vision, and mission is essential, along with willingness to travel and work in field locations.
- Proven ability to develop and implement communication strategies, create high-quality content, and manage organizational messaging across multiple channels.
- Experience designing and implementing advocacy campaigns, developing policy briefs, and influencing decision-makers, including government, donors, and partner organizations
- Strong skills in media engagement, crisis communication, spokesperson preparation, and managing relationships with journalists and media outlets
- Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain strategic relationships with governments, NGOs, UN agencies, donors, private sector partners, and community leaders
- Proficiency in digital platforms, social media, content management systems, analytics tools, and managing multi-channel communication and advocacy campaigns.

**Travel and/or Work Environment, Language Requirement**

- Good physical health is required
- Ability and willingness to travel up to 50% of the time in the region
- English and French required

 **Applicant Types Accepted:** Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Emergency Human Resources Coordinator
jobs.body:
To fulfill its mission of assistance to victims of conflicts, epidemics or natural disasters, OCG has created an Emergency Pool, whose members are experienced individuals capable of evaluating a humanitarian crisis, opening, closing and coordinating emergency projects.

The Emergency Human Resources Coordinator is a key member of this pool and reports directly to the Emergency Coordinator, as well as to the E-Cell HR Referent.

The successful candidate is expected to:

- Deploy rapidly in all contexts set by the Emergency cell
- Have the flexibility to assume different HR roles according to operational needs (HR Coordinator but also HR/Administration Manager)
- Gap fill in regular cells if required.

As a member of the Emergency Pool, the Emergency HR Coordinator must be available for deployment within 48 hours for short-term emergency interventions. You will be part of a multidisciplinary response team -including medical, paramedical, and support staff - mobilized for emergencies such as epidemics, armed conflicts, natural disasters, and other acute crises. You may also be involved in exploratory missions, short-term assignments within regular missions or gap filling in the Emergency Cell in Geneva HQ.

Job Description (but not limited to)

- Act as a strategic partner to Operations by contributing to mission planning and execution. Support the design of appropriate emergency organizational structures and ensure adequate HR capacity and sizing.
- Define, adapt, and oversee the implementation of human resources policies for emergency interventions, ensuring alignment with the operational context and challenges.
- Ensure MSF operates as a responsible employer within the mission. Oversee all HR management, administrative, and legal matters, proactively addressing HR-related risks and adapting processes to the emergency context.
- Is the technical referent for all HR and Administration related issues at Mission level (recruitment, management and development of teams, contracting and remuneration of national staff, follow up of daily workers, etc.). Coordinates the urgent recruitment of HR required for the mission. Ensures the timely deployment of critical staff in coordination with the E-Cell HR Referent.

- Monitor working conditions and staff wellbeing, with a focus on high-stress environments. In collaboration with the medical department, coordinate psychosocial support as needed.
- Design, recruit and train the HR teams at coordination and project level.
- Contribute to emergency preparedness and surge capacity planning by assessing HR risks and implementing appropriate mitigation strategies.
- Participate in exploratory missions and evaluations, upon request of the Ecell.

Your Profile

Required Skills and experience

**Field Experience**

- Minimum of 2 years in HR management in the field with MSF, gained through exposure to various contexts, including emergency contexts (population displacement, epidemic outbreaks, natural disasters and/or conflicts).
- At least one field experience with MSF in HR coordination (HR Coordinator or Deputy HR Coordinator).
- Ability to quickly evaluate an emergency on the ground and propose an adapted HR strategy.
- Experience in Finance management is an advantage.

**Strategic and Interpersonal Skills**

- Ability to work effectively in volatile and insecure environments, with strong resilience and stress management skills.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills
- Strong people management skills.
- Strong coordination and organizational skills.
- Strong adaptability and flexibility to navigate changing priorities, dynamic operational environments, and evolving team dynamics.
- Responsible behavior that contributes to the safety and integrity of everyone - prevent, report, and refuse any abusive behavior and/or behavior that goes against MSF's values.
- Ability to thrive in a multicultural environment and demonstrate commitment and support for diversity, inclusive and non-discriminatory attitudes and behaviors.

**Language skills**

- Fluency in both French and English is highly desirable. Alternatively, candidates must demonstrate an excellent command of either language and at least B1 proficiency in the other.
- Knowledge of other mission languages is an advantage (Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic).
- Proficiency in an additional language, especially Spanish, Arabic, and/or Portuguese.

Terms of Employment

- Field-based contract. One year fixed-term contract, renewable based on operational needs and performance.
- Duration of field assignments: 4 weeks to 3 months (flexibility required according to needs).
- Accommodation and travel arrangements such as visa-related costs will be taken in charge by MSF.
- Comprehensive support and guidance will be provided by dedicated technical referents throughout the assignment.

**We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment.**

jobs.title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
jobs.body:
**Desired start date: 01/12/2026**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: Adwa - Tigray Region**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION:

Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region).

In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors.

In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement.

SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone.  
Representation and Internal / external communication:  
The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings  
The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures   
The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep).

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements.

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

-Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams.   
-Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans.   
-Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components.   
-Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring.   
-Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies.   
-Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context  
-Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making.

YOUR PROFIL :

DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required.

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years

EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes.

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection).

LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset.

SI WILL OFFER YOU :

**A salaried position:**

  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:**

Guest House conditions :

\- There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit.  
-Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa  
-Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa :

\- Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

jobs.title: Casework Supervisor
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:**   
The Casework Supervisor manages staff providing direct client services across the Program for Initial Resettlement (PIR) and Refugee Social Service (RSS) case management program. The Casework Supervisor plans programming, coordinates service delivery, supervises a team, ensures program goals are met, and satisfies budgetary, compliance, and reporting responsibilities for the assigned portfolio. This position is based in Louisville, Kentucky, with regular on-site presence within the office.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Staff Supervision responsibilities**

- Lead and develop direct service staff through facilitation of team meetings and individual supervision, including coaching and goal setting.
- Liaise regularly with HQ colleagues for guidance, case consultations, direct financial assistance, and other support as needed, and share relevant information with the casework team.
- Cultivate a respectful and supportive environment for team members and clients.
- Recruit, train, and manage the team in accordance with IRC’s People Manager Standards.
- Carry out timely, professional interventions to ensure responsive, appropriate, and client-centered service delivery.
- Train direct reports on using IRC systems such as Integra, ETO, and IRIS.
- Representing IRC in public, professional, and governmental fora as needed.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Service Delivery**

- Guide PIR program implementation and ensure all required services are completed in a timely manner.
- Assign cases to caseworkers and manage timely provision of services including airport pickups, provision of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing, home visits, school enrollment, domestic health assessments, and connection to community resources as applicable.
- Supervise the RSS Case Management Program, including staff referrals, connection of clients to services, and tracking client participation and progress
- Ensure follow-up on all necessary services, including application to public benefits as applicable, referrals to immigration services, applications for Supplemental Security Income (SSI), and medical and mental health needs.
- Provide oversight so each client receives at least one meaningful interaction every 30 days during their service period.
- Ensure case closeout procedures are followed once a client has reached the goals of their program.

**Partnership Building**

- Manage relationships with property owners and managers to expand access to sources of affordable housing.
- Collaborate with colleagues to encourage timely internal referrals for additional services, such as employment, immigration services, and intensive case management.
- Identify and maintain relationships with local government and community-based organizations to connect clients with necessary benefits and services.
- Develop relationships with community resources such as shelters for temporary housing, domestic violence shelters, mental health providers, and medical specialists.
- Develop and maintain vendor relationships that create budgetary savings and improve efficiency.

**Documentation, Reporting and Contract Compliance**

- Ensure that case file documentation is maintained in compliance with contract requirements.
- Guide the timely implementation of program updates as needed.
- Liaise with the HQ colleagues to ensure thorough understanding of program guidelines and disseminate guidelines to the direct service team.
- Review data to meet donor reporting requirements.
- Assist with the preparation for all monitoring visits, including IRC, the Kentucky Office for Refugees (KOR), and the Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR).
- Monitor program execution to ensure compliance with all funding requirements; communicate program needs to the management team.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree is strongly preferred, preferably in social work or related field

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum two to three years of experience implementing domestic refugee resettlement or similar programs
- Experience supervising, supporting, and training staff strongly preferred
- Experience in program management and responsibility for budget management preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Familiarity with Integra, IRIS, SMART, and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO) strongly preferred.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications
- Ability to prioritize and manage time effectively
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively as a team member in a multicultural environment
- Excellent written and oral communication skills in English; proficiency in a language spoken by client populations is a plus
- Valid driver’s license, reliable access to a vehicle with current insurance, and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of a standard office environment and ‘field’ time in and around the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($$59,962.5 - annually). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements”.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet basic needs and support client achievement of self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs, engaging a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements. The Caseworker is expected to follow guidelines and standard practices, connecting clients to services that support wellbeing.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Conduct intake to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals. Address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- Collaborate with colleagues across grants and programs, ensuring that clients access services for which they are eligible. Complete program quality assurance activities to ensure appropriate use of funds.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Ability to transport, lift and move items as needed to set up homes and otherwise support new arrivals. Lifting and carrying of items 50+ lbs, including larger items such as furniture

- Ability to drive a large van or other passenger vehicles, as needed to conduct work.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities. Typically, this position is based at the office 4 days/week and remotely 1 day/week, with potential field work all days.
- Requires schedule flexibility to perform weekend and/or evening work, including but not limited to airport pick-ups.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $26.80/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Director - Head of International Programs
jobs.body:
PCPM - Polish Center for International Aid is one of the leading Polish INGOs, operating in Ukraine, Lebanon, Syria, oPt, Ethiopia, South Sudan and Kenya, funded by the Polish Government, DG ECHO, OCHA pooled funds, WFP and other institutional donors.

PCPM has three pillars of operations: 1) emergency preparedness and response, including through the WHO-classified Emergency Medical Team.

2\) humanitarian aid, including assistance in refugee crises

3\) long-term development programs, including refugee-centered and social programs in Poland.

As part of its new programmatic approach, PCPM aspires now, funding permitting, to open humanitarian and/or development operations in new geographic and sectoral areas.

Responsibilities:

1. Participate in development of and take lead in implementation of strategy of expanding PCPM's international program presence.
2. Set up or expand PCPM program presence abroad in selected countries, including identification of programs and local partners, establishing and registering local presence as appropriate, implementing initial program activities.
3. Supervising PCPM project teams and staff in designated countries of PCPM program presence, particularly Ukraine, Lebanon, Syria, Kenya and Ethiopia.
4. Apply for institutional and other funding to set up or expand PCPM program presence abroad in selected counties, which includes developing project proposals, including DG ECHO, BHA and others and building strategic relationships with regional and national actors to form consortia and secure joint funding.
5. Undertake frequent travels and field missions to the countries of current and prospective PCPM program presence abroad of Poland.
6. Contribute video and other materials to PCPM fundraising activities./Promote PCPM's visibility and institutional presence by representing the organization at national and international events, as well as capturing and delivering compelling field materials to support public outreach and fundraising.
7. Actively participate in media interviews and other related activities.

Goals (KPIs):

1. First-year objectives: Establish a strategic partnership with at least one major institutional actor (such as an INGO, UN agency, or bilateral donor) and successfully launch operations or projects in at least one new target country.
2. Three-year objectives: Build long-term, multi-year strategic partnerships with at least two key institutional donors/partners and expand PCPM’s operational presence into at least two new geographic locations.

Requirements:

1. Proven experience in humanitarian crises and implementation of donor-funded humanitarian / development aid at the medium management level or above,
2. Familiarity with and proven experience in securing institutional donor financing, including EU institutions, UN Agencies, BHA and other donors as appropriate.
3. Flexibility to undertake field missions with a short advance notice.
4. Fluency in English and knowledge of at least one more language relevant to the current or prospective countries of PCPM program presence.
5. Fluency in Polish would be a major advantage.
6. Citizenship of a EU Member states or another country with privileged access to the EU / Poland labor market.

Working arrangements

1. Preferred: part-time work from Warsaw with part-time travels or field missions. Alternative working arrangements possible, but preference given to office work.

jobs.title: PIR Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

***This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.***

**Job Overview:** The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other qualified immigrants to support a positive resettlement experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency . The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Coordinate timely pre- and post-arrival services to ensure each client has essentials such as airport pick up upon arrival, initial and permanent housing, food, medical care, access to transportation, and is oriented to their new environment.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop individualized self-sufficiency plans and SMART goals in partnership with each client.
- Provide services that are relevant to the client’s goals, including the distribution of direct financial assistance, applications for public benefits, referrals to medical and mental health services, and housing. Ensure active clients receive at meaningful interactions over the course of the service delivery period in accordance with program requirements.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in ETO and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work or related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Relevant professional experience in human services field required; minimum of 2 years’ experience strongly preferred.
- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations strongly preferred.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Ability to learn to navigate or familiarity with database systems such as IRIS and Efforts to Outcomes (ETO)
- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships.
- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluency in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is desired; including Dari, Farsi, and/or Pashto.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research and problem-solving purposes.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

**Compensation:** ($21 - $23). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
