jobs.title: Director of Learning
jobs.body:
**ABOUT US**

Beit Karam is a first-of-its-kind community organization for education, healing, and rebuilding in Syria. Founded in Aleppo, it is a home for possibility created for young people and families returning after years of displacement, as well as those who never left, to carry their communities forward. Beit Karam is where Syrian youth discover their potential, explore creative learning, and shape the future of their communities. It’s where people access training and mentorship, and find a space to heal from trauma. This work is made possible through our partnership with Karam Foundation and Karam Evi, two organizations committed to restoring dignity and rebuilding futures across the Syrian diaspora. Beit Karam deepens this mission by bringing it home. We believe in building not just what was lost, but what was always possible. At Beit Karam, we are growing a generation of changemakers, dreamers, and leaders who will help shape a free, thriving Syria.

This year, we launched the first Karam Caravan, a mobile maker lab bringing fun, creative, and learning activities directly to schools in and around Aleppo and Idlib. Together with our School Rehabilitation program, this new pathway for our [innovative education program](https://karam.nuvustudio.com/discover/studios) establishes a foundation for scaling our reach and impact in the education of Syria’s youth.

**OVERVIEW**

Beit Karam is seeking a Director of Learning to provide leadership in the design, implementation, and growth of Karam’s youth-focused learning and innovation ecosystem in post-conflict Syria. This role is responsible for transforming fragmented learning into a scalable, creative, and dignified educational experience that meets Syrian youth where they are and builds a future with them.

This is not a traditional education role. The role is not about creating course content remotely or pushing standard learning indicators. Karam’s Director of Learning will be on the ground, leading a team and designing an educational infrastructure that merges studio-based learning, maker spaces, mentorship, and entrepreneurship into a new kind of personal and skill that is inspiring, personal, purposeful, and owned by the program participant.

The Director of Learning will manage the creation of learning environments where young Syrians not only learn, but also build, design, fail, start over, and lead. In succeeding, they will redefine the concept of “education” for youth who lost years, not potential, so that learning builds leaders, understanding, and opportunity.

**OBJECTIVES**

- Directly manage the Innovative Education Program, its initiatives, and team by providing them with direction and mentorship, and building the program's capacity and effectiveness.
- Supervise the hiring of new Mentors, oversee onboarding and performance evaluation, and identify areas for continued technical, curriculum, and teaching development.
- Serve as the primary point of contact for Karam’s program partner, NuVuX, to design, implement, and maintain continuous innovation in impact and scale.
- Develop and implement Karam’s educational strategy, and advocate, consult, and negotiate with educators, policymakers, and government stakeholders to ensure long-term partnerships.
- Lead in developing strategies to attract and retain students in the programs through school- or community-based initiatives.
- Advise national and local education authorities on integrating creative, studio-based, and project-driven learning into public educational systems.
- Lead Karam partnerships with local schools, ministries, and education authorities to secure access, align policies, and build trust.
- Translate programs into real-world outcomes, including portfolios, products, services, start-ups, and community projects.
- Guide the creation and integration of Karam’s studios, learning spaces, and entrepreneurial hubs in Syria that are flexible, modular, and scalable.
- Identify strategies and opportunities to involve local experts and leaders in the Syrian diaspora in the program, create student pathways, and bridge between the curriculum and employment and economic empowerment.
- Help define key performance indicators, ensure the efficiency and quality of collected data, and participate in analysis. Ensure that lessons learnt are incorporated into program plans.
- Develop and manage program plans and budgets.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

- An advanced degree (Masters or PhD) or a combination of an undergraduate degree and at least six years of experience working in education in development, emergencies, or post-conflict settings.
- A degree in education, engineering, architecture, international development, or similar fields.
- Proficiency in Arabic and English
- Effective and persuasive communication skills.
- Successful management of staff, teams, and budgets.
- Experience working with a geographically dispersed leadership team and building effective working relationships across organizations,
- Demonstrated ability to contribute to strategy, be accountable for action plans, and report on progress.
- Effective quantitative, qualitative, and systems thinking analytical skills.
- A sense of urgency coupled with a drive of mission and the curiosity to experiment, test, and improve new ideas.
- A willingness to do big things with limited resources and the creativity to make that happen.

jobs.title: WASH Assistant – National Position
jobs.body:
**Location:** Nyakabande

**Duration of contract:** 12 months

**Report to:** Senior WASH Officer

**About IsraAID:**

IsraAID is an international non-governmental humanitarian aid organization based in Israel. Since we were founded in 2001, our teams have worked in emergency and long-term development settings in more than 60 countries around the world. IsraAID responds to emergencies and helps communities affected by crises rebuild their lives and their futures together. From hurricanes to refugee crises to global pandemics, we mobilize quickly and collaborate with communities at the deepest level, accompanying the process of becoming self-reliant in the ability to prepare and respond to emergencies and crises and return to adaptive functioning.

In Uganda, we support the recovery and restoration of people affected by humanitarian crises and to cultivate and nurture resilience and build agency while establishing systems and partnerships to reduce the risk of future disasters. We work in 3 geographical locations in Uganda. In Northwestern Uganda in the Palorinya refugee settlement and Southwestern Uganda in the Nakivale Settlement and Nyakabande Transit centre.

**About The Position**

IsraAID Uganda is seeking a dedicated and skilled WASH Assistant to join our team to implement our WASH activities in Nyakabande Transit Center, Kisoro. Under the guidance of the Senior WASH Officer, the WASH Assistant will implement field level institutional and community WASH interventions in line with program targets, national and humanitarian standards in Nyakabande TC and host communities. This position will play a key role in planning, implementing, and monitoring WASH projects to ensure that Forcibly Displaced and Stateless Persons (FDSPs) and host communities including institutions have access to adequate quantities of safe drinking water, improved sanitation facilities, and promoting the practice of optimal WASH behaviors for better health and nutrition outcomes.

**Detailed responsibilities:**

1. **Program technical support**

- Under the guidance of the Senior WASH officer ensure adequate access to clean and safe water at the transit center, refugee, and host communities
- Apply appropriate behavioral change and communication (BCC) approaches, methods and practices to mobilize and sensitize communities and institutions on best Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) practices.
- Work closely with Persons of Concern (POCs), refugees / asylum seekers and host communities to assess their WASH priorities, needs, and devise strategies of addressing them effectively.
- Lead the promotion of sanitation campaigns in selected communities through latrine construction, desludging, wastewater, and drainage management as appropriate.
- Lead efforts to end open defecation and to improve sanitation facilities in target areas.
- Working collaboratively with POCs, refugees and host communities, support promotion of appropriate hygiene practices and behaviors at the transit center, refugee, and host communities.
- Assist the Senior WASH Officer to manage and distribute WASH materials related to assigned project activities.
- Facilitate meaningful involvement and participation of POCs, refugees/ asylum seekers and host communities in planning, implementing, and maintaining of WASH and infrastructure projects to promote ownership, continuity, and sustainability.

**2. Coordination, Networking and partnership building**

- Ensure non-duplication of programs with other partners operating in the same locations, and in similar sectors of activity.
- Promote integration of WASH programs with other IsraAID project sectors and activities.
- Participate in inter-agency discussions at national and settlement level, ensuring that IsraAID’s position, interests and priorities are fully considered and integrated in the planning and agenda setting.

**3. Documentation and reporting of project activities**

- Timely develop and share weekly project updates, monthly report and quarterly reports on WASH project activities.
- Contribute to the monitoring and evaluation of IsraAID’s WASH interventions and ensure that all required progress and other reports are submitted in an efficient and timely manner.
- Support in providing necessary data for the successful implementation of all the WASH software activities and ensure they’re implemented timely and are of high quality.
- Identify and document significant change stories and key learnings that arise from WASH interventions.

**Essential skills, knowledge, and competencies**

**Essential Requirements**

- Must be a Ugandan National
- A Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Public Health, Community Health, Water Engineering or similar field from a recognized higher institution is required.
- A minimum of 3 years of demonstrated professional experience in WASH programmes in similar contexts is required.
- Experience in implementing WASH-related activities or public health-related activities, preferably within an International NGO context/ humanitarian context.
- Knowledge about WASH Social Behaviour Change and Communication approaches such as CLTS, CHAST, MHM and PHAST is an added advantage.
- Very strong facilitation skills, community mobilization skills and the ability to effectively communicate key issues to communities.
- Good Computer skills and ability to write technical reports.
- Strong organisational abilities to manage inventory, schedules, and documentation effectively.
- Ability to work collaboratively with team members to achieve common goals.

**Specific Skills:**

- **WASH Technical Expertise**: In-depth knowledge of water supply, water quality, sanitation infrastructure, and hygiene promotion – as they relate to WASH programme design and implementation strategies. This includes understanding the technical aspects of water supply systems, waste management, and the promotion of hygiene practices among communities.
- **Adaptability and Problem-Solving**: The capacity to adapt to rapidly changing situations and find innovative solutions to complex challenges.
- **Cultural Sensitiveness and Cross-Cultural Communication:** Proficiency in communicating effectively across different cultures and languages. This skill ensures respectful, efficient, and effective engagement with local communities, stakeholders, and team members from diverse backgrounds.

**Competencies**:

- **Attention to Detail**: Ability to meticulously follow procedures and maintain high standards of performance.
- **Organizational Skills:** Strong organizational abilities to manage inventory, schedules, and documentation effectively.
- **Safety Awareness:** Commitment to following safety protocols and guidelines to ensure a safe work environment.
- **Teamwork:** Ability to work collaboratively with team members to achieve common goals.
- **Commitment to IsraAID’s values:** Professionalism, Humanity, Collaboration, Flexibility and Adaptability, and Resilience.

**ETHICAL STANDARDS**

IsraAID has zero tolerance towards any acts of misconduct, sexual exploitation, and abuse. The recruitment process will include all candidates’ declarations and reference checks focused on misconduct and SEA.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES**

IsraAID is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability status.

jobs.title: Area Operations Manager Cameroon Kousseri
jobs.body:
**About the Context**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) operates in Cameroon’s Far North region, delivering humanitarian assistance through multi purpose emergncy response, including RRM, and resilience programmes through its core competencies in Information, Counselling and Legal Assistance (ICLA), Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods.

The Area Office (AO) in Kousseri oversees emergency operations implemented directly and through four local partners across Makary, Blangoua, and Hile Alifa, with additional programming supporting durable solutions in Logone-Birni.

The operational environment presents moderate living conditions but requires strong operational oversight due to logistical constraints and periodic security volatility linked to the broader Lake Chad Basin context.

The Area Operations Manager will play a key role in supporting programme implementation and operational management for a team of approximately 25 staff, while ensuring effective coordination with regional, divisional and sub-divisional authorities, local councils, and humanitarian actors.

The role also involves representing NRC in the Area-Based Coordination (ABC) mechanisms established as part of the humanitarian reset and transition currently underway in Cameroon, including regular engagement with stakeholders in Kousseri.

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

The Area Operations Manager leads the day-to-day operational oversight of the designated Area Office by coordinating programme implementation and ensuring compliant, high-quality support services. The role drives for the achievement of key programme objectives, addressing operational bottlenecks, maintains the area delivery of services, and escalates risks to country leadership to ensure high quality and cost-effective programme/project implementation within the area operations.

**What you will do**

- Organise grants opening and closure meetings for the area office in coordination with the country office programme and support relevant staff.
- Represent the organisation externally at the local level in the area and build professional networks to promote NRC as delegated by the Country Director.
- Contribute to assessments for new areas of operation, outline possible areas of intervention and develop program strategies for implementation in relevant area.
- With the support of the Country Office management teams, contextualize, adapt and implement SOPs and procedures to ensure the effective provision of assistance within designated area.
- Ensure work and development plans are completed by all staff members in the field office area of operations and performance feedback sessions are conducted on regular basis as per NRC global standards.
- Ensure NRC’s data collection systems for the designated area are in place and information is properly stored/shared.
- Coordinate the area specific periodic reporting to the Country Management Group. Provide analysis and escalate high risk areas as needed.
- Carry out any other tasks relevant to the area office as delegated by the line manager.

Please download the detailed job description to learn more about the position [JD\_Area Operations Manager Cameroon Kousseri\_Approved.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQAninZvpOKvT5R1FYrUWIAGAcclrk1W2ynfh0NZ1LTntOA?e=rctABD)

**What you will bring**

1\. Professional competencies

- Minimum 3 years of experience in office or operations management, preferably within a humanitarian or recovery context.
- Demonstrated experience in team leadership and project management, including planning, coordination, and oversight of operational activities.
- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and support programme implementation in complex operational environments.
- Fluency in English and French, both written and spoken.

## **Context Related Skills, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Experience supporting the implementation of cash-based interventions and market-based programming.
- Strong knowledge of the humanitarian and socio-political context in Far North Cameroon, including displacement dynamics in the Lake Chad Basin region.
- Experience with durable solutions programming, H-D-P Nexus, and transitional approaches linking humanitarian and recovery interventions.
- Experience coordinating with local authorities, partners, and humanitarian actors at regional or field level.
- Knowledge of local languages is considered an asset.

2\. Behavioural competencies

- Handling insecure environment and Coping with change
- Planning and delivering results
- Working with people and Build meaningful relations
- Analysing
- Communication with impact and respect and Act with integrity
- Empower people

Leadership Profile Competencies

- Build meaningful relations
- Act with integrity
- Empower people
- Deliver results

**What we offer**

- **Duty station:** Kousseri Cameroon
- **Contract: National** Fixed Term *contract* 12 months renewable based on funding and performance
- **Salary&Benefits**: Grade 9 on NRC Cameroon **National salary scale**
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

jobs.title: Cash and Market Systems Specialist Mozambique Pemba
jobs.body:
**Background:**

The Cash & Market Systems Specialist position holder is responsible for leading the design, development and implementation of programmes using market based approach, including cash and voucher assistance (CVA). The post holder will support the institutionalization of market-based approaches in Mozambique, within Rapid Response Mechanism Consortium (RRM-Mozambique). The RRM Consortium, despite the challenging cash policy context, has a high ambition level in promoting ethical, effective, efficient, and large-scale market-based programming, either separately (through a ‘basic needs’ approach, e.g. multipurpose cash) or as a modality to achieve sectoral outcomes (e.g. market-based approaches for Shelter, etc ). As such, the position holder is required to lead technical negotiations with the government and influence policy.

The position holder will provide technical leadership on Cash and Voucher assistance and where applicable, Market Systems programming, within and between Core Competencies (CCs) in new business development and program design as well as technical support for implementation, monitoring, and closeout.

**What you will do:**

General Responsibilities:

1. Identify trends, technical standards and donor priorities in view of Cash and Markets
2. Ensure cash and market systems is embedded in RRM consortium responses.
3. Provide technical directions to field teams and support in the implementation of projects applying Cash and Voucher modality in line with proposals, strategies, and donor requirements
4. Ensure capacity building of project staff and transfer key skills.
5. Participate in country-level business development activities to secure resources for programs, influence stakeholders, and create an enabling environment for success
6. Develop guidelines, SOPs, training materials, and indicators for the integration of cash and market systems across RRM Responses.
7. Engage with local and national authorities, stakeholders, support technical negotiations with government and represent the RRM Consortium in relevant forums related to Cash and Market systems.
8. Promote the rights of IDPs and conflict-affected populations in line with CO advocacy strategy
9. Comply with and adhere to NRC policies, guidance and procedures

Specific responsibilities :

- Identifying Rand using appropriate technology and tools/approaches, and carrying out periodic appraisals of cash-based programs.
- Ensure cash-based intervention procedures, standards and operational guidelines are followed and updated in accordance with NRC policies, in collaboration with RRM partners
- Support the RRM Consortium in identifying gaps in terms of capacity to deliver programs using CVA modality on time and at scale; as well as supporti.ng the activities to be undertaken to increase the capacity
- Build capacity of program field teams to use CVA as a modality and market systems as a foundation to their program design and implementation
- Support logistics and program colleagues planning, conducting certain types of market analysis.
- Given the restrictions in use of Cash in Mozambique, promote and strengthen voucher modality, including digital voucher, in CVA interventions
- Oversee reconciliation with the finance department after project implementation
- Oversee large-scale multipurpose voucher/e-voucher programme development and operations across NRC Mozambique, to help displacement- and conflict-affected families meet their basic needs and where possible achieve financial inclusion.
- Support critical interactions and decision-making with key actors/suppliers in application of CVA modality
- Support relevant teams (finance, logistic) in managing relationships with financial service providers, mobile network operators, and relevant private sector, to deliver efficient and large-scale CVA operations
- Ensure documentation of lessons learned, success stories and programme impact of applying CVA as a modality and, where applicable, MS programing

- programmes

**Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Understanding and experience of the specific demands of CVA and market-based programming in Mozambique and other similar context is required
- Competent in building networks, strong problem-solving skills, and ability to influence stakeholders with effective listening, persuasion, negotiation, and other techniques.

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Pemba, Mozambique
- Contract: 12 Months (Renewable)
- Travel: at least 30-40%
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **International** salary scale (USD 5,189).
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.

Learn more about [NRC in Mozambique.](https://www.nrc.no/countries/africa/mozambique)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Community Center and Free Shop General Volunteer
jobs.body:
Glocal Roots is searching for volunteers to join our project in Kos, Greece.

On Kos, Glocal Roots is the sole NGO providing material and integration support outside the camp on the island of Kos. Our hub located in Kos town provides assistance to refugees who reside in the camp or have self-accommodated in the town, especially in their initial stages in Greece. Our primary focus is to cover gaps in basic needs and aid in peoples inclusion into society and empowerment, and do it fairly.

In The Hub, we have a FreeShop where we distribute hygiene and food products once a month to the displaced people that reside on the island. We also have a Community Center, providing a safe space where people can have a cup of tea or coffee, eat some snacks and spend time on it. In this area other different activities are happening, such as English classes, different cultural events, recreational activities, or workshops, depending on our volunteer and team members skills. We also run a Help Desk, where we aim to support refugees and asylum-seekers in the different questions they might have according to access integration basic services, for instance, the research for jobs and housing, or any other questions or concerns.

**Tasks and responsibilities**

The days at the shop and center are very dynamic and tasks may change a little bit from day to day. Each team member will be assigned tasks and roles.

However, the main daily tasks and responsibilities of volunteers may include:

- Registering new people in the FreeShop
- Explaining how the FreeShop works and assisting people in their shopping
- Preparing the FreeShop and keeping track of the stock and storage
- Shopping, going to suppliers, shops, collecting or gathering aid.
- If you are a driver you may be needed for transportation of aid, supplies, other volunteers, and those we are helping to support with their general wellbeing.
- Welcoming and maintain the community center and the common areas
- Cleaning the bathrooms, community center, shop, storage, kitchen, garden area and the entrance
- Organizing recreational and other type of activities
- Sitting and chatting with and preparing tea and coffee for the people in the community center
- Supporting people through our Help Desk (replying to WhatsApp inquiries, searching apartments, referrals to other organizations, organizing doctor’s appointments, etc.)
- Supporting in other administrative tasks (mail, receipts, advertisements, etc.(
- Social media content
- Running errands
- Teaching English classes (beginner level)
- Preparing and going on deliveries
- … and more!

jobs.title: Project Evaluation Consultant
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23684**  
Position Title: **Project Evaluation Consultant (Type B)**  
Duty Station City: **Port Vila**  
Duty Station Country: **Vanuatu**  
Contract Type: **Consultant B**  
*Recruiting Type:* **Consultancy**  
*Vacancy Type:* **Call for Applications**  
Initial duration: **2 months**  
Closing date: **03 November 2026**

**Context:**

Since 2015, more than 30 per cent of Ni-Vanuatu citizens have experienced temporary or protracted displacement due to disasters. Vanuatu's approximately 300,000 people (Vanuatu Bureau of Statistics, 2020) spread across 83 islands are exposed to cyclones, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, ashfalls, earthquakes, mudslides, flooding and drought. As the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events increases due to climate change, disasters pose a primary threat to Vanuatu's national security and human development.

Tropical Cyclones (TC) Judy and Kevin (both of Category 4 intensity) made landfall over Vanuatu on 1 and 3 March 2023. TC Judy and Kevin affected an estimated 24,657 households (123,288 people) with 90 per cent of houses in Shefa and Tafea provinces destroyed or severely damaged. The cumulative impact of compounding events such as previous cyclones (TC Harold), high La Nina rainfall and COVID-19, has had a devastating impact on basic living conditions, access to basic services, livelihoods, and coping capacities. While traditional resilience in Vanuatu is strong, emergency preparedness needs strengthening at all levels - national, provincial, area council and community – particularly in light of intensifying climate change impacts in the Pacific.

In response, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is implementing a project to support the Vanuatu National Disaster Management Office (NDMO) in strengthening the capacity of national and provincial government institutions, Community Disaster and Climate Change Committees (CDCCCs), Area Councils, faith-based organizations, and community leaders — particularly women leaders — to develop and maintain safe and dignified evacuation arrangements during emergencies.

This builds on the existing work being undertaken by the Displacement and Evacuation Centre Management (DECM) Cluster which brings together key partners to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities. It will strengthen and extend the work of the DECM Cluster to provincial and community level, moving towards improved localization of emergency response measures in Vanuatu.

Specifically, the Sef Ples Blong Yumi Phase 2 project funded by the Government of Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), implemented by the National Disaster Management Office, Vanuatu in collaboration with the International Organization for Migration, supports the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness, coordination, and evacuation centre management across multiple hazards. The project focuses on strengthening the DECM Cluster’s coordination capacity, updating and rolling out the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and Evacuation Toolbox / Training Materials, improving information management systems, and supporting preparedness at national, provincial, and Area Council levels.

**The Objective of the project is:**

To contribute to the protection and resilience of people at risk of displacement in Vanuatu by supporting the Government of Vanuatu to strengthen disaster preparedness and evacuation procedures.

The project will update and finalize the National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines (NECMG) and developing the Evacuations Toolbox / Training Materials for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to strengthen:

1. National, provincial and area council-level coordination of evacuations.
2. Capacity of communities, CDCCCs, faith-based groups to manage and lead their own community-based evacuations in ways that both draws on traditional knowledge about evacuations and increases protections for vulnerable groups, especially women, children, older people and people with disability.

The Outcomes and Outputs of this project are the following:

Outcome 1: Government, faith-based groups and communities have enhanced capacity to coordinate, develop, maintain and monitor safe, dignified evacuation accommodation in emergencies.

Output 1.1: Improved information management at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in sudden-onset emergencies.

Output 1.2: Improved coordination at national and provincial level to deliver effective multi-sectoral assistance and protection for displaced populations and host communities in emergencies.

Output 1.3: Updated National Evacuation Centre Management Guidelines and Evacuations Toolbox for Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

Output 1.4: Roll out of Evacuations Toolbox training for national trainers, Provinces, Area Councils, faith-based groups and communities to support evacuation preparedness as well as strengthen community-based management of evacuations.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Disaster Risk Reduction - Humanitarian

Project code: CC0083

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

**The Final Evaluation Report shall include the following sections:**

- Executive Summary
- Introduction, objectives, methodology, and limitations
- Findings (relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, sustainability and cross-cutting issues)
- Discussions of outcomes and results
- Lessons learned and good practices (success factors and/or those which challenged performance)
- Conclusions
- Recommendations
- Annexes (i.e. TOR, Data Sources, Evaluation Matrix, etc.)
- Further details of the deliverables are:
    
    **Other general tasks to be undertaken as part of this assignment will include**
- Providing advice and input to project direction and methods.
- Reporting to and keeping up good communication with National Programme Officer and Project Manager.
- Attendance at project meetings online or in person.
- Meetings, where requested, with IOM Chief of Mission, IOM Project Staff, or Government of Vanuatu representatives.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Performance should be assessed according to the tangible and measurable deliverables of the work assignment as stated in Section 7 above.
- Payment instalments to be made upon the satisfactory completion of each of the deliverables and approval by the project manager.
- Performance will be assessed against the outputs as provided above.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- The evaluator should preferably have a master's degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 2 years of relevant professional experience.
- Or the evaluator should have a bachelors degree in political science, public policy, development, social science, government administration, climate change, sustainable development, refugee and migration studies, international relations, or related field from an accredited academic institution and 4 years of relevant professional experience.

**Experience**

- Demonstrated experience in carrying out similar evaluation assignments for projects related to humanitarian preparedness, response, recovery, disaster resilience, climate change, evacuation center management, or displacement and evacuation center management coordination.
- Demonstrated capacity to coordinate with and secure key informants (including government actors, community networks, other key stakeholders, and community participants) is required.
- Minimum 4 years of experience working with research, policy development, analysis, monitoring and evaluation, and program evaluation preferably in the field of climate change, disaster risk reduction, emergency response, and / or environment.
- Understanding of Vanuatu displacement, emergency response, evacuation centres, and climate change context are an advantage
- Experience of working in the Pacific region is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Good communication and coordination skills.
- Computer skills required (MS Word and basic MS Excel) for reporting.
- Strong facilitation, mentoring, and stakeholder coordination skills.

**Languages**

- For this consultancy, Fluency in Bislama and English language is required. Working knowledge of French is an advantage.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required**

One trip to Port Vila will be required as part of this ToR:  
Trip 1: Approximately 10 days (estimated early - December 2026 or early January 2027) – this travel is required to coordinate evaluation activities, attend meetings, and conduct key informant interviews. Exact dates of the trip to be coordinated between IOM Project Management Team and the selected evaluator(s).  
If budget allows a second trip can be considered in mid or late January 2027.  
IOM will cover costs relating to round trip airfares, accommodation, and a consultant / evaluator daily subsistence allowance. Travel and health insurance will not be covered by IOM and is the responsibility of the consultant / selected evaluator(s).

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at [this link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

jobs.title: MEAL Coordinator (MEAL Advisor) - Caracas
jobs.body:
The Danish Refugee Council is one of the world's leading humanitarian NGOs, working in over 30 countries to provide adequate assistance and protection to refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, returnees, people on the move, and vulnerable local populations/host communities. Currently, DRC is seeking a highly qualified national o International **MEAL Coordinator (MEAL Advisor)** based in Caracas, Venezuela.

**About the job:** DRC is managing its operations in Venezuela under the direction of the country office in Caracas and four field offices located in the states of Sucre, Apure, and Zulia (Maracaibo and Santa Barbara de Zulia). DRC Venezuela is implementing an integrated Action encompassing the Protection, Food Security & Livelihood, WASH and Disaster Preparedness sectors.

**The overall purpose of the role**:

The MEAL Coordinator provides country-level technical advice and capacity strengthening to support the development of DRC Venezuela’s Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning function. Under the supervision of the Head of Programmes, the role works closely with the existing MEAL leadership, MEAL staff, programme teams and partners to strengthen practical systems, improve the quality and use of evidence, and support accountable programming across emergency response, recovery and longer-term interventions.

The role supports a collaborative review of MEAL capacities, systems and ways of working, translates findings into a prioritised improvement plan, and accompanies its implementation through mentoring, coaching and hands-on technical support. The Coordinator promotes sustainable approaches adapted to country needs and team capacities, in line with DRC’s Global MEAL Model and donor requirements.

The position provides advisory and technical coordination support. The existing MEAL leadership retains responsibility for departmental management and day-to-day delivery. Priorities and recommendations are agreed with the Head of Programmes in consultation with relevant colleagues.

**Responsibilities:**

**MEAL development and technical advisory support**

- Facilitate a participatory review of MEAL systems, staffing capacities, workflows, tools and coordination arrangements, recognising existing strengths and identifying opportunities for improvement.
- Review how MEAL commitments are translated into workplans and delivered across country and field offices, including the factors affecting timeliness, data quality and utilisation of findings.
- Develop an achievable MEAL strengthening plan with the existing MEAL leadership and Head of Programmes, with clear priorities, responsibilities, timelines and measures of progress.
- Advise on the country MEAL strategy, departmental workplan, resourcing and division of responsibilities between MEAL, programme teams and partners.
- Provide regular, evidence-based recommendations to the Head of Programmes and support follow-up on agreed improvement actions.

**Capacity strengthening and accompaniment**

- Identify learning needs jointly with MEAL and programme staff and develop a tailored capacity-building plan covering country and field teams.
- Provide structured mentoring, coaching and practical support to MEAL leadership and staff, including through joint field visits and review of actual project tools and outputs.
- Facilitate practical learning sessions on MEAL planning, indicator design, sampling, mixed methods, data analysis, accountability and communication of findings.
- Develop accessible guidance and reusable resources and support their consistent application across offices.
- Assess the application of learning in practice and progressively transfer strengthened tools and processes to the responsible teams.

**Results monitoring and programme quality support**

- Support the integration of MEAL throughout Project Cycle Management, including proposals, grant opening, periodic reviews and close-out.
- Advise on theories of change, logframes, indicators, MEAL plans and realistic MEAL budgets, in collaboration with technical coordinators and grants colleagues.
- Review and strengthen indicator tracking tables, means of verification and reporting processes to improve consistency, completeness and timely consolidation.
- Support the design and refinement of context-appropriate quantitative and qualitative data collection methods for assessments, baselines, monitoring and outcome measurement.
- Provide technical quality assurance for sampling, data collection, data entry, analysis and reporting, and support resolution of recurrent bottlenecks.
- Work with relevant colleagues to strengthen data protection, secure storage, responsible sharing and practical use of digital collection and visualisation tools.

**Accountability to affected populations**

- Support MEAL and programme teams in strengthening accessible, inclusive and safe community feedback mechanisms and information provision.
- Review feedback workflows and advise on timely handling, appropriate referral of sensitive complaints and closure of the feedback loop, in line with DRC procedures.
- Build staff capacities on accountability, ethical data collection and Core Humanitarian Standard commitments.
- Support regular analysis of feedback trends and their use in programme reviews and decision-making.

**Evaluation analysis and learning**

- Advise on evaluation and research planning, methodologies and terms of reference in line with DRC policy and donor requirements.
- Support the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and evaluation findings and their translation into practical programme recommendations.
- Facilitate learning reviews and reflection sessions across teams and partners, documenting lessons and following up agreed actions.
- Support the preparation of clear evidence products and presentation of key findings to programme teams and senior management.

**Partner support and coordination**

- Work with partnership and MEAL colleagues to assess partner capacities and agree proportionate monitoring, reporting and accountability arrangements.
- Provide targeted technical support and capacity building to partners and facilitate joint learning and harmonisation of tools where appropriate.
- Coordinate technical exchanges across country and field offices and with relevant DRC global MEAL counterparts.
- Represent DRC in relevant technical coordination forums when delegated by the Head of Programmes.
- Perform other relevant duties assigned by the Head of Programmes within the scope of the role.

**Experience and technical competencies**

- Minimum five years of relevant MEAL experience in humanitarian or development programmes, including country-level technical coordination or advisory responsibilities.
- Demonstrated experience strengthening existing MEAL departments or systems through collaborative assessment, prioritised improvement planning and sustained technical support.
- Proven mentoring, coaching and facilitation skills, including experience supporting national staff and working effectively through technical influence and collaborative relationships.
- Strong practical knowledge of theories of change, logframes, indicator design, sampling, quantitative and qualitative methods, data quality assurance and evaluations.
- Experience translating data and community feedback into programme improvements and organisational learning.
- Experience with accountability mechanisms, CHS, ethical research and data protection in humanitarian settings.
- Advanced Excel skills and experience with digital data collection tools such as KoboToolbox or ODK; experience with Power BI or statistical analysis software is an asset.
- Experience meeting institutional donor MEAL requirements and supporting local partners.
- Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to propose practical solutions and support constructive dialogue.
- Previous experience with DRC systems, Latin American contexts or emergency response is an asset.

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, social sciences, statistics, research, public health or another relevant discipline
- A relevant postgraduate qualification or specialised training in MEAL is an asset.

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in Spanish and English, spoken and written.

**We offer:**

- The opportunity to be part of one of the best NGOs worldwide.
- Access to over 1,000 free online trainings and certifications.
- Contract duration: subject to budget availability.
- Salary: Band G / Terms of Employment for national or expatriate staff, as applicable
- HCM insurance fully covered by the organization.

**DRC Core Competencies:**

- Achieving Excellence: Focus on achieving results and ensuring efficient processes.
- Collaboration: Engage relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- Taking the Initiative: Take ownership and initiative while seeking innovation.
- Communicating: Listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- Demonstrating Integrity: Act in accordance with DRC's vision and values.

**Application Process:** All applicants must upload a cover letter (max. 1 page) and an updated CV (max. 2 pages, without attachments) in English or Spanish, on the DRC employment platform. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

**Application Deadline:** Sunday, november 01 at 11:59 pm Local Time. Please note that applications will be reviewed continuously, and interviews will be scheduled as soon as a suitable candidate is identified. DRC reserves the right to close the vacancy before the deadline once a suitable candidate is identified.

**Start Date:** November 2026

## We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

The Financial Inclusion Officer will support the delivery of Blue Ventures’ Financial Inclusion programme in Senegal and The Gambia, working closely with partners and coastal communities to strengthen financial resilience and improve household livelihoods. Reporting to the West Africa Head of Technical Capacity, this is a full-time role based in Senegal.

jobs.title: Website Redesign and Development Consultancy
jobs.body:
**Location:** Kenya-based consultants, web development organisations or digital agencies  
**Client:** Sightsavers Kenya on behalf of the Kenya Business and Disability Network (KBDN)  
**Duration:** 10 weeks of delivery and implementation work, followed by 6 months of post-launch support and maintenance.

**About the Assignment**

Sightsavers Kenya, on behalf of the Kenya Business and Disability Network (KBDN), is seeking a qualified consultant or firm to redesign and redevelop the KBDN website.

The successful bidder will deliver a modern, accessible and mobile-responsive website that showcases KBDN's members, resources, events, news, advocacy work and organisational impact. The assignment includes content migration, administrator training, deployment and the development of a simple performance and learning dashboard.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Review the existing website and recommend improvements.
- Develop an improved sitemap and navigation structure.
- Design and develop a CMS-based website.
- Ensure responsiveness across desktop, tablet and mobile devices.
- Implement accessibility best practice, targeting WCAG 2.2 Level AA where applicable.
- Migrate approved content.
- Configure basic SEO functionality.
- Develop an administrator-managed performance and learning dashboard.
- Conduct testing and quality assurance.
- Deploy the website and provide administrator training and handover documentation.

**Required Experience**

Applicants should demonstrate:

- Proven experience in website design and CMS development.
- Experience delivering responsive and accessible websites.
- Experience working with NGOs, membership networks, development organisations or public information platforms.
- Knowledge of accessibility standards, website security and data protection.
- Experience providing website training and handover to non-technical users.
- At least three examples of comparable assignments completed within the last five years.

**Submission Requirements**

Interested bidders should submit:

- Organisation/company profile.
- Proposed methodology and implementation plan.
- Team composition and lead contact details.
- Examples of at least three comparable assignments.
- Financial proposal, clearly separating core costs from optional enhancements or recurring services.
- The consultant/consultancy will hold an ICT Authority Accreditation (ICTA-6) and an ODPC certification of registration as either a Data Processor or Data Controller.

jobs.title: Responsable des activités de santé mentale (psychologues & psychiatres)
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF recrute en urgence des Responsables d'activités de santé mentale, notamment dans le cadre des projets médicaux déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo (maj octobre 2026). IMPORTANT : la durée de mission sur ce contexte est inférieure à 6 mois, de l'ordre de 3 mois. Merci d'indiquer durée de mission = 6 mois dans le formulaire de candidature, même si vous vous intéressez à un départ sur les projets de riposte contre Ebola en République Démocratique du Congo.

**Responsabilités :**

- Coordonner et veiller à ce que les activités de santé mentale auprès des patient·e·s s'accompagnent d'un suivi régulier, en assurant que l’équipe de santé mentale est calme et neutre au cours des sessions indépendamment des sentiments personnels et/ou des croyances et veiller à faire former les interprètes à la terminologie et à l'attitude à adopter durant les séances
- En collaboration avec les membres de l'équipe médicale, les patients et la communauté locale, identifier les besoins dans le but d'une co-définition et d'une co-création des activités de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (MHPSS). Définir, planifier et organiser la stratégie de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial, ainsi que le budget
- Répertorier et mettre à jour les services de santé mentale existants, y compris les autres ONG internationales et locales, groupes communautaires et services de santé gouvernementaux, et maintenir une communication et une collaboration adéquates et régulières avec les autres parties prenantes du projet
- Identifier les éventuelles problématiques qui pourront faire l’objet de plaidoyer et informer le personnel de coordination médicale et de projet avant de prendre des mesures
- Assurer, en collaboration avec le département médical, l'intégration des activités de santé mentale et de soutien psychosocial (MHPSS) dans d'autres domaines/services, tels que la santé sexuelle et génésique, la pédiatrie, la malnutrition et les maladies chroniques non transmissibles, entre autres
- S’assurer que les patient·e·s psychiatrique se présentant dans les structures MSF reçoit un traitement adéquat, y compris des médicaments psychotropes et un soutien psychosocial dans un programme MSF ou par une référence à une ressource appropriée
- Veiller à la mise en œuvre de tous les protocoles et procédures standards de santé mentale MSF
- Gérer, former et superviser l'équipe de santé mentale via des activités comme le recrutement, la définition des descriptions de fonction, le développement des compétences, le briefing/débriefing du personnel et son évaluation

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

- Diplôme de niveau Master ou équivalent en psychologie avec formations pertinentes pour la pratique clinique, une spécialisation en psychologie clinique, conseil, psychothérapie, psychopathologie ou matière connexe
- Autorisation de pratique valide et à jour
- Une composante de formation clinique avec un nombre défini d'heures cliniques supervisées effectuées.
- La formation doit inclure des soins cliniques en face-à-face aux personnes que nous soignons (séances individuelles et en groupe) avec une supervision appropriée et le développement de compétences / techniques psychothérapeutiques clés

**Expériences :**

- Deux ans d'expérience professionnelle après le diplôme de niveau Master - avec des adultes, y compris les techniques comportementales ou le conseil
- Expérience clinique récente (au moins six mois au cours des 24 derniers mois)
- Expérience de travail avec des populations vulnérables dans un contexte interculturel

**Aptitudes :**

- Engagement dans la mission sociale et les valeurs de MSF
- Volonté de travailler dans tout type de contexte, y compris dans des zones instables
- Flexibilité et résistance au stress
- Capacité et expérience dans la formation des autres, le coaching et la supervision

**Langues :**

- maîtrise de l'anglais obligatoire (niveau B1 minimum)
- la connaissance de l'arabe littéraire ou du français est un plus

**Disponibilité** : Engagement de **3 à 6 mois.** Missions de 3 mois pour les projets déployés face à l'épidémie Ebola en cours en République Démocratique du Congo.

**Ce que nous offrons**

- Salaire en fonction de l'ancienneté et de l'expérience pertinente
- Prise en charge des frais liés à la mission (transport, visas, logement, vaccins, etc.).
- Assurances santé, rapatriement, retraite.
- Perspectives d’évolution : formations, accompagnement et développement de carrière dans un large éventail de contextes humanitaires.

**Pourquoi vous ?**

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, engagé·e, stratégique, à l’écoute, et vous souhaitez mettre vos compétences au service de populations en situation de vulnérabilité.

jobs.title: Helios+ Center Assistant
jobs.body:
**BACKGROUND:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933, the IRC offers lifesaving care and life-changing assistance to refugees forced to flee from war or disaster. At work today in over 40 countries, the IRC aims to restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure. In response to the arrival of refugees in Greece in 2015, the IRC has been offering SMS, WASH and Protection services. Among others, through its child protection programs, the IRC has been offering individual support through case management to vulnerable children and their families, non-formal educational activities for children through Safe Healing and Learning Spaces and emergency accommodation and protection to unaccompanied children. Since 2019, IRC Hellas implements an alternative care project for unaccompanied children and will now pilot this project to Greek born children and adults.

**SCOPE OF WORK:** Helios+ - Comprehensive Actions for the integration of Third Country Nationals in the Labor Market - (MIS 6016874) is a portfolio of regional Integration Projects, dedicated to fostering the integration of third-country nationals into Greece's labor market and society. Designed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) with the support of the Government of Greece (GoG), co-financed by the European Union under the Regional Programs (RP) for 2021–2027 and aligns fully with Greece's National Strategy for Integration. HELIOS+ is committed to empowering Beneficiaries of International and Temporary Protection residing in Greece by providing them with the tools and resources needed to achieve socio-economic independence and actively participate in the Greek community, while promoting self-reliance and inclusion through a comprehensive set of services tailored to the needs of the target group.

In the Attica Region, International Rescue Committee Hellas participates as a partner of IOM Greece, together with Solidarity Now, in the consortium led by Caritas Hellas.

The IRC supports access to job counseling and job matching, life skills, education and psychosocial support – directly and in collaboration with partners. The IRC is recruiting a HELIOS+ Center assistant for the reception and registration of beneficiaries, providing first-level information, and guiding beneficiaries to the specialized services of the center. The HELIOS+ Center assistant will also be responsible for preparing the necessary documents for their registration, monitoring the security of the center, and ensuring the smooth operation of the center’s overall spaces and equipment.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Welcome and receive beneficiaries and visitors to the Center warmly and friendly**;**
- Provide information about the Center and its services to the beneficiaries of the subproject, as required**;**
- Provide administrative support to ensure the smooth daily operation of the Center**;**
- Manage the Center’s calendar and scheduling of sessions, appointments, etc., in coordination with the Center’s Manager**;**
- Manage the Center’s correspondence and communications (phone/email/mail)**;**
- Update and maintain a contact list**;**
- Effectively maintain filing systems, both electronic and paper-based**;**
- Collect and organize the data required for each beneficiary;
- Monitor the Center’s spaces and their security, maintain cleanliness and order, aim to ensure smooth and efficient operation, in close cooperation with the Center’s Manager;
- Other related duties as assigned by the subproject Coordinator;
- Participate in regular team meetings and external meetings as requested;

**REQUIREMENTS:**

- BA/BS Degree in Pedagogical Studies, Administrative Studies, and/or other related fields;
- At least three (3) years of experience in a corresponding position of responsibility, preferably in the field of humanitarian organizations;
- Excellent knowledge of Greek and English, spoken and written (level C1/C2).
- Computer skills, in particular word processing, excel spreadsheets and internet services;
- Excellent interpersonal, team and communication skills;
- Ability to organize and prioritize workload using initiative;
- Ability to work under pressure;

**PREFERRED EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:**

- Experience in customer service.
- Ability to manage multiple tasks.
- Intercultural awareness and flexibility.
- Ability to work on own initiative and at the same time as part of a multicultural and interdisciplinary team.
- Knowledge of French, or Arabic, or Farsi, or Pashto, or Urdu is an advantage.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

Working hours: 9:00-17:00

Travel and other requirements: Occasionally to other areas of IRC programs within Athens

**This position is expected to end on May 30, 2027.**

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: £1,300 - £1,590/month). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Mobile Implementation Officer (MIO) – Sécurité F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Dans le cadre d’un remplacement, nous recherchons un·e : MIO – Mobile Implementation Officer – Sécurité (H/F)

**MISSION**

Le département des Opérations a créé en octobre 2017 un poste de MIO Sécurité. Le·a MIO travaille sous la responsabilité du Point Focal Sécurité. Il·elle a pour mission d’accompagner les équipes dans la révision de leur gestion de la sécurité, en lien avec le contexte local et les opérations.

L’intervention du MIO Sécurité consiste à soutenir les équipes sur les besoins qu’elles ont elles-mêmes identifiées tout en intégrant les différents départements (Opés, Med, Log, Admin) dans la réflexion. Elle se conclura par la rédaction d’un plan d’action. Ce plan d’action, réfléchi et travaillé par les équipes, sera dès lors adopté et mis en œuvre par la coordination et la cellule. Il·elle pourra aussi, si la demande est faite par les responsables opérationnels, aider les équipes terrain à mettre en place des procédures de sécurité standardisées. Le MIO Sécurité s’attachera aussi à promouvoir les bonnes pratiques sur les projets au sein de la mission et à les partager avec les autres terrains.

Le·a MIO Sécurité joue aussi un rôle essentiel chez MSF OCP dans la réponse à un incident critique : il·elle prépare les équipes en amont sur le terrain ; il·elle pourra être déployé·e sur le terrain en coordination ou en appui de la cellule de crise terrain.

Entre ses affectations sur le terrain, le·a MIO Sécurité appuie le Point Focal Sécurité à travailler sur la capitalisation et la diffusion des bonnes pratiques et à participer aux discussions sur la mise en œuvre d’opérations dans des zones dangereuses avec les cellules.

**Principales responsabilités :**

Le poste est principalement basé sur le terrain avec un ratio d’environ 70/30 entre terrain et siège, avec des durées de séjour entre 2 semaines et 1 mois par déplacement. Entre les missions, le MIO travaillera au siège au sein de l’unité sécurité.

**1. Organise ses visites terrain pour l’accompagnement des équipes dans la révision de leur gestion de la sécurité**

- Préparer les termes de référence des visites en fonction des objectifs fixés par la coordination terrain, le desk et la direction des opérations.
- Sensibilisation du personnel MSF à la politique de prise de risque et de gestion de la sécurité, en portant une attention particulière à la participation du personnel national.
- Diagnostic de la gestion de la sécurité, impliquant la sécurité appliquée, sur le terrain avec proposition d’amélioration.
- Animation d’atelier (mapping d’acteurs, analyse des risques…) et de sessions de formations avec les équipes terrain en impliquant le personnel national.
- Aide à la rédaction et mise en place des politiques de sécurité sur les missions.
- Ecriture avec les équipes sur le terrain d’un plan d’action.
- Être en support des cellules (RC, ARC, RRH et superlog) pour assurer une continuité du travail réalisé sur le terrain.

**2. Apporter un conseil et un support direct aux opérations en collaboration avec le SFP.**

- Participer à l’identification d’équipements dédiés à la gestion de la sécurité, à leur mise en œuvre sur le terrain et à la capitalisation d’expérience sur leur usage.
- Mettre à disposition des cellules et des terrains un ensemble de trames de documents et de protocoles pour la gestion de la sécurité et les maintenir à jour.
- Contribue à la préparation pour la « gestion » d’incidents majeurs, conseille et accompagne dans les prises de décisions relatives à la gestion de ces situations.
- Réalise des missions d’évaluation / conseil / apprentissage sur le terrain portant sur l’analyse et la gestion de risques généraux ou spécifiques (par exemple kidnapping).
- A la demande, conseille et accompagne les responsables des cellules, les responsables logistiques et les chefs de mission dans l’analyse des risques, le développement des guides de sécurité et procédures, plans de contingence et système de reporting.
- Participe, au briefing et débriefing des équipes sur les sujets spécifiques de la sécurité
- Administre le logiciel de remontée d’incident Sindy.

**3. Appuyer le département des opérations à la mise en œuvre d’opérations dans des zones dangereuses.**

- Participer à une cellule de crise à la suite d’un incident critique.
- Assurer l’intérim coordinateur projet ou chef de mission dans des zones dangereuses ou à la suite d’un incident critique.
- Participer aux discussions sur la mise en œuvre d’opérations en zone dangereuse avec la direction des opérations et les cellules.

**4. Appuyer l’unité sécurité sur la préparation de MSF OCP à la réponse d’incident critique.**

- Identifier avec les missions le personnel-cible.
- Organiser et animer un atelier de réponse à un incident critique sur le terrain.
- Identifier avec les équipes terrain les axes de travail pour améliorer notre préparation sur le terrain.
- Assister le point focal sécurité sur l’organisation d’atelier de formation à la réponse d’incident critique du personnel du siège.

**Profil recherché**

**Expérience :**

- Au moins 12 mois d’expérience sur 2 terrains humanitaires différents en tant que coordinateur (chef de mission, coordinateur logistique, coordinateur projet) sont indispensables.
- Expérience préalable dans la formation d’adultes est un atout.
- Expérience requise dans la gestion de contextes sécuritaires complexes et appréciée dans les situations de crise. Une expérience au siège de MSF à Paris est un plus.

**Compétences :**

- Production de supports.
- Méthodes d’animation et d’évaluation d’ateliers de formation (participation antérieure à la formation de formateurs ou animateur de formations dispensée par l’Unité de Formation OCP par exemple).

**Aptitudes** :

- Goût du travail en équipe, très bon relationnel, capacité d’organisation.
- Bonne capacité d’analyse, de synthèse et de transmission de compétences.

**Langues :** Français et anglais B2 minimum à l’écrit et à l’oral

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDD de 12 mois à temps complet. Poste terrain, rémunération niveau 13 selon la grille de salaires terrain MSF et en fonction de l’ancienneté et de l’expérience pertinente pour ce poste. **Conditions :** 70% du temps sur nos terrains d’intervention et 30% au siège (Paris ou lieu à définir). Prise en charge de l’hébergement, des déplacements et perdiem lors des passages et séjours au siège.

**Poste à pourvoir :** début novembre 2026

*A MSF, nous valorisons la diversité et cherchons à avoir un environnement de travail inclusif et accessible. Nous encourageons toutes les personnes qui possèdent les qualifications requises à postuler, indépendamment de leur origine ethnique, nationale ou culturelle, de leur âge, de leur sexe, de leur orientation sexuelle, de leurs convictions, de leur handicap ou d'autres aspects de leur identité.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 2 novembre 2026

jobs.title: Oficial MEAL (Proyecto RET)
jobs.body:
## **Antecedentes**

RET está comprometido a trabajar en emergencias, en crisis prolongadas y en contextos frágiles para aliviar los sufrimientos más profundos, construir la resiliencia de las personas y mejorar su autosuficiencia.

Somos una de las ONG líderes en ofrecer soluciones a medida y programas pertinentes para reducir las brechas y responder a las necesidades y retos reales de las comunidades.

Asumimos un papel catalizador decisivo en el desarrollo sostenible. Nuestro objetivo es provocar un cambio positivo significativo que permita a jóvenes y mujeres jóvenes especialmente vulnerables tomar las riendas de sus vidas y hacer realidad sus derechos sociales y económicos.

Acompañamos a las personas, a los refugiados, a los retornados, a los desplazados internos y a las comunidades de acogida, adoptando los principios fundamentales de humanidad, imparcialidad, neutralidad e independencia.

En el marco de los proyectos que RET International implementa en Venezuela, se publica la posición de Oficial MEAL (Proyecto RET).

## **Descripción del puesto**

### **Objetivo del Puesto**

El/la Oficial MEAL – Proyecto será responsable de implementar y dar seguimiento al sistema de Monitoreo, Evaluación, Rendición de Cuentas y Aprendizaje del proyecto en las intervenciones bajo responsabilidad de RET, asegurando el seguimiento sistemático del Marco de Resultados, la recolección, procesamiento, análisis, calidad, integridad y trazabilidad de la información, así como la adecuada documentación de los resultados y Medios de Verificación.

Será responsable de recopilar, revisar, validar y consolidar la información generada por los equipos y Oficiales de Monitoreo Local de RET, y remitirla oportunamente al Oficial MEAL – Punto Focal del Consorcio, de conformidad con las definiciones de indicadores, herramientas, metodologías, protocolos y calendarios establecidos a nivel consorcial.

Asimismo, asegurará la aplicación por parte de RET de los procedimientos comunes establecidos para el registro de participantes, control de duplicación y deduplicación, seguimiento de cohortes, calidad y protección de datos, rendición de cuentas a las poblaciones afectadas (AAP), evaluación y aprendizaje, generando evidencia oportuna para la toma de decisiones y la mejora continua de la implementación.

### **Ubicación del puesto**

La posición está basada en la Oficina Nacional de RET, ubicada en el Área Metropolitana de Caracas, con misiones frecuentes a las zonas de intervención, de acuerdo con las necesidades del proyecto.

### **Línea de Reporte y coordinación**

- Reporta al Oficial MEAL (Punto focal del Consorcio).
- Supervisa directamente a los/las Oficiales de Monitoreo Local del proyecto (Falcón, Carabobo y Aragua; La Guaira, Miranda y Distrito Capital).
- Trabaja en estrecha coordinación con el/las Coordinador del Proyecto, Gerencia de Programas de RET en Venezuela y el equipo MEAL del Consorcio.
- Participa en los espacios técnicos MEAL del Consorcio y aplica, en el ámbito de las intervenciones de RET, las metodologías, herramientas, procedimientos y estándares acordados para el proyecto.

**Responsabilidades Específicas**

#### ***1***\*\*. Implementación y seguimiento del sistema MEAL\*\*

- Implementar, en el ámbito de las intervenciones bajo responsabilidad de RET, el Plan MEAL, Marco de Resultados, herramientas y procedimientos de monitoreo establecidos para el proyecto.
- Monitorear periódicamente el avance de los indicadores, productos, resultados y metas correspondientes a RET, verificando el cumplimiento de los criterios y metodologías de medición establecidos.
- Mantener actualizadas las matrices y herramientas de seguimiento correspondientes a RET, incluyendo avances por indicador, territorio, actividad, población objetivo y demás desagregaciones requeridas.
- Monitorear mensualmente los indicadores clave de desempeño (KPIs) e informar oportunamente sobre el grado de cumplimiento, desafíos, riesgos y oportunidades identificadas.
- Emitir alertas tempranas sobre desviaciones, brechas o riesgos que puedan afectar el cumplimiento de las metas y resultados asignados a RET y contribuir a la definición y seguimiento de acciones correctivas
- Supervisar, acompañar y brindar asistencia técnica continua a los/las Oficiales de Monitoreo Local de RET, asegurando la correcta aplicación de herramientas, metodologías y procedimientos MEAL.

#### *2. Recolección, revisión, validación y consolidación de información de RET*

- Recopilar periódicamente la información programática y de monitoreo generada por los Oficiales de Monitoreo Local y demás equipos de RET, conforme a los formatos y calendarios establecidos para el proyecto.
- Revisar y validar la información recibida antes de su consolidación, verificando su completitud, consistencia, exactitud, oportunidad y correspondencia con las definiciones de indicadores, metas, desagregaciones y Medios de Verificación establecidos.
- Identificar inconsistencias, vacíos, errores o información faltante y coordinar con los equipos responsables de RET las aclaraciones, correcciones y ajustes requeridos.
- Consolidar la información de las intervenciones implementadas por RET en las bases de datos, matrices y herramientas de seguimiento correspondientes, asegurando la trazabilidad de la información hasta sus fuentes y Medios de Verificación.
- Remitir al Oficial MEAL – Punto Focal del Consorcio la información de RET previamente revisada, validada y consolidada, de acuerdo con los formatos, protocolos y calendarios de reporte establecidos a nivel consorcial.
- Atender y dar seguimiento a las observaciones, solicitudes de aclaración o ajustes derivados de los procesos de revisión y consolidación a nivel del Consorcio.

#### *3. Lineamientos, Estándares Institucionales y Calidad de Data*

- Apoyar la elaboración y actualización de los instrumentos de la Caja de Herramientas de M&E de RET.
- Diseñar y adaptar instrumentos para la recolección de datos operativos y de contexto, garantizando la inclusión de mecanismos accesibles de retroalimentación y quejas (AAP) con niñas, niños, docentes y familias.
