jobs.title: Consultant.e Expert.e en gouvernance des données – Actualisation du cadre de gouvernance des données de la coopérative hulo
jobs.body:
**Titre :** Consultant.e Expert.e en gouvernance des données – Actualisation du cadre de gouvernance des données de la coopérative hulo

**Date :** 15/10/2026

**Référence : ​**HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-003​

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La Coopérative hulo, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur de l’humanitaire. En décembre 2025, hulo compte 16 organisations membres : ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, la Croix-Rouge française (CRF), Fleet Forum, Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross, International Rescue Committee (IRC), INTERSOS, Médecins du Monde (MDM), Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Solidarités International (SI), et Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement. Les « initiatives mutualisées » de hulo, sont déjà en cours dans 7 countries (Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, RDC, Liban, Jordanie pour la crise syrienne, Colombie, et Tchad). Les activités sur le terrain sont composées d'achats mutualisés, de ressources humaines partagées, d’une plateforme web permettant la mise en commun de ressources, et d’initiatives environnementales mutualisées. Ces initiatives permettent d'économiser du temps et de l'argent, d'améliorer la qualité des biens et des services fournis, et donc de fournir une aide plus efficace à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin.

Hulo développe actuellement son écosystème Data autour de Microsoft Fabric, avec l'objectif de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence.

Hulo a développé un cadre de gouvernance des données pour garantir l'exactitude, la sécurité, la conformité et l'exploitabilité des données tout au long de leur cycle de vie dans un cadre de gouvernance coopérative.

L’utilisation de services spécifiques liés à ces données se développant rapidement, hulo souhaite renforcer le cadre de gouvernance existant pour optimiser l’utilisation et la sécurisation des données de la coopérative.

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'accompagner hulo dans la revue, l’évolution et la préparation au déploiement d’un cadre actualisé de gouvernance des données composé de principes, de rôles, de processus, de normes et de contrôles qui garantit que les données hulo sont exactes, sécurisées, conformes et exploitables tout au long de leur cycle de vie.

Le.la consultant.e apportera une expertise indépendante en matière de :

- Data quality management
- Data stewardship and ownership
- Data privacy and security
- Data policies and standards
- Data integration and interoperability

La mission devra permettre à hulo de disposer d'un cadre de gouvernance des données actualisé et de recommandations spécifiques pour le déploiement et le suivi interne.

**Priorités et livrables :**

1\. Analyse de situation -

- Contexte et enjeux spécifiques à la coopérative hulo
    - Identification et prise de connaissance des politiques existantes
    - Identification des exigences éthiques, réglementaires et de gouvernance coopérative
    - Identification des données concernées, de leur qualité et de l’infrastructure technique de gestion des données.
    - Identification des perspectives futures à considérer (IA, privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs)…)
    - Collecte des besoins exprimés
- « Gap analysis » du cadre existant
    - Analyse comparative entre les enjeux identifiés et le cadre existant
    - Identification
    - Recensement et priorisation des points critiques d’amélioration
    - Validation de la proposition d’actualisation.

2\. Actualisation du cadre existant

- Echanges avec les postes impactés par les changements
- Actualisation du cadre existant à trois niveaux :
    - Principes (niveau stratégique) : engagements généraux applicables à l'ensemble de l'entreprise ;
    - Politiques (niveau tactique) : règles spécifiques régissant les activités de gestion des données ;
    - Normes et procédures (niveau opérationnel) : instructions détaillées de mise en œuvre.
    - Glossaire métier en impliquant activement les responsables des données, en tant que garants des définitions, qui les défendront et les maintiendront au fil du temps.
- Présentation et actualisation en fonction des retours.

3\. Mise en œuvre

- Recommandations sur les livrables, calendrier, budgétisation et responsabilités du déploiement
- Recommandations sur les solutions techniques associées à la mise en œuvre. Exemple - Catalogue de données (Collibra, Alation, Microsoft Purview ou similaire) pour la gestion du glossaire, la traçabilité et l’automatisation des workflows.
- Définition d’un cadre de suivi (Indicateurs clés de performance (KPI), notamment sur les domaines suivants - couverture du glossaire, scores de qualité des données par domaine, problèmes de gestion en suspens, taux de conformité aux politiques et indicateurs d’adoption du catalogue.
- Proposition d’un modèle personnalisé de maturité (inspiré de modèles comme le DCAM ou DAMA-DMBOK) pour évaluer la situation actuelle et définir la feuille de route permettant de passer au niveau de maturité supérieur.

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la data governance ;
- Expérience démontrée dans la création et la révision de cadre de gouvernance de données ;
- Bonne connaissance de la sécurité des données ;
- Expérience de l'écosystème Microsoft Azure ;
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaire contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles ;
- Capacité démontére à pouvoir travailler sur des documents en anglais.

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist et le Data Protection Officer.

**Calendrier**

Octobre – Décembre 2026

**Candidature et processus de contractualisation :**

Le.la Consultant.e séléctionné.e sera contractualisé.e par hulo pour une durée de 10 à 15jours, sans obligation de travailler à temps plein pour hulo durant cette période. Il.Elle devra mettre en avant les étapes clefs de la consultance dans sa candidature. Les taches décrites peuvent être menées à bien à 100% en distanciel.

Hulo appelle à candidater pour la provision des services décrits ci-dessus. Les Consultant.e.s intéressé.e.s devront soumettre leurs candidatures avec propositions financières détaillées (taux journalier avec descriptifs des autres coûts, en plus d’une proposition de coût total), proposition pour répondre aux termes de référence, calendrier et CV renseignant sur les compétences et expériences qualifiant le.la candidat.e pour répondre au service détaillé ci-dessus.

**Critères de sélection:**

Les candidatures seront évaluées selon les critères suivants :

- Expertise en data governance
- Expertise sur la sécurité des données
- Expérience démontrée dans la création et la révision de cadre de gouvernance de données ;
- Compréhension des besoins métier et capacité à les traduire en exigences techniques
- Capacité d’analyse et d’écriture en anglais
- Communication, documentation et transfert de compétences
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaires et/ou de gestion coopérative contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles ;
- Capacité démontrée à pouvoir travailler sur des documents en anglais.

jobs.title: Project Manager – Humanitarian Food Assistance and Resilience Program
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Project Manager – Humanitarian Food Assistance and Resilience Program**, will lead the planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of two humanitarian and resilience programmes implemented by World Vision Sudan across East and South Darfur, West Kordofan, and White Nile States. These include the General Food Assistance to Vulnerable Populations programme, funded by the US Government, and Restore Resilience in Sudan, funded by Global Affairs Canada.

You will ensure quality, timely, and accountable delivery, achievement of programme outcomes, effective resource management, stakeholder coordination, donor compliance, safeguarding, risk management, and accountability to affected populations, promoting continuous learning and sustainable impact for vulnerable communities.

**(a) Strategic Programme Leadership and Delivery**

You will provide strategic leadership and oversight for both programmes, translating approved proposals, workplans, and budgets into implementation plans and measurable targets. You will oversee programme start-up, staffing, partner mobilization, and operational systems, adapt implementation to changing humanitarian and security conditions, coordinate food assistance and resilience activities, and address implementation challenges through regular reviews and field visits.

**(b) Grant Management and Donor Compliance**

You will ensure compliance with donor agreements, budgets, reporting schedules, US Government and USDA requirements, GAC obligations, CRS consortium agreements, and World Vision policies. You will maintain grant management and compliance systems, oversee timely and accurate reporting and grant modifications, ensure complete documentation, and coordinate donor visits, audits, and compliance reviews.

**(c) Programme Quality and Technical Oversight**

You will ensure programme delivery meets technical standards, donor commitments, and humanitarian principles. You will oversee food assistance, cash assistance where approved, and resilience interventions while integrating protection, safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, child well-being, and conflict sensitivity. You will ensure transparent targeting and beneficiary verification, coordinate technical teams, and promote quality improvements and innovation.

**(d) Programme Quality, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL)**

You will maintain quality assurance frameworks and lead MEAL planning, assessments, monitoring, evaluations, and learning activities. You will monitor indicators and data quality, use findings to improve programme implementation, document lessons and good practices, maintain knowledge management systems, review technical reports, and guide needs assessments, targeting, and intervention prioritization.

**(e) Reporting, Compliance and Donor Accountability**

You will ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality narrative, situation, indicator, and donor reporting. You will monitor performance against targets and milestones, strengthen staff and partner reporting systems and capacity, coordinate with MEAL teams to identify corrective actions, and respond promptly to donor requests and recommendations.

**(f) Financial Management and Resource Stewardship**

You will oversee programme finances, ensuring value for money and responsible use of donor resources. You will work with Finance and programme teams to manage budgets, forecasts, expenditure plans, and cash flow; review financial performance; address under-expenditure and overspending; and maintain effective controls, risk mitigation, transparency, and accountability.

**(g) Coordination, Representation and Partnerships**

You will represent World Vision in coordination meetings, technical working groups, donor engagements, and humanitarian forums. You will coordinate with government authorities, UN agencies, clusters, and implementing partners, strengthen partnerships through joint monitoring, support donor visits and external reviews, and organize programme field visits and review sessions.

**(h) Leadership, People Management and National Capacity Strengthening**

You will lead and supervise programme managers, coordinators, technical specialists, and other assigned personnel, establishing clear objectives and supporting performance and professional development. You will foster a collaborative, inclusive, and results-oriented team culture, mentor national leaders and technical teams, strengthen staff and partner capacity, address development gaps through training and coaching, and promote knowledge sharing, succession planning, and the transition of responsibilities to qualified national colleagues.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor's Degree in Social Sciences, International Development, Humanitarian Studies, Law, Social Work, Development Studies or another relevant discipline.
- A Master's degree is an added advantage.
- At least 5 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian assistance, international development, food security, food and cash assistance, resilience programming or related fields, including substantial senior programme management responsibility.
- Demonstrated experience managing large, complex, multi-location programmes with significant budgets, multiple implementation partners and demanding donor requirements.
- Proven experience managing US Government-funded awards and/or Global Affairs Canada-funded programmes, with a strong understanding of applicable grant compliance and reporting obligations.
- Demonstrated experience in budget oversight, financial forecasting, risk management, procurement coordination and partner financial monitoring.
- Strong knowledge of food assistance, food security and livelihoods, cash and voucher assistance or resilience programming.
- Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected or emergency humanitarian settings, preferably in Sudan or comparable operating environments.
- Experience strengthening national staff capacity, mentoring teams and promoting localisation.

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- The job requires regular travel to project sites
- Staff are required to be physically fit
- Proficiency in English and Arabic is an added advantage

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: Program Manager- GFFO and BMZ
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Program Manager- GFFO and BMZ**, you will provide overall leadership, coordination, quality implementation, and compliance for GFFO and BMZ-funded integrated emergency and resilience projects in East Darfur, South Darfur, and Blue Nile.

Reporting to the Zonal Operations Manager and receiving technical support from relevant Technical Advisors, you will oversee Protection, Health, Nutrition, WASH, Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA), and Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) interventions delivered through World Vision and implementing partners.

You will ensure timely delivery of project objectives, donor compliance, effective budget management, quality reporting, stakeholder coordination, and strong team leadership to achieve measurable humanitarian outcomes.

**(a) Grant Management, Compliance and Reporting (GFFO & BMZ)**

You will lead programme implementation across the three target areas, strengthen collaboration and information sharing across GFFO, BMZ, and related grants, and maintain effective communication with World Vision Germany, the Regional Office, and donor focal points. You will provide timely programme updates, oversee high-quality donor reports and information requests, conduct field monitoring visits, and address implementation challenges through adaptive management.

**(b) Protection, Safeguarding and Capacity Strengthening**

You will strengthen organizational capacity in protection and safeguarding, provide technical guidance on safeguarding standards and survivor-centred programming, and deliver training for staff and partners. You will improve safeguarding risk management, reporting pathways, and accountability mechanisms while ensuring compliance with World Vision policies, international standards, protection mainstreaming, AAP, gender equality, disability inclusion, and humanitarian principles.

**(c) Programme Quality, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL)**

You will ensure compliance with donor requirements, World Vision policies, and humanitarian standards. You will oversee implementation, procurement, workplans, cash forecasts, and MEAL plans; coordinate assessments, monitoring, evaluations, and learning activities; maintain data quality and documentation; and promote evidence-based improvements and the sharing of best practices and lessons learned.

**(d) Reporting, Compliance and Donor Accountability**

You will maintain donor satisfaction through proactive communication, timely and accurate reporting, regular field engagement, and at least two quality case studies or success stories per quarter in collaboration with Communications and MEAL teams. You will monitor performance against logframe indicators and targets, analyse results with MEAL teams, recommend improvements, and respond promptly to donor requests and recommendations.

**(e) Financial Management, Resource Stewardship and Compliance**

You will monitor project budgets, expenditures, and burn rates, forecast spending, and recommend budget realignments when necessary. You will ensure procurement, logistics, and financial processes comply with donor regulations and World Vision policies, while reviewing partner financial performance and supporting grant compliance.

**(f) Coordination, Representation and Partnerships**

You will represent World Vision in coordination meetings, technical working groups, donor engagements, and humanitarian forums. You will strengthen collaboration across GFFO, BMZ, and related grants, coordinate with government authorities, UN agencies, clusters, and implementing partners, and support joint monitoring, donor field visits, and external reviews.

**(g) Team Leadership and Capacity Strengthening**

You will lead, supervise, and manage the performance of Project Coordinators and project staff. You will strengthen staff capacity in project management, donor compliance, reporting, safeguarding, and humanitarian programming, promote teamwork and cross-sector collaboration, and support recruitment, onboarding, and performance appraisal processes.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor's Degree in Social Sciences, International Development, Humanitarian Studies, Law, Social Work, Development Studies or another relevant discipline.
- A Master's degree is an added advantage
- Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible humanitarian programming experience.
- At least 5 years managing large donor-funded projects (preferably UNHCR, GFFO, BMZ, ADH).
- Demonstrated experience managing multi-location programmes.
- Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams.
- Demonstrated experience managing multi-sector emergency projects involving Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection and/or Cash Assistance.
- Experience in protection programming within humanitarian settings.
- Experience working with government institutions, UN agencies and national NGOs.
- Promote community-based protection approaches.
- Ensure protection risks are identified, monitored, and addressed through coordinated interventions.
- Strengthen accountability to affected populations through effective complaint and feedback mechanisms.

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement**

- The job requires regular travel to project sites in Darfur and Blue Nile States
- Staff is required to be physically fit.
- Proficiency in the English language; Arabic is an added advantage

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

jobs.title: National Consultant – Community-Based Flood Management (CBFM) and GEDSI Implementation, Cambodia
jobs.body:
**A. About the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes, with the vision of creating safer communities and fostering sustainable development through strengthened disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. Since its establishment in 1986 as a regional technical capacity-building center, ADPC has evolved into a leading regional organization supporting countries to reduce disaster and climate risks through evidence-based, innovative, and inclusive approaches.

ADPC delivers a wide range of programs across its strategic **priority areas**, including:

- Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics
- Policy and Institutional Systems
- Effective Localization for Resilience
- Climate Services
- Resilient Planning and Implementation
- Preparedness and Anticipatory Action
- Nature-based Solutions
- Financing for Resilience
- Resilient Recovery
- Food and Water Security
- Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance
- Health Risk Management
- Urban and Infrastructure Resilience
- Private Sector Engagement
- ADPC Knowledge Academy

These priority areas are reinforced by ADPC’s **cross-cutting themes**, which are embedded across all programs and operations:

- Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)
- Disaster and Climate Innovations
- Regional and Transboundary Cooperation

ADPC supports countries in implementing global frameworks including the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030**, the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, the **Paris Agreement/UNFCCC**, and the **New Urban Agenda**, while contributing to national and regional policy advancement on resilience. Through multi-sectoral partnerships, technical advisory services, capacity development, and program implementation across multiple countries, ADPC works to strengthen systems, institutions, and communities to better manage disaster and climate risks.

For additional details, please visit: **http://www.adpc.net/**

**B. Department Introduction**

The **Preparedness and Climate Actions Department** enhances the preparedness and climate action capacities of governments, NGOs, the private sector, and communities. It focuses on:

- Ensuring frameworks and implementation plans for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery are in place **before disaster strikes**.
- Strengthening institutional and community capacities for anticipatory action and resilient recovery.
- Promoting **locally led DRR and climate resilience interventions** through multi-stakeholder partnerships.

**C. Statement of Intent**

ADPC is supporting the implementation of the Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems (CREWS) 2.0 Project in Cambodia, which aims to strengthen people-centered early warning systems, preparedness, and community resilience to climate and disaster risks.

As part of the project, ADPC will support the implementation of Community-Based Flood Management (CBFM) approaches in three target communities in Cambodia, in coordination with the National Committee for Disaster Management (NCDM), relevant subnational authorities, community representatives, and other project stakeholders.

The CBFM intervention will focus on strengthening community capacities to understand and manage flood risks; improving community-level preparedness, coordination, warning communication, and response arrangements; and promoting practical measures that can be sustained by communities and local authorities.

Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) will be integrated throughout the intervention. Attention will be given to ensuring the meaningful participation of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other groups that may face barriers in accessing early warning information, preparedness services, decision-making processes, and emergency support.

To support effective implementation of these activities, ADPC seeks to engage a national consultant to provide technical, coordination, facilitation, implementation, monitoring, and documentation support for the CBFM and GEDSI components.

**D. Responsibilities and Tasks**  
The purpose of the consultancy is to provide technical and implementation support to ADPC in coordination with NCDM for the delivery of the Community-Based Flood Management and GEDSI components in the three target communities.

The Consultant will:

- Lead detailed planning and coordination of CBFM and GEDSI activities with NCDM, local authorities, communities, and relevant stakeholders.
- Lead in conducting community-level consultations, trainings and assessments to identify flood risks, preparedness capacities, vulnerabilities, and inclusion barriers.
- Lead in facilitating the development and implementation of practical community-based flood preparedness and management measures.
- Strengthen community capacities by developing / updating community-based flood management plans and conducting training events for flood preparedness, early warning communication, coordination, evacuation, and response.
- Ensure that GEDSI considerations are systematically incorporated into community assessments, planning, training, warning communication, preparedness measures, and community participation.
- Facilitate meaningful participation of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other potentially marginalized groups.
- Lead community simulation exercises, validation activities, and documentation of implementation results.
- Monitor progress and provide evidence-based documentation, lessons learned, and recommendations for sustaining and scaling the interventions.

**This is an output-based consultancy.**

**Key Deliverables**

Under the guidance of the program manager, the consultant shall be responsible for the delivery of the following outputs:

**Deliverables 1 :** Inception Report and Implementation Work Plan

- Conduct national-level consultations and meetings with relevant agencies in coordination with ADPC and NCDM.
- Organize inception and review meetings in the three target communities.
- Submit an inception report outlining the implementation methodology, detailed work plan, stakeholder coordination arrangements, and CBFM and GEDSI activities.

**Indicative Timeline :** 01 – 30 Nov 2026

**Deliverables 2 :** Community-Based Awareness, Training and Vulnerability Mapping

- Organize and conduct community-based awareness and training activities in three communities.
- Undertake mapping of vulnerable houses and hazard zoning in the pilot communities.
- Identify and prioritize appropriate flood risk management measures through community consultations.
- Submit training reports, vulnerability maps, and supporting documentation.

**Indicative Timeline :** 15 Nov to 30 Dec 2026

**Deliverables 3 :** Community Flood Management Plans (CFMPs) and Updated CBFM Manuals

- Facilitate the development of Community Flood Management Plans (CFMPs) for the three target communities.
- Update community-based flood management manuals incorporating lessons learned and feedback received.
- Integrate GEDSI considerations into CFMPs and preparedness arrangements.
- Submit three CFMPs and updated CBFM manuals.

**Indicative Timeline :** 01 Jan – 31 Jan 2027

**Deliverables 4 :** Implementation of Flood Risk Management Measures and Gender Mainstreaming

- Coordinate and implement agreed flood risk management measures in the three pilot communities.
- Implement gender mainstreaming in community-level data collection on water levels, vulnerability, and exposure information.
- Ensure inclusive participation of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other vulnerable groups.
- Submit an implementation report with evidence of completed CBFM and GEDSI activities.

Gender mainstreaming (Throughout)

**Indicative Timeline :** 01 Feb – 27 Feb 2027

**Deliverables 5 :** Community Simulation Exercises and Voices from the Field Report

- Organize simulation exercises in three communities to test the CFMPs with Community Flood Management Committees (CFMCs) and community members.
- Document findings, preparedness gaps, and recommendations from the exercises.
- Develop the Voices from the Field Report covering success stories, challenges, lessons learned, and sustainability approaches.
- Submit three simulation exercise reports and the Voices from the Field Report.

**Indicative Timeline :** 01 Mar – 31 Mar 2027

**Deliverables 6 :** National Reflection Workshop and Final Consolidated Implementation Report

- Organize the national reflection workshop with an after-action review and experience sharing from the three communities.
- Document achievements, lessons learned, GEDSI outcomes, and sustainability approaches.
- Submit the national reflection workshop report and final consolidated CBFM and GEDSI implementation report with supporting evidence and recommendations.

**Indicative Timeline :** 01 April – 30 April 2027

**E. Working Principles**

**Overall Supervision and Reporting:**

In performing the duties and responsibilities indicated above, the Consultant will be supervised by the Program Manager, ADPC. The Consultant will also closely work with other Unit Heads, Program Managers and Coordinators for the delivery of the project.

**Administrative Coordination and Liaison:**

The Consultant will coordinate closely with the PCA Department's administrative and support teams to ensure smooth operational functioning. This includes scheduling meetings, coordinating with internal and external stakeholders, and managing communications related to program documentation and knowledge management activities.

**General Requirements:**

The consultant must operate within all ADPC Guidelines & Procedures/ Policies and within the specific program needs

**F. Qualifications**

- An advanced university degree, preferably a Master's degree, in Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Gender Studies, financing or a related discipline.
- At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in disaster risk management, climate resilience, humanitarian action, community development, or related fields.
- Demonstrated experience in community-based disaster risk management, community preparedness, flood risk management, or early warning systems.
- Demonstrated experience working directly with communities and local government authorities in Cambodia.
- Experience in integrating gender equality, disability and social inclusion considerations into disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, humanitarian, or development interventions.
- Experience in facilitating community consultations, participatory assessments, training, workshops, and community preparedness activities.
- Familiarity with Cambodia's institutional arrangements for disaster risk management and relevant national and subnational government structures.
- Experience working with government agencies, civil society organizations, international organizations, and community-based actors.
- Strong experience in technical documentation, activity reporting, and preparation of implementation reports.
- Proficiency in Khmer and working proficiency in English.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

- Self-motivated, proactive, and takes initiative.
- Demonstrated ability to plan and organize work and time independently.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, team-oriented work style, and experience working in a multicultural environment.
- With a strong desire to learn, undertake new challenges, a willingness to work hard, and a good sense of humor, balanced with seriousness about the quality and excellence of work.

**Duty Station:** Phnom Penh, Cambodia, and field missions based on program needs

**Contract Duration:**

This is an output-based consultancy for 6 Months from November – April 2027

**Itinerary:**

In case of official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC travel policy. All travel must be pre-approved and undertaken only upon written request and consent by the Director, PCA Department, ADPC.

jobs.title: Consultant - Consolidation of Technical Guidance on Return, Readmission and Reintegration
jobs.body:
**Job Identification:** 23354

**Posting Date:** 16/10/2026 7:57 AM

**Apply Before:** 29/10/2026 11:59 PM

**Contract Type**: Consultancy (3 months with possibility of extension)

**Initial Contract Duration:** Three months

**Org Type:** Headquarters

**Vacancy Type:** Consultancy

**Recruiting Type:** Consultancy

**Grade:** UG

**Is this S/VN based in an L3 office or in support to an L3 emergency response?:** No

**Short Description**

IOM, UN Migration Agency in Geneva, Switzerland is looking for a consultant who will consolidate and harmonize existing guidance on return, readmission and reintegration including the readmission manual and the technical guidance on return and reintegration, into a single integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR).

**Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

To support rights-based migration governance, the consultant will consolidate and harmonize existing guidance on return, readmission and reintegration including the readmission manual and the technical guidance on return and reintegration, into a single integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR). The final document will be primarily targeted at government practitioners and authorities responsible for the development, implementation and management of return, readmission and reintegration processes, while also serving other relevant stakeholders. The guidance will aim to clarify the applicable standards and frameworks for rights-based RRR management and provide concrete operational recommendations to help practitioners establish or strengthen RRR systems including through effective inter-State cooperation.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Within the Department of Mobility Pathways and Inclusion, under the overall supervision of the Head of the Border Management, Returns and Readmission Division, and under technical management of the Head of the Return and Reintegration team and the Head of the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit, and in close coordination with Cooperation on Migration and Partnerships to Achieve Sustainable Solutions (COMPASS).

**Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

Produce a coherent and comprehensive integrated guidance document on Return, Readmission and Reintegration (RRR) based on the consolidation and harmonization of the existing draft of the Technical Guidance on Return and Reintegration, developed by IOM’s Regional Office in Vienna, and the draft Readmission Manual, developed by the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit in IOM’s Headquarters. More precisely the consultant will:

1. Identify overlaps and complementarities, and propose the appropriate structure and lay out of a coherent document for optimal user experience.
2. Consult appropriate teams and partners as needed.
3. Integrate the concepts and guidance from both documents into a single coherent narrative.
4. Ensure the final document is primarily targeted at government practitioners and authorities responsible for the development, implementation and management of return, readmission and reintegration processes, while also serving other relevant stakeholders.
5. Prepare dissemination material for external use.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

Timely Delivery:

- Adherence to the agreed-upon schedule for each deliverable, including meetings, reports, and final submission dates.

Quality of Output:

- The deliverables are of good quality, technically sound, with attention to coherent structure, flow, writing style, and user experience.

  
**Category B Consultants: Tangible and measurable outputs of the work assignment**

1. First deliverable – Inception meeting with the Return and Reintegration team and the Immigration, Visa, and Readmission Unit. Proposed new structure for the document. First instalment payment - Deliverable by email.
2. Second deliverable – First draft of the consolidated guidance - Deliverable by email.
3. Third deliverable – Revised draft of the consolidated guidance based on comments received - Second instalment payment - Deliverable by email.
4. Final deliverable – Final guidance – Third and Final instalment payment (no less than 25% of overall contract value) - Deliverable by email.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in International Relations, Economics, Business Administration, Social Sciences, Law, Development Studies, International Affairs, or a related field.

**Experience**

- Experience in guidance development, policy and technical support to governments; and,
- Previous experience working with international organizations, NGOs, or government entities involved in migration and protection assistance is desirable.

**Skills**

- Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present findings in a clear and concise manner; and,
- Knowledge of return migration, readmission, reintegration and protection.

**Languages**

IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish. All staff members are required to be fluent in one of the three languages.

For this consultancy, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

  
**Notes**

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies

jobs.title: Capacity Building Specialist (Public Health) – Philippines
jobs.body:
**A.** **About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific and Africa. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to serve scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs on the strategic themes of Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. Our strategic themes are complemented and underpinned by the cross-cutting themes of gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**B. Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Action Department (PCA) strengthens the capacities of governments, response organizations, civil society, private sector actors, and at‑risk communities to prepare for, respond to, recover from disasters and adapt to the increasing risks associated with disasters and climate change. PCA emphasizes locally led preparedness and adaptation, ensuring that resilience-building efforts are rooted in local systems, institutions, knowledge, and leadership.

PCA contributes to ADPC’s regional mandate by designing and implementing programs aligned with ADPC’s strategic priority areas, including Climate Services, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Health Risk Management, Nature‑based Solutions, Resilient Recovery, and Financing for Resilience, among others. These programs support countries in advancing the Sendai Framework, SDGs, and the Paris Agreement, while strengthening institutional, community, and system-wide resilience. The department also ensures that all interventions incorporate ADPC’s core cross‑cutting themes, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Disaster and Climate Innovations, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation, as foundational elements across program design, implementation, monitoring, and knowledge generation. PCA is structured into three functional units that work together to deliver integrated preparedness and climate action programming:

- **Climate Action and Impact (CAI) –** driving climate action strategies, impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation systems, and evidence generation.
- **Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR)** – strengthening preparedness capacities, emergency response planning, and health risk management.
- **Resilience Building and Localization (RBL)** – supporting resilient recovery, localization approaches, and capacity development at national and subnational levels.

Through multi‑country operations, technical advisory services, and strategic partnerships, PCA ensures coherent, evidence‑based, and impact‑driven delivery of ADPC’s mandate across Asia and the Pacific.

**C. Statement of Intent:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) seeks to strengthen its regional programming and technical capacity for public health emergency preparedness and response across the Asia-Pacific region. Building on its experience in disaster preparedness, emergency response, regional cooperation, and multi-country program implementation, ADPC aims to strengthen its support to countries and communities in preparing for and responding to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Effective public health emergency preparedness and response require timely and coordinated action, supported by strong technical and operational capacities, effective coordination mechanisms, and capable national and local response actors. Through partnerships with governments, regional institutions, UN agencies, civil society organizations, academic and research institutions, and technical networks, ADPC promotes nationally and locally led approaches that strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery capacities.

Within this broader commitment, ADPC is a consortium partner in the Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings, led by International Medical Corps (IMC). LEARN aims to strengthen Local First Responders (LFRs), particularly Local and National Non-Governmental Organizations (L/NNGOs), to improve their readiness and multisectoral response to infectious disease outbreaks of epidemic or pandemic potential in humanitarian settings.

As a consortium partner, ADPC will provide technical and implementation support for LEARN activities in South and Southeast Asia, including the Philippines. In the Philippines, ADPC will work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to provide technical support for capacity-strengthening activities, including contextualization of LEARN materials, training facilitation, organizational capacity strengthening, remote coaching and technical assistance to participating L/NNGOs. To support this work, ADPC seeks to engage a **Capacity Building Expert (Public Health) – Philippines**. The consultant will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point, working closely with the ADPC project team, the Health Emergency Management (HEM) Specialist, the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating L/NNGOs and relevant stakeholders to plan, deliver and follow up practical technical support within the agreed country implementation arrangements.

A key focus of the assignment will be to ensure that LEARN's capacity-strengthening approaches and resources are appropriately contextualized to the Philippine public health, humanitarian, disaster risk, and institutional context, and that participating L/NNGOs receive practical technical support to strengthen their readiness and capacity to respond to infectious disease outbreaks.

**Note:** *It is not the intent of the ToR to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**D. Duties and Responsibilities:**

Under the overall guidance of the Unit Head, Emergency Preparedness and Response/LEARN Program Lead of ADPC, the Capacity Building Expert will serve as ADPC’s technical capacity-strengthening and coordination focal point for LEARN activities in the Philippines. The consultant will work closely with participating L/NNGOs, relevant stakeholders, the ADPC project team and the IMC Philippines Country Team on day-to-day planning, implementation coordination, organizational engagement and follow-up, and translation of LEARN technical approaches into practical, context-appropriate support responsive to identified organizational and operational needs. The consultant will undertake the following key responsibilities:

**1. Technical and Capacity-Building Support**

- Provide technical expertise in public health emergency preparedness and response to support ADPC's technical contribution to LEARN implementation in the Philippines.
- Jointly plan capacity-strengthening activities with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, and undertake agreed technical preparation, contextualization, facilitation and follow-up of training, exercises and other capacity-development interventions for participating L/NNGOs and local first responders, in accordance with the approved workplan and country implementation arrangements.
- Adapt relevant LEARN training materials, tools and technical resources in consultation with the IMC Philippines Country Team, participating organizations and relevant stakeholders to reflect organizational capacities, priorities and Philippine realities; submit substantive technical products to the ADPC LEARN team for technical review and quality assurance before use, and incorporate agreed feedback.
- Support the review of English-to-Filipino/Tagalog and relevant local-language translations of LEARN training materials, tools and guidance for accuracy, clarity, consistency of public health terminology and suitability for participating organizations. Work with the IMC Philippines Country Team and qualified translators or language reviewers, drawing on the Consultant’s language competencies, and coordinate with project team to resolve technical ambiguities before use.
- Provide technical facilitation and resource support for agreed LEARN training and capacity-development activities, coordinating participant engagement, schedules, field access, event arrangements and logistical requirements with the IMC Philippines Country Team and ADPC according to their agreed responsibilities.
- Apply appropriate adult-learning, participatory and practical training methodologies to strengthen the application of knowledge and skills by participating organizations.
- Provide practical technical support according to assessed needs on infectious disease preparedness and response, including Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) or equivalent response mechanisms, health emergency management (HEM) systems, activation and escalation arrangements, emergency operations/incident coordination, community-based surveillance and reporting, risk communication and community engagement (RCCE), infection prevention and control (IPC), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), referral pathways and multisectoral coordination.
- Apply the 7-1-7 framework as an additional ADPC technical framework, rather than an existing LEARN contractual requirement, with participating L/NNGOs and local first responders as appropriate to their roles and Philippine public health systems: detect a suspected infectious disease outbreak within seven days of emergence, notify the appropriate public health authority within one day of detection, and complete priority early response actions within seven days of notification.
- Integrate relevant 7-1-7 concepts into assessments, training, coaching and exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team to identify bottlenecks and enabling factors in detection, notification and early response, and strengthen reporting, activation and coordination pathways. Organizational support will contribute to wider system performance within each organization’s mandate; the Consultant will not be responsible for measuring national 7-1-7 performance.

**2. Organizational Capacity Strengthening and Technical Assistance**

- Work closely with the IMC Philippines Country Team to plan and conduct the agreed technical components of organizational and readiness assessments using agreed tools; document baseline capacities, strengths and gaps, validate findings with participating L/NNGOs, and submit findings to project team for technical review to inform capacity-strengthening support.
- Translate validated assessment findings into organization-specific capacity-strengthening action plans with participating L/NNGOs and the IMC Philippines Country Team, identifying priorities, responsible persons, timelines, training and coaching requirements, and evidence of progress. Align implementation with the Program’s approved workplan, country implementation arrangements and available resources.
- Provide ongoing technical assistance, mentoring, practical exercises and remote or in-person just-in-time coaching, as appropriate and authorized, to participating organizations to implement agreed capacity-strengthening priorities and apply learning in their preparedness and response arrangements, coordinating support and follow-up with the IMC Philippines Country Team.
- Support L/NNGOs in developing, testing and updating organizational preparedness arrangements and community response plans, including roles and responsibilities, activation triggers, reporting and referral pathways, coordination and resource needs, based on assessed priorities.
- Monitor progress against organization-specific action plans through documented follow-up, evidence of practical application and reassessment where appropriate; identify additional coaching needs, support problem-solving, and escalate unresolved technical issues and operational constraints to the Program Lead and IMC Philippines focal point, as appropriate.

**3. Stakeholder Engagement and Field Coordination**

- Coordinate regular technical engagement with participating L/NNGOs, local first responder networks, public health and humanitarian actors, community-based organizations and other relevant stakeholders in close collaboration with ADPC and the IMC Philippines Country Team, following agreed country engagement and communication arrangements.
- Jointly conduct participatory stakeholder mapping exercises with the IMC Philippines Country Team, building on existing country mapping, and periodically update the mapping of L/NNGOs, local first responders, community-based organizations, public health authorities, health facilities, surveillance and laboratory actors, humanitarian coordination mechanisms and technical partners relevant to approved project locations.

- Maintain an updated stakeholder map/database in coordination with the IMC Philippines Country Team, applying appropriate data protection procedures and sharing relevant information with ADPC.

- Contribute to consultations, technical discussions, workshops and other LEARN engagements as required.

jobs.body:
**A.** **About Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**

ADPC is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes with a vision of safer communities and sustainable development through disaster risk reduction and climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific and Africa. Established in 1986 as a technical capacity-building center, ADPC has grown and expanded its role to serve scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR).

ADPC develops and implements cross-sectoral projects/programs on the strategic themes of Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics, Policy and Institutional System, Effective Localization for Resilience, Climate Services, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Nature based Solutions, Financing for Resilience, Resilient Recovery, Food and Water Security, Disaster Risk Finance Insurance, Health Risk Management, Urban & Infrastructure Resilience, Private Sector Engagement, and ADPC Knowledge Academy. Our strategic themes are complemented and underpinned by the cross-cutting themes of gender equality and social inclusion, disaster and climate innovations, and regional and transboundary cooperation.

Through its work, ADPC supports the implementation of the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the New Urban Agenda, the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the agenda defined at the World Humanitarian Summit in 2016, and other relevant international frameworks.

For details, please refer to the ADPC website at http://www.adpc.net/.

**B. Department Introduction**

The Preparedness and Climate Action Department (PCA) strengthens the capacities of governments, response organizations, civil society, private sector actors, and at‑risk communities to prepare for, respond to, recover from disasters and adapt to the increasing risks associated with disasters and climate change. PCA emphasizes locally led preparedness and adaptation, ensuring that resilience-building efforts are rooted in local systems, institutions, knowledge, and leadership.

PCA contributes to ADPC’s regional mandate by designing and implementing programs aligned with ADPC’s strategic priority areas, including Climate Services, Preparedness and Anticipatory Action, Resilient Planning and Implementation, Health Risk Management, Nature‑based Solutions, Resilient Recovery, and Financing for Resilience, among others. These programs support countries in advancing the Sendai Framework, SDGs, and the Paris Agreement, while strengthening institutional, community, and system-wide resilience.

The department also ensures that all interventions incorporate ADPC’s core cross‑cutting themes, Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Disaster and Climate Innovations, and Regional and Transboundary Cooperation, as foundational elements across program design, implementation, monitoring, and knowledge generation. PCA is structured into three functional units that work together to deliver integrated preparedness and climate action programming:

- **Climate Action and Impact (CAI) –** driving climate action strategies, impact measurement, monitoring and evaluation systems, and evidence generation.
- **Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR)** – strengthening preparedness capacities, emergency response planning, and health risk management.
- **Resilience Building and Localization (RBL)** – supporting resilient recovery, localization approaches, and capacity development at national and subnational levels.

Through multi‑country operations, technical advisory services, and strategic partnerships, PCA ensures coherent, evidence‑based, and impact‑driven delivery of ADPC’s mandate across Asia and the Pacific.

**C. Statement of Intent:**

The Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) seeks to strengthen its regional programming and technical capacity for public health emergency preparedness and response across the Asia-Pacific region. Building on its experience in disaster preparedness, emergency response, regional cooperation, and multi-country program implementation, ADPC aims to strengthen its support to countries and communities in preparing for and responding to emerging and re-emerging infectious disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies. Effective public health emergency preparedness and response require timely and coordinated action, supported by strong technical and operational capacities, effective coordination mechanisms, and capable national and local response actors. Through partnerships with governments, regional institutions, UN agencies, civil society organizations, academic and research institutions, and technical networks, ADPC promotes nationally and locally led approaches that strengthen preparedness, response, and recovery capacities.

Within this broader commitment, ADPC is a consortium partner in the Local Engagement and Response Network (LEARN): Strengthening Localized Multi-Sectoral Readiness and Response to Infectious Disease Outbreaks in Humanitarian Settings, led by International Medical Corps (IMC). LEARN aims to strengthen Local First Responders (LFRs), particularly Local and National Non-Governmental Organizations (L/NNGOs), to improve their readiness and multisectoral response to infectious disease outbreaks of epidemic or pandemic potential in humanitarian settings.

As a consortium partner, ADPC will provide technical and implementation support for LEARN activities in South and Southeast Asia, including the Thailand–Myanmar border region. ADPC will lead field implementation in approved project locations on the Thai side of the border, including stakeholder engagement, organizational and capacity assessments, contextualization and delivery of capacity-strengthening activities, and ongoing technical assistance and mentoring for participating L/NNGOs. jobs.body:
**Job Identification:** 23420

**Posting Date:** 16/10/2026 8:03 AM

**Apply Before:** 29/10/2026 11:59 PM

**Contract Type**: Fixed-term (1 year with possibility of extension)

**Initial Contract Duration:** One Year

**Org Type:** Headquarters

**Vacancy Type:** Vacancy Notice

**Recruiting Type:** Professional

**Grade:** P-3

**Is this S/VN based in an L3 office or in support to an L3 emergency response?:** No

**Short Description**

IOM, UN Migration Agency in Geneva, Switzerland is looking for a Legal Officer who will work in the General and Administrative Law Division (LEGGL) and provide legal advice, recommendations and services related to the legal status, constitution, functions, rules and activities of the Organization, particularly involving human resources legal issues.

**Description**

**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.  
  
IOM is committed to ensuring a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally, while working towards harnessing the full potential of migration. Read more about IOM's workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration.

Applications are welcome from first- and second-tier candidates, particularly qualified female candidates as well as applications from the non-represented member countries of IOM. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process.

For the purpose of this vacancy, the following are considered first-tier candidates:

1. Internal candidates
2. Candidates from the following IOM Member States that are not represented among staff members in the Professional and higher categories: *Bahamas, Barbados, Comoros, Congo (the), Cook Islands, Dominica, Federated States of Micronesia, Grenada, Guinea-Bissau, Holy See, Iceland, Israel, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Namibia, Nauru, Palau, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Samoa, Sao Tome and Principe, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Suriname, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Vanuatu*

Second tier candidates include:  
All external candidates, except candidates from non-represented member states of IOM.

**Context**

The Office of Legal Affairs provides legal advice to the Director General, the Deputy Directors General, the regional offices, the country offices, and other departments and offices of the Organization. The Office provides support to ensure that the activities and operations of the Organization are carried out in accordance with the legal framework governing IOM, including the IOM Constitution, decisions of the governing bodies of IOM, the Unified Staff Regulations and Rules, the Financial Regulations and Rules, IOM instructions and international law.

The General and Administrative Law Division is responsible for:

- Advising on misconduct cases and the management of disciplinary processes, including the imposition of disciplinary and non-disciplinary measures.
- Reviewing the legality of contested decisions in formal Requests for Review by staff members.
- Representing the Organization in internal justice processes, including the Joint Appeals Review Board and the International Labour Organization Administrative Tribunal.
- Reviewing investigation reports and other findings of the Office of Internal Oversight in relation to IOM personnel.
- Reviewing policies related to management and human resources, including revisions to the Unified Staff Regulations and Rules, instructions and other issuances.
- Assisting with the roll-out of the Unified Staff Rules to local staff members in IOM country offices worldwide.
- Advising on privileges and immunities matters related to employment disputes, including on litigation filed in national courts.
- Preparing legal advice on the interpretation and application of personnel policies, contractual terms and complex administrative law matters.
- Reviewing contracts, agreements and templates for staff and non-staff personnel (including for internships, consultancies, escorts, loans, secondments, Junior Professional Officers, and settlements with staff members).

Under the overall supervision of the Head, General & Administrative Law Division and the direct supervision of the Senior Legal Officer, the Legal Officer will work in the General and Administrative Law Division (LEG-GL) and provide legal advice, recommendations and services related to the legal status, constitution, functions, rules and activities of the Organization, particularly involving human resources legal issues.

**Responsibilities**

**Responsibilities and Accountabilities**

1. Provide legal advice to IOM offices on privileges and immunities issues arising from, for example, claims filed by staff or individual contractors before national authorities, arrest and detention of IOM personnel, tax exemption, affiliation of staff in the national security system etc.
2. Draft submissions on behalf of the Organization in administrative and tribunal proceedings, including before the Joint Administrative Review Board (JARB) and the International Labour Organization Administrative Tribunal (ILOAT).
3. Review Investigation Reports received from the Office of the Internal Oversight (OIO), make a legal assessment as to whether a disciplinary process is warranted, and either initiate a disciplinary process or draft legal advice on other measures to be taken.
4. Draft legal advice to senior officials on matters involving application of international administrative law, including recommendations for amicable settlement of litigation, final decisions by the Director General upon completion of the internal appeal process, disciplinary measures or other administrative measures upon completion of disciplinary processes; further assist in the implementation of these recommendations.
5. Attend internal and external meetings and conferences relevant to LEG-GL.
6. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Law from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- At least five years of relevant professional experience is required for candidates holding a Master's degree (seven years for candidates holding a University/ Bachelor's degree), including at least four years in International Administrative Law, with demonstrated experience over those years in: (i) staff misconduct cases, including disciplinary proceedings, and (ii) drafting internal justice system and ILOAT pleadings.

**Skills**

- Excellent writing and research skills; and,
- Knowledge of public international law, in particular knowledge of the ILOAT jurisprudence and international administrative law, are required.

**Languages**

All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators Level 2

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- **Delivering results**: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- **Managing and sharing knowledge**: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- **Accountability**: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- **Communication**: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

Internationally recruited professional staff are required to be mobile. Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

Vacancies close at 23:59 local time Geneva, Switzerland on the respective closing date. No late applications will be accepted.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
