Plan International started working in Egypt in 1981 and has a presence in ten of the 27 governorates in which the country including Greater Cairo, Alexandria, Giza, Beheira, Kalyoubia, Damietta, Qena, Assuit and Sohag. Plan international Egypt implements programmes designed to enable communities to improve the lives of the most marginalised children and their families. Plan Egypt’s Country Strategy focuses on five strategic objectives.

Through a five-interconnected, gender transformative and context-fit country objectives, PIE intends along with the various stakeholders at all levels to continue delivering positive and transformative changes so that **“Children, especially girls, and young people grow up in an enabling environment, realizing their rights and contributing in both development and humanitarian settings as active agents of change”.**

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

Driven by the overall purpose of PII and anchored on Plan International core values, bolder commitment to gender transformation and feminist leadership, program quality and influencing and a more vibrant and efficient operating model.

**ABOUT THE ROLE**

The Project Officer is responsible for the implementation of the “Smart Production: Enhance Competitiveness and Employability” project in the assigned governorate (Alexandria). In addition, the post holder supervises the Project Assistant implementing the “Enhance Stability and Social Cohesion in Egypt, Phase 2” project in the same location, and is accountable for the quality and timely delivery of both projects at governorate level. He/she will work with various stakeholders, including WFP, government entities, schools, the private sector, consultants and community partners.

**THE SCOPE**

Under the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, the Project Officer leads the day-to-day implementation of the Smart Production project in the assigned governorate, including coordination with production units, consultants, schools, education directorates, private sector actors and community partners. The Project Officer also supervises the Project Assistant of the Enhance Stability project in the same location, providing day-to-day direction, quality assurance and review of field, data and administrative work, and ensuring both projects are implemented in line with the approved work plans, budgets and WFP requirements.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES AND MAIN WORK ACTIVITIES**

**Smart Production project implementation**

- Develop and monitor implementation, procurement, and training plans, in line with the overall work plan, budget and WFP requirements.
- Assess production units and workshops, and oversee coaching, improvement plans, and quality compliance.
- Coordinate occupational health and safety training and safe work practices.
- Facilitate artisan linkages with production units and shared workspaces.
- Support seed fund assessments and monitor fund utilization and improvements
- Coordinate practical training placements and participant documentation.
- Manage Digital Skills Accelerator training, participant selection, and employment linkages.
- Coordinate vocational, soft skills, and employability training with education stakeholders.
- Build private sector partnerships to enhance market access and youth employment opportunities.

**Supervision and oversight of the Enhance Stability project (location level)**

- Supervise and coach Project Assistants, including work planning and performance management.
- Oversee quality implementation of participant selection, training, mentorship, and grant follow-up activities.
- Review participant data, selection decisions, and reports for accuracy and compliance.
- Review procurement requests and supporting documentation against budgets and procedures.
- Promote project integration by creating linkages between beneficiaries, training initiatives, and market opportunities.

**Partnerships and Coordination**

- Represent the organization and maintain stakeholder relations with government, partners, donors, and the private sector.
- Coordinate and oversee consultants and service providers, including deliverables and performance.
- Secure approvals and facilitate smooth implementation of field activities through effective stakeholder engagement.

**Finance, procurement and administration**

- Raise and manage purchase requisitions in SAP, ensuring budget and donor compliance.
- Monitor project budgets and expenditures, and report variances.
- Maintain complete, accurate, and audit-ready financial and activity documentation.

**Monitoring, reporting and learning**

- Ensure timely collection, verification, and reporting of participant data and project indicators.
- Prepare monthly progress reports, highlighting achievements, challenges, and mitigation actions.
- Support monitoring visits, assessments, and post-distribution monitoring activities.
- Document success stories, lessons learned, and good practices to support project learning.
- Promote and monitor the project feedback and complaints mechanism for effective stakeholder engagement.

**Safeguarding Children and Young People and Gender Equality and Inclusion (GEI)**

- Understands and puts into practice the responsibilities under Global Safeguarding and GEI policies and Plan International’s Code of Conduct (CoC), ensuring that concerns are reported and managed in accordance with the appropriate procedures. Ensure the said policies are fully embedded during implementation, including in activities with school students, and applied in the day-to-day work of the team.
- Ensures that the Project Assistant, consultants and service providers are properly inducted on and understand their role in upholding Plan International’s safeguarding and GEI policies.

**What we are looking for:**

**Qualifications**

- A bachelor degree in Social Sciences, Business Administration, Economics, Development Studies or similar field.
- 3-5 years of experience in livelihoods, economic empowerment, employability or vocational training projects, preferably in an INGO or UN agency.
- Experience working with the private sector, small businesses or production units on market linkages, product quality or value chains.
- Experience coordinating with government entities, including education directorates and schools, and with civil society organisations.
- Experience working with refugees and host communities in Egypt.
- Experience supervising staff or volunteers.
- Experience in planning, conducting and facilitating trainings and workshops.
- Proven skills in documentation, reporting and analysis of lessons learned, good practices and project outcomes.

**Knowledge:**

- Advanced understanding of the development needs and vulnerabilities of youth, women, refugees and host communities, the root causes of the issues affecting them, and the key actors most relevant to their interests.
- Knowledge of labour market dynamics, employability and enterprise development in Egypt.
- Knowledge on gender transformative approaches, working in partnership, evidence-based approaches, and working to strengthen civil society.

**Skills**

- Providing clear direction and support to team members.
- Using on-going monitoring and assessment, working closely with project teams to improve the quality of implementation.
- Interpreting and contextualising data, assessing results and drawing conclusions to inform initiatives and communicate lessons learned.
- Numeracy and the ability to interpret financial data to support budget planning, monitoring and reporting.
- Ability to interact and work effectively with others at all levels.
- Strong skills in facilitation, team player, time management, negotiation and problem-solving and good report writing skills.

**Please respond to the requirements of this role in your application.**  
**Only applications in English language will be accepted.**

**Location: On site working and the role is based in Alexandria**

**Reports to: Project Coordinator WFP**

**Job Grade: Hay Level 12**

**Contract end date: 30th April 2028**

**Vacancy advert closing Date: 29th October 2026**

**This vacancy is open to Egypt nationals only.**

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**Disclaimer: Plan International is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate applicants on any basis. We also do not charge Job seekers any fees at any point of the recruitment process.**

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:**  Casework Supervisor
- **Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Youth Employability Technical Expert
jobs.body:
**EXTERNAL ANNOUNCEMENT**

**TITLE: Youth Employability Technical Expert**

**Contract Type: National**

**TEAM/PROGRAMME: Programme Development & Quality**

**LOCATION: Bangkok**

**CONTRACT LENGTH: 12 months, renewable based on performance and continued funding availability/** **PART-TIME (8-12 days PER month)**

**ROLE PURPOSE:**

The Youth Employability Technical Advisor will ensure that Save the Children delivers technically sound, evidence-based youth employment programming across all priority cohorts — Not in Education, Employment, or Training (NEET) youth, and youth in vocational/Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) pathways — with a focus on innovative, inclusive employability skills, entrepreneurship, and life skills development. The post holder will ensure key organizational principles (child participation, accountability, disability and gender inclusion) are embedded throughout the project cycle. S/he will provide the technical backbone connecting concurrent donor-funded grants (UNIQLO(80%), and Accenture(20%)), ensuring coherence of approach, quality of donor reporting, and cross-cohort learning, while developing strategic partnerships with private sector employers, government institutions (including the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities), and civil society organizations.

Save the Children (Thailand) Foundation (SCT) has found it challenging to identify a single technical expert with the breadth of experience to credibly cover this range of youth groups while maintaining the depth expected of a senior technical advisor. This Terms of Reference has been strengthened accordingly: rather than a general youth-employability generalist, SCT is seeking a senior, multi-disciplinary technical advisor capable of providing credible, high-quality technical leadership across NEET programming and TVET/vocational pathways, , while ensuring coherent reporting and learning across these concurrent donor-funded grants.

The Youth Employability Technical Advisor will ensure that Save the Children delivers technically sound, evidence-based youth employment programming across all priority cohorts — NEET youth, and youth in vocational/TVET pathways, with a focus on innovative, inclusive employability skills, entrepreneurship, and life skills development. The post holder will ensure key organizational principles (child participation, accountability, disability and gender inclusion) are embedded throughout the project cycle. S/he will provide the technical backbone connecting the concurrent donor-funded grants (UNIQLO, and Accenture), ensuring coherence of approach, quality of donor reporting, and cross-cohort learning, while developing strategic partnerships with private sector employers, government institutions, and civil society organizations.

**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

**Reports to**: Director of Strategy, Program Quality and Impact

**Dotted line report to**: Director of Program

**Role Dimensions**: Coordination with Youth Employability Program Coordinators across all three grants, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team, Save the Children US Skills to Succeed / Life Skills for Success (LS4S) program team, other Technical Advisors, donor focal points, and key external partners (e.g., Klong Toei Deejang, Vulcan Coalition, TVET institutions, and relevant government counterparts).

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**

**Key Area 1:** Technical Leadership Across Vulnerable Youth Cohorts

- Provide credible, high-quality technical guidance spanning all four priority youth groups — not a single specialization.
- Provide ongoing technical support and leadership to program staff working with youth with disabilities, NEET youth, and youth in TVET/vocational pathways, ensuring each cohort's distinct barriers and needs are reflected in program design.
- Make use of the labour market assessments and needs analysis (e.g., NEET Youth Needs Analysis in Khlong Toey), ensuring that it is applied to define future works where cohort-specific barriers, aspirations, and employer demand are taken into account
- Ensure the Life Skills for Success (LS4S) / Skills to Succeed (S2S) modules are contextually adapted — including disability-accessible formats and migrant-sensitive content — for each cohort and delivery setting.
- Identify and develop strategic partnerships with private sector employers (including hospitality, retail, and property-sector partners linked to Ascott, CapitaLand, and UNIQLO), government institutions, and disability/civil society organizations.

**Key Area 2:** Program Quality and Capacity Building

- Ensure technical consistency and build sustainable capacity among SCT staff and partners.
- Design and deliver workshops and Training of Trainers (ToT) sessions for SCT staff and partner organizations (TVET institutions, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)) to build and sustain technical capacity.
- Ensure MEAL systems disaggregate data by cohort (NEET status) so that equity of outcomes across groups can be tracked and reported, not just aggregate program reach.

**Key Area 3:** Multi-Donor Program Coordination and Development

- Maintain technical coherence and quality across three concurrent donor-funded grants.
- Support project teams in producing high-quality, timely technical reporting across all donor portfolios (UNIQLO (80%), Accenture (20%)), ensuring a coherent technical narrative and avoiding duplication of effort.
- Maintain a coordinated planning cycle (annual, quarterly, monthly) across grants, ensuring complementarity between cohort-specific activities and shared program infrastructure.
- Contribute to funding strategies and proposal development to expand or sustain the youth employability portfolio, packaging concepts for a range of institutional and private donors.

**Key Area 4:** Representation, Networking, and Advocacy

- Represent SCT's technical position externally and build the partnerships needed for scale.
- Co-present research and assessment findings to government counterparts, TVET institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Actively participate in technical coordination meetings and sector fora to ensure synergy with other agencies working on inclusive youth employment.

**Key Area 5**: Evidence, Learning, and Documentation

- Ensure learning across cohorts and grants strengthens the wider portfolio.
- Ensure lessons derived from implementation across all cohorts are well articulated, documented, and disseminated both internally and externally.
- Feed learning and evidence of impact into the strategic development and quality assurance of the overall Child Poverty / youth employability portfolio.

**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice):**

**Accountability:**

- Holds self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values
- Holds the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

**Ambition:**

- Sets ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourages their team to do the same
- Widely shares their personal vision for Save the Children, engages and motivates others
- Future orientated, thinks strategically and on a global scale.

**Collaboration:**

- Builds and maintains effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, Members and external partners and supporters
- Values diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength
- Approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

**Creativity:**

- Develops and encourages new and innovative solutions
- Willing to take disciplined risks.

**Integrity:**

- Honest, encourages openness and transparency; demonstrates highest levels of integrity

The post holder must commit to work in an international agency that promotes diversity, equity and inclusion and fights racism, gender inequality and discrimination in all forms; and to model positive behaviours that demonstrate a commitment to equality and respect to all colleagues, partners and communities.

**QUALIFICATIONS**:

- Master's degree (or equivalent post-graduate qualification) in a field relevant to economics, international development, social development, education, or disability studies.
- Minimum 5–7 years of progressive professional experience in youth employability and livelihoods programming, with demonstrated breadth across at least two of the following: NEET youth programming, TVET/vocational pathways, and/or migrant youth employment.

**EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS**

**Essential**

- Demonstrated technical expertise spanning multiple vulnerable youth cohorts, rather than a single specialization — this is a core requirement given the program's intersectional caseload.
- Experience adapting life-skills/employability curricula (e.g., Skills to Succeed, Life Skills for Success, or comparable models) for different population needs, including disability-accessible adaptation.
- Experience developing private-sector partnerships for inclusive hiring, ideally within hospitality, retail, or real estate/property sectors.
- Experience providing technical inputs across multiple concurrent donor-funded grants, including coordinated reporting and cross-portfolio learning.
- Strong quantitative and qualitative research skills, including labour marketassessments and needs assessments.
- Demonstrated experience in monitoring and evaluation, including disaggregated data systems for equity tracking.
- Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship-management skills across government (including disability-focused bodies), UN agencies, private sector, and civil society.
- Strong facilitation skills, with experience delivering training and workshops (including ToT) to diverse audiences.
- Excellent spoken and written communication skills in English; professional working proficiency in Thai preferred.
- Commitment to Save the Children's mission, values, and approach, including child focus, gender equality, disability inclusion, and child rights.

**Desirable**

- Experience working in Thailand or Southeast Asia.
- Understanding of Thailand's disability employment quota law and Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEP) employer guidelines.
- Familiarity with the regulatory context for migrant worker employment in Thailand.
- Experience with digital or AI-enabled employability and job-readiness tools.
- Experience implementing programs with corporate/CSR-funded partners (e.g., retail, hospitality, or real estate sector donors).

**Additional job responsibilities**

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience

**Equal Opportunities**

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the Save the Children International (SCI) Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

**Child Safeguarding:**

We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.

**Health and Safety**

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SCI Health and Safety policies and procedures.

**“We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse”**

jobs.title: Oficial de Finanzas - Maracaibo
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Finanzas** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

El Oficial de Finanzas tendrá la tarea de apoyar las operaciones financieras para cumplir con los requisitos internos, externos y reglamentación legal, así como velar por el cumplimiento de los criterios de Donantes. El Oficial de Finanzas deberá estar familiarizado con la preparación de presupuestos, seguimiento presupuestario, actividades contables y procedimientos de auditorías externas.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Gestión Financiera y Presupuestaria**

- Asegurarse que los datos y las transacciones se registren correctamente y se ingresen en el ERP de DRC.
- Preparar y conciliar estados de cuenta bancarios acorde a las fechas límites establecidas semanales y mensuales.
- Asegurar el correcto manejo contable, de acuerdo con las leyes, normas y procedimientos contables aplicables.
- Mantener archivos y registros financieros ordenadamente.
- Realizar un seguimiento mensual de los contratos y asegurarse de que todos los contratos se renueven, cierren o paguen a tiempo.
- Archivar, escanear y enviar mensualmente documentos financieros a la oficina LAC.
- Usar correctamente las funcionalidades del ERP de DRC, Microsoft Dynamics.
- Realizar seguimiento presupuestal para todos los presupuestos asignados a la oficina Maracaibo.
- Apoyo en la elaboración de informes a donantes.
- Apoyar la organización de auditorías externas, internas y solicitud de información de donantes.
- Asegurarse del cierre contable semanal de la oficina de Venezuela y el envío de los “Conteos de Caja” a tiempo.
- Asegurarse del cierre mensual contable de la base dentro de los tiempos establecidos.
- Preparación y revisión de los pagos gestionados en la oficina.
- Manejar la plataforma bancaria.
- Causar pagos en el sistema DRC Dynamics y montarlos al banco, previa revisión del cumplimiento de los procedimientos internos de DRC, así como de los soportes correspondientes.

**Gestión de efectivo.**

- Mantener los controles de efectivo de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos por DRC.
- Monitorear las reservas de efectivo.
- Preparar las solicitudes de efectivo a la sede Venezuela.
- Efectuar transacciones bancarias.
- Mantener el registro diario actualizado de las transacciones en el sistema DRC Dynamics.
- Manejo y gestión de los recursos de caja menor de acuerdo con los procedimientos establecidos por DRC

**Administración**

- Actuar como auditor/verificador de los procesos del área contable y de finanzas en la base.
- Cumplir con los requisitos internos de los donantes.
- Gestionar los procesos documentales correspondientes a la contratación.
- Apoyar el proceso administrativo de reclutamiento y selección de personal.
- Apoyar el proceso administrativo de gestión documental de las áreas de finanzas.
- Asesorar en procesos de perdiem y legalización de gastos del personal de la base DRC Maracaibo.

**Competencias esenciales:**

- Al menos 2 años de experiencia laboral con una ONG internacional en un rol similar.
- Competencias elevadas en el manejo de computadores
- Experiencia trabajando con ERP
- Dominio básico en PowerPoint y Word y con experiencia en Excel.
- Buena capacidad de comunicación y organización documental.

**Competencias deseables:**

- Manejo experto de la suite de Microsoft Office.
- Conocimiento en Microsoft Dynamics.

**Educación (Incluir certificados, licencias)**

- Titulo universitario en Finanzas / Administración de Empresas / Contabilidad o su equivalente en experiencia.

**Idiomas:**

- Fluidez en inglés ( Deseable )escrito y hablado

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 25 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

jobs.title: Data Analyst and Modeler, VisionFund International
jobs.body:
VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Data Analyst and Modeler, VFI**, you will contribute to VisionFund’s distinct approach to inclusive financial services by supporting impact-first financial products with layered training and delivery through the World Vision Partnership to improve outcomes for children in the poorest households. You will help ensure the credibility of VisionFund’s impact on household and child well-being through high-quality evidence, data models, and analysis.

You will be responsible for developing new data models and optimizing and maintaining existing data models for financial and data analysis. You will analyse, design, structure, and manage data sources that support business requirements and align with enterprise standards. You will apply strong technical skills in business analytics, particularly with MS Excel, DAX formula language, Power BI Data Modeling, and related technologies. You will also apply advanced knowledge and skills in developing reports and dashboards using tools including, but not limited to, Power BI and Excel.

You will design, develop, deploy, and optimize new and existing data models in line with approved standards and practices. You will gather and understand customer requirements and translate these needs into data models or reports. You will manage the maintenance or extraction of data sources required for data models, reports, and analyses, liaising with data owners and stakeholders to ensure data integrity and resolve data quality issues. You will maintain VFI Power BI data models for VFI Financial Reporting and Analysis and other departments as assigned, provide support to users of existing data models, and develop, maintain, and ensure proper documentation of data models and data fields.

You will design and implement data governance to support proper data management. You will collaborate with GTD and other departments to ensure the timely refresh, maintenance, and validation of existing data models, where applicable. You will perform all other duties assigned to you and attend and participate in meetings, team events, and conferences as assigned. You will attend chapel services, daily devotions, and group devotions. You will promote World Vision’s values through your example and hold yourself and others accountable across the team.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor or University degree in Finance, Computer Science or related field.
- Minimum 4 years of experience in positions on data analysis or related areas.
- Experience working in an international non-profit organization or multinational corporation.
- At least 1 year of experience with business intelligence tools or financial software (e.g. Sunsystems, Datawarehouse, Dashboards) and reporting tools.
- At least 2 years of experience in Power BI Data modelling and writing complex DAX code for data manipulation.
- Excellent skills in structured problem solving and ability to perform complex analyses and draw meaningful and actionable insights.
- Demonstrate ability to understand multiple data sources and how they relate to each other.
- Strong technical skills in Microsoft Office.
- Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written at all levels with a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail: ability to communicate technical information to non-technical audiences.
- Superior organization, prioritization, and self-motivation skills.

**Preferred:**

- Experience in Financial Reporting and understanding finance and accounting is an advantage.

**Work Environment/Travel:**

- 5% Travel as needed. If employed in GCMO, this position is eligible for hybrid work and its application must comply with GCMO and/or GFSC hybrid policies and procedures.

jobs.title: Asistente WASI - Maracaibo
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Asistente WASI** altamente calificado con sede en **Maracaibo, Edo. Zulia.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO:**

Bajo la supervisión del Gerente de base, y acompañamiento técnico de especialista WASI (basada en Maracaibo) la/él Asistente de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene (WASI) estará directamente involucrado y velará por la implementación diaria de las actividades de Agua, responsable de brindar apoyo en la implementación de actividades del proyecto en terreno, principalmente en la preparación y ejecución de las jornadas de entregas, así como en procesos logísticos, comunitarios y de documentación garantizando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos y directrices de DRC.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

**Apoyo operativo y logístico**:

- Participar en evaluaciones de necesidades relacionadas con el agua, el saneamiento y la higiene en las comunidades de acogida, instituciones y otros sitios de interés en Zulia, según las instrucciones del Gerente de Base y bajo la gestión técnica del especialista de WASI.
- Participar en el alistamiento y organización del sitio de distribución, garantizando condiciones adecuadas de orden, seguridad, señalización, flujo de atención, control de multitudes y accesibilidad para personas con necesidades específicas.
- Colaborar activamente en la entrega directa kits de WASI, NFI, TANDAS, entre otros, promoviendo un trato digno, respetuoso y libre de discriminación hacia las Personas de Interés (PDI), y asegurando orden y fluidez en el proceso.
- Apoyar en la recepción, descarga, verificación de cantidades y control de calidad de alimentos y otros insumos, asegurando su almacenamiento temporal adecuado conforme a estándares básicos de higiene y conservación.
- Asegurar el resguardo, organización y control de materiales, inventarios en campo y medios de verificación (actas, listados firmados, formatos logísticos, reportes de incidencias).
- Participar en la verificación conjunta de bienes y equipos adquiridos, comprobando su conformidad con las especificaciones técnicas, cantidades y condiciones establecidas.
- Otras actividades necesarias para la correcta implementación del proyecto, según lineamientos del Team Leader o Gerente de Recuperación Económica.
- Completar los formularios y la documentación adecuada del sector WASH para los proyectos de intervención, como: levantamiento de necesidades, propuestas de proyectos, cómputos métricos, cronogramas, planos, diseños esquemáticos, manejo de coordenadas GPS, mapeo de las actividades/áreas del proyecto, especificaciones y diseño del contenido de kits WASH, entre otros.
- Hacer un seguimiento e inspección adecuados de las obras de agua y saneamiento en terreno, así como el seguimiento de la ejecución física y financiera y las gestiones para el pago a las empresas de servicios y obras
- Realizar cualquier otra tarea relevante según lo soliciten los gerentes de línea y el equipo de agua, saneamiento e higiene.

**Acompañamiento comunitario**

- Brindar orientación a beneficiarios sobre el proceso de entrega y tiempos de entrega.
- Dar prioridad a personas con necesidades específicas: personas mayores, mujeres embarazadas, personas con discapacidad, entre otros.
- Apoyar en la planificación y preparación operativa de las actividades comunitarias (convocatorias, coordinación con líderes comunitarios, verificación de listados y organización de cronogramas).
- Respetar las prácticas culturales de las comunidades indígenas y apoyar en la logística de actividades participativas.
- Facilitar la realización de los talleres o actividades comunitarias requeridas por el programa, acorde con la identificación de necesidades.

**Documentación y soporte al monitoreo**

- Apoyar en la recopilación y organización de medios de verificación requeridos para reportes, monitoreo post-distribución (PDM) y líneas de base.
- Informar al TL o Gerente sobre cualquier incidencia, reclamo o dificultad presentada durante las actividades.
- Llevar la bitácora de actividades y de rutas cuando será requerida por el gerente de bas

**Experiencia y Competencias Técnicas:**

- Al menos 1 año de experiencia en trabajo con comunidades o en proyectos sociales/humanitarios.
- Experiencia en entrega y administración de ayudas humanitarias.
- Experiencia en contextos rurales y de difícil acceso o comunidades indígenas será un valor agregado.
- Capacidad de auto-organización
- Conocimiento e interés por el sector humanitario
- Capacidad de trabajar bien bajo presión y en condiciones adversas.
- Conocimiento básico de Excel

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda I.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Domingo 25 de Octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.

**Fecha de inicio aproximada:** Noviembre 2026

jobs.title: Regional Safeguarding and Protection Advisor - MEER
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Regional Safeguarding and Protection Advisor - MEER**, you will empower Middle East and Eastern Europe Field Offices to implement World Vision International’s Safeguarding and Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) policies and deliver quality, sustainable programmes in line with international humanitarian standards and commitments on safeguarding, PSEAH, and gender equality. You will support safeguarding policy implementation, strengthen protection and GEDSI practices, build staff and partner capacity, and promote inclusive programming and organizational practices across the region.

**A. Regional Safeguarding and Protection**

You will strengthen safeguarding leadership and culture across Field and Regional Offices by building the capacity of safeguarding focal points, advising on risks and programme design, promoting compliance, and ensuring adequate resources. You will support implementation of child and adult safeguarding policies, accessible complaints mechanisms, safeguarding self-assessments and action plans, staff and partner training, and incident preparedness and response. You will promote confidentiality and survivor-centred approaches while coordinating support for affected individuals and staff.

**B. Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)**

You will lead regional GEDSI and protection initiatives by strengthening staff, partner, and volunteer capacity; promoting partnerships with women’s organizations and organizations of persons with disabilities; and integrating gender equality, disability inclusion, and social inclusion across development, humanitarian, and nexus programming. You will guide GEDSI policy implementation, gender and disability analysis, inclusive data collection, programme indicators, and adequate budgeting. You will also develop and share regional GEDSI research and learning, strengthen strategic partnerships and networks, and promote inclusive organizational practices through self-assessments, action planning, and awareness-building.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor’s or master’s degree in law, social work, gender studies, development studies, or other relevant field
- Technical skills: direct programming or management experience in child protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), gender-based violence (GBV) or safeguarding
- Experience: 2 years’ + experience in overseeing child protection, PSEA, GBV, or safeguarding work
- Understanding of institutional donors and INGO GEDSI frameworks, emerging models, policies and/or programming
- Excellent project management, partnering and communications skills
- Strong relationship building/network capacity, excellent communication skills, spiritual maturity in Christian faith, ability to influence, innovative, and proactive personality
- Five years of direct programming or management experience in gender and protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), gender-based violence (GBV) or safeguarding in an international NGO
- Experience in supporting GESI responsive and transformative designs and related mainstreaming strategies and activities across various sectors
- Experience leading GESI analysis (specifically gender and disability analysis) to inform design and to support GESI-Responsive monitoring and evaluation
- Experience leading or supporting Organisational GESI Self-Assessments or GESI Audits
- Experience in capacity building and staff empowerment

**Required Language(s):** Fluency in spoken and written English.

**Required travel and/or work environment accommodations:** The position requires ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to 20% of the time.

jobs.title: Especialista en Comunicaciones y Relaciones Públicas
jobs.body:
La organización Plan International es una organización humanitaria y de desarrollo independiente que promueve los derechos de los niños y la igualdad de las niñas.

Creemos en el poder y el potencial de cada niño. Pero esto a menudo se ve reprimido por la pobreza, la violencia, la exclusión y la discriminación. Y son las niñas las más afectadas.

Trabajando junto con los niños, los jóvenes, nuestros partidarios y socios, luchamos por un mundo justo, abordando las causas profundas de los desafíos que enfrentan las niñas y todos los niños vulnerables.

Apoyamos los derechos de los niños desde su nacimiento hasta que llegan a la edad adulta. Y permitimos que los niños se preparen para las crisis y la adversidad y respondan a ellas. Impulsamos cambios en la práctica y las políticas a nivel local, nacional y global utilizando nuestro alcance, experiencia y conocimiento.

Hemos estado construyendo alianzas poderosas para los niños durante más de 85 años y ahora estamos activos en más de 80 países.

## PROPOSITO DEL CARGO

El/la Especialista en Comunicaciones y Relaciones Públicas (México) implementa la estrategia de comunicación externa del país, asegurando su alineación con los objetivos de país, del clúster CAM-RD y regionales. Esta posición integra responsabilidades estratégicas y operativas clave de comunicación institucional, relaciones públicas, campañas, gestión digital, producción de contenido y apoyo de diseño gráfico.

El rol fortalece la visibilidad, reputación y posicionamiento de Plan International en México, promoviendo los derechos de la niñez, la igualdad de las niñas y mujeres, la influencia, la recaudación de fondos y el relacionamiento con stakeholders. Asimismo, garantiza que los contenidos, canales y materiales de comunicación cumplan con los lineamientos de marca, salvaguarda, consentimiento de uso de imagen y estándares institucionales.

## DIMENSIONES DEL CARGO

- Diseña e implementa la estrategia de comunicación externa de México, alineada a prioridades nacionales, del clúster CAM-RD y regionales.
- Gestiona relaciones públicas, comunicación institucional y posicionamiento con medios, socios, donantes y stakeholders clave.
- Diseña, adapta e implementa campañas globales, regionales y locales, asegurando mensajes clave y materiales de calidad.
- Diseña e implementa estrategia de marketing digital a través de los canales digitales priorizados del país, incluyendo redes sociales, sitio web y otros espacios digitales definidos.
- Crea, adapta y coordina contenidos escritos, visuales y audiovisuales, incluyendo apoyo básico en diseño y edición cuando se requiera.
- Monitorea métricas de comunicación, medios y canales digitales, y reporta avances y aprendizajes para la toma de decisiones.
- Asegura el cumplimiento de lineamientos de marca, salvaguarda, protocolos digitales y consentimiento de uso de imagen.
- Apoya la comunicación interna, la respuesta comunicacional ante emergencias y la gestión administrativa del área.

## RESPONSABILIDADES

### 1. Estrategia de comunicación externa

1. - Diseña e implementa el plan anual de comunicaciones de México, alineado a prioridades nacionales, del Clúster CAM-RD y regionales.
    - Define prioridades de comunicación, mensajes clave, audiencias y oportunidades de posicionamiento junto con la Coordinación de Comunicaciones del Clúster.
    - Da seguimiento a KPIs, resultados y aprendizajes de comunicación para orientar decisiones y mejorar la efectividad del trabajo.
    - Mantiene informada a la Coordinación de comunicaciones del Clúster y a la Representación de país sobre contexto, oportunidades, riesgos reputacionales y necesidades comunicacionales del país.
    - Implementa el presupuesto del área de comunicaciones a nivel local y da seguimiento a procesos administrativos vinculados con el área como gestión con proveedores, entre otros.

### 2. Relaciones públicas, medios y comunicación institucional

- Fortalece relaciones con periodistas, medios, socios, donantes, instituciones y actores clave para aumentar la visibilidad de Plan International México.
- Coordina notas de prensa, comunicados, entrevistas, talking points, historias institucionales y publicaciones sobre el trabajo del país.
- Acompaña a vocerías y equipos técnicos en oportunidades de prensa, eventos y espacios de posicionamiento.
- Monitorea presencia en medios y recopila aprendizajes para mejorar la estrategia de relaciones públicas.

### 3. Campañas, contenidos y diseño gráfico

- Diseña campañas locales en México, adapta campañas globales y regionales que se implementen en el país, articulando mensajes, materiales, canales y acciones con el Clúster.
- Produce y coordina contenidos para influencia, recaudación de fondos, relacionamiento con donantes y visibilidad de proyectos.
- Desarrolla historias de vida, testimonios, guiones, publicaciones, notas y contenidos para audiencias externas e internas.
- Prioriza productos de campaña según objetivos estratégicos, oportunidades, recursos disponibles y capacidad operativa de una sola posición.

### 4. Gestión digital, redes sociales y comunidad

- Diseña e implementa estrategia de marketing digital para las redes sociales de Plan International México.
- Administra las redes sociales priorizadas de Plan International México, siguiendo la estrategia digital, protocolos institucionales y lineamientos de salvaguarda.
- Planifica, programa, publica y actualiza contenidos para redes sociales, sitio web, blogs, email marketing u otros canales definidos.
- Gestiona interacciones con audiencias digitales, incluyendo comentarios, mensajes, alertas y oportunidades de engagement, con orientación del Clúster cuando sea necesario.
- Da seguimiento a métricas digitales, gestiona presupuesto y pauta digital aprobada y desempeño de contenidos para ajustar formatos, mensajes y frecuencia de publicación.

### 5. Producción visual, audiovisual y calidad de materiales

- Realiza o coordina el levantamiento de fotografías, videos, entrevistas y contenidos de campo, asegurando consentimiento informado y protección de imagen.
- Diseña o adapta piezas para redes sociales, comunicación interna y canales digitales con herramientas disponibles como Canva, Adobe u otras plataformas.
- Edita o adapta contenidos visuales y audiovisuales de manera básica, procurando calidad institucional y recomendando contratación externa cuando el producto requiera especialización.
- Organiza y mantiene actualizada la biblioteca de fotografías, videos, historias, testimonios y materiales finales del país.

### 6. Marca, salvaguarda, coordinación interna y soporte operativo

- Asegura el cumplimiento de identidad visual, lineamientos de marca, lenguaje institucional, salvaguarda, consentimiento informado y protección de datos.
- Brinda orientación básica a equipos de país y proyectos sobre uso de marca, contenidos seguros, calidad de materiales y canales de comunicación.
- Apoya acciones de comunicación interna, emergencias y gestión administrativa del área, en coordinación con la Coordinación de Comunicaciones del Clúster.
- Coordina proveedores, briefs, TDRs y servicios externos de comunicación, diseño, fotografía, video, eventos o pauta digital cuando corresponda

## EXPERIENCIA TECNICA, COMPETENCIAS Y CONOCIMIENTOS

### Formación Académica:

- Título universitario en Comunicaciones, Relaciones Públicas, Periodismo, Marketing, Marketing Digital, Multimedia o campo relacionado.

### Experiencia:

- Mínimo de 5 años de experiencia en comunicación institucional, relaciones públicas, campañas o comunicación digital en organizaciones de sociedad civil en México.
- Experiencia en gestión de redes sociales, creación de contenidos, métricas digitales, cobertura de eventos y coordinación de proveedores.
- Experiencia en storytelling, historias de vida, contenidos audiovisuales y materiales para diferentes audiencias.
- Experiencia en comunicación para programas sociales, derechos de la niñez, igualdad de género, cooperación o sector humanitario será valorada.

### Conocimientos Técnicos y Habilidades:

- Conocimiento de las problemáticas que afectan a niñas, niños y adolescentes en México.
- Estrategias de comunicación externa, relaciones públicas, campañas y posicionamiento institucional.
- Redacción, edición, storytelling y adaptación de mensajes a audiencias y canales diversos.
- Gestión de redes sociales, programación de contenidos, análisis de métricas y pauta digital.
- Diseño gráfico y edición de video con herramientas como Canva, Adobe Creative Suite u otras plataformas similares.
- Fotografía, video, cobertura digital y organización de archivos audiovisuales.
- Políticas de marca, comunicaciones, salvaguarda, consentimiento informado y protección de datos de Plan International.

### Competencias:

- Pensamiento estratégico con capacidad de ejecución práctica.
- Organización, priorización y manejo de múltiples entregables.
- Creatividad, criterio editorial y atención al detalle.
- Comunicación interpersonal y trabajo colaborativo con equipos multiculturales.
- Capacidad para pedir orientación, escalar prioridades y trabajar con acompañamiento técnico del Clúster.
- Compromiso con los derechos de la niñez, igualdad de género, inclusión y rendición de cuentas.

**Ubicación: CDMX**

**Tipo de rol: Personal técnico de comunicaciones**

**Informes a: Coordinación de Comunicaciones Cluster CAMRD**

**Fecha de cierre: 22 de octubre 2026**

La igualdad, la diversidad y la inclusión están en el centro de todo lo que Plan International representa.

Queremos que Plan International refleje la diversidad de las comunidades con las que trabajamos, ofreciendo igualdad de oportunidades a todos sin importar edad, discapacidad, reasignación de género, matrimonio y unión civil, embarazo y maternidad, raza, religión o creencia, sexo u orientación sexual.

Plan International se basa en una cultura de inclusión y nos esforzamos por crear un ambiente de trabajo que garantice que cada equipo, en cada oficina, en cada país, sea rico en personas, pensamientos e ideas diversas.

Fomentamos una cultura organizacional que abraza nuestro compromiso con la justicia racial, la igualdad de género, los derechos de las niñas y la inclusión.

Plan International cree que en un mundo donde los niños enfrentan tantas amenazas de daño, es nuestro deber garantizar que nosotros, como organización, hagamos todo lo posible para mantener a los niños seguros. Esto significa que tenemos responsabilidades particulares hacia los niños con los que entramos en contacto y no debemos contribuir de ninguna manera a dañar o poner a los niños en riesgo.

Se llevarán a cabo una serie de controles previos al empleo de conformidad con la política de Protección de niños y jóvenes de Plan International. Plan International también participa en el Programa de divulgación de mala conducta entre agencias. De acuerdo con este esquema, solicitaremos información a los empleadores anteriores de los solicitantes sobre cualquier hallazgo de explotación sexual, abuso sexual y/o acoso sexual durante el empleo, o incidentes bajo investigación cuando el solicitante dejó el empleo.

Al enviar una solicitud, el solicitante de empleo confirma que comprende estos procedimientos de contratación.

Tenga en cuenta que Plan International nunca enviará correos electrónicos no solicitados solicitando pagos a los candidatos.

jobs.title: Case Coordination Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized. Follow up with any referrals made to other programs.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:**  Case Coordination Supervisor
- **Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

**Work Experience:**

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

**Language Skills:**

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

**Certificates or Licenses:**
