## **Acted**

***Qui sommes-nous***

Acted travaille avec 19 millions de personnes dans 43 pays au carrefour de l’humanitaire, du développement, et des programmes climatiques et environnementaux. Grâce à une connaissance poussée des contextes et l’adoption de technologies émergentes, nous sauvons des vies, allégeons les souffrances, et protégeons et restaurons notre planète. Travaillant avec un écosystème croissant de partenaires locaux, nationaux et internationaux, nous poursuivons un objectif commun : un monde 3Zéro : Zéro Exclusion, Zéro Carbone, Zéro Pauvreté.

***Qui cherchons-nous***

Vous apportez les compétences clefs attendues d’un travailleur humanitaire et de développement, mais également une conscience climatique et environnementale active, et vous pouvez naviguez les défis qui émergent lorsque les souffrances environnementale et humaine se rencontrent. Vous avez l’esprit entrepreneurial : vous décelez les opportunités, connectez les points, adaptez votre approche aux différents environnements, et vous prenez des risques mesurés dans la poursuite de résultats. Vous alliez les principes au pragmatisme, et l’ambition à l’humilité.

## **Acted Haïti**

Présente en Haïti depuis 2004, Acted répond aux urgences et soutien le relèvement des populations dans le besoin, notamment dans les domaines de l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement, de la sécurité alimentaire et de la reconstruction. En collaboration avec la société civile et les institutions, Acted développe et met aussi en œuvre des programmes axés sur le développement socio-économique et l’adaptation au changement climatique. Acted travaille actuellement dans 5 départements en Haïti à savoir la Grand’Anse, le Sud, le Sud-Est, l’Ouest, et le Centre, et prochainement dans les Nippes.

Concernant les réalisations majeures d’Acted en 2020-2021 :

• 5 562 personnes ont reçu une assistance monétaire afin de subvenir à leurs besoins prioritaires  
• 12 centres de santé réhabilités et soutenus afin de répondre à la pandémie de COVID-19  
• 35 réseaux d’eau et infrastructures réhabilités pour améliorer l’accès à l’eau, l’hygiène et l’assainissement  
• 1 125 personnes relogées grâce à la reconstruction de leur maison  
• 394 532 personnes sensibilisées aux mesures de prévention contre la Covid-19

Suite au tremblement de terre du 14 aout 2021 qui a dévasté les départements du Sud, de la Grande Anse et des Nippes en Haïti, Acted recrute. Acted a été une des première organisation humanitaire à mener des évaluations rapides pour déterminer l’ampleur des dégâts et des besoins, et est déjà fortement mobilisée pour apporter une aide d’urgence aux victimes du séisme, en étroite collaboration avec les autorités haïtiennes. Les activités menées actuellement concernent l’acheminement d’eau potable, la distribution de kits d’hygiène et la conduite de travaux d’assainissement et de réhabilitation des réseaux d’eau, mais aussi la distribution de nourriture, le versement d’aides financières d’urgence, la distribution de biens de première nécessité et, prochainement, la mise en place de solutions de logement pour les personnes les plus vulnérables, dans 12 communes des 3 départements.

## **Rôle et responsabilités principales**

Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint soutient le/la Directeur.rice Pays en représentant les intérêts d’Acted dans le pays vis à vis du gouvernement, des bailleurs et autres partenaires clef. Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint.e participe à l’élaboration du profil du Programme en accord avec la stratégie régionale et globale d’Acted . Le/la Directeur.rice Pays Adjoint.e soutient les équipes pour atteindre l’excellence dans le programme et assure les plus hauts niveaux de redevabilité.

***Principales Responsabilités :***

1\. Positionnement et fundraising

- *Analyse du contexte ;*
- *Développement et déploiement de la stratégie ;*
- *Networking, positionnement et représentation générale ;*
- *Relation avec les bailleurs et élaboration de propositions de projets ;*
- *Plaidoyer : (Co-)produire des notes stratégiques, des notes de plaidoyer, communiqués de presse pertinents sur les questions humanitaires et de développement.*
- *Communication : Superviser et assurer la production, dans les délais, d’éléments de communication externe en termes de programming, de méthodes et d’enjeux critiques.*
- *Promotion des organisations sœurs d’ Acted;*

2\. Management et Coordination interne

- *Gestion d’équipe ;*
- *Coordination interne ;*
- *Gestion de crises/conflits ;*
- *Mettre en place et former une équipe de crise au sein du pays ;*

3\. Suivi de la mise en œuvre des projets

- *Mise en œuvre et suivi des projets ;*
- *Grant Management ;*
- *Contrôle qualité des projets ;*
- *Gestion des partenaires ;*

4\. Management FLATS

- *Gestion Financière ;*
- *Gestion Logistique & IT ;*
- *Gestion RH et Administration ;*
- *Suivi des audits externes ;*
- *Gestion Transparence/Conformité ;*
- *Gestion sécurité ;*
- *Suivi de légalisation et d’enregistrement.*

## **Qualifications et compétences requises**

- Etudes supérieures (Master) ;
- Capacités rédactionnelles ;
- Expérience à l’étranger sur des postes de management de 3 ans minimum ;
- La connaissance de la zone est un atout ;
- Très fortes capacités organisationnelles ;
- Expérience en management d’équipes importantes, nationales et internationales ;
- Expérience en management de projets, particulièrement avec une composante institutionnelle ;
- Expérience dans le domaine de la participation communautaire, le lien avec les autorités locales ;
- Compétences en gestion et administration ;
- Flexibilité, adaptation, résistance au stress ;
- Patience et esprit de négociation, excellentes capacités de communication écrite et oral..

## **Conditions**

- Salaire défini par la grille des salaires Acted en fonction du niveau d’études, de l’expertise, du niveau de sécurité et du niveau d’expérience : entre 3100 et 3200€ net mensuel (avant impôts sur le revenu)
- Indemnité mensuelle de frais de vie 300$
- Logement en guesthouse et nourriture pris en charge par Acted
- Sécurité sociale, mutuelle (MSH) et assistance rapatriement (SOS International) pris en charge par Acted
- Transport vers la mission et billet retour totalement pris en charge tous les 6 mois (vers l’adresse spécifiée sur le contrat de travail)
- Frais de visa pris en charge par Acted
- R&R tous les 3 mois (billet d’avion pris en charge jusqu’à 500$ + indemnité supplémentaire de 200$)
- Une semaine de préparation au départ comprenant 4 jours de formation sécurité en immersion
- Possibilité d’avoir un appel de 30minutes avec un.e consultant.e en fiscalité
- Soutien psychologique (rendez-vous avec un.e professionnel.le)
- Ce poste est classé comme un poste international dans la grille de recrutement d’Acted. L’éligibilité à un contrat international est donc requise.

jobs.title: Global Communication Coordinator
jobs.body:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified and enthusiastic Global Communication Coordinator.

**About the job**

You will be working with a diverse and dynamic team at the Mixed Migration Centre (MMC), which is an intrinsic part of DRC. MMC is a leading source for independent and high-quality data, research, analysis and expertise on mixed migration. MMC aims to increase understanding of mixed migration, to positively impact global and regional migration policies, to inform evidence-based protection responses for people on the move and to stimulate forward thinking in public and policy debates on mixed migration. MMC’s overarching focus is on human rights and protection for all people on the move.  
Reporting to the director of MMC, the Global Communication Coordinator leads and oversees the implementation of all MMC activities in relation to internal and external communication and visibility, finalization of MMC publications for release, report launches, organization of events and MMC’s online (social media, website, etc.) presence

  
Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

***Communications strategy***

- Lead the implementation of MMC's external communication strategy across the global team and regional hubs.

***Publications, events, online presence and campaigns***

- Oversee the updating and maintenance of the MMC website.
- Be responsible for all MMC social media output, including the MMC X, LinkedIn and YouTube accounts and channels.
- Oversee the finalisation of all MMC research outputs in line with MMC editorial and brand guidelines, and act as guardian of MMC's global publication calendar.
- Lead the release of all publications, including the Quarterly Mixed Migration Updates, and develop and execute the associated communication plans and toolkits, including social media launches.
- Oversee the release of MMC's regional and global newsletters.
- Lead the implementation of the extensive communication campaign around the annual Mixed Migration Review (MMR).
- Prepare and deliver virtual and in-person events (registrations, social media promotion, hosting of online conference platforms, etc.).

***External engagement and identification of opportunities***

- Work closely with MMC regional hub staff to proactively identify and develop new communication tools, such as podcasts, videos on key research findings and human-interest stories.
- Track events calendars, and signal and organise speaking opportunities for MMC.
- Draft press releases, maintain an up-to-date list of MMC media contacts and strengthen media outreach.
- Engage with global and regional partners to disseminate MMC research products.
- Liaise with DRC Communication and Press offices at HQ (Copenhagen), Geneva, Brussels and in the regions.

***Coordination, reporting and management***

- Report on MMC's external visibility (e.g. monthly and annual website and social media statistics, event attendance and post-event surveys, external references to MMC) as input into MMC's Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning.
- Manage the work of MMC's communication officers/specialists (currently two).

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to be able to take the lead on your tasks and be able to oversee all internal and external communication and visibility activities across the global MMC network. Attention to detail while capable of keeping the big picture in sight is key in this role. Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- 5+ years of professional experience in external communication, ideally in the NGO, UN, research or humanitarian/development sector.
- Proven experience planning and running social media campaigns and managing social media output.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an excellent eye for detail.
- Strong organisational and multitasking skills, and flexibility to manage many tasks of varying size at the same time.
- Full proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint); proficiency in WordPress, InDesign and Canva.
- Ability to develop data visualisations using different visualisation software.
- Ability to work effectively with a team based remotely across several countries.
- University degree within relevant field of study

*Desirable*

- Strong affinity with matters relating to (mixed) migration, forced displacement and humanitarian/development work.
- Previous work with NGOs or UN in the development or humanitarian sector
- Fluency in French and/or Spanish
- Academic background in migration studies, including some experience in research (field-level research is a strong asset)

All employees are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Work location: Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station

Start date: 1st December 2026

End date: 31 June 2027

The position is temporary as it is currently funded until the end of June, but likely to be extended, upon donor funding confirmation.

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC The position is at “fuldmægtig” level. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply.

Please note that you need to have the right to work in Denmark (through nationality or existing work visa) in order to be considered for this role.

**Further information**

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Gretel Ana Martin Araya by email gretel.araya@mixedmigration.org. We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website [drc.ngo](https://reliefweb.int/javascript:void(0)).

*Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.*

jobs.title: Senior Advisor - Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Senior Advisor - Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI)**, you will provide strategic and technical leadership to advance gender equality, disability inclusion, and social inclusion across the East Asia region. You will develop and deliver a regional GEDSI roadmap, strengthen organizational practices and staff and partner capabilities, embed GEDSI across strategy, programme and proposal design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning, and position World Vision with donors, governments, UN agencies, civil society, and representative organizations.

**Core Areas of Focus**

You will develop and execute an East Asia regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organizational policies and child well-being priorities. You will lead GEDSI mainstreaming and quality assurance across regional and national office programming, grants, and organizational systems. You will strengthen the capabilities of GEDSI focal points, technical teams, leaders, partners, and representative organizations. You will generate evidence, learning, and innovation and strengthen World Vision’s external positioning on GEDSI across development, humanitarian, and fragile contexts. You will also manage and coordinate GEDSI-related consultancies, technical assistance engagements, and partnerships, including developing scopes of work, providing procurement inputs, ensuring quality assurance, overseeing delivery, and disseminating outputs aligned with global and regional priorities and standards.

**Lead regional GEDSI strategy, policy implementation and organizational change.**

You will develop and monitor a regional GEDSI strategy and roadmap aligned with organizational priorities and policies. You will engage regional and national leadership, People & Culture, operations, programmes, grants, advocacy, and communications teams to embed GEDSI in programming, organizational practices, advocacy, external engagement, and communications in accordance with World Vision’s GEDSI Policy. You will guide organizational GEDSI self-assessments and action plans, promote inclusive language, accessible workplaces, non-discrimination, and reasonable accommodation, and ensure GEDSI is reflected in organizational priorities, programme strategies and design, key messages, and resource allocation.

**Lead GEDSI mainstreaming in programs, implementation and proposals across funding streams.**

You will provide technical leadership for GEDSI-responsive and transformative programme and proposal design across sectors and contexts. You will ensure designs are informed by GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, barriers, disparities, harmful norms, root causes, and intersectional risks. You will advise teams on GEDSI objectives, theories of change, indicators, budgets, risk mitigation, Do No Harm, safeguarding, and donor requirements. You will contextualize and promote GEDSI tools, approaches, minimum standards, domains of change, the continuum, and markers. You will strengthen the identification and use of disaggregated data, including the appropriate use of Washington Group Questions or other approved tools, to inform programme and project design. You will coach teams to monitor emerging barriers and adapt implementation to improve equitable access, participation, decision-making, systems, and well-being. You will promote rights-based and social-model approaches that address attitudinal, environmental, communication, and institutional barriers. You will also develop, manage, and monitor the Disability Consultant’s workplan and project deliverables, communicate progress, and ensure alignment with EAS GEDSI priorities and agreed objectives.

**Build GEDSI capability, networks and communities of practice.**

You will assess competency and capacity gaps and develop regional capacity-strengthening plans for staff, focal points, partners, and leaders. You will deliver and coordinate contextualized training, coaching, mentoring, and peer learning on gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, and related frameworks. You will equip GEDSI focal points and technical teams with tools, models, resources, and quality-assurance support. You will also strengthen regional collaboration networks and communities of practice, including linkages with gender equality and disability inclusion leadership networks.

**Lead evidence, learning, innovation and knowledge management.**

You will develop and implement a regional GEDSI learning agenda linked to child well-being outcomes. You will initiate and oversee research, pilots, and testing of new or adapted GEDSI approaches and programming models. You will support the analysis and use of data, evaluations, learning reviews, impact stories, case studies, and promising practices. You will facilitate knowledge sharing across national offices, the wider World Vision Partnership, and external audiences.

**Build strategic partnerships, external positioning and thought leadership.**

You will represent and position World Vision with governments, donors, UN agencies, clusters, working groups, NGOs, faith actors, academia, and regional networks. You will build or strengthen the capacity to establish strategic and equitable partnerships with women-led organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities, and minority groups as part of social inclusion, including children, to ensure their meaningful participation in assessment, design, implementation, monitoring, learning, and advocacy. You will identify opportunities for shared learning, advocacy, policy influence, resource mobilization, and thought leadership. You will also support communications and external engagement colleagues in using inclusive, rights-based, and evidence-informed GEDSI language and narratives.

**Requirements include:**

- A bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience may be considered.
- Master’s degree or equivalent in gender studies, disability studies, social or political sciences, social work, international development, economics, public policy, programme management or a related field highly preferred
- Relevant professional development in gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, safeguarding, programme design, MEAL or humanitarian programming.
- Minimum 5 years of demonstrated experience providing strategic and technical leadership on gender equality, disability inclusion and social inclusion in international development and/or humanitarian programming.
- Experience supporting GEDSI-responsive and transformative designs, mainstreaming strategies and activities across multiple sectors and funding streams.
- Experience leading GEDSI analysis, including gender and disability analysis, and integrating findings into design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and learning.
- Strong facilitation, coaching, relationship-building, partnership, influencing, writing and presentation skills.
- Experience working in or across the East Asia region and adapting global approaches to diverse national and local contexts.
- Substantial experience in disability-inclusive programming, accessibility, disability-disaggregated data, partnership with organisations of persons with disabilities, and rights-based approaches.
- Experience in organisational change, policy implementation, advocacy, research, knowledge management, external engagement and donor positioning.
- Experience leading or supporting organisational GEDSI self-assessments, audits or action plans and building the capability of staff and partners.
- Experience applying Do No Harm, safeguarding and ethical approaches to gender-based violence and other GEDSI-related risks.

**Required Language(s):**

- English, both written and verbal

**Required travel and/or work environment accommodations:**

- The position requires approximately 20% travel, subject to field office needs.
- The successful candidate will be based in their home country and will work remotely, with travel to field locations, regional offices, and partner meetings as required.

jobs.title: Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)
jobs.body:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, proudly supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are renowned for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME) Division** is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the 165 plus staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)** will support the Coastal Fisheries Science Team with providing advice to governments, stakeholders and the private sector in planning and implementing coastal fisheries science activities, focusing on coastal finfish and/or invertebrate resources and their supporting habitats.

**The key responsibilities of the role include the following:**

**Assist the CFAP Science team in providing support and training to PICT members to enhance science capacity and capability in coastal living resources data collection, entry, quality control, analysis, interpretation and reporting in support of sustainable management.**

- Assists in the development of coastal fisheries survey (independent and dependent) training materials for countries through needs-based stakeholder consultations, taking into account gender, culture and human rights in the country or territory.
- Assists in the training of local staff in-country and/or online in all areas of data collection, data management, analysis and reporting for coastal fisheries and associated habitats.
- Ensure there are no gender or social inclusion barriers to training activities.

**Contribute to the design and implementation of assessments of coastal living resources, the development and application of innovative tools and approaches for data collection, data management and reporting to inform coastal fisheries management.**

- Participates in the design of surveys based on standardised methodologies and lessons learned.
- Assists in the promotion of the standardisation of data collection and assists with the expansion of standardised data collection and/or monitoring systems for coastal fisheries (finfish, invertebrates, habitat and catch and effort) and programmes at the national level
- Assists in the development and implementation of data systems, tools and approaches that will improve data collection and monitoring of coastal fisheries at the national and regional levels.
- Assists in the collection of biological samples to help inform coastal fisheries assessments.
- Support PICTs to analyse available scientific data on coastal finfish and invertebrate fisheries and associated habitats to provide updates on the status of coastal fishery resources.

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration with partners in coastal fisheries and aquaculture science in support of evidence-based management**

- Liaises, encourages collaboration and works with national, regional and international organisations, research institutes and NGOs on coastal finfish and invertebrate fishery issues.
- Assists in collaboration with other sections/programmes/Divisions within SPC on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.

**Contribute to Section administration and communication**

- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures including training data for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, Programme reports to RTMCFA and HoF.
- Contributes to peer-reviewed scientific publications that highlight results and/or developments of international interest.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Pacific Islands**

- Only applicants from Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply.
- Applicants must be employed in a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment department or a recognised NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Qualifications**

- A recognised degree in a discipline relevant to coastal fisheries science (finfish and/or invertebrates), or related field or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least two years’ direct relevant experience in PICT coastal fisheries, particularly applied field research for coastal finfish and/or invertebrates
- Demonstrated experience in undertaking surveys for coastal finfish and/or invertebrates using a range of methodologies
- Understanding of current Pacific Island regional coastal fisheries management and science issues, and experience of working with gender issues relating to fisheries
- Strong PC based computer skills (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook) with knowledge of software programmes for data entry and analysis

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written) in English

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in a team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and communicate with people from various ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries, sometimes under difficult physical conditions.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Requirements:** Only applicants who are nationals and residents of Pacific Island countries are eligible to apply. Applicants must be employed in or contracted by a Pacific Island fisheries or conservation / environment agency, or a recognized NGO working in the field of fisheries science, management or monitoring in a Pacific Island country.

**Letter of endorsement –** A signed letter from the employer, stating they agree to release the applicant for the attachment and that the position will be held for the applicant to return to at the end of the attachment with SPC must be provided before an appointment can be finalized.

**Contract duration –** This appointment will last for a duration of 364 days and will not be renewable.

**Remuneration –** The **Pacific Island Fisheries Professional (Coastal Fisheries Science)** is a Band 8 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a salary of SDR (special drawing rights) 3,038 per month, which currently converts to approximately XPF 438,381 (USD 4,071; EUR 3,674). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea –** SPC provides housing support in Noumea and an establishment grant, return airfare, and will reimburse excess accompanied luggage of up to two additional bags. Employees are entitled to: 25 days annual leave and 30 days sick leave per annum; medical and life insurance; and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

We encourage all eligible candidates to apply but please note that as this is a special short-term contract, the full list of benefits included in other international contract types are not available. Appointees may bring their families, but all extra costs for travel, insurance, education, housing and other additional expenses will be their own responsibility.

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Finance and Support Services Director
jobs.body:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Finance and Support Services Director**, you will provide overall leadership, oversight, and management support for all aspects of financial management in the Field Office (FO).

You will serve as a strategic partner and member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) of WV Mauritania, focusing on accountability, stewardship, planning and budgeting, accurate financial data and analysis, and financial advice. You will develop a financial strategy that supports the Field Office’s strategic and programme objectives. You will also strengthen finance staff capacity, develop and implement effective internal controls and risk management practices, and ensure the proper utilization and safeguarding of assets in accordance with World Vision-approved policies and procedures.

**(a) Leadership, Capacity Development, and Strategic Partnering**

You will provide strong and positive leadership to the Finance Department, ensuring competent and motivated staff are recruited and retained to deliver efficient services. You will coordinate the professional and personal development of Finance, ICT, Fleet, and Administration staff through orientation, on-the-job coaching, training, and succession planning. You will model Christ-centred servant leadership and support your team’s spiritual development. You will actively participate in Field Office Senior Leadership Team meetings and strategic regional meetings, help the National Director (ND), Operations, and other non-finance staff understand financial statements, and ensure relevant stakeholders understand partnership finance policies and procedures. You will strengthen collaboration and communication between the Field Office and Regional Office, develop internal and external networks, promote shared resources across the region and partnership, and adhere to WVI’s mission, core values, and Covenant of Partnership.

**(b) Stewardship**

You will ensure that appropriate cost-efficiency and effectiveness measures are implemented and followed. You will provide cost analyses, promote benchmarking, and make recommendations to improve resource utilization at all levels. In collaboration with the Supply Chain team, you will contribute to developing appropriate policies and procedures for procuring goods and services.

**(c) Financial Planning and Budgeting**

In collaboration with the Regional Finance Director, you will advise the National Director on strategic resource acquisition and allocation in line with Partnership Resource Allocation Committee (PRAC) guidelines. You will coordinate planning and budgeting processes, provide technical support to ensure compliance with global and regional guidelines, and develop and implement financial strategies in response to changing constraints and circumstances. You will review budget alignment across the Field Office, projects, grants, MyPBAS, and Support Offices, ensuring effective cost recovery practices. In collaboration with the Integrated Programs Director (IPD), you will monitor and manage the WV Mauritania budget, cash flow, and project funding, providing timely and relevant information to budget managers. You will closely monitor budgets and expenditures at Area Development Program (ADP), Cluster, and Field Office levels to ensure funds are used for their intended purposes, including monitoring field expenses. You will also contribute to developing WV Mauritania’s strategic direction and priorities.

**(d) Fiscal Accounting, Compliance, Monitoring, and Reporting**

You will design and manage systems, policies, and procedures that provide appropriate security and control over WV assets, resources, and operations. You will establish effective internal controls and ensure timely, accurate, and complete reporting to the partnership and internal stakeholders. You will comply with partnership policies, procedures, and guidelines outlined in the WVI Financial Manual and related documents, including grant compliance, planning and budgeting, year-end closing, carryforward, accounting, and reporting. You will coordinate the timely and accurate submission of financial reports through the Field Financial Reporting database on SharePoint, review monthly MyPBAS-to-FFR reconciliations, and develop action plans to address outstanding items. You will provide monthly analyses of ADP and grant financial reports, giving timely feedback to ADP and grant managers to support decision-making. You will also ensure that Finance, ICT, Fleet, and Administration staff visit programmes and projects to monitor accountability, follow up on audit findings, and provide necessary support.

**(e) Financial Risk Management and Controls**

You will manage appropriate financial systems and controls to minimize significant finance audit risks at both Field Office and project levels. You will coordinate management responses to financial audits, ensure timely submission to the Audit Department, and oversee the timely implementation of audit recommendations. You will coordinate adequate preparation for Global Centre (GC) and external audits, manage financial risks and integrity, and implement anti-corruption and fraud prevention strategies.

**(f) Support to Supply Chain Processes**

You will coordinate and maintain an effective interface between the Supply Chain and Finance teams. You will review Purchase Requests and Purchase Orders to ensure compliance with Supply Chain Management (SCM) policies, budget availability, and appropriate controls against fraudulent activities. You will also review procurement activities to ensure purchases contribute to ministry objectives and align with donor budget line items.

**(g) Improve ICT Infrastructure and Provide Quality Service**

You will ensure improved connectivity across the office and programmes and facilitate the development and implementation of computer usage policies. You will oversee ICT security and integrity, ensuring office disaster preparedness measures and policies are regularly updated to address new technologies, trends, and threats.

**(h) Administration and Fleet Management**

You will ensure that WV staff and assets remain secure, safe, and well-maintained, while overseeing logistics coordination and providing quality hospitality services to staff and visitors. You will implement fleet management policies covering vehicle tracking, fuel management, and vehicle and motorcycle maintenance. You will also manage asset disposals in compliance with WVI and WV Mauritania policies.

**(i) Talent Management and Capacity Building**

You will contribute to capacity assessment, development, and implementation as part of the overall Talent Management Plan, ensuring an integrated WV Mauritania capacity-building plan informed by finance priorities and strategy. You will identify Finance staff development needs, including grant financial management, and facilitate relevant training opportunities while developing diverse leadership. In collaboration with the People and Culture (P&C) Team Leader, you will co-lead the recruitment of Field Office Finance staff. You will advise and support the induction of new functional directors, grant managers, and project team leaders. You will also coach, advise, and mentor Finance staff to identify their strengths and development gaps and address them effectively.

**Requirements include:**

- Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or Economics or a related field
- Minimum 5 years of experience in a finance position with a medium business/medium NGO/government agency
- Minimum 3 years of experience in a senior finance management position
- Experience with financial planning and forecasting
- Solid knowledge of accounting principles, financial systems, budget/cash flow monitoring, and internal accounting controls.
- Highly flexible and agile in style, with the ability to produce creative and pragmatic solutions to complex problems.
- Good working knowledge of computerized accounting systems, preferably Sun Systems & ProVision.
- Demonstrates systems thinking and is a high champion and Manages Innovation.
- Able to work in a cross-cultural environment with a multi-national staff.
- Ability to travel within the country, regionally, and internationally.
- French is non-negotiable (both written and spoken)
- Proficiency in written and spoken English
- Excellent oral/written and interpersonal skills

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted

**Job Overview:**   
The Caseworker provides trauma-informed, client-centered services to recently arrived refugees and other qualified immigrants to meet immediate needs and support progress toward self-sufficiency.
