jobs.title: Venezuela - Gerente de Socios y Subvenciones (Nacional)
jobs.body:
## Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela y, a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos financiados por distintos donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro, Bolívar y otros estados del país, en los sectores de protección, salud, WASH, ambiente, seguridad alimentaria, fortalecimiento institucional y respuesta a emergencias.

En el marco del crecimiento y diversificación de su portafolio, COOPI Venezuela busca reforzar la gestión de subvenciones y alianzas mediante una función especializada que asegure el seguimiento contractual, la calidad y oportunidad de los procesos de reporting y formulación, y una coordinación eficaz con socios de los consorcios actuales y donantes.

## Objetivo/descripción del puesto

Bajo la supervisión de la Coordinación País y con acompañamiento funcional de la Coordinación de Programas, el/la Gerente de Socios y Subvenciones será responsable de asegurar la gestión coordinada del portafolio de subvenciones y alianzas de COOPI Venezuela, garantizando el seguimiento oportuno de obligaciones contractuales, propuestas, modificaciones, reporting y procesos de coordinación con socios.

El puesto actuará como punto focal para la planificación y seguimiento de los principales procesos de gestión de subvenciones, facilitando la coordinación entre Programas, Operaciones, Administración, MEAL, Jefes/as de Proyecto, socios, Coordinación Regional y Sede.

Asimismo, apoyará en la coordinación institucional y contractual del Consorcio ÍNTEGRAS y de futuras alianzas o consorcios en los que COOPI ejerza funciones de liderazgo, adaptando el nivel de coordinación a la complejidad y características de cada alianza.

La posición se coordinará estrechamente con Programas, los equipos de proyecto y Administración País, articulando sus respectivos aportes para asegurar una gestión coherente, oportuna y alineada con los compromisos asumidos con donantes y socios.

**Áreas de responsabilidad**

**Gestión del portafolio de subvenciones:**

- Mantener actualizado un calendario consolidado de obligaciones contractuales, reportes, modificaciones, auditorías, entregables y principales hitos de todos los proyectos de la misión.
- Dar seguimiento a los plazos y responsabilidades asociados a cada subvención, alertando con suficiente anticipación sobre entregables y riesgos de incumplimiento.
- Asegurar la adecuada circulación de información entre Jefes/as de Proyecto, Programas, Operaciones, Administración, MEAL, Coordinación País, Región y Sede.
- Mantener organizados y accesibles los principales documentos contractuales, versiones aprobadas, modificaciones, comunicaciones con donantes y documentación relevante para la gestión de cada subvención.
- Apoyar la interpretación y difusión interna de requisitos contractuales y lineamientos de los donantes.
- Identificar oportunamente riesgos de cumplimiento, reporting o gestión contractual y escalarlos a las funciones responsables.

**Reporting y seguimiento contractual:**

- Coordinar el calendario y proceso de preparación de informes narrativos intermedios y finales.
- Solicitar y consolidar los aportes de Jefes/as de Proyecto, equipos técnicos, MEAL, Administración y socios.
- Revisar la coherencia, integridad y consistencia de los informes antes de su validación por Programas y Coordinación País.
- Asegurar la coherencia entre información narrativa, indicadores, ejecución operativa y datos financieros, en coordinación con las áreas responsables.
- Dar seguimiento a comentarios y solicitudes de aclaración de donantes hasta su cierre.
- Mantener control de versiones y trazabilidad de los principales documentos enviados y aprobados.
- Coordinar la revisión y consolidación de informes y otros entregables, articulando la validación técnica con Programas y los equipos técnicos, y la validación financiera con Administración País.

**Formulación y modificaciones de proyectos:**

- Coordinar, en estrecha articulación con Coordinación País y Programas, los procesos de preparación de nuevas propuestas, notas conceptuales y expresiones de interés.
- Establecer cronogramas de formulación, distribuir responsabilidades y asegurar la entrega oportuna de los distintos componentes.
- Consolidar los aportes de Programas, MEAL, Administración, Operaciones, equipos de proyecto y socios.
- Asegurar la coherencia entre narrativa, marco lógico, indicadores, cronograma, plan operativo y presupuesto.
- Coordinar los procesos de modificación contractual, extensiones, realineamientos, adendas y reprogramaciones.
- Preparar o consolidar las justificaciones y documentación requerida por donantes.
- Mantener actualizada la información sobre oportunidades de financiación y apoyar a Coordinación País y Programas en la planificación del pipeline de propuestas.
- Apoyar la formulación de nuevas propuestas a partir de las prioridades estratégicas y orientaciones técnicas definidas por Coordinación País y Programas, asegurando su adecuada traducción en los documentos de proyecto.
    
    **Gestión de socios y alianzas:**
- Mantener una visión consolidada de los socios institucionales, co-solicitantes, co-partners y organizaciones implementadoras vinculadas a los proyectos de COOPI.
- Facilitar la coordinación contractual y documental con socios durante formulación, implementación, reporting y cierre.
- Dar seguimiento a acuerdos de partnership, calendarios de reporting y otras obligaciones de los socios, en coordinación con Administración y los responsables de proyecto.
- Facilitar procesos de due diligence, documentación institucional y seguimiento de capacidades cuando corresponda.
- Identificar dificultades recurrentes en la gestión de alianzas y proponer medidas de mejora.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento de herramientas y procedimientos internos de COOPI para la gestión de socios.
- Coordinar con los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto el seguimiento de los socios implementadores en los aspectos contractuales, documentales y de reporting, articulando los requerimientos del grant con la gestión operativa del proyecto.

**Apoyo a consorcios y alianzas:**

- Apoyar la gestión de consorcios y alianzas en los aspectos vinculados a grants, reporting, propuestas, modificaciones y obligaciones contractuales.
- Facilitar la consolidación de aportes de socios y equipos internos para propuestas, informes y otros entregables conjuntos.
- Dar seguimiento a compromisos, plazos y requerimientos documentales vinculados a subvenciones gestionadas en consorcio.
- Apoyar, junto con Coordinación País y Programas, los procesos de formulación y gestión contractual con donantes y socios.

**Coordinación interna y calidad de la gestión de subvenciones:**

- Trabajar estrechamente con Programas para asegurar la coherencia técnica y programática de propuestas, modificaciones e informes.
- Coordinar con Operaciones y los equipos de proyecto el seguimiento de avances, hitos y riesgos de implementación relevantes para las obligaciones contractuales.
- Coordinar con Administración la preparación de presupuestos, modificaciones financieras, informes y seguimiento de requisitos administrativos.
- Coordinar con MEAL la disponibilidad y consistencia de indicadores, medios de verificación y resultados reportados.
- Promover herramientas comunes para calendarios, reporting, seguimiento contractual y archivo.
- Facilitar reuniones de lanzamiento, revisión y cierre de subvenciones cuando resulte necesario.
- Contribuir a identificar aprendizajes y mejoras en los procesos de gestión de subvenciones de la misión.

**Relación con donantes y representación:**

- Mantener, por delegación de la Coordinación País, comunicación operativa con donantes sobre reporting, modificaciones, aclaraciones y procesos contractuales.
- Apoyar en la preparación de reuniones, revisiones y visitas de donantes asegurando la disponibilidad y coherencia de la información requerida.
- Apoyar a Coordinación País y Programas en reuniones de seguimiento, negociación y diseño de nuevas intervenciones.
- Representar a COOPI en espacios relacionados con gestión de subvenciones y partnerships cuando sea requerido.

**Actividades complementarias:**

- Promover el cumplimiento de las políticas, procedimientos y Código Ético de COOPI.
- Contribuir a un ambiente de trabajo colaborativo y a una comunicación fluida entre departamentos.
- Apoyar el fortalecimiento de capacidades de equipos y socios en gestión de subvenciones, reporting y requisitos de donantes.
- Ejecutar aquellas tareas inherentes al puesto y que sean solicitadas por la Coordinación País, según contexto y necesidades de la intervención.

## Perfil deseado

Profesional con experiencia sólida en gestión de subvenciones, formulación de propuestas, reporting y gestión de alianzas en organizaciones humanitarias o de cooperación internacional. Se busca un perfil altamente organizado, con capacidad para manejar simultáneamente distintos donantes, proyectos y plazos, coordinar aportes de múltiples departamentos y socios y producir documentos de elevada calidad.

### ESENCIALES

- Título universitario en Cooperación Internacional, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Economía, Derecho o áreas relacionadas.
- Al menos 5 años de experiencia relevante en cooperación internacional o acción humanitaria, incluyendo experiencia demostrable en gestión de subvenciones con donantes institucionales.
- Experiencia en formulación de propuestas, notas conceptuales, marcos lógicos, modificaciones contractuales y preparación/consolidación de informes narrativos.
- Conocimiento de procedimientos y requisitos de donantes institucionales, particularmente Unión Europea/ECHO y/o agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Experiencia en trabajo con consorcios, alianzas y socios implementadores, incluyendo seguimiento de compromisos, reporting y coordinación documental.
- Capacidad para coordinar procesos complejos con múltiples actores, áreas y plazos simultáneos, asegurando coherencia entre componentes programáticos, operativos y financieros.
- Excelentes capacidades de redacción, análisis, síntesis y atención al detalle, manteniendo al mismo tiempo una visión global de los procesos.
- Alta capacidad de organización, planificación y priorización, con orientación a resultados y cumplimiento de plazos.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, trabajo en equipo y coordinación transversal, con capacidad para facilitar acuerdos y mantener relaciones de trabajo constructivas con equipos internos, socios y donantes.
- Empatía, escucha activa, flexibilidad y adaptabilidad, especialmente en contextos de trabajo exigentes y con prioridades cambiantes.
- Autonomía, proactividad y capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y gestionar varios procesos concurrentes manteniendo rigor y calidad.
- Dominio del español e inglés oral y escrito.
- Buen manejo de herramientas de Microsoft Office.
- Compromiso con los principios, Código Ético y políticas institucionales de COOPI.
- Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

### DESEABLES

- Experiencia con AICS, Unión Europea/INTPA, OIM, UNICEF u otras agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Experiencia en due diligence y gestión de acuerdos con socios locales.
- Experiencia previa con COOPI.

jobs.title: Venezuela - Coordinador/a de Operaciones (National)
jobs.body:
## Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela y, a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos con diferentes donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro y Bolívar, en protección, salud sexual y reproductiva, WASH (agua, saneamiento e higiene), alimentación escolar, ambiente y fortalecimiento institucional.

Tras los sismos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026, COOPI en Venezuela ha ampliado adicionalmente su cartera de intervenciones mediante proyectos de respuesta a la emergencia.

## Objetivo/descripción del puesto

Bajo la supervisión directa de la Coordinación País, el/la Coordinador/a de Operaciones será responsable de supervisar y acompañar la implementación operativa del portafolio de proyectos de COOPI en Venezuela, asegurando el cumplimiento de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, presupuestos y compromisos operativos.

Acompañará a los/las Jefes/as o Gerentes de Proyecto en la gestión de sus proyectos, facilitando el seguimiento de la ejecución, el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades y la resolución oportuna de bloqueos y desviaciones.

Trabajará en estrecha coordinación con Programas, Administración, Logística, MEAL, RRHH, Coordinaciones de Base y otras funciones de la misión, respetando los ámbitos de responsabilidad técnica y funcional de cada departamento.

La función estará principalmente orientada a la gestión y ejecución de proyectos, sin sustituir las responsabilidades de las Coordinaciones de Base en la gestión territorial de las oficinas y servicios de soporte, ni las responsabilidades técnicas y programáticas de la Coordinación de Programas.

El puesto buscará reforzar la autonomía y capacidad de gestión de los/las responsables de proyecto, proporcionando acompañamiento y soporte proporcional a las necesidades y experiencia de cada perfil. Se priorizarán perfiles nacionales.

**Áreas de responsabilidad**

**1. Supervisión de la implementación de proyectos**

- Acompañar y dar seguimiento a los/las Jefes/as y Gerentes de Proyecto en la definición de prioridades, objetivos y mecanismos periódicos de seguimiento.
- Asegurar que cada proyecto disponga de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, herramientas de seguimiento y responsabilidades claramente definidas y actualizadas.
- Dar seguimiento sistemático al avance de actividades, productos, resultados y principales hitos contractuales, identificando oportunamente retrasos, desviaciones y riesgos de implementación.
- Trabajar con los/las responsables de proyecto en la definición y seguimiento de medidas correctivas cuando existan retrasos o dificultades de ejecución.
- Promover una gestión proactiva de los proyectos, apoyando a los PM en la identificación de alternativas y soluciones ante bloqueos operativos.
- Asegurar el seguimiento y cierre oportuno de decisiones, procesos y acciones pendientes relacionados con la ejecución de los proyectos.
- Realizar visitas regulares a las áreas de intervención y reuniones de seguimiento con los equipos de proyecto y de base.
- Informar regularmente a la Coordinación País sobre avances, riesgos, necesidades de decisión y situaciones que puedan comprometer la ejecución de los proyectos.

**2. Gestión y desarrollo de los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto**

- Acompañar a los/las Jefes/as y Gerentes de Proyecto en la planificación, organización y priorización de su trabajo y en la gestión de los equipos bajo su responsabilidad.
- Fortalecer capacidades y desempeños en gestión del ciclo de proyecto, planificación, seguimiento financiero, gestión de equipos, anticipación de riesgos y resolución de problemas.
- Realizar reuniones individuales y colectivas de seguimiento y proporcionar retroalimentación periódica sobre desempeño y prioridades.
- Participar, junto con RRHH y la Coordinación País, en los procesos de selección, inducción, evaluación y desarrollo de los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto.
- Identificar necesidades de formación y acompañamiento, particularmente para perfiles nuevos o junior.
- Favorecer una cultura de responsabilidad, iniciativa, cumplimiento de compromisos y colaboración entre proyectos y departamentos.

**3. Seguimiento financiero y planificación operativa de los proyectos**

- Asegurar, en coordinación con Administración País y sin sustituir sus responsabilidades de control financiero y administrativo, el seguimiento periódico de la situación financiera de sus proyectos.
- Revisar con los PM el presupuesto, burn rate, previsiones y proyecciones de gasto, verificando su coherencia con los planes de actividades y cronogramas.
- Identificar tempranamente desviaciones entre ejecución programada y ejecución financiera y asegurar la preparación de medidas correctivas.
- Asegurar que las proyecciones financieras y necesidades operativas de los proyectos sean preparadas con suficiente anticipación y compartidas con Administración.
- Facilitar la coordinación entre PM y Administración cuando existan bloqueos o decisiones que puedan afectar la ejecución presupuestaria.
- Dar seguimiento, desde la perspectiva de ejecución del proyecto, a modificaciones presupuestarias, realineamientos y otras necesidades identificadas durante la implementación.
- La validación contable, financiera y de elegibilidad de los gastos seguirá correspondiendo a Administración.

**4. Seguimiento de procurement y logística de proyecto**

- Asegurar, en coordinación con Logística País, Administracion y las Coordinaciones de Base, que cada proyecto disponga de un plan de compras y adquisiciones actualizado y coherente con su plan de trabajo y cronograma.
- Asegurar que los PM y equipos de proyecto anticipen adecuadamente las necesidades de bienes, servicios, transporte y demás recursos necesarios para la ejecución.
- Dar seguimiento al estado de los principales procesos de compra y contratación vinculados a proyectos, identificando tempranamente posibles retrasos que puedan afectar actividades o resultados.
- Facilitar la coordinación entre PM, Logística y Base cuando existan bloqueos operativos.
- Asegurar que los PM integren adecuadamente los tiempos de los procedimientos logísticos y administrativos en su planificación.
- Dar seguimiento a la disponibilidad y utilización de recursos de proyecto desde la perspectiva de su impacto sobre la implementación.
- La gestión de proveedores, procedimientos de adquisición, flota, almacenes, activos y demás funciones logísticas institucionales seguirá siendo responsabilidad de Logística País y, en su ámbito territorial, de las estructuras correspondientes de Base.

**5. Coordinación de la ejecución y relación con otros departamentos**

- Actuar como principal punto de articulación entre los PM y las diferentes funciones de coordinación cuando existan necesidades o bloqueos relacionados con la ejecución.
- Mantener una coordinación sistemática con Programas sobre aspectos técnicos, calidad programática, indicadores, MEAL y modificaciones que puedan afectar el diseño de las intervenciones.
- Coordinar con Administración los aspectos financieros y contractuales vinculados a la ejecución.
- Coordinar con Logística los procesos operativos necesarios para la implementación.
- Coordinar con RRHH sobre necesidades de personal, desempeño y gestión de equipos de proyecto.
- Mantener una coordinación regular con las Coordinaciones de Base para asegurar la adecuada articulación entre la gestión del proyecto y las condiciones operativas de cada territorio.
- Favorecer una comunicación clara sobre responsabilidades, decisiones y plazos entre proyectos, departamentos y bases.
- La Coordinación de Operaciones no ejercerá supervisión jerárquica sobre las Coordinaciones de Base ni sobre los departamentos de soporte, salvo delegación temporal y expresa de la Coordinación País.

**6. Seguimiento de reporting y compromisos de proyecto**

- Asegurar que los PM mantengan actualizado el calendario de principales entregables, hitos contractuales y obligaciones de sus proyectos.
- Dar seguimiento a la preparación oportuna de los insumos técnicos, operativos y financieros requeridos para informes internos, informes a donantes, modificaciones y otros procesos contractuales.
- Asegurar que los PM proporcionen información completa y dentro de los plazos establecidos a las funciones responsables de consolidación y revisión de informes.
- Alertar oportunamente sobre retrasos o dificultades que puedan comprometer entregables contractuales.
- La revisión técnica, consolidación programática y gestión especializada de grants se realizará en coordinación con las funciones responsables de Programas/Grants.

**7. Gestión de riesgos y resolución de bloqueos**

- Identificar, junto con los PM, riesgos operativos, financieros, contractuales, de recursos humanos o de implementación que puedan afectar los proyectos.
- Asegurar que se definan medidas de mitigación, responsables y plazos para los principales riesgos identificados.
- Facilitar la resolución de bloqueos entre proyectos, bases y departamentos y escalar a la Coordinación País aquellos que requieran decisiones de nivel superior.
- Mantener una visión consolidada de los principales riesgos y necesidades operativas del portafolio de proyectos.
- Contribuir al aprendizaje institucional identificando problemas recurrentes, cuellos de botella y oportunidades de mejora de los procesos internos.
- Los riesgos técnicos serán abordados con Programas; los financieros con Administración; los logísticos con Logística; y los relativos a seguridad de acuerdo con la estructura y responsabilidades establecidas por la misión.

**8. Apoyo temporal a proyectos, bases y nuevas intervenciones**

- Por solicitud expresa de la Coordinación País, proporcionar refuerzo operativo temporal durante el lanzamiento de nuevos proyectos, transiciones, fases críticas o períodos de alta carga de trabajo.
- Asumir temporalmente funciones de gestión de proyecto cuando exista una vacante de PM, hasta la incorporación de la persona responsable.
- Apoyar excepcionalmente una Base cuando exista una vacante o necesidad temporal de refuerzo de coordinación, con un mandato y período previamente definidos.
- Apoyar la puesta en marcha de nuevas operaciones y facilitar su posterior transferencia al responsable correspondiente.
- Contribuir a respuestas de emergencia o incrementos rápidos de operaciones cuando la misión requiera capacidad adicional de gestión.
- Estas funciones tendrán carácter temporal y no modificarán las responsabilidades permanentes de las estructuras de Proyecto, Base o departamentos nacionales.

**9. Actividades complementarias**

- Promover el cumplimiento de los procedimientos institucionales de COOPI y del Código de Conducta en los equipos bajo su supervisión.
- Contribuir a un ambiente de trabajo profesional, colaborativo y respetuoso.
- Participar en reuniones de coordinación y planificación de la misión.
- Representar a COOPI, cuando sea delegado por la Coordinación País, en reuniones vinculadas específicamente a la implementación operativa de proyectos.
- Ejecutar aquellas tareas inherentes al puesto y que sean solicitadas por la Coordinación País, según contexto y necesidades de la misión.

## Perfil deseado

Profesional con sólida experiencia en gestión e implementación de proyectos humanitarios y/o de desarrollo, supervisión de Project Managers y coordinación entre equipos multidisciplinarios. Se busca especialmente un perfil con fuerte capacidad de project management, seguimiento, resolución de problemas y desarrollo de equipos, capaz de combinar una visión global del portafolio con acompañamiento práctico a los responsables de proyecto.

### ESENCIALES

- Título universitario en Cooperación Internacional, Gestión de Proyectos, Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Ingeniería, Relaciones Internacionales o áreas afines.
- Al menos 5 años de experiencia relevante en gestión de proyectos humanitarios o de desarrollo con ONG internacionales, agencias internacionales u organizaciones similares.
- Experiencia demostrable como Coordinador/a de Proyectos Senior, Coordinador/a de Operaciones o posición equivalente.
- Experiencia comprobada en supervisión, acompañamiento y desarrollo de Project Managers o equipos de gestión de proyectos.
- Dominio del ciclo de gestión de proyectos: planificación, ejecución, seguimiento, reporting y cierre.
- Experiencia en seguimiento financiero de proyectos, incluyendo presupuestos, forecast, spending plans, análisis de ejecución y planificación de gasto.
- Experiencia en planificación y seguimiento de adquisiciones y necesidades logísticas vinculadas a proyectos.
- Conocimiento de procedimientos y requisitos de donantes institucionales, particularmente Unión Europea/ECHO, Naciones Unidas y/o cooperación bilateral.
- Capacidad demostrada para detectar bloqueos, analizar problemas y desarrollar soluciones prácticas.
- Experiencia en gestión de equipos, evaluación de desempeño, feedback y fortalecimiento de capacidades.
- Excelentes capacidades de organización, priorización y seguimiento.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera transversal con equipos técnicos, administrativos, logísticos y territoriales, respetando los diferentes ámbitos de responsabilidad.
- Liderazgo colaborativo, orientación a resultados y capacidad para acompañar y desarrollar equipos.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y gestionar simultáneamente múltiples proyectos y prioridades.
- Excelente comunicación interpersonal, capacidad de negociación y manejo constructivo de desacuerdos.
- Idioma castellano imprescindible; buen nivel de inglés oral y escrito.
- Manejo de herramientas informáticas y ofimáticas, con buen dominio de Excel.
- Disponibilidad para viajar regularmente a las diferentes áreas de intervención de COOPI en Venezuela.
- Respeto de la Visión y Misión de COOPI, de su carta de valores y de las políticas institucionales.

### DESEABLES

- Experiencia previa en Venezuela o en contextos latinoamericanos de elevada complejidad.
- Experiencia en contextos de emergencia y en lanzamiento o escalamiento rápido de proyectos.
- Experiencia previa con COOPI.
- Experiencia en proyectos financiados por ECHO, Unión Europea, AICS y agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Formación de posgrado en gestión de proyectos, acción humanitaria, cooperación internacional o áreas relacionadas.
- Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

jobs.title: Senior Finance Associate (Fiji Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23549**  
Position Title: **Senior Finance Associate**  
Duty Station City: **Suva**  
Duty Station Country: **Fiji Islands**  
Grade: **G-6**  
Contract Type: **One-Year Fixed Term**  
Recruiting Type: **General Service**  
Vacancy Type: **Vacancy Notice**  
Initial duration: **12 months**  
Closing date:  **27 October 2026**

**Context:**

Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) in Fiji and direct supervision of the Head of Resources Management; and, in collaboration with relevant units at Headquarters, Regional Office and the Global Shared Services Centre, the Senior Finance Associate will be responsible and accountable for managing or supporting the financial operations, budget monitoring, accounting processes, and financial reporting in accordance with IOM policies and procedures to countries in the South Pacific.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

1. Provide procedural guidance to managers and staff; supervise, guide and train other finance support staff;
2. Manage financial resources through monitoring and controlling assets, reserves, funds, supplies, etc. in accordance with IOM rules and regulations;
3. Provide specialized advice and support to Project Managers and/or Chief of Missions/Head of Office/ on financial and administrative matters;
4. Provide specialized support preparing annual budget submission and revisions including estimating the cost of staff as well as rental and utilities, office equipment and supplies, printing, and other contracts, services or running expenses;
5. Assist in monitoring compliance with financial policies, procedures, rules and regulations;
6. Consolidate data into financial statements and assist in monitoring expenditures to ensure they remain within authorized levels;
7. Provide regular and ad hoc financial information to support informed financial decision making;
8. Assist monitoring that bank reconciliations for IOM accounts are regularly performed and reviewed by designated stakeholders;
9. Manage and prepare the payroll by executing validity checks on monthly payroll results;
10. Ensure that disbursements are made based on proper authorizations and supported by legitimate and sufficient documentation;
11. Provide assistance responding to audit queries and follow up on audit recommendations;
12. Review the status and monitor the proper maintenance of Vendor Accounts in accounting system;
13. Verify vendor claims for accuracy and conformance with IOM finance policies and instructions;
14. Assist in the preparation of budget, accounting, financial, statistical reports and other reports as required; and,
15. Perform other related duties as required.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- High School diploma with six years of relevant experience; or,
- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finances, or related field with four years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications e.g. Word, Excel, PowerPoint, E-mail, Outlook; previous experience in SAP is a distinct advantage;
- Attention to detail, ability to organize paperwork in a methodical way;
- Discreet, details and clients-oriented, patient and willingness to learn new things; and,
- Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Knowledge of IOM/UN finance procedures and rules;
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, especially Excel;
- Knowledge of International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS); and,
- Knowledge of Oracle/SAP is highly desirable..

**Languages**

- Required for this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).
- IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this [link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

jobs.title: Human Resources Associate (Fiji Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
Job Identification (Reference Number): **23551**  
Position Title: **Human Resources Associate**  
Duty Station City: **Suva**  
Duty Station Country: **Fiji Islands**  
Grade: **G-5**  
Contract Type: **One-Year Fixed Term**  
Recruiting Type: **General Service**  
Vacancy Type: **Vacancy Notice**  
Initial duration: **12 months**  
Closing date: **27 October 2026**

**Context:**

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) Coordination Office for the South Pacific (COSP) in Suva, Fiji oversees and provides strategic and technical support to IOM activities within the South Pacific Country Offices (CO) under the COSP. Within the CO Fiji structure, the Resources Management Unit (RMU) provides support to 6 IOM Country Offices (COs) within the Pacific on budgeting, accounting, human resources, procurement, ICT and other administrative functions.

Under the overall supervision of the Head of Resources Management for the South Pacific Sub-Region and direct supervision of the Human Resources Officer (HRO) in Suva, Fiji, the incumbent will provide day to day human resources support to the COSP in Suva, Fiji.

**Description for Internal Candidates**

**Responsibilities for Internal Candidates**

**Human Resources:**

1. Assist in coordination of recruitment processes, including but not limited to, providing guidance to hiring managers on preparation of Post Description (PD), drafting and posting Vacancy Notice (VN)/Special Vacancy Notice (SVN), screening and shortlisting applications, drafting interview protocols, preparing and administering written tests, taking part in interview panels as assigned, drafting candidates’ assessment forms, conducting reference checks, preparing job offers, administering recruitment mailbox, etc.
2. Carry out pre-employment activities, such as preparation of Entry-on-Duty (EoD) documentation and collection of supporting documentation, coordination of EoD Medical Exam, follow up with Heath Insurance Unit in support centres on Medical Clearance, coordination of orientation sessions, arrangement for security briefing, inclusion in insurance plans as appropriate, creation of personal file, etc.
3. Assist in coordinating and monitoring the Human Resources Management of the COSP in Suva, Fiji accordance with the organization’s regulations, instructions, policies, procedures and practices and in light of operational activities in the Office in coordination with the Regional Office (RO), and Human Resource Management (HRM) in Geneva as appropriate.
4. Assist in verifying Human Resources processes and actions in conformity with relevant IOM policies and procedures. Ensure that Human Resources processes and procedures remain consistent with relevant IOM set rules and regulations.
5. Prepare HR communications, letters, presentations, infographics, and information materials using digital productivity and design tools.
6. Maintain HR communication resources, templates, and digital content to ensure accuracy and accessibility.
7. ​Perform the role of Timekeeper; monitor, maintain, update and reconcile leave quotas based on supporting documentation; generate, edit and analyse leave-related reports; respond to questions concerning leave administration; guide staff on request and approval procedure in the system.​​
8. Prepare monthly payroll for Consultant and Interns and monitor the payments.
9. Carry-out Personnel Action (PA) roles and Performance Appraisal System Agent role in Oracle paying special attention to data consistency and accuracy; input and maintain data based on approvals and supporting documentation; monitor and follow up on contractual situation and entitlements and generate reports, contract extensions, personnel actions and other related documentation.
10. Support separation, classification, and promotion processes by collecting necessary documentation, drafting forms, making calculations, obtaining approvals, and coordinating with relevant Units in support centres.
11. Update and maintain electronic archiving systems in the HR Unit, including personnel files with all supporting documentation, recruitment files, HR policies, regulations, guidelines and manuals, internal controls, etc.
    
    **Administration:**
12. Assist with/guide on logistics and administrative formalities related to travel arrangements of new colleagues, facilitating of entry visa and guide on the entry process to IOM personnel and dependents.
13. Ensure updating and maintaining of relevant policies and procedures of Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Immigration Bureau and other key departments as needed.
14. Ensure all protocol activities (e.g. visas, re-entry visas, stay permits, ID cards (IOM, UN, MFA), etc.) relating to personnel and dependents as applicable, are in accordance with requirement of the organization and national government, including correspondence with the national authorities in relation to these protocol arrangements.
15. Maintain up-to-date database on stay permit and re-entry visa and send alerts to personnel including provision of advice as required.
16. Perform such other related duties as may be assigned.

**Qualifications for Internal Candidates**

- Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology or related field with three years of relevant professional experience; or,
- High School diploma with five years of relevant experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Progressively responsible secretarial, administrative and operational experience, preferably in an international, non-profit environment;
- Experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities as well as with national and international institutions;
- Demonstrated ability to manage multiple work assignments efficiently, effectively, and with minimla supervision;
- Strong digital literacy, including proficiency in Microsoft 365 applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Copilot), online research, data analysis, document automation, and virtual collaboration tools.
- Prior work experience with international humanitarian organizations, non-government or government institutions/organization in a multi-cultural setting is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Excellent interpersonal skills with high professionalism;
- Attention to detail, ability to organize paperwork in a methodical way;
- Discreet, details and clients-oriented, patient and willingness to learn new things; and,
- Ability to create visually engaging HR communications, training materials, employer branding content, and workforce data visualizations using digital design and AI-enabled tools is a distinct advantage.

**Languages**

- Required for this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).
- IOM’s official languages are English, French and Spanish.
- Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this [link](https://www.iom.int/sites/g/files/tmzbdl486/files/about-iom/Competency_Framework-EN.pdf). Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these three values:

- Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

Core Competencies – behavioural indicators (Level 1)

- Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

**Notes**

- Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.
- This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months.
- This post is subject to only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration.
- Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, verification of residency, visa, and authorizations by the concerned Government, where applicable.
- IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.
- IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.
- IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM online recruitment system. The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.
- For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

jobs.title: Partner-Centred Design Consultant
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Location**: Global

**Closing date for applications:** Monday**,** 26 October 2026

**Start date:** As soon as Possible

**Consultancy duration:** Three to Four Months

## We unlock power with coastal communities

Blue Ventures connects coastal communities, restoring the ocean, providing the resources and partnerships they need to unlock their power and turn local action into global impact. We link communities with allies, knowledge and influence to create unstoppable waves of change.

Together, we’re placing communities at the centre of solutions to sustain fisheries, manage ecosystems and redefine how the world protects the ocean.

## **Summary job description**

We seek a consultant or team with strong experience in service design, customer experience (CX), user experience (UX) or human-centred service transformation to bring an independent partner-experience perspective and organisational critique to this work.

The consultancy will examine the end-to-end experience of working with Blue Ventures and connect it to the organisational choices shaping that experience. This includes how functions such as training and learning, partnerships, programme performance, data science and advocacy engage partners and coordinate their work.

Direct partner research will inform the assignment. The consultant must also bring the expertise to interpret and challenge existing arrangements, develop alternative approaches and demonstrate how support could be designed and delivered differently.

The work should introduce a shared framework that Blue Ventures can continue using beyond the consultancy. By applying this framework to selected priority areas, the consultant should demonstrate its value and help teams develop the understanding and practices needed to maintain it. The assignment is not expected to identify or design every change the organisation may need.

The primary focus will be partners funded through the Frontline Community Fund (FCF) and their interactions across Blue Ventures. The consultancy will complement our wider Partnership Strategy and internal operating model review, informing both without taking responsibility for the overall strategy, a comprehensive internal efficiency review or full implementation of recommendations.

### To download the full Terms of Reference, please click [here](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kceKwGi3lGg4hhkxuyB6Byv9lQWPV6Kp/view?usp=drive_link).

jobs.title: Program Manager I – Emergency Response
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Program Manager I - Emergency Response

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Nakivale or Rhino Camp

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm

***Please note that CRS is recruiting in anticipation of an award – recruitment for all candidates is contingent upon successful award of the project.***

**Background**

CRS is seeking Program Manager candidates for an anticipated integrated Shelter and WASH Response for Newly Arrived Refugees and Persons with Specific Needs (PSNs) in Nakivale and Rhino Camp Refugee Settlements. The project will improve the protection, health, and living conditions of newly arrived refugees PSNs in Nakivale and Rhino Camp through increased access to safe shelter, household sanitation, safe water and improved hygiene practices. The position is expected to be based in Nakivale, with regular travel to Rhino Camp for supervision and program oversight.

**Job Summary**

As the Program Manager, you will lead the management and technical oversight of all Shelter and WASH related programming in the proposed refugee settlements. You will ensure effective systems and processes are in place to support high-quality programming that advances Catholic Relief Services' (CRS) mission of serving poor and vulnerable populations.

The Program Manager will be responsible for the overall planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities in line with the project scope of work, results framework, and M&E plan. The successful candidate will provide technical guidance and capacity strengthening support to local partners and stakeholders and oversee project implementation across assigned geographic areas, ensuring quality, accountability, and timely delivery of results. Your management skills and knowledge will ensure that the CRS Uganda delivers high-quality programming and continuously works towards improving the impact of its emergency response and recovery programming.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

- Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight of all Shelter and WASH program activities throughout the project cycle to ensure project design, start-up, implementation and close-out are in line with CRS quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices.
- Effectively manage talent for emergency response and recovery programs and supervise. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being. Provide coaching, strategically tailored individual development plans, and complete performance management for direct reports.
- Oversee technical assistance and capacity strengthening activities in emergency and humanitarian response for CRS staff, local partner organizations, government counterparts, and other relevant stakeholders to enhance preparedness, response capacity, program quality, and impact.
- Provide technical leadership and assistance to strengthen humanitarian systems, policies, standards, and practices in Uganda. Support government, civil society, faith-based, and community actors to develop and operationalize frameworks, standard operating procedures, tools, and guidance at national and subnational levels.
- Collaborate with the CRS Uganda Programming leadership and colleagues from the global CRS Humanitarian Response Department to identify, document, and disseminate lessons learned, promising practices, and innovations from proposed Shelter and WASH program. Support knowledge management, adaptive management, and the integration of evidence and learning into program design and implementation.
- Contribute to the growth of CRS's emergency and humanitarian response portfolio by proactively identifying funding opportunities and supporting proposal development. Serve as a technical lead and/or writer for emergency and humanitarian response proposals, ensuring quality design, budgeting, staffing plans, and alignment with CRS and donor requirements.
- Oversee the identification, assessment and strengthening of partnerships relevant to Shelter, WASH and emergency and humanitarian response, and the appropriate application of partnership concepts, tools and approaches.
- Ensure timely and appropriate project expenditures in line with financial plans and efficient use and stewardship of project material sources.
- Represent CRS in relevant coordination forums, clusters, and technical working groups, engaging effectively with government counterparts, donors, UN agencies, local partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and advance humanitarian and program objectives.
- Undertake other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the scope and level of the position, to support evolving programmatic priorities and advance the broader CRS Uganda emergency and humanitarian response portfolio.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills with ability to make sound judgment.
- Staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information management systems.
- Good experience in project grants management, including project design, preferably for grants from multiple public donors, including US government and UN.
- Demonstrated ability to write high quality technical proposals and reports.
- Strong relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Strategic in how you approach each relationship.
- Strong presentation and facilitation skills.
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s Degree in International Development, International Relations, Community Development, or in the field of disaster management, climate adaptation or resilience required.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience in relevant field-based project management experience.
- Strong knowledge of Shelter, WASH and humanitarian response sectors, Uganda's coordination mechanisms, and protection principles to support safe, dignified, and effective planning, coordination, and program implementation.
- Experience in managing moderately complex projects.
- Experience in an international NGO.
- Experience working closely with local partner organizations.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master's Degree in International Development, International Relations, Community Development, or in the field of disaster management, WASH or engineering.
- Demonstrated ability to convene, coordinate, and facilitate complex multi-stakeholder consultations and partnerships involving government, development partners, technical agencies, academia, and community stakeholders.

**Required Languages** - Fluent English is required. Working proficiency in local language is a plus.

**Travel** - include percentage of required travel, if applicable. Could be stated as Must be willing and able to travel up to 30 %.

**Supervisory Responsibilities:** Yes, including but not limited to Project Officers and Senior Project Officers and project MEAL staff.

**Key Working Relationships:**

Internal: CRS Country Representative, Head of Programs, Head of Operations, Uganda-based technical experts for MEAL, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI) and Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), Regional and Headquarters technical staff.

External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders.

- **Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**
- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.
- **Agency Leadership Competencies:**
- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

**Job Title:** Technical Advisor II – Climate Change & Landscape Restoration

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm.

**Job Summary**

You will provide strategic technical leadership, advice, guidance, and support across program design, business development, implementation, learning, and evidence generation in the areas of Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation and Landscape Restoration. Working in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices, you will support Country Office(CO) teams to develop, implement, and scale innovative, high-quality programming that advances resilience, environmental stewardship, and sustainable livelihoods for poor and vulnerable communities. Your technical knowledge, advice and guidance will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Climate Change and Landscape Restoration programming is across Uganda.

Your technical expertise, strategic vision, and leadership will contribute to the growth and positioning of CRS Uganda's Climate Change and Landscape Restoration portfolio. You will help identify and pursue new funding opportunities, lead technical design for priority investments and proposals, build relationships and partnerships, and support the effective implementation of strategic initiatives that generate evidence, demonstrate impact, and inform future programming. Through collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will strengthen CRS' reputation as a trusted partner and technical leader in climate resilience, nature-based solutions, and landscape restoration across Uganda.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities**

jobs.title: Middle East Head of Operations
jobs.body:
The position is to be filled as soon as possible, with an initial contract duration of 6 months with very good prospects for an extension. Employment location will be Amman, Jordan (JO) .The position is paid according to SG8 of WHH's salary grid in Jordan.

As a member of the hub, your duty will be to lead procurement, IT and relevant legal matters of its work in Jordan and beyond, with your technical expertise, your problem-solving skills and onsite presence where necessary. You’ll lead the logistic and operations team, work closely with other members of the hub, closely liaise with legal counsellors, and provide solutions to operational issues. As the Middle East Head of Operations, your main task would be to oversee procurement, handle IT issues, manage facilities, oversee visa/permit issues for WHH staff, support in relations with the authorities and legal matters. You’ll work in close collaboration with the Logistics Coordinator and support the Head of Mission.

## Your responsibilities

**Tasks**

**Facilities**

- Identification, setup, and establishment of premises (offices, warehouses, guesthouses) across countries under WHH Amman hub’s responsibility. The role will involve overseeing the leasing processes, including due diligence, contract negotiation and compliance with WHH and local regulations.
- Close coordination with office, warehouse, and guesthouse focal points to assess facility needs, resolve issues, and ensure functionality, safety, and alignment with operational requirements.
- Supervise facility operations including utilities, services, maintenance, health and safety compliance, and security measures.
- Ensure proper management of facility-related assets and inventories, maintain accurate documentation (e.g., contracts), and promote sustainable facility practices such as energy efficiency and waste reduction.
- Support contingency planning for facility-related disruptions, and coordinate space planning to ensure effective use of premises in line with evolving programmatic needs.

**Fleet & Transportation**

- Establish or actively support the establishment of WHH’s fleet management systems in operational areas.
- Supervise and ensure proper use of vehicle logbooks (or apps), fuel tracking systems, and maintenance records. Conduct regular reviews and audits to ensure accuracy, accountability, and compliance with WHH and donor regulations.
- Provide technical supervision and capacity building for fleet personnel to maintain safe, cost-effective, and reliable transport operations.

**Inventory and Asset**

- Establish & implement standardized asset and inventory management software for WHH hub in Amman and its operational areas and ensure alignment with WHH procedures and donor requirements.
- Monitor the availability of supplies (inventory, stationery etc.) and establish a system for their replenishment for each operational area tailored to the needs of each operational area.
- Support stock management and warehousing and maintain updated inventory list for all locations with accurate data in collaboration with field logisticians, office responsible, and ensure accurate documentation and proper storage conditions
- Collaborate closely with field logisticians and office responsible to maintain up-to-date inventory and asset records across all locations, ensuring data accuracy and traceability.

**Procurement**

- Establish a sound procurement system for Amman hub, capable of adapting to changing operational needs and donor requirements across diverse contexts.
- Launch and manage framework agreements for commonly used items in each operational area, while ensuring market assessments and supplier prequalification remain up to date for rapid response in volatile environments.
- Closely follow up on digitalization processes lead by Head Office and make sure that the hub countries are well adopting new solutions and systems.
- Organize and oversee cross-border shipments through multiple supply corridors, proactively addressing access constraints, border procedures (custom clearance), and documentation to ensure timely delivery in dynamic settings.
- Ensure procurement documentation is collected and archiving practices are in place, maintaining full traceability and audit compliance.

**IT**

- Ensure that IT systems of the hub are up to standard with WHH systems
- Ensure that IT support personnel of the hub are well coordinated and that they are working closely with the regional IT.
- Ensure that all personnel have access to necessary equipment and systems and are not facing IT related challenges in conducting their tasks.
- Be aware and advice on digital solutions that would increase efficiency and effectives of WHH’s work.

**Partnerships**

- Provide active technical support to local partner organizations in conducting transparent and compliant procurement processes, aligned with WHH and donor regulations.
- Strengthen partner logistics capacity through training, mentoring, and support in the development or improvement of logistics manuals, tools, and procedures for sustainable operational management.
- Provide support to partners on other operations topics as needed.

**Legal & Admin Matters**

- Support the Head of Mission in legal & admin related matters for the hub such as (Registration process, renewal of required licenses, permits, visa & work permits for International staff) in Iraq, Yemen, Palestine, Jordan and other countries, if necessary,
- Give advice on legal matters to head of mission in ensuring compliance with national laws and regulations in each country.
- Act as focal point for legal advisors in each country, follow up on requests/permits/approvals, lead the preparation of necessary documentation, and keep the head of mission and the legal counsellors in head office up to date on these.
- Ensure that international staff and visitors receive necessary legal support for their travels to Jordan and other countries.
- Support registration related processes in all countries.

**Other**

- Take overall ownership establishing, standardizing and continuously improving all operations related processes in the hub countries, ensuring efficiency, compliance, digitalization, and adaptability to changing operational contexts.
- Proactively identify capacity building needs of WHH staff, by identifying development opportunities, delivering practical training, and fostering a culture of continuous learning and improvement in operation practices.
- In coordination, with the other logistics personnel, represent the organization in forums such as logistics clusters, meetings amongst partners, authorities and different local actors involved in operations.

## Your profile

- University degree in humanitarian logistics, supply chain or similar
- Minimum 5 years of experience in operations of which **at least 2 years as head of logistics or operations department**
- Experience in working in conflict zones would be an asset
- Demonstrated experience in supporting local organizations in their capacity strengthening is required
- **Previous international experience in similar roles beyond Jordan is a must**
- Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, experience with logistic and operations software would be an asset
- Excellent inter-personal, communication, advisory and facilitation skills
- Fluency in verbal and written Arabic and English is a must
- **Willingness and ability to travel to OPT, Syria, Yemen, Iraq and Lebanon** (Ideally not blacklisted or barred from entering to any of the countries)

## Our offer

We offer you the opportunity to work in a responsible and interesting field as part of an extremely dedicated team. Welthungerhilfe attaches great importance to the personal and professional development of its employees. Remuneration is based on our gender-independent salary scale.

*\*Welthungerhilfe values diversity and ensures an inclusive, non-discriminatory working environment. We welcome applications from suitably qualified people from all sections of the community.*

jobs.title: Agricultural Value Chains - Project Manager (Cashew & Coffee) - Mozambique
Medical Supply Planner
jobs.body:
**\*\*The compensation range for this position is $60,300–$63,000 USD. Compensation will be based on experience, qualifications, and other relevant factors. This is a full-time, hybrid position located in Lindale, Texas, with one in -person workday per week\*\*.**

Mercy Ships is seeking an experienced Medical Supply Planner. In this role, you will be part of the Global Supply Chain Planning department. This department supports our hospital ships operating in Africa.

As a Supply Planner, you are responsible for planning the delivery of Medical Supplies to our Hospital ships serving in Africa. You monitor inventory levels and buffer targets across the supply chain and fulfilling customer special / annual order requests. You work closely with the Medical Demand Planners, a fellow Medical Supply Planner, and various departments within the Global Supply Chain.

The intensive coordination with departments at both the Dutch and U.S. offices, as well as with the ships themselves, makes this a dynamic role at the heart of the organization.

**How You Will Contribute:**

- To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.
- Execute the replenishment of vessels by generating container orders using the Supply Planning Tools
- Aligning operational timelines with Procurement, Logistics and Warehouse departments.
- Monitor inventory health across ships, depots, and ad-hoc/non-inventory streams.
- Establishes, evaluates, and sets Safety Stock (SS) levels across the supply chain.
