jobs.title: Country Director – Ethiopia
jobs.body:
**Job Title:** Country Director – Ethiopia

**Terms:** Two-Year Fixed Term, Accompanied terms

**Location:** Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

**Salary:** GB8: €63,461 - €70,513

**Requirements:** At least 20% travel to programme sites

**About Concern:** Established in 1968, Concern is a non-profit, non-governmental humanitarian organisation, dedicated to the reduction of suffering and the ultimate elimination of extreme poverty in the world’s poorest countries.

Concern’s vision, our mission and our work are all defined by one goal – ending extreme poverty, whatever it takes. Concern strives for a world free from poverty, fear and oppression.

Our culture is values driven and we believe that our people are central to all that we do and are key to delivering on our goal of Reaching the Furthest Behind First. We are committed to ensuring a workplace where everybody feels valued and are enabled to succeed in their work and contribute to delivering on our mission.

**Role Purpose:** You will have the overall responsibility for strategic planning, programmatic direction, and management oversight of all programmes and operations of Concern Worldwide in Ethiopia. You will provide strategic direction and leadership to the Country Management Team ensuring effective and professional management of all aspects of the country programme, ensuring compliance with Concern’s organisational procedures, policies, and values.

**Responsibilities:**

**Leadership**

- Develop and implement a coherent country programme that contributes to achieving Concern’s global strategy and objectives in particular addressing emergency needs of conflict/disaster affected population.
- Provide leadership in the overall effective planning and direction of Concern’s programme and operations at country level.
- Build strong and committed team of national and international staff adhering to Concern policies and procedures and applying key principles of transparency, accountability, good stewardship and participation.
- Create and maintain shared vision, amongst all Concern staff, of Concern’s programme aims and objectives and their role in achieving these.
- Lead and support in strengthening coordination and collaboration within teams and across all teams, maintain and ensure constructive communications, contribute to a positive working environment.

**Security Management**

- Take overall responsibility for the security and safety of Concern personnel and resources.
- Be responsible for participatory development and implementation of the Country Security Management Plan and Standard Operating Procedures.
- Liaise with necessary external bodies to keep abreast of current affairs in order to maintain an awareness of economic, political, humanitarian and security developments.
- Ensure a functioning Security Focal Group (SFG) and keep up to date with security incidents at central and field locations.
- Work with the SFG to ensure the development and maintenance of effective security systems for Concern employees, programmes and property including the regular revision and implementation of the Security Management Plan.
- Report any security threats and incidents to the Regional Director.

**Programme Development and Management**

- Lead the strategic development and implementation of programmes in line with Concern organisational strategic plan and following the Concern Project Cycle Management policy including proposal writing and sourcing funding.
- Ensure effective coordination of technical inputs (e.g. Head Office advisors) in designing, implementing, monitoring and evaluating programmes.
- Take lead in ensuring targets of the country level funding strategy are met and establish productive working relationships with donors and be responsible for undertaking country level negotiations related to securing funding, programming contracts, and reports.
- Develop partnerships with local NGOs and CBOs through the application of Concern assessment tools
- Manage the country programme effectively including allocation of resources and ensuring that appropriate monitoring and controls are established and maintained at all levels by working with programme and systems managers, staff and where relevant partners.
- Provide adequate leadership and support to programme managers in setting up high quality standards and implementation of programmes to include equality, prevention of GBV and DRR.
- Ensure that all programmes are implemented and completed according to programme documents including agreed plans and budget, and in compliance with donors and internal policies.
- Maintain effective communication and liaise with Concern Head office in Dublin and ensure that high standard internal and donor reports are produced and submitted in timely manner and in line with relevant targets and objectives.

**People Management**

- Line manage senior management staff (Country Management Team – CMT) and be responsible for the overall management and development of national and international staff.
- Manage and support country programme team ensuring that there is clearly defined structure and job descriptions for all staff.
- Ensure that regular staff Performance and Development Review (PDR) system is established and maintained and that PDRs are adequately undertaken at all levels.
- Develop, review, and effectively implement all Human Resources related procedures in accordance with Concern policies and procedures and in line with the national labour laws.
- Establish and maintain regular, participative and documented forums and meetings for all key staff to discuss policy, strategic, operational and management issues, coordinate planning and implementation of activities, and ensure information sharing.

**Budget and Financial Management**

- Responsible for overall financial management including participatory budget preparation, revision and monitoring and timely submission of budgets and reports.
- Ensure that the Concern organisational financial guidelines and procedures are adhered to.
- Develop and implement work and expenditure plans and ensure that the country programmes are implemented within agreed and approved budget through undertaking regular budget monitoring of expenditure against budget.
- Ensure that internal and donor financial reports are submitted in timely manner and up to high-quality standard.

**Representation and networking**

- Represent Concern in and establish/maintain coordination and networking relationships with the government, local authorities, donors and other national and international humanitarian actors including Alliance 2015 members in the country.
- Ensure compliance with Concern’s statutory obligations in relation to registration compliance, including submission of mandatory reports to the authorities.
- Ensure that relationship and formal agreements with the government are established, maintained and updated as appropriate.
- Represent Concern at various coordination forums.
- Promote the humanitarian principles of Concern in external settings, ensuring that the organisation’s neutrality, impartiality and independence is well communicated and consistently presented, and that we are perceived as an independent humanitarian organisation addressing the needs of the most vulnerable.

**Policies and procedures**

- Ensure that support systems are in place and functioning in accordance with best practices in order to ensure transparency and accountability to programme participants, donors, government, and other relevant stakeholder.
- Promote and ensure compliance with the requirements of Concern’s Code of Conduct and its associated policies and implementation of the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS), along with Concern’s community-based complaints and response mechanism (CRM) to ensure maximum protection of and accountability to programme beneficiaries.

**Accountability**

- Promote and ensure compliance with the Core Humanitarian Standard (CHS) commitments and quality criteria
- Ensure that all staff are familiar with the principles underpinning accountability, safeguarding and Concern's Complaints and Response Mechanism (CRM) and ensure that information about Concern's commitments on accountability and safeguarding are disseminated among programme participants and communities
- Ensure that the CRM is functional, effectively implemented and accessible in all programmes' locations, enabling safe reporting of both programmatic and sensitive complaints, including safeguarding concerns
- Ensure that complaints are welcomed, managed and responded to in a timely, fair and appropriate manner; ensure that sensitive complaints, including safeguarding concerns, are handled with utmost confidentiality and that the safety of the complainants and those affected is prioritised at all stages.

**Other**

- As a commitment to our humanitarian mandate the Country Director will be responsible for the implementation of any new emergency response.
- The programme is in a dynamic context that requires continuous contextual analysis and adaptation of the strategic planning frameworks.

**Role Holder Requirements:**

**Essential:**

This position demands a dynamic individual with a demonstrated ability to achieve results in a demanding and fast-paced environment.

- Advance Degree preferably in social science or development management or business management or related discipline or equivalent in experience.
- At least 5 years’ overseas experience in management and coordination of development and humanitarian programmes with at least 3 years’ experience in a senior management position.
- Strong leadership skills and ability to manage change effectively.
- Excellent communication and presentation skills in English
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills with an ability/confidence to engage and represent Concern at public forums, media and donors.
- Strong coordination and conflict resolution skills.
- Cross cultural awareness and sensitivity.
- Ability to work under pressure and to strict deadlines.
- Good coaching, motivational, facilitation and capacity-building skills.
- Dynamic and willing to take initiatives to complete assigned tasks and work independently.
- Delegation, time management and prioritizing skills and coping with broad range of demands.
- Willingness to travel regularly to the project sites.
- Experience of managing major donor grants such as ECHO, EU, USAID/BHA, UN Agencies and Irish Aid

**Desirable:**

- Previous work experience in Horn of Africa generally, or Ethiopia specifically
- Experience with commercial contracts and climate financing
- Affinity with organisational values, mission and vision, commitment to humanitarian principles
- Familiarity with sector and governmental coordination mechanisms

jobs.title: Online Training Facilitator for African Mental Health CSOs and OPDs: Project Management, Resource Mobilization, Financial Management, and M&E
jobs.body:
## Background

The Africa Mental Health Leadership Programme (MHLP) is funded by the Wellcome Trust through the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and is implemented by Africa CDC in collaboration with CBM Global, the Mental Health Innovation Network (MHIN), the Pan-African Network of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (PANPPD), and other key stakeholders. The programme aims to build a new generation of mental health leaders across Africa who are equipped to advance mental health policy, advocacy, and service delivery.

As the lead partner for Pillar Four: Civil Society Engagement and Networks, CBM Global works in collaboration with MHIN and PANPPD to strengthen civil society engagement, networking, and collective action within the mental health sector. Through this pillar, the programme seeks to strengthen the capacity of civil society organisations (CSOs), including organisations of persons with lived experience of psychosocial disabilities (OPDs), to advocate for quality, rights-based mental health services and to hold service providers and policymakers accountable. A key focus of CBM Global's role is to ensure the meaningful participation of people with lived experience at all stages of programme implementation, while supporting the institutional strengthening of representative organisations.

To inform these efforts, a Mental Health Organizations Needs Survey was conducted under Pillar Four across Africa to identify the needs, aims and priorities of the organizations among other key areas. The survey findings revealed significant capacity gaps in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation (M&E). In response to these identified needs, this Terms of Reference (ToR) proposes the development and delivery of an accessible online training initiative focused on these key capacity areas. The initiative aims to strengthen the organizational capacity, sustainability, and effectiveness of mental health CSOs and OPDs across the continent by equipping them with practical knowledge, skills, and tools in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and Monitoring &Evaluation (M&E). Furthermore, the initiative emphasizes a shift from one-off training workshops towards practical application, ongoing mentorship, and follow-up support to enable participating organisations to strengthen internal systems, improve funding readiness, and enhance accountability and organizational performance.

## **Purpose of the Assignment**

The purpose of this consultancy is to engage a qualified facilitator to design, facilitate, and provide a post training technical support for an accessible online capacity strengthening programme for mental health CSOs and OPDs across Africa.

The facilitator will develop and deliver practical, interactive and accessible training in project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and in M&E, equipping participants with practical tools and templates. The Facilitator will also provide follow-up mentorship and technical support to strengthen organizational capacity, sustainability and accountability

## Overall Objective

To strengthen the institutional capacity of mental health CSOs and OPDs across Africa to sustainably mobilize resources, effectively manage programmes and finances, and generate evidence to improve accountability advocacy, and mental health outcomes in their communities.

## 4. Specific Objectives of the Assignment

- Design and deliver an accessible online capacity strengthening programme that starts with the project management cycle and progressively covers fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and M&E.
- Develop practical tools, templates, and learning assignments that participants can adapt and apply within their organizations.
- Provide structured mentorship and technical assistance to support participants in applying learning to real organizational priorities and strengthening institutional practices.
- Support the programme team in participant onboarding, baseline and endline assessments, and reporting on the training process and outcomes.
- Facilitate the development of organizational action plans and provide follow-up support to enable participating organizations to implement improvements in project management, fundraising, financial management, and M&E systems.

## Scope of Work

The Facilitator will be responsible for the full design, delivery, mentorship, and reporting of an online capacity strengthening programme for CSOs and OPDs across Africa. The assignment will include the development and adaptation of training content for a fully online, accessible, and low bandwidth. Deliver interactive training sessions; provide practical assignments and post-training mentorship; and documentation of programme outcomes and recommendations. to reinforce institution learning uptake.

## Key Tasks and Responsibilities

- Review the approved concept notes and other relevant background documents. Develop an inception report outlining the understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology, delivery plan, work plan, and timeline.
- Support the refinement of participant application, selection and onboarding criteria, taking into account the concept note’s indication that small, emerging, and mid-sized organizations with clear institutional strengthening needs should be prioritized and that, where feasible, at least two representatives per organization should participate.
- Develop and administer baseline assessment to identify capacities, needs and priorities expectations, and institutional priorities in project design.
- Design a structured online curriculum covering project management, fundraising and resource mobilization, financial management, and M&E.
- Develop training materials, facilitator guides, presentations, practical exercises, assignments and participants' resources.
- Develop practical tools and include concepts, donor mapping, concept note development, budgeting, financial tracking, M&E frameworks, and organizational action planning tools.
- Deliver the online training sessions in an interactive format.
- Facilitate practical assignments and provide feedback to participants throughout the programme.
- Provide post-training mentorship and technical assistance to support the application of learning and strengthening of organizational systems. Facilitate peer learning and knowledge exchange among participating organizations.
- Administer or support endline evaluation and document lessons learned, participant feedback, and recommendations for future support.

## Required Training Modules

- **Module 1:** Project Management Cycle (foundation module) – including situation and stakeholder analysis, problem tree and objective setting, results frameworks and activity planning, risk analysis, implementation planning, and progress monitoring and reporting basics.
- **Module 2:** Fundraising and Resource Mobilization – including the funding landscape for mental health CSOs and OPDs, cross-sectoral positioning of mental health within broader development priorities, donor mapping and opportunity tracking, concept note development, and grant proposal writing basics. The Facilitator should provide useful donor websites and practical guidance on how to search and screen opportunities.
- **Module 3:** Financial Management and Minimum Financial Standards – including budget development and monitoring, internal controls and financial accountability, financial documentation and record keeping, procurement basics, expenditure tracking, financial reporting, and donor compliance requirements.
- **Module 4:** Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) – including results frameworks and log frames, indicator development and selection, data collection and management, data quality assurance, routine monitoring and reporting, adaptive management and organizational learning, and use of evidence for advocacy and fundraising.
- **Module 5:** Integration and Organizational Action Planning – including how to link project design, fundraising, financial management, and M&E into an integrated organizational system, organizational capacity strengthening priorities, development of a practical organizational action plans 6–12 months.

## Deliverables

- Deliverable 1: Inception report outlining the Facilitator’s understanding of the assignment, methodology, workplan, training schedule, and recommendations on participant selection and onboarding.
- Deliverable 2: Baseline assessment tool and summary report highlighting participants' needs, priorities and capacity gaps.
- Deliverable 3: Complete training package, including curriculum, session plans, presentations, facilitator notes, assignments, participant handouts and supporting resources.
- Deliverable 4: Delivery of the online training programme, including facilitation of all agreed sessions and participant engagement activities.
- Deliverable 5: Participant tool package, including project concept template, donor mapping template and funding tracker, basic grant-writing checklist, minimum financial standards self-assessment tool, simple budget and budget monitoring templates, M&E framework template with sample indicators, and organizational action planning template.
- Deliverable 6: Delivery of post training mentorship and technical assistance, including documentation of support provided and participant progress.
- Deliverable7: Final consultancy report summarizing activities completed, participant engagement, pre/post learning reflections or assessment findings, key outputs produced by participants, lessons learned, and recommendations.

## **Intellectual Property Rights**

- All reports, materials, data, tools, publications, and other deliverables developed under this assignment shall become the property of the contracting organization (CBM Global) upon payment in full, and the Facilitator shall not use, reproduce, distribute, or publish such materials without prior written consent from the organization.

## Expected Outputs from Participants

By the end of the assignment, the Facilitator will support participating organizations to develop practical draft outputs that can be further refined and applied within the organizations. These outputs may include: a simple project concept, donor map, draft concept note, financial management self-assessment, basic M&E framework, and an organizational action plan for organizational strengthening.

## Indicative Duration and Level of Effort

The consultancy is expected to be delivered within a period of 2 (two) months from the date of contract signing.

Month 1 is expected to cover inception, onboarding, baseline assessment, and delivery of the core training sessions.

Month 2 is expected to focus on mentorship, peer learning activities, assignments, and organizational action planning.

Applicants should propose a realistic number of working days consistent with the scope of work and deliverables.

## Reporting and Supervision

The Facilitator will report to the designated programme focal person/team throughout the assignment.

The Facilitator will work closely with the organizing institution and programme team on scheduling, participants' engagement, and delivery of agreed activities. All key deliverables will be submitted for review and approval by the CBM Global in collaboration with programme focal persons.

## Facilitator Profile and Qualifications

- Advanced degree in public health, project management, development studies, business administration, finance, monitoring and evaluation, social sciences, or another relevant field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience in organizational capacity strengthening, preferably with CSOs, OPDs, NGOs, or networks in Africa.
- Demonstrated experience designing and facilitating training on project management, fundraising/resource mobilization, financial management, and/or M&E.
- Demonstrated experience in grant writing, donor engagement, institutional development, and practical organizational systems strengthening.
- Strong knowledge of the civil society and/or mental health landscape, disability inclusion, and rights-based programming in African contexts is highly desirable.
- Experience delivering engaging online training using adult learning methods and accessible facilitation approaches.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and French.
- Experience working with people with lived experience is an added advantage

## **Facilitator Selection Criteria**

- Demonstrated understanding of the assignment and responsiveness to the requirement outlined in this ToR.
- Quality, feasibility, and practicality of the proposed methodology, workplan, and delivery approach.
- Relevant technical expertise and proven experience in thematic areas.
- Experience working with African CSOs/OPDs and/or mental health and disability inclusion actors in Africa.
- Experience in designing and facilitating online capacity strengthening initiatives including mentorship, and development of practical tools and templates.
- Qualifications and experience of the Facilitator or consulting team, including demonstrated ability to deliver similar assignments.
- Financial proposal and value for money.

## Application Requirements

Interested Facilitator(s) are requested to submit:

(a) A technical proposal outlining understanding of the assignment, methodology, workplan, and suggested level of effort;

(b) A financial proposal detailing the proposed consultancy fee and any associated costs;

(c) Curriculum Vitae(s) of the Facilitator or consulting team highlighting relevant qualification and experience;

 (d) At least two examples of similar previous work, such as capacity strengthening programmes, training curricula, facilitation assignments, mentorship initiatives, or toolkits;

 (e) Contact details for at least two professional referees.

- Applicants with disability are strongly encouraged to apply.

## Indicative Assessment Matrix (Optional)

- Technical proposal / methodology: 35%
- Relevant experience and qualifications: 35%
- Sample work / evidence of similar assignments: 10%
- Financial proposal / value for money: 20%

## Ethical and Accessibility Considerations

The Facilitator shall ensure that all training, mentorship, and engagement activities are delivered in an inclusive, respectful, and accessible manner, considering the diverse needs and contexts of participating CSOs and OPDs.

Specifically, the Facilitator shall:

- Apply accessible and participatory approaches that support the meaningful engagement of all participants.
- Ensure training materials and learning activities are practical, user-friendly, and adapted for online delivery, including low-bandwidth options where feasible.
- Promote a safe and respectful learning environment that values diversity, equity, and inclusion.
- The Facilitator must maintain confidentiality and privacy of participant information and organizational data shared during the assignment.
- Use any information or data collected solely for the purposes of this assignment and in accordance with applicable ethical and data protection standards.

## **Compliance with CBM Global policies**

- All Facilitators are required to sign and be bound by CBM Global code of conduct for Facilitators and CBM Global Safeguarding Policy and Behaviour Code and CBM [Accessibility](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) [Policy.](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) These will be provided upon contracting.
- Canvassing of any kind by applicants, whether direct or indirect, with the intention of influencing the selection process may result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

## Payment schedule

- The payment will be made based on approved invoices in accordance with CBM Global’s specifications (see the CBM Global Consultancy Invoice Information).

1. The consultancy rate is agreed as following:
2. Payments will be paid as follows

- 30% upon acceptance of inception package.
- 70% after delivery of all the deliverables.

jobs.title: Responsable du Pôle Conformité et Finances CDI (H/F)
jobs.body:
Rejoindre l’ONG Plan International France, c’est donner un sens à sa vie professionnelle en s’engageant dans la solidarité internationale et en adhérant aux valeurs de transparence, de respect, de durabilité, de communauté et d’inclusion.

Notre ONG est fière d’œuvrer pour un monde meilleur dans lequel les droits des enfants, et en particulier des filles, sont respectés. C’est ainsi qu’en 2025, le réseau Plan International a permis à 5,1 millions de filles dans le monde de bénéficier d’un meilleur accès à l’éducation.

Rejoindre notre ONG, c’est aussi intégrer une équipe conviviale d’une quarantaine de salarié·es et de bénévoles, aussi expert·es que passionné·es. Nous travaillons dans la bienveillance et la confiance, en gardant pour objectif le bien-être des salarié·es. Télétravail, flexibilité des horaires, grande autonomie sont autant d’aménagements qui favoriseront votre équilibre vie pro/vie perso. Vous trouverez une palette de métiers variés et une organisation qui s’inscrit dans une dynamique de progression.

Pour compléter cette belle équipe, nous recherchons des talents qui partagent nos valeurs et qui souhaitent apporter leur pierre à l’édifice. Venez donc nous rencontrer pour découvrir les belles missions qui nous animent et nous motivent.

## **Le poste que nous proposons** 

Au sein du Pôle Conformité et Finances de la Direction Administrative et Financière, vous aurez pour objectif de garantir l’expertise en conformité et en finances pour les programmes de développement et d’urgence mis en œuvre.

Directement rattaché·e à la Directrice Administrative et financière, le∙la Responsable du pôle conformité et finances assurera les missions suivantes :

**Sécurisation des volets financiers et contractuels dans la phase de montage et d’élaboration des programmes**

- Valider le montage budgétaire et les informations administratives et financières des programmes en cohérence avec les activités, les procédures de Plan International et les règles des bailleurs de fonds ;
- Valider les volets financiers des conventions signées par Plan International France avec les bailleurs de fonds et avec les bureaux pays ;
- Participer aux négociations sur les aspects budgétaires et contractuels lorsque nécessaire

**Sécurisation des volets financiers, conformité et contrôle interne des programmes**

- Assurer le suivi de conformité finance sur les programmes de son portefeuille ;
- Valider la qualité et la conformité des rapports financiers à destination des bailleurs de fonds ;
- Valider les transferts de fonds liés aux programmes, vers le terrain ;
- Garantir l’utilisation et l’amélioration des outils de gestion financière et contrôle interne existants ;
- Superviser le bon déroulement des missions d’audit demandées par les bailleurs et assurer la mise en œuvre et le suivi des recommandations ;
- Capitaliser sur les recommandations préconisées par les différents organes de contrôle en lien avec la référente audit interne
- Assurer l’identification des risques financiers et/ou de fraude et de corruption sur son activité et la mise en place d’actions préventives et de contrôle.

**Renforcement de la collaboration financière avec les bureaux pays**

- Superviser le suivi conformité et finance des programmes en appui aux bureaux pays et selon les procédures de Plan International et des bailleurs de fonds ;
- Superviser l’accompagnement et la formation des bureaux pays à la mise en œuvre des exigences de conformité spécifiques aux bailleurs français et européens ;
- Assurer et superviser des missions d’appui et de conformité finances lors de déplacements dans les Bureaux pays (1 par trimestre en moyenne).

**Renforcement des capacités du pôle Conformité et Finances**

- Capitaliser les bonnes pratiques de gestion financière et budgétaire et s’assurer de leur respect ;
- Assurer l’actualisation des procédures et des outils en fonction de l’évolution des exigences bailleurs ;
- Assurer la création et l’amélioration d’outils de gestion financière afin de faciliter la gestion quotidienne des programmes et le pilotage financier global du portefeuille de programmes ;
- Intéragir avec l’équipe Finance de Plan international France, dans la gestion et clôture comptable des programmes (transmission informations) ;
- Préparer le budget annuel des recettes Bailleurs institutionnels et privés, ainsi que le budget annuel des dépenses liées aux programmes

**Participation à l’exploration de nouvelles sources de financement innovantes**

En lien avec la direction des Programmes et Partenariats stratégiques :

- Contribuer, à la stratégie de réponse aux appels d’offres de bailleurs publics (contrats commerciaux)
- Identifier les besoins d’accompagnement et de formation de l’équipe
- Participer à l’identification des bureaux pays en capacité de répondre à des appels d’offre
- Mise en place d’une méthodologie de gestion financière des contrats commerciaux

**Management de l’équipe Conformité et Finances**

- Assurer le management quotidien de son équipe ;
- Participer aux recrutements ;
- Créer, organiser et animer des formations pour son équipe
- Coordonner le pilotage de l’activité en lien avec l’équipe Programmes et Partenariats Stratégiques.

## **Le profil que nous cherchons** 

Vous disposez d’un Diplôme de gestion financière, contrôle de gestion/audit, école supérieure de commerce, formation Bioforce administration. Et vous justifiez de 7 ans minimum en contrôle de gestion de programmes dont 2 au sein d’une ONG au siège. Expérience de terrain souhaitée.

Également :

- Très bonne maitrise d’Excel
- Anglais et français courant à l’écrit et à l’oral (B2)
- Maîtrise des exigences financières et de conformité des bailleurs institutionnels français et européens (AFD, Expertise France, CDCS, INTPA, ECHO, …)
- Analyse des risques en matière de conformité et d’éligibilité des dépenses
- Gestion financière, contrôle interne,
- Bonne capacité d’organisation et autonome (prise d’initiative)
- Sens de l’organisation et fort dynamisme
- Résolution de problèmes
- Aisance relationnelle et qualités de communication
- Vous savez vous adapter, êtes rigoureux·reuse
- Première expérience en management

## **Pour postuler** 

- Poste en CDI à pourvoir dès que possible.
- Poste basé à Pantin (93) avec déplacements dans les pays d’intervention ;
- Statut cadre forfait jour, JRTT, 10 jours de télétravail par mois ;
- Rémunération brute annuelle minimum de 43 K€ sur 12 mois, selon l’expérience, le profil et la grille de rémunération interne.
