jobs.title: Account Manager
jobs.body:
Overview of position

The Account Manager is responsible for the overall management and delivery of services to clients, ensuring CTG’s operations align with client requirements, contractual obligations, and financial goals. This role oversees the end-to-end management of assigned projects, including client engagement, scope management, compliance, and team supervision. As the primary point of contact for clients, the Account Manager is accountable for resolving issues and ensuring that recruitment, onboarding, payroll, consultant contract issuance, and reporting processes are executed efficiently and within agreed timelines. They balance client expectations with CTG’s operational and financial interests.

Role objectives

**Project Management**

- Lead initial client engagements, clearly articulating CTG’s services and project scope as per contract terms and conditions.
- Ensure alignment between the scope of work, client expectations, and CTG’s service delivery, proactively managing and agreeing on any adjustments.
- Act as the focal point for clients, maintaining strong relationships and addressing concerns promptly to ensure satisfaction and smooth project execution.
- Take ownership of issue resolution, ensuring timely and effective solutions related to service delivery, consultant performance, or client concerns.
- Monitor financial performance, ensuring proper management of costs, revenue, and resource allocation to maintain project profitability.
- Ensure the timely and accurate delivery of monthly reports to clients, covering key metrics such as headcount, payroll, DSA amounts, consultant activities, and financial status.
- Contribute to financial forecasting and planning for ongoing and future projects.

**Operations, Legal, and Compliance Management**

- Oversee recruitment, onboarding, payroll, and contract issuance processes for CTG consultants, ensuring efficiency and compliance with CTG policies and legal frameworks.
- Ensure all operations related to the project comply with CTG policies, local labor laws, and client requirements, including adherence to deadlines, quality standards, and financial controls.
- Support the timely and compliant onboarding of international consultants per contractual requirements.
- Ensure the accurate and timely issuance of consultant contracts, ensuring compliance with CTG policies, local labor laws, and client agreements.
- Provide regular operational and financial updates to internal stakeholders, including the Country Operations Manager and Regional Director, regarding the status of client accounts, project delivery, and financial performance.
- Proactively implement measures to prevent mismanagement of resources, client expectations, or deliverable
- Ensure strict compliance with CTG’s operational policies to mitigate legal and financial risks
- Obtain necessary approvals for any deviations from CTG’s standard operating procedures to prevent legal or financial repercussions.
- Notify in-country management of any client-recommended deviations from CTG’s processes.
- Report any fraudulent activities or irregularities to in-country management immediately.
- Maintain professional and official communication channels to avoid disputes with clients.
- Uphold CTG’s ethical standards, ensuring all interpersonal interactions remain professional, culturally sensitive, and aligned with CTG’s core values.
- Foster a respectful and inclusive work environment that acknowledges diverse cultural values and beliefs.
- Promote CTG’s values in all aspects of team operations and client interactions.

**Client Relationship and Communication**

- Serve as the primary liaison for clients, maintaining long-term relationships and addressing any concerns or issues that arise.
- Ensure clear and transparent communication with clients to build trust and maintain satisfaction.
- Take ownership of any challenges that arise in client relationships, whether related to service delivery or internal operations, and ensure appropriate solutions are implemented swiftly.
- Ensure that client expectations are met without compromising operational efficiency or profitability.

**Business Development Support**

- Support the establishment and growth of CTG's presence in Afghanistan by building and maintaining relationships with clients, partners, government counterparts, and other key stakeholders.
- Monitor the humanitarian and development landscape, identifying upcoming opportunities, market trends, and potential areas for CTG engagement, and share relevant intelligence with Country Management and the Business Development team.
- Contribute to business development efforts by providing local market knowledge, operational insights, staffing plans, and technical inputs for proposals, concept notes, and client presentations.
- Represent CTG at client meetings, coordination forums, and networking events to strengthen the organisation's visibility and develop strategic relationships.
- Support the mobilisation and operational planning of newly awarded projects, ensuring a smooth transition from business development to implementation.
- Work closely with Country Management and the Business Development team to support the successful establishment and expansion of CTG's operations in Afghanistan.

Project reporting

This position reports to Regional Operations Manager

Key competencies

- Outstanding people management skills and very familiar with delegation, performance management, and providing feedback and guidance to team members.
- Strong communication, problem-solving skills.
- Financial acumen, ideally with experience managing budgets and financial reporting.
- Proficiency in HR systems and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
- Strong attention to detail, especially in managing contracts, consultant data, and reporting.
- Proactive and results oriented.
- Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

Team management

This role does not have team management responsibilities.

Further information

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Coordonnateur·Trice de Projet
jobs.body:
**COORDONNATEUR·TRICE DE PROJET- RCEAM BÉNIN**

**RÉSUMÉ**

Sous la supervision du/de la Représentant(e) Pays et en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe programme de Catalyste+, le/la Coordonnateur·trice de Projet sera responsable de **coordonner et de soutenir la mise en œuvre efficace du projet** ***Renforcement des capacités d’exportation et de l’accès aux marchés des petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) béninoises (RCEAM-Bénin).***

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice assurera la planification, la coordination, le suivi de la mise en œuvre des activités du projet, en collaboration avec notre partenaire local, la Chambre de Commerce et d’Industrie du Bénin (CCI Bénin), les PME bénéficiaires, le/la conseiller.ère Catalyste+ et l'équipe projet de Catalyste+. Il/elle veillera au respect du plan de travail, des échéanciers, de la qualité des livrables, des objectifs du projet, et assurera la coordination des aspects opérationnels et logistiques nécessaires à la réalisation des activités.

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice sera également responsable du **suivi des résultats et de l’impact du projet**, notamment de la collecte, de la validation et de l’analyse des données relatives aux activités et aux indicateurs de performance. Il/elle contribuera à la documentation des résultats, des bonnes pratiques et des leçons apprises, ainsi qu’à la préparation des rapports d'activités et financiers destinés à Catalyste+ et aux bailleurs de fonds.

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice travaillera en étroite collaboration avec les différentes parties prenantes afin de **garantir la bonne mise en œuvre des activités et de contribuer à l’atteinte des résultats du projet**, dans le respect des politiques, procédures et normes de Catalyste+.

**Lieu d’affectation**

Le/la Coordonnateur·trice de Projet doit être basé(e) à **Cotonou, au Bénin,** et être disponible pour assurer une présence régulière auprès de la CCI Bénin et des autres parties prenantes du projet.

**Durée du contrat**

Il s’agit d’un contrat à durée déterminée jusqu’au 31 mars 2027.

**RESPONSABILITÉS PRINCIPALES**

**Gestion et coordination de la mise en œuvre du projet**

- Coordonner la planification, l’organisation et la mise en œuvre des activités du projet en collaboration avec la CCI Bénin, l'équipe projet et les autres partenaires concernés.
- Assurer le suivi du plan de travail et des échéanciers du projet, et identifier rapidement tout retard, risque, enjeu ou écart par rapport aux objectifs établis, en proposant des mesures correctives au besoin.
- Coordonner les aspects opérationnels et logistiques liés aux formations, ateliers, missions du/de la conseiller.ère et autres activités prévues dans le cadre du projet.
- Assurer la liaison et la coordination avec la CCI Bénin, les PME bénéficiaires, le/la conseiller.ère de Catalyste+, l'équipe projet et les autres parties prenantes du projet.
- Coordonner la préparation et le suivi des réunions de projet, avec les partenaires, l'équipe projet et le bailleur de fonds au besoin.
- Suivre l’avancement global de la mise en œuvre du projet et assurer la circulation de l’information pertinente entre les différentes parties prenantes.
- Contribuer à la préparation des rapports d'activités et financiers destinés à Catalyste+ et aux bailleurs de fonds.
- Participer au suivi administratif et financier du projet, notamment en contribuant au suivi des dépenses, à la planification budgétaire et à l’identification des écarts nécessitant une attention de la direction.

**Suivi des résultats, collecte et gestion des données**

- Assurer la collecte et la compilation des données nécessaires au suivi des activités et des résultats du projet.
- En collaboration avec l’équipe du projet, valider les méthodes et outils de collecte des données.
- Veiller à ce que les données collectées soient complètes, fiables et alignées avec les indicateurs et cibles établis dans le cadre du suivi et de l’évaluation.
- Suivre régulièrement les progrès du projet par rapport aux résultats et indicateurs prévus et signaler tout écart ou enjeu nécessitant un ajustement.
- Assurer le suivi de la qualité des résultats auprès des 30 membres du personnel de la CCI Bénin, des 10 formateurs et des 50 PME bénéficiaires.
- Contribuer à la préparation des données et informations requises pour les rapports de suivi et de performance du projet.

**Communications, visibilité et apprentissage**

- Contribuer à la mise en œuvre du plan de communication et de visibilité du projet, en collaboration avec l’équipe de Catalyste+ et les partenaires.
- Identifier et documenter les résultats, histoires de succès, témoignages et autres contenus pouvant être valorisés dans les communications du projet.
- Coordonner les activités de communication et de visibilité du projet, notamment la liaison avec les médias locaux, la couverture médiatique et la diffusion des résultats à travers les réseaux sociaux et les canaux des partenaires.
- Veiller au respect des exigences de visibilité de Catalyste+ et des bailleurs de fonds.

**Administration, conformité et soutien au projet**

- Veiller à la confidentialité et à la protection des données, conformément aux politiques et procédures de Catalyste+.
- Veiller au respect des procédures administratives, financières et opérationnelles applicables au projet.
- Appuyer la préparation et le suivi des documents administratifs et financiers nécessaires à la mise en œuvre des activités.
- Effectuer toute autre tâche pertinente confiée par la direction afin de soutenir la bonne mise en œuvre et l’atteinte des résultats du projet.

**CONNAISSANCES, COMPÉTENCES ET EXPÉRIENCE REQUISES**

**Formation et expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en administration des affaires, gestion de projet, développement international, économie, commerce international, gestion des entreprises ou dans une discipline connexe, et/ou au moins trois (3) ans d’expérience pertinente dans un poste de coordination de projet ou dans un rôle similaire.
- Expérience démontrée en coordination et mise en œuvre de projets, idéalement dans le domaine du développement international, du développement du secteur privé, du développement des PME, du commerce ou du renforcement institutionnel.
- Expérience de travail avec des entreprises, associations professionnelles, chambres de commerce, institutions publiques, organismes de développement ou partenaires internationaux constitue un atout important.
- Expérience dans la coordination de formations, ateliers, missions, activités de renforcement des capacités ou autres activités impliquant plusieurs parties prenantes.

**Connaissances techniques**

- Bonne compréhension des enjeux liés au développement international, notamment le développement du secteur privé, les chaînes de valeur, le commerce, la gouvernance, l’environnement et les changements climatiques, ainsi que l’égalité des genres et l’autonomisation économique des femmes (EG/AEF).
- Bonne compréhension des principes de gestion axée sur les résultats (RBM), notamment la définition et le suivi des indicateurs, la collecte et la validation des données, la documentation des résultats et l’identification des écarts par rapport aux cibles.
- Connaissance des principes de suivi-évaluation et de gestion de données appliqués aux projets de développement.
- Connaissance des principes de gestion budgétaire, de suivi des dépenses, de conformité administrative et de reddition de comptes constitue un atout.

**Compétences en gestion de projet et de suivi des résultats et gestion des données**

- Excellentes capacités de planification, coordination et organisation permettant de gérer plusieurs activités et échéanciers simultanément.
- Capacité à assurer un suivi rigoureux des livrables et à veiller à leur qualité et à leur conformité aux attentes du projet.
- Capacité à anticiper les besoins opérationnels et logistiques et à résoudre rapidement les problèmes rencontrés lors de la mise en œuvre.
- Capacité à collecter, compiler, vérifier, analyser et présenter des données liées aux activités et aux résultats du projet.
- Capacité à suivre les progrès d’un projet par rapport aux résultats, indicateurs et cibles établis.
- Capacité à documenter les résultats, bonnes pratiques, leçons apprises, histoires de succès et changements observés auprès des PME bénéficiaires.

**Communication, relations avec les parties prenantes et visibilité**

- Excellentes aptitudes interpersonnelles et relationnelles, avec la capacité de travailler efficacement avec des interlocuteurs de différents niveaux et de différents milieux professionnels.
- Excellentes capacités de communication orale et écrite, notamment pour préparer des rapports, comptes rendus, présentations, notes de suivi et autres documents professionnels.
- Excellente capacité à établir et maintenir des relations de travail constructives avec les partenaires locaux et internationaux.
- Sensibilité culturelle et capacité à traiter des questions délicates avec tact, diplomatie et discernement.
- Bonne compréhension des principes de communication et de visibilité liés aux projets de développement international.
- Capacité à coordonner des activités de communication avec les partenaires, médias et autres intervenants.
- Bonne compréhension des principes de visibilité et de reconnaissance des bailleurs de fonds.

**Utilisation d’outils et langue**

- Capacité à utiliser les réseaux sociaux et les outils numériques pour contribuer à la diffusion des résultats du projet constitue un atout.
- Excellente maîtrise de Microsoft Office, notamment Word, Excel, PowerPoint et Outlook.
- Excellente maîtrise du français, à l’oral comme à l’écrit.

**Date limite de candidature : 10.22.2026**

Catalyste+ est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. Nous remercions tous les candidats de leur intérêt, mais seuls ceux retenus pour un entretien seront contactés.

jobs.title: Appel à propositions pour la mise en œuvre d’une enquête de couverture dénommée « PECS », après les activités de routinisation de la supplémentation e
jobs.body:
Guidée par l'héritage remarquable de sa cofondatrice, Helen Keller, Helen Keller Intl s'associe à des communautés qui s'efforcent de surmonter les cycles de pauvreté de longue date. En fournissant les éléments essentiels d'une bonne santé, d'une bonne nutrition et d'une vision claire, nous aidons des millions de personnes à créer un changement durable dans leur propre vie. Travaillant dans plus de 20 pays – à travers l'Afrique, l'Asie, l'Europe et les États-Unis – et avec une communauté mondiale de sympathisants, nous veillons à ce que chaque personne ait la possibilité – comme Helen l'a fait – d'atteindre son véritable potentiel.

Helen Keller Intl soutient la supplémentation en vitamine A de 40 millions d'enfants chaque année dans 14 pays d'Afrique subsaharienne. Lorsqu'elle est administrée deux fois par an à au moins 80% des enfants âgés de 6 à 59 mois dans les pays où la mortalité des enfants de moins de cinq ans est élevée et où les taux de carence en vitamine A sont élevés, la supplémentation en vitamine A peut contribuer à réduire la mortalité infantile jusqu'à 24%.

A Madagascar, Helen Keller Intl appuie techniquement et financièrement le Ministère de la Santé Publique pour la prestation de Supplémentation en Vitamine A (SVA) dans 08 régions à savoir Menabe, Ihorombe, Betsiboka, Boeny, Sofia, Melaky, DIANA et SAVA par le biais de l’activité de routine.

Afin d'évaluer le nombre d'enfants touchés par ces distributions en mode routine, Helen Keller Intl mène des enquêtes transversales auprès des ménages en suivant la méthodologie développée par l'OMS pour mesurer la couverture de la SVA.

Nous sommes actuellement à la recherche d'un cabinet de consultance pour accompagner les équipes de Helen Keller Intl dans le pays afin de mener une enquête de couverture prévue en janvier 2027 et qui évaluera la couverture du second semestre de 2026. Elle concernera une strate qui sera composée des huit (08) régions soutenues par Helen Keller International, dont la liste est la suivante : DIANA, SAVA, SOFIA, BOENY, BETSIBOKA, MELAKY, IHOROMBE, MENABE

Le cabinet sera responsable de la préparation de l'enquête, y compris l'adaptation des protocoles et des outils, la soumission des protocoles et des outils au comité d'éthique, le recrutement et la formation des enquêteurs ainsi que la supervision de la collecte de données sur le terrain, l'analyse des données et la production de rapports.

jobs.title: AI Platform Engineer
jobs.body:
**Job Background / Overview**

The IRC is actively investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As the organization expands its use of AI platforms, including tools from Anthropic, OpenAI, and integrated data environments, the IT department is building dedicated technical capacity to keep these systems running reliably, securely, and effectively.

The IRC is investing in enterprise AI to improve the speed, quality, and scale of its programs and operations. As that investment grows, so does the need for someone to own the technical layer underneath it: the systems, integrations, and infrastructure that make AI tools work at scale.

The AI Platform Engineer is that person. This is a technical operations role, not a user-facing one. This role is responsible for keeping the IRC's enterprise AI environment running managing platform configurations and API access, building and maintaining integrations between AI tools and IRC systems, writing scripts and automations, and serving as the technical point of contact for data engineering and InfoSec. Day-to-day, this person is more likely to be reading logs, troubleshooting a broken pipeline, or pushing a configuration change than answering questions from end users.

The role works in close coordination with the AI Platform Support Director, who owns vendor relationships, licensing, and adoption strategy. This role owns the technical execution underneath that, ensuring the systems are reliable, observable, and properly connected to the rest of the IRC's data and operational environment.

**Major Responsibilities**

**AI Systems Administration & Operations (40%)**

- Serve as primary technical administrator across IRC enterprise AI environments, currently including Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI platform deployments
- Manage user access, API key governance, workspace configurations, and environment-level settings across AI platforms
- Monitor system health, usage patterns, and API performance across AI tools; triage and resolve operational issues as they arise
- Maintain and improve observability across AI systems
- Tracking uptime, error rates, token consumption, and integration reliability
- Oversee and document configuration changes, environment updates, and deployment procedures across managed platforms
- Support responsible use by flagging anomalous usage patterns and coordinating with InfoSec on policy adherence and access controls

**Integrations & Technical Implementation (35%)**

- Coordinate with the DevOps, SW Engineering and Data Engineering team(s) on deployment processes, environment access, and infrastructure dependencies required to build and maintain AI integrations
- Follow established change management procedures for all configuration changes, environment updates, and integration deployments, including documentation, testing, and appropriate approvals before pushing to production
- Develop lightweight scripts, connectors, and automations to support AI-assisted workflows across teams, primarily in Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript
- Troubleshoot integration failures, data flow issues, and API connectivity problems across the AI ecosystem
- Collaborate with the data engineering team on AI/KM pipeline work, including vector store ingestion, retrieval configuration, and source data connections
- Contribute to technical design discussions with engineering partners, translating operational requirements into implementable solutions
- Maintain technical documentation for all integrations, including architecture notes, runbooks, and dependency maps

**Monitoring, Resource Optimization & InfoSec Liaison (15%)**

- Track and report on AI resource utilization across platforms, identifying opportunities to reduce waste and improve cost efficiency in coordination with the AI
- Serve as the technical point of contact with the InfoSec team on matters related to AI system security, data handling, access controls, and compliance requirements
- Support risk assessments and security reviews for new AI tools or integrations by providing accurate technical context on system behavior and data flows
- Contribute to the development of technical SOPs and best-practice guidelines for AI system use, in coordination with the AI Platform Support Director and relevant stakeholders

**Stakeholder Support & Collaboration (10%)**

- Act as a technical resource for program and operations teams adopting AI tools, including answering implementation questions, supporting troubleshooting, and identifying configuration solutions
- Participate in rollout planning for new AI capabilities, providing grounded input on technical feasibility, integration requirements, and operational readiness
- Collaborate with the AI Platform Support Director on onboarding documentation and technical guidance materials for end users
- Contribute to sprint and project planning with accurate estimates on technical effort and dependencies

**Required Experience & Skills**

**AI & Cloud Platforms**

- Hands-on experience administering enterprise AI platforms (Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, or comparable tools), including API management, access controls, and environment configuration
- Familiarity with LLM application infrastructure: prompt pipelines, Model Context Protocol (MCP), other tool-calling integration frameworks, vector databases, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns, and embedding workflows
- Experience working with Databricks or comparable data/ML platforms is a strong plus

**Integration & Development**

- Proficiency in Python and/or JavaScript for scripting, automation, and lightweight integration work
- Experience building and maintaining REST API integrations, including authentication patterns, webhook handling, and error management
- Comfort reading and working within existing codebases without requiring significant architectural guidance
- Familiarity with version control (Git) and standard deployment practices for scripts and integrations

**Systems Administration & Monitoring**

- Experience monitoring distributed systems or SaaS platforms, including setting up alerting, reviewing logs, and diagnosing performance or availability issues
- Familiarity with usage/cost monitoring for cloud or API-based services
- Comfort operating in live production environments where reliability and data integrity are critical

**Security & Compliance**

- Working knowledge of information security principles as they apply to SaaS and API-based systems: access controls, credential management, data handling, and audit logging
- Ability to engage constructively with InfoSec teams, providing clear technical context to support reviews and risk assessments

**Collaboration & Communication**

- Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical colleagues and program staff
- Experience contributing to cross-functional teams alongside product, engineering, and operations stakeholders
- Strong documentation habits: runbooks, SOPs, architecture notes, and internal guides

**Working Environment**

This role is remote, with the possibility of in-person work depending on location. Stakeholders are located across multiple time zones (GMT-8 to GMT+3), which may require occasional early or late meetings.

**Compensation:** ($88,277 - $102,451 pay range annual). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Project Director (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health Limited](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Reports to:** Chief Executive Officer

**Expected Project Start:** 1 January 2027

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced Project Director to provide strategic and operational leadership for a prospective donor-funded, multi-country project expected to commence on **1 January 2027.**

The project will focus on improving access to quality-assured maternal and newborn health (MNH) products through country-led interventions addressing systemic barriers across policy and guidelines, forecasting and quantification, financing, procurement, regulation, supply and distribution.

The Project Director will translate the approved project strategy into measurable results across participating countries, providing overall oversight of implementation, government ownership, consortium and partner coordination, financial and operational stewardship, donor compliance, risk management, quality, learning and sustainability. The role will also serve as a senior representative of inSupply Health, engaging with donors, governments, consortium partners, technical teams, communities and other strategic stakeholders.

**Important:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the selection process.

**Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership & Project Governance**

- Provide overall strategic leadership and direction for the project.
- Translate project objectives and contractual commitments into clear priorities, implementation approaches and measurable results.
- Establish effective governance, accountability, decision-making and performance management mechanisms.
- Provide strategic oversight across participating countries while ensuring interventions are adapted to country contexts and priorities.
- Champion equity, innovation, sustainability, local ownership and value for money.

**Country Implementation & Project Delivery**

- Provide strategic oversight of project start-up, country planning and implementation.
- Ensure country teams translate project strategy into realistic, prioritised and measurable implementation plans.
- Oversee delivery of agreed milestones, outputs and outcomes within approved timelines, resources and quality standards.
- Ensure effective coordination across country, technical, operational and functional teams.
- Lead timely corrective and adaptive action where implementation deviates from approved plans or expected results.

**Government, Consortium & Strategic Partnerships**

- Serve as the senior project representative with donors, governments, consortium partners and other strategic stakeholders.
- Build and maintain effective relationships with government ministries, procurement agencies, regulatory bodies, financing institutions and other national stakeholders.
- Promote government leadership, ownership and sustainability.
- Lead effective coordination across consortium partners, ensuring clear roles, accountabilities and delivery expectations.
- Represent inSupply Health in relevant national, regional and international forums.

**Financial & Resource Stewardship**

- Provide overall accountability for effective stewardship of project resources.
- Ensure resources are strategically allocated across countries, interventions and activities to maximise results and value for money.
- Review financial performance, forecasts, expenditure and material variances and ensure timely corrective action.
- Work closely with Finance and Operations leadership to ensure effective financial controls, forecasting, budget management and donor reporting.
- Ensure personnel, consultants and other project resources are appropriately planned and deployed.

**People Leadership & Project Capability**

- Lead multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive and accountable environment.
- Establish clear performance expectations, decision rights and accountability across the project leadership structure.
- Guide, coach and support Project Managers, technical leads and other project leaders.
- Ensure the project has the skills, capacity and leadership capability required to deliver its objectives.
- Promote staff engagement, wellbeing, safeguarding, inclusion and organisational values.

**Quality, Compliance, Risk & Safeguarding**

- Provide oversight of compliance with donor agreements, contractual obligations, applicable laws and organisational policies.
- Oversee strategic, financial, operational, implementation, safeguarding and reputational risks.
- Ensure high and critical risks have clear owners, mitigation measures and escalation pathways.
- Ensure material compliance issues, audit findings and management actions are addressed within agreed timelines.
- Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, ethical conduct and safeguarding.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning & Evidence**

- Provide strategic oversight of monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting systems.
- Ensure reliable data and evidence inform strategic decisions, adaptive management and resource allocation.
- Monitor progress towards improvements in MNH product access, including on-shelf availability of selected tracer products.
- Lead cross-country learning and knowledge exchange.
- Promote documentation and dissemination of evidence, innovations and good practices to support replication and scale-up.

**Sustainability, Scale & Project Development**

- Provide strategic leadership for project sustainability, institutionalisation, scale-up and transition.
- Strengthen local systems, government ownership and institutional capacity to sustain results beyond the project period.
- Identify opportunities to leverage complementary investments, partnerships and financing.
- Provide senior-level input into proposals, concept notes, project extensions, partnerships and resource mobilisation opportunities.

**Project Reporting, Communication & Close-Out**

- Ensure accurate, timely and high-quality donor, technical, financial and management reports.
- Communicate project performance, achievements, financial status, risks, challenges and opportunities to senior management, donors and stakeholders.
- Lead periodic project performance reviews and ensure agreed actions are followed through.
- Provide strategic oversight of project close-out and transition planning.
- Ensure final evaluations, reports, knowledge products, stakeholder handovers and sustainability or transition plans are completed to the required standards.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Academic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree in Project Management, Business Administration, Public Health, Development Studies, International Development, Supply Chain, Economics or a related field.
- A Master's degree in a relevant discipline is **mandatory.**

## **Professional Qualifications**

- Membership in a relevant professional body, such as PMI or an equivalent recognised professional association.
- Professional certification in Project or Programme Management, such as **PMP, PRINCE2** or an equivalent internationally recognised qualification, is highly desirable.
- Additional certification in Monitoring & Evaluation, Results-Based Management, Risk Management, Agile Project Management or another relevant discipline is an advantage.

**Professional Experience**

- At least **12 years** of progressively responsible experience in global health, international development, health systems strengthening, health supply chains or a related field, including substantial senior project or programme leadership experience.
- Demonstrated experience providing strategic leadership for complex, multi-country, donor-funded projects, with accountability for strategy, implementation, budgets, teams, partnerships, compliance and results.
- Experience working with government institutions and public-sector health systems, preferably across multiple countries and operating contexts.
- Strong understanding of health systems and supply-chain ecosystems, including systemic barriers related to access, financing, procurement, policy, data, regulation or service delivery.
- Proven experience leading multi-partner or consortium-based projects.
- Demonstrated experience engaging and influencing donors, government institutions, implementing partners and senior stakeholders.
- Experience leading multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams.
- Experience overseeing workplans, budgets, forecasts, risks, contractual deliverables and performance frameworks.
- Demonstrated experience in monitoring, evaluation, learning, evidence generation and adaptive project management.
- Experience in maternal and newborn health, health products, pharmaceutical or medical supply chains, procurement, market shaping or related areas is highly desirable.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a leader who demonstrates:

- Strategic & Systems Thinking
- Multi-Country & Consortium Leadership
- Government & Stakeholder Engagement
- Results & Adaptive Management
- People & Resource Leadership
- Risk, Integrity & Accountability

jobs.title: Deputy Finance Director (Kenya Nationals Only)
jobs.body:
**Location:** Nairobi, Kenya

**Employment Type:** Full-time

**Company/Division:** [inSupply Health Limited](https://insupplyhealth.com/)

**Reports to:** Project Director

**Functional Relationship:** Finance Director

**Expected Project Start:** 1 January 2027

**Organization Overview:**

inSupply Health is an East African health advisory firm that designs people-centered, scalable, sustainable supply chain solutions. We focus on optimizing data visibility and use, workforce development, and continuous performance improvement. inSupply operates as a social enterprise, aiming to achieve business sustainability while advancing our social mission. We aim to transition short-term supply chain fixes into sustainable solutions that transcend specific projects or funding streams. Our work focuses on democratizing access to quality, affordable, and context-specific supply chain learning and innovations so that local and regional supply chain actors can improve the performance and efficiency of their supply chains and health systems, towards better health outcomes.

inSupply Health is headquartered in Nairobi, with offices in Dar es Salaam and across East Africa, and is affiliated with JSI Research & Training Institute, Inc. (JSI). We collaborate closely with public and private-sector clients to design optimized, responsive, and resilient supply chain systems. Our dynamic team of local consultants delivers critical services supporting essential health products, adapting proven methodologies to local contexts for long-term impact.

**Job Summary**

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced **Deputy Finance Director** to provide senior financial and operational leadership to the Project Management Unit (PMU) for a prospective donor-funded project expected to commence on **1 January 2027**.

The role will provide financial and operational oversight across multiple countries, consortium members and implementation partners, ensuring effective stewardship of project resources, sound financial management, donor compliance and timely financial decision-making.

The Deputy Finance Director will work closely with the Project Director, Finance Director, country and technical teams, consortium partners and other stakeholders to translate project priorities into practical financial and operational plans and provide financial analysis and insights to support effective project delivery.

**Important:** Appointment to this position is contingent upon the project being awarded and the position being confirmed in the final project staffing plan. Further details about the project and donor will be shared with candidates who reach the final stages of the selection process.

**Responsibilities:**

## **1. Financial Leadership & Performance Management**

- Provide day-to-day financial leadership and oversight across participating countries and implementation areas.
- Monitor project financial performance and provide timely financial advice and analysis.
- Promote accountability, financial discipline, value for money and responsible resource utilisation.

## **2. Budgeting, Forecasting & Cost Management**

- Lead preparation, consolidation and review of annual and multi-year project budgets.
- Coordinate budget revisions, forecasts and financial projections across countries and project components.
- Monitor expenditure, commitments, burn rates and budget variances.
- Advise project leadership on the financial implications of implementation and resource decisions.

## **3. Financial Reporting & Analysis**

- Lead the preparation and review of accurate and timely financial reports and management information.
- Provide financial analysis and insights to support project performance and decision-making.

## **4. Grant, Contract & Partner Financial Management**

- Ensure compliance with donor requirements, grant agreements, contracts and organisational policies.
- Oversee financial aspects of consortium partners, subrecipients and implementing partners.
- **Identify financial risks and coordinate corrective actions and capacity strengthening.**

## **5. Financial Controls, Compliance & Risk Management**

- Implement and monitor effective financial controls and ensure compliance with delegated authorities and financial procedures.
- Identify control weaknesses and ensure corrective actions are implemented.
- Maintain oversight of project-level financial risks and ensure appropriate escalation.
- Ensure financial records and supporting documentation meet donor, statutory and organisational requirements.

## **6. Audit & Donor Compliance**

- Coordinate financial aspects of internal, external, donor and project audits.
- Monitor donor financial conditions and reporting requirements.
- Track audit findings and coordinate corrective actions.
- Escalate material compliance concerns and financial risks.

## **7. Cash Flow, Treasury & Financial Operations**

- Monitor cash requirements, liquidity, commitments and short-term funding needs.
- Prepare and review cash-flow forecasts.
- Coordinate funding requests, transfers and other financial requirements.
- Work with the broader Finance function on banking, payments, reconciliations and treasury processes.

## **8. Project Operations & Resource Coordination**

- Provide financial and operational input into project planning and resource allocation.
- Coordinate with Finance, Procurement, HR, Grants, Administration and other shared services.
- Identify and address operational bottlenecks affecting project delivery.
- Support project mobilisation, expansion and close-out from a finance and operations perspective.

## **9. Financial Systems & Process Improvement**

- Ensure effective use of inSupply's ERP and financial management systems.
- Identify opportunities to automate, streamline and improve financial and operational workflows.
- Support system enhancements, integrations and reporting tools.
- Strengthen the integrity and consistency of financial data.

## **10. Team Leadership & Strategic Finance Partnership**

- Provide leadership, coaching and technical guidance to finance and operations staff supporting the project.
- Build financial management capacity among non-finance project staff.
- Serve as a strategic finance partner to the Project Director and PMU leadership.
- Provide financial recommendations to support project strategy, planning, resource allocation and implementation decisions.
- Deputise for the designated finance lead on project matters when required.

**Qualifications & Experience**

## **Academic Qualifications**

## **Professional Qualifications**

- Qualified accountant with active membership in a recognised professional accounting body, such as ICPAK, ACCA or equivalent, and in good standing.

**Professional Experience**

- At least **12 years** of progressive experience in finance and financial management, preferably within international development, consulting, non-profit or project-based environments.

## **Key Competencies**

We are looking for a leader who demonstrates:

jobs.body:

✅ Experience with assessment, compliance or organisational-development systems

? Experience with international NGOs, humanitarian/development organisations, multilingual platforms, safeguarding information systems or Caritas/faith-based networks is an asset.

**? Timeline**

?️ **Digitisation:** October 2026 – December 2027  
?️**Maintenance & technical support:** December 2027 – November 2029

Interested consultants/consultancy firms are invited to submit:

? **Technical proposal**

jobs.title: Development of E-Learning Module Content — Tdh Migration and Displacement programme
jobs.body:
## **1. Background**

Terre des hommes (Tdh) is Switzerland's largest child rights organisation, active in over 30 countries. Its Migration and Displacement sector has developed two evidence-based Models of Action (MoA) to guide Tdh staff and partners working with migrant, displaced and at-risk children and youth:

**MoA 1 — Employability and access to employment for young migrants and refugees:** Employability and access to employment through (1) Skills and capabilities development, (2) Labour market linkage, and (3) Policy and system strengthening.

**MoA 2 — Education for children and youth on the move:** Structured around the 4As (Availability, Accessibility, Acceptability, Adaptability), leading to empowerment and socio-economic (re)integration.

Tdh wishes to make these frameworks accessible to its staff and implementing partners through the **development of related self-paced e-learning modules**. Tdh already runs a Migration and Displacement e-learning course for staff: the two new modules will be produced in the same format and uploaded to the existing platform by Tdh. This assignment covers content development only as platform integration is handled internally.

## **2. Objective and scope of work**

The consultant will develop content for two standalone e-learning modules, one for each MoA. The modules are intended for individual, self-paced learners. For each module, the consultant will submit a complete Word script that Tdh's technical team can upload to the existing CYM e-learning platform. The assignment does not include visual design, coding, platform configuration or upload work

**2.1 Consultant deliverables**

For each of the two modules, the consultant will deliver the following:

- Full content script (Word document): A complete, structured module script covering all learning content, activities and resources. The script must follow the format of the existing Tdh Migration and Development module series and be clear enough for Tdh's technical team to translate it into the online platform. It must include section text, activity instructions, external resource links with precise timecodes where relevant, correct answers for exercises, definitions and call-out boxes. It must be sufficiently clear and structured for the technical team to identify content blocks, activity types, correct answers, feedback text and any resources to be embedded or linked.
- Glossary: A list of 10-15 key terms with concise, learner-friendly definitions tailored to the thematic focus of the module.
- Learner summary sheet: A one-page printable reference sheet summarising the module's key concepts and takeaways, suitable for download alongside the module.
- Review and revision: The consultant will take part in an iterative review process, incorporate consolidated feedback from Tdh and submit revised versions until the module content is validated within the agreed workplan and timeline.

**2.2 Module format, components and minimum requirements**

Existing Migration and Development module scripts will be shared with the selected consultant as a formatting and style reference at the start of the assignment. Each module should follow the expected approach and minimum requirements below.

**Component**

1. Learner experience. **Expected approach:** Individual, self-paced learning. Content should be structured into short thematic sections that combine explanation, examples and activities. **Minimum requirement per module:** 45–60 minutes of learning time.
2. Narrative and voice. **Expected approach:** Write directly to the individual learner in the second person, using a clear and accessible register suitable for practitioners with varied educational backgrounds and operating contexts. **Minimum requirement per module** : Consistent second-person learner voice throughout the script.
3. Script length.**Expected approach :** Provide enough detail for direct platform integration, including all section text, activity instructions, answer keys and feedback text. **Minimum requirement per module** 2,500–4,000 words, including activity instructions and answers.
4. External resources. **Expected approach :** Curate publicly accessible, up-to-date and directly relevant resources, such as short videos, interactive data tools, websites, maps, reports or other practical materials. For any video used, provide precise start and end timecodes.**Minimum requirement per module** : Relevant external resources selected according to the learning objectives and availability of suitable materials. Each resource must include guided comprehension questions and correct answers where appropriate.
5. Interactive activities.**Expected approach :** Embed activities throughout the script and describe them clearly for platform build. Suitable formats include flip cards, matching or association exercises, multiple-choice questions, fill-in-the-blank questions and open reflection prompts. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 interactive activities, plus at least 1 open reflection prompt. Correct answers and short feedback text must be provided where relevant.
6. Case studies.**Expected approach :** Use real-world or fictionalised case studies grounded in Tdh field contexts, including Asia, Africa and Europe/MENA where relevant. Cases should include named fictional or anonymised characters and guided analysis questions. **Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.
7. Glossary and key concepts. **Expected approach :** Define core terms in concise, learner-friendly language and use call-out boxes to reinforce critical concepts, legal definitions, common misconceptions and section takeaways.**Minimum requirement per module** : At least 2 case studies, each with analysis questions and model answers.

## **3. Required profile**

## **Mandatory**

- Demonstrated experience writing e-learning content scripts or instructional materials for NGO or UN audiences
- Strong ability to translate programmatic frameworks into clear, engaging learning content for individual practitioners
- Capacity to identify and integrate high-quality external resources (videos, data tools, reports) into a structured learning narrative
- Substantive knowledge in at least one of the two thematic areas: youth employability, education in emergencies / migration
- Excellent written English; ability to write in a direct, accessible register suitable for diverse field staff

### **Advantageous**

- Familiarity with child rights frameworks and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child
- Knowledge of all two thematic areas covered by the MoAs

jobs.title: Regional Coordinator – Middle East (M/F) - 4 Months
jobs.body:
HAMAP-Humanitaire is seeking for an interim Middle East Regional Coordinator to replace our collaborator for a period of 4 months, based in Lebanon with potential trips to Iraq, Syria and Jordan.

**Introduction to HAMAP-Humanitaire**

Founded in 1999, HAMAP-Humanitaire is a non-governmental organisation (NGO) dedicated to development aid. Its mission is to take concrete action to ensure that ever more men, women and children have access to safe drinking water and sanitation, education, healthcare and security. Its objective is to support and strengthen its local partners from the initial identification of needs right through to the implementation and sustainability of their projects. HAMAP-Humanitaire’s work focuses on two main areas of activity: water and sanitation engineering and hygiene, and Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA).

**Mine Action:**

HAMAP, which later became HAMAP-Humanitaire, originally stood for ‘Halte Aux Mines Anti-Personnel’ (Stop Anti-Personnel Mines). Mine action is therefore the organisation’s original purpose. Various training and awareness-raising projects on the risks posed by landmines have been carried out in Mauritania, Senegal and Benin in the past. HAMAP-Humanitaire is currently active in mine clearance, risk education and advocacy in the Middle East and Ukraine.

**HAMAP in Middle East:**

HAMAP currently has 3 simultaneous projects in Lebanon working alongside with the LMAC, Beatoona and the University of Balamand, under French, Belgian and German MoFA funds. In Syria HAMAP is working with Safe Land for a one year project funded by French government. The Regional Coordinator is responsible for monitoring programmes and project activities, liaising with partners and maintaining relations with HQ.

**JOB MISSION:**

Under the supervision of the Head of the HMA Division, the Regional Coordinator establishes the operational and strategic framework for the Middle East region by analysing the humanitarian, security, political and social situation. He or she is responsible for the growth of the HMA sector, provides support to country teams, oversees the coherence of support functions and drives the localisation agenda. The role **involves structuring, harmonising and developing the programmatic, operational, security and partnership frameworks** for missions in the Middle East.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1) Management, HR and Team Cohesion (25%)**

- **Support for Coordinators**: Support Syria Country Coordinator and the regional team in their management and steering roles.
- **‘Problem-Solving**’: Acting as a ‘*problem solver*’ to propose viable solutions to operational, institutional and financial bottlenecks, or issues arising in partnership relationships.
- **Supporting innovation**: Working with technical leads and head office, identify and propose innovations for projects: digital awareness, integration of artificial intelligence, and others.
- **Team dynamics**: Ensure teams are well-led and cohesive by fostering a positive atmosphere amongst staff and maintaining a suitable working environment.
- **HR management**: Support the structuring of teams, clarify responsibilities, support recruitment and skills development processes, and contribute to resolving sensitive HR issues in collaboration with head office.

**2) Supervision of Support Functions (40%)**

- **Budgetary consistency**: Ensure the financial balance of the region and oversee the preparation of provisional budgets in line with funding strategies.
- **Monitoring and control**: Ensure budgets are adhered to, analyse variances and propose corrective measures to head office.
- **Logistical optimisation**: Ensure compliance with financial and procurement procedures and optimise the pooling of technical and material resources amongst the various offices in the region.
- **Internal structuring**: Lead the development and harmonisation of regional management tools: development plans, monitoring matrices, budgetary tools, reporting frameworks, document templates, internal procedures and coordination mechanisms.

**3) Security Management (25%)**

- **Security Validation**: Validate the security context analysis carried out by the field units and escalate critical alerts to head office; in tense situations, provide regular security analyses to HQ.
- **Crisis Management**: Activate a regional crisis unit and liaise with HQ in the event of a critical security incident.
- **Compliance**: Ensure that all teams within the regional area comply with security regulations.

**4) Development, Advocacy and Localisation (10%)**

- **Localisation Agenda**: Keep the issue of localisation at the top of the agenda (publications, workshops, training) and develop long-term partnerships with local NGOs.
- **Representation**: Enhance HAMAP’s sectoral legitimacy by participating in or leading working groups, regional clusters or sectorial events.
- **Donors**: Maintain good relations with our key donors and financial partners by regularly taking part in visits, targeted reporting or specific activities.
- **Lead the development of projects;** upon request, in the region in collaboration with the HMA and WASH divisions at head office. Identify potential donors, with a view to diversifying funding sources, and liaise with donors or their representatives in the region.
- **Communication**: Maintain HAMAP’s visibility to a high standard by adhering to the communication plans developed in each country, in consultation with HQ.

**DESIRED PROFILE**

**Education & Experience**

- **Education:** Master's degree in international relations, Humanitarian Action or Project Management, Development Studies, Political Science, or equivalent field experience
- **Experience:** Minimum 8 to 10+ years of progressive field-based experience with at least 3 to 5 years in senior management roles (Country Director, Deputy CD, Regional Coordinator) ;
- Experience in Humanitarian Mine Action and/or Armed Violence Reduction programming, familiar with integrated approaches (early recovery, basic services, WASH...)
- Confirmed operational experience in the **Middle East** (Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Jordan, Yemen) or comparable high-risk, fragmented political and security environments.
- Good practice in multi-country budget consolidation, financial forecasting, variance analysis (BVA), and cash-flow management. Direct oversight of field logistics and public procurement audits. Demonstrated track record managing institutional grants.

**Skills & Interpersonal Skills**

- Advanced budget design, cost-allocation frameworks, and donor compliance controls.
- High-level representation at mine action authorities, Protection/HMA clusters, and donor.
- **Technical:** Proficiency in the Project Cycle Management (PCM) framework, HMA standards and how donors operate.
- Capacity to untangle complex operational, regulatory, and financial bottlenecks calmly and methodically.
- Empathetic, clear-headed manager capable of fostering cross-cultural team cohesion and coaching senior managers remotely and in-person.
- **Languages:** Fluency in English is essential. Arabic and/or French are strong assets.
- **Personal Skills:** Ability to take decisions and lead in security-sensitive contexts, diplomacy, resilience under pressure and excellent interpersonal skills.

**Conditions:**

- 4 months, full time.
- Contract start date: 16/11/2026
- Remuneration according to profile;
- Hardship alllowance
- Perdiem
- Health and repatriation insurance – 100% covered by Hamap
- Paid leaves :2.08 day /Month
- RnR : 1.66 days/Month

jobs.title: Med Cell Support - Based in Nairobi (W/M)
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF operates through several operational directorates, each supported by main sections and offices worldwide. MSF OCP (Operational Centre Paris) is one of these directorates. Its operations are implemented by field and coordination teams and supported by Operational Cells based in Paris, Nairobi, Dakar, Dubai and Tokyo. Cell 6, also known as the Nairobi Cell, is based in Nairobi and holds the operational portfolio for the missions of South Sudan, Chad, Kenya and Sudan. The Cell is made up of; Cell Manager and Deputy Cell Managers (medical and operations), and key technical and support functions, Logistics, Finance, Human Resources, Supply and Communication.

**MISSION**

The objective of the Medical Manager is to work together with the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical in ensuring implementation of the medical-operational priorities of Cell 6, in line with the MSF OCP operational strategy, and to provide technical and strategic support to the mission teams.

S/he reports hierarchically and functionally to the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical, who provides support, guidance, supervision and development of professional competences.

When requested, s/he will cover for the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical during periods of leave, ensuring continuity of medical-operational decision-making and support to the cell and its missions.

This position is for the Cell 6 portfolio and is based in Nairobi.

S/he will take the lead on the day-to-day follow-up, technical and strategic support to the mission teams on topics including, but not limited to, pharmacy management and medical international order follow-up, health information systems/data analysis, staff health, Nursing and IPC (Infection Prevention and Control), Hospital management, patient safety and operational research in collaboration with the Epicentre focal point.

  
**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES AND TASKS:**

- Provide lead strategic and technical support, independently, to field teams on specific delegated dossiers, including Pharmacy management, medical international order follow-up, Nursing care, IPC, Patient Safety, Staff health, health information systems and hospital management; maintain overview of project implementation to ensure alignment with operational and medical department objectives.
- Support the implementation of medical strategies and policies within Cell 6, in line with the broad guidelines set out in MSF OCP's medical and operational strategic plan and contribute to the consistency of the medical aspects of projects, considering contextual constraints and realities. Actively participate and contribute in the preparation and discussions of key operational milestones such as the mid-year activity review, mise à plat, annual budget commissions.
- Support the missions with guidance and recommendations in defining annual medical supplies plans, estimating medical supplies budgets and related human resource needs, in close collaboration with supply and finance teams, and contribute to validating the annual medical supplies budget.
- Validate international medical orders and local purchases in line with organisational protocol, and ensure appropriate procurement, monitoring and management of medical supplies in the supported missions, in close collaboration with the relevant departments.
- Guarantee that emergency buffer stocks, HR in the missions are consistent with the Emergency Preparedness Plan (EPreP), in liaison with the Emergency cell focal point and other cell members.
- Follow up on health information system/data analysis, ensuring the quality of medical data for project interventions is regularly collected according to MSF standards, and that medical and pharmacy reporting from missions is timely and accurate.
- Analyse the fulfilment of medical objectives, indicators and hypotheses for the mission, and feed into medical-operational monitoring and analysis for the cell, preparation of quarterly and annual medical reports for the portfolio, including presentation of findings at cell level and other relevant platforms such as operations meetings as required.
- Supervise and support implementation of Staff Health Policies, medical evacuation guidelines and referral policies in the supported missions, ensuring the organisation's medical principles, guidelines and policies are respected.
- Act as a liaison between the field, the cell and the medical department, ensuring the organisation of work and dissemination of information in line with the specific issues and questions arising from the projects, and ensuring that agreed solutions are properly implemented in the field.
- Consult, collaborate and actively spar with other cell members on priority dossiers under your lead and other crosscutting medico-operational topics as needed.
- Provide functional support and guidance to Medical Coordinators in the supported missions, in close collaboration with the Deputy Cell Manager – Medical.
- Propose/develop and monitor the cell's operational research opportunities, and formulate epidemiological questions in conjunction with the EPICENTRE focal point
- Participate in technical briefings and debriefings within the cell, involving Technical Referents from the Medical and Supply departments when needed, and help identify individual training needs.
- Guarantee that medical teams and support department staff receive technical and methodological information through briefings and dedicated sessions; contribute to the design and delivery of relevant training and tools.
- Conduct periodic field visits and cover for MedCos as delegated and contribute to Cell 6's medical mission by remaining globally acquainted with the activities of all projects.

 **OTHERS:**

- Consult support services for sparring and as technical content providers when needed.
- Participate, and chair as requested, in meetings and activities organised by the cell and the medical department, contributing to regular and meaningful dialogue between departments in order to improve the support given to the field.
- Participate in relevant internal and external meetings.
- Perform any other related task as required.

**Profile desired:**

**Education and Training:** Qualified Medical Doctor, Clinical officer or Nurse.

**Experience:**

- 2 years of field experience with a medical NGO as a medical coordinator level is required. Previous experience in emergency interventions is an asset. MSF experience is an asset.
- Knowledge of pharmacy tools, International Medical Order procedures and medical data software (e.g. HMIS/DHIS2) is required.
- Strong project management and organisational skills, with good command of team management techniques and a good knowledge of MSF management and monitoring tools.
- Required qualities: ability to define medical and operational strategies suited to a variety of contexts; availability, adaptability and responsiveness in line with the constraints of humanitarian operations; strong teamwork and negotiation skills; and good analytical and summarising skills.

**Language:** French B2 and English B2 minimum are required.

**Status and Conditions:**

- Full-time position based in Nairobi, Kenya with international travel to MSF field missions.
- Fixed-term 2-year contract. Grade 10 Kenya salary scale.

**Position available:** 1st of December 2026

*Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.*

*A MSF, nous valorisons la diversité et cherchons à avoir un environnement de travail inclusif et accessible. Nous encourageons toutes les personnes qui possèdent les qualifications requises à postuler, indépendamment de leur origine ethnique, nationale ou culturelle, de leur âge, de leur sexe, de leur orientation sexuelle, de leurs convictions, de leur handicap ou d'autres aspects de leur identité.*

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 25 octobre 2026

jobs.title: Knowledge and Learning Manager
jobs.body:
**Program Background**

The Education Quality for Inclusive Prosperity (EQUIP) is a new Australian-funded program, implemented in the Philippines. EQUIP supports the Philippine Government’s efforts to strengthen senior secondary school education and ensure that senior secondary school learners have the skills to participate meaningfully in the labour force. EQUIP is a partnership between the Governments of Australia and the Philippines and will contribute to Philippine Government-led education reforms including the Philippine Department of Education (DepEd) 5-Point Reform Agenda which aims to harness the potential of young Filipinos.

EQUIP aims to support the Philippines’ inclusive economic growth ambitions by ensuring the labour force is well equipped with skills relevant to meet the needs of the country’s rapidly transforming economy. EQUIP aims to promote skills development in senior high school and enable a smooth transition to the labour force, whether immediately upon leaving school or after further education. It will also support Philippine Government agencies improve its policies and practices to support relevant skills pathways for senior secondary school learners.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [www.dt-global.com](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**The Role**

The Knowledge and Learning Manager is responsible for designing, implementing, and continuously improving the program's knowledge management and learning systems. The role will facilitate the generation, documentation, synthesis, sharing, and utilization of knowledge, evidence, innovations, and lessons learned across the program. Working closely with technical teams, MERL team, government counterparts, implementing partners, and other stakeholders, the Knowledge and Learning Manager will promote a culture of learning and adaptive management to enhance program effectiveness, influence policy and practice, and support sustainability of program results.

Key Responsibilities

- Develop and implement the program's Knowledge Management and Learning (KML) Strategy and Plan, establishing systems, processes, tools, and digital platforms to effectively capture, organize, store, retrieve, analyze and disseminate knowledge, evidence, and learning accessible across the program.
- Foster a culture of continuous learning, reflection, innovation, and adaptive management by facilitating learning reviews, pause-and-reflect sessions, after-action reviews, and other learning events that enable program teams to identify lessons learned, emerging challenges, and opportunities for improvement.
- Lead the development and quality assurance of the technical content and evidence base for knowledge products, including learning briefs, case studies, technical reports, policy briefs, research summaries, ensuring the systematic documentation of program achievements, innovations, and best practices. Promote evidence-based learning and knowledge utilization among stakeholders by identifying and synthesizing emerging trends, lessons, and best practices from program implementation and evaluation data, and translating these into actionable insights to inform program decision-making and adaptive management.
- Facilitate knowledge-sharing and collaborative learning among government agencies, the Department of Education (DepEd), schools, local government units, civil society organizations, private sector partners, development partners, and other stakeholders through communities of practice, learning forums, workshops, webinars, and other engagement platforms
- Collaborate with the MERL, communications and technical teams to prepare, package, and disseminate knowledge, research findings, lessons learned, and best practices through appropriate channels, while providing evidence, learning insights, and technical inputs for donor reports, technical publications, and external communications materials by the Communications team.
- Develop and implement capacity-building initiatives that strengthen knowledge management, documentation, learning, and adaptive programming practices, mentoring staff and partners in knowledge capture, evidence utilization, and organizational learning to enhance program effectiveness and impact.
- Work with EQUIP technical teams, MERL, DepEd and other stakeholders to ensure that relevant knowledge, evidence and learning are effectively applied, shared and, where appropriate, institutionalised in policies, systems and practices.
- Undertake, from time to time, any other related knowledge management and learning functions, activities, or tasks as may be assigned by the Team Leader and/or MERL Lead.

**About You**

- Relevant tertiary qualifications in Development Studies, Public Administration, Social Sciences, Knowledge Management, Organizational Learning, International Development, or a related field.
- At least 5 years of progressively responsible experience in knowledge management, organizational learning, monitoring, evaluation, research and learning (MERL), education, or international development programs.
- Strong understanding of knowledge management, policy development and implementation, organizational learning, adaptive management, and evidence utilization, with experience applying monitoring, evaluation, research, and learning (MERL) methodologies to support program improvement and decision-making.
- Demonstrated experience managing knowledge management and learning functions in donor-funded development programs, including the development of learning agendas, learning sessions or stakeholder consultations, knowledge products, evidence dissemination initiatives, and stakeholder engagement activities.
- Proven ability to synthesize complex information into clear, actionable knowledge products, facilitate learning and reflection processes, and engage effectively with government agencies and stakeholders.
- Experience in the education sector and familiarity with the Philippine education context are desirable.

**The Role**

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MERL) Officer provides operational and technical support to the MERL Lead, contributing to the implementation of EQUIP’s MERL framework. The role focuses on data collection, entry, verification, and basic analysis, and supporting the MERL Lead in producing high-quality reports and learning products.

Key Responsibilities

• Supports the implementation of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, and Learning (MERL) activities across EQUIP projects by assisting in the execution of MERL plans, data collection, management, analysis, reporting, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

• Contributes to the development and application of data collection tools and methodologies, conducts field data collection activities, and ensures the accurate, timely, and quality-assured entry, verification, and maintenance of data within MERL databases and management information systems.

• Undertakes data processing and quantitative calculations, maintains project indicator trackers and dashboards, supports required data analysis, and contributes to the preparation of reports, case studies, and other knowledge products such as presentations, briefing materials, data summaries, and other materials to support MERL reporting, learning, and decision-making.

• Ensures that data is appropriately disaggregated by gender, age, and disability status in accordance with GEDSI principles and supports the generation of scheduled and ad hoc reports on project progress, outputs, outcomes, risks, and performance.

• Supports routine data quality assurance processes, including data completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness and verification, and flags data quality issues for appropriate action.

• Assists in organizing MERL-related meetings, workshops, training sessions, and learning events; maintains accurate records and documentation; and coordinates with finance and administrative teams on logistical and operational requirements for MERL fieldwork and activities.

• Supports the documentation and synthesis of monitoring findings and MEL activities, lessons learned and emerging implementation issues to contribute to learning and adaptive management;

• Conducts field monitoring activities and provides regular updates to the MERL Lead on progress, issues, and risks; contribute information required for the implementation of the Program MERL Plan; and ensures that all work aligns with the EQUIP Annual Implementation Plan, MERL Plan, Action Plans, and other program planning documents.

• Supports adherence to EQUIP quality standards, performance management requirements, risk management processes, and other program strategies, while undertaking additional MERL-related responsibilities as assigned.

• Undertake, from time to time, any other MERL-related functions, activities, or tasks as may be assigned by the Team Leader and/or MERL Lead.

**About You**

• Relevant tertiary qualifications in social sciences, development studies, statistics, or a related field.

• At least three years of experience in MERL or data-related roles, preferably in development programs.

• Demonstrated understanding and practical application of MERL concepts, methodologies, tools, and processes such as key informant interviews, designing questionnaires, and focus group discussions.

• Relevant experience in data collection and entry using digital tools and maintaining electronic databases, indicator trackers or management information systems.

• Experience supporting evaluations, research activities, outcome monitoring or other forms of applied learning and evidence generation.

• Experience using digital data collection platforms such as KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK or similar tools.

• Basic knowledge and / or understanding of applying GEDSI and safeguards principles, including the development and use of PowerBI dashboards.
