jobs.title: Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning, VisionFund International
jobs.body:
VisionFund International is World Vision’s microfinance provider serving vulnerable clients through loans, savings, and insurance. We enable families to grow their livelihoods in hard to reach, rural locations in 28 countries so that caregivers can create secure futures for their children.

We believe in brighter futures for children; empowering families to create incomes and jobs; unlocking economic potential for communities to thrive.

Join VisionFund as we seek to end intergenerational poverty through microfinance.

**Here’s where you come in:**

As **Director of Monitoring, Evaluation, Research and Learning, VFI**, you will lead the design and delivery of VisionFund’s measurement, evaluation, research, and learning function, ensuring the quality and credibility of evidence underpinning VisionFund’s impact claims. You will oversee the network monitoring architecture, client voice instruments, external research partnerships, internal impact evaluations, and capability building for impact staff across the MFI network.

You will also strengthen fundraising capabilities by leading MERL design for institutional, philanthropic, and blended-finance proposals from opportunity qualification through implementation. You will build joint measurement capability with World Vision and ensure measurement commitments are appropriately resourced and tracked.

You will own VisionFund’s monitoring and evaluation approach, including indicator architecture, data collection protocols, quality assurance, reporting cadence, and client voice methodologies. You will establish technical standards for impact measurement, provide assurance on their application, and ensure evidence is consistently used to inform decisions.

You will lead MERL design for funding proposals, advise on measurement-related go/no-go decisions, and ensure measurement requirements are credible, costed, and deliverable. You will build measurement capability with World Vision support and field offices and track commitments throughout implementation.

You will own and maintain VisionFund’s theory of change and manage the organisational research agenda, prioritising questions where stronger evidence can influence decisions. You will manage flagship academic research partnerships, commission and quality-assure third-party research, and strengthen the evidence base supporting child-level results and defensible impact claims. You will also contribute to sector methodology development through publications, technical working groups, and peer review.

You will design and deliver capability-building for impact measurement staff across the MFI network through technical curricula, coaching, methodological guidance, and tooling support. You will manage the measurement implications of network changes, including reporting close-out for exiting entities and maintaining the integrity of network-level aggregates across reporting periods.

You will lead the MERL team, including performance management, capability development, and succession planning, while fostering a Christ-centred, high-performing culture. You will establish routines that ensure evidence reaches and influences decision-making and will contribute to departmental and organisational strategy as a member of the Impact & Engagement senior leadership team.

**Requirements include:**

- Graduate-level degree in Economics, Development Economics, Statistics, Public Policy, Evaluation, or a related quantitative discipline, or demonstrably equivalent applied expertise
- Minimum 10 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership role leading MERL, evaluation, research, or impact functions within a multinational NGO, development finance institution, inclusive finance organization, or similarly complex global organization.
- Demonstrated experience leading the design and implementation of measurement frameworks, evaluation methodologies, and impact-monitoring systems across multi-country or decentralized organizations.
- Minimum 5 years of experience designing and overseeing MERL components of institutional donor, foundation, climate-finance, or other externally funded proposals, including results frameworks, indicator selection, evaluation design, and budget development.
- Demonstrated experience serving as a technical counterpart to academic institutions, research organizations, consultants, or external evaluators, including commissioning, quality assurance, interpretation, and application of research findings.
- Proven experience strengthening technical capability and performance of geographically dispersed teams through coaching, training, curriculum development, and technical guidance.
- Experience influencing and maintaining quality standards across teams and stakeholders that are not under direct line management.
- Demonstrated experience leading organizational change, establishing, redesigning, or significantly strengthening a MERL, research, or evidence function.
- Evidence of external technical contribution through publications, conference presentations, participation in technical working groups, peer review, or other recognized sector contributions.
- Proven experience leading and developing diverse professional teams, including performance management, talent development, succession planning, and fostering high-performance cultures.
- Fluent in English. Working French or Spanish desirable.
- **Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement: Home** based role with 20% travel

*For positions filled in the United States, the typical salary range for this role is $102,000 to $140,000 USD. Ranges are based on various factors, including the labor market, job type, job level, internal equity and budget. Exact salary offers will be determined by factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, experience and geographic location.*

jobs.title: Administration and Finance Officer, Tuvalu
jobs.body:
## Job Brief

Full-time opportunity in Tuvalu.

Locally based role

**Program Background**

Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across Timor-Leste and the Pacific. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of prior Australian Government support for skills and training in Timor-Leste.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [**www.dt-global.com**](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**Objectives of Role**  
The Administration and Finance Officer will play a key role in delivering efficient and comprehensive administrative, procurement and finance support to the Country Director Tuvalu and Learners of the Pacific Australia Skills program.  
This position is responsible for a broad range of functions, including administrative support services, finance support services, sourcing and procurement activities, and records management. The role ensures that all operations are carried out in compliance with Pacific Australia Skills policies, procedures, and work instructions, while contributing to a well-organised, responsive, and effective office environment.

**Roles and Responsibilities**

**Administration and Procurement Support**

- Assist in maintaining updated procurement files and records, including purchase orders, supplier  
    invoices, and service agreements.
- Support the Assets & Procurement Coordinator with asset register updates, tagging, and filing of asset documentation.
- Support for the sourcing of quotations and liaising with service providers (e.g. hotels, rental car companies, catering businesses).
- Support logistics for meetings, training events, and procurement deliveries.
- Coordinate routine office administration tasks such as stationery orders, courier arrangements, and filing.
- Provide support for any other administration/procurement-related tasks as directed by the Country Director Tuvalu.

**Finance Support**

- Process routine financial transactions including supplier invoices, expense reimbursements, staff advances, participant payments, and acquittals in accordance with Pacific Australia Skills procedures.
- Assist with maintaining accurate records for accounts payable/receivable and advances.
- Support preparation of monthly reconciliations, cash flow requests, and filing of finance documentation.
- Assist in collecting and scanning financial correspondence for submission to Regional Head Office Finance.
- Assist with budget monitoring by maintaining expenditure records and providing supporting information for financial reports.
- Support audit activities by preparing financial records and documentation as required.
- Ensure compliance with DT Global financial policies, donor requirements, and local statutory obligations.
- Provide finance support to program activities and participant-related payments.
- Provide support for any other finance-related tasks as directed by the Country Director Tuvalu.

**Selection Criteria**

- Post secondary qualifications in finance, business administration, IT or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience in finance or administration roles in a busy organisational environment.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with ability to prioritise and meet deadlines.
- Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively as part of a small team and provide cross-functional support.
- Experience working with financial systems and/or asset management systems.
- Experience in liaising with vendors and service providers.
- Understanding of procurement principles processed and best practises.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint).
- Experience working in a donor funded program.
- Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental protection, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.

**About You**

**Essential Experience and Knowledge**

· Experience working in the education, training, or development sector.

· DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities.

· People with lived experience of the regions in which Pacific Australia Skills operate are strongly encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: ASSISTANTE OU ASSISTANT SERVICE SUPPORT - MISSION FRANCE
jobs.body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2025, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 21 millions de personnes dans 54 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision, tu assisteras le.la coordinateur.rice support pour les activités des départements supports (finance, logistique et RH) de la Mission France  
 Concrètement, tes missions seront :  
Gestion logistique :  
Réalisation achats de la base IDF et coordination et faire le suivi dans le logiciel LINK.  
Participation à la gestion des fournisseurs et contrats cadre de la mission.  
Suivi des équipements/matériel et de l'environnement de travail du bureau  
Gestion les réservations pour les déplacements des équipes  
Veille aux respects des procédures et participer à leur mise à jour et outils associés  
  
Gestion financière et comptable:  
Traitement, préparation et suivi des factures fournisseurs ainsi que des demandes de remboursement de notes de frais de l'équipe.  
Réalisation des enregistrements comptables sous Excel et archivage des documents comptables.  
Préparation de la clôture mensuelle de la comptabilité.  
Participation aux réunions de suivi budgétaire.  
Veille au respect des procédures et participation à leur mise à jour ainsi qu'à l'actualisation des outils associés.  
  
Gestion ressources humaines:  
Gestion des plannings d'intégration des nouveaux arrivants.  
Participation à l'accueil et au briefing des nouveaux collaborateurs sur la Mission ainsi qu'aux sessions de présentation des procédures support.  
Contribution à la formalisation et à la mise à jour des politiques, processus et outils RH applicables sur la Mission.  
  
Participation à la mise en place des activités:  
Appui à l'équipe programme sur les enjeux logistiques et administratifs dans le cadre du déploiement de leurs activités  
Participation aux temps d'équipes et préparer les compte-rendu  
Contribution à des chantiers transversaux prioritaires sur la Mission

  
Profile :

 Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e engagé·e, motivé·e et disposant des qualités suivantes :  
  
Tu es titulaire ou en cours d'obtention d'une formation supérieure généraliste de niveau Licence 3 à Master en action humanitaire, gestion des organisations, logistique, action sociale, ressources humaines ou comptabilité.  
Tu fais preuve d'une excellente capacité d'organisation et d'analyse.  
Tu disposes de très bonnes qualités relationnelles.  
Tu possèdes une excellente capacité de rédaction écrite et d'expression orale.  
Tu es reconnu.e pour ta proactivité, ta réactivité, ta rigueur et ta flexibilité.  
Tu maîtrises Excel, compétence indispensable pour ce poste.  
Tu as idéalement une première expérience en gestion logistique, financière ou administrative.  
Tu as une expérience dans le milieu associatif.  
Tu partages les valeurs d'Action contre la Faim.  
Tu témoignes d'un fort intérêt pour les activités et les principes défendus par la Mission France.  
Tu souhaites particulièrement t'investir dans les fonctions support.  
  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
Condition Obligatoire : Avoir une convention de stage délivrée par un établissement scolaire de droit français  
Durée du Stage : 6 mois (basé à Montreuil, 102 rue de paris)   
Prise de Poste Souhaitée : 21/09/2026   
  
Conditions Salariales :   
Stage indemnisé à hauteur de 4,57euros net par heure (sur une base de 35h par semaine). Temps de travail hebdomadaire (38,75h).   
Titres restaurant à 8EUR (pris en charge à 60% par ACF).   
Prise en charge à hauteur de 50 % des frais de transport en commun.   
Télétravail : ACF dispose d'une politique de télétravail qui encadre les activités nécessitant une présence impérative au siège, tout en te permettant d'exercer une partie de ton travail à distance. Une présence régulière au siège de Montreuil est ainsi prévue, selon une fréquence définie avec ton manager. À cela s'ajoutent environ trois jours par mois dédiés aux réunions et événements collectifs.

En 2025, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 21 millions de personnes dans 54 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Nous recherchons un·e stagiaire capable d'apporter un appui par les missions suivantes :  
  
Apporter un support aux activités de Plaidoyer sur les questions humanitaires Faim et Conflit et les régions/pays cibles de plaidoyer en lien avec les programmes  
  
Apporter un support aux activités de plaidoyer thématique en particulier sur la protection des travailleurs humanitaires et l'utilisation de la faim comme arme de guerre.  
  
Apporter un support à la préparation d'une conférence internationale à Bruxelles.  
  
Apporter un support général à l'équipe plaidoyer humanitaire en fonction des besoins et urgences

  
Profile :

 Nous recherchons un·e candidat·e qui partage notre engagement et qui dispose des qualités suivantes :   
  
Tu prépares un Master 1 ou un Master 2 en Droit, Sciences Politiques, Sociologie, Développement ou Action Humanitaire. Toutefois, une personne motivée, quelle que soit sa formation, est tout aussi légitime à postuler.  
  
Tu es à l'aise dans les échanges avec de nombreuses parties prenantes et tu possèdes d'excellentes compétences de communication orale et écrite en français, ainsi qu'une très bonne maîtrise de l'anglais.  
  
Une première expérience, en stage ou en bénévolat, dans le secteur associatif ou au sein d'une instance politique constitue un véritable atout.  
  
Conditions d'emploi

Durée du Stage : 6 mois (basé à Montreuil, 102 rue de paris)

Conditions Salariales :  
Stage indemnisé à hauteur de 4,57euros net par heure (sur une base de 35h par semaine).   
Temps de travail hebdomadaire (38,75h).   
Titres restaurant à 8 EUR (pris en charge à 60% par ACF).

jobs.title: Education Project Manager Palestine West Bank
jobs.body:
**What we are looking for**

We are looking for a **strategic,** **experienced**, and **collaborative** Project Manager with a strong track record of managing complex humanitarian or development programmes in challenging and volatile environments.

The ideal candidate combines strong project, financial management and managerial skills. Its an added advantage to have technical expertise and background in education programming.

If you are **an experienced Project Manager** with experience in either protection, child safeguarding, psychosocial support, or any other programming for vulnerable and displacement-affected children and youth, we invite you to apply for this position.

To excel in this position you should be able to lead, mentor and build team and partner capacities while maintaining **strong relationships with donors, government counterparts, clusters, and other stakehold**ers.

A strong understanding of the West Bank operating context and the challenges affecting access to education is essential. The successful candidate will demonstrate sound judgement, adaptability, strategic thinking, and a commitment to quality, accountability, inclusion, and protection.

**Applicants must be legally eligible to work in the West Bank, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.**

**What you will do**

The Education Project Manager will lead the implementation and quality delivery of NRC’s Education portfolio across the West Bank. The role will oversee projects throughout the full project cycle—from design and planning to implementation, monitoring, reporting, and learning—ensuring alignment with NRC’s strategy, donor commitments, and quality standards.

The position will provide strategic and technical leadership to Education programming, support field teams and partners, manage budgets and resources, and contribute to coordination, advocacy, emergency preparedness, and integrated programming across sectors.

Key responsibilities:

- **Lead Education project implementation**: Oversee the planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and quality assurance of NRC’s Education portfolio across the West Bank, ensuring projects achieve their objectives and meet NRC and donor standards.
- **Manage budgets and resources:** Provide overall budget oversight, maintain appropriate spending and burn rates, and ensure effective management of procurement, logistics, staffing, cash forecasting, and other project resources.
- **Provide technical leadership and team development:** Guide and mentor Education teams and implementing partners, strengthen technical capacity, support performance management, and promote continuous learning and improvement.
- **Support programme development and strategy:** Contribute to needs assessments, programme design, proposals, budgets, project extensions, emergency preparedness, and strategic direction, while promoting integrated and durable solutions across NRC’s Core Competencies.
- **Coordinate stakeholders and partnerships:** Build effective relationships with donors, implementing partners, government counterparts, clusters, working groups, and communities, ensuring effective coordination, communication, accountability, and representation of NRC.

**What you will bring**

- Minimum 4 years of experience developing and leading large, complex and/or multi-sectoral projects in humanitarian, protracted crisis, or development settings.
- Senior-level project management experience, including working with consortia, partnerships, or equivalent structures.
- Demonstrated experience managing development donors, including donor compliance and reporting.
- Proven experience in capacity building, coaching, and mentoring technical teams.
- Strong experience working in complex and volatile operating environments.
- Strong leadership, strategic thinking, planning, coordination, problem-solving, and communication skills.
- Fluency in Arabic and English, both written and spoken.

**Context-specific expertise:**

- Strong understanding of the education sector and operational context in the West Bank, including access restrictions, movement constraints, and risks affecting schools and communities.
- Practical expertise in protection mainstreaming, child safeguarding, and gender-sensitive programming in formal and non-formal education settings.
- Demonstrated experience delivering needs-based non-formal education (NFE), remedial education, and emergency education interventions for vulnerable and displacement-affected children and youth.
- Proven experience designing and delivering psychosocial support (PSS) within learning environments.
- Experience designing and implementing flexible NFE pathways, TVET, and market-oriented technical skills programmes for vulnerable youth.
- Strong financial, programme, partnership, reporting, and project-cycle management capabilities.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDjT7SRNPfYS4F0F4jiYNI6AfBuJ8zwJzSqbZ6-qPHYrXQ?e=Xv9C8J) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: West Bank Palestine
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 40%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 8 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in West Bank Palestine, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV and cover letter.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

**This is an opportunity to provide strategic and technical leadership to education programming that supports vulnerable children and youth in one of the world's most challenging humanitarian contexts. The role offers the opportunity to shape high-quality, needs-based education programming while strengthening teams, partnerships, and systems across the West Bank.**

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Palestine](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/palestine)

jobs.title: Wash and Shelter Specialist Cameroon
jobs.body:
**About the Context**

Cameroon is currently facing three overlapping humanitarian crises. Since 2017, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been working in the country to support people who have been forced to flee their homes. NRC helps protect displaced communities and supports them as they rebuild their lives.

Operations are ongoing in all crisis-affected regions, including the Far North, Northwest, Southwest, East, and Adamawa. NRC’s work focuses on four main areas: legal assistance (ICLA), water and sanitation (WASH), shelter, and education. These programmes are designed to respond to urgent needs while also supporting long-term recovery. From 2027, NRC Cameroon country office will ensure supervision and support to operations implemented in Central African Republic.

Across its offices, NRC promotes an integrated approach, aiming to provide coordinated support that helps communities move from emergency to stability.

Find out more about NRC [https://www.nrc.no/](https://www.nrc.no/%22%20/t%20%22_blank) and Watch this short video to see NRC in action [https://vimeo.com/736782633](https://vimeo.com/736782633%22%20/t%20%22_blank)

**What we are looking for**

As WASH & Shelter Specialist you will provide technical oversight and strategic direction to Country and Area offices to further the development of the WASH & Shelter Core Competency (CC).

You will also lead the strategic direction and strengthen the technical quality of the NRC’s Shelter and WASH programme in Cameroon.

Additionally, you will be responsible for supporting the WASH and Shelter projects implementation at field level. You will be expected to travel within the country to provide quality assurance for all projects, develop a collaborative country strategy, capacity build staff through mentoring and training to increase their technical capacity, and develop a donor strategy to further grow the program.

**What you will do**

1. To be responsible for the support to colleagues and partners with WASH and Shelter responsibilities and develop relevant WASH and Shelter training including coaching of WASH and shelter staff and partners to ensure they meet NRC’s WASH and Shelter standards. Also contribute to the induction of new staff with a role in the WASH and Shelter processes.
2. Develop partnership inclusive WASH and Shelter CC strategies, technical guidance and Macro Logframes that are aligned with regional and global strategies and priorities.
3. Contribute to fundraising, develop and revise funding proposal, budgets and donor reports.
4. Follow up on compliance with contractual commitments within CC, ensure high technical quality and synergies in project implementation NRC policies, guidance and procedures.
5. Provide technical direction and project implementation support to the implementation team.
6. Ensure that key learnings are extracted from CC implementation, and incorporate them in CC and staff development processes.
7. Represent NRC in relevant forums/clusters, including with national authorities and donors.
8. Compliance and adherence to NRC policies, guidance and procedures, and a specific responsibility for the functions policies and procedures.

**What you will bring**

**1.Professional Competencies**

- Minimum 3 years of experience within technical expertise area in a humanitarian/ recovery context
- Minimum 2 years of WASH and/or Shelter expertise (as Specialist/PDM or Project Manager)
- Master’s degree or similar in relevant fields
- Experience from working in complex and volatile contexts.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities.
- Knowledge about own leadership skills/profile
- Fluency in French and English, both written and verbal
- This position requires 60% travel in field offices

***Context related skills, knowledge and experience***

- Knowledge of the Central African region
- Experience in team capacity building
- Experience in partnership-based programming for WASH and Shelter
- Experience with a diverse range of donors and funding opportunities, including humanitarian, durable solutions, and development-oriented programming.
- Technical knowledge and experience of behaviour change process in a humanitarian context
- Technical knowledge and experience of the community engagement process and integration of gender and diversity in program design.
- Experience implementing cash and market project approaches
- Knowledge of House, Land and Property rights applied to shelter and WASH responses
- Experience with management of borehole programs is desired
- Experience with alternative WASH in a humanitarian context an asset
- Understanding of SPHERE and INEE Minimum Standards is required
- Understanding of environmental and climate tools like NEAT+ is an asset

**2.Behavioural competencies**

- Handling insecure environments
- Strategic thinking
- Empowering and building trust
- Influencing
- Initiate action and change
- Analyzing

Find more details [JD\_WASHelter Specialist Cameroon.pdf](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQBpxHNWXge9Trfl7So4WpnMATXHVo1gnnMk8g9Ruvl7LYk?e=IusBMa)

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Yaounde, Cameroon
- Contract: 12 months Resident/National Contract
- National Salary&benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.
- Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC [https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)
- Kindly send any questions about the application process to: ***cwa.recruitment@nrc.no***. *Applications sent via email will not be accepted. Please check your application status on your NRC application profile.*

***\*\*Potential Female profiles highly encouraged to apply\*\****

jobs.title: Stagiaire - Coordination éditoriale et communication médicale
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Ouverture dans le cadre d’une création de poste.

Le département médical a pour finalité de contribuer, avec le département des opérations et les autres départements, à la mission sociale de l’association dans les principaux domaines suivants :

- La co-construction des stratégies médico opérationnelles
- L’appui médical aux terrains en termes d’expertise, de stratégie, de formation et de recherche
- L’amélioration continue de la qualité des soins et le respect de l’éthique médicale
- Les formations médicales
- La recherche, la veille scientifique, l’introduction/le suivi des innovations médicales
- Le plaidoyer en interne et en externe sur les sujets médicaux

Le département est dirigé par une directrice médicale et 2 directeurs médicaux adjoints. L’équipe de direction est complétée par une attachée de direction, une assistante de département et un(e) alternante. Le département est constitué de pôles d’activités thématiques regroupant les référents médicaux des spécialités concernées, principalement basés à Paris et autres localisations en France mais aussi à New-York, Sydney, Dakar, Nairobi.  
Nous recherchons un(e) stagiaire au sein de l’équipe de direction du département :

**Missions principales**

**1. Coordination et édition du rapport annuel des activités médicales**

- Appuyer l'équipe dans l'élaboration et le suivi du rétroplanning de production et de diffusion.
- Participer à la structuration du contenu
- Soutenir l'équipe dans le suivi de la collecte des contributions, auprès des référents médicaux et s’assurer qu’elles soient fournies à temps
- Fournir une aide à la rédaction des contenus si besoin
- Participer à la relecture et la cohérence éditoriale du document, en français et en anglais
- Collaborer avec notre prestataire pour le graphisme
- Participer à la publication du rapport sur les différentes plateformes de communication
- Appuyer le suivi de l’impression et de la distribution/communication auprès du mouvement MSF
- Contribuer au suivi de l’avancement du rapport à l’équipe de direction

**2. Communication des informations médicales** :

- Participer à l’élaboration de la partie médicale du "Mutual Accountability Report” de MSF
- Contribuer à la structuration et à la mise à jour et la diffusion des informations médicales sur l’intranet MSF
- Participer à la préparation des points infos médicaux (réunion hebdomadaire réunissant l’ensemble du département médical ainsi que certains représentants des autres départements)
- Prendre les notes et synthétiser des discussions sur différentes thématiques médico-opérationnelles

**3. Support à l’organisation de divers évènements organisés au siège**

- Apporter un support logistique et organisationnel aux organisateurs de divers évènements (Coordo Week, journées médicales thématiques, workshop...).

**Profil recherché**

**Formation :**

- Niveau BAC +3 ou plus
- Formation en communication, sciences politiques ou équivalent

**Aptitudes et compétences**

- Excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et organisationnelles
- Force de proposition
- Polyvalence
- Autonomie, rigueur et sens du travail en équipe
- Intérêt pour les enjeux humanitaires, les sujets médicaux et les activités de MSF
- Capacité à travailler dans l’urgence et à faire preuve de flexibilité

**Langues :**

- Anglais B2, Français C1

**Statut et conditions :**

- Stage de 6 mois, avec convention de stage obligatoire.
- Basé à Paris 19ème. Le montant de la gratification est compris entre 4,35€ et 7,70€ brut par heure en fonction du niveau d’études.
- 1 ticket restaurant est attribué par jour travaillé, d’une valeur faciale de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). 2 jours de repos indemnisés par mois.
- Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir :** Janvier 2027

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures**28 octobre 2026

jobs.title: Protection Lead - National Only
jobs.body:
## **The Role:**

**Oxfam Syria is looking for** **Protection Lead**

**DEPARTMENT PURPOSE:**

The Programme Quality department, under the Deputy Country Director – Programmes, brings together Oxfam in Syria's technical advisors. It strengthens the quality, safety, relevance and impact of programmes across humanitarian, recovery and development interventions through technical guidance, quality assurance, capacity strengthening, and the integration of cross-cutting standards such as protection, gender, safeguarding and accountability to affected populations.

**TEAM PURPOSE:**

Oxfam in Syria's protection work aims to reduce the risks faced by conflict-affected communities and strengthen their capacity to stay safe and claim their rights. Protection activities are implemented directly and with partners by the programmatic protection team. The Protection Lead, based in Programme Quality, provides technical direction and quality assurance to that team through a matrix relationship.

**JOB PURPOSE**:

The Protection Lead provides strategic leadership, technical oversight, and quality assurance for Oxfam Syria’s Protection portfolio. The role leads the technical design, and quality improvement of protection programmes, ensuring evidence-based, principled, and context-responsive approaches that address the evolving needs and priorities of affected populations. The Protection Lead provides technical inputs to programme strategy, design, advocacy, and resource mobilisation, while strengthening safe programming (protection mainstreaming) across the country portfolio. The role works closely with programme teams, partners, coordination mechanisms, networks, and external stakeholders to build capacity, promote learning, and influence protection practice and policy. The role ensures emerging protection risks inform programme adaptation and decision-making.

## **What we are looking for:**

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Protection Programming, representation and Influencing**

- Carry out ongoing Protection Analysis for the Syria programme, including identifying key protection risks and coping capacities, conflict analysis and risk management.
- Lead Oxfam Syria’s protection strategy and approach ensuring effective protection programming, advocacy, and partnership approaches that address humanitarian needs, supports recovery and transition and strengthen community resilience.
- Develop and maintain strategic relationships with relevant government institutions, including the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour (MOSAL), civil society, national partners and other stakeholders, to identify opportunities for collaboration on social protection and other systems and policies that can contribute to sustainable protection outcomes.
- Build the capacity of Protection staff and partners to implement protection activities in line with Oxfam’s approach and global protection standards.
- Lead technical design of protection components within donor proposals. Develop logical frameworks, theories of change, indicators, and protection outcomes.
- Support the implementation of high-quality effective protection activities and programmes and provide ongoing technical support to protection field teams.
- Support programme teams in developing work plans, technical tools, SOPs, referral pathways, and guidance documents.
- Review programme designs and activities to ensure protection outcomes are achieved.
- Commission or carry out learning reviews, evaluations, etc. of protection activities and projects and ensure learning is used to improve programme quality.
- Maintain an up to date understanding of and network of contacts within the Protection sector in Syria and ensure that programme teams have access to relevant, up to date information, including identifying overlaps and collaboration with other sectors.
- Support the DCD for Programmes and the Programme Coordinator on inclusion of protection programmes within the overall humanitarian and early recovery programme design and proposal development for protection programming.
- Develop and/or strengthen reporting tools and support the monitoring and evaluation of protection-related activities across all projects and sectors, working closely with the MEAL Manager and Project Managers.
- Support the DCD for Programs and the Programme Coordinator in identifying new protection partners for Oxfam in Syria.
- Represent Oxfam externally in protection-related UN, INGO and NGO coordination and planning mechanisms, including humanitarian, recovery and development fora, to strengthen coordination, complementarity and influence. Promote a joined-up protection approach that links immediate humanitarian response with longer-term recovery, resilience, social protection and systems strengthening, while supporting field teams to engage effectively in field-level protection coordination and ensuring Oxfam’s protection priorities inform relevant sectoral and policy discussions.
- Ensure that Oxfam Syria’s protection portfolio contributes to influencing and learning on the relationship between humanitarian protection, social protection and longer-term development, identifying opportunities to move beyond short-term service delivery towards more sustainable and locally owned protection outcomes.
- Contribute towards Oxfam’s regional and global protection work through active participation in Oxfam’s Protection Peer Group and maintaining a regular and constructive relationship with the Regional and/or the GHT Protection Advisor.
- Link with EFSVL, WASH and Gender staff to integrate protection in all aspects of the work.
- Contribute technical expertise to the recruitment of protection staff for the Syria country

**Safe Programming**

- Contribute to strengthen Syria team capacity on Safe Programming as well as to support senior and medium management to take the lead and the responsibility on it.
- Support the DCD for Programs, Humanitarian Coordinator and Area Managers in team and partner risk analysis related to programme activities before and during implementation, and advise on amending activities and approaches where necessary.
- Participate in country planning, strategy development and reviews.

**Other**

- Required to adhere to Oxfam’s principles and [values](https://login.salesforce.com/?ec=302&startURL=%2F0060N00000XTrqu) as well as the promotion of [gender justice and women's rights](https://policy-practice.oxfam.org.uk/our-work/gender-justice#855afbea-dfa4-4084-a924-2e7d160e8a85).
- Understanding of and commitment to adhere to equity, diversity, gender, child safety and staff health and wellbeing principles.

**Person Specification**

**Most importantly, every individual at Oxfam International Secretariat needs to be able to:**

- **Live our values of INCLUSION, ACCOUNTABILITY, EMPOWERMENT, COURAGE, SOLIDARITY and EQUALITY (read more about these** [**here**](https://oxfam.box.com/s/yfy4iyac8ulvoc01rkdg51awssv7ie1x)**)**
- **Ensure you commit to our ORGANIZATIONAL ATTRIBUTES (including adhering to the Code of Conduct):**

1. **Be committed to our** [**feminist principles**](https://compass.oxfam.org/communities/gender-justice/wiki/feminism-practice)**, and to applying them in your day-to-day behaviour and your work. Be ready to keep learning, with accountability to those who experience oppression as a result of their identities, such as their gender, race/ethnicity, disability, class, or LGBTQIA identity.**
2. **Be committed to undertaking Oxfam’s safeguarding training and adhering to relevant policies, to ensure all people who come into Oxfam are as safe as possible.**

**EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE & COMPETENCIES**

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS ALL STAFF ARE EXPECTED TO FULFIL:**

- Demonstrate Oxfam values and behavioral competencies.
- Behavioral skills: able to work successfully with and mentor others, often under challenging circumstances, and to demonstrate competencies in "listening and creating dialogue" and "working with others", as well as strong networking skills. In particular:
- Sound judgement: weighs risks, context and the principle of "do no harm" to make balanced, well-reasoned decisions, including on sensitive protection issues.
- Listening: actively listens to colleagues, partners and affected communities, and makes sure their perspectives shape programme decisions.
- Self-awareness: understands own strengths, limitations and biases, seeks feedback, and manages own wellbeing and reactions under pressure.
- Decisiveness: makes timely, clear decisions in fast-changing or uncertain situations, takes ownership of them, and adjusts course when new information emerges.

**ESSENTIAL:**

- Advanced level in international development or gender related degree or relevant work experience.
- Experience in working in the Syrian crisis;
- Minimum of 5 years involvement in humanitarian and development work, preferably in field-based protection work in conflict settings or environments in transition as well as experience of working in a senior advisory role
- Proven experience in carrying out protection analysis and providing strategic advice to protection staff and/or partner teams;
- Strong conceptual and practical understanding of protection standards, key sectoral issues and processes;
- Experience and understanding of community-based protection at the field level, including the constraints, sensitivities and risks associated with such work;
- Ability to represent Oxfam in country in sector meetings and with other NGOs/INGOs, donors, and local authorities;
- Excellent written and verbal communication, including ability to fluently articulate key protection issues verbally and in writing;
- Demonstrable understanding of protection work and ability to implement protection activities with a strong emphasis on the gendered aspects of conflict, violence and abuse.
- Commitment to gender equity, diversity and equal opportunities.
- Experience in capacity building of staff and partners, and the professional development of protection staff.
- Fluency in English.

**DESIRABLE**

- Understanding of Oxfam’s protection approach.
- Knowledge of protection programming in early recovery and longer-term contexts (e.g. housing, land and property rights, civil documentation, social cohesion, etc.).
- Experience in working with partners.
- Experience in integrating programs.
- Understanding of advocacy and campaigning work.
- Experience in participatory research.
- Conflict analysis skills.
- Fluency in Arabic.

**KEY ATTRIBUTES**

- Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to cultural differences and protection issues, as well as the commitment to equal opportunities;
- Ability to demonstrate an openness and willingness to learn about the application of protection mainstreaming, children’s rights, and diversity for all aspects of development work
- Commitment to Oxfam’s safeguarding policies to ensure all people who come into contact with Oxfam are as safe as possible;
- Behavioural competencies: Influencing, relationship building, strategic thinking and judgment, vision setting, self-awareness.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT:** Oxfam is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults. Oxfam expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us. Offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks.

## **We offer:**

We offer a competitive salary and a range of additional benefits to staff including flexible working options, generous pension scheme, annual leave, additional leave allowances, company sick pay, life assurance and a range of other benefits.

From the day you join Oxfam we invite you to stretch and learn in your role. Our wide range of Learning & Development opportunities includes in-house courses, e-learning modules, on-the job learning opportunities, coaching and mentoring, and much more.

You can read more about all Oxfam has to offer [here.](https://www.oxfam.org.uk/about-us/working-oxfam/what-we-offer/)

jobs.title: Oficial de Gestión de Información
jobs.body:

- Implementar la estrategia de gestión de información de DRC en los programas desarrollados en la organización.
- Uso de Kobo para diseñar formularios de ingreso de información y herramientas de recogida de datos sobre el terreno.
- Proporcionar formación y apoyo al personal de DRC, socios implementadores, a los encuestadores y a los trabajadores sobre la gestión de información, herramientas de recopilación de datos y en caso de dificultades técnicas o preguntas relacionadas con las bases de datos y IM en general.
- Apoyar en el uso de dispositivos y sus configuraciones.
- Uso de PowerBI para generar reportes gráficos de monitoreo de indicadores del programa de DRC y del monitoreo de protección (mapas, gráficos, infografías, dashboards).
- Control de calidad y supervisión de los datos que se recogen, identificar y abordar los errores en la recogida o la introducción de datos.
- Asegurar que la recolección de datos cumple con los principios de manejo de datos de protección (PIM).
- Mantener y conservar las bases de datos de todos los programas de DRC en ejecución, teniendo en cuenta la política de protección y confidencialidad de los datos.
- Garantizar la seguridad del intercambio y la actualización de las bases de datos y otros archivos que documentan el progreso del programa en los tiempos acordados y según los estándares de DRC.
- Contribuir al diseño e implementar estrategias y presentación de datos, que permitan la reflexión sobre los datos y permitir la toma de decisiones basadas en evidencia
- Manejar información a través de software especializado para el análisis estadístico de información (Orange, Python).
- Apoyo en la preparación de mapas SIG (Sistema de Información Geográfica).
- Gestión de calidad de datos mediante rutinas automatizadas.
- Garantizar una coordinación constante con los miembros de los equipos de programas.
- Aplicar técnicas y procedimientos técnicos para el análisis de datos de los programas ejecutados por DRC.

**Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo**

- Procurar el cuidado integral de su salud.
- Participar activamente en la conformación del COPASST – Comité de Convivencia Laboral – Brigadas de emergencia, así como las actividades que los mismos realicen.
- Cumplir con las normas reglamentos e instrucciones del SG SST.
- Informar oportunamente de los peligros y riesgos latentes con su sitio de trabajo.
- Asistir a las capacitaciones en SST definidas por el programa de capacitación del SG-SST.
- Velar por el mantenimiento del orden y aseo de su puesto y área de trabajo.
- Suministrar información clara, veraz y completa sobre su estado de salud.
- Reportar inmediatamente al área de SST y su jefe inmediato los accidentes de trabajo que se presenten, incidentes (casi Accidentes) y enfermedades diagnosticadas como laborales.
- Reportar al jefe inmediato la necesidad de tomar acciones correctivas o preventivas, que correspondan ante no conformidades reales o potenciales del proceso al cual pertenece.
- Participar en las actividades de capacitación, simulacros y las que sean programadas desde seguridad y salud en el trabajo
- Participar y contribuir con el cumplimiento de la política y los objetivos del SG-SST.

**Experiencias y competencias técnicas:**

- Mínimo 3 año de experiencia laboral en gestión de información con funciones en desarrollo sistemas de datos y gestión de datos, análisis y tecnología de la información (programación de plataformas, análisis y transformación de datos).
- Conocimiento de Microsoft 365
- Conocimiento de PowerApps y PowerBI
- Conocimiento de diseño y maquetado de Dashboards y reportes.
- Nivel experto de manejo de Excel (Tablas, Tablas Dinámicas, PowerQuery y Fuentes de datos)
- Nivel avanzado de manejo de bases de datos relacionales (SQL, Formas normales y modelos E-R)
- Conocimiento de al menos un lenguaje de programación de análisis de datos (Python)

**Deseado:**

- Experiencia de trabajo en el sector humanitario y manejo de datos para la protección humanitaria.
- Conocimiento moderado de manejo de datos masivos.
- Conocimiento de manejo de información no estructurada.
- Conocimiento en Sistemas de información geográfica SIG (QGIS- ArcGIS)

**Educación** (Incluir certificados, licencias) Profesional en ingeniería, Sistemas, Estadística, Matemáticas, Informática, Ciencias Sociales o campos relevantes.

**Idiomas:** (Indicar el nivel de manejo), Deseable: conocimiento inglés hablado y escrito.

**Todas las funciones de DRC requieren que el titular domine las competencias básicas de DRC:**

- Lograr la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes
- Colaboración: involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación
- Tomar la iniciativa: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación
- Comunicar: escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad
- Demostración de integridad: actuar de acuerdo con la visión y los valores de DRC

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONG's a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Medicina prepagada, cubrimiento del 100% de la póliza para el empleado y precio especial para beneficiarios.
- Contrato nacional a término Obra o Labor con todas las prestaciones de ley posibilidad.
- Salario iniciando en $ 4.344.000 según experiencia y competencias del candidato.
- Fecha de inicio: noviembre 2026
- Salario y condiciones de acuerdo con los términos de empleo en Colombia.

**Proceso de solicitud**

Todos los solicitantes deben subir únicamente una carta de presentación (1 página) y una hoja de vida actualizada (que no supere las 3 páginas) no se reciben más soportes por este medio.

Fecha de cierre de solicitudes: 21 de octubre de 2026 a las 11:59 am Hora Local.

¡Queremos que hagas parte de nuestro equipo!

En DRC creemos que la diversidad fortalece nuestros equipos y que cada persona aporta habilidades, experiencias y perspectivas valiosas. Por ello, invitamos especialmente a personas con movilidad reducida que cumplan con el perfil del cargo a postularse y participar en nuestros procesos de selección.

Nuestro compromiso es evaluar a cada candidato por sus competencias, experiencia y potencial. *Si usted aplica, se da por entendido que tiene disponibilidad inmediata para trabajar y tiene la posibilidad de desplazarse ocasionalmente a las zonas de intervención de la organización. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un(a) candidato(a) adecuado(a). DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo. Se recomienda hacer la aplicación a esta vacante lo más pronto posible, si esta es de su interés.*

**Nota 2:** El postulante que aplique a esta convocatoria autoriza a DRC a validar la información personal suministrada en la hoja de vida. **Nota 3:** El/la postulante que de forma libre y voluntaria deseen hacer parte del proceso de selección para ocupar la posición de la presente convocatoria, deberán observar un estricto apego a las normas que apliquen para la materia (idoneidad en los títulos presentados, ejecución de pruebas de forma personal e individual y veracidad en la información) adhiriéndose a los manuales y Políticas anti fraude de DRC, so pena de declarar descalificado el postulante que incurra en cualquier irregularidad a juicio de la organización, aún por la mera sospecha, e incluso en posibles conductas de tipo penal conforme la legislación colombiana.

source: UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East
jobs.body:
## Org. Setting and Reporting

UNRWA is a United Nations agency established by the General Assembly in 1949 and is mandated to provide assistance and protection to a population of some 5.8 million registered Palestine refugees. Its mission is to help Palestine refugees in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, West Bank and the Gaza Strip to achieve their full potential in human development, pending a just solution to their plight. UNRWA's services encompass education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure and improvement, microfinance, and emergency assistance. UNRWA is the largest UN operation in the Middle East with more than 30,000 staff. UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions.

If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to make a tangible difference for one of the most vulnerable communities in the world, UNRWA would like to hear from you.

- Supervisor: The incumbent reports to the Director of Communications.

## Responsibilities

- Translates documents, reports, and website content from English into Arabic and vice versa for internal or external use, ensuring accuracy and precision.

- Acts as interpreter at internal and external meetings, press briefings and other official occasions as required.

- Assists the Head of Creative Digital Multimedia Communications with editing of UNRWA's official Arab language materials; collaborates with the Communications Division's Arabic desk in these tasks.

- Edits and proofreads agency-wide documents, as required, including sensitive documents, pertaining to the work of the Executive Office and from other departments such as the Department of Legal Affairs, Department of Human Resources, Ethics Office, Office of the Ombudsman, Protection and Neutrality unit; and assists such departments in overseeing the final production of their key

documents, bulletins and other issuances.

- Performs other duties as may be assigned by the Director of Communications, including, where required, in support of other offices or departments in the Agency.

## Competencies

UN Core Values of Integrity, Professionalism and Respect for Diversity, and Core Competencies of Communication, Working with People and Drive for Results apply by default.

- Applying Technical Expertise
- Analyzing
- Planning and Organizing
- Delivering Results
- Demonstrating Self-Awareness
- Ability to work independently or in a team.
- Tactful and well-developed political awareness.
- Knowledge and experience of using computer with proficiency in word processing in English and Arabic.

## Education

- Advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in English, translation and interpretation or a related field.

## Job Specific Qualifications

**Work Experience**

Indicate your current involvement in any outside activities, as it is required. Including but not limited to employment, independent contractor/freelance consultant, board member (corporate, academic, etc), expert group, lobby, public speaking/writing (article, book, blog, social media etc), teaching, conferences, training, press statement, voluntary work, political activity, fundraising/donation for non-UNRWA entity, running for public office, role in political party or orgs, owning business, work for gov./NGO/private company/charity, UNRWA partner/vendor, full/part-time, paid or not. A "yes" answer doesn't necessarily lead to exclusion from future work at UNRWA, yet misrepresentation in providing accurate/complete info can lead to disqualification/termination of appointment, if hired.

- You are required to have at least seven years of experience in translation and interpretation work from Arabic into English and vice-versa, of which three years were in an international organization.

- Excellent command of written and spoken English and Arabic is required.

- You are required to have an advanced university degree (Master's or equivalent) from an accredited educational institution in English, translation and interpretation or a related field.

- Are you currently residing in Duty Station. It is required that you specify your current location.

- Do you currently hold a contract of 1 year or more with UNRWA? If yes, please confirm whether you have completed your mandatory probation period is required.

- Have you previously been a recipient under the EVR (Early Voluntary Retirement) or EVS (Early Voluntary Separation) Schemes? You are required to answer.

## Languages

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English **and** Arabic are required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult [https://languages.un.org](https://languages.un.org/) for details).

## Required Languages

**Language**

**Reading**

**Writing**

**Listening**

**Speaking**

**English**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

**Arabic**

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

UN Level III

### Assessment

During the assessment, the applications will be given preference based on the following desirable qualifications:

- Previous experience at a UN agency or international non-governmental organization;
- Knowledge of contemporary Middle East political and cultural affairs.
- Provided very good understanding of the context of Palestine refugees and UNRWA operations.

The shortlisted candidates will be afterward evaluated based on:

- Technical Test
- Competency-based Interview

Candidates who meet the post requirements and the required language level will be considered for the ongoing competitive process.

To ensure alignment with the UN language levels, please refer to the guidance below: Level I: Basic knowledge of English.

Level II: Good to very good command of English. Level III: Excellent English language skills.

Level IV: Expert level or native proficiency.

### Special Notice

Providing incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on an application form will result in the immediate disqualification of the candidate.

Contract Type:

Fixed Term Appointment for 1 year; 1 year probation period, with the possibility of further extension, subject to the availability of funds, satisfactory performance, and continuing need.

Grade and Salary:

Grade 17 Monthly basic salary JD 1156.600 fils. Special Occupational Allowance (SoA) 69.9% of basic salary. The salary may be subject to a reduced work schedule.

Other benefits: Other benefits include monthly Provident Fund contribution (15.4% of basic salary paid by the Agency), compulsory medical insurance, 30 days of annual leave, and dependency allowance (if applicable).

Additional benefits:

-2 days of sick leave for each completed month of service.

-14 weeks of Maternity Leave.

-2 weeks paternity leave.

Department/Office: UNRWA - External Relations and Communications Duty Station: Headquarters Amman

Other Information:

- The incumbent may be required to travel in the Agency's areas of operations within the Middle East, including on short notice.
- The incumbent may be expected to work beyond regular working hours.

Equivalency:

Equivalency may apply for this post.

- Candidates with a combination of additional relevant academic qualifications and/or additional years of progressive work experience may also be considered on equivalency.
    
    NB: Work experience alone or formal qualifications with no relevant work experience are not considered an acceptable combination.

General Information:

- This vacancy notice is open to internal and external candidates. Only candidates residing in Jordan, and within commuting distance of the duty station with authorization to work in the duty station at the time of application are eligible to apply.

- The Agency will not assume responsibility or accountability to support or facilitate the issuance of work permit in Jordan, and without a valid work permit, the appointment may be rescinded.

- Since the Vacancy is an Area Staff post, the Agency will not provide coverage for relocation costs.

- Preference will be given to registered Palestine refugees and candidates assisting the Agency to meet its commitment to gender parity. UNRWA welcomes applications from qualified candidates with disabilities.

- To ensure efficiency and timeliness of the recruitment process, if a large number of applicants pass the test, the Agency may decide to invite to the interview only the candidates with the top scores to ensure a manageable number of candidates to proceed to the personal interview stage.

- UNRWA is committed to achieving gender balance in its workforce. Qualified and experienced female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

- A roster may be created from the selection exercise, and successful candidates may become eligible for appointment to the same post or a similar post. In the case of multiple or recurring posts, that a roster will be created from which the candidates will be selected for appointment;

- Only applications that have been fully completed in UNRWA's online e-recruitment system inspira will be considered and no late applications will be accepted. The PHP should be completed with full relevant work experience under the experience tabs as per the requirements in the Job Opening. All acquired university degrees must also be stated, if applicable. Please make sure that your application is filled in properly, correctly, and completely; any missing or incomplete information may lead to the rejection of the application by the system. Applicants applying to positions for Grades 12 to 20 or LDC Bands E to H must submit a cover letter/motivational statement in order to be considered.

Additionally, providing incorrect or misleading information on an application will result in the immediate disqualification of a candidate.

- Applicants will be disqualified when it becomes apparent that he or she provided incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on his or her personal history profile or during the recruitment process. If the applicant is also a staff member, the provision of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information in the personal history profile may also amount to misconduct. The Agency may indefinitely refuse to accept applications from an applicant who has previously provided incorrect, incomplete or misleading information on his or her personal history profile or during a recruitment process or committed plagiarism.

- For UNRWA internal staff, they are required to specify and include their current UNRWA grade level. To do so applicants should select under "Category" RLG, scroll down to see all categories, then select their local grade.

- Please find below the link to a video that guides applicants on how to apply to Job Openings: https:

//drive.google.com/file/d/1MH-IYA6Y8kxA1fgao5qyTV8VwNajgx4u/view?usp=sharing

- Advertisements published only in English will only accept applications in English, and Arabic submissions will not be considered.

- UNRWA has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and UNRWA, including sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment, racism/racial discrimination and other forms of conduct, including but not limited to discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment. To uphold these standards, background checks are conducted for

all recommended candidates and those placed on a roster to help ensure that individuals with a history of such conduct are not hired. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles. Background checks will include the verification of academic credential(s), employment history, ClearCheck and INTERPOL, as well as certification of non-conviction, where available. Selected candidates may be required to provide additional information to conduct a background check. By applying for a position with UNRWA, candidates acknowledge and consent to these verification processes.

- The Agency may disqualify applicants whose name appears on the UN Sanctions List or a UN database of staff separated for reason of misconduct or of staff who separated whilst misconduct processes were pending.

- UNRWA shares investigation and misconduct information with other UN Agencies, and past and prospective employers about staff members who have been separated for misconduct, or who have separated while an investigation and/or disciplinary process for misconduct was underway; and those individuals may be prohibited from employment with the United Nations.

- The Agency will immediately disqualify applicants who are ineligible for any reason in accordance with the Agency regulatory framework.

- UNRWA is funded almost entirely by voluntary contributions from UN member states, regional

bodies, business foundations and individual contributions. The mission of UNRWA is to help Palestine

refugees achieve their full potential in human development under the difficult circumstances in which they live.

For more details on UNRWA, please visit: [https://www.unrwa.org](https://www.unrwa.org/)

- Applications from UNRWA staff member who had been demoted with deferred eligibility for promotion will not be considered.

- Applications from Staff members who were recipients under the Early Voluntary Retirement or Exceptional Voluntary Separation Schemes will not be considered.

- Applications from Internal candidates serving for less than one year in their current post will not be considered.

- The Agency reserves the right not to make an appointment, to make an appointment at a lower grade, or to make an appointment with a modified job description or to change the contract Modality.

- A candidate is not eligible for consideration if he or she was short-listed and found not suitable for the same post within the previous 12 months unless the post description has since been altered by 30% or more, as determined by ODCS.

- UNRWA reserves the right to proceed only with internal candidates or proceed with the candidates of an under-represented gender for any vacancy announcement when it determines that the short-list for a single post at any grade level is excessively long.

### United Nations Considerations

Staff members are subject to the authority of the Commissioner-General of UNRWA and to assignment by him or her.

UNRWA is committed to achieving gender parity at all levels of staffing under the current UN-wide gender agenda and strongly encourages applications from qualified applicants from under-represented groups.

At UNRWA, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. UNRWA is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. Reasonable accommodation for applicants with disabilities may be provided to support participation in the recruitment process when requested and indicated in the application.

UNRWA Considerations

UNRWA staff are expected to uphold the highest standards of efficiency, competence, neutrality,

impartiality and integrity. This includes respect for and commitment to human rights, diversity and non-violent means of dealing with all kinds of conflict. Only persons who fully and unconditionally commit to these values should consider applying for UNRWA jobs. Candidates will not be considered for employment with UNRWA if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. Candidates who have committed crimes other than minor traffic offences may not be considered for employment. The Agency may disqualify applicants who have separated for reason of misconduct, who left a UN Agency while misconduct processes were pending, or who appear on the UN Sanctions List.

UNRWA is a non-smoking work environment.

Applicants are urged to follow carefully all instructions available in the online recruitment platform, inspira. For more detailed guidance, applicants may refer to the Manual for the Applicant, which can be accessed by clicking on "Manuals" hyper-link on the upper right side of the inspira account-holder homepage.

The evaluation of applicants will be conducted on the basis of the information submitted in the application according to the evaluation criteria of the job opening and the applicable internal legislations of the United Nations including the Charter of the United Nations, resolutions of the General Assembly, the Staff Regulations and Rules, administrative issuances and guidelines.

Applicants must provide complete and accurate information pertaining to their personal profile and qualifications according to the instructions provided in inspira to be considered for the current job opening. No amendment, addition, deletion, revision or modification shall be made to applications that have been submitted. Candidates under serious consideration for selection will be subject to reference checks to verify the information provided in the application.

Job openings advertised on the Careers Portal will be removed at 11:59 p.m. (New York time) on the deadline date.

### No Fee

THE UNITED NATIONS RELIEF AND WORKS AGENCY FOR PALESTINE REFUGEES IN THE NEAR EAST (UNRWA) DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE OR REQUEST MONEY FROM CANDIDATES AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT AND ONBOARDING PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING, ONBOARDING).
