jobs.title: Market Systems Technical Coordinator
jobs.body:
**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Market Systems Technical Coordinator contributes, under the leadership of the FES lead, to the design of Oxfam's market systems and enterprise portfolio in Syria, across humanitarian, recovery and development programming. Key responsibilities cover market analysis and programme design, enterprise development and financial inclusion, support to producer organisations, engagement with private and public market actors, partner and team capacity, and integration with WASH, protection, gender and MEAL. The role pays particular attention to the participation and role of women, vulnerable groups and other excluded actors within the market system. The role contributes market evidence to funding proposals and to Oxfam's policy and advocacy work.

In the first 12 months, the post holder is expected to: (1) lead on a value chain selection exercise and deliver two value chain or market studies with intervention designs; (2) map priority producer organisations, market actors and open working relationships with chambers, agro-processors and financial institutions; and (3) supply market evidence and results frameworks to at least two funding proposals and/or learning papers.

**Market analysis and programme design**

- Lead the selection of value chains, using economic, environmental, employment and gender criteria, starting from a shortlist of two to three sectors agreed with the FES Lead for year one, drawn from the priority sectors in the FES strategy, including but not limited to: livestock and fodder, fruit and olive, vegetables, dairy, fisheries, textiles, handicraft and heritage, and construction and mechanics.
- Design and manage market assessments, value chain studies, feasibility studies and market actor mapping; commission and quality-assure consultancies where needed.
- Apply market analysis to humanitarian as well as recovery design, including EMMA and market monitoring for cash programming, so that emergency response supports rather than displaces local markets.
- Translate analysis into intervention logic: identify where the constraints (input supply, finance, storage, transport, standards, regulation, information) and support or lead the design of interventions against it.
- Contribute market evidence and results frameworks to concept notes, proposals and donor reports, working with the funding team.

**Enterprise development and financial inclusion**

- Design and quality-assure business development services, delivered through hub teams and partners, including advisory support, business planning, market information, incubation and links to buyers.
- Develop financial inclusion pathways for small producers and enterprises: savings groups, cooperative finance, and engagement with microfinance and other financial actors as liquidity allows.
- Ensure enterprise support reaches women and young people on terms that do not push them into unprotected informal work, and design against that risk explicitly.

**Producer organisations and collective action**

- Design Oxfam's approach to producer collective action (aggregation, quality improvement, direct market linkage and internal governance, with representation of women and young members) and support hub teams and partners to deliver it, so that producers strengthen their bargaining position with traders and middlemen.

**Market actor and private sector engagement**

- Build working relationships with the chambers of commerce, agriculture and industry, agro-processors, input suppliers, traders, transporters and financial institutions.
- Identify where private actors will co-invest, and develop arrangements, for agreement by the FES Lead and project budget holders, designed to hold after the project ends.
- Engage public institutions on market regulation, standards and licensing at governorate and local level, in coordination with the policy and advocacy function.
- Represent Oxfam in technical working groups, coordination forums and consortia on livelihoods, markets and early recovery, as relevant.

**Partner and team capacity**

- Assess partner capacity in market programming and provide structured accompaniment as needed.
- Build market systems literacy across the Food and Economic Security Oxfam teams, so that market thinking is applied across all interventions.

**Integration, learning and influencing**

- Work with the WASH, protection, advocacy, and MEAL functions so that market interventions address water-linked enterprise and shared infrastructure, decent work and exploitation risks, and documented learning shared between hubs.
- Collaborate with gender justice teams on addressing challenges at the intersection of women’s economic participation and unpaid care work.
- Supply evidence to Oxfam's advocacy on market regulation, fair competition, protection of small producers and social protection for informal workers.

Other duties may be reasonably required in supporting the delivery of team objectives and outcomes.

**EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE & COMPETENCIES**

**Essential**

**Core competencies:**

- Agility, complexity and ambiguity
- Relationship building
- Systems thinking
- Decisiveness
- Enabling

**In addition:**

- Bachelor's degree in agricultural economics, economics, business administration, development studies or a related field, with at least seven years of progressively responsible experience in livelihoods, value chain development, agribusiness, financial inclusion, enterprise or SME support, or private sector development.
- Good understanding of rural economies, agricultural livelihoods, producer organisations, and MSMEs.
- A technical diploma in a related field with at least seven years of the same experience may be accepted in place of a bachelor's degree.
- Experience coordinating technical work across teams, field locations or partner organisations without direct line management.
- Demonstrated experience of at least 5 years analysing and developing agricultural, rural or other relevant value chains, including identifying market opportunities.
- Experience conducting or commissioning market assessments, value chain studies or feasibility studies, and using the findings to change a programme design.
- Familiarity with market-based programming and market assessment approaches (for example EMMA or comparable tools).
- Experience working with producers, cooperatives, associations, small enterprises or private sector actors (including financial institutions), with credibility among business people as well as communities.
- Understanding of gender dynamics in Syrian markets and labour, and commitment to designing so that women and young people gain rather than absorb risk.
- Fluency in Arabic; working proficiency in English, sufficient to write reports, assessments and proposal inputs.
- Numerical analysis skills: able to build and interrogate a simple cost structure, margin calculation or business plan.
- Strong facilitation and negotiation skills, including with government bodies, chambers and traders.
- Willingness and ability to travel regularly to hubs across Syria, up to 40 per cent of time.
- Understanding of security protocols and access constraints in conflict-affected areas.
- Commitment to Oxfam's mission, feminist principles, safeguarding policies and code of conduct.

**Desirable**

- Master's degree in a relevant field.
- Familiarity with market systems development (M4P/MSD) approaches through formal training or project experience.
- Experience with cash and voucher assistance in a market analysis role.
- Experience with cooperative or solidarity economy models, savings groups or microfinance.
- Prior INGO or donor-funded project experience, including institutional donor compliance.
- Experience linking programme evidence to advocacy or policy dialogue.

jobs.title: Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment
jobs.body:
Terms of reference (TOR)

Consultancy service to conduct a programme baseline assessment

UGANDA & KENYA

· Project: Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP)

· Procuring Organisation: IsraAID

· Contract Type: Consultancy

· Contract Period: October 2026 to December 2026, 75 days (Phased implementation)

· Target Start Date: Tentatively 26/10/2026

· Application Deadline: 23/10/2026

· Submission Method: EMAIL – see 'how to apply'

BACKGROUND

IsraAID is an International Humanitarian Non-Governmental Organization founded in 2001 and headquartered in Israel. It supports people and communities affected by humanitarian crises, combining rapid emergency response with longer-term recovery, resilience, and preparedness. Over the years, IsraAID has worked in more than 60 countries, responding to disasters, displacement, epidemics, and other crises. Its mission is centered on partnering closely with local communities to provide urgent assistance while helping them rebuild and strengthen their resilience to future shocks.

IsraAID is implementing a project titled Integrated Community Nutrition Management Programme (ICNMP) in Nakivale Refugee Settlement in Uganda and in Kakuma Refugee Camp in Kenya. The programme intends to improve health outcomes and reduce morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition in vulnerable communities participating in the Program. ICNMP is designed as a regional initiative that responds to acute and chronic nutrition needs across East Africa, beginning its phase zero in Q2 of 2026, and actual implementation in September 2026. Although the immediate program launch focuses on Uganda and the emergency phase in Kenya, early 2027 will see Kenya incorporating the full package while the broader intention is to establish a model that can later expand to South Sudan as funding becomes available. The regional framing is essential, as the scale of displacement, vulnerability, and recurring shocks across these countries requires harmonized technical standards, shared learning, and coordinated supply chain approaches. The program will expand decentralized nutrition services by placing screening, early identification, and treatment within spaces that families already use daily, including schools, Child-Friendly Spaces, transit points, and primary health facilities. To be able to achieve the intended outcomes, IsraAID seeks services of a consultant to conduct a baseline upon which project progress and successes will be measured.

This Terms of Reference (ToR) sets out the background, purpose, objectives, scope of work, expected deliverables, and management arrangements for the baseline study, and invites eligible firms to submit technical and financial proposals for consideration.

PURPOSE

This assignment aims at establishing both quantitative and qualitative baseline information on access to integrated nutrition services, nutrition and food security practices and programme systems to ensure that these are addressed by programme interventions to realise the intended overall goal. The baseline will also establish baseline information on several learning areas under the OECD criteria and the IsraAID Community Resilience framework (CRF). The baseline therefore aims at obtaining verified, disaggregated benchmark values for the programme indicators, enabling precise measurement of outcomes and impacts at endline (Year 2, 2028).

OBJECTIVES OF THE ASSIGNMENT

The assignment will specifically

A. Assess the 3 programme outcome indicators

1\. Vulnerable communities — especially children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) — access integrated, quality nutrition services delivered through a multi-tier workforce (community and formal system) and functional multi-sectoral pathways.

2\. Caregivers and community structures adopt improved nutritional and food security practices that prevent and protect against malnutrition.

3\. Programme systems — accountability, information, governance and supply chain, inventory management systems, logistics & distribution modalities — are functional and progressively integrated into and owned by national, district and community structures.

B. Provide baseline information on the specified Community Resilience Framework (CRF) and OECD learning questions.

SCOPE

The baseline survey will be conducted in programme’s area of implementation, covering Nakivale Refugee Settlement and its surrounding host communities in Western Uganda and Turkana West Sub-County specifically targeting Kakuma Refugee Camp, Kalobeyei settlement and its surrounding host communities in Kenya. There are several credible data sources that will benefit the project including, among others, District Information Health System (DHIS 2),

Food Security and Nutrition Assessment reports (FSNA), Demographic Health Surveys, and Population Census reports. Primary baseline information will be obtained from, among others, health facilities, schools, households, children-friendly spaces, community structures and partners engaged in nutrition interventions

METHODOLOGY

IsraAID anticipates a mixed-methods baseline design combining quantitative and qualitative approaches, consistent with the evidence requirements set out in the MEAL Plan. The final design will be proposed by the Firm and refined collaboratively with IsraAID’s MEAL team.

The baseline study should be designed so that its instruments, sampling frame, and methodology can be replicated with fidelity at endline, enabling credible before and after comparison and contribution analysis.

ETHICAL CONSIDERATIONS

The consultant will be expected to demonstrate how the assessment will be conducted in line with research ethics while protecting the human rights of the participants. It will also be the responsibility of the consultant to ensure strict adherence to IsraAID Safeguarding Policy. The consultant will also be responsible for ensuring that any persons hired, engaged, or consulted during the process are familiar with the policy and commit to abide by it during the delivery of the assignment.

EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND TIMELINE

This assignment will last approximately 75 days from the date of signing of the contract. The consultant will provide a detailed work plan with realistic timelines to the logical conclusion of the baseline survey. The following deliverables are expected from the consultant:

The baseline assessment will be undertaken by one consultant/firm. Fieldwork will be conducted sequentially, beginning in Uganda and subsequently moving to Kenya.

1\. Inception & Evaluation Design – Week 1

Key activities

· Desk review of programme proposal, Theory of Change, Logic Model and MEAL Plan.

· Inception meetings with IsraAID.

· Refine evaluation design, sampling strategy and evaluation matrix.

Deliverables

· Inception report.

· Refined methodology and sampling plan.

· Approved work plan and evaluation/indicator matrix.

2\. Tool Development, Piloting & Field Preparation – Weeks 2–3

Key activities

· Finalize quantitative and qualitative data collection tools aligned with Indicator Reference Sheets.

· Share tools with relevant teams and incorporate feedback.

· Pilot testing and tool refinement.

· Enumerator training/orientation and field preparation.

· Ethics/safeguarding clearance preparation.

Deliverables

· Approved final data collection tools and protocols.

· Pilot findings and revisions.

· Enumerator training/orientation completed.

· Ethics/safeguarding documentation.

3\. Data Collection – Uganda – Weeks 4–5

Key activities

· Deploy quantitative and qualitative surveys/interviews with agreed respondents in Uganda.

· Conduct ongoing field-level data quality assurance.

· Hold regular field debriefs with participating stakeholders.

· Complete Uganda fieldwork and initial data quality checks.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

Deliverables

· Uganda quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Uganda dataset.

3\. Transition & Data Collection – Kenya – Weeks 5–7

Key activities

· Close out any outstanding Uganda data collection activities.

· Uganda findings first draft submission

· Transition/travel from Uganda to Kenya.

· Conduct quantitative and qualitative data collection in Kenya.

· Maintain ongoing data quality assurance and stakeholder debriefs.

· Provide the IsraAID team with access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected.

· Complete Kenya fieldwork and initial data checks.

Deliverables

· Uganda fieldwork close-out and initial findings draft shared.

· Kenya quantitative and qualitative data.

· Field notes/transcripts.

· Data quality assurance records.

· Cleaned Kenya dataset.

4\. Analysis & Validation – Weeks 7–9

Key activities

· Clean, code and analyze quantitative and qualitative data.

· Triangulate findings across methods and countries.

· Develop and populate indicator baseline values.

· Prepare and conduct validation workshop with IsraAID/programme stakeholders.

Deliverables

· Analyzed datasets.

· Populated indicator baseline table.

· Draft findings.

· Validation workshop summary.

5\. Reporting & Dissemination – Weeks 9–10

Key activities

· Incorporate feedback from IsraAID.

· Finalize evaluation/baseline report.

· Prepare executive summary/brief and presentation deck.

· Present findings to relevant stakeholders.

· Hand over final datasets, tools and supporting documentation.

Deliverables

· Final report in MS Word and PDF.

· Executive summary/brief.

· Presentation deck.

· Final clean datasets and tools.

Summary of Key Milestones

· Week 1: Inception phase completed

· Week 2 & 3: Tools finalised/piloted and field preparation completed

· Week 4 & 5: Uganda fieldwork completed

· Weeks 6 & 7: Kenya fieldwork completed and initial Uganda finding draft

· Weeks 8 & 9: Analysis and validation completed; draft report ready

· Week 10: Final report, presentation and data/tools handover completed

Note: The timeline is indicative and may be adjusted in consultation with IsraAID, provided the overall 10-week period and Uganda-to-Kenya sequencing are maintained. Analysis may overlap with final data cleaning. IsraAID will want to be provided access to data on a rolling basis as it is collected, to enable ongoing data quality checks and early identification of gaps or issues.

Summary of Key Baseline Deliverables

· Inception report by the consultant within one (1) week upon signing of the consultancy contract.

· Draft Baseline Survey report with clear findings in line with the aim and outcomes of the programme, conclusion, and recommendations for review.

· Final Baseline Survey report in electronic format (MS Word as well as PDF)

· Summary of the findings in (MS PowerPoint) to be used for subsequent dissemination.

· All raw data: transcripts from In-depth Interviews, Individual Surveys, FGDs and cleaned data set used for analysis and production of the final report in an acceptable electronic format shared on a rolling basis.

KEY ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

IsraAID and the Programme Team

· Draw the contract and manage its implementation within the period.

· Coordinate the baseline study

· Share relevant documentation that are important for this assignment

· Introduction of the consultant and team to the relevant bodies within the study locations.

· Organize a validation meeting for the baseline findings.

· Review and approve the deliverables presented by the consultant.

Consultant

· Recruit, contract, remunerate, train, coordinate, and supervise data collectors, ensuring compliance with the agreed methodology, ethical standards, data quality requirements, and timelines.

· Lead consultancy assignment including data collection and analysis.

· Develop and review the data collection tools.

· Lead the development of the consultancy report and incorporate any feedback from IsraAID

· Ensure all deliverables of the assignment are accomplished and approved by IsraAID

· Present findings to the IsraAID team and relevant stakeholders for validation.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

IsraAID expects the successful consultant/firm to field a multidisciplinary team with a balance of quantitative, qualitative, and GESI expertise, complemented by strong in-country presence across ICNMP priority geographies where possible. The indicative team composition below is provided as guidance; consulting firms may propose an alternative structure provided all required competencies are demonstrated and justified.

· Team Leader / Baseline Study Lead: Advanced degree in public health, social sciences, statistics, international development, or related field; minimum 10 years’ experience leading baseline/endline evaluations for complex, multi-country development programs; demonstrated experience with forced displacement, refugee, or migration programming; strong track record managing mixed-methods research teams across multiple African countries. Excellent interpersonal and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with the IsraAID team.

· Quantitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in statistics, economics, or related field; expertise in survey design, sampling methodology, and quantitative data analysis (e.g., STATA, R, SPSS); experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., KoboToolbox, SurveyCTO, ODK).

· Qualitative Research Specialist: Advanced degree in social sciences; expertise in qualitative methods including KIIs, FGDs, and complexity-aware approaches (e.g., Outcome

· Data Management / MEL Support: Experience in data cleaning, database management, and dashboard/data visualization; familiarity with data protection standards applicable to work with protected persons.

GOVERNANCE AND REPORTING LINES

The consulting firm will report to IsraAID’s ICNMP MEAL Coordinator, who holds day-to-day responsibility for the MEAL leadership of the ICNMP programme, and will work closely with the ICNMP program teams in both Uganda and Kenya Country Offices on tool design, data quality assurance, analysis, and reporting. The ICNMP MEAL Coordinator retains overall accountability for the assignment and will review and approve the inception report and final baseline report.

PAYMENT PLAN

50% after the approval of the inception report, 50% after the approval of the final report.

APPLICATION PROCESS

Interested candidates should submit the following:

· Technical proposal outlining approach and methodology

· A financial proposal in US Dollars (USD), detailing all consultancy-related costs (operational, and logistical costs for conducting the assignment in Kenya and Uganda).

· CVs of the Lead Consultant and the entire team

· At least three relevant samples of previous similar work

· At least two (2) recommendation letters from recent clients for similar assignments.

· Copy of the company registration, Memorandum, and Articles of Association if a company/ firm is applying.

· Copy of tax compliance Certificate

· TIN Number

· VAT Number

· Any other relevant information supporting the application.

EVALUATION CRITERIA FOR SELECTION OF THE CONSULTANT/CONSULTING FIRM

Proposals from the interested bidders will be evaluated against the following criteria:

1\. Technical Approach & Understanding of the Assignment (30%): Understanding of the programme, evaluation objectives and scope; quality and appropriateness of the proposed methodology; sampling approach; quantitative and qualitative

methods; data analysis, triangulation and validation; and ethical/safeguarding considerations.

2\. Relevant Experience & Technical Capacity (25%): Demonstrated experience conducting baseline studies, evaluations or similar assignments, particularly in humanitarian, refugee, displacement and development contexts. Experience working with refugee and host communities in Uganda and/or Kenya will be an advantage. Qualifications and expertise of the proposed consultant/team will also be considered.

3\. Workplan, Fieldwork & Data Quality Approach (20%): Feasibility of the proposed workplan within the 10-week period; capacity to undertake fieldwork sequentially in Uganda and Kenya; approach to data quality assurance, data management, safeguarding and secure access to data on a rolling basis during data collection.

4\. Financial Proposal & Value for Money (25%): Completeness, clarity and reasonableness of the financial proposal, including professional fees and all logistical and operational costs required to conduct the assignment in Uganda and Kenya.

ANNEXES

1\. Program Document

2\. Program LogFrame

RESERVATION OF RIGHTS

Nothing contained in this RFP/TOR shall be construed as creating any obligation on the part of IsraAID to enter into a contract with any bidder. IsraAID reserves the unrestricted right to determine the evaluation criteria, request additional documentation, waive minor irregularities, seek clarifications, reject any or all proposals, and terminate the procurement process at its sole discretion and without prior notice.

  
Appendixes can be found here - [**public folder**](https://israaid-my.sharepoint.com/:f:/g/personal/eoyoo_israaid_org/IgC0MsUIQfMjR5rArPJsF2AmAZsbCmAQ5eV4Ul5n7Gh-fS8)

jobs.title: Head of Support Services - Lebanon (Readvertised)
jobs.body:
**Who are we?**

DRC has been responding to various humanitarian crises in Lebanon since 2004, working with Palestinian, Iraqi and Syrian refugees. Since 2011, DRC has focused on responding to the Syrian refugee crisis in Lebanon and the resulting impact on Lebanese host community, and more recently the impact of the economic and financial crises as well as responding to the ongoing conflict. DRC Lebanon’s focus is to ensure that we are able to respond to critical emerging humanitarian needs whilst improving the living conditions of displacement-affected populations and contributing to the achievement of durable solutions. DRC is focusing its response in protection, economic recovery, shelter and site coordination and management, and humanitarian mine action across the country directly and through partners. DRC is also contributing to the broader humanitarian response through our Referral Information Management System (RIMS), utilised by 170 organisations.

**About the job**

The Head of Support Services (HoSS) is operationally and strategically responsible for Finance, Human Resources, Logistics and Procurement, Administration and/or IT. S/he oversees, develops and provides strategic direction to his/her support areas. This role has a country focus (Lebanon) and ensures compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country activities.

With senior level management experience, you are expected to have demonstrable successful track record of organizational development and resource mobilization and play a leadership role in developing and implementing country-specific strategies as well as improving operational systems, processes, and policies in support of DRC’s mission and values.

**Previous experience in a Finance Manager/Director or similar role and/or a Finance-related qualification is highly recommended.**

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Responsibilities:**

**Staff Management**

- Lead and manage the support managers (including people planning, performance, well-being and development) whilst providing dotted technical line support to wider country support team.
- Work to build the capacity of the operational support staff throughout the operation though frequent in-service training sessions, mentoring support and frequent visits to field offices.
- Role model and lead the wider country programme against DRC values, diversity and inclusion as well as code of conduct.

**Support Services Management**

- Responsible for the strategic development, management and implementation of the support operations as per DRC operational handbook. This includes developing and improving operational approaches, compliance and systems, and support the Country Director to build and deliver effective and sustainable interventions.
- Support the Country Director and the Senior Management Team in liaising with donors and authorities, especially as relates to issues of compliance, registration, and audit
- Ensure appropriate technical support is available to programs, in line with organizational priorities
- Provide strategic guidance to the HR/Admin department to develop and implement DRCs HR policy in Lebanon. This includes providing strategic guidance for all staff management, career & development recruitment and induction process as well as appropriate stress management and care for Expatriates and National Staff.
- Lead on DRC Lebanon annual master budgets and ensuring that monthly monitoring of expenditure informs management decision making.
- Lead on the effective implementation and adherence of organization and stakeholder financial regulations.
- Overseeing the operationalization of the contextual/localized finance handbook.
- Ensure the implementation of sustainable and robust supply chain and financial system for an efficient and effective support to all DRC programs and support services.
- Ensure an efficient ICT Operating environment is in place to meet operational needs.

**Operational Management**

- Responsible for maintaining and improving operational resource management in the mission, together with SMT, identifying both short term and long-term resource needs and translate these into objectives and priorities for future DRC projects in Lebanon
- Responsible for leading the development and update of the resource management component of the Country Strategy, ensuring the Support Services facilitate the delivery of the strategy in line with DRC global policies and strategy.
- Ensure that DRC retains and continually develops its operational capacity to provide rapid emergency response in particular within its procurement and HR systems
- Ensure that Lebanon operation complies to DRC Risk Management Framework, and operational Compliance Tools and processes are duly implemented. This includes development of a risk management plan for the country that identifies the major financial and operational risks and implement a mitigation strategy
- Regular review and improvements to Country SOPs to ensure the internal control environment strengthened as well as develop policies as required where gaps are noted.
- Supervision, audits and controlling and implementation of corrective actions related to DRC’s operational standards within support area. This also includes ensuring the timely implementation of DRC’s internal audit and external audit recommendations and contextualize HQ understanding of local challenges.
- Participate as a member of the SMT in drafting project proposals, and on the use of resources according to budgets and policies.
- Together with the Head of Programs, lead the mainstreaming of Project Cycle Management and partnership best practices throughout the organization.
- Contribute to the delivery of DRC Lebanon’s localisation strategy, development and oversight of partnerships and ensure Support Services are fit for purpose to support equitable partnerships and capacity exchange.
- Ensure that all administrative and legal-related systems are accurate and maintained, and that DRC Lebanon is legally compliant with Government of Lebanon directives and processes.
- Contribute to the development and implementation of DRC’s global development initiatives
- As and when required, substitute the Country Director when is requested as such (leaves, field visits, long meetings etc)

**DRC Dynamics ERP System**

- Ensure ERP functionality is properly used by relevant staff
- Apply reports and data analytics from DRC Dynamics to improve overall performance
- Act as heavy user for most of the Projects & Finance functionalities

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect the following:

*Required*

- Minimum 7 years’ experience in a similar role in an international NGO.
- 4 years’ experience in people management with proven leadership skills.
- Proven operational management experiences and capability, including in complex and emergency settings
- Proven significant financial, information and systems management experience as well as in procurement and tender processes
- Understanding and experience of institutional fundraising.
- Excellent communication, negotiation and problem-solving capacities; with the ability to work flexibly in a diverse team in a dynamic environment, fostering a positive working environment
- Strong capacity building, facilitation, and presentation skills with the ability to collaborate, network and negotiate in order to facilitate communication and support to staff, local partners, Governments, UN, donors & other NGOs without losing sight of the strategic objective
- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems
- Full professional proficiency in English and Arabic

*Desirable*

- Strong organizational and planning skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple competing deliverables on varying timelines
- Experience working in an ERP system, including Supply Chain, Finance and HR systems

**Languages**

- Full professional proficiency in English
- Full professional proficiency in Arabic

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Education**

A Master’s Degree or advanced professional qualification in Finance, Business Administration, Logistics or HR

**We offer**

- Contract length: 1 year
- Band: Management - E1
- Designation of Duty Station: Beirut - Lebanon
- Start date: ASAP

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for **national and expatriate employees.**

  
**DRC as an employer**  
By working in DRC, you will be joining a global workforce of around 6000 employees in approximately 30 countries. We pride ourselves on our:

- Professionalism, impact & expertise
- Humanitarian approach & the work we do
- Purpose, meaningfulness & own contribution
- Culture, values & strong leadership
- Fair compensation & continuous development

  
  
DRC’s capacity to ensure the protection of and assistance to refugees, IDP’s and other persons of concern depends on the ability of our staff to uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. DRC conducts thorough and comprehensive background checks as part of the recruitment process.  
  
**If you have questions or are facing problems with the online application process, please visit** [**drc.ngo/jobsupport**](https://drc.ngo/jobsupport)**.**  
  
  
***Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer and we consider all applicants based on individual merit and qualifications, regardless of personal characteristics or attributes. We are committed to increasing the diversity of our workforce, aiming for a 50% balance of men and women in management roles and ensuring that at least 50% of management roles are filled by national staff. We recognize that a diverse and inclusive team is crucial for achieving our organizational goals and making a positive impact on the communities we serve.***

jobs.title: MANAGER RÉGIONAL·E DES RESSOURCES HUMAINES – SAO (H/F)
Country Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.body:
**Position**: Country Finance Manager Lebanon

**Location**: Beirut, Lebanon

**Reporting Relationship**: Country Representative (Line Management) and Regional Finance Manager (Functional Management)

**Family Duty Station**: NO

**Starting date**: ASAP

**Application deadline**: 07/11/2026

**Working Context**

WeWorld has been working in Lebanon since 2006 and is currently supporting vulnerable refugee, IDP and host community populations through WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods, Local Economic Development, Education and Social Cohesion in Bekaa, Baalbek-Hermel, Akkar, Saida and Beirut. Our interventions span immediate emergency response and recovery in view of building preparedness and longer-term resilience for populations affected by conflict and/or displacement. The operation is run by over 50 employees, divided in three offices (Beirut, Zahle and Saida). We work closely with local partners, including NGOs and institutional actors at different levels, and are part of large consortia with other actors.

**Purpose of the Role**

The **Country Finance Manager** is responsible for all the administrative and accounting processes, including financial reporting, budget planning, development and monitoring. They manage staff within the Finance Department in country.

**MAIN FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES**

**General Administration**

- Track and manage deliverables and timelines related to grants, contracts, vendors, and partners
- Monitor grant administration to ensure compliance with reporting and expenditure requirements
- Supervise compliance of administrative documents and their proper filing
- Ensure the smooth flow of administrative information and data to the HQ
- Supervise flow of administrative information from project partners and the compliance with MoU
- Ensure smooth and punctual communications and reporting with local banks

**Accounting**

- Supervise and approve regular accounting, including monthly reconciliations, monthly and yearly closing of accounts, monthly journal entries
- Supervise cash and bank balance checking process when closing the monthly accounts

**Financial Reporting**

- Responsible for the preparation of financial reports, in coordination with Regional Finance Manager, and administrative team
- Ensure the compliance of financial reports with donors’ and internal rules and procedures

**Budget & Planning**

- Prepare and regularly monitor/updateWeWorld’s core budget for the Lebanon operation and provide an analysis to the Country Representativefocusing on gaps and risks
- Collaborate with the Country Representative, Head of Programmes and Project Managers to develop project budgets with quality, on time, in line with the operation’s core budget and according to donors’ regulations;
- Review administrative/financial terms of grant contracts before signature (payment & financial reporting schedule, etc.)
- Collaborate with the Head of Programmes, Project Managers and Procurement & Logistics Managers to regularly monitor actual and forecasted expenses against budget to avoid under and overspending on the projects in compliance withdonor flexibility rules
- Monitor financial flows of ongoing projects
- Anticipate financial risks, present budget updates and mitigation plans and report them to the Country Representative;
- Participate with the Country Management Team in reflecting on the evolution of the mission, and the programming of new projects and/or reorientation

**Audit Process**

- Collaborate to the management of financial audit performed on the projects
- Supervise yearly financial audit on general accounting for local authorities
- Prepare information and is directly responsible for any assessment/audit performed by donor on WeWorld administrative procedure

**Procedure**

- Design and implement administrative routines, procedures, and systems to increase efficiencies within the finance department, in particular relating to better structuring Budget Follow Ups, Forecasts, Payment Follow Ups and optimizing staff roles and responsibilities within the team
- Update the Local Operational Manual based on WeWorld procedures to implement organizational policies related to the Finance Department

**Operational**

- At Country level, liaise with the Human Resources and Procurement and Logistic departments for a fluid and collaborative collaboration
- Follow-up payments from donors and financial project close-out

**Human Resources**

- Participate in analyzing staffing needs & costs, compensation & benefits
- Supervise administrative and finance local personnel to complete routine tasks
- Capacity building of local finance staff and partner organizations in areas such as financial management, administration, good governance and management of accountability and transparency
- Support the Country Representative and the HR Manager to monitor and revise salary scale, if necessary

**Representation**

- Participate in inter-admin meetings with other INGOs and NGOs
- Ensure official representation for the administrative management of the Mission to the competent authorities

The duties and responsibilities set forth above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to perform additional duties requested by the Line Manager. Proper handover must be ensured before the end of the assignment.

**WHAT WE OFFER**

**Type of contract**: a first 6 (six) month collaboration contract subject to verification of the achievement of specific objectives (these objectives will be agreed together with the Line Manager upon arrival on assignment); a second collaboration contract of 6 (six) months renewable, following the positive evaluation of the first months of contract and availability of funds.

**Economic conditions**: according to WeWorld Expatriates Compensation Policy Base Salary (2950€ - 3550€ monthly) + Contributions reflecting role complexity and hardship level of the duty station + Housing contribution

**Wellbeing & Inclusion**: One day of paid menstrual leave per month. We promote a positive and inclusive work environment based on psychological safety, respect, and team empowerment.

**Flight ticket**: One round-trip air ticket every 12 months of service (between country of residence and duty station)

**Health insurance**: covered

**Family duty Station**: NO

**R&R**: NO

**Equal Opportunities**

We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive and respectful workplace where everyone has equal access to opportunities. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and organizational needs, without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, nationality, religion or belief, age, family or parental status, disability or any other status protected by applicable law.

We are committed to building talented teams and welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds.

**ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS**

**Qualifications and Knowledge**

- Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent experience in Financial/Accounting management
- Knowledge of institutional donor procedures (AICS, EU, AFD, UN)
- Fluent in English both written and verbal

**Professional experience**

- At least 5 years of specific experience in finance/administrative positions in the international cooperation sector, in similar roles and levels or responsibility
- Experience of representation to institutions and participation in coordination meetings
- Experience in budget design and management and monitoring of logistics procedures
- Experience in using accounting software
- Experience in managing teams

**Skills and Abilities**

- Strong flexibility and capacity to adapt behavior to the needs of the situation
- Capacity to work autonomously and in problems prevention/resolution
- Proven organizational skills and ability to effectively manage multiple tasks while fostering quality, team spirit and positive working relationships with colleagues
- Ability to identify, initiate and maintain good relationships with partner organizations, donors and national authorities including building professional relationships with senior decision-makers and influencers / leaders
- Good communication, negotiation skills and sensitivity in dealing with local institutions on critical issues
- Cultural, gender, religion, and age sensitivity and adaptability
- Strong commitment to the Mission of WeWorld, genuine interest for international cooperation development topics

**Desirable Requirements**

- Knowledge of Arabic would be considered an asset
- Previous experience in the Middle East Region is an asset

jobs.title: Country Representative
jobs.body:
Habitat for Humanity is looking for “**Country Representative**” that serves as primary country focal point of Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) and external representative in Jordan and is a key member of the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) leadership structure.

**1.Introduction and background:**

**Habitat for Humanity (HFH)** is an international nonprofit organization founded in 1976 as the world’s leader in addressing the housing challenges faced by vulnerable communities. Currently it operates in more than 60 countries around the world and brings people together to build more prosperous and vibrant communities by making sure everyone has a safe, affordable place to call home. Since its founding in 1976, it has helped more than 62 million people globally build their futures on their own terms through access to decent housing. HFH works alongside people of all walks of life to build, repair and finance their homes, by innovating new ways of building and financing, and by advocating for policies that make constructing and accessing housing easier for everyone.

HFHI works through a broad network of national Habitat organizations and other strategic partners, such as corporations, financial service providers, individuals, non-governmental organizations, foundations, local governments, as well as the private sector actors. HFHI supports program and project implementation by national HFH organizations and directly implements some projects and programs regionally. HFH started operating in Jordan in 1989 and has supported more than 48,000 households in 6 governorates across Jordan to improve their housing conditions in partnership with strategic local partners and community members.

**2. Position Description:**

The Country Representative (CR) reports to MENA Hub Director and supports the Director in identifying and nurturing relationships with country-based donors, local authorities, development partners, and target communities, all within the framework of HFHI’s regional and global strategies. Under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director, the CR is also responsible for leading country-level fundraising and resource mobilization efforts, while positioning HFHI as a housing thought leader in national dialogues and debates.

While the CR is also expected to deliver on standard country management tasks such as operational planning, financial and risk management, compliance, and safeguarding, our newly integrated model and structure require daily collaboration with MENA Hub staff on all the above.

The CR collaborates closely with thematic leads enabling and facilitating their technical leadership, and supports program managers in delivering against agreed objectives, embracing a people-centric approach.

**3.Scope of work and deliverables:**

**Strategic Alignment and Country Planning:**

1. Support overall strategic leadership for HFHI’s engagement in Jordan aligning country goals and plans with the MENA Strategy and HFHI global priorities.
2. Working closely with thematic leads to incorporating strategies and priorities into the overall country strategy, ensuring country plans reflect and operationalize agreed thematic approaches.
3. Support the annual country planning and budgeting process (for HFHI-funded work in-country), under the guidance of the MENA Hub Director and relevant Hub teams and monitor performance against approved plans.
4. Conduct regular country-level risk reviews, maintain a country risk register, develop mitigation plans, and escalate high/ “red” risks to the MENA Hub Director.

**Operation, Finance, Governance and Compliance:**

1. Oversee HFHI’s operational footprint in Jordan (offices, staff, contracts, and major activities), ensuring effective and efficient use of resources and compliance with HFHI standards, donor requirements and local legislation.
2. Ensure day-to-day operational compliance, local registration, and risk monitoring.
3. Provide day-to-day administrative line management for country-based staff, including leave approvals, budget oversight related to country operations, and coordination of operational support in line with HFH policies and procedures.
4. Ensure HFHI complies with all relevant registration, licensing, tax, and regulatory requirements in Jordan, working closely with the MENA Hub, Legal and Finance teams.
5. Enforce the Code of Conduct, Conflict of Interest, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies, ensuring they are understood and applied in day-to-day operations and partnerships.
6. Oversee basic financial management and internal controls for HFHI operations in-country, including oversight of budgets, expenditures, and financial reporting to the MENA Hub
7. Ensure procurement, contracting and vendor management for HFHI activities in Jordan comply with HFHI and donor policies, and that value for money, transparency and fairness are upheld.
8. Implement and oversee HFHI global safety and security standards for all HFHI staff, consultants, and visitors in-country, including maintaining country security plans, contact trees and incident protocols.
9. Ensure prompt reporting, investigation and follow-up of safeguarding and security incidents in line with HFHI policies and national law.
10. Coordinate external and internal audits related to HFHI’s country presence and support the timely closure of audit findings and implementation of management actions.

**Program Implementation Oversight, Resources mobilization and Partnership:**

1. Support local funding opportunities relevant to Jordan (institutional donors, multilaterals, private sector, foundations, etc.) and share intelligence with the MENA Hub.
2. Network and coalition building.
3. Support the development of country-level concept notes and project proposals, and support HFHI’s participation in multi-country or regional proposals that include Jordan.
4. Support the identification, scoping and design of quality projects in Jordan, aligned with HFHI’s priorities and in collaboration with the MENA Hub Subject Matter Experts (SMEs)
5. Map and engage potential donors, partners, and stakeholders in Jordan (government, private sector, financial service providers, civil society, faith organizations, academia, UN and other international actors)
6. Maintain a country partnership mapping and engagement tracker, including pipelines, contacts and agreed follow-up actions.
7. Facilitate the negotiation of country-level Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and partnership agreements, in coordination with the MENA Hub, Legal Programs and Finance.

**Advocacy, Policy Engagement & External Representation:**

1. In coordination with the MENA Hub Director and HFHI Advocacy teams, support the development and implementation of a national advocacy and policy engagement plan aligned with regional advocacy priorities (e.g. housing policy, housing finance, urban development, resilience).
2. From an advocacy perspective, supports building and maintaining relationships with government counterparts, donors, United Nations (UN) agencies, European Union (EU) delegations, financial institutions, sector networks, civil society organizations, and other policy stakeholders at country level.
3. Represent HFHI in national forums, sector working groups, donor coordination platforms and, where appropriate, media opportunities, positioning HFHI as a credible housing and urban development actor in Jordan.
4. Support the development and implementation of a country communications approach that promotes HFHI’s brand, programs and advocacy messaging, and provides content for regional and global communications.
5. Ensuring advocacy and communication efforts are evidence-based, reflecting learning and impact from HFHI-supported programs and partnerships in Jordan.

**People Leadership, Culture and Volunteer Engagement:**

1. Provide direction, support to any HFH staff and consultants based in Jordan, fostering a culture of accountability, inclusion, learning and safeguarding.
2. In collaboration with Regional Human Resources (HR), support recruitment, onboarding, performance management and development of country-based staff and key consultants, as applicable.
3. Model and promote HFHI’s values and commitments to safeguarding, diversity, equity and inclusion in all country-level interactions and decisions.
4. Where applicable, support planning and hosting of HFHI-associated volunteer builds and events in Jordan, ensuring that they are safe, ethical, and aligned with HFHI standards and community priorities.
5. Ensure volunteer activities comply with safeguarding and duty-of-care standards, and that relevant stories and data are captured for visibility and fundraising purposes.

**4.Required Skills & Competencies:**

1. Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, combined with substantial professional experience in international development, organizational leadership, or a related area. An advanced degree is an asset.
2. Experience:
    - 7-10 years of progressively responsible experience in international development, including at least 5 years in a senior leadership or management role.
    - Experience with traditional and emerging institutional donors including the Gulf countries.
    - Proven experience in resource mobilization including donor engagement and proposal development.
    - Experience managing diverse teams remotely.
    - A proven track record of both winning and executing multimillion projects.
    - Extensive experience working in Jordan's international development sector, with a strong understanding of the local operating environment, stakeholder landscape, and partnership networks.
    - Ability to adapt a changing environment and navigating market turbulences.
    - Management of teams and experience operating in a matrix structure.
    - Excellent written and spoken English and Arabic language.
    - Experience working with private philanthropy is an asset.
    - Previous experience in a hub structure is a plus.
3. Active support for **HFHI Values**:

**Humility** – We are part of something bigger than ourselves,

**Courage** – We do what’s right, even when it is difficult or unpopular,

**Accountability** – We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission),

***Safeguarding:***

*HFHI requires that all employees take seriously their ethical responsibilities to safeguarding our intended beneficiaries, their communities, and all those with whom we work*

*Managers at all levels have responsibilities to support and develop systems that create and maintain an environment that prevents harassment, sexual exploitation and abuse, safeguards the rights of beneficiaries and community members (especially children), and promotes the implementation of Habitat for Humanity’s code of conduct).*

jobs.title: CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director
jobs.body:
## Candidates must currently reside in Indonesia.

**Position Title**: CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director

**Hiring Organization:** CORE, Inc. to be paid from the US

**Type of Employment:** Full-time consultancy.

**Duration of Contract:** November 1, 2026 – August 31, 2027 (with the possibility of extension)

**Duty Station:** Jakarta, Indonesia (with frequent travel to project-supported regions)

**Reports to:** CGPP Global Deputy Director

## **Background**

The CORE Group Partners Project (CGPP) is a multi-country, multi-partner initiative that provides on-the-ground technical assistance and guidance to support host country efforts to strengthen immunization systems, disease surveillance, and essential community-based health services. Globally, CGPP works across five technical areas (polio, maternal and child health, nutrition, malaria, and global health security) through existing networks of international and local NGOs operating in hard-to-reach areas with low immunization coverage. At the country level, a Secretariat coordinates the work of CGPP partner organizations in a manner that complements the efforts of all implementing partners. In Indonesia, CGPP supports national health strategies by strengthening routine immunization and polio eradication efforts while promoting maternal and child health through integrated community-based interventions.

## Consultancy Purpose

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director will be based in Jakarta, Indonesia and support CGPP National Program Manager and Provincial Team Leaders in operations in Indonesia to improve maternal and child health (MCH) outcomes in the selected districts of Papua and East Java provinces or any other selected CGPP work areas in Indonesia.

Serving as CGPP’s senior in-country representative, the CGPP Secretariat Director will maintain close coordination with government and the US Department of State (DOS) Foreign Assistance team.

The CGPP Indonesia Secretariat Director will provide leadership across all aspects of project planning and implementation and will maintain and strengthen CGPP's relationship with key partners and stakeholders. These include the Government of Indonesia’s Ministry of Health (and other relevant government ministries) the US Department of State (US DOS), UNICEF, STRIDES implemented by FHI 360, other Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI) partners, and Wahana Visi/ World Vision (WV) Indonesia.

In fulfilling this role, the Secretariat Director will ensure that:

- CGPP activities address stated project objectives, support national MCH and polio priorities, and are aligned with global MCH and polio objectives; and
- The needs and concerns of CGPP field teams and the communities they serve for all program related needs are effectively communicated to decisionmakers at all levels.

## Key Responsibilities

The Secretariat Director will be responsible for the following:

- **Strategic Leadership**  
    Provide strategic leadership for CGPP programming in Indonesia, in coordination with the CGPP global headquarters team, and CGPP National Program Manager including guiding the development of technical priorities and strategic plans that expand access to lifesaving services, strengthen routine immunization systems, and improve maternal and child health outcomes through integrated and sustainable approaches aligned with national and global priorities.
- **Government and Donor Engagement**  
    Lead institutional engagement with the Ministry of Health and relevant national and subnational structures, as well as with US DOS-Foreign Assistance.
- **Secretariat Leadership and Capacity Strengthening**  
    Provide leadership, mentorship, and oversight performance management for the CGPP National Program Manager; ensure the adequacy and quality of capacity strengthening for field-level teams and guide continuous improvement of implementation approaches.
- **Program Oversight, Quality, and Integration**  
    Provide oversight to the CGPP National Program Manager to effectively track progress toward CGPP MCH and polio goals, ensuring high-quality, coordinated implementation across program areas, and guide adjustments to strategies and approaches based on performance, risk analysis, and evolving context.
- **Planning, Budgeting, and Accountability**  
    Review, approve, and oversee implementation of the activities as per approved annual work plans and budgets, ensuring coherence, feasibility, alignment with agreed priorities, and adherence to approved budgets, with proactive identification of risks and timely course correction as needed.
- **Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning**  
    Oversee monitoring, evaluation, and learning activities, including planned CGPP assessments/ evaluations; ensure data quality and validation processes; guide the interpretation and use of data and evidence to inform strategic, technical, and operational decision-making; and work closely with the CGPP MEAL Officer to align workflows, strengthen MEAL capacity across secretariat and partner teams, coordinate partner support, and maintain MEAL standards in data quality and reporting across all partners.
- **Partner Coordination and Representation**  
    Serve as the focal point for strategic coordination and engagement with national and international stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, and peer organizations; represent CGPP in relevant technical, policy, and coordination platforms; and sustain informal engagements with government counterparts and peer organizations, including cultivating ongoing informal communication channels to strengthen relationships, identify emerging issues, and foster trust and collaboration across stakeholders.
- **Reporting and Knowledge Management**  
    Ensure timely preparation and submission of required CGPP reports and briefings; validate monthly data updates, performance indicators, and partner-reported results; and oversee systematic documentation, timely synthesis, and dissemination of policy developments, coordination outcomes, and lessons learned as well as key discussions, decisions, action points, and follow-up items arising from all secretariat engagements – including technical coordination meetings, internal secretariat discussions, partner consultations, stakeholder engagements, and informal coordination touchpoints – to strengthen transparency, institutional memory, and accountability.

## Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

- **Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership** for complex, multi-partner initiatives, with strong analytical judgment and systems thinking to navigate ambiguity, risk, and competing priorities.
- **Exceptional relationship management and diplomatic skills**, with the ability to build trust, influence outcomes, and manage alignment across diverse stakeholders, including government counterparts, donors, implementing partners, and civil society organizations.
- **Proven ability to lead, mentor, and hold accountable senior and multidisciplinary teams**, fostering a culture of collaboration, performance, learning, and results in complex operating environments.
- **Strong executive communication and representation skills**, with demonstrated ability to synthesize complex information, brief senior decisionmakers and donors, and represent the Secretariat credibly in high-level national and international forums.
- **Demonstrated capacity to convene, align, and harmonize partners** around shared lifesaving priorities, ensuring integrated approaches and avoiding fragmentation or vertical implementation.
- **Sound judgment and decision-making capacity**, including the ability to make timely, evidence-informed decisions with significant organizational, financial, and reputational implications.

## Preferred Qualifications

- **Experience leading or supporting a secretariat or partnership platform**, including stewardship of collective decision-making processes across multiple institutions.
- **Demonstrated experience navigating complex political or institutional environments**, including managing sensitivities across government, donors, and implementing organizations.
- **Experience leading programs during periods of transition or uncertainty**, such as scale-up, funding shifts, public health emergencies, or changes in government or donor priorities.

## Required Languages

- **English** (Required): Advanced professional proficiency required, with ability to communicate effectively in meetings, presentations, and written reports with international stakeholders.
- **Bahasa Indonesia** (Required): Professional proficiency in speaking, reading, and writing.

## Travel

- Must be willing and able to travel approximately 30% to 50% of the time.

## Supervisory Responsibilities

- Will supervise staff as assigned.

## Working Relationships

- Within CGPP Indonesia (e.g., National Program Manager, MEAL Officer, Provincial Team Leaders), Wahana Visi leadership, and finance, procurement, and grants teams.
- External: Ministry of Health and relevant provincial, district, and local MOH, US DOS, GPEI partners, and others.
- CGPP Global Secretariat Team: Coordinate with the global secretariat team and Asia regional team and obtain technical guidance as needed.

## Qualifications

- Master's degree in public health or a related technical field.
- At least 12 years of progressively responsible experience, including at least five years in a senior management or leadership role, overseeing multidisciplinary teams in international and/or multicultural settings.
- Demonstrated experience providing strategic leadership and operational oversight for complex programs or initiatives.
- Demonstrated experience working with or supporting governance structures and engaging effectively with government counterparts and institutional partners.
- Proven experience in managing donor-funded programs, including compliance with donor regulations, financial accountability, audits, and high-quality reporting.
- Strong knowledge and experience in budget management and financial oversight.
- Technical expertise and demonstrated experience in maternal and child health (MCH), combined with strong familiarity with the Indonesian health system and context.
- Ability to use data, evidence, and learning to inform strategic decision-making and program improvement.
- Proficiency in standard office and data analysis software.
- Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills, with demonstrated ability to represent organizations at senior national and international levels and to build effective partnerships with donors, government, and implementing partners.

## Disclaimer

- This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.

jobs.title: Consultor Experto en Diseño de Ejercicios y Preparación ante Crisis
jobs.body:
## Términos de Referencia (TdR)

**Título**: **Consultoría –** Consultor Experto en Diseño de Ejercicios y Preparación ante Crisis

**Fecha en que se emite la convocatoria**: 30 de septiembre de 2026

**Fecha de cierre**:30 de octubre de 2026

**Mecanismo de contratación**: Consultoría

**1.ANTECEDENTES**

La Fundación Panamericana para el Desarrollo (PADF) busca crear un hemisferio justo, pacífico y próspero donde todas las personas tengan la oportunidad de prosperar. Trabajamos con personas vulnerables en todo el hemisferio para abordar algunos de los mayores desafíos de desarrollo de nuestra región. Nos asociamos, empoderamos y capacitamos a la sociedad civil, los gobiernos y el sector privado para el bien mayor de los pueblos de América Latina y el Caribe.

**VISIÓN**

Fortalecer la preparación y capacidad de coordinación de las instituciones civiles panameñas para anticipar, gestionar y responder de manera articulada a crisis que puedan afectar la continuidad y resiliencia del Canal de Panamá y su infraestructura crítica. A través de un ciclo progresivo de ejercicios, aprendizaje y mejora, la consultoría contribuirá a consolidar capacidades institucionales sostenibles y a desarrollar un marco conjunto de preparación y respuesta ante crisis.

**Descripción de la posición**

Como parte de la implementación de CANAL READY – Strengthening Panama Canal Crisis Preparedness and Response, un programa de 24 meses orientado a fortalecer las capacidades de las autoridades civiles panameñas para prepararse, coordinar y responder ante amenazas físicas, cibernéticas, geopolíticas y ambientales que puedan afectar el Canal de Panamá y la infraestructura crítica asociada, PADF contratará a un/a Líder Senior de Diseño de Ejercicios y Preparación ante Crisis, con base en la Ciudad de Panamá.

La supervisión técnica, programática y operativa de la consultoría estará a cargo del área temática de Paz, Justicia y Seguridad (PJS), con sede en Washington, D.C. Para facilitar una adecuada implementación y articulación a nivel país, el consultor/a requerirá coordinación con la oficina nacional de PADF en Panamá.

**2. ESPECIFICACIONES**

**Objetivos de la consultoría**

Brindar servicios técnicos especializados para diseñar, preparar, facilitar, evaluar y documentar ejercicios y actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades que contribuyan a mejorar la coordinación interinstitucional ante amenazas físicas, cibernéticas, geopolíticas y ambientales que puedan afectar el Canal de Panamá y la infraestructura crítica circundante.

### Alcances:

- Diseñar una metodología integral para el ciclo de ejercicios, incluyendo diagnóstico de capacidades, definición de objetivos, desarrollo de escenarios, validación técnica, preparación de participantes, ejecución, evaluación, informe posterior y plan de mejora.
- Realizar consultas, revisión documental y análisis de amenazas, vulnerabilidades, capacidades, dependencias y consecuencias relacionadas con el Canal de Panamá y la infraestructura crítica circundante, incluidos puentes, represas, carreteras, ferrocarriles, plantas eléctricas y líneas de transmisión.
- Diseñar ejercicios de mesa, simulaciones, escenarios y otras actividades apropiadas para autoridades civiles de nivel medio y superior, de acuerdo con los objetivos, resultados e indicadores del proyecto.
- Desarrollar los materiales técnicos requeridos para cada ejercicio, incluyendo situaciones iniciales, eventos, líneas de tiempo, preguntas de decisión, mapas de actores, matrices de roles, guías de facilitación, manuales de participantes, instrumentos de observación y criterios de evaluación.
- Incorporar en los escenarios amenazas físicas, cibernéticas, geopolíticas y ambientales, así como efectos en cascada, dependencias intersectoriales y necesidades de coordinación bilateral e interinstitucional.
- Asegurar, en el marco de los servicios contratados, que los escenarios desarrollados se mantengan dentro del alcance civil autorizado por el proyecto y no constituyan capacitación, asistencia operativa ni apoyo prohibido para fuerzas militares o policiales.
- Facilitar técnicamente los ejercicios y actividades programadas, manteniendo el enfoque en toma de decisiones, coordinación, comunicación, continuidad de operaciones y recuperación.
- Preparar sesiones de orientación para facilitadores, evaluadores y participantes sobre objetivos, supuestos, roles, reglas de participación, confidencialidad y criterios de desempeño.
- Facilitar y apoyar técnicamente los procesos de validación técnica de escenarios y materiales con especialistas sectoriales y representantes institucionales autorizados, resguardando la información reservada o sensible.
- Diseñar y aplicar, en coordinación con el equipo de Monitoreo, Evaluación y Aprendizaje (MEL), instrumentos de evaluación pre y post actividad, rúbricas de observación, encuestas y otras herramientas para medir cambios en capacidades y coordinación.
- Conducir sesiones de retroalimentación posteriores a los ejercicios y elaborar informes con hallazgos, lecciones aprendidas, recomendaciones y acciones de mejora.
- Elaborar y actualizar una matriz consolidada de brechas de capacidad, buenas prácticas, lecciones aprendidas, acciones de mejora, responsables sugeridos y avances identificados.
- Brindar asesoría técnica respecto de los requisitos, secuencia metodológica, perfiles de participantes, recursos, riesgos y criterios de calidad aplicables a cada actividad.
- Proporcionar servicios técnicos especializados para desarrollar el contenido y los componentes técnicos del plan conjunto Facilitar la revisión técnica y validación del plan conjunto con las partes autorizadas, incorporando las lecciones obtenidas de los ejercicios y resguardando la información sensible.
- Preparar insumos técnicos para informes, presentaciones y reuniones del proyecto, cuando sean requeridos por PADF.

**Perfil Requerido:**

- Título universitario en gestión de emergencias, gestión de riesgos, seguridad, continuidad de operaciones, ingeniería, ciberseguridad, relaciones internacionales, políticas públicas o carreras afines. Se valorará maestría en áreas relacionadas.
- Mínimo diez (10) años de experiencia profesional en preparación y respuesta ante crisis, gestión de emergencias, continuidad de operaciones, resiliencia de infraestructura crítica o áreas afines.
- Mínimo diez (10) años de experiencia comprobable en diseño, facilitación y evaluación de ejercicios de mesa, simulaciones o ejercicios interinstitucionales para participantes de nivel medio y superior.
- Experiencia en desarrollo de escenarios multimodales, elaboración de informes posteriores a ejercicios, lecciones aprendidas y planes de mejora.
- Experiencia de trabajo con instituciones gubernamentales y equipos multidisciplinarios. Se valorará experiencia en Panamá o Centroamérica y conocimiento del Canal de Panamá o de sistemas de infraestructura crítica.
- Experiencia en al menos dos de las siguientes áreas: amenazas físicas, ciberseguridad o tecnología operacional, riesgos geopolíticos y amenazas ambientales.
- Dominio profesional del español e inglés, con capacidad para facilitar sesiones técnicas y elaborar productos de alta calidad en ambos idiomas.
- Se valorarán certificaciones en diseño de ejercicios, gestión de emergencias, continuidad del negocio, gestión de riesgos, ciberseguridad o metodologías equivalentes.

**Productos Esperados:**

- Plan de trabajo y metodología integral para el diseño, facilitación y evaluación de ejercicios.
- Diagnóstico técnico de amenazas, vulnerabilidades, capacidades, dependencias y brechas relevantes para el diseño de las actividades.
- Paquetes técnicos para cada ejercicio, incluyendo escenarios, guías de facilitación, manuales de participantes, matrices de roles, instrumentos de observación y criterios de evaluación.
- Informes posteriores a cada ejercicio, con hallazgos, lecciones aprendidas, recomendaciones y acciones de mejora.
- Matriz consolidada y actualizada de lecciones aprendidas, brechas de capacidad, buenas prácticas y avances.
- Borrador técnico del plan conjunto de preparación y respuesta ante crisis.
- Versión final validada del plan conjunto de preparación y respuesta ante crisis.
- Informe final de consultoría, con el resumen de actividades, productos entregados, resultados, riesgos y recomendaciones.

**Precio y Duración del contrato:**

- El costo del contrato es de USD $3,000 mensual. El periodo del contrato es de 11 meses con la posibilidad de una renovación de hasta 12 meses adicionales para el segundo año - sujeta a desempeño satisfactorio y disponibilidad de fondos.

**Forma de Pago:**

- Los pagos se realizarán de manera mensual contra entrega de informe de actividades y productos, previa aprobación técnica. Se incluirán los costos asociados a la impresión de materiales y actividades de divulgación.

**Lugar de Prestación del Servicio:**

Principalmente en Ciudad de Panamá con modalidad híbrida (presencial y remota) según las necesidades del servicio.

**3. CRITERIOS DE EVALUACIÓN**

**Criterios de elegibilidad - Puntuación (de 100)**

- Experiencia en diseño, facilitación y evaluación de ejercicios de mesa, simulaciones o ejercicios interinstitucionales - 30 puntos
- Experiencia en preparación y respuesta ante crisis, continuidad de operaciones, gestión de emergencias o resiliencia de infraestructura crítica - 30 puntos
- Propuesta - 30 puntos
- Formación académica, certificaciones y dominio profesional de español e inglés - 10 puntos

**4. PROPIEDAD INTELECTUAL**

Al profesional le queda prohibido cualquier tipo de publicación, divulgación o comercialización de los productos objeto de esta contratación pues se entenderá que pasará a ser propiedad de PADF, de la misma forma le queda prohibida la divulgación de información confidencial que llegue a su conocimiento como parte de la ejecución de sus actividades.

**5. DETALLES PARA LA PRESENTACIÓN**

1. **Fecha límite**: 30 de octubre de 2026
2. **Documentos a presentar**: Las entidades aplicantes deberán incluir:
    1. Hoja de información (Apéndice 1. Información del Proveedor)
    2. Experiencia en el desarrollo de productos similares
    3. Perfil del consultor (se debe adjuntar la hoja de vida del consultor)
3. **Envío de propuestas**: Las personas aplicantes deben enviar estos documentos al correo **operaciones-pan@padf.org**con el asunto: PROPUESTA DE CONSULTORÍA – LÍDER EXPERTO EN CRISIS
4. **Consultas**. Las personas aplicantes pueden enviar consultas a este mismo correo hasta el 22 de octubre de 2026.

**6. TÉRMINOS Y CONDICIONES**

**Adjudicación resultante**

Este documento de solicitud no obliga a PADF a ejecutar ningún contrato ni orden de compra ni compromete a PADF a pagar ningún costo incurrido en la preparación o presentación de aplicaciones. Además, PADF se reserva el derecho de rechazar cualesquiera y todas las ofertas si considera que tal medida conviene a los intereses de PADF. PADF seleccionará la propuesta ganadora a su discreción y no está obligado a divulgar los resultados de las evaluaciones individuales.

**Confidencialidad**

Toda la información de propiedad exclusiva proporcionada será tratada de manera confidencial y no se divulgará a ningún solicitante potencial ni existente durante el proceso de convocatoria.

Esto incluye, pero no se limita, cotizaciones de precios, propuestas de costos y propuestas técnicas. PADF podrá, pero no está obligado a hacerlo, publicar adjudicaciones de adquisiciones en su sitio web público luego de que haya concluido el proceso de convocatoria y se haya adjudicado el contrato. Los resultados de la evaluación de PADF son confidenciales y la puntuación de los solicitantes no se compartirá con los licitantes.

**Protección contra la explotación y el abuso sexuales (PEAS)**

Como parte de los controles internos y las normas de conducta de empleados, el contratista debe cerciorarse de que sus empleados se adhieran a estas normas de conducta de una manera conforme con las normas para empleados de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas (ONU) que figuran en la Sección 3 del Boletín del secretario general de la ONU—Medidas especiales de protección contra la explotación y el abuso sexual (ST/SGB/2003/13).

**Contratación de empresas pequeñas, de propiedad de minorías y de propiedad de mujeres**

PADF tomará todas las medidas necesarias para garantizar que se usen, siempre que sea posible, empresas de propiedad de minorías, empresas de propiedad de mujeres y empresas locales con excedente de mano de obra.

**Exclusiones y suspensiones**

Las ofertas de aquellas entidades que aparezcan en cualesquiera listas de exclusión, del Sistema de Administración de Subvenciones (SAM), de la Oficina de Control de Activos Extranjeros (OFAC), de Sanciones de la ONU u otras listas de observación no se evaluarán y las entidades no serán elegibles para recibir ninguna subvención que pueda surgir de esta Solicitud de Cotizaciones.
