jobs.title: Psychiatrist or Clinical Psychologist - West Africa
jobs.body:
**Position summary:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is anticipating a project in West Africa with a focus on managing the flow of migrants into the region. Included in the project’s objectives will be structured movement and resettlement of migrants within and outside Guinea-Bissau, while providing basic food, shelter and other humanitarian assistance.

SFL is seeking a clinical psychologist to provide mental health and social support to migrants in West Africa. The clinical psychologist will be responsible for designing and implementing a psychological and psychosocial support program for migrants who are navigating displacement and resettlement. This role involves providing direct clinical care, occasional crisis intervention, and building the capacity of local staff to ensure culturally appropriate mental health services during the resettlement process. The position will be based in Bissau, Guinea-Bissau.

**Areas of Responsibility:**

- Conduct psychological assessments and provide professional mental health support to newly arrived and transitioning migrants, with referral to in-country medical professionals if needed.
- Develop and implement support protocols for individuals experiencing stress or trauma.
- Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, including medical staff as needed, to ensure a holistic approach to migrant well-being and basic needs.
- Conduct psychoeducational workshops to help migrants cope with acculturative stress, build resilience, and prepare for resettlement in new host countries.
- Maintain strictly confidential clinical records and monitor mental health trends within the migrant population to adapt programs and inform SFL management.

**Education and Experience Requirements:**

- Medical doctor degree (M.D., D.O., or M.B.B.S.) with Psychiatry residency, Master’s degree or Doctorate (Ph.D. or Psy.D.) in Clinical Psychology from an accredited institution.
- Valid professional license to practice clinical psychology in your home jurisdiction.
- Minimum of 3 to 5 years of post-graduate clinical experience, specifically focusing on trauma, displacement, or working with refugee/migrant populations.
- Must be fluent in English (written and spoken), with a working knowledge of Spanish. Additional language skills relevant to the demographic context (e.g., French, Portuguese) are a plus.
- Proven experience working in humanitarian emergencies, international development, or low-resource, post-conflict settings.
- Experience in cross-cultural counseling and effectively conducting clinical sessions with the assistance of language interpreters.

**Personal Skills and Abilities:**

- Exceptional cross-cultural communication skills and sensitivity to the diverse religious, cultural, and social backgrounds of multi-national migrants.
- Strong adaptability and psychological resilience, with the capacity to thrive in a dynamic and challenging physical environment with limited local amenities.
- High emotional intelligence and the ability to maintain strong professional boundaries to prevent burnout in a high-stress environment.
- Collaborative leadership style with the ability for capacity-building and empowering local staff for assistance.
- Sound judgment, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to make rapid clinical decisions independently in the event of crises.
- Commitment to the humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, as well as the core mission of Shelter For Life International.

SFL is interested in applicants whose professional ethics, values, and determination to achieve impact are evident and aligned with organizational priorities.

Additional Notes:

- A minimum of 12 months' commitment to live and work in Guinea-Bissau is required.
- Applicants must be comfortable with travel within the project area.
- Competitive pay and benefits, including paid time off, ACA-compliant health insurance, and housing allowance.

Job description in PDF here: [https://shorturl.at/gYIwz](https://shorturl.at/gYIwz)

**About us:**

Shelter For Life International (SFL) is an international faith-based relief and development organization with over 30 years’ experience providing sustainable development and humanitarian assistance to post-conflict countries worldwide. We are currently operational in Afghanistan, The Gambia, and Ukraine, with headquarters located in Minnetonka, MN, USA. Our team provides support and assistance in the following areas:

1. Population Movement and Settlement
2. Public Infrastructure Reconstruction
3. Economic and Social Development

Our mission is to demonstrate God’s love by enabling people affected by conflict and disaster to restore their lives and rebuild their communities. To learn more about us, please visit [www.shelter.org](http://www.shelter.org/)

jobs.title: Technical Advisor I, Cash & Markets
jobs.body:
**NOTE: The Pay Range referenced in this job announcement only applies to applicants who perform the job within the US and to applicants classified by CRS as International Assignees. Staff hired on local payroll would follow the respective Country pay range. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your anticipated work location during the candidate selection process.**

**Pay Range**  
$71,349 - $88,085 Annually

**NOTE: This is a remote position, with a preference for candidates based in the LACRO and EMEA regions; CRS will also give preference to candidates who are based in countries where we have existing offices. CRS does not sponsor visas for remote employees.**

Catholic Relief Services is implementing a global emergency response initiative designed to deliver timely, lifesaving humanitarian assistance in rapidly evolving crises worldwide. Over 18 months, the program enables fast, flexible action to address urgent needs arising from sudden shocks and protracted emergencies. It supports critical humanitarian sectors through context-appropriate assistance while emphasizing operational readiness, locally led implementation, accountability to affected communities, and safe, dignified programming. The initiative strengthens the organization’s ability to respond at speed and scale in complex and resource-constrained environments, ensuring help reaches people most in need when it matters most. This role will support cash readiness efforts of Country Programs and partners, as well as provide technical support for ongoing programming, and new emergency programs, related to cash, market-based programming, and emergency food security and livelihoods.

**Job Summary:**

This position is embedded in the Humanitarian Response Department (HRD) Market-based Rapid Response and Recovery (MBRRR) Team. The HRD MBRRR Team is the agency lead for Cash & Market-based Programming and the emergency Food Security & Livelihoods Sectors. As part of this team, you will provide technical advice and support to a range of program design and implementation issues in Cash & Markets as well as Food Security & Livelihoods, in line with Catholic Relief Services (CRS) program quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices to Country Program (CP) teams and partners to advance the delivery of high-quality humanitarian assistance programming to the poor and vulnerable impacted by crises. Your advice, knowledge, and support will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive, and innovative CRS’ Cash and Market-based programming is across the agency.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Support the development and contribute to the implementation of agency-wide strategies, standards, tools, and best practices in relation to Cash and Market Based Programming that effectively engage partners, donors, and governments. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, protection mainstreaming, and disaster risk reduction.
- Provide programmatic and operational (including administrative and finance) technical solutions to CP teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools and M&E, helping to ensure high-quality implementation.
- Contribute to, and in some cases lead, the development of the technical design for proposals. Support the process of preparation, design, submission and approval of project concepts and full-fledged proposals. As needed, act as a technical writer on proposal development teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technical requirements into CRS’ approach.
- Support capacity strengthening initiatives in relation to Cash and Market based programming for staff and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and coaching.
- Collect and analyze program data, capture, and share lessons learned and best practices for specific projects to facilitate improvements in decision-making and contribute to the Cash and Market Based Programming learning agenda.
- Contribute to maintaining relationships with donors, peer organizations, research, and other institutions, participate in forums in the area of Cash and Market Based Programming to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work.
- Support Country Programs and partners in strengthening their cash readiness through targeted technical support, particularly in relation to developing capacities, identifying suitable cash delivery mechanisms and Financial Service Providers (FSPs), developing Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and tools, and supporting the design and implementation of pilot cash programs.

***Knowledge, Skills and Abilities***

- Strong relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings
- Good strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Good technical writing skills
- Presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented

***Required Languages*** – English and Spanish required. French, Portuguese and Arabic highly desired.

***Travel*** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 50%, including at short notice and to emergency situations.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor's Degree in humanitarian assistance, social policy, economics or related field required.
- Minimum of five-eight years relevant work experience with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO, with minimum of two years relevant emergency response and field-based experience in cash and market-based programming, including in protracted and rapid onset crisis contexts.
- Experienced trainer in CVA Programming. Knowledge of technical principles and concepts in cash and market-based programming, including experience with multiple CVA delivery mechanisms.
- Demonstrated experience in designing CVA Programs, particularly for US Government funding, and designing and implementing Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) or sectoral cash and voucher programs related to Food Security, Livelihoods, Shelter or WASH sectors. Experience in other sectoral cash programming, such as Nutrition, DRR, and/or Protection, desirable. Experience with e-voucher platforms highly desirable.
- Knowledge of, and experience in, conducting market assessments and response analysis to inform modality decisions across different areas of programming, particularly in emergency rapid-onset humanitarian contexts.
- Experience in innovative project design for rapid response with market-based programming in a diversity of contexts.
- Experience in proposal development, for government and/or private donors.
- Knowledge of capacity strengthening and technical accompaniment best practices, with a focus on collaboration and supporting partner-led responses.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based and civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), data analytics and PowerBi.
- Master's Degree in humanitarian assistance, social policy, economics or related field is an advantage.

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

**Agency Leadership Competencies:**

- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

**What we offer**

CRS offers U.S. based staff a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, life insurance, vision, and a generous retirement savings plan. Benefits packages for successful candidates employed outside the U.S. are based on the country of employment/in-country office where the candidate will perform the role. CRS´ work culture is a collaborative, mission-driven culture committed to improving the lives of the poor throughout the world.

jobs.body:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**

In this senior leadership role, you will shape the strategic direction of Inclusive Community Support and Care, Inclusive Education, and Inclusive Livelihood, strengthen CBM’s leadership in disability-inclusive development, and drive greater impact for persons with disabilities through community-based approaches worldwide.

**This full-time position is only filled locally in one of CBM permanent established entities.** (ex: Bensheim (Germany), UK (Cambridge or remote), Nairobi (Kenya), Abuja (Nigeria), Lomé (Togo), Yaoundé (Cameroon), Lusaka (Zambia), Addis Abeba (Ethiopia), Guatemala City, Kampala (Uganda), Niamey (Niger), etc.).

jobs.title: TCA - COORDINATEUR TERRAIN (H/F) - EST TCHAD
jobs.body:
**Que faisons nous ...**

**Date de début souhaitée :** 16/11/2026  
**Durée de la mission:** 5 mois  
**Localisation:** Iriba

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

**La mission**

SI est présente au Tchad depuis 2008, au Cameroun depuis 2014 et en Centrafrique depuis 2007. Les missions Tchad et Cameroun ont fusionné en 2021 et la Centrafrique à rejoint cette fusion en 2025. La mission multi-pays Tchad-Cameroun-Centrafrique (TCA) est composée de 10 bases/sous-bases au total. Au Cameroun: 1 base de coordination mission à Yaoundé et 1 base opérationnelle à Maroua dans l'Extrême Nord, ainsi qu'une sous-base à Makary. Au Tchad: 1 bureau de coordination zone Tchad à Ndjaména, et 4 bases opérationnelles à Bagasola dans la province du Lac, et Adré, Iriba et Amdjarass dans l'est du pays. En RCA: 1 bureau de coordination zone RCA à Bangui, et 3 bases opérationnelles à Markounda dans le Nord-Ouest, à Bouar dans l'Ouest et à Zémio dans le Haut-Mbomou.

SI est présente au Tchad depuis 2008 et dispose actuellement de 4 bases opérationelles à Bagasola (Lac), Adré (Ouaddai), Iriba (Wadi Fira) et Amdjarass (Ennedi Est). À l’Est, la réponse de SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL a visé à améliorer l'accès des réfugiés soudanais et populations tchadiennes à l'eau potable, aux services d'assainissement et à des conditions d'hygiène améliorées, afin de prévenir la propagation des maladies diarrhéiques. Une assistance d’urgence en réponse à l’épidémie de choléra a également été mise en œuvre par les équipes au second semestre de 2025. Bailleurs : ECHO, CDCS, SDC, FHRAOC, PWC, Sida

**Descriptif de l'offre**

DIMENSIONNEMENT DE L'EQUIPE EN BASE / COORDINATION :

Est Tchad: CT, Adjoint CT Prog, Log Manager, Admin Manage, Assist log (Adré, Iriba), Assist fin (Adré, Iriba), Gestionnaire log (Iriba), Gestionnaire fin (Iriba), RP et équipes prog (Adré, Iriba, Amdjarass), chargé de liaison (Iriba uniquement)  
Ndjamena : DZO, Responsable Admin Fin, Gestionnaire log, Resp Grant, Resp E&C   
Yaoundé: DP, DP Adjoint Prog , Coo Techniques Prog, Coo Log, Coo Fin, Coo RH, Coo Grant

OBJECTIF GENERAL DU POSTE :

Le/la coordinateur/trice de terrain assume le rôle de chef(fe) de mission délégué(e) pour une région d’un pays dans lequel Solidarités International intervient.  
Il/elle propose une stratégie régionale adaptée au contexte géopolitique et humanitaire, et veille à sa mise en œuvre une fois celle-ci validée.  
Il/elle vérifie et s'assure que les projets sont menés conformément à la charte de Solidarités International, dans le respect de toutes les procédures internes et contractuelles.  
Il/elle mobilise les ressources matérielles et financières nécessaires au bon déroulement des programmes et supervise la gestion des ressources.  
Il/elle coordonne les équipes sur le terrain et est responsable de leur sécurité dans la zone qui lui est assignée.  
Il/elle est l'interlocuteur direct et le représentant du chef de mission.

ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES :

\- Contexte sécuritaire volatile avec notamment frappes de drone (Tiné, Adikong) et incursions à la frontière   
\- Equipe de l'Est dispersée géographiquement   
\- Fermeture base d'Abéché à finalsiée et finalisation ouverture de la nase d'Amjarass   
\- Volume opérationnel important entre Adré, Iriba et Amdjarass (6 à 7 contrats)  
\- Contraintes opérationelles spécifiques à l'Est qui entravent la mise en oeuvre des projets

PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS :

\- Appui à la structuration des bases de l'Est (suivi carburant, suivi budgétaire, suivi paiements fournisseur)  
\- Gestion de la sécurité et des mouvements et suivi de la tendance avec le conflit soudanais  
\- Représentation externe auprès des autorités locales, des fora régionaux de coordination, et des autres partenaires ONGI et ONGN  
\- Finalisation de la fermeture de la base d'Abéché et finalisation ouverture de la base de Amdjarass

CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES :

Adré Iriba et Amdjarass (niveau 3) avec risque de détérioration de la situation sécuritaire (débordement du conflit soudanais avec attaques de drone). Le Coordinateur Terrain Est sera basé à Iriba mais avec des déplacements fréquents sur les bases de Adré et de Amdjarass.

**Votre profil**

DIPLÔME REQUIS : Un master en études humanitaires ou en développement, en sciences sociales, en gestion ou dans une autre discipline connexe.

EXPERIENCE DANS LE SECTEUR HUMANITAIRE : 3-4 ans

EXPERIENCE SUR POSTE EQUIVALENT : 0-2 ans

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES :

1\. Coordination interdépartementale (suivi budgétaire, procédure d'achat, process RH)

2\. Bonne connaissance du cycle de gestion des projets

3\. Gestion de la sécurité et de l'accès

4\. Capacités de représentation externe (autorités, bailleurs, fora de coordinatin)

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSES :

1\. Leadership et management

2\. Anticipation, organisation, et suivi

3\. Réflexion et analyse stratégique

LANGUES :

1\. Français (obligatoire)

2\. Anglais (obligatoire)

3\. Arabe (un plus)

**SI vous offrira les conditions suivantes**

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3080 bruts par mois (2800 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de 600 euros.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**Condition de vie** : Iriba est classée en niveau 3. Il y a peu d'activité à faire à Iriba mais la base a été rénovée récemment avec de bonnes conditions de vie.   
La liaison UNHAS avec Ndjaména a lieu 5 jours par semaine sur Abéché ou Adré (hors aléat liées à des intempéries ou des pannes) et il est également possible de rejoindre Ndjaména par la route en dernier recours.

jobs.title: Project Director, Chad
jobs.body:
**Role:** Full Time

**Contract Duration**: 2 Years

**Deadline for submission:** 30th October 2026

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

**About Us**

Founded in 1992, Nutrition International is a global organization dedicated to delivering proven nutrition interventions to those who need them most. Working in partnership with countries, donors and implementers, our experts conduct cutting-edge nutrition research, support critical policy formulation, and integrate nutrition into broader development programs. In more than 60 countries, primarily in Asia and Africa, Nutrition International nourishes people to nourish life.

For more than 30 years now, Nutrition International has focused on delivering low-cost, high-impact, nutrition interventions to people in need, driven by our mission to achieve a world where everyone, everywhere, is free from malnutrition and able to reach their full potential. Nutrition International’s work is guided by a dedicated and talented team of experts working globally, regionally and within countries to end malnutrition worldwide.

**About the role**

Nutrition International is supporting the Ministry of Health in Chad to implement Child Survival programming including to maintain coverage and ensure that all eligible children receive two doses of vitamin A supplementation (VAS) every six months and to preposition zinc & low-osmolarity oral rehydration salts (LO-ORS) to treat childhood diarrhea in line with WHO -recommended treatment protocols.

To ensure the supported rounds are successful, and program data is available for decision-making, Nutrition International will conduct regular post-event coverage survey (PECS) after campaigns. Doing so will ensure review data is available quickly post-event to allow course corrections in time for the next round of the vitamin A supplementation implementation. The program will also produce data and guidance that is needed to curb child deaths and maximize every dollar invested.

Nutrition International will scale up its technical assistance and advisory services to reinforce government capability and programming. Nutrition International will ensure campaigns are designed and delivered effectively and with attention paid to gender equity. This includes the application of best practices and the adaptation of global guidance to the country’s context.

The Project Director is the lead focal person for Nutrition International’s programming in Chad. The job holder will be responsible for external relationships and accountable for program delivery in Chad, in line with NI’s vision, mission and values and the VAS program design. The Job holder will also provide high-level representation of Nutrition International and oversee support to the Government at national and sub-national levels.

The Project Director will provide overall leadership of the Nutrition International Country Team and Child Survival programming in Chad, will lead the management of relations with the Government of Chad and with other key local stakeholders and oversee the work of a country team in developing, managing, monitoring and reporting on Nutrition International Child Survival programming in Chad. The Project Director will be accountable for programmatic and financial delivery and reporting against Nutrition International requirements and will also manage Nutrition International’s country operations including ongoing compliance with legal and financial regulations in the country.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**1. External Relations and Representation**

- Lead Nutrition International’s representation in Chad, building strong relationships with national and sub-national government, donors, UN agencies, NGOs, the private sector, academia and communities.
- Position Nutrition International as a key actor in nutrition and public health, including through national task forces, alliances and conferences.
- Engage in advocacy, directly and with partners, to influence government policy and partner investment in nutrition.
- Harmonise Nutrition International’s work with other partners and actively support government leadership and ownership.
- Identify opportunities to leverage and mobilise additional resources to expand Nutrition International’s work in Chad.

**2. Programme Management and Delivery**

- Be accountable for achieving agreed results, programme quality and disbursement targets within agreed timelines.
- Manage the performance of partners and sub-contractors against agreements, negotiating corrective action where needed and assessing value for money.
- Monitor progress against workplans and performance frameworks, account for variances and prepare reports for donors and stakeholders.
- Convene and participate in programme review and steering meetings with government and partners and negotiate adjustments to plans and budgets.
- Ensure vitamin A programming mainstreams gender equality in line with Nutrition International’s global strategy, including Sex and Gender Based Analysis.

**3. Financial Management**

- Working with the administrative support partner, ensure country resources are managed in line with Nutrition International policies and within approved budgets.
- Guide the team in costing, budgeting, expenditure forecasting, variance analysis and value-for-money reporting for donor purposes.

**4. Team Leadership and Country Operations**

- Lead and develop the country team of three Senior Programme Officers and a Project Officer.
- Manage country operations, including ongoing compliance with legal and financial regulations in Chad.
- Keep Nutrition International staff informed of progress and ensure contributions are recognised.

**5. Focal Point for Nutrition International Child Survival programming in Chad**

- Be the primary focal point and lead for Nutrition International Child Survival programming in the country.
- Build strong relationships with and engage regularly with senior government officials to ensure programming gaps. and needs are clearly articulated and coordinated with other partner support.
- Ensure visibility of Nutrition International’s support to national and sub-national authorities.

## **Requirements**

**Education/Professional Designations/Experience:**

- Master’s degree from a recognized university in management, international development, public health, nutrition or related area;

\- Additional post graduate certification in project or general management is desirable.

\- Certificate in research and/or monitoring and evaluation an added advantage.

- At least 10 years of experience in the management of programs in public health, nutrition, international development or a related field;
- Significant experience managing complex budgets and diverse teams in progressively more senior leadership roles;
- At least 5 years’ experience in networking at a high level with international partners and country government, desirable;
- At least 5 years’ experience of working in Chad; regional and/or global experience highly desirable;
- Previous experience as a Country Manager or Director or equivalent role in scope and responsibility for an international organization/NGO highly desirable.

**Languages Skills**

- Fluent in English and French required.
- Fluency in local Chad languages would be an asset.

## **Benefits**

Competitive market pay, comprehensive medical benefits, flexible working hours, generous annual leave, support for professional learning and development, and dedicated health and wellness allowance.

Nutrition International is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and accessible work environment. Applicants with special needs who require adjustments or support are encouraged to reach out during the recruitment process.

**Our Commitment to Safeguarding**

Nutrition International has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment (SEAH), or any other form of safeguarding misconduct. We incorporate safeguarding-related questions throughout the recruitment process, including during interviews and reference checks, to ensure a safe and respectful working environment. In accordance with the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme, reference checks will include safeguarding verifications with previous employers.

**Candidate Consent**

By applying for this position, you consent to professional reference checks and appropriate background screening as part of the selection process. Any offer of employment is conditional on satisfactory completion of these checks.

jobs.title: Consultancy: Situation Analysis for the SHINE Rehabilitation Project – Kenya
jobs.body:
**CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V. (CBM) is looking for an experienced professional to conduct a Situation Analysis for a project in Kisumu, Makueni, Nyeri, Homabay, Laikipia, Kiambu and Nakuru Counties, Kenya. This assignment will be based on consultancy work for approximately 30 days in November 2026.**

**About the Project:**

SHINE Project ((Strengthening capacities for Holistic and Inclusive Need-based rehabilitative services that Empower individuals and communities in Kenya) aims to contribute to a sustainable rehabilitative healthcare and inclusive social system that enables persons with functional limitations and participation restrictions to attain the highest quality of life in Kisumu, Homa Bay, Makueni, Kiambu, Nakuru Nyeri and Laikipia Counties, Kenya. It seeks to improve delivery of quality rehabilitative services and access to assistive technology through strengthening capacity of health care system across primary (including community based rehabilitative structures and referral pathways) and secondary levels in target Counties by 2030.

The aim of the requested consultancy is to conduct comprehensive situation analysis of the proposed project of CBM in partnership with Nyabondo Centre for Persons with Disabilities, Naromoru Disabled Children's Home, and AIC CURE Children’s Hospital of Kenya toanalyze and generate robust evidence on the rehabilitation services status, capacity, accessibility, utilization, quality, and financing, as well as the unmet needs of persons with disabilities and other populations requiring rehabilitation support. It will also generate evidence on how persons with disabilities and their families currently organize support, care, and mutual aid in daily life, and how these community practices interact with, and shape uptake of, the formal rehabilitation system. The findings show county-specific gaps, priorities, opportunities and practical entry points for strengthening services

For more information, please refer to the Terms of Reference [here](http://www.cbm.org/shine-cure-nyabondo-naromoru).

jobs.title: Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Specialist
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY  
Habitat for Humanity International seeks a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEAL) Specialist to support and advance the Terwilliger Center for Innovation in Shelter's work with small and growing businesses. The purpose of the Terwilliger Center is and always has been to influence market actors – i.e., private companies, public officials, civil society, consumers, and households – to change attitudes, behaviors, policies, business models, and products and services in ways that lead to scalable affordable housing solutions. This is the essence of the Terwilliger Center's contribution to the HFHI mission of ensuring that everyone has a decent place to live.

The Terwilliger Center supports enterprises expanding innovative and client-responsive services, products and financing so that low-income households can improve their housing more effectively and efficiently. The Terwilliger Center operates in a dynamic environment where projects are often executed using a matrix structure, leveraging cross-functional teams within the center and, at times, across the wider Habitat network to achieve success.

The MEAL Specialist will play a key role in supporting the implementation, learning, and continuous improvement of the Small and Growing Businesses (SGB) Framework, the Terwilliger Center's global approach to identifying, supporting, and learning from enterprises with solutions for affordable housing via direct support and capital mobilization. This position strengthens the systems, evidence, and coordination needed to align global strategy with regional implementation. The role will also contribute to MEAL and learning efforts connected to the Shelter Venture Fund (SVF), the Center's mechanism for deploying investment into housing SGBs, ensuring coherence between the SGB framework and investment-related evidence. The MEAL Specialist will help advance learning, insights, and network engagement that elevate the Center's ability to support SGBs, influence entrepreneurial ecosystems, and inform future program design. Specifically this role designs and implements MEAL systems for impact investment portfolios and SGB programs, ensuring evidence-based decision-making and will contribute to global learning agendas, donor reporting, and impact measurement frameworks aligned with GIIN/IRIS+ standards.

**Key Responsibilities:**

ESSENTIAL DUTIES 1) Design and implement the MEARL framework for the SGB framework.  
Develop results chains/frameworks for SGB framework and Shelter Venture Fund investments.  
Ensure alignment with global impact measurement standards (IRIS+, SDG indicators).  
Supports SGB team in target setting for annual and multi-year projections and puts a rigorous but realistic plan in place to track and monitor against these targets.

2)Ensure Data Quality and Insight Generation to support the SGB framework and strengthen evidence of uptake.

Working with global MEARL, geographic MEARL and SGB leads, lead rigorous data collection, validation, and analysis using mixed methods. Lead stakeholder reporting requirements and ensure integrity of reporting. Produce dashboards and learning briefs for internal strategy and external stakeholders.

3)Learning and Knowledge Management.

Facilitate learning loops across regions; synthesize cross-portfolio insights. Translate evidence into actionable recommendations for the SGB framework, including investment insights and program design. Promote adaptive management. Use evidence and real-time insights to inform strategic pivots and improve program effectiveness.

4\) Capacity Building and Systems Strengthening.  
Develop and maintain digital data systems (such as CRM, Airtable, PowerBI) for real-time monitoring and data visualization.  
Keep up to date on industry trends and build insights into continuous improvement of MEAL systems.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS

Master’s in Monitoring & Evaluation, Development Economics, Statistics, Impact Measurement, or related field.

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS

Minimum 5 years in MEAL roles, including impact investing or enterprise development contexts.

Proven ability to design and implement MEAL systems.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance.

For work locations in Slovakia, the minimum monthly gross pay starts at:

€3,060.00 EUR

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS
jobs.body:
Dans le cadre de la gestion de ses projets en **République du Congo**, la FONDATION AVSI recrute **un/e Coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS**.  
Le/la coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS est chargé de concevoir, de mettre en œuvre et de superviser les systèmes de suivi, d’évaluation, de responsabilisation et d’apprentissage des programmes d’AVSI Congo. Ce poste vise à garantir la qualité, l’exactitude et la ponctualité de la collecte de données et de l’établissement de rapports pour l’ensemble des projets en cours, à renforcer les mécanismes de responsabilisation envers les populations concernées et à favoriser l’apprentissage organisationnel grâce à la documentation systématique des bonnes pratiques et des enseignements tirés. Le/la coordinateur/Coordinatrice MEALS travaille en étroite collaboration avec le responsable des programmes, les chefs de projet et le conseiller régional MEALS.

**? Lieu d'affectation:** Pointe-Noire

**? Starting** **Date:** 01/01/2027

**⏳Période:** 12 mois

**Langue:** French

**Salary:** 1800-2300€ net

**De faire rapport à:** Représentante Pays (report hiérarchique) et MEALS régional (report fonctionnel)

**?Objectif de la position:**

- En collaboration avec le responsable régional du MEALS et les responsables des programmes et des projets, établir un ensemble fiable et cohérent d’indicateurs de résultats et de produits pour toutes les activités des programmes, des projets et les nouveaux appels à propositions.
- Superviser l’élaboration des plans de suivi et d’évaluation des projets en accord avec le cadre logique du projet et en consultation avec les équipes de projet pour tous les projets en cours.
- Fournir un soutien au suivi et à l’évaluation des organisations partenaires, à travers des ateliers de renforcement des capacités; renforcer la communication entre AVSI et les partenaires.
- Soutenir l'élaboration de procédures opérationnelles standard (POS/SoP) et de lignes directrices et les mettre à jour lorsque cela est nécessaire, en particulier pour le travail contre rémunération et la distribution d'espèces.
- Préparer des revues après action des projets en cas de besoin.
- Assurer la compilation en temps opportun des rapports d'avancement internes et externes et des rapports finaux des projets en cours (mise à jour MEALS tous les mois/deux mois) et numériser les rapports.
- Partage des défis, des bonnes pratiques, des retours d'expérience et des leçons apprises du terrain et des données collectées.
- Superviser et guider le travail du personnel MEALS d'AVSI en République du Congo et améliorer la communication entre les départements, MEALS et les programmes (réunions régulières).
- Garantir une formation constante du staff MEALS, améliorer leurs compétences et agir comme un mentor pour leurs staffs.
- Coordonner les visites sur le terrain à effectuer par le staff du département MEAL pour garantir la qualité des données collectées par les programmes et pour vérifier l'exactitude des données rapportées (au moins une visite par mois).
- En étroite collaboration avec les équipes de projet, mener des séances d’information et de retour d’information auprès des bénéficiaires pour les guider dans l’expression de leurs besoins et la recherche d’aide.
- Garantir et coordonner le système d’archivage pour les livrables des différents projets.
- Représenter l'AVSI en externe au sein du groupe de travail MEALS et établir un réseau avec d'autres organisations pour partager les apprentissages et les bonnes pratiques en matière de MEALS; Pour les projets basés sur un consortium, travailler en étroite collaboration avec les partenaires pour élaborer des plans de suivi et suivre leur mise en œuvre.

**? Autres compétences et expériences requises:**

***Compétences techniques***

- Au moins 4 ans d'expérience professionnelle dans le secteur MEALS au sein d'organisations humanitaires et de développement
- Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite en français, la connaissance d’une autre langue (anglais ou italien) est un avantage
- Expérience avérée dans l’utilisation d’outils de collecte, de gestion et d’analyse de données qualitatives et quantitatives.

***Atouts Supplémentaires***

- De préférence Bonne connaissance du contexte local (ou régional)
- Solides compétences en communication et de management.

?AVSI applique, dans le processus de sélection, le principe d’inclusivité et de non-discrimination, garantissant l’égalité des chances indépendamment du sexe, de l’âge, de l’ethnie, de la nationalité, de l’orientation sexuelle, de l’identité de genre, de l’état civil, des convictions religieuses, du handicap et de l’appartenance à des catégories protégées.

?AVSI se réserve le droit de demander aux employeurs précédents des informations concernant d’éventuels différends, préoccupations liées à la protection, enquêtes ou mesures disciplinaires, et de solliciter la communication des antécédents judiciaires et civils du candidat, aux fins d’évaluer son aptitude professionnelle à exercer des fonctions impliquant un contact avec des personnes vulnérables, y compris des enfants et des adultes.

jobs.title: Sudan - Field Coordinator (M/F) - Ed Daein
jobs.body:
**Desired start date: 12/01/2027**  
**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: Ed Daein - Darfur**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was one of the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.  
In February 2024, SI opened a base in El Fasher (North Darfur) to provide emergency assistance to populations, as very few humanitarian organizations were operational in the state. Then, SI opened offices in Tawila (North Darfur), in Zalingei (Central Darfur) in october & November 2024 and East Darfur and West Kordofan in early 2026. In addition, an office in Khartoum was maintained and in 2025 operations were opened in Jazeera state.  
Today, thanks to the support of SHF, CDCS, SDC, GFFO, SIDA, ECHO, UNDP and Unicef, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, North Darfur, East Darfur, West Kordofan, Jazeera and Khartoum States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors. Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.  
Across the Darfurs and in West Kordofan, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH -from 1st line to 2nd line & beyond- with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, networks, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc.  
SI also has Emergency Response Teams based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, and in Tawila covering North Darfur, both implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA).  
Besides, SI implements food assistance mostly through cash and voucher modalities. West and North Darfur team also implements agricultural support activities (seeds distribution, provision of tools, training) as well as market strengthening support  
In Darfurs & in West Kordofan, SI is the leader of WASH, co leading the North Darfur WASH Cluster and managing also a part of UNICEF pipeline from West Darfur to West Kordofan. SI is also coleading the SNFI clusters in East Darfur and in North Darfur, and the FSL Cluster in North Darfur.  
In May 2026, SI opened our new base in Al Dein, East Darfur and in Ghobeish, West Kordofan. The teams have been working on strong WASH and cholera responses in several localities.

## About the job

SIZING OF THE TEAM ON THE BASE / IN COORDINATION :

Mission size around 45 international staff and 190 National staff across different bases  
The East Darfur & West Kordofan is composed by 1 FC, 1 admin Mgr, 1 log Mgr, 1 WASH PM, 1 AM WASH (based in WK), a Security & access Officer, WASH Officers, a MEal Supervisor, and Log & admin assistants. The team scaling-up is underway.

GENERAL OBJECTIVES :

The Field Coordinator oversees the development of Solidarites International's (SI) presence and response in their area of intervention, in line with the Country Strategy and the organisation's mandate.  
Delegated by the Country Director, they are SI's representative in the area to aid workers, local administrative, military and political authorities, civil society and the media.  
They are responsible for ensuring the security of SI teams and assets in their area, as well as compliance with the organisation's ethical framework and values.

ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES :

1 - High level and severity of emergency needs  
2 - 2 bases, 2 states, vast operational area with a limited humanitarian presence compared to other States.  
3 - Access & security challenges

PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS :

Implementation of new activities in West Kordofan & set up of the teams  
Support the access strategy  
Security analysis

SECURITY CONSTRAINTS :

Security Level 4  
High risk environment, threats less predictable and requiring strict protocols, Curfews in place (often 6pm–8pm), Walking strictly limited to approved times, locations.

## Your profile

DIPLOMAS : Masters degree in a related field (humanitarian response, international cooperation, development studies, political sciences…).

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : 3- 4 years

EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : 3- 4 years

TECHNICAL SKILLS :

1\. Security and access management

2.. Rapid need Assesement

3\. Strong negociations skills

4\. Conflict sensitivy skills

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS :

1\. Work under pressure

2\. Adaptability

3\. Strong initiative capacities and solution-finding attitude

LANGUAGES

1\. Fluent English

2\. Arabic would be an advantage

3\. French would be an asset

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**

**According to experience,** starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**Living conditions:** In Darfur, the guesthouses are of good standard with solar panels, STARLINK internet connection, and running water. Social life is limited to contact with other NGO staff. Access to Markets and local food is possible, but restaurants are scarce and not diversified.  
SI main base is located in Ed Daein (East DArfur): big building divided in 2 parts with GH & Office and is well equiped: TV, modern kitchen, salons, 5-6 bedrooms and with large outdoor space.  
SI sub base is located in Ghobeish, charming but smaller house serving as both an office and a guesthouse.

jobs.title: Protection Officer
jobs.body:
TEAM PURPOSE:  
To identify, analyse and address risks affecting the safety, dignity, rights and wellbeing of individuals and communities affected by conflict, displacement and other crises, in Rural Damascus, Daraa and Assweida governorates. The team designs, implements and oversees protection interventions through direct implementation and partner-led modalities, while strengthening community capacities, local protection systems, social cohesion, and community-based protection mechanisms. The team contributes to the prevention, mitigation and response to protection risks through individual assistance, community-based protection, protection monitoring, evidence generation, advocacy, social cohesion and other protection programming in line with Oxfam Syria's strategy and humanitarian principles.  
  
JOB PURPOSE:  
The Protection Officer in the Southern hub is responsible for the technical leadership and operational management of Oxfam's protection portfolio within the hub, ensuring that all protection activities are implemented in accordance with Oxfam Safe Programming standards and Oxfam Syria's endorsed SOPs, methodologies and guidance. This responsibility applies to both directly implemented and partner-led interventions. The Team Leader leads the identification, analysis and monitoring of protection risks affecting individuals and communities and oversees the design and implementation of appropriate protection responses, including Individual Protection Assistance (IPA), community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion activities, and other protection interventions. The role is responsible for determining the most appropriate implementation modality for each intervention, including direct implementation, partner-led implementation, or phased transition approaches. This role establishes and maintains collaboration with affected communities, local authorities, community leaders, community-based organizations (CBOs), implementing partners and other humanitarian and development actors.  
Where activities are implemented through partners, the Protection Team Leader remains responsible for technical oversight, partner capacity strengthening, mentoring, accompaniment, quality assurance, compliance and risk management. This includes supporting partners to progressively assume leadership of protection activities while ensuring adherence to Oxfam standards and protection outcomes.  
  
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:  
Assessments, analysis and evidence generation  
•Lead and supervise protection staff, and/or support protection partners, in the planning and implementation of Community Gendered Protection and Social Cohesion Analyses, protection monitoring exercises, stakeholder mapping, service mapping, and other assessments required to inform programme design and advocacy priorities.  
•Ensure timely consolidation, dissemination and utilization of assessment findings to inform protection responses, programme adaptation, advocacy efforts and strategic decision-making across Oxfam sectors and external stakeholders.  
•Contribute to research, learning and evidence-generation initiatives informing protection and social cohesion programming, advocacy and policy development.  
Programme and project development  
•Contribute to the development, implementation and adaptation of Oxfam Syria's protection and social cohesion strategy and operational plans based on field evidence, protection trends, emerging risks and organizational priorities.  
•Lead the identification and design of protection and social cohesion interventions, including community-based protection, IPA, protection monitoring, social cohesion, and other protection approaches implemented through direct and/or partner-led modalities.  
•Contribute to concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports, ensuring technical quality and alignment with Oxfam standards, Protection and social cohesion priorities and contextual needs.  
•Identify opportunities for protection and social cohesion integration across sectors and support the design of protection-sensitive as well as conflict-sensitive interventions, in coordination with relevant technical teams.  
Programme implementation and oversight  
•Lead and supervise the implementation of protection and social cohesion activities within the hub, ensuring compliance with Oxfam standards, donor requirements and endorsed SOPs and methodologies.  
•Directly supervise Protection staff and/or support protection partner, and provide technical guidance, coaching and performance management under their responsibility.  
•Oversee the delivery of IPA, community-based protection activities, social cohesion programming, distributions, protection monitoring activities and other protection programming implemented directly by Oxfam.  
•Ensure effective collaboration with case management and other specialized strategic partners to strengthen referrals, complementarity of services and protection outcomes for individuals facing protection risks.  
•Ensure that referral pathways, service mapping mechanisms and coordination arrangements remain functional, updated and accessible to affected populations. Monitoring, reporting, learning and accountability  
•Ensure interventions' outputs, outcomes and impact are monitored and evaluated, in line with methodologies and tools, and in coordination with MEAL staff at hub level  
•Supervise programme quality, protection outcomes, risks and implementation progress through regular field visits, partner monitoring systems, data review and engagement with affected communities.  
•Ensure timely and accurate programme reporting to enable timely contribution to donor, management and sector reporting requirements, including for both direct and partner-led implementation.  
•Work closely with MEAL teams to ensure data quality and the collection and analysis of sex-, age- and diversity, including disability-disaggregated data.  
•Promote learning, adaptive management and continuous improvement based on monitoring findings, community feedback and lessons learned.

  
Representation and coordination  
• Represent Oxfam in Protection Sector and other relevant coordination platforms.  
•Coordinate with local authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, community leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen protection and social cohesion outcomes and facilitate implementation.

  
Partnership Management Responsibilities  
•Lead and oversee the planning and quality assurance, as well as support the implementation and monitoring when needed and requested, of protection and social cohesion programmes implemented through partners.  
•Manage strategic protection partnerships to ensure the timely, effective, and accountable delivery of project activities, outputs, and outcomes.  
•Provide technical guidance, mentoring, and capacity strengthening to partners, in line with partner priorities, on protection programming, including community-based protection, protection monitoring, social cohesion, individual protection assistance (IPA), referrals, safeguarding, and protection mainstreaming.  
•Support partners in developing, maintaining, and regularly updating service mapping and safe, confidential, and survivor-centred referral pathways in line with agreed protocols.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable the delivery of survivor-centred, timely, and quality protection services, including appropriate referrals to specialized service providers.  
•Ensure adequate support is provided to partners to enable timely and quality monitoring of the quality and effectiveness of partner-led protection interventions.  
•Support partners in identifying and designing high-quality protection and social cohesion interventions that respond to evolving humanitarian needs.  
•Promote integrated, protection-sensitive, and conflict-sensitive programming by facilitating coordination between partners and relevant technical sectors i.e. WASH and FES.  
•Together with protection partners, monitor partner-led project implementation against agreed work plans, indicators, budget& burn rates, deliverables, and implementation timelines, and support timely corrective actions where needed.  
•Conduct regular partner review meetings, field monitoring visits, and joint supervision missions to assess programme quality, identify challenges, and strengthen implementation.  
•Review partner reports and ensure timely, accurate reporting on progress, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and best practices.  
•Identify implementation risks and operational bottlenecks and work collaboratively with partners to develop and implement corrective action plans.  
•Promote continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and partner capacity development through joint learning moments.  
•Build and maintain strong working relationships with partners, promoting accountability, mutual learning, and high-quality programme delivery.

jobs.title: 22954 Programme Officer (Immigration and Border Governance (IBG) (P)
Oficial de Gestión de Información (IM) - Caracas (Personal Nacional)
jobs.body:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Gestión de Información (IM)** altamente calificado con sede en Caracas**, Venezuela.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Objetivo general del puesto:**

Bajo la supervisión de la Gerencia MEAL, brinda soporte en la gestión de información (recolección, limpieza, transformación, análisis y visualización de la información), asegura la calidad de la misma de acuerdo con los requerimientos técnicos y los lineamientos establecidos, que permitan la toma de decisiones de DRC y de sus socios implementadores de todos los programas implementados en Venezuela, coordina con los equipos programáticos y respalda las solicitudes de manejo de información, contribuye en el desarrollo de nuevas herramientas y aplicaciones que aporten a mejora y optimización de los programas implementados.

**Responsabilidades:**

- Uso de PowerApps para desarrollar plataformas de gestión de datos, y asegurar continuas mejoras para el manejo seguro, responsable y sistematizado de los datos.
- Implementar la estrategia de gestión de información de DRC en los programas desarrollados en la organización.
- Uso de Kobo para diseñar formularios de ingreso de información y herramientas de recogida de datos sobre el terreno.
- Proporcionar formación y apoyo al personal de DRC, socios implementadores, a los encuestadores y a los trabajadores sobre la gestión de información, herramientas de recopilación de datos y en caso de dificultades técnicas o preguntas relacionadas con las bases de datos y IM en general.
- Apoyar en el uso de dispositivos y sus configuraciones.
- Uso de PowerBI para generar reportes gráficos de monitoreo de indicadores del programa de DRC y del monitoreo de protección (mapas, gráficos, infografías, dashboards).
- Control de calidad y supervisión de los datos que se recogen, identificar y abordar los errores en la recogida o la introducción de datos.
- Asegurar que la recolección de datos cumple con los principios de manejo de datos de protección (PIM).
- Mantener y conservar las bases de datos de todos los programas de DRC en ejecución, teniendo en cuenta la política de protección y confidencialidad de los datos.
- Garantizar la seguridad del intercambio y la actualización de las bases de datos y otros archivos que documentan el progreso del programa en los tiempos acordados y según los estándares de DRC.
- Contribuir al diseño e implementar estrategias y presentación de datos, que permitan la reflexión sobre los datos y permitir la toma de decisiones basadas en evidencia
- Manejar información a través de software especializado para el análisis estadístico de información (Orange, Python).
- Apoyo en la preparación de mapas SIG (Sistema de Información Geográfica).
- Gestión de calidad de datos mediante rutinas automatizadas.
- Garantizar una coordinación constante con los miembros de los equipos de programas.
- Aplicar técnicas y procedimientos técnicos para el análisis de datos de los programas ejecutados por DRC.

**Experiencias y comeptencias técnicas:**

- Mínimo de 3 años de experiencia laboral en gestión de información con funciones en desarrollo de sistemas de datos y gestión de datos, análisis y tecnología de la información (programación de plataformas, análisis y transformación de datos).
- Conocimiento en Microsoft 365
- Conocimiento de PowerApps y PowerBI
- Conocimiento de diseño y maquetado de Dashboards y reportes
- Nivel experto de manejo de excel (Tablas, Tablas dinámicas, PowerQuery y Fuentes de datos)
- Novel avanzado de manejo de bases de datos relacionales (SQL, Formas normales y modelos E-R)
- Conocimiento de al menos un lenguaje de programación de análisis de datos (Python)

**Deseado:**

- Experiencia en trabajo en el sector humanitario y manejo de datos para la protección humanitaria
- Conocimiento moderado de manjeo de datos masivos
- Conocimiento de manejo de información no estructurada
- Conocimiento en Sistemas de Información geográfica SIG (QGIS - ArcGIS)

**Educación:**

- Profesional en ingeniería, Sistemas, Estadística, Matemáticas, Informática, Ciencias Sociales o campos relevantes

**Idiomas:**

- Deseable: conocimiento inglés hablado y escrito.

**Ofrecemos:**

- La oportunidad de pertenecer a una de las mejores ONGs a nivel mundial.
- Acceso a más de 1,000 capacitaciones y certificados en línea gratuita.
- Duración del contrato: según disponibilidad presupuestal.
- Salario: **Banda H.**
- Seguro HCM cubierto en su totalidad por la organización.

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- **Lograr la excelencia**: centrarse en alcanzar resultados y garantizar procesos eficientes.
- **Colaboración:** involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- **Tomar la iniciativa**: tomar posesión e iniciativa mientras se busca la innovación.
- **Comunicar:** escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- **Demostración de integridad**:

**Proceso de solicitud:** Todos los solicitantes deben cargar una carta de presentación (máx. 1 página) y un CV actualizado (**máx. 2 páginas, sin soportes**) en español, en la plataforma de empleo de DRC. Las solicitudes enviadas por correo electrónico no serán consideradas.

**Fecha de cierre de solicitudes**: Miércoles 21 de octubre a las 11:59 pm Hora Local. Tenga en cuenta que las solicitudes se revisarán continuamente y las entrevistas se planificarán tan pronto como se identifique a un candidat@ adecuado. DRC se reserva el derecho a cerrar la vacante antes de la fecha límite una vez se identifique a un candidato idóneo.
