jobs.title: Senior Case Management Officer
source: International Network For Aid Relief and Assistance
jobs.body:
**GENERAL INFORMATION**

Job Title : Senior Case Management Officer

Location : Ankara, Türkiye (On-site)

Job Type : Full-time

Contract Duration : The contract is for an initial period of **one (1) year**, with the possibility of extension depending on the availability of funding and the continued need for the role.

**ABOUT INARA:**

International Network for Aid, Relief and Assistance (INARA) is a U.S.-registered 501(c)(3) humanitarian organization founded in 2015 by Arwa Damon. Established in response to critical gaps in the humanitarian system, INARA works to support children affected by conflict, displacement, and natural and human-induced disasters who are often unable to access sustained medical and psychosocial care.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming that combines life-saving interventions with long-term recovery support. The organization focuses on children facing complex and overlapping vulnerabilities, including injury, trauma, disability, and exclusion from essential services. Through a multidisciplinary approach, INARA provides access to medical treatment, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and coordinated case management, ensuring continuity of care beyond the immediate emergency phase.

INARA delivers integrated, child-centered programming across multiple sectors to support children affected by crisis. Its interventions include comprehensive medical and rehabilitative care, providing specialized treatment and long-term follow-up; mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), offering trauma-informed and community-based services; and livelihood and economic empowerment initiatives that strengthen household stability. INARA also supports education in emergencies by creating safe and inclusive learning environments, implements water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) interventions to improve health conditions, and maintains a rapid emergency response capacity to deliver immediate medical, psychosocial, food, and non-food assistance during acute crises.

**Vision**

A world where every child has the agency to create a dignified life.

**Mission**

Fostering a future where we empower children to shape their own dignified lives.

**Purpose**

Enhancing children’s capacity to shape their own fulfilling futures through integrated health, empowerment, and community-driven interventions.

**JOB SUMMARY:**

The Senior Case Management Officer is responsible for supervising and supporting INARA’s case management and MHPSS staff in Türkiye while directly managing and following up medical cases in Ankara. The position ensures that children and their families receive coordinated, timely, safe, and high-quality support throughout assessment, treatment, recovery, and case closure. The role provides day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, reviews case documentation and service quality, coordinates closely with hospitals and service providers, and maintains an active caseload in Ankara. The position also verifies hospital and treatment-related expenses against services received, reconciles case expenditures and cash advances with Finance, prepares donor-required case and program reports, and works with Partnerships/Program Management and Communications to ensure reporting, case stories, and communication materials are accurate, timely, and appropriately documented.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Case Management, Medical Follow-up & Care Coordination**

- Manage an active caseload of children receiving medical support in Ankara, ensuring continuous follow-up from intake and assessment through treatment, rehabilitation, recovery, referral, and case closure.
- Conduct and/or review comprehensive assessments of children’s medical, psychosocial, protection, social, and practical needs and develop individualized care plans in coordination with children, caregivers, medical providers, and relevant INARA staff.
- Coordinate appointments, diagnostics, procedures, hospitalization, rehabilitation, medication, referrals, transportation, and other treatment-related needs, and follow up with hospitals and service providers to ensure continuity and quality of care.
- Maintain regular contact with children and caregivers, provide practical guidance and support, explain treatment pathways and next steps, and ensure that changes in needs or treatment plans are communicated promptly.
- Advocate for children and families with hospitals, healthcare providers, social services, and other relevant actors to address barriers to care and secure appropriate services.
- Ensure timely identification and escalation of safeguarding, protection, medical, or psychosocial concerns in accordance with INARA policies and referral pathways.
- Ensure medical and MHPSS services are coordinated as part of an integrated, child-centered case management approach.

**Team Supervision, Technical Oversight & Quality Assurance**

- Provide direct day-to-day supervision to Case Management Officers and MHPSS Officers, ensuring clear work planning, appropriate caseload allocation, service coverage, and accountability.
- Conduct regular team meetings, individual supervision, case review sessions, and multidisciplinary discussions to monitor progress, address complex cases, and support sound case management decisions.
- Review case files, assessments, care plans, follow-up notes, referrals, service records, and closure documentation to ensure completeness, accuracy, confidentiality, and compliance with INARA standards.
- Monitor staff caseloads, case progress, service timelines, and follow-up actions, and intervene where delays, gaps, risks, or quality concerns are identified.
- Provide coaching, technical guidance, and practical support to staff; identify capacity-building needs and support learning and consistent application of case management and MHPSS procedures.
- Promote a supportive, respectful, and accountable team environment and ensure adherence to safeguarding, confidentiality, data protection, professional boundaries, and organizational policies.
- Coordinate with relevant managers on staff performance, workload, operational challenges, and corrective actions where required.

**Hospital & Service Provider Coordination**

- Establish and maintain effective working relationships with hospitals, doctors, rehabilitation providers, pharmacies, laboratories, and other service providers supporting INARA children.
- Confirm treatment plans, services delivered, follow-up requirements, and relevant medical documentation with providers, while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and informed consent.
- Review hospital invoices, treatment bills, and related medical expenses against the treatment and services actually received by each child, flagging discrepancies or unclear charges for clarification before processing.
- Support resolution of service delivery issues, appointment delays, documentation gaps, or billing discrepancies in coordination with hospitals, Finance, and relevant INARA colleagues.

**Case-related Financial Reconciliation & Cash Advances**

- Work closely with Finance on a regular basis to reconcile medical and case-related expenditures with approved treatment plans, supporting documents, and services received.
- Maintain clear records of treatment-related expenses and provide the programmatic and case documentation required to validate hospital, pharmacy, transportation, accommodation, and other approved day-to-day medical costs.
- Manage and clear cash advances received for children’s treatment and day-to-day medical expenses in a timely manner, ensuring that receipts and supporting documentation are complete and submitted in accordance with INARA procedures.
- Follow up on outstanding advances, missing documentation, discrepancies, or corrections with Finance and relevant staff until fully reconciled and cleared.
- This role verifies and reconciles case-related costs but is not responsible for program budgeting, financial management, or budget ownership.

**Monitoring, Documentation & Donor Reporting**

- Maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date beneficiary records, medical follow-up information, service documentation, consent records, and case progress notes in accordance with INARA’s data protection and confidentiality requirements.
- Track case progress, treatment status, outputs, outcomes, pending actions, and relevant indicators and ensure reliable information is available for internal monitoring and donor reporting.
- Prepare monthly and quarterly reports on children and case management activities using existing donor templates, ensuring that information is accurate, evidence-based, complete, and submitted on time.
- Share completed reporting inputs and supporting information with the Partnerships and Program Management Department for review, consolidation, and donor submission.
- Maintain and follow a clear calendar of donor reporting deadlines and required case-related deliverables, including narrative inputs, beneficiary information, case updates, and communication materials.
- Provide timely clarifications, case data, and supporting documentation requested by Partnerships/Program Management for donor reports, reviews, monitoring visits, or audits.

**Communications, Case Stories & Visibility**

- Work closely with the Communications Department to identify appropriate treatment journeys, case stories, milestones, and impact examples that can be documented in line with consent, safeguarding, confidentiality, and dignity standards.
    - Coordinate access to accurate case information and appropriate follow-up with children and caregivers so that treatment progress and case stories are captured responsibly and without disrupting care.
    - Review case-related facts in communication materials for accuracy and ensure that medical and treatment information reflects the services actually received.
    - Track and follow up on donor deadlines for required communication, visibility, case-story, photo, video, or other program materials, coordinating with Communications and Partnerships/Program Management to ensure timely completion.

**Cross-Departmental Coordination**

- Work closely with Program Management, Partnerships, Finance, Communications, Administration, and Operations to ensure coordinated support to children and timely completion of case-related actions.
- Participate in relevant internal meetings and provide concise updates on case progress, team workload, treatment challenges, reporting requirements, and issues requiring management attention.
- Support coordination with external service providers and relevant actors where this directly contributes to referral pathways, continuity of care, or improved services for children.

**REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS**

**Qualification**

- Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Psychology, Nursing, Public Health, or another relevant field; a Master’s degree is an asset.
- Strong understanding of child-centered case management, care coordination, safeguarding, confidentiality, and data protection.
- Strong organizational, interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and sensitive cases.
- Fluency in Turkish and strong working proficiency in English are required; Arabic is a strong asset.
- Ability to work on-site in Ankara and to travel locally to hospitals and service providers as required.

**Experience**

- Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in case management, medical care coordination, protection, MHPSS, or humanitarian programming, preferably with an international NGO.
- Demonstrated experience supervising case management, MHPSS, social work, or multidisciplinary teams.
- Proven experience coordinating medical cases with hospitals and healthcare providers and following treatment pathways and patient needs.
- Experience reviewing case documentation and treatment-related supporting documents and coordinating expense reconciliation with Finance.
- Experience preparing accurate narrative or beneficiary-level reports using donor or organizational templates and working to fixed reporting deadlines.
- Experience working with children and families affected by conflict, displacement, disaster, or other vulnerabilities is strongly preferred.

**CONFIDENTIALITY AND SAFEGUARDING**

**Confidentiality**

As the position is involved in sensitive topics, he/she must observe absolute discretion within and outside the organization. Non-respect of this clause or any breach of responsibility may result in a written warning or immediate dismissal.

**Safeguarding**

INARA has zero tolerance for abuse, exploitation, or harm to children and vulnerable adults. INARA employees must adhere strictly to safeguarding policies, maintain professional boundaries, and report concerns immediately.

jobs.title: Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA
jobs.body:
**Titre : Consultant.e Expert.e en Architecture et IA Générative – Projet HAVA**  
**Date : 11/09/2029**  
**Projet :**  
**Référence : ​HULO-TDR-BAR-2026-001​**

Cet appel à candidatures est ouvert à tous les consultants éligibles, en accord avec les procédures et principes de hulo.

**Contexte de la consultance :**

La **Coopérative hulo**, créée en juin 2021, est la première Société Coopérative Européenne (SCE) opérant dans le secteur de l’humanitaire. En décembre 2025, hulo compte 16 organisations membres : ACTED, Action contre la Faim (ACF), Bioport, la Croix-Rouge française (CRF), Fleet Forum, Handicap International / Humanity & Inclusion (HI), International Federation of the Red Cross, International Rescue Committee (IRC), INTERSOS, Médecins du Monde (MDM), Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), Oxfam Intermón, Plan International, Première Urgence International (PUI), Solidarités International (SI), et Welthungerhilfe (WHH).

Son objectif est d'accroître l'impact de l'aide humanitaire en renforçant les liens et la solidarité entre les acteurs de la logistique humanitaire et en améliorant les performances grâce à la mise en commun des ressources et de l'expertise en matière de logistique et de chaîne d'approvisionnement. Les « initiatives mutualisées » de hulo, sont déjà en cours dans 7 countries (Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, RDC, Liban, Jordanie pour la crise syrienne, Colombie, et Tchad). Les activités sur le terrain sont composées d'achats mutualisés, de ressources humaines partagées, d’une plateforme web permettant la mise en commun de ressources, et d’initiatives environnementales mutualisées. Ces initiatives permettent d'économiser du temps et de l'argent, d'améliorer la qualité des biens et des services fournis, et donc de fournir une aide plus efficace à ceux qui en ont le plus besoin.

Hulo développe actuellement son écosystème Data autour de Microsoft Fabric, avec l'objectif de renforcer ses capacités en matière de Data Science, Business Analytics et Business Intelligence.  
L'utilisation des outils d'Intelligence Artificielle Générative (GenAI) se développant rapidement en interne, cela crée de nouvelles opportunités pour les équipes de hulo, mais également des risques, notamment concernant le shadow AI.  
Hulo souhaite donc étudier et préparer la mise en place de HAVA (Hulo AI for Value-added Assistance), un assistant d'IA générative d'entreprise, sécurisé et gouverné.  
Le concept actuellement réfléchi repose sur une approche Hybrid Enterprise AI Assistant, combinant des modèles d'IA générative opensource et les documents et mécanismes de sécurité contrôlés par hulo.  
L'architecture envisagée s'appuie notamment sur :

- Azure OpenAI Service
- Microsoft Fabric
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Microsoft Entra ID
- Microsoft Purview
- Microsoft Defender
- les bases de données et modèles analytiques de hulo

Le concept HAVA et ses annexes constituent le premier kit de travail qui servira de base à la présente consultance.

**Perimètre général du travail attendu du.de la Consultant.e :**

L'objectif principal de cette consultance est d'accompagner hulo dans la revue, la validation et la finalisation du cahier des charges fonctionnel et technique du projet HAVA.  
Le.la consultant.e apportera une expertise indépendante en matière de :

- Generative AI
- Large Language Models (LLM)
- Architecture Cloud
- Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
- Sécurité des données
- Gouvernance de l'IA
- Microsoft Azure et Microsoft Fabric

Le.la consultant.e n'aura pas pour objectif de développer l'intégralité de HAVA pendant cette mission.

La mission devra permettre à hulo de disposer, à l'issue de 20 jours estimés (A confirmer dans la proposition), d'un cahier des charges suffisamment complet et robuste pour permettre la mise en œuvre ultérieure de HAVA, en interne et/ou avec l'appui d'un prestataire externe.

Cette mission de consultant sera mise en oeuvre en coordination avec le département Business Analytics & Research (BAR). Une personne ressource sera désignée par département pour identifier les enjeux et faciliter les échanges.

**Priorités et livrables :**

**Cahier des charges HAVA finalisé** **incluant** :

1\. Analyse de situation -

- Contexte et enjeux
- Besoins identifiés et priorisés par service
- Contraintes techniques et d’intégration
    - Analyse de l'architecture existante, points forts, limites et recommandations
    - Données disponibles et leur qualité
    - Exigences éthiques, réglementaires et de gouvernance
    - Budget, planning et modalités de collaboration

2\. Solution recommandée

- Périmètre -
    - Objectifs
    - Périmètre fonctionnel
- Proposition -
    - Recommandation sur les modèles IA (Comparaison et recommandation des modèles et stratégie de modèles)
    - Connexions / liens avec d’autres usages IA internes (ex. Usages spécialisés de certains départements)
    - Modèle de coûts et ressources (Coûts d'implémentation, coûts récurrents et ressources nécessaires)
    - Registre des risques (Risques techniques, sécurité, données, opérationnels et adoption)
    - Spécifications sécurité et gouvernance (Identité, accès, confidentialité, RAG sécurisé, logs, gouvernance et guardrails)
    - Architecture RAG (Ingestion documentaire, métadonnées, recherches web, embeddings)

3\. Préparation de la mise en oeuvre

- Déploiement - Livrables, calendrier et responsabilités
- Critères de réussites
- Maintenance, support et réévaluation après déploiement

**Qualifications et expérience:**

- Minimum 3 ans d'expérience dans les domaines de la Data, de l'IA ou de l'architecture Cloud ;
- Expérience démontrée dans la conception de solutions Enterprise Generative AI ;
- Solide connaissance des LLM et architectures RAG ;
- Expérience de l'écosystème Microsoft Azure ;
- Bonne connaissance de la sécurité des données ;
- Expérience en gouvernance de l'IA ;
- Expérience dans la conception de solutions utilisant des documents internes ;
- Capacité à transformer des besoins métier en spécifications techniques ;
- Expérience avec des environnements humanitaire contenant des données sensibles ou confidentielles.

**Management et lignes hiérarchiques**

Ce · tte consultant·e sera placé·e sous la responsabilité du directeur du département « Business Analytics & Research » et travaillera de concert avec un Data Scientist.

**Calendrier**

Mi-octobre – décembre 2026

jobs.title: Técnico/a Sanitario/a. Campamentos Saharauis
jobs.body:
## Misión

El puesto tiene por objeto apoyar en el diseño, desarrollo y supervisión de las acciones en apoyo a los programas de salud sexual y reproductiva (PNSR) y salud infantil (PISIS) de los proyectos que la organización desarrolla en los Campamentos de personas Refugiadas Saharauis enTindouf.

## Ámbito geográfico deIntervención

Campamentos de Población Refugiada Saharaui, Tindouf, Argelia.

## Organigrama

Trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la Coordinación Sanitaria y trabajará junto con todo el equipo de Médicos del Mundo en terreno para el logro de los objetivos.

## Responsabilidades

1. En coordinación con la Coordinación Sanitaria, realizar evaluaciones de necesidades en salud en las áreas de intervención para los proyectos en curso o posibles nuevas intervenciones y contribuir a la formulación de proyectos.
    - En coordinación con responsables del Ministerio de Salud Pública Saharaui (MSP), identificar las necesidades de productos farmacéuticos (medicamentos, material consumible y equipos médicos durables) para los programas PNSR PISIS.
    - Apoyar técnicamente en los procesos de formulación con enfoque de marco lógico relacionados con Salud Sexual y Reproductiva (SSR) / Salud Infantil (SI) de los proyectos de MdM en los CRS, asegurando la transversalización de los enfoques de género y antropológico
2. Promover, planificar y ejecutar actividades sanitarias y de fortalecimiento de los servicios públicos de salud:
    - Acompañar a los equipos del PNSR(coordinaciones nacionales, coordinaciones regionales, secretaría) de acuerdo con un ciclo de mejora continua (planificar, implementar, verificar, actuar)
    - Proporcionar apoyo técnico al personal de salud adherido al PNSR y PISIS de los tres niveles asistenciales: Hospital nacional, hospitales regionales y dispensarios.
    - Liderar la realización de estudios de corte de los programas PNSR y PISIS. Acompañar la recogida de datos del Sistema de Información Sanitaria. En colaboración con la Coordinación Sanitaria contribuir al análisis de indicadores de salud y a la propuesta de proponer soluciones de mejora al MSP.
    - Apoyar en la actualización, implementación y seguimiento de protocolos y procedimientos estándar del PNSR y PISIS para garantizar intervenciones de calidad. Monitorizar su implementación y acompañar a las responsables del MSP para fomentar su cumplimiento en los diferentes niveles asistenciales.
    - Verificar técnicamente dosieres de compras de medicamentos, equipos médicos y material consumible.
    - Promover el adecuado funcionamiento de herramientas de seguimiento y coordinación del MSP como la Plataforma del PNSR-PISIS, las reuniones de coordinaciones mensuales y con el resto de los programas prioritarios. Promover y acompañar la celebración del Comité de muerte materna. Participar en la organización de la Asamblea Anual de la Mesa de Concertación y Coordinación en salud y contribuir a la preparación de información para donantes.
    - Contribuir a la transversalización de género en salud, de acuerdo con el Plan de Género y Salud del MSP, las políticas de MDM y la orientación de la Coordinación de Género y Derechos humanos.
    - Apoyar técnicamente en el ciclo de gestión del voluntariado sanitario y pasantías en terreno.
    - Contribuir activamente en la respuesta humanitaria en caso de emergencias y catástrofes.
3. Acompañamiento y monitoreo del componente sanitario de los proyectos en curso considerando la lógica de intervención de los proyectos, así como su coherencia y complementariedad con otras acciones, productos y actividades
    - Dar seguimiento a las actividades sanitarias de los proyectos activos de la organización y en concreto en lo referido a laSSR ySI, incluyendo la malnutrición materno-infantil.
    - Recoger y sistematizar los datos e indicadores de salud / sanitarios del sistema de monitoreo de MDM, en concreto en lo referido a la SSR,SI y malnutrición materno-infantil y los programas PNSR y PISIS. Participar en el análisis de indicadores junto a la Coordinación Sanitaria.
    - Asegurar la disponibilidad de fuentes de verificación en especial en relación con SSR y SI. Contribuir a la justificación de los proyectos.
4. Apoyar en el ciclo de capacitación y formación del personal sanitario:

- Apoyar al MSP en la detección de necesidades de capacitación y formación del personal de salud, en relación con SSR/SI y Derechos sexuales y reproductivos (DDSSRR).
    - Dar apoyo técnico y promover la realización de formaciones periódicas al personal de salud adherido al PNSR y PISIS.
    - Apoyar en las evaluaciones de estudiantes de matrona y enfermería de la Escuela de Enfermería, y en su caso, en la revisión de programas y contenidos.
    - Acompañar en el desarrollo de habilidades/sensibilización de temas relevantes respecto a la SSR y Salud Infantil. Fomentar la sensibilización e integración del enfoque de género en salud.

1. Contribuir activamente a la sistematización y adopción de buenas prácticas en MDM:

- Contribuir a la articulación y coordinación con el resto de las áreas, y en concreto con logística, administración, género y derechos humanos, farmacia e incidencia política, participando activamente en las reuniones de equipo
    - Contribuir activamente a la transversalización de los enfoques de género, antropológico y medioambiental en las intervenciones de MDM.
    - Contribuir al seguimiento de la estrategia de la misión y la coherencia entre los diferentes proyectos en marcha desde las diferentes áreas sanitarias.
    - Participar en espacios técnico-sanitarios de discusión y coordinación regulares y transmitir a la Coordinación Sanitaria elementos que requieran atención y contribuir al análisis de alternativas.
    - Apoyar en la implementación y seguimiento de los protocolos y procedimientos de seguridad y salud para el personal contratado y voluntario de MDM.
    - Contribuir a la actualización de la Estrategia País.

Otras tareas que le puedan ser requeridas por la Coordinación Sanitaria en el ámbito de sus responsabilidades y funciones.

## Formación

### Titulación Académica:

Requerida: Enfermero/a especialista en Obstetricia y Ginecología/Matrona.

### Formación Adicional:

Altamente deseable: Formación complementaria vinculada al ejercicio de su profesión, género y antropología de la salud. Máster/Postgrado en Cooperación Internacional/ Acción Humanitaria/ Salud pública.

## Requisitos

**Idiomas**: Imprescindible excelente nivel de castellano Altamente deseable: inglés, francés y/o árabe

**Informática**: Imprescindible nivel usuario de Word, Excel, internet y correo electrónico. Deseable nivel medio de Excel.

## Experiencia

Imprescindible experiencia en terreno en cooperación internacional en las funciones mencionadas.

Deseable experiencia en contextos similares y contextos críticos de seguridad.

## Competencias

- Excelente capacidad de organización y planificación
- Capacidad de trabajo en equipo y en red
- Flexibilidad
- Capacidad de trabajo en condiciones difíciles
- Elevada capacidad de comunicación escrita y hablada
- Conciencia cultural y adaptabilidad. Facilidad para las relaciones interpersonales
- Cumplimiento estricto de los protocolos de seguridad establecidos para el país y la misión de MdM
- Identificación con principios y valores de Médicos del Mundo

## Retribución/Condiciones

Tablas salariales de Médicos del Mundo. Contrato Indefinido.

Jornada laboral: 40 horas.

Categoría: Grupo 1. Personalsanitario

Las personas interesadas pueden enviar el CV a través de nuestra página web:

Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. ## **Responsibilities**

Execute Procurement with Excellence

- Strategic Relationships: Help build and maintain deep partnerships with fertilizer suppliers and industry organizations beyond seasonal procurement needs.

People Management

jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Italian Teacher
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background**

 In response to the increased refugee arrivals into Europe, the IRC established the program initially in Greece, which was expanded with programs in Serbia and wider Balkans and with programs in Germany. Following a first assessment conducted in January 2017 in Italy and another one in July 2017, several critical protection gaps were identified within assistance provided to refugees and migrants in Italy: mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), assistance to unaccompanied children, information provision and legal support. To respond to the identified gaps IRC established a small presence in Italy. The IRC in Italy provides essential safety, empowerment, education, livelihood and health services to migrants, refugees and asylum seekers. Our programs operate across the country, including in Trieste, Milan, Rome, Turin and various locations in Sicily and Calabria, with a strong focus on supporting the most vulnerable populations, such as women and children.

**Context of the Assignment**

IRC, in partnership with Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Piemonte, Ente Nazionale Acli Istruzione Professionale (E.N.A.I.P.) Friuli Venezia Giulia, Powercoders, Progetto Tenda, is implementing the **Digital Horizons projec**t in Turin and Trieste, since February 2025.  
Digital Horizons helps young refugees and migrants in Italy accessing sustainable employment through free software development training, job support, individual guidance and social support. The project focuses on youth aged 16–25, arrived in Italy in recent years, who are seeking to break down integration barriers, improve mental health and build pathways to long-term work opportunities.

By working with public job centers (PES), vocational training providers (VET), IT companies and employers, the project prepares participants for high-demand digital careers and supports them with mental health services, individual job counselling and psychosocial support, job placement, a safe and quiet space to study, access to social services, language training, and childcare.

Simultaneously, it also builds the capacity of institutions and employers to create more inclusive opportunities for the target population.

The Digital Horizons intensive (5hs day, monday-friday) training in software development has been delivered in Trieste since mid October 2025, by IRC partner ENAIP FVG. To support the group of participants with heterogeneous knowledge of Italian language, IRC is seeking a teacher for **italian classes (A2-B1-B2),** includingspecific IT **vocational language,** to support students learning outcomes, before the start of the IT training.

**Purpose of the Assignment**

**Job Overview**

The Digital Horizons Italian Teacher will be based in Trieste and will design and deliver middle advanced (A2-B1-B2 as needed) Italian language classes and IT vocational language, to a group of Digital Horizons students, in person. Under the Economic Wellbeing Manager’s supervision and in collaboration with the IRC Italy Integration Counselor and ENAIP FVG staff, the Italian teacher will conduct classroom teaching activities in Trieste, ensuring no student is left behind.

**SCOPE OF WORK**

**Specific Duties and Responsibilities:**

- **Plan, design, and deliver lessons** in Italian at A2-B1–B2 level, integrating IT-related terminology and vocational language relevant to software development.
- **Develop tailored teaching materials** that combine general Italian language learning with specialized IT vocabulary and contexts.
- **Address student questions** and provide clarification on both general and IT-specific language content.
- **Help develop students’ confidence and learning skills**, encouraging students to use Italian effectively in technical and professional settings.
- **Identify learning gaps** and adapt teaching strategies to meet diverse linguistic needs within the group.
- **Promote intercultural communication** by clarifying information and bridging cultural differences that may affect learning.
- **Manage classroom dynamics** and handle any critical issues that arise during sessions, ensuring a supportive learning environment.
- **Encourage collaborative learning** through peer-to-peer support and group exercises for language practice with IT-related content.
- **Maintain accurate records** of attendance, progress, and outcomes to support monitoring and reporting requirements.
- Collaborate with the IT trainer, other ENAIP vocational training staff and IRC Integration Counselor to achieve the course objectives.

The **Digital Horizons Italian teacher** will deliver updates to IRC Staff, on the classroom learning process and possible challenges identified.

**Deliverables**

- Italian classes sessions conducted (40 hs)
- Attendance Sheets signed

**Timeframe**  
The assignment will end upon completion of above-listed deliverables and in any case no later than on 16th November 2026. Classes schedule will be decided in agreement with IRC and ENAIP staff and will be held in the morning (Monday to Friday, between 9.00 and 13.00 am)

**Competencies and skills**

- Proven experience developing learning content and delivering Italian language group teaching activities
- Experience working with migrant population and/or youth is highly desirable.
- Experience or knowledge of IT Sector is an asset
- Bachelor's degree in language or social sciences
- Proven experience in multicultural work or educational environments
- Knowledge of strength-based education and participatory learning
- Understanding of fundamental educational and psychological principles related to learning and communication
- Strong organizational and planning skills.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- Problem-solving abilities
- Personal qualities: empathy and patience, works well in and promotes teamwork, comfortable in a multi-cultural environment, flexible, communicates clearly.
- Additional knowledge of English, Arabic, Spanish, French, Ukrainian, Urdu, Pashtu, Farsi are an asset

**Application Process and Requirements:**

**Application Documentation:**

CV in English OR Italian

**Agreement and payment terms**

The specific details of the agreement, including the scope of work, timelines, deliverables, intellectual property rights, and any other pertinent provisions, will be negotiated and outlined in the contractual agreement to ensure clarity, transparency, and mutual understanding between IRC and the consultant/group of consultants.

**Compensation:** (Total of 1200 EUR). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Lead, Client Impact, BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF)
jobs.body:
**BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: Lead, Client Impact, BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF)**

**Job Location: Nairobi, Kenya | Open to Kenyan and international candidates.**

**Application deadline: 23 October 2026**

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC International Microfinance (BI MF) oversees its microfinance subsidiaries outside Bangladesh, which are wholly or majority owned by the legal entity BRAC International Holdings B.V. (BIHBV), operating across eight countries in Africa and Asia. Within this mandate, BI MF expands financial inclusion by responsibly delivering financial services to people at the bottom of the pyramid, particularly women living in poverty in rural and hard-to-reach areas, to create self-employment opportunities, build financial resilience, and harness their entrepreneurial spirit by empowering them economically. The achievement of both ‘Impact and Scale’ are critically important, ensuring that each subsidiary has systems in place to realise both components of the mission.

BI MF provides strategic direction, governance oversight, and institutional strengthening across the portfolio. Today, its operations serve clients (97% women) across the eight operating countries, managing a loan portfolio of approximately USD 277 million, and employing over 7,000 staff, of whom 87% are women.

**About the Role:**

This is an opportunity to shape how one of the world’s leading INGO measures, manages and improves its impact across a multi-country microfinance portfolio.

The **Lead, Client Impact** is responsible for providing overall leadership on Impact Measurement & Management (IMM) and Social Performance Management (SPM) within BI MF and ensuring appropriate technical support required to all BI MF entities in these areas. The role gathers insights and works with operations teams to ensure we achieve our impact objectives. The role will leverage BRAC’s established impact measurement capabilities, research, client insights and multi-country microfinance experience to ensure BI MF focuses on the right outcomes and the right processes to drive impact as the bottom line. This role will assist BI MF entity teams to measure performance against metrics in key social impact categories: client access, social outcomes, financial resilience, client agency, client protection, and client experience and satisfaction, among others. It will strengthen how BI MF measures, manages and improves impact at scale, ensuring our services remain inclusive, scalable and client-centric, particularly for women, youth and people living in poverty.

The position will report to the Associate Director, Strategy and will work across the BI MF team and closely with the leadership of each entity. They will also work closely with the BRAC International Learning & Effectiveness team to deliver on our promise as a learning organization, continuously examining and changing practices based on data and reflections from the field. They will also collaborate with BRAC’s social development programmes and various affiliates for overall achievement of BRAC’s goals and mission.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**A. Impact Measurement & Management (IMM):**

- Lead and support the BI MF Client Impact team to ensure quality implementation of our flagship annual IMM activities across BI MF country entities:
- **60 Decibels Lean Data Report** to provide standardized and actionable client insights pertaining to poverty outreach, household wellbeing, quality of life, and challenges faced by BI MF clients.
- **Internal Dropout Surveys** to better understand drivers of client retention and address issues that cause attrition at the BI MF entity level.
- Maintain and institutionalize a detailed **customer journey map** framework to help BI MF entities enhance and promote a positive client experience as well as address key pain points.
- Strengthen **poverty outreach measurement** and cross-country learning through review, integration, and documentation of effective poverty tracking mechanisms; ensure that our BI MF entities have in place an innovative approach to poverty outreach and tracking.
- Continuously improve the **complaint handling framework** to strengthen client protection pathways and provide clients with means to resolve issues safely and efficiently.
- **Ensure knowledge transfer and capacity building for BI MF entity teams strengthening their capability to implement the client impact agenda consistently and effectively across BI MF entities.**
- Work closely with the Technology team to ensure that client impact related data is captured, stored and available to country leadership and frontline staff.

**B. Social Performance Management (SPM):**

- Oversee the Social Performance Management function to ensure quality reporting and dissemination on client impact data for both internal and external stakeholders.
- Oversee the Social Performance Management team to guide BI MF entities through the quarterly SPI5 Audit process to assess BI MF entities against the Universal Standards of Social Performance Management (USSPM) and Client Protection Principles (CPPs).
- Ensure timely updates to the BI MF leadership team, including on client impact metrics related to poverty outreach and key social outcome indicators.
- Serve as the focal point for client impact reporting needs to Boards (both BIHBV and BI MF entities), investors, and donors.
- Lead client impact reporting integration across BI MF (aligning with global frameworks as applicable).
- Collaborate with BI MF Finance and Technical teams to lead design standardized templates for client impact data collection and narrative reporting.
- Oversee quality assurance of client impact data from BI MF country entities and support them in meeting applicable compliance standards.
- Identify client impact reporting requirements and gaps; develop action plans for compliance and implementation.

**C. Operationalisation of the BI MF Strategy:**

- Operationalise and support the BI MF strategy and direction as it relates to Impact Management & Measurement (IMM) and Social Performance Management (SPM) in consultation with BI MF senior management, technical teams, and BI MF entity leadership teams to strengthen impact research, client outcomes, Lean Data, dropout/retention insights and impact dashboards, and embed evidence into business decisions.
- Develop and implement strategies that will maximize the synergies between microfinance and other programmes and ensure quality implementation for achievement of BRAC’s overall holistic goals.
- Lead or oversee research design and project management on IMM activities.

**D. Team Leadership:**

- Responsible for building a high performing, motivated team by capitalizing on each team members' individual strengths, skill sets, experience and ambitions.
- Ensure clear roles and responsibilities and fluid collaboration within and between departments and teams for timely and high level output.
- Coach and develop team members to translate IMM and SPM expertise into actionable business insights, stronger client outcomes and portfolio-level impact.
- Provide individual mentorship to each team member to continuously develop leadership skills and ensure succession planning, with a focus on creating women leadership.

**E. Safeguarding:**

- Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation. Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
- Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
- Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place and encourage others to do so.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Bachelor's Degree in Concentration / Major in Economics, Development Studies, Business, Finance, or related fields
- Master’s degree (or higher) in Economics, Development Studies, Business, Finance, or related fields (preferred)

**Experience:**

- 8-12 years’ experience, including 5 years plus working in the financial inclusion space.
- Previous management roles in financial Inclusion for women, program design and project management, strategy development and implementation, impact measurement and management.
- Deep understanding of challenges and issues in financial inclusion for women, youth, and people at the bottom of the pyramid.

**Knowledge, Skills and Competencies:**

- Knowledge of impact frameworks with demonstrated ability to turn impact data into management decisions
- Highly motivated with a strong interest and experience in development and social issues
- Experience of bringing structure to ambiguous problems and driving solutions at scale.
- Ability and willingness to train and mentor people and experience working with a diverse, global team.
- Strong communication and presentation skills. Fluency in English required (spoken, reading and written)
- Strong data analysis skills and attention to detail
- Ability and willingness to work in a challenging environment with poor infrastructure and human capacities and difficult security conditions

Core Competencies:

- Collaboration, Innovation, Accountability, Trust, Strategic Alignment

Leadership Competencies:

- Develops Talent, Drives Purpose, Mission Focus, Communication, Adaptability, Results-Oriented

**Employment type:** Contractual

**Salary:** Negotiable

**Duration of the mission: 6 Months**  
**Location: West and Central Darfur**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## ABOUT THE MISSION

Following the outbreak of the conflict in April 2023 and forced evacuation of Khartoum and West Darfur (El Geneina), SI was one of the first international NGO to re-enter Darfur and resume its emergency response.  
In February 2024, SI opened a base in North Darfur to provide emergency assistance to populations, as very few humanitarian organizations were operational in the state. Similarly, SI opened an office in Zalingei, Central Darfur in November 2024 and East Darfur and West Kordofan in early 2026. In addition an office in Khartoum was maintained and in 2025 operations were opened in Jazeera state. Today, thanks to the support of SHF, CDCS, SDC, GFFO, SIDA, ECHO and BHA, activities are being implemented in West Darfur, Central Darfur, North Darfur, East Darfur, West Kordofan, Jazeera and Khartoum States across WASH, Shelter and NFI support, Food Security and Livelihood sectors.  
Across the Darfurs, the main share of the portfolio remains WASH with the provision of water through water trucking, rehabilitation of water points/water yards, borehole drilling, hygiene promotion, sanitation (emergency latrine construction, semi-permanent latrine, showers, desludging), solid waste management, WASH NFI distribution, and WASH in Health etc. In the East the focus is on rehabilitation and recovery of water systems as well as emergency WASH interventions for health crises. Besides, SI implements food assistance mostly through cash and voucher modalities. West and North Darfur team also implements agricultural support activities (seeds distribution, provision of tools, training) as well as market strengthening support.  
SI also has an Emergency Response Team based in Zalingei, Central Darfur, roving across Central and West Darfur, implementing rapid responses in WASH, Shelter/NFI and Food (CVA) as well as in North Darfur.  
In North Darfur, SI was one first to intervene and are presently a leader in WASH response. The FSL work has brought in some great result in North Darfur.   
Recently, we opened our new base in Al Dein in East Darfur and West Kordofan. The teams are already working on strong WASH response along with some critical Cash response. The team is currently assessing and opening new areas in Kordofans.   
In the Eastern part of the country, SI is present with Wash and FSL activities in Khartoum and Jazeera, under ECHO, CDCS, and SHF.  
Most of the programs are being implemented in Consortium, 2 led by SI, and require strong coordination efforts to provide area-based interventions. SI also has a strong localization approach, with diverse local partners in all states.

## ABOUT THE JOB

**General objective:**

The WASH PM will be in charge of launching and implementing SI's WASH activities in West and Central Darfur states.  
S/he will be in charge of ensuring projects are delivered in a timely manner according to WASH quality standard and in accordance with context specifications and communities preferrences.  
S/he will be in charge of coordinating and providing support to two technical teams accross West and Central Darfur states, providing adequate support and capacity-building when needed and working in a remote managemet set up.  
S/he will be in responsible to lead needs assessments in different areas of West and Central Darfur and consequently developing the SI response plan, including with local partners.

**The main challenges:**

- Important workload with a wide range of WASH activities in different geographical areas
- Remote management context as 2 WASH teams in 2 different states
- Access & security challenges

**Priorities for the 2/3 first months:**

- Launch newly starting projects and update workplan according to priorities
- Supervision of technical works including new borehole drilling and water points solarization
- Coordinate WASH response with SI stakeholders, mainly WASH actors, authorities and line ministries

**Security constraints:**

Level 4: High risk environment, threats less predictable and requiring strict protocols, Curfews in place (often 6pm–8pm), Walking strictly limited to approved times, locations,

### YOUR PROFILE

**DIPLOMAS AND EXPERIENCE**

A Bachelor or Master's degree in Water Resource Management, Engineer, Project management

Experience in the humanitarian sector: 3 Years

Experience on a similar position : 3 Years

**SKILLS**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. Proven experience in WASH emergency/ealry recovery programming and WASH in institutions
2. Strong experience in water points solarization, solid waste management
3. Proven experience in partnership - preferable with local organizations
4. Experience in cholera prepardness or response
5. Strong experience in management
6. Good analytical skills and proactive, solution-oriented approach to work.
7. Experience in protracted crisis context (being able to switch between short/medium/long-term solutions).

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. Strong organizational skill
2. Interpersonal and communication skills
3. Ability to work under pressure
4. Ability to adapt to different implementation contexts including remote supervision
5. Experience working with SI and prior experience working in Sudan is an assest

**LANGUAGES**

- English Mandatory
- Arabic would be an advantage

## SI WILL OFFER YOU...

**A salaried position:**  
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2310 gross per month (2100 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

The Guest house is of good standard, with good internet connexion, solar panels and running water. Social life is limited to contact with other NGO staff

jobs.title: Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator
jobs.body:
**Base:** Kyiv

**Starting date:** November 2026

**Contract duration:** 4 months' probation period with prolongation upon successful probation period end

**About PIN Ukraine:**

People in Need (PIN) has been active in Ukraine since early August 2014. Currently, PIN is one of the major humanitarian actors in Ukraine responding to the recent military escalation, providing humanitarian aid to conflict-affected people across Ukraine. Since 2014, PIN has implemented emergency food and cash assistance, NFI, shelter, protection, livelihoods and WASH interventions supporting 5 million vulnerable IDPs, returnees and host communities in urban and rural areas.

PIN is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of race, ethnicity, nationality, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic. PIN encourages applications from individuals of diverse backgrounds and values diversity.

**General information about the role of the person:**

Under the supervision of the Economic and Green Recovery Technical Lead, the Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator will provide technical and analytical support to the design, quality assurance, monitoring, and continuous improvement of PIN's economic recovery programs in Ukraine.

The position involves:

• supporting the development and adaptation of economic recovery methodologies, tools, and technical guidance;

• providing technical support to program teams without taking over the management of their implementation;

• supporting the development of proposals, concept notes, needs assessments, studies, and program frameworks;

• documenting lessons learned, best practices, and evidence generated within economic recovery programs;

• supporting capacity development of teams on relevant technical approaches and tools;

• participating in coordination and technical exchange with relevant internal and external stakeholders;

• supporting the Technical Lead in ensuring coherence and quality across the economic recovery program portfolio.

• conducting and supporting field-based technical work, including field visits, assessments, consultations, data collection, and technical follow-up, either jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead;

• engaging with external stakeholders and representing PIN’s interests in relevant technical discussions, meetings, consultations, and coordination forums, as needed

**Description of general duties:**

**1. Technical Quality and Methodology**

• Facilitate the development, analysis, and adaptation of technical approaches, methodologies, tools, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and recommendations for economic recovery programs. Maintain a clear record of methodological revisions, consolidate feedback from teams, and submit proposed changes to the Technical Lead for review before wider use.

• Analyze the technical quality, relevance, and consistency of programmatic approaches and provide recommendations for their improvement.

• Provide support to teams in adapting and aligning technical approaches across different projects and contexts.

**2. Technical Support to Program Implementation Teams**

• Participate in grant committees and conduct application assessments. Review applications and business plans against agreed eligibility and scoring criteria, assess technical feasibility and market assumptions, and document recommendations and clarification requests for committee consideration.

• Provide program teams with technical advice on the application of economic recovery methodologies and tools. Respond to technical questions during implementation, review practical examples with staff, and escalate unresolved methodological issues to the Technical Lead. Keep programme delivery decisions with the responsible implementation teams.

• Support teams in interpreting and applying technical guidance, targeting approaches and selection criteria, monitoring requirements, and program methodologies.

**3. Technical Monitoring and Quality Assurance**

• Conduct regular technical monitoring visits to program implementation regions and activity sites. Agree visit objectives with the Technical Lead and implementation teams; prepare checklists, review available project records, and consult participants, businesses, partners, and staff as relevant. Conduct visits jointly with or on behalf of the Technical Lead as agreed.

• Assess the technical quality of implementation against approved methodologies, SOPs, program frameworks, and relevant standards.

• Identify technical, methodological, and quality issues and prepare recommendations for corrective actions.

• Coordinate monitoring work with MEAL, Protection, Grants, Partnerships, and Programme Implementation as needed.

• Prepare technical monitoring reports, action lists, and recommendations for follow-up. Record findings, supporting evidence, recommended actions, responsible colleagues, and agreed timeframes. Follow up on technical improvements with the relevant teams and flag recurring or unresolved quality issues to the Technical Lead.

**4. Program Analysis, Evidence, and Learning**

• Support the development and interpretation of economic recovery indicators and monitoring tools. Work with MEAL on indicator definitions, data sources, collection methods, and interpretation of baseline, monitoring, and endline findings. Identify data gaps and limitations before drawing conclusions about results.

• Contribute to the analysis of program results, including economic impact and changes in livelihoods, income, employment, business performance indicators, and resilience, as relevant. Compare results across locations and participant groups where the data allow; examine barriers to economic recovery and explain the practical implications for programme adjustments.

• Support the identification of needs within the economic recovery sector.

**5. Program Development and Proposal Preparation**

• Support the Technical Lead and relevant program teams in developing new economic recovery concepts and project proposals.

• Participate in technical discussions during program design and implementation where specialized economic recovery expertise is required.

• Collect and analyze information needed for program design.

• Conduct stakeholder mapping in the economic recovery sector.

• Support the development of intervention logic, targeting approaches, selection criteria, technical methodologies, and monitoring systems. Prepare technical inputs on activities, expected outputs and outcomes, assumptions, risks, and resource needs. Check that proposed approaches are feasible, evidence-based, and consistent with the agreed programme framework.

• Support the development of new economic recovery initiatives in line with PIN's strategic priorities and identified needs.

**6. Needs Assessments, Research, and Analytical Work**

• Support needs assessments, market and sector analyses, and other economic recovery research to contribute to PIN’s evidence base on economic recovery in Ukraine. Help define research questions, assessment tools, stakeholder consultations, and field data collection plans. Analyse market demand, employment opportunities, business constraints, access to services, and recovery needs as relevant; validate findings with teams and stakeholders and prepare practical recommendations.

**Coordination with Programme Implementation and Livelihood Functions**

The Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator works closely with the Livelihood Coordinator and relevant Programme Implementation teams.

The Coordinator does not:

• manage the day-to-day implementation of program activities;

• replace the Livelihood Coordinator in coordination with operational departments;

• take on responsibility for logistics, procurement, finance, or administrative support to implementation;

• take on Programme Implementation's responsibility for delivering program activities;

• duplicate the operational reporting and control mechanisms of the Programme Implementation structure.

**Internal Coordination**

• Maintain regular coordination with Programme Implementation, MEAL, Grants, Partnerships, and other relevant departments. Agree technical priorities and follow-up actions, share findings that affect programme quality or reporting, and clarify responsibilities where technical and implementation functions intersect.

• Coordinate with technical colleagues in Protection, WASH, Shelter, and Education when economic recovery activities involve cross-sectoral approaches.

**External Technical Engagement**

Under the guidance of the Technical Lead:

• participate in relevant technical working groups, coordination meetings, workshops, and consultations;

• support technical communication with relevant CSOs, private sector representatives, service providers, research institutions, and other stakeholders;

• support stakeholder mapping and identification of relevant technical resources and partnerships;

• represent PIN at selected technical meetings as needed. Prepare agreed technical inputs and briefing points, document discussion outcomes, and share relevant opportunities and follow-up actions with the Technical Lead and programme teams.

**Functional Relationship with the Livelihood Coordinator**

The two positions are complementary:

**Livelihood Coordinator > Programme Implementation**

• oversight of implementation;

• coordination with operational departments;

• implementation planning and follow-up;

• resolution of operational issues;

• ensuring delivery of program activities.

**Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator > Programme Quality / Technical Function**

• technical quality;

• methodology and tools;

• technical monitoring;

• analysis and learning;

• technical capacity development;

• program improvement;

• technical input into program design.

**Development of the Role**

The position of Economic Recovery Technical Coordinator is being created to strengthen PIN Ukraine's technical capacity in the field of economic recovery.

As the economic recovery program portfolio expands, the position may gradually take on responsibility for specific technical areas or thematic components, including coordination of particular technical strands across multiple projects.

The role may also evolve toward greater responsibility for technical coordination, quality assurance, program development, and technical representation, depending on program needs and demonstrated performance.

**Team and Partner Capacity Development**

• Identify technical capacity needs of teams and partners and agree development activities with the Technical Lead.

• Deliver technical onboarding, refresher training, and mentoring on economic recovery methodologies and tools. Use practical exercises and programme examples, gather participant feedback, and provide follow-up support to help staff apply the tools consistently.

• When requested, support technical recruitment, preparation of terms of reference, and assessment of candidates’ technical skills; this does not imply line management.

• Provide technical guidance to PIN partners, support monitoring of their programme quality, and facilitate knowledge sharing.

**Documentation and Application of Learning**

• Document lessons learned, good practices, and research findings; prepare technical materials, recommendations, and internal updates.

• With MEAL, support review of baseline and endline tools and use evidence to improve programmes.

**Inclusion, Environmental Sustainability, and Accountability**

• Integrate age, gender, diversity, equality, non-discrimination, and do-no-harm principles into technical approaches and selection criteria.

• Under the Technical Lead’s guidance, support environmental sustainability and climate resilience in relevant economic recovery activities.

• Ensure accountability through appropriate communication and information sharing within PIN and with partners and communities.

• Comply with PIN policies and procedures, including Finance, Logistics, HR, and Security; report identified technical risks to the relevant responsible staff.

**Qualification Criteria:**

**Education and Speciality:**

Higher education in economics, development studies, business administration, agriculture, social sciences, or a related field.

**Required Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong analytical and methodological skills. Ability to conduct field visits, assessments, and technical monitoring. Skills in preparing technical recommendations, reports, tools, and training materials. Ability to advise teams without taking over implementation management functions. Strong communication and coordination skills. Fluency in Ukrainian and working proficiency in English.

**PIN OFFERS**:

- A competitive salary according to the People in Need salary scale in amount of **1882 EUR Gross (Based on qualifications) + 3% after probation period.**
- Opportunities for professional development through various capacity-building activities, including trainings, workshops, and seminars.
- 28 calendar days of annual leave, plus 3 additional New Year bonus leave days.
- Health insurance — becomes effective after completion of the first month of the probationary period.
- Life insurance — effective from the first day of employment, 24/7, providing additional financial protection for employees and their families.
- Possibility to work one day per week remotely for office-based staff.
- Coverage of accommodation and per diem costs for work-related travel outside the assigned office region and/or in cases of excessive travel distance or time, in accordance with People in Need travel policy.
- Provision of a laptop, mobile phone (including prepaid SIM cards), and People in Need branded items (backpack, thermal mug, notebook, portable power bank).
- People in Need offices are equipped with all necessary security and energy-resilience measures, ensuring uninterrupted internet access.
- Free coffee, tea, milk, and water available in all offices.
- A multicultural and friendly working environment, with approximately 400 staff members in the Ukraine programme.

**Application procedure:**

Please send clearly marked CV and Motivation letter in English. Please note, only the shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Written test and interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis and the vacancy will be closed when filled.

Please note that PIN does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process.

*We support the principles of inclusiveness and non-discrimination in the selection process. You can submit an anonymized resume - without specifying your name, age, gender, photo or other personal data. Such resumes will be reviewed on a general basis in accordance with professional experience and qualifications.*

jobs.title: CHARGE-E DE PROJET APPUI AUX PARTENAIRES
jobs.body:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Le.la chargé.e de projet Appui aux partenaires contribue à la définition et la mise en oeuvre de la stratégie de la Mission France en Ile-de-France   
  
Contribuer à la définition des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires dans sa zone d'intervention  
Contribuer à la définition et au cadrage des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires de la base en lien avec la coordinatrice terrain et en concertation avec les autres chargé.es de projet et le coordinateur programme ;  
Assurer le déploiement des activités d'accompagnement des partenaires dans sa zone d'intervention  
Proposer les protocoles d'intervention, les outils de diagnostics, les outils et méthodologie de suivi et évaluation, et formation sur base du cadre défini avec la coordinatrice terrain   
  
  
Assurer la qualité des activités menées sur le terrain  
Appuyer la participation active à la coordination externe, aux dynamiques de mutualisation inter-partenariales et aux formations externes des partenaires (réunions externes, sessions de travail inter-acteurs, sessions de restitution inter-acteurs, etc.).  
Assurer le suivi et la mise en oeuvre des projets co-portés dans sa zone d'intervention en lien avec la stratégie d'influence de la mission France  
Participer à la rédaction de nouveaux projets en coordination avec l'équipe et les partenaires  
Proposer les protocoles d'intervention, les outils de diagnostics, les outils et méthodologie de suivi et évaluation adaptés et nécessaires pour le déploiement des activités, en co-construction avec les différents acteurs et personnes impliqués et en lien avec la coordinatrice terrain   
Animer ou co-animer des cadres de travail collectif et/ou des dynamiques de gouvernance en lien avec le déploiement des projets, en lien avec la coordinatrice terrain ;  
Développer et assurer un suivi du Plan de Suivi Evaluation Redevabilité et Apprentissage des activités des projets ainsi que le suivi des changements, en lien avec la coordination ACF ;  
Appuyer la remontée des informations de terrain à des fins de communication et de plaidoyer  
Contribuer à la rédaction des documents de communication interne et externe  
Assurer le reporting des activités et l'analyse des données qualitatives et quantitatives et contribuer à la rédaction des reporting  
Manager et superviser l'équipe  
Recruter, encadrer, piloter et accompagner l'équipe

  
Profile :

 Vous êtes titulaire d'un diplôme niveau Master (Bac+5) dans l'un des domaines suivants : sciences politiques, développement local et territorial, gestion ou coordination de projet, politiques publiques, affaires publiques, design social ou domaine équivalent.  
Vous avez un minimum de 4 ans d'expérience professionnelle en gestion de projet principalement en France, dans les domaines de l'action sociale, de la sécurité alimentaire, de la lutte contre la précarité alimentaire, de l'accès aux droits ou du suivi-évaluation.  
Vous avez une expérience avérée de coordination de projets multi-acteurs associant collectivités territoriales, services de l'Etat, associations et autres partenaires locaux.  
Vous maîtrisez des méthodes de diagnostic des besoins, de collecte, d'analyse et de valorisation de données.  
Vous avez la capacité à concevoir et à animer des ateliers participatifs, en vous appuyant sur les méthodes d'intelligence collective et d'éducation populaire.  
Votre connaissance fine du tissu associatif et institutionnel de Seine-Saint-Denis constitue un réel atout.  
Vous avez la capacité à fédérer et à travailler en équipe.  
Vous êtes reconnue pour votre créativité, force de proposition et de votre aisance à travailler dans des environnements complexes.  
  
Conditions d'emploi  
  
  
Statut : Cadre intégré - CDD - Temps plein  
Lieu : Montreuil   
Rémunération : De 37K à 41Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience,  
Prime d'ancienneté à partir de 3 années de présence au siège   
Avantages: 25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT   
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF. Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)  
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail  
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up):Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros  
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)   
Télétravail : 12 jours/mois en présentiel   
  
 Déplacements terrains : déplacements et représentation en IdF  
  
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.
