jobs.title: FIELD COMMUNICATION OFFICER
Intern - Humanitarian Affairs
source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
jobs.body:
**Work Location**

New York, in person/hybrid/remote, full-time/part-time

**Expected duration**

February - July 2027

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The United Nations (UN) Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. All internships are within the Central Emergency Response Fund (CERF) secretariat, which provides timely, flexible aid where it's needed most, supporting humanitarian reform efforts and coordination led by Humanitarian and Resident Coordinators. The CERF team values diversity, empathy, and collaboration, encouraging open communication and the sharing of knowledge. Members lead their areas of work independently while contributing to team decisions, voicing opinions, and focusing on continuous improvement. Interns will monitor humanitarian developments, support anticipatory action frameworks, and draft funding application responses. Responsibilities include preparing guidance, conducting training, and coordinating with Resident and Humanitarian Coordinators. Interns will manage data on localization, gender, and funding trends, maintain information resources, and assist in partnerships with Member States and UN agencies. They will help organize high-level events, analyze complex data, and create dashboards to improve efficiency and transparency in funding allocations. This internship is based in New York and may be undertaken on a full-time or part-time basis. For all positions, the preferred modality is in-person. However, remote or hybrid arrangements may be discussed and mutually agreed upon with the manager. Interns will participate in all aspects of the programmatic and partnerships work at CERF, and will be under the general guidance and direct supervision of a supervisor within CERF. Within the delegated authority, the incumbents will be responsible for performing the following duties, or a combination thereof, as determined by CERF: 1. Monitor, analyze, and research humanitarian developments: collaborate with OCHA desk officers on disaster-affected countries, using quantitative and qualitative research to support funding decisions for underfunded emergencies and anticipatory action frameworks. 2. Support anticipatory action frameworks: assist in setting up Anticipatory Action (AA) frameworks through research, analysis, document development, and work plan implementation, while coordinating with AA teams. 3. Review funding applications: work with Programme Officers to review and draft responses for funding applications, ensuring accountability with other OCHA branches and UN agencies. 4. Contribute to CERF’s work on climate-smart humanitarian action, including conducting analysis, reviewing project proposals and strategies, developing guidance and other work. 5. Support the partnership and reporting efforts of the CERF secretariat, including the preparation of the Fund’s annual reports, the meetings of the CERF Advisory Group and other events, as well as the development of CERF advocacy materials. 6. Support CERF’s responsible use of artificial intelligence by helping test and improve CERF AI agents, develop practical guidance, and validate AI-assisted outputs against source documents. 7. Prepare guidance and conduct trainings: support the preparation and revision of internal and public guidance, participate in training, and provide support to Resident and Humanitarian Coordinators for pooled funding processes. 8. Document preparation: prepare or contribute to drafting documents like presentations, briefings, guidance notes, and talking points for senior staff. 9. Data collection and management: assist in collecting and organizing data on themes such as localization, gender, and funding trends, and prepare updates and dashboards for management and external audiences. 10. Maintain information resources: develop and maintain reference information on humanitarian topics, respond to inquiries, and provide updates on latest developments. 11. Coordinate lessons learned and good practices: liaise with field offices to gather lessons learned, share good practices, and identify story hooks to raise visibility for pooled fund efforts. 12. Support partnerships with key stakeholders: assist in CERF partnerships processes with Member States, UN agencies, and humanitarian partners, including key working groups and advisory bodies. 13. Conduct quantitative and qualitative research and draft advocacy materials: support research, data analysis and visualization on CERF-related topics, contributing to advocacy and information products, including thematic areas and fund allocations. 14. Analyze complex data sets: analyze and interpret complex data to drive informed decision-making in humanitarian projects and pooled fund allocations. 15. Perform other duties as required.

**Qualifications/special skills**

Be a student in the final year of a first university degree (bachelor or equivalent), in a Master's or a Ph.D. Programme or equivalent, or have completed a first university degree (bachelor or equivalent), Master's or Ph.D. Programme (typically with completion date not more than one year before the start-date of the internship). Please note that an official certificate will have to be provided at a later stage. Applicants to the UN Internship Programme are not required to have professional work experience. However, a field of study that is closely related to the type of internship that you are applying for is required. All applicants must be students in the final year of a first university degree (bachelor or equivalent), a Master's or a Ph.D. Programme or equivalent, or have completed a first university degree (bachelor or equivalent), Master's or Ph.D. Programme (with completion date not more than one year before the start-date of the internship). Do you meet any of the above criteria? Please indicate which one, and attach proof to the application. Please note an official certificate will be required at a later stage. Excellent knowledge of standard software applications, especially MS Word, MS PowerPoint, MS Excel and MS Teams is required. Knowledge of Statistics, Python, and data visualization tools is desirable.

**Languages**

• English and French are the official working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this position, fluency in spoken, read, understood and written English is required for all internship positions. • Fluency in French is desirable. • Knowledge of an additional official UN language is an advantage. Arabic, Chinese, Russian and Spanish are the official languages of the United Nations Secretariat.

**Additional Information**

• OCHA encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. • The United Nations will assist with arrangements for a G-4 visa for interns who are serving in the United States of America and require such a visa.

**Intern Specific text**

Interns are not financially remunerated by the United Nations. Costs and arrangements for travel, visas, accommodation and living expenses are the responsibility of interns or their sponsoring institutions. Interns who are not citizens or permanent residents of the country where the internship is undertaken, may be required to obtain the appropriate visa and work/employment authorization. Successful candidates should discuss their specific visa requirements before accepting the internship offer.

**No Fee**

THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CHARGE A FEE AT ANY STAGE OF THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS (APPLICATION, INTERVIEW MEETING, PROCESSING, OR TRAINING). THE UNITED NATIONS DOES NOT CONCERN ITSELF WITH INFORMATION ON APPLICANTS’ BANK ACCOUNTS.

jobs.title: COORDINATEUR.RICE URGENCE - ITURI - H/F
jobs.body:
L’ESPRIT ALIMA : La raison d’être d’ALIMA est de sauver des vies et de soigner les populations les plus vulnérables, sans aucune discrimination identitaire, religieuse ou politique, à travers des actions basées sur la proximité, l’innovation et l’alliance d’organisations et d’individus. Nous agissons avec humanisme, impartialité et dans le respect de l’éthique médicale universelle. Pour accéder aux patients et aux patientes, nous nous engageons à intervenir de façon neutre et indépendante.

LES VALEURS et PRINCIPES de notre action, inscrits au sein de notre CHARTE :

1. Le patient et la patiente d’abord
2. Révolutionner la médecine humanitaire
3. Responsabilité et liberté
4. Améliorer la qualité de nos actions
5. Faire confiance
6. L’intelligence collective
7. Responsabilité environnementale

ALIMA promeut et défend les principes des droits humains fondamentaux. ALIMA a une approche de tolérance zéro envers les personnes coupables d’actes de violences sexistes et sexuelles ainsi qu’envers l’inaction face à des faits de violence supposés ou avérés. La protection des personnes bénéficiant et impactées par notre intervention est notre priorité absolue dans tout ce que nous faisons. Toute personne collaborant avec ALIMA s’engage à :

- respecter la charte, le code de conduite, les politiques institutionnelles incluant la politique de protection contre les abus de pouvoir et les violences sexistes et sexuelles, la politique de prévention de la corruption et de la fraude ;
- signaler toute violation aux politiques, documents cadre et procédure à une supérieure, un supérieur, une référente, un référent ou à l’adresse alert@alima.ngo

SOIGNER - INNOVER – ENSEMBLE :

Depuis sa création en 2009, ALIMA a soigné plus de 10 millions de patients et patientes, et déploie aujourd’hui ses opérations dans 12 pays d’Afrique. En 2019, nous avons développé 41 projets de réponse médicale humanitaire pour répondre aux besoins de populations touchées par les conflits, les épidémies et l’extrême pauvreté. L’ensemble de ces projets se font en appui aux autorités sanitaires nationales à travers 330 structures de santé (dont 28 hôpitaux et 300 centres de santé). Nous travaillons en partenariat, notamment avec des ONGs locales, dès que cela est possible afin de nous assurer que nos patients et patientes bénéficient de l’expertise là où elle se trouve, que ce soit au niveau de leur pays ou du reste du monde. Par ailleurs, pour améliorer la réponse humanitaire, nous menons des projets de recherches opérationnelles et cliniques notamment dans le domaine de la lutte contre la malnutrition et les fièvres virales hémorragiques. ALIMA mène également des opérations en réponse à la pandémie covid-19 dans l’ensemble de nos missions.

NOS THÉMATIQUES PROJET : Malnutrition, Santé sexuelle et reproductive incluant les violences basées sur le genre, Santé Primaire et secondaire, Pédiatrie, Paludisme, Épidémies (Fièvres hémorragiques, méningite, Choléra, Rougeole, Dengue, Covid-19).

NOS PAYS D’INTERVENTIONS : Mali, Burkina Faso, République Centrafricaine, Nigeria, Niger, Tchad, République Démocratique du Congo, Cameroun, Guinée, Soudan du Sud, Mauritanie, Ethiopie, Haiti et Soudan.

ALIMA

ALIMA dispose d’une présence opérationnelle en Ituri depuis 2022, notamment dans les Zones de Santé de Bunia et de Rwampara, et bénéficie d’une bonne connaissance du contexte et des acteurs sanitaires locaux. Dès la déclaration de l’épidémie d’Ebola, ALIMA a activé son dispositif d’urgence, mobilisé ses équipes et ses stocks prépositionnés, et obtenu l’accréditation de l’Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) pour participer officiellement à la riposte.

ALIMA possède une expertise reconnue dans la gestion des épidémies de fièvres hémorragiques virales en RDC et à l’international. L’organisation a joué un rôle majeur lors de plusieurs flambées d’Ebola en RDC (11e à 16e épidémies) ainsi qu’en Guinée, en Ouganda, en Guinée Équatoriale et au Rwanda, à travers la prise en charge des cas, la surveillance, la prévention et contrôle des infections (PCI) et le renforcement des capacités des personnels de santé.

Depuis 2020, ALIMA s’appuie sur un plan national de préparation et de réponse aux fièvres hémorragiques virales lui permettant de déployer rapidement du personnel qualifié et des ressources médicales et WASH. L’organisation est également à l’origine du concept CUBE (Chambre d’Urgence Bio Sécurisée pour Épidémies), une innovation reconnue internationalement pour la prise en charge sécurisée des patients atteints de maladies hautement infectieuses.

Plus récemment, ALIMA a participé à la réponse à la précédente épidémie d’Ebola à Bulape ainsi qu’à la riposte contre l’épidémie de Mpox en RDC en 2024–2025, confirmant sa capacité à intervenir rapidement et efficacement dans les urgences sanitaires majeures.

A nos jours, ALIMA intervient à Bunia, Rwampara et Nizi avec

Lieu de mission : Bunia

PROTECTION DES BÉNÉFICIAIRES ET DES MEMBRES DE LA COMMUNAUTÉ

Niveau 3 : Dans le cadre de ses fonctions, le ou la titulaire du poste sera amené·e à visiter les programmes et être en contact avec des enfants ou/et des adultes vulnérables. Par conséquent, la vérification du casier judiciaire ou la présentation d'un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs sera nécessaire. Dans les situations où l’impossibilité de fournir un casier judiciaire ou un certificat de bonne vie et mœurs est constatée, une déclaration sur l’honneur sera demandée.

LIENS FONCTIONNELS ET HIERARCHIQUES

Il·Elle rend compte au Responsable Programme SUO (responsable hiérarchique)

MISSIONS ET ACTIVITES PRINCIPALES

Dans le cadre de la riposte à l’épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) 2026, ALIMA déploie une réponse médicale et humanitaire d’urgence. Le·la Coordinateur·trice Urgence assure la coordination opérationnelle globale de la réponse, en garantissant le pilotage quotidien des activités, la coordination multisectorielle des équipes terrain et la bonne mise en œuvre des interventions, en cohérence avec la stratégie d’ALIMA, les priorités de la riposte et l’évolution du contexte.

## Représentation, coordination et partenariats

- Représente ALIMA auprès des autorités sanitaires nationales et provinciales (Ministère de la Santé, COUSP, DPS, Zones de Santé), de l'OMS, des agences des Nations Unies, des ONG partenaires, des bailleurs et des autres acteurs de la riposte.
- Assure la participation active aux mécanismes de coordination de la riposte (IMS, clusters, groupes techniques, réunions partenaires).
- Développe, entretient et renforce les partenariats stratégiques avec les institutions nationales et internationales impliquées dans la réponse.
- Veille au maintien de relations de travail constructives avec les autorités locales et facilite les processus administratifs nécessaires au déploiement des activités.
- Contribue au positionnement stratégique d'ALIMA au sein de la réponse Ebola.

## Analyse stratégique, planification et pilotage de la riposte

- Assure une veille permanente de l'évolution épidémiologique, humanitaire, sécuritaire et politique.
- Analyse les données de surveillance, les tendances de transmission et les risques d'expansion géographique afin d'orienter la stratégie opérationnelle.
- Identifie les nouveaux besoins opérationnels et propose l'ouverture, l'extension, la réduction ou la fermeture des interventions selon l'évolution de l'épidémie.
- Coordonne l'élaboration, la mise en œuvre et l'actualisation de la stratégie de riposte d'ALIMA.
- Garantit la cohérence des interventions médicales, logistiques, WASH, IPC, laboratoire, engagement communautaire, santé mentale et soutien psychosocial.
- Assure le suivi des indicateurs opérationnels et épidémiologiques afin d'adapter rapidement les activités.

## Coordination opérationnelle

- Supervise le déploiement des équipes d'urgence et assure leur coordination quotidienne.
- Garantit la mise en place et le bon fonctionnement des CTE, centres d'isolement, unités de transit, équipes d'intervention rapide (RRT) et autres dispositifs de prise en charge.
- Coordonne les activités de préparation et de réponse (preparedness et response) selon les scénarios épidémiques.
- Veille à la qualité technique des interventions et au respect des protocoles nationaux et internationaux.
- Coordonne les référents métiers (médical, logistique, finances, RH, sécurité, WASH, laboratoire, engagement communautaire, MHPSS).
- Assure la coordination entre les bases, les équipes terrain et le siège.

## Gestion des financements et des bailleurs

- Identifie les opportunités de financement liées à la riposte.
- Coordonne l'élaboration des propositions de projets et des budgets.
- Assure les relations opérationnelles avec les bailleurs institutionnels et privés.
- Garantit le respect des engagements contractuels, des indicateurs et des exigences de reporting.
- Supervise la rédaction des rapports narratifs intermédiaires et finaux.
- Suit l'évolution budgétaire des projets et propose les ajustements nécessaires.

## Gestion logistique, approvisionnement, financière et administrative

- Supervise le suivi budgétaire de l'ensemble de la riposte.
- Veille au respect des procédures ALIMA et des exigences des bailleurs.
- Veille à la planification et à la disponibilité en temps opportun des approvisionnements et des intrants nécessaires aux opérations.
- Suit les prévisions de trésorerie et les besoins financiers des opérations.
- Valide les dépenses selon les procédures en vigueur.
- Garantit la conformité administrative, financière et logistique des activités de la riposte

## Sécurité

- Suit en permanence l'évolution du contexte sécuritaire et son impact sur les opérations.
- Met à jour l'analyse des risques et adapte les mesures de mitigation.
- Valide les plans de sécurité et veille à leur diffusion auprès des équipes.
- Assure le suivi des incidents sécuritaires et coordonne les réponses appropriées.
- En lien avec le siège, décide des adaptations opérationnelles, des relocalisations ou des évacuations lorsque nécessaire.

## Management des ressources humaines

- Encadre l'équipe de coordination de la riposte et les coordinateurs terrain.
- Définit les objectifs individuels et assure le suivi des performances.
- Organise les réunions de coordination opérationnelle.
- Identifie les besoins en recrutement, formation et renforcement des capacités.
- Favorise le développement des compétences des équipes nationales et internationales.
- Veille au bien-être du personnel et à la prévention des risques psychosociaux liés aux interventions en contexte Ebola.

## Qualité, suivi-évaluation et amélioration continue

- Met en place les mécanismes de suivi de la qualité des activités.
- Analyse régulièrement les performances de la réponse et propose les ajustements nécessaires.
- Organise les revues opérationnelles, les retours d'expérience (After Action Reviews) et les exercices de capitalisation.
- Contribue au développement et à la mise à jour des SOP, guides opérationnels et outils de gestion de la riposte.

## Reporting et gestion de l'information

- Coordonne la production des SitReps, tableaux de bord et rapports de situation.
- Garantit la qualité, la fiabilité et la diffusion des informations opérationnelles.
- Produit les analyses nécessaires à la prise de décision du siège et des partenaires.
- Assure un reporting adapté au rythme de l'épidémie.

## Juridique et conformité

- Veille à ce que tous les accords, MoU et autorisations nécessaires soient en vigueur.
- Coordonne la négociation et le renouvellement des accords avec les autorités sanitaires.
- Garantit le respect des cadres réglementaires nationaux ainsi que des politiques ALIMA.

## Communication, plaidoyer et visibilité

- Contribue à la stratégie de communication d'ALIMA sur la riposte.
- Identifie les enjeux nécessitant un plaidoyer auprès des autorités ou des partenaires.
- Appuie la préparation des visites de bailleurs, partenaires et médias.
- Veille à la cohérence des messages institutionnels et opérationnels en lien avec le siège.
- Contribue à la valorisation des résultats et des leçons apprises de la riposte.

## EXPERIENCES ET COMPETENCES

- Expérience sur des interventions d’urgence
- Expérience indispensable en termes de management d’équipe, gestion de projet, mise en place de stratégies d’intervention et gestion de la sécurité
- Connaissances dans un domaine technique humanitaire
- Compréhension des principales tâches administratives et financières
- Connaissance des procédures bailleurs EU, UN, Écho, Startfund etc.
- Compétences rédactionnelles indispensables
- Capacité à entretenir des réseaux et mener un lobbying pro actif

### Qualités du candidat 

- Capacités d’analyse et de synthèse
- Capacité d’organisation, d’adaptation et d’animation d’équipe
- Diplomatie et capacité à la négociation
- Sang-froid, patience et maturité professionnelle

### Langues parlées du candidat 

- Maîtrise du Français (oral et écrit) indispensable

### Conditions

- **Durée et type de contrat :** CDD de droit français de 03 mois avec possibilité de prolongation
- **Prise de poste :** Dès que possible
- **Salaire :**  Salaire grille salariale ALIMA + valorisation d’expériences + Perdiem journalier
- **ALIMA prend en charge :**
- Les frais de déplacements entre le pays d’origine de l’expatrié et le lieu de mission
- 2,08 jours de congés par mois
- La couverture médicale du premier jour de contrat à un mois après la date de départ du pays de mission pour l’employé et ses ayants droits
- La politique de break tous les 3 mois (pour 6 mois de mission)
- L’évacuation pour l’employé

jobs.title: Caseworker
jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Caseworker provides trauma-informed services to refugees and other ORR qualified immigrants to support a positive integration experience and the achievement of client self-sufficiency. The Caseworker works closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service and/or self-sufficiency plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Provide comprehensive case management services enrolled clients.
- Conduct intake services with clients to assess needs. Develop self-sufficiency plans and timelines in partnership with each client. Provide individualized support through direct services, referrals, and advocacy.
- Receive referrals for case management for ORR-eligible and TANF-eligible clients and participate in any needed case conference meetings to assure continuity of care.
- Assess client needs, creates Family Self-Sufficiency Plans (FSSPs) and Individual Employability Plans (IEPs), focusing on removing employment barriers, stabilizing, and obtaining and retaining employment.
- Assess and monitor client progress to support their attainment of established goals, address challenges, and to ensure that available resources are utilized.
- Detail each client interaction in accordance with program requirements. Input client information in database(s) and assist with tracking and reporting as needed.
- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations. Build and maintain relationships with area service providers for the benefit of clients.
- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.
- May train and lead the activities of volunteers and interns.
- Conduct outreach to case management staff, refugee-serving agencies, ethnic community-based organizations, and others to inform service providers and refugees of programs and services.
- Complete eligibility screenings for all referral and enrollment paperwork for all eligible Program participants.
- Provide comprehensive case management services, including assisting with benefits applications as appropriate.
- Guide/assist participants to establish contact and receive support services in the community based on their service plan.
- Ensure all services are linguistically appropriate and help advocate with mainstream service providers for linguistically appropriate services.
- Complete case notes in a detailed and timely fashion.
- Ensure all family data is entered into data management system in a timely manner.
- Assist with the preparation of donor funding reports and new funding proposals.
- Participate in all program meetings, staff development activities, and fully engages as a member of the team.
- Follow all IRC policies, procedures and protocols including adherence to the IRC Way and Child Safeguarding.
- Other related duties as assigned.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:**  Casework Supervisor

**Indirect Reporting:** Interns/Volunteers

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Undergraduate degree Social Work or similar field strongly preferred; comparable related work experience may be substituted.

***Work Experience:***

- 2+ years of case management experience in a social services environment.
- Experience working with vulnerable or under served populations preferred

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Computer proficiency with an emphasis on Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook).
- Strong organizational skills and detail-oriented
- Public Speaking and/or presentation experience preferred
- Ability to effectively communicate and work as a team member with collaborative partners, the community, and clients in a cross-cultural, multi-disciplinary environment.
- Ability and willingness to drive 15 passenger van.
- Strong attention to detail with the ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Problem solver capable of working well independently and as a part of a team.

***Language Skills:***

- Proficiency in written and spoken English, bilingual ability preferred in Spanish, Dari, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, Arabic, French or other refugee/immigrant language used in Arizona. Cross-cultural understanding and strong communication skills, both written and verbal.

***Certificates or Licenses:***

- Must have a valid driver’s license, active insurance policy, access to reliable transportation and the ability to travel regularly throughout the service delivery area.
- In accordance with Arizona State Law, must possess or be eligible to receive a fingerprint clearance card.

**Working Environment*****:***

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above outlined responsibilities.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.
- Must be able to lift 35 to 50 pounds (furniture, household supplies, and food boxes).

**Commitment to Diversity and Inclusivity:** IRC is committed to building a diverse organization and a climate of inclusivity. We strongly encourage applications from candidates who can demonstrate that they can contribute to this goal.

**Compensation:** ($20.97). Compensation is based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Head of Humanitarian Mine Action
jobs.body:
**The Danish Refugee Council (DRC)** is a leading protection agency with a mandate to protect, advocate for and promote durable solutions for displacement-affected populations. DRC has been operating in Ukraine since 2014 and currently employs over 800 staff implementing emergency and recovery programming across the Protection, Livelihoods, Shelter/NFIs and Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (humanitarian mine action) sectors through direct interventions and support to duty bearers and civil society organisations (CSOs).

DRC’s programming is based on an integrated approach in which sectors are designed to complement and reinforce one another to maximise impact for conflict-affected communities. Within this model, humanitarian mine action is not viewed solely through clearance outputs such as square metres released, but as an enabler for recovery and durable solutions. The focus is on outcomes for communities — whether land can safely be cultivated again, infrastructure restored, services resumed and displaced populations supported to rebuild their lives.

DRC implements this approach through a decentralised operational model in which most of the programme delivery, coordination and day-to-day decision-making takes place through its area offices rather than the Country Office. The Country Office provides strategic coordination, technical guidance, oversight and support services to enable field operations. This structure is intended to ensure that programmes remain closely connected to local realities and community needs while maintaining coherent technical and operational standards across the response.

This integrated and outcome-oriented approach differentiates DRC from other mine action operators. The Head of HMA, while focused on the responsibilities outlined below, is therefore expected to work across functions and sectors to enable integrated, area-based programming and support operational decision-making that contributes to broader recovery outcomes for conflict-affected communities.

**Overall purpose of the role**:

**The role of the Head of Humanitarian Mine Action (HMA)** is to provide the overall leadership, management and oversight of the delivery of DRC’s HMA portfolio in Ukraine.

The Head of HMA works under the supervision of the Head of Operations (HoO) and in close collaboration with the Head of Programs and Country Director (CD). The Head of HMA will cut across the Programme and Operations departments of DRC Ukraine and have responsibilities across both areas of work. Engagement on any programmatic elements will be in consultation with the Head of Programme (HoP) while engagement on operational elements with the Head of Operations (HoO).

The role of the Head of HMA is to guide the development of the HMA Programme Strategy, serve as the focal point for external engagement and fundraising on HMA and provide the overall leadership, management and oversight of the delivery of DRC’s HMA portfolio in Ukraine. The role also leads the liaison with Mine Action Authorities at central level and drives the capacity building and nationalization strategy for HMA staff.

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**People Management**

- Lead and line manage direct reports (including people planning, development, performance appraisal and well-being) in line with DRC policies and national legislation.
- Maintain strong oversight of the HMA team structure at Country and Area Office levels. Ensure sound management practices are in place within the team. Advise the management on critical positions and flag challenges.
- Drive capacity building of key HMA staff in technical functions and oversee the development and implementation of nationalisation plans for key roles within the HMA teams.

**Strategic Leadership and Programme Oversight**

- Sets the strategic direction of the HMA Programme in alignment with DRC Ukraine country and area strategies.
- Leads the design, review, and updating of the HMA strategy in coordination with the HoP.
- Ensures HMA priorities are aligned with national mine action strategies, donor priorities, and DRC global technical standards.
- Represent HMA in extended SMT.
- Work closely with Protection and VA teams to identify synergies and conflict-sensitive, people-centred programming opportunities.
- Identify and promote opportunities for integration between HMA and other DRC sectors (Protection, Shelter, Economic Recovery) and support joint analysis and integrated responses based on protection monitoring and community needs.

**Programme Design and Development**

- Participates in relevant Go/No-Go decision-making processes for HMA funding opportunities.
- Leads all HMA technical inputs to concept notes and proposals, including setting targets, outputs and indicators and developing budgets and workplans for both direct and partner-led implementation
- Conduct technical review of partner proposals and budgets in coordination with Grants, MEAL and Partnerships.

**Programme Reporting, Monitoring & Communications**

- Ensures quality and timely HMA inputs are provided to donor reports and communication products.
- Provides technical review of all HMA-related reporting before submission.
- Oversees data collection and management in line with IMSMA standards, in coordination with the Deputy Head of Programme and MEAL Manager.

**Localisation and Partnership Development**

- Lead the HMA localisation strategy under the coordination of the HoP.
- Ensures capacity assessments inform the selection of national HMA partners and that capacity development plans are designed in line with DRC's strategy.
- Ensures partner-led implementation and partners' capacity development meet DRC's technical and quality standards.

**Operational Delivery**

- Holds overall responsibility for the planning and delivery of DRC's HMA portfolio in Ukraine, ensuring workplans and technical implementation plans are followed throughout project implementation, with regular updates and adjustments as needed.
- Oversee all phases of implementation and closure for both direct and partner-led activities.
- With the support of the HMA Operations Manager, ensures operational planning for the delivery of clearance, survey, and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education activities.
- Ensure Training and Quality Management take place and are followed up.
- Ensure that priorities set by the NMAA, MAC, Oblast authorities and the donors are taken into consideration in the planning and implementation of operational activities.
- Ensure that HMA projects adhere to operational Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and National and International Mine Action Standards in the field.
- Accountable for centralized and country level initiatives including procurements, certifications, partners capacity building, team training etc. in close coordination with the relevant colleagues.
- Ensure regular monitoring and quality assurance are provided including direct and partner led implementation including monitoring report and support to corrective actions.
- Regularly follow up with IM, MEAL and Grants to ensure achievements are understood and reported
- In close coordination with the Head of Safety, ensure coordination with Safety and Management takes place at area level regarding the selection of training areas and polygons. Coordinate regularly with the HoS to discuss any challenges faced in the area

**Finance, budget, Supply Chain & Procurement – in close cooperation with the Humanitarian Mine Action Operations Manager**

- Prepares and updates monthly budget forecasts, workplans, and procurement plans for country office-level lines and initiatives
- Ensure all country office-level HMA procurements are planned, initiated and followed up.

**External Engagement**

**Donors:**

- Serve as the focal point for HMA donor engagement in close coordination with the HoP and CD.
- Prepare technical talking points for donor meetings, visits, and events.
- Contribute to donor relationship management, including participation in donor visits and sector events, in coordination with HoP and CD.

**Authorities**

- Ensures coherent and high-quality technical engagement with national and local mine action authorities.
- Maintains oversight of technical communication with authorities and inform SMT of key developments, policy changes, or risks.

**Mine Action Actors and UN System**

- Represent DRC Ukraine in mine action coordination mechanisms (e.g. AoR, technical working groups).
- Engages with other HMA actors to promote coordination, learning, and best practice sharing.

**About you**

To be successful in this role, we expect you to bring deep technical expertise and a strong track record in operations and people management. You are a confident and structured manager, able to lead diverse teams while keeping a clear focus on capacity building and the nationalisation of roles. Diplomatic, patient and persistent, you build lasting professional relationships with national authorities and other mine action actors while holding the line on technical and operational standards. A genuine team player, you approach challenges with a constructive, cooperative and problem-solving mindset.

Beyond technical excellence, you bring a genuine interest in integrated programming and are comfortable working across functions and sectors to contribute to broader recovery outcomes for conflict-affected communities.

We also expect the following:

- Minimum 7 years of working experience with strong knowledge in the HMA sector at senior level, evidenced by recognised technical qualifications. EOD qualifications are an asset but not a requirement.
- Minimum 5 years of experience managing and leading multi-disciplinary teams in complex humanitarian contexts, including experience of working in conflict settings.
- Demonstrated experience in programme strategy design and development, including proposal writing and budget management for multiple concurrent grants.
- Solid understanding of HMA programme cycle management, including IMAS/NMAS compliance.
- Experience in external engagement with donors, Mine Action Authorities and UN coordination bodies.
- Experience in partner and localisation management, including capacity development of national partners.
- Experience coordinating across departments (Programme, Operations, Finance, Supply Chain, HR) at field and country office level.
- Demonstrated commitment to DRC's integrated and outcome-oriented programming approach.

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

- **Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- **Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- **Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- **Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- **Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

- **Contract length**: 12 months fixed-term contract with the possibility of extension depending on performance and availability of funding after successful completion of a 3-month probationary period
- **Band**: E1 – Manager
- **Designation of Duty Station**: Kyiv, non-family duty station
- **Start date:** ASAP

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national and international employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-us/work-with-us/working-at-drc/salary-package-and-benefits/).

jobs.title: Call for Projects
jobs.body:
**PROGRAMME NAME:** SYRIA HEALTH RECOVERY AND RECONSTRUCTION EFFORT (SHERE)

**OBJECT OF THE CALL FOR PROJECTS:** GRANT AWARDS FOR REHABILITATION, EQUIPMENT AND QUALITY IMPROVEMENT OF HEALTH FACILITIES IN DAMASCUS AND RURAL DAMASCUS

**AVAILABLE AMOUNT OF THE CALL FOR PROJECTS:** 699,750 $

**FINANCIAL SIZING OF GRANTS:**

*Maximum grant amount:*

- *Lot 1 (Ashmar PHC): 114,064* *$*
- *Lot 2 (J. Artuz PHC): 88,194* *$*
- *Lot 3 (Kiswa PHC): 92,927* *$*
- *Lot 4 (* *PHC Equipment): 106,860* *$*
- *Lot 5 (Al-Zahrawi hospital):* *246,614 $*
- Lot 6 (Training): 51,091 *$*

**DATE, TIME AND LOCATION OF THE CALL FOR PROJECTS INFORMATION MEETING:** October 8th 2026 AT 3PM DAMASCUS TIME (2PM PARIS TIME) - THE SESSION WILL BE CONDUCTED ONLINE

**DISCLAIMER**

For open call for projects. All documents must be submitted at the same time (concept note and full application). During the first stage, only the concept notes will be evaluated. Subsequently, full applications will be evaluated for the shortlisted lead applicants. After assessment of the full applications, the eligibility of the provisionally shortlisted applicants will be verified on the basis of supporting documentation requested by Expertise France and in light of the declaration signed by the lead applicant, submitted at the same time as the full application.

## Syria Health Recovery and Reconstruction Effort (SHeRE)

## Context

Expertise France (EF) developed the "*Health Recovery in Northeast Syria*" (HERNES) program in 2019 that was funded jointly by the French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs (French MoEFA) and the European Union (EU). The program was delivered in 4 phases until 2026.

Transitioning from HERNES, EF developed the “*Syria* *Health* *Recovery and Reconstruction Effort* ” (SHERE) project to cover all of Syria. This program aims to support an inclusive and sustainable recovery of the health system in Syria by improving access to quality Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health (RMNCH) services. Through targeted rehabilitation of health facilities, provision of essential equipment, capacity strengthening of health personnel, and technical support at national and sub-national levels, the project seeks to enhance service availability, strengthen health system functions, and improve health outcomes for conflict-affected populations.

Working closely with national authorities, implementing partners, and community stakeholders, SHERE promotes harmonized standards, evidence-based practices, and coordinated sector-wide approaches to contribute to long-term resilience and better health for women, children, and vulnerable groups across Syria.

### Program objectives and priorities

This programme aims to address gaps in access to quality health care through the **comprehensive rehabilitation, equipping, and quality improvement of five strategically selected health facilities** in Damascus and Rural Damascus with the Syrian Ministry of Health (MoH), prioritizing those with the greatest potential to meet urgent community health needs and serve as sustainable centres of care.

After preliminary assessment in consultation with the Ministry of Health, 5 health facilities were identified and distributed into lots of this Call for Proposals. These conflict-afflicted facilities are in need of rehabilitation, they serve large populations and provide maternal and child health services, in line with the SHeRE project objective. Expertise France teams conducted off-site and onsite data collection in close coordination with the MoH to provide a comprehensive overview of each facility needs which were prioritized by MoH.

The **overall objective** of this call for projects is **to rehabilitate, equip and improve quality of five critical health facilities in Damascus and Rural Damascus**, in line with facility-level technical assessments and subsequent MoH-led recovery strategy for the sector (*kindly refer to annex H of this Call for Proposals*).

The **specific objectives** of this call for projects are:

**SO1 - Rehabilitation**

Facility-level technical assessments identified structural, electrical, plumbing, and environmental health needs in targeted health facilities. Rehabilitation will focus on restoring essential infrastructure, ensuring compliance with safety standards, and enabling the facility to operate at full capacity. The rehabilitation will target 3 PHCs and 1 Hospital. Eligible activities may include repairs to walls, ceilings, floors, and roofs; restoration of water and sanitation systems; installation of backup power systems; and upgrades to ventilation and infection prevention and control (IPC) infrastructure. Intervention priorities under this component have been disaggregated for each lot in Annex H to this Call for Proposals.

**SO2 - Provision of Equipment and Supplies**

Selected partners should equip the targeted health facilities with the necessary medical equipment, furniture, and consumables to enable the delivery of quality services. Equipment packages will be tailored to the facility’s intended service scope—such as primary health care, maternal and newborn care, or basic emergency services. Eligible activities may include the provision of diagnostic devices, delivery beds, neonatal resuscitation equipment, laboratory tools, sterilization units, and essential medicines and consumables, as needed in each target health facility. Intervention priorities under this component have been compiled into one lot for all the PHCs in Annex H to this Call for Proposals.

**SO3 - Capacity Support**

For services in target health facilities to be effectively ru n and sustained, this programme believes that rehabilitation and equipping efforts must be paired with capacity building support – which constitutes the sixth and last lot of this Call for Proposals. Activities under Lot 6 will include strengthening the skills of health personnel, improving management and organizational skills, as well as improving aspects that enhance coordination, accountability, and service quality in all five targeted health facilities. Priorities for capacity development include a wide-range of technical thematic topics such as standardized Infection Prevention & Control (IPC) processes, Medical / Clinical Waste Management, Pharmacy Management & Safe Storage, Cold Chain Management & Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) Diabetes & Chronic Disease Management, Laboratory Quality & Biosafety, Patient Referral System as well as Disability-Inclusive Healthcare & PwD-Sensitive Care. Intervention priorities under this component have been compiled into one lot in Annex H to this Call for Proposals.

For lots 1 to 3, and 5, prospective applicants must submit a project proposal covering SO1 and SO2 (Rehabilitation and Equipment) and/or SO3 (Capacity Support).

For lot 4, prospective applicants must submit a project proposal covering SO2 and/or SO3 in one or more health facilities.

For lot 6, prospective applicants can submit a project proposal for capacity development programme in line with priorities identified under SO2 and SO3 for health personnel from all five health facilities to enrol.

**The full package of the call for project rules and guidelines, annexes and required forms can be accessed via the link below:**

[Call for Projects Package](https://1drv.ms/f/c/8854364942ecc3de/IgCz0p6b9M2STL8zfR46ZvPsAXaPWLlNpj13JZWAYE9oYX4?e=239DxP)

jobs.title: Digital Community Liaison (Dari and Pashto)
jobs.body:
**Job Overview:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) is one of the leading providers of high-quality programming for refugees resettling to the United States. The IRC is committed to developing innovative programs that respond to the refugees’ unique strengths and needs, using our learning and experience to shape policy and practice, and highlighting and promoting best practices in refugee services provision.

The IRC is seeking a Digital Community Liaison for Settle In, a program providing information and support for newcomers in multiple languages through its website (SettleInUS.org), mobile app, and social media platforms. More information on Settle In can be found on [https://www.settleinus.org](https://www.settleinus.org).

The Digital Community Liaison will support the Settle In Facebook page ([https://www.facebook.com/SettleInUS](https://www.facebook.com/SettleInUS)), which is available in Dari, Pashto, Spanish, Haitian-Creole, and English. Digital Community Liaisons interact with newcomers in the United States on social media primarily through private messaging and social media post comments. They help users navigate information on Settle In platforms, clarify and share information, support live events, and lend a friendly, empathetic ear. This position reports to Settle In’s Senior Digital Community Officer.

**Major Responsibilities:**

- Support the Settle In Facebook page in collaboration with the Settle In team.
- Reply to messages and comments received on Settle In with the help of trusted resources and by following moderation guidelines and escalation protocols.
- Translate articles, video scripts, and social media posts in Dari and Pashto focused on key Cultural Orientation messages in coordination with the Senior Digital Community Officer.
- Record live event audio and other video scripts in Dari and Pashto
- Contribute to a Frequently Asked Questions document in English, Dari, and Pashto that can be used to answer user questions on the platform.
- Based on user messages, comments, and questions or misunderstandings, propose new content topics to feed into content creation.
- Share opinions, feedback, cultural awareness, contextual knowledge, and learning with the wider team on an ongoing basis. Present findings to relevant external partners, as needed.
- Collaborate with other staff to ensure maximum visibility and integration of all new resources.
- Support collection of monitoring and evaluation data for Settle In initiatives.
- As needed, backstop and support other Settle In team members.

**Job Requirements:**

- 4-year college degree in relevant field required (or equivalent experience).
- Minimum one year of relevant professional experience.
- Fluent in English and Dari and Pashto.
- Strong computer proficiency and well-acquainted with basic software tools. Can navigate autonomously in Windows and Microsoft Suite.
- Knowledge of social media platforms, especially Facebook, and cultural use of these platforms or ability to learn new technologies quickly.
- Previous experience working with refugee resettlement or other immigration pathways preferred.
- Excellent written and oral communication skills: the ability to communicate effectively in English and Dari and Pashto.
- High emotional intelligence (our users are in difficult periods of their lives and moderators need to empathize with them).
- An understanding of the power and importance of accurate information. Fantastic attention to detail.
- Solid organizational skills with the ability to juggle multiple tasks, set priorities, effectively manage time, and meet deadlines.
- Experience in supporting newcomers’ access to timely, relevant, and accurate information about life in the United States.

***Language Skills:** Fluent in written and spoken Dari, Pashto, and English.*

**Working Environment:** This position is a remote working environment. Required domestic travel up to 20%.

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $28 - $34/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Software Developer Analyst
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
**Background/IRC Summary**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities which support them, as well as those who remain within their homes and communities. At work today in over 40 countries and 25 U.S. cities, we improve outcomes in the areas of health, safety, economic wellbeing, education and power.

The IT department provides end-to-end technology solutions for the organization, including Application Development, Integration and Management, Enterprise Architecture, User Experience, Quality Assurance & Testing, and overall Product Management. While this role sits within IT, its focus is on partnering with the Measurement, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning (METAL) Unit — bringing IT's systems and development expertise to METAL's technology and data priorities. The METAL Unit supports Crisis Response, Recovery & Development (CRRD) in building a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and coordinates the piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions across four pillars: Global METAL Practice, Technology for Programs, Regional METAL Support, and CRRD Data & Analytics. This role is anchored in Technology for Programs which maintains the tools and systems that support program teams' data collection and use in the field.

**Job Overview/Summary**

Focused on data collection and program administration technology support, the Software Developer Analyst is a member of the team responsible for developing, implementing, and supporting IRC’s global Data Toolkits and the analysis of the data generated by these products. This includes CommCare, Microsoft Power BI, and Microsoft SQL Server Azure based data warehouse. Working in partnership with staff at various levels and locations, the Software Developer Analyst performs a key role in analyzing, developing, and improving tools and processes contributing to the successful rollout of the Data Toolkits products.

Specific tasks include data platform development, support, configuration, technical assistance and issues routing, second line help desk support, and participation in setting standards for processes, data quality, security, and systems configurations.

**Major Responsibilities**

- Design, develop, and maintain Data Toolkits in CommCare
- Design and build PowerBI Dashboards linked to live CommCare data
- Review and analyze software requirements, confirm the feasibility and complexity of these requirements, and convert them into estimated developer tasks, validating that each requirement traces cleanly to system design and existing configuration before work begins
- Provide updates and technology insights/clarifications to the relevant stakeholders
- Develop and maintain data and metadata definitions, documentation and versioning.
- Create technical documentation including system diagrams and implementation manuals
- Implement and maintain data quality processes and development standards
- Ensure compliance with IRC’s data protection, confidentiality, and security policies
- Provide Tier-2 and Tier-3 support emerging from Countries and Regional Technology support team for the measurement technology products rolled out.
- During piloting and rollout, provide training and hyper-support on measurement technology products in close collaboration with the regional technology teams.
- Any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

## **Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Business Systems Analyst
- Direct Reports: None
- Management in Partnership: None

## **Key Internal Relationships:**

- ## CommCare Product Manager
- METAL QA Analyst
- IT Data Team

**Required Skills**

- Three to six years of experience working in technology domain to develop and rollout data or technology platforms for programs – out of which, at least three years of experience developing, implementing, and supporting CommCare development for large and complex programs.
- Experience in source code and version control platforms, for example, GitHub, Azure DevOps, or similar.
- Strong in team development processes including pair programming, shadow sessions, code reviews and other strategies to ensure high-quality programing.
- Strong code quality assurance practices including unit testing, integration testing, as well as regression testing to ensure quality of the code getting shipped into production.
- Working knowledge of agile software delivery practices (user stories, backlog grooming, sprint ceremonies) and a demonstrated preference for iterative, requirements-driven development.
- Ability to effectively communicate in English both in verbal (i.e., day-to-day discussions, team meetings) and written (requirements and design specifications) form, as well as an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications. More specifically, the ability to clearly explain complex technology issues in layman’s terms and simplify tech-related language depending on the audience/stakeholders is a huge asset.
- Strong attention to detail to ensure fidelity to requirements and high-quality products.
- Strong analytic curiosity and innovative problem-solving skills using a system thinking approach.
- Demonstrable ability to work both independently and in a dynamic, cross-functional team structure.
- Demonstrable ability to establish and maintain working relationships across all departments and levels of the organization.

**Education:**

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, or related discipline
- Experience with Databricks, Dataverse connectors, APIs, and Microsoft Azure

**This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.**

**Compensation:** (UK Pay Rate: £49,598 - £60,040/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. jobs.title: WASH Technical Advisor, Nepal (Local Consultant)
jobs.body:
**Project HOPE** is an international NGO with more than 1,000 engaged employees and volunteers who work around the globe, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients, provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up, and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

**Code of Conduct**

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a ***culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.***

**Summary:**

Project HOPE is seeking a **WASH Technical Advisor** to support its emergency response to landslides and flooding in Nepal. The consultant will provide technical guidance and support for the design, implementation, monitoring, and coordination of emergency WASH activities serving affected communities and supporting health delivery points.

The consultant will work closely with Project HOPE's emergency response and program teams, local partners, government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, and other humanitarian organizations. The consultant will provide technical recommendations, monitor progress and water quality, support coordination, and identify and address challenges affecting WASH activities.

**Scope of Consultancy**

The consultant will provide services in the following areas:

- Provide technical guidance on emergency WASH activities, including water supply, sanitation, hygiene promotion, water trucking, and water quality monitoring.
- Support the design, implementation, and rehabilitation of water systems, as appropriate to the emergency context.
- Monitor WASH activities and provide recommendations and mitigation measures to address implementation challenges.
- Conduct and document water quality testing associated with water trucking, water distribution, and other relevant WASH activities.
- Support the integration of WASH activities with health, gender, protection, nutrition, and other relevant humanitarian sectors.
- Coordinate with government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, UN agencies, NGOs, local implementing partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Provide technical input to WASH-related planning, procurement, budgeting, partner activities, monitoring, and reporting.
- Participate in relevant coordination meetings and provide regular technical updates to the Emergency Response Team.
- Support monitoring of WASH-related partner deliverables and identify and flag implementation, performance, or compliance concerns.
- Provide technical input to internal and donor reporting related to WASH activities.

**Expected Outputs**

During the consultancy period, the consultant is expected to contribute and deliver the following:

- Effective technical oversight and support for implementation of emergency WASH activities in Nepal.
- Regular monitoring of WASH activities, including water trucking, water distribution, water quality testing, and hygiene-related interventions.
- Timely identification of WASH-related challenges, with practical recommendations and mitigation measures provided to the Emergency Response Team.
- Regular technical updates and reporting on WASH activities, progress, challenges, and priorities.
- Effective coordination with government authorities, WASH Cluster actors, humanitarian organizations, local partners, and other relevant stakeholders.
- Support technical input to WASH-related planning, procurement, budgeting, partner activities, and reporting.
- Documentation of water quality testing and other relevant WASH monitoring data.
- Technical recommendations to support quality, accountability, and alignment of WASH activities with applicable humanitarian standards, including Sphere standards.

Detailed deliverables, timelines, and performance expectations will be agreed upon with the consultant and documented as part of the consultancy engagement.

Duration of Assignment: Approximately 1 month

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:**

- Bachelor's degree in water and sanitation engineering, civil engineering, or a related WASH technical field.
- At least 5 years of experience designing and implementing emergency WASH programs, preferably in humanitarian, IDP, refugee, or migrant settings.
- Experience with water supply systems, sanitation, hygiene promotion, water quality testing, and WASH activities in or around health facilities.
- Experience working in emergency and early recovery contexts.
- Knowledge of Sphere standards and humanitarian WASH practices.
- Experience coordinating with government authorities, humanitarian organizations, partners, and WASH Cluster actors.
- Experience with WASH monitoring, reporting, proposal development, and/or donor reporting.
- Strong communication and coordination skills.
- Experience working in Nepal or a similar humanitarian emergency context.
- Experience integrating WASH with health, gender, protection, and other humanitarian sectors.
- Experience working with local implementing partners and supporting WASH-related procurement and activity planning.
- Fluency in Nepali and working proficiency in English are required.

The consultancy fee will be determined based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

**Notice to applicants:** Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only applicants who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

jobs.title: Manager de Programme – Maison des Droits Humains
jobs.body:
**INTRODUCTION**

Le Centre Carter est fondamentalement engagé pour la promotion des droits de l’Homme et l’atténuation des souffrances humaines. Il cherche à prévenir et à résoudre les conflits, à renforcer la liberté et la démocratie et à améliorer la santé.

L’objectif primordial du Centre Carter en RDC est de promouvoir la redevabilité, la transparence et le respect des droits de l’homme en renforçant les capacités des acteurs de la société civile et des institutions gouvernementales. En 2007, le Centre Carter a créé la Maison des Droits Humains (MDH) au niveau national comme un véhicule pour construire une citoyenneté dynamique et tenir le gouvernement responsable.

**CONTEXTE ET RÉSUMÉ DU POSTE**

Sous la supervision du/de la Représentant(e) Pays principal(e) (SCR) du Centre Carter en RDC et en étroite coordination avec le/la Directeur(trice) associé(e) pour les droits humains basé(e) au siège à Atlanta, aux États-Unis, le/la Manager de Programme – Maison des Droits Humains (MDH) dirige et gère la mise en œuvre d’un portefeuille de projets dans le domaine des droits humains. Il/Elle assure le leadership stratégique, programmatique et opérationnel de la Maison des Droits Humains afin de garantir la mise en œuvre efficace des activités, le renforcement des capacités des partenaires et l’atteinte des objectifs du programme en RDC.

Il/Elle représente l’initiative Maison des Droits Humains en RDC et entretient des relations de collaboration avec les bailleurs de fonds, les autorités gouvernementales ainsi que les organisations non gouvernementales nationales et internationales partenaires. Il/Elle travaille en étroite collaboration avec le/la Responsable Principal(e) des opérations et du support, le/la Responsable des ressources humaines, le/la Conseiller(ère) sécurité et le/la Directeur(trice) des finances et de l’administration afin d’assurer la mise en œuvre efficace du programme conformément aux procédures applicables. Il/Elle supervise l’équipe de la Maison des Droits Humains et collabore avec le/la Responsable Principal(e) du programme Gouvernance des Ressources Naturelles, le/la Programme Manager Observation Citoyenne, les consultants et les experts externes en vue d’atteindre les objectifs du programme. Il/Elle exécute toute autre tâche connexe requise dans le cadre de ses fonctions.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

Sous la supervision du SCR, et en collaboration avec le/la Directeur(trice) associé(e), le /la Manager des Programmes de la MDH assure les responsabilités suivantes :

**1. Leadership stratégique du programme**

Analyse en continu le contexte national des droits humains.

Évalue les capacités des acteurs locaux et les priorités nationales et internationales.

Fournit des analyses et recommandations stratégiques au Carter Center.

**2. Conception et mise en œuvre des programmes**

En collaboration avec le/la Directeur(trice) associé(e), dirige la conception des initiatives de la MDH.

Contribue à l’élaboration de nouvelles propositions de projets.

Supervise la mise en œuvre des plans de travail et budgets approuvés.

Dirige et encadre le personnel et les consultants impliqués.

Garantit la mise en œuvre efficace et dans les délais des activités.

Suit les données quantitatives et qualitatives liées aux projets, les met à disposition du/de la Coordinateur(trice) Suivi Evaluation et participe dans les processus de vérification des données menés par le/la Coordinateur(trice) Suivi Évaluation.

**3. Représentation**

Sous l’autorité du SCR, représente l’initiative MDH en RDC.

Maintien des relations stratégiques avec les partenaires, autorités, ONG, bailleurs et autres acteurs clés.

**4. Gestion des ressources humaines**

Supervise le personnel du programme MDH notamment le Chargé(e) du renforcement des capacités organisationnelles, l’Assistant(e) en renforcement des capacités, Chargé(e) genre, Chargé(e) de protection, Chargé(e) web et réseaux sociaux, Chargé(e) de bases de données.

En collaboration avec le/la Responsable de Ressources Humaines, favorise un environnement de travail coopératif.

Élabore des plans de gestion des performances des agents, valide les objectifs et réalise les évaluations périodiques.

Apporte un appui et collabore avec le personnel et les consultants dans l’atteinte des objectifs.

Veille aux besoins du personnel et contribue à leur développement professionnel.

Participe au recrutement du personnel local et expatrié ainsi que des consultants si nécessaire.

**5. Gestion financière**

Assure la conformité des financements HRH aux règles bailleurs et procédures du Centre Carter.

Suit les dépenses et établit des prévisions opérationnelles.

Appuie la direction financière dans la préparation des rapports.

Contribue à l’élaboration et à la révision des budgets\*\*.\*\*

**6. Gestion des sous-subventions**

Veille à l’élaboration de sous-subventions pertinentes visant à renforcer les capacités des partenaires.

Appuie le personnel technique et les partenaires dans la préparation et la mise en œuvre.

Coopère avec l’officier des sous-subventions pour assurer la conformité, la mise en œuvre des activités et le reporting financier. Maintient les dossiers d’archivage conformément aux procédures du Centre.

**7. Gestion opérationnelle**

Développe avec le/la Chef(fe) des opérations et support les plans logistiques et administratifs et supervise leur mise en œuvre.

S’assure du respect des lois congolaises ainsi que des politiques et du code de conduite du Carter Center dans les opérations de la MDH.

Travaille avec les équipes opérationnelles (SCR, RH, opérations).

**8. Communication et rapports**

Assure une communication et coordination efficaces avec le SCR et le siège.

Facilite les échanges entre le bureau pays et les partenaires de la société civile.

Contribue à la rédaction de rapports pour les bailleurs.

Rédige des communiqués de presse et déclarations publiques (avec validation préalable).

Soumet des rapports écrits et oraux hebdomadaires au SCR.

**QUALIFICATIONS MINIMALES**

- Diplôme de maîtrise en droit, sciences politiques ou sciences sociales.
- Au moins sept (7) ans d’expérience professionnelle en gestion de projets, directement pertinente pour la promotion et la protection des droits humains.
- Expérience substantielle préalable en gestion d’équipe et de personnel.
- Expérience démontrée dans la gestion de projets complexes financés par des bailleurs.
- Expérience démontrée de travail direct avec la société civile, y compris l’appui aux approches dirigées localement et le renforcement des capacités.
- Excellente maîtrise du français écrit et parlé.

**QUALIFICATIONS SOUHAITÉES**

- Master en droit, sciences politiques ou sciences sociales.
- Maîtrise de l’anglais.
- Expérience en gestion de sous-subventions et de micro-subventions accordées aux acteurs locaux.
- Expérience substantielle dans un ou plusieurs domaines prioritaires, dans des environnements politiquement sensibles ou en évolution rapide, notamment :
    
    -protection des défenseurs des droits humains ;
    
    -droits des femmes et égalité de genre ;
    
    -renforcement des capacités organisationnelles et institutionnelles de la société civile ;

-droits environnementaux, fonciers ou des peuples autochtones.

- Expérience en analyse contextuelle, plaidoyer et préparation de briefings à l’intention de hauts responsables.

**CONNAISSANCES SPÉCIALISÉES, COMPÉTENCES ET ATTRIBUTS**

- Solide connaissance des institutions, normes et approches de protection des droits humains pertinentes pour la RDC.
- Capacité démontrée à analyser les évolutions politiques, juridiques, sécuritaires et de l’espace civique et à traduire cette analyse en décisions pratiques pour le programme.
- Compétences avancées en gestion de programmes, notamment en planification du travail, budgétisation, prévisions, gestion des risques, suivi, reporting et gestion de plusieurs subventions et partenaires.
- Solides compétences en gestion des subventions et sous-subventions et compréhension des exigences de conformité des bailleurs et de redevabilité des partenaires.
- Capacité démontrée à superviser, encadrer, motiver et responsabiliser une équipe multidisciplinaire et culturellement diverse.
- Excellentes compétences en analyse, résolution de problèmes, établissement des priorités, organisation et prise de décision.
- Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et orale, notamment la capacité à produire des rapports clairs destinés aux bailleurs, des propositions, des notes analytiques et des mises à jour destinées à la haute direction.
- Solides compétences interpersonnelles, de facilitation, de négociation et de gestion des relations.
- Diplomatie et discernement démontrés dans les interactions avec le gouvernement, la société civile, les bailleurs, les missions diplomatiques et les organisations internationales.
- Capacité à travailler efficacement sous pression, à gérer des échéances concurrentes, à s’adapter à des conditions changeantes et à préserver la confidentialité appropriée.
- Engagement démontré envers l’intégrité, la sauvegarde, l’égalité de genre, les approches dirigées localement, les partenariats respectueux et les principes de ne pas nuire.

jobs.title: Midterm Evaluation of a USDA McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Project in Cameroon
jobs.body:
**Please read the full TOR here (below is only a summary):** [https://nascents.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Nascent-Solutions-MGD-Cameroon-FY23-ToR-midterm-evaluation-SEPT2026.pdf](https://nascents.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Nascent-Solutions-MGD-Cameroon-FY23-ToR-midterm-evaluation-SEPT2026.pdf)

**Midterm Evaluation of a 5-year USDA McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Project in Cameroon**

**Implementer:** Nascent Solutions Inc. (Nascent)

**Funder:** United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)

**Location:** Adamawa, East, North and North West regions of Cameroon

**Duration:** January-August 2027

**Purpose of this ToR:** To solicit bids for a midterm evaluation for Nascent’s McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Project in Cameroon. This will continue a quasi-experimental evaluation set up at baseline.

**Project Description**
