This is a five-year project funded under USDA’s McGovern-Dole International Food for Education and Child Nutrition Program. Implemented by Nascent, the project is designed to improve the literacy of school-age children through improved literacy instruction, student attentiveness, and student attendance. Secondarily, the project intends to increase the use of positive health and dietary practices. The project runs from 2024-2029.

**Profile of Evaluation Team**

Firms and groups of independent consultants are welcome to apply. Team member skills should be complementary, with one person identified as the Team Lead, who will bear responsibility for all work products. Combined, the team should have the following skills and attributes:

- Demonstrated experience leading complex impact evaluations.
- Demonstrated expertise in study design and sampling.
- Demonstrated experience in the development of quantitative data collection tools and managing field data using SurveyCTO and Tangerine for digital data collection.
- Demonstrated experience in using qualitative methods such as focus group discussions and key informant interviews.
- Demonstrated experience in data management and analysis using statistical software, including analyzing complex (multi-stage cluster samples) surveys.
- Demonstrated experience using propensity score matching and difference-in-differences analysis techniques.
- Demonstrated experience in concise, illuminating report writing, including data visualization.
- Demonstrated experience in training and managing field data collectors and complex logistics.
- Subject matter expertise in literacy and education.
- Subject matter expertise in maternal nutrition, child nutrition, and hygiene.
- Strong teamwork ability across cultures and time zones.
- Demonstrated cultural sensitivity and gender balance to effectively communicate with a variety of stakeholders, ranging from young students to government officials.
- Experience with EGRA.
- Experience with the Stallings teacher observations method.
- Experience with dietary diversity surveys.
- Experience with USDA McGovern-Dole projects.
- Experience in Cameroon.
- High proficiency in written and verbal French.
- High proficiency in written and verbal English.

jobs.title: Portfolio Manager, Inclusive Health Initiative (IHI) – French Speaking
country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
jobs.body:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**  
The Portfolio Manager supports the design and delivery of Inclusive Health Initiative (IHI) programmes that contribute to broader country programme goals. Working closely with country offices, national counterparts, and partners, you will support project design, proposal development, and programme implementation while promoting high-quality programme delivery and strengthening CBM's role as a trusted partner in inclusive health.

**This position is only filled locally in one of CBM permanent established entities.** (ex: Berlin or Bensheim (Germany), UK (Cambridge or remote), the US (remote), Nairobi (Kenya), Abuja (Nigeria), Lomé (Togo), Yaoundé (Cameroon), Lusaka (Zambia), Addis Abeba (Ethiopia), Guatemala City, Kampala (Uganda), Niamey (Niger), etc.).  
Local contractual conditions of the respective country will apply. An expatriation is not intended

## **You Will:**

- Provide programmatic support in project design, ensuring alignment with the IHI strategy and global best practices in eye health, ear and hearing care, and physical rehabilitation across assigned countries.
- Guide and support IHI project planning processes, ensuring detailed planning documentation for projects in assigned countries.
- Monitor the implementation of IHI plans and projects, actively contribute to evaluations, and ensure lessons learned inform future planning.
- Deliver training to country office programme staff and partner staff on Inclusive Health-related topics, such as inclusion in health projects.
- Proactively contribute to the development of high-quality funding applications for IHI projects.
- Monitor policies, trends, data, and research in eye health, ear and hearing care, and physical rehabilitation to inform programme implementation.
- Foster a culture of learning and adaptive management within the team and across country offices.
- Support country office teams to ensure data quality and promote the use of evidence for adaptive management.
- Work closely with Advocacy and Communications colleagues to translate programme data and learning into messages that influence policy and practice.
- Represent CBM's programmatic learning and quality initiatives to external audiences, including donors, technical working groups, and other development partners, as required.
- Participate in relevant networks.
- Contribute to research and publications to strengthen the evidence base for inclusive health, where appropriate.

## **These are your qualifications**

- An advanced degree in Public Health, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or a related field.
- A minimum of 7 years of experience in international development, including at least 3 years focused on health programmes.
- A strong understanding of trends and policy frameworks in the international health sector, with sound knowledge of project cycle management and logical frameworks.
- Strong analytical skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information into clear, actionable learning.
- Proven experience in proposal writing, developing monitoring and evaluation frameworks and budgets, and designing and delivering training to build the capacity of others.
- Excellent communication, presentation, and writing skills.
- Strong self-management, time management, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with an independent, agile, flexible, proactive, and collaborative working style.
- Fluency in French and English is required, with strong written and verbal communication skills in both languages.
- Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite.
- A demonstrated commitment to disability inclusion and safeguarding principles.
- Identification with the Christian values and mandate of CBM.

## **What we offer**

- A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development
- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
- An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

jobs.title: Chef·fe de délégation – République démocratique du Congo
jobs.body:
L’EPER emploie plus de 1500 personnes à titre permanent. L’EPER est active sur 24 sites en Suisse et dans plus de 35 pays à travers le monde. Elle y mène 290 programmes et projets, pour un montant total de CHF 144 millions. En 2024, le travail de l’EPER a bénéficié à environ 16 millions de personnes.

Le travail de l’organisation est porté par la vision d’un monde juste, dans lequel la paix règne, la dignité de tous les êtres humains est respectée et les moyens de subsistance naturels sont préservés. L’objectif est d’amener une transition aux niveaux social, économique et politique. L’EPER contribue à améliorer les conditions de vie des personnes en Suisse et à l’étranger et revendique leurs droits. À cette fin, elle sensibilise et mobilise.

**Une diversité vécue – L'inclusion nous tient à cœur :**  
Nous accueillons les candidatures sans distinction de sexe, de nationalité, d'origine ethnique, de religion, d'âge ou d'orientation sexuelle.

**HEKS/EPER en RDC**

Confrontée à un conflit persistant dans l'est du pays, en particulier dans le Nord-Kivu, le Sud-Kivu et l'Ituri, la République démocratique du Congo fait face à une crise humanitaire majeure marquée par des déplacements massifs de population, une insécurité alimentaire chronique et des besoins de protection considérables. HEKS/EPER y déploie un programme d'aide humanitaire et de développement en cohérence avec sa stratégie institutionnelle, en s'appuyant sur des partenaires opérationnels et stratégiques locaux et internationaux, afin d'apporter une réponse pertinente et un impact substantiel aux populations affectées, notamment dans les zones difficiles d'accès et sous-desservies.

HEKS/EPER recherche un·e Directeur pays pour la RDC afin de diriger son programme à un moment déterminant de la réponse humanitaire dans l'Est de la RDC.

Basé·e au Nord-Kivu, le/la Directeur pays assurera la direction stratégique et opérationnelle du programme, tout en jouant un rôle central dans la mobilisation de ressources, les relations avec les bailleurs et la représentation de HEKS/EPER dans le pays.

**Lieu d'affectation :** Nord-Kivu, RDC

**Déplacements :** Réguliers sur les sites du programme (Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu et Ituri), ainsi qu'à Kinshasa

**Contrat :** Temps plein, durée d'un an, renouvelable

**Prise de fonction :** 1er janvier 2026 ou à convenir

## **Chef·fe de délégation – République démocratique du Congo**

### **Votre rôle**

Vous serez chargé·e de :

- Assurer la direction stratégique et opérationnelle du programme de HEKS/EPER en RDC, avec une attention particulière aux zones difficiles d'accès et sous-desservies, en cohérence avec la stratégie et les standards de l'organisation.
- Développer et positionner des programmes pluriannuels de stabilisation et de consolidation de la paix, incluant notamment la réhabilitation d'infrastructures routières, le développement d'infrastructures hydroélectriques et l'appui à des chaînes de valeur agricoles, en coordination avec les équipes de coopération au développement de HEKS/EPER.
- Développer et gérer un portefeuille de projets cohérent, incluant la sélection des partenaires stratégiques et opérationnels.
- Assumer la responsabilité finale des finances du bureau pays et des projets, en assurant un suivi budgétaire rigoureux.
- Mobiliser les fonds nécessaires au programme en développant et en mettant en œuvre une stratégie nationale d'acquisition.
- Développer des propositions de qualité pour les bailleurs bilatéraux et multilatéraux ainsi que les fondations.
- Entretenir des relations solides avec les bailleurs institutionnels, les agences des Nations Unies et les partenaires bilatéraux et multilatéraux.
- Représenter HEKS/EPER auprès des autorités, des bailleurs, des agences onusiennes, des structures de coordination, des ONG internationales et nationales.
- Diriger, encadrer et développer les capacités de l'équipe pays, et assurer la gestion de la sécurité du personnel, des opérations et des biens.
- Garantir un programme pays de haute qualité, pertinent et financièrement soutenable.
- Assurer une coopération étroite et continue avec le siège de HEKS/EPER.

### **Ce que nous recherchons**

Vous êtes un·e professionnel·le expérimenté·e de l'humanitaire ou de la coopération internationale avec :

- Un diplôme universitaire de niveau Master, ou une expérience équivalente.
- Au minimum 5 ans d'expérience à un poste de direction dans la conception, la gestion et la mise en œuvre de projets de dans le secteur de l’aide internationale, notamment dans les zones difficiles d’accès.
- Une expérience avérée dans l'acquisition et la mise en œuvre réussies de projets financés à l'international (en consortium, via des partenaires ou en mise en œuvre directe).
- Une connaissance approfondie de l'aide humanitaire internationale et du contexte régional en RDC.
- Une expérience de travail avec les principaux bailleurs humanitaires, notamment US, ECHO, la DDC et les Nations Unies.
- Une expertise solide en gestion financière, en développement stratégique et en gestion de la sécurité.
- De solides compétences en leadership d'équipe, communication, représentation et réseautage.
- Une expérience de travail dans des contextes fragiles ou à haut risque, avec une disponibilité pour des déplacements réguliers dans les trois provinces d'intervention.

**Langues**

- La maîtrise du français est obligatoire.
- Une bonne maîtrise de l'anglais est également requise.

jobs.title: Chargé(e) d’Administration et Finances
jobs.body:
## Contexte

Interpeace est une organisation intemationale de consolidation de la paix qui soutient des initiatives de consolidation de la paix menées localement dans le monde entier. Interpeace adapte son approche à chaque société et veille à ce que son action soit menée localement. En étroite collaboration avec ses equipes et partenaires locaux, Interpeace développe des programmes de consolidation de la paix et soutient la mise en place de processus de changement qui relient les communautés locales, la société civile, le gouvernement et la communauté intemationale.

En sa qualite de partenaire strategique des Nations Unies, Interpeace a son siege a Geneve, en Suisse, et possede des bureaux dans le monde entier.  
Pour plus d'informations sur Interpeace, veuillez visiter [www.interpeace.org](http://www.interpeace.org)

## Objet et aperçu général

Sous la supervision du gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, le/la Chargé(e) de l’Administration et finances aura la responsabilité de veiller à la qualité des données financières des partenaires œuvrant dans la zone qui lui sera assignée. Il/Elle appuiera en outre dans la gestion administrative de sa zone et contribuera dans la gestion budgétaire de l’organisation en veillant sur les affectations budgétaires ainsi que les suivis budgétaires des partenaires.  
Il/Elle aura des rôles à jouer dans le secteur de la comptabilité, l’administration, les contrôles internes, les audits, l’appui à la gestion budgétaire et dans le renforcement des capacités des partenaires. Mais aussi dans le suivi et le soutien de la mise en œuvre du programme en veillant au respect des politiques internes, des réglementations des bailleurs de fonds et de la législation locale en RD Congo.

## Position au sein de l’organisation

Le/La chargé(e) d’Administration et finances est membre de la section financière de l'unité de soutien global, qui apportera un appui opérationnel dans le domaine d'administration, de finances et appui à l’audit. L'unité de soutien administratif mondial est dirigée depuis le bureau du siège à Genève, bien que les membres de l'équipe soient basés dans différents pays.  
Sous la supervision régulière du gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, le /la chargé (e) d’administration et des finances travaille en étroite collaboration avec les autres membres de l’équipe opérationnelle, notamment le personnel administratif, les ressources humaines, le personnel du programme et le personnel des partenaires afin de créer une fonction financière et administrative plus efficace et efficiente pour un Interpeace agile, réactif et performant.

Taches Spécifiques

Sous orientations et en collaboration avec le gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, ce poste aura comme objectifs principaux :

- Garantir l'exactitude de toutes les informations et de tous les documents comptables enregistrés dans le logiciel de comptabilité Quick Books pour les partenaires de mise en œuvre et Sun Systems pour Interpeace, tout en tenant compte du respect strict des procédures internes.
- Centraliser toutes les importations comptables de sa zone, pour ce qui est des partenaires et bureaux Interpeace sur une base mensuelle et dans les délais impartis.
- Réconcilier tous les paiements effectués par Mobile Money sur une base mensuelle.
- Apporter un appui au Gestionnaire Principal des Finances et Administration dans la réalisation des audits de projets et des audits statutaires de consolidation dans les délais impartis.
- Apporter un appui dans le suivi budgétaire des partenaires de sa zone : produire et partager le BvA avec une analyse détaillée après concertation et validation du gestionnaire principale de l’administration et finances.
- Fournir sur une base mensuelle, en temps opportun, des dossiers financiers révisés précis et complets et des documents justificatifs pour les partenaires et/ou le bureau assigné par le biais de l'outil en ligne pour la consolidation.
- Suivre avec les financiers des partenaires et/ou du bureau la mise en œuvre des recommandations de contrôle interne jusqu'à leur résolution (contrôles mensuels, audits internes et externes, revues internes, etc.)
- Avec les conseils du gestionnaire principal des finances et de l'administration, soutenir la performance d'Interpeace en examinant les politiques et les procédures, en offrant une formation au personnel et/ou aux partenaires, en surveillant les finances ou en évaluant les risques au sein des partenaires et/ou des bureaux assignés.
- Appui administratif dans sa zone en assurant les contacts avec les différents services étatiques ainsi que les partenaires externes conformément au besoin qui se présente.  
    Garantir l’exécution des opérations d’approvisionnement conformément à la procédure en vigueur.

### Compétences techniques requises :

- Maîtrise des outils comptables et de gestion financière (ex. : QuickBooks,, Sun System).
- Connaissance approfondie des normes comptables.
- Excellente maîtrise d’Excel et des outils bureautiques (Word, PowerPoint).
- Capacité à établir des rapports financiers clairs et fiables.
- Bonne compréhension des processus administratifs et financiers des ONG Internationales.

### Qualités personnelles :

- Rigueur, sens de l’organisation et discrétion.
- Esprit d’analyse et capacité à résoudre les problèmes de manière proactive.
- Bonne relationnel et aptitude à travailler en équipe.
- Capacité à gérer le stress et les priorités.
- Intégrité et sens de l’éthique professionnelle.

### Expériences souhaitées :

- Minimum 3 à 5 ans d’expérience dans un poste similaire, idéalement dans une ONG.
- Expérience en gestion opérationnelle des partenaires de mise en œuvre et des projets.
- Une expérience dans la gestion de fonds de bailleurs internationaux constitue un plus.

### Formation :

- Titulaire d’un Bac +5 en gestion financière, finance d’entreprise ou dans un domaine pertinent en lien avec les missions du poste, ou justifiant d’une expérience professionnelle significative dans le domaine.

*Interpeace attache de I 'importance à la diversite de son personnel et vise à atteindre une plus grande parite hommes-femmes à taus les niveaux de son travail.*

## Compétences d'Interpeace

- Collaboration
- Communication
- Recherche de résultats
- Adaptabilité et apprentissage continu
- Respect de la diversité

Facteurs de réussite :

- Excellentes compétences sociales et interculturelles, compétences de communication exceptionnelles pour une variété de parties prenantes de différents horizons ;
- Approche flexible pour travailler dans un contexte en évolution et capacité à livrer sous pression et dans des délais serrés ;
- Compétences exceptionnelles de développement des réseaux relationnels et de mise en confiance
- Créatif avec un engagement en faveur de l'inclusion et développement de consensus;
- Compétences exceptionnelles dans la coordination de processus complexes et sensibles et la conception de processus participatifs ;
- Être de bonne intégrité et forte sensibilité aux différences de culture, de genre, de religion, de sexualité, de nationalité et d’âge.
- Personnalité équilibrée et calme avec tact

### Désire

- Forte attention aux détails et une capacité à travailler de manière autonome et sous pression ;
- Esprit ouvert, créatif, flexible et orienté vers la recherche de solutions lorsqu’un problème se pose ;
- Bonne intégrité et forte sensibilité aux différences de culture, de genre, de religion, de race, de nationalité et d’âge ;
- Facteur de succès
- Identifie et adhère aux valeurs fondamentales et aux principes de travail d’Interpeace
- Engagement pour l’inclusion ;
- Un penseur novateur et critique doté de vastes compétences en résolution de problèmes

*Interpeace attache de l’importance à la diversité de son personnel et vise à atteindre une plus grande parité hommes-femmes à tous les niveaux de son travail.*

jobs.title: Strategic Planning and Projects Management Coordinator – (f/m/x) – MSF Belgium
jobs.body:
**CONTEXT**

A qualitative, lean, professional, and cost-effective supply chain is essential to enable MSF activities and ensure that critical resources are delivered efficiently and effectively to those in need, regardless of context or operational complexity.

OCB Supply Chain comprises several sites and segments, in the countries where we operate (including projects and capital), in regional hubs (for instance in Kenya and South Africa), in Europe with a global range (MSF Supply in Belgium). The Supply Chain Department defines the global strategy of this supply chain, pilots its performance, and ensures that each site has the relevant support for its development.

Supply Chain is a network of people, organizations, resources, processes, activities, and tools working together so that supply meets demand.

The technical domains to design and run a Supply Chain include procurement, warehousing, transport, customs, demand planning & inventory management, supply information systems, supply processes synchronization and user service management.

As a **Strategic Planning and Projects Management Coordinator**, you lead the strategic planning and project management office (PMO) function for the Supply Chain department of the **Operational Centre Brussels** and the joint Supply ecosystem with **Ubuntu Operational Directorate.** You support the Supply Chain Management Team in ensuring that priorities in countries of operation, departmental ambitions, and strategic initiatives across the MSF movement are aligned and fully operational.

You steer the Supply Chain department's strategic planning and budgeting cycles, helping transform the strategic ambitions of the Operational Centre Brussels, Ubuntu Operational Directorate and the wider MSF movement (including SPARC and Supply Chain Transformation initiatives) into measurable roadmaps. In doing so, you ensure coherence, impact, and long-term sustainability across Supply Chain activities and may contribute to the formalization of inter-operational directorate partnerships.

Occasionally, you provide strategic planning and PMO support to other MSF units, including departments within Operational Centre Brussels, the General Direction and the International Office.

You will report to the Supply Chain Director. You will have no team to directly manage.

**MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Planning and Strategic Cycles**

- Lead the Supply Chain contribution to MSF's strategic planning cycles
- Ensure that strategic ambitions from countries of operation, Operational Centre Brussels, Ubuntu Centre, the European Supply Chain Centre and the Supply Chain department are translated into and integrated within Supply Chain roadmaps
- Monitor the implementation of strategic priorities and ensure alignment between departmental objectives and organizational ambitions

**Project Management Office**

- Lead the Supply Chain Project Management Office (PMO) and set project/scrum management standards across the department
- Monitor initiative prioritization, interdependencies, risks and resource allocation to ensure timely delivery of value
- Coach and support Supply Chain staff involved in project delivery, using both agile and waterfall methodologies
- Promote effective change management practices across projects and initiatives
- Lead the Supply Chain budgeting and prioritization process at headquarters
- Capture priorities from countries of operation and ensure alignment with departmental ambitions
- Provide the Supply Chain Management Team with the information required to assess priorities and arbitrate trade-offs where necessary

**Data-Driven Strategy and Decision Support**

- Develop and maintain portfolio performance and strategy analytics
- Provide timely and reliable qualitative and quantitative insights to support governance and decision-making bodies, including to the Supply Chain Management Team
- Identify trends, risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to support strategic objectives

**Inter-Operational Center Collaboration and Representation**

- Act as the focal point for Supply Chain participation in selected inter-operational directorate initiatives.
- Contribute to the negotiation and formalization of collaborative agreements and partnerships, such as the Ubuntu Common Supply Chain Ecosystem
- Represent Supply Chain interests in selected cross-organizational strategic discussions and working groups.

**Strategic Framework for Countries of Operation**

- Oversee the development and maintenance of a framework for multi-year strategic planning in countries of operation
- Ensure strategic coherence across countries of operation and facilitate the integration of operational priorities into departmental planning cycles

**Organisational Transformation and Change Adoption**

- Support the implementation of change management strategies within the Supply Chain department and countries of operation
- Facilitate the adoption of new ways of working, processes and organizational changes
- Contribute to transformation initiatives that strengthen the effectiveness and sustainability of Supply Chain operations

**REQUIREMENTS**

**Education & Experience**

- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in program/portfolio management, ideally using waterfall and agile methodologies and within an international environment
- An advanced certification in program, portfolio or project management is a strong asset
- Proven experience in change management is a strong asset. Relevant certification is an asset
- Experience in humanitarian settings is a strong asset
- Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Strategy, or a related field is an asset
- Experience in developing and implementing complex supply chain strategies is an asset

**Competencies**

- Strong analytical and strategic skills
- Ability to apply systems thinking and data-driven decision-making
- Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills
- Organizational change leadership capabilities
- Proven ability to influence and drive change in complex environments
- Strong facilitation skills
- Cross cultural awareness and ability to work in multicultural environments

**Languages**

- Proficiency in English, written and spoken, is mandatory
- French is a strong asset, other languages (Arabic, Spanish, Portuguese) are an asset

**CONDITIONS**

- Expected starting date: asap
- Location: Brussels, Belgium
- Contract type: Open-ended contract, full-time
- Salary according to MSF-OCB grid
- Homeworking is possible as per MSF policy
- Meal Vouchers – Hospital Insurance (DKV) – Pension Plan – 100% reimbursement for public transportation costs
- *Adhere to the MSF principles and to our managerial values: Respect, Transparency, Integrity, Accountability, Trust and Empowerment*
- *Adhere to the MSF Behavioral Commitments*

**Deadline for applications: 22 October 2026**

jobs.title: General Director f/m/x
jobs.body:
**Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international humanitarian aid organization that provides assistance in more than 70 countries to populations in distress, to victims of natural or manmade disasters and to victims of armed conflicts, without discrimination and irrespective of origin, religion, creed or political affiliation.** **Our actions are guided by medical ethics and the principle of impartiality, independence and neutrality.**

## **CONTEXT**

MSF Luxembourg celebrates its 40th anniversary in 2026. Throughout this time, we have maintained a fierce determination to act, providing care to those in need and bearing witness when the world looks the other way.  
From its first mission in Ethiopia in 1986, to becoming a fully operational cell of Operational Center Brussels (OCB), pioneering operational research, participating in movement-wide strategic platforms, and contributing to OCB and a new Operational Directorate with AKWABA, the Luxembourg section has demonstrated versatility, innovation, and unwavering commitment to the mission of Médecins Sans Frontières.

With 35 staff members, the section’s team works to raise awareness on humanitarian issues among Luxembourg’s population, raise funds needed to finance humanitarian interventions, hire and support MSF Mobile Staff deployed internationally and carry out, with the LuxOR unit, epidemiological support and operational research projects directly linked to health programs, helping to improve their efficiency and effectiveness.

## **ROLE PURPOSE**

As General Director, you will lead MSF Luxembourg in delivering its strategic ambitions while ensuring alignment with Médecins Sans Frontières' principles, values and international frameworks. Reporting to the Board, you will provide overall leadership of the section, represent MSF externally and within the international movement, and ensure the sustainable development of MSF Luxembourg's activities, teams and resources.

## **KEY RESPONSABILITIES**

### **Strategic Leadership and Governance**

- Guide and lead new collaboration with partners in the MSF movement, in the light of the MSF movement evolution, and the strategic vision of MSF Luxembourg section.
- Lead the implementation of MSF Luxembourg's strategic vision and organisational objectives.
- Ensure alignment of the organisation's activities with MSF's values, charter, international frameworks and governance requirements.
- Advise and collaborate closely with the Board and the Management Team. This includes regular reporting to the Board during board meetings and/or under specific requests.
- Monitor organisational performance, risks, compliance and accountability.

### **Organisational Leadership and People Management**

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the Management Team (LuxOR, Foundation, Communication & Fundraising, Public Engagement, Human Resources, Finance and IT), ensuring alignment with MSF Luxembourg's strategic objectives and organisational priorities.
- Foster a collaborative, high-performing inclusive and accountable organisational culture that promotes staff engagement, wellbeing, development and safeguarding.
- Ensure the organisation has the people, systems, resources and financial capacity required to deliver its strategic ambitions sustainably, through effective planning, resource allocation, budget oversight and financial stewardship.
- Drive organisational development, change management and continuous improvement.
- Ensure compliance with Luxembourg legal requirements (Association statute, financial audit &reporting, …)

### **Representation, Advocacy and Partnerships**

- Serve as the primary representative and spokesperson of MSF Luxembourg.
- Build and strengthen collaborative relationships with other MSF sections, further consolidate MSF Luxembourg's partnership with the Operational Centre Brussels (OCB) and actively contribute to the development of the AKWABA Operational Directorate while ensuring that MSF Luxembourg maintains its distinct identity, added value and recognition within the movement.
- Contribute actively to international MSF platforms, governance bodies and collaborative initiatives.
- Build and maintain strategic relationships with government authorities, media, private donors, academia, humanitarian organisations, civil society and Association members.
- Promote and advocate for MSF's humanitarian principles, medical action and positions on key humanitarian issues.

## **PROFILE REQUIRED**

We are looking for an inspiring leader with a strong commitment to humanitarian action and a proven ability to lead complex organisations and diverse stakeholders.

### **Essential**

- Strong commitment to MSF's principles, values and humanitarian mission.
- Significant senior leadership and management experience, ideally 10+ years.
- Experience within MSF (Intl - HQ experience) and/or humanitarian or non-profit sector.
- Understanding of MSF medical operations and humanitarian challenges.
- Demonstrated ability to develop and implement strategy.
- Structured and results-oriented professional with excellent organisational skills and a strong ability to translate strategy into measurable objectives, track performance through relevant indicators, and ensure high-quality reporting and accountability.
- Strong people leadership skills with experience managing senior teams and driving organisational change.
- Excellent stakeholder management, networking and partnership-building abilities.
- Strong analytical, political and negotiation skills.
- Proven financial and organisational management capabilities.
- Excellent communication, representation and public speaking skills.
- Ability to work effectively in a complex international and multicultural environment.
- Fluency in English and French; Luxembourgish and/or German are considered assets.
- Availability for frequent travel, when necessary.

### **Desirable**

- Good understanding of the Luxembourg context and institutional environment.
- Strong knowledge of international humanitarian issues and the MSF movement.
- Experience in advocacy and engagement with high-level stakeholders.

## **CONDITIONS**

- Full-time contract, based in Luxembourg with frequent travels abroad
- Mandate of 4 years (extendable for max. 2 more years)
- Gross salary over 12 months from 75600 to 90600 € according to MSF experience
- 29 days annual paid leaves
- Possibility of teleworking 2 days per week
- Medical complementary insurance (including hospitalization)
- 18 Lunch vouchers each with a face value of 10,80 € (2/3 covered by MSF).
- Public transport allowance & relocation package (if applicable)
- **Expected starting date: January 2027** **(preferred)**

jobs.title: Senior Research Monitoring Evaluation and Learning Officer
jobs.body:
**Role Summary**

Siren Associates is seeking a Senior RMEL (Research, Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning) Officer to coordinate the design and implementation of ANCHOR’s RMEL system, ensuring rigorous data collection, analysis, and reporting across all components. Based in Amman and reporting to the Project Manager while working closely with Siren’s HQ RMEL Lead, the Senior RMEL Officer will lead perception surveys (baseline, midline and endline), and drive learning processes to inform adaptive management and donor reporting. This role combines technical expertise in quantitative and qualitative methods with strong field engagement and coordination skills.

*Want to learn more about us? Check our digital brochure:* [*https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure*](https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure)

This position is ***subject to funding availability***. Recruitment, onboarding, and contract issuance will proceed once final donor approvals and funding confirmations are secured.

**Key Responsibilities**

**RMEL System Desing & Implementation**

- Develop a comprehensive RMEL plan to translate the project’s logical framework into actionable tools, processes, and timelines.
- Define data collection methods and frequency of monitoring activities to ensure alignment with donor requirements.
- Set up digital data collection and management systems (e.g., Kobo or similar platforms) to ensure accurate and efficient data gathering and analysis.
- Establish protocols for data quality assurance, verification, and secure storage.
- Work with the project team to embed RMEL requirements into activity planning and implementation.

**Monitoring and Data Collection**

- Oversee routine monitoring across project components, ensuring timely and reliable collection of quantitative and qualitative data.
- Design and manage perception surveys (baseline, midline, and endline), including sampling strategies, tool development, and analysis.
- Recruit, train, and supervise external enumerators to conduct surveys and other data collection exercises, ensuring adherence to ethical and methodological standards.
- Coordinate with project officers to support continuous data collection and provide technical guidance on RMEL tools and practices.

**Evaluation and Learning**

- Support the commissioning and implementation of the external final project evaluation, ensuring access to relevant data and documentation.
- Analyse and interpret monitoring and survey data to produce high-quality outputs, including perception survey reports, quarterly RMEL updates, and donor reports.
- Lead internal reviews to assess progress, identify trends, and extract lessons learned for adaptive management.
- Provide evidence-based recommendations to the Project Manager and HQ RMEL Lead to guide strategic decision-making.
- Support the preparation of clear, data-driven presentations and briefs for internal and external stakeholders.

**Requirements**

**Essential**

- Minimum 5 years of professional experience in RMEL, including design and implementation of monitoring frameworks and field data collection.
- Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., statistics, social sciences, economics, development studies, or related discipline).
- Proven experience with both quantitative and qualitative research methods, survey design, and data analysis.
- Knowledge of RMEL tools and platforms (e.g., Kobo Toolbox).
- Strong analytical, writing, and presentation skills.
- Fluency in English (spoken and written).
- Excellent coordination and organizational skills, with the ability to manage external enumerators and multiple data streams.
- Based in Amman with regular travel to project sites across Jordan.

**Desirable**

- Master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., statistics, social sciences, economics, development studies, or related discipline).
- Fluency in Arabic.
- Familiarity with security sector reform, health interventions and/or development partnerships with police and government agencies.
- Familiarity with civil society grant mechanisms.
- Familiarity with agile project management approaches and/or technology-enabled interventions.

***Competitive Employment Conditions***

jobs.title: Country Director - JRS Thailand
jobs.body:
**Position Title: Country Director, JRS Thailand**  
**Location: Bangkok, Thailand with possibility to move Chiang Mai**  
**Reports to: Regional Director, JRS Asia Pacific**  
**Starting date: January 2027**  
**Type of Employment: Localised position open for all nationalities**  
**Local salary package, individual medical insurance, and visa support.**

(Note on family status: This is typically structured as an individual/non-family posting given the inclusion of "individual insurance" and local contract terms, but we need to explicitly add "Non-family posting" or "Family posting" at the top of the ad for absolute clarity.)

**Contract duration: 2 years (possibility of renewal)**  
**Starting Salary: THB88,495-THB102,141 (depending qualification)**

Jesuit Refugee Service (JRS) is an international Catholic organization, with a mission to accompany, serve, and advocate for refugees. Our advocacy flows from a service that is direct, pastoral, human and exposed to the sufferings and limitations of refugee life. Through our presence we help to sustain the goodness and hope in people who live in situations of evil and who have reason to despair. To support such an approach, JRS welcomes people who are able to contribute to and draw from the mission of JRS and the desire to share in the lives of the people we serve.

In Thailand, JRS serves refugees, asylum seekers and other forcibly displaced persons in urban Bangkok Metropolitan Area (BMA) and in two camps in Mae Hong Son. The field offices are located in Bangkok and Mae Hong Son, while the country office in Bangkok with a possibility to move to Chiang Mai. The main areas of work include education, psychosocial services, livelihoods, and advocacy.

**Overall Position Purpose:**

As the leader of JRS operations in Thailand, the Country Director oversees the overall management and success of country programmes, personnel, and offices to fulfill the JRS mission and humanitarian sector standards. Reporting directly to the Regional Director, the role provides strategic management support to project directors and teams while driving country-level operations. Key responsibilities include exploring emerging needs of refugees as well as emerging opportunities, developing and implementing project proposals as participatory as possible, overseeing country finances, evaluating projects, managing staff recruitment and care, managing partnerships especially critical for JRS Thailand’s work in Thailand, and maintaining vital external relations with the local Church, the Society of Jesus, government authorities, and international organizations.

**Responsibilities**

**Provision of Strategic Direction**

- Safeguard and promote the mission, vision, identity, values, and unity of JRS across all programmes in Thailand.
- Monitor political, social, economic, and migration trends to formulate proposals for new initiatives, project designs, and advocacies responding to the greatest needs of refugees and displaced persons.
- Lead the development and implementation of country strategic plans that is translated into annual programming, financial budgets, and in-country policies with participation and consultation of the staff.
- Facilitate critical reflection, monitoring, and evaluation of JRS projects to continuously improve program quality and services.
- Provide direction and guidance for JRS Thailand advocacy in country, in collaboration with JRS Asia Pacific and Global Offices.
- Identify capacity development/strengthening needed by the staff to do their roles
- Act as the gatekeeper of the JRS communication strategy and products to ensure. risk management, submitting required reports to Regional Director.

**People Management & Care**

- Review HR needs against available resources to ensure effective and efficient service delivery.
- Provide leadership, inspiration, and holistic care for staff well-being, fostering a supportive, multicultural, and professional working environment.
- Guide and support field teams through regular visits and listening sessions to maintain high standards of quality and accountability.
- Oversee staff recruitment, contracts, appraisals, and terminations in collaboration with HR and Project Directors.
- Lead regular reviews and updates of JRS Thailand’s Personnel, Travel, and Child Protection and Safeguarding policies.

**Programming**

- Guide the programming strategy to adapt to dynamic contexts for urban and in-camp refugees, as well as other emerging displacement issues aligned with the JRS mission.
- Collaborate with the Country Programme Officer, Project Directors, and Finance Manager to design proposals addressing the evolving needs of displaced populations.
- Ensure all projects comply with donor partnership agreements and humanitarian sector standards.
- Oversee timely and accurate reporting on project progress, challenges, and field updates through six-month and annual reports.
- Maintain regular communication with field teams to share critical updates regarding government policies, refugee situations, and organizational developments.
- Oversee database development and management to ensure data used for program development and reporting is accurate, while maintaining strict protection for sensitive information.

**Operations (Finance, Administration & Procurement)**

- Ensure financial administration and procurement strictly adhere to JRS policies to maintain full accountability.
- Lead the annual country planning and budgeting process collaboratively alongside the Finance Manager, Project Directors, and key staff.
- Oversee annual project and institutional audits, implementing corrective actions based on auditor recommendations in consultation with the Finance Manager and relevant team members.
- Monitor project budgets and financial reports, actively overseeing funding status and managing re-budgeting processes as needed.

**Partnership Management & Representation**

- Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with the local Jesuit Provincial, diocesan Church, local Jesuit communities, government authorities, key NGOs, and UNHCR.
- Sustain existing partnerships and forge new ones to ensure JRS Thailand's mission remains context-driven and responsive to the evolving needs of the communities we serve.
- Works closely with CCSDPT representatives and other NGOs in Thailand, UNHCR and the Royal Thai government at national level. JRS together with other organizations and networks also advocate changes to government policy/practice as needed for the benefit of the refugees.
- Represent JRS at national-level meetings with NGOs, UNHCR, government bodies, and stakeholder forums.
- Ensure prominent representation in donor forums while strictly complying with Thai government and donor requirements.

**Qualifications & Experience:**

- Education: Degree in Development Studies, Social Work, International Development, or a related field.
- Experience: Minimum of five years in a senior management role, overseeing complex programs, diverse multi-cultural teams, and strategic partnerships (experience in Asia is an advantage).
- Financial & Technical Skills: Strong background in project cycle management, budgeting, financial monitoring, and accounting, alongside high computer literacy (Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
- Communication: Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with a proven track record in report writing and proposal development (knowledge of Thai is an advantage).
- Values & Mindset: Deep empathy for refugees, a strong grasp of local cultural sensitivities, and a service-minded, patient, and self-motivated approach.
- Personal Attributes: Exceptional diplomatic, leadership, and stress-management skills, with the ability to thrive under pressure in a multicultural, multi-faith, and resource-constrained environment.

jobs.title: Director of Program Development, Quality & Learning (PQL) - Port au Prince, Haiti
jobs.body:
**Location:** Port-au-Prince, Haiti

**Position Status:** Full-time, Regular

**Language:** Required language fluency in French

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) X **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.

Now, and for the future.

## **Program/Department Summary**

Mercy Corps helps communities develop their own ideas to solve Haiti’s most daunting problems by using innovative approaches to bring Haitians new social and economic opportunities and to make their country more secure, productive and just. Established in January 2010, Mercy Corps Haiti has offices in Port-au-Prince, Jeremie, and Miragoane and more than 80 staff implementing programs in WASH, financial inclusion, economic development, agriculture, natural resource management and humanitarian response. Mercy Corps’ economic development work is guided by the principles of pro-poor development and demand driven strategies. Mercy Corps takes a progressive approach to development that leads communities and entrepreneurs from relief to sustainable livelihoods to resilience.

Mercy Corps Haiti is going through a transformational change at this moment. As a catalytic organization, our future impact will increasingly focus on **sustainability and transformative change,** supporting lasting improvements in the lives of the communities we serve. This ambition will be supported through several key drivers, including: evidence-based programming, learning generation to influence systems change, scaling impact through Mercy Corps and strategic partners, stronger knowledge management and impact measurement, expanded partnerships and alliances, greater commitment to gender equity and diversity and strategic advocacy and fundraising.

## **General Position Summary**

As a member of the Senior Management Team (SMT) in Haiti, the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning (PQL) is responsible for driving cross-functional engagement in the development and delivery of Country Program Strategy, developing annual plans and reporting on results. S/he is responsible for ensuring development and delivery of high quality, evidence-based, innovative programs that contribute to Mercy Corps Global Strategy and Mercy Corps Haiti new strategic vision. The Director of PQL ensures that a robust monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) system is in place, that the country office engages in the collection and use of evidence and that this is shared across the global organization, and that reliable data is used for decision-making. One key aspect of the role is ensuring capability building, mentoring and coaching of the Program/Project Managers in order to support program quality in line with global standards and key performance indicators. As a senior leader in the country office s/he plays a representational role with the government, donors, partners, peer agencies, and others. The Director of PQL supports strategic positioning with donors and partners and leads on project design to ensure that the country office strategy can be delivered in line with Mercy Corps vision.

As one of the most senior staff in the Country Office, the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning must demonstrate the qualities of agile leadership. This role plays a key role in defining and pursuing the strategic direction for Mercy Corps programs in Haiti, ensuring the relevance, coherence, safety and impact of our programs. It is essential that the Director of Program Development, Quality and Learning builds and maintains strong relationships across functions within the Country Program.

## **Essential Job Responsibilities**

**STRATEGY & VISION, PLANNING & REPORTING**

- Lead the development/updating of the analysis of the country context ensuring community, partners and other stakeholders’ participation as necessary.
- Lead the SLT to develop/update and drive forward the Country Program Strategy that is in line with the global strategy.
- Provide leadership on development of the Country Annual Implementation Plan, monitoring of progress against the plan, and completion of accurate, on-time Country Annual Report of outcomes and impact, aligned with the Global Results Framework.
- Facilitate the development and pursuit of thematic and cross-cutting strategic priorities in line with the Country Program Strategy, including gender equality, to guide current and future Mercy Corps programming and Humanitarian Principles.
- Support ownership and commitment to the Country Program Strategy by all staff and departments through clear communication, regular feedback on progress and engagement of all functions in updates.
- Participate in global discussions and working groups to represent country programs, in learning for a, in strategy design and policy development.
- Support change processes and roll out new ways of working to improve achievement of the Country Program Strategy.
- Drive Innovation and thought leadership at all levels in the CO (strategy, programme, project and individual levels).

**PROGRAM DESIGN & DEVELOPMENT**

- Lead strategic resource (financial, materials & human) mobilization drive and ensure the Country Program is always resourced to drive programme design and development.
- Work with CD and SMT to set funding targets and drive implementation at all levels ensuring the entire Country Program is committed to and aware of these contributions to these targets.
- In consultation with the Country Director and Members, ensure technical engagement with donors to pre-position and prepare for opportunities, and engage in strategic positioning work directly as appropriate.
- Lead the identification of new initiatives and opportunities that respond to identified needs and the country strategy, in coordination with the Country Director and Program Managers, as well as the Regional Program Director, headquarters-based Senior Program Officer, Technical Advisors and other relevant staff.
- Play a leading role in designing innovative projects/proposals, including:
    - Engaging with technical experts as needed to ensure high quality, evidence-based designs that draw on needs assessments, learning from past programs and program standards principles.
    - Ensuring partners are identified and appropriately engaged in program design, linking with Operations as need be for assessments, especially to strengthen gender sensitivity at design stage.
    - Ensuring proposal designs and their budgets include robust MEAL plans that are aligned with the Global Results Framework and build in critical learning questions.
    - Ensuring the project budget will enable the project to be delivered as designed.
    - Incorporating community participation into design, as relevant.

**PROGRAM QUALITY AND PROGRAM TECHNICAL EXCELLENCE**

- Ensure the Country Program delivers high quality, multi-sectoral programming in both development and humanitarian contexts (as appropriate).
- Monitor and advance technical and operational quality of programmes, including conducting regular field visits to provide feedback on quality benchmarks, soliciting inputs for design of new programs and collecting ideas for innovation.
- Monitor program Key Performance Indicators and, in partnership with other functions, take steps to improve the quality programming platform to meet agreed upon standards.
- Work closely with the Director of Operations to ensure procedures are followed throughout the project cycle and across the portfolio.
- Ensure Program/Project Managers proactively and regularly communicate planned requirements for program design, learning and implementation to relevant Country Program departments/functions.
- Oversee program startup and ongoing program management and administration of teams across various field locations.
- Ensure that program implementation is responsive to communities and partners and consistent with Mercy Corps’ relevant program guidelines, principles, values, quality standards and strategic plan.
- Ensure that beneficiaries are effectively targeted according to established and well-defined criteria and processes.
- Develop partners’ MoUs and contracts and ensure that partners are delivering in accordance with the agreements.
- Support the PMs and team in the development and ongoing refinement of implementation strategies.
- Integrate community approaches, gender sensitivity and capacity building into all activities as appropriate.
- Ensure program implementation is on time, target and budget, using effective M&E systems to reach desired impacts (adaptive management).
- Create and maintain systems ensuring effective and transparent use of financial resources for timely and informative reporting in line with donor and Mercy Corps policies and procedures.
- Conduct frequent field visits to all project sites for monitoring, quality control and program staff mentoring and coaching.
- Ensure that community feedback mechanisms are in place, functioning, and clearly communicated to staff and beneficiaries.
- Review all draft reports and ensure that reports are ready for submission to HQ on time.
- Lead and coach the Program/Project Managers to enable them to successfully deliver against the Country Program Strategy.
- Ensure effective working relationships with Mercy Corps global, Member and regional technical advisors, procuring technical support as needed to support program and advocacy efforts, including during Emergencies.
- Ensure that program technical experts engage in larger communities of practice within and external to Mercy Corps, to link with the most relevant and evidence-based approaches and conduct timely and useful review of project reports to support quality reporting for Members and donors.
- Ensure that the different technical sectors of the Country Program are coordinated, integrated and support each other to optimize programs and projects.

**DRIVING EVIDENCE, MEAL AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT**

- Work to develop a monitoring system that provides timely and accurate project results by embedding MEAL across program implementation. This requires ensuring effective collaboration across MEAL staff, Technical Specialists, Technical Advisors and program implementation teams to develop logframes, indicators, implementation plans, quality benchmarks, monitoring and evaluation frameworks and related tools.
- Lead programme quality improvements by monitoring and improving Programme KPI performance, including resourcing and conducting high-quality evaluations to demonstrate outcomes and impact and ensuring that accountability mechanisms are in place for all projects so that identified actions are resolved, with critical issues escalated to senior management.
- Ensure the research, evaluation and policy work of the Country Program contributes to generation of evidence for development and improvement of program quality, sound decision making and policy influencing internally and externally.
- Establish effective program learning and knowledge management systems to support adaptive programming and innovation that improves outcomes for children through service delivery, policy & advocacy and campaigns.

**STAFF MANAGEMENT, MENTORSHIP, AND DEVELOPMENT**

- Ensure appropriate staffing of Program Development and Quality team, and engagement of additional technical support when needed to deliver quality project design and delivery.
- Ensure that staff proactively build and maintain technical, managerial and leadership skills, , providing coaching opportunities when needed.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations and provide constructive feedback via regular performance reviews.
- Supervise, hire and orient new team members as necessary.
- Provide team members with information, tools and other resources to improve performance and reach objectives.
- Contribute to country team-building efforts, help team members identify problem-solving options and ensure the integration of all team members into relevant decision-making processes.
- Be comfortable and able to manage a team remotely and with limited travel based on the security situation.

**FINANCE & COMPLIANCE MANAGEMENT**

- Ensure compliance with donor and Mercy Corps regulations related to programming.
- Review BVAs with Finance and Program managers to identify any issues and undertake any necessary budget revisions.
- Ensure program close-out begins in a timely manner to minimize any significant under or overspends at the end of the grant (i.e. final variance for all grants should be within 5%).

**INFLUENCE, ADVOCACY & REPRESENTATION:**

- Guide functions and thematic tracks to identify advocacy issues and lead them at the national level.
- Ensure Mercy Corps is represented in the relevant networks.
- Develop and / or participate in various networks for opportunities to extend the program and defend interests.
- Ensure Program issues are subject to pressure and advocacy at national and other levels.
- Ensure programming models are demonstrated/documented and scaled up in line with strategic directions.
- Undertake an in-depth analysis of the powers and policies of the country's structures, systems and networks to identify opportunities for changes in law, policy, budget and behavior at the national level that will achieve the goals and objectives strategies set by the national office.
- Lead and manage the design and implementation of the influence strategy in coordination with staff and partners, taking an integrated approach to influence.
- Revise and update the advocacy strategy according to the evolution of the context.
- Ensure strong links with programs and monitoring, evaluation, research and learning (MERL) so that advocacy and policy approaches are evidence-based.
- Monitor and report on progress in influencing and its contribution to change, including to donors where appropriate.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

Project Directors, Program Managers, CARM Manager, MEL Manager, Safeguarding Manager, Program Development & Knowledge Manager and other staff as needed.

## **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Country Director  
**Works Directly With:** All program staff, both national and expatriate in Haiti; HQ-based program, operations, recruiting, human resources, finance, and technical support teams.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- BA/S or equivalent in international studies, social science, management, economics or other relevant fields. MA/S preferred.
- 7+ years of experience with European and US institutional and private donors, including proposal development.
- 5+ years overseas experience, including at least 3 years in a senior management position.
- Experience managing humanitarian relief and/or transitional programs in areas affected by insecurity and natural disasters.
- Previous experience working in Haiti or similar contexts strongly preferred.
- Proven track record in program design, proposal writing and development, and donor reporting.
- Be trained and knowledgeable in design, monitoring, and evaluation concepts and methodologies. M&E experience should include conducting assessments and surveys, program design using a logical framework approach, selecting indicators, implementing monitoring plans, coordinating evaluations and data analysis.
- Experience supervising international and national staff, starting up programs and working in difficult environments.
- Experience managing programs in relevant technical areas including Participatory Community Development, Livelihoods, Agriculture, Water and Sanitation, Economic Recovery, Women’s Empowerment and GBV programming, Peacebuilding, Civil Society Capacity Building and Youth.
- Knowledge of major donor requirements and compliance issues.
- Strong management skills with good understanding of relevant cross-cultural issues.
- Understanding of advocacy, policy, and government systems in the host country.
- Strong skills and proven experience in leading strategic planning, change management and program management processes, also from the knowledge and learning perspective.
- Strong skills and proven experience in new program development, project design and proposal writing with corporate, foundations and/or institutional donors.
- Skills in training, capability building, coaching, mentorship, problem solving, and project cycle management.
- High level of self-awareness and willingness to take feedback for growth and self-development.
- Proven experience as a team player and leader in an international organization.
- Demonstrated attention to detail, ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines and work independently and cooperatively with team members.
- History of working effectively with host country government, national and international NGO partners, and collaborating with other actors, including the private sector.
- Solid knowledge of and experience with security protocols is essential.
- **Fluency in written and oral French and English is required.**

## **Success Factors**

A successful candidate will be conscientious, with excellent judgment and will display an entrepreneurial spirit that is both creative and flexible. S/he will combine strong communication skills, creativity, initiative, participatory leadership and tactful decisiveness to assist in the development and implementation of Mercy Corps’ country strategy. Prioritizing, problem solving and simultaneous attention to detail and strategic vision are essential. The individual will be a strategic thinker able to bring ideas to implementation in growing program operations. They will have exceptional proposal development skills and an outstanding ability to design, implement and manage innovative programs that respond to current needs. An interest and ability to travel and work in remote environments, and awareness of and sensitivity to multi-cultural international development work and ability to train and facilitate dialogue among a diverse group of individuals with various skill sets and working styles is required. An even temperament and a good sense of humor are appreciated. Language proficiency in English/French is a must.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

Haiti is a country of 11 million people and is the poorest country in the Western Hemisphere. The country has been wracked by a series of major natural disasters since 2010 including earthquake, hurricanes, and drought. A new government is in place for the next five years which is anticipated to reduce instability, however occasional violent demonstrations and flare-ups in crime can occur. Haiti suffers from chronic high unemployment, severe environmental degradation, food insecurity, and health issues like cholera exacerbated by low levels of access to water and poor infrastructure. Nonetheless, Haiti also has great beauty including beaches and mountainous national parks. Its international airport provides daily flights to multiple destinations in the US, as well as access to DR, Canada, Paris, Cuba, Panama, Curacao, and other locations in the Caribbean.

The position is based in Port au Prince, which is estimated at around 2.5 million people. Although infrastructure is also poor in the capital, comfortable housing with water and electricity are readily available. There are many places to eat in all price ranges, as well as shops, and supermarkets which are comparable to a US supermarket. Self-drive is permitted, however driving can be challenging, and traffic is often very heavy. Housing is provided for this position.

Mercy Corps Team members represent the agency both during and outside of work hours when deployed in a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and Mercy Corps' policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

## **Team Engagement and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.body:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

The IRC is looking for a Deputy Director, Programs (DDP) for IRC CAR & Cameroon, a newly merged Country Program (CP)With a total operating budget of roughly $12M.

***Cameroon Context:***

The IRC began its operations in Cameroon in 2016 to address violence from Boko Haram in the Far North. By 2018-2019, they expanded into South-West and North-West regions. With offices in Yaoundé, Maroua, and Buea, the IRC focuses on providing access to water, improving hygiene, offering cash assistance, enhancing food security, and delivering education and protection services. Their programs also include child protection and support for victims of gender-based violence and human rights violations.

***CAR Context:***

 The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has been operating in the Central African Republic (CAR) since 2006. With its main office located in Bangui, the IRC CAR conducts activities across four provinces: Haut-Mbomou, Ouham-Pendé, and Bamingui-Bangoran, with sub-offices in Zemio, Ndele, and Bocaranga. The organization provides comprehensive services in several key areas, including health and nutrition, education, food security and economic recovery and development (ERD), as well as protection services encompassing women's protection and empowerment (WPE) and child protection.

***IRC Cameroon-CAR Country Program***

 In the coming months, the team will work on the Strategic Action Plan (SAP) for the IRC Cameroon-CAR country program, identifying synergies for coherent programming in both countries, and exploring opportunities for cross-border response. The IRC SAP aims to provide significant impact for boys, girls, women, and men affected by humanitarian crises. The team adheres to IRC’s core values of Integrity, Accountability, Service, and Equality. Additionally, IRC Cameroon-CAR plans to enhance the quantity and quality of its partnerships with national and local NGOs.

**Job overview**

The DDP provides leadership, decision-making, and oversight of the IRC Cameroon-CAR’s program portfolio, ensuring a strategically coherent program direction and compliance with IRC and donor regulations. The DDP assures strong collaboration and coordination on programmatic issues both internally and externally, including the development of quality proposals and the delivery of high quality and timely programs for our clients. DDP will work closely and collaboratively across departments of the country’s program, region, headquarters, as well as external stakeholders and partners.

The DDP is a senior member of the Cameroon-CAR country program, reporting directly to the Country Director.

For this role, we are seeking a dynamic leader who can drive continued success across our strategy, deliver on priorities, and motivate a diverse and inclusive, partly remote, team with a joined vision and shared goals. You will be skilled in fostering collaboration across departments and across sectors, and empowering staff, particularly female leaders, to succeed.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Program Implementation**

- Oversee and ensure programs are implemented to high-quality standards and on time, including supporting Program Coordinators and Technical Coordinators to use structured and realistic project management tools in coordination with Operations teams, including workplans, procurement plans, and spending plans.
- Closely monitor budgets, spending, and program progress to ensure grants are run within budget and closed on time, assuring consistent Project Cycle Management routines and taking well-structured and timely corrective action as needed.
- Assure clear accountability, roles and responsibilities, and highly effective communication and coordination channels across teams within the Programs Department
- Guide the implementation of the IRC Cameroon-CAR Partnership Strategy and sectoral partnership plans to ensure the IRC is delivering on localization commitments while also maintaining high quality and efficient services for clients.
- Provide the CD with accurate and up-to-date advice on developments and opportunities in program and project implementation, together with any necessary recommendations for action.
- Support the MEAL Coordinator in delivering on the country office MEAL strategy, and assuring use of information collected through MEAL systems and client feedback mechanisms informs all stages of the project cycle.
- Ensure the development of new opportunities related to the IRC Mission Statement and the CP Strategic Action Plan.
- Ensure high-quality, timely reporting for submission to donors, per IRC and donor guidelines.
- Ensure the provision of appropriate technical assistance from IRC’s Technical Units, external consultants, or partner agencies as necessary.

**2. Strategic Planning & Implementation**

- Lead the development, review, and implementation of the Country Strategy Action Plan (SAP), focusing on driving ownership of the strategy by all program departments, delivering against strategic commitments, and implementing the IMPACT quality standards
- Ensure programming is aligned with the IRC Cameroon-CAR SAP priorities and IRC Outcomes and Evidence Framework (OEF), including program planning, project design, and communications with staff.
- In coordination with the CD and other colleagues, annually update country program and sector strategies while remaining relevant to evolving contexts and operational effectiveness.
- Lead the development and roll-out of strategic initiatives such as expanding the IRC’s partnership model to drive the localization agenda, research and innovation, and ensure integration of cross-cutting issues of gender, partnership, climate change and disaster risk reduction in sectoral programming.

**3. Grants, Partnership and Business Development**

- Provide overall guidance and leadership to the IRC Cameroon-CAR Grants and Program Development teams, ensuring sound business development strategy, process, and systems are in place, and adequate financing is secured to deliver the targeted outcomes for clients
- Oversee strong program design and proposal strategy for each new funding opportunity, including need and evidence-based program design, strong technical and operational engagement in design processes, and sound budgeting and competitiveness.
- Ensure program, grants and finance teams produce high-quality financial and narrative donor reports, including assuring program and MEAL teams provide timely and quality contributions addressing all reporting requirements.
- Grow the impact of IRC programming by ensuring excellent and high-quality program delivery, maintaining and strengthening the trust of key donors, partners, collaborators, and proactively positioning the IRC for program development opportunities.
- Spearhead the integration of program design and implementation with robust stakeholder analysis, fostering strategic, long-term partnerships with local civil society, government, and private sector actors to drive locally led decision-making and service delivery. Lead the implementation of IRC’s PEERS framework, ensuring cross-departmental collaboration, effective partnership risk management, and responsive partner feedback systems, while building internal capacity through structured training, staffing, and performance management aligned with partnership principles.
- Lead engagement with consortium partners, including on strategic direction and coordinating program design or delivery;

**4. Human Resources and Staff Development**

- Staffing: In coordination with the Human Resources management team, ensure that the IRC Cameroon & CAR Program\[FS1.1\] team is composed of quality staff, living the values of the organization. He/she participates in the recruitment, development, and retention of qualified individuals in all necessary positions of the Program to support effective, efficient, and high-quality programs/projects;
- Team building: he/she ensures that the Program team is consistent and that colleagues work in good collaboration with each other, with an excellent understanding of mutual expectations; and that support for field teams is prioritized. He/she establishes and evaluates performance standards/objectives and the behaviors of team members.
- Leads and supports geographically dispersed teams through effective remote management practices, fostering collaboration, accountability, and staff well-being via clear communication channels, regular virtual check-ins, performance monitoring systems, and adaptive leadership tailored to remote work dynamics.
- Individual Development and Performance Management: He/she manages and develops the performance of Program teams across the country to ensure the quality of the Program. This includes monitoring and evaluation of individual performance and professional development plans in accordance with the organization's standards.

**5. Liaison/Representation and Coordination**
