jobs.title: Head of support services (F/M) - Lebanon
jobs.body:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## **MdM in Lebanon**

MdM has been working in Lebanon for 30 years and actively contributed to respond to needs of the most vulnerable communities as the context unfolded (2011 Syrian crisis, 2019 severe economic crisis, 2020 Beirut Blast) and the current period since October 7th, 2023 – especially as the war resumed in Lebanon since March 2nd, 2026.

MdM’s intervention in Lebanon aims to strengthen the national health system and increase access to quality healthcare.

MdM is recognized in Lebanon as a major actor in the areas of mental health (MHPSS) and sexual and reproductive health (SRH). MdM supports several health centers and mobile clinics in the South, Beirut Mount Lebanon, Bekaa, and Baalbek Hermel; and works with other partners.

Despite the June 2026 ceasefire, the situation remains highly volatile and high needs remain, particularly in the South of the country. MdM continues to closely monitor the situation to ensure an appropriate, timely and flexible intervention, always in line with the needs of the various conflict-affected populations.

## **About the role**

You are responsible for the overall strategy and compliance, through the management of logistics, human resources and finance departments in the MdM Lebanon mission.

You ensure support services are fully compliant with MdM policies, donor requirements, national authorities' regulations, and applicable legislation.

## **Who you’ll work with**

Under the line management of the General coordinator, and the technical management of the Desk manager, you work in close collaboration with the other departments: Program, Medical/MHPSS, Grants, Security-Safety-Access, MEAL.

## **What you’ll do**

**Support services leadership & strategic planning**

- Provide strategic leadership and guidance to the General Coordinator and Country Management Team on all support-related matters
- Contribute to country strategy development, annual planning and financial planning processes
- Lead support services planning and ensure alignment between operational and programme priorities
- Anticipate operational challenges and oversee contingency planning to ensure humanitarian response continuity

**Development & reporting**

- Ensure support functions contribute effectively to proposal development, reporting and donor-related processes
- Coordinate the timely provision of analyses and support inputs required for programme development and decision-making

**Support services management & quality**

- Oversee the quality, compliance and performance of all support functions in accordance with organizational policies, donor requirements and local regulations
- Ensure sound resource management, accountability and legal compliance across the mission
- Monitor support systems, identify risks and corrective actions, and strengthen tools and procedures to support informed decision-making
- Promote effective integration and collaboration between Finance, HR, Logistics and programme teams

**Risk management, compliance & internal control**

- Strengthen internal control systems and ensure appropriate management of mission resources
- Identify and mitigate financial, operational, compliance, safeguarding, fraud and corruption risks
- Lead or coordinate audits, investigations and follow up on recommendations in collaboration with relevant stakeholders
- Promote adherence to anti-fraud, anti-corruption and safeguarding policies across the mission

**Team management & capacity building**

- Recruit, manage and develop the support services team through coaching, performance management and capacity-building initiatives
- Foster effective coordination, communication and information sharing across teams
- Identify learning and development needs and ensure access to appropriate technical support and resources

**Coordination & representation**

- Ensure strong coordination between support, programme, field and headquarters teams
- Facilitate effective information sharing and contribute to organizational reporting
- Represent the organization with authorities, partners and donors, alongside the General Coordinator, when required.

## REQUIREMENTS

**You are the right match if you...**

- Have significant experience in humanitarian operations, including in complex contexts, and have held a senior support coordination role within an international NGO
- Have strong expertise across HR, Finance, Logistics and Administration, ideally supporting health programmes and donor-funded projects
- Are a strategic and analytical leader, able to drive operational performance, manage risks and support decision-making
- Have a proven ability to lead, coach and develop teams while fostering collaboration across departments
- Are organized, adaptable and solution-oriented, with the confidence to make decisions and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
- Are an excellent communicator and relationship builder, comfortable engaging with partners, authorities, donors and diverse teams
- Are comfortable using Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel
- Are fluent in English; knowledge of French and/or Arabic and experience in the Middle East are strong assets.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Prefer a specialist role rather than overseeing multiple support functions and leading cross-department coordination
- Are uncomfortable working in complex, evolving humanitarian environments where priorities can shift rapidly
- Are not motivated by team leadership, capacity building and stakeholder engagement responsibilities

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info:  
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.  
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

## **EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3392€
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Beirut, Lebanon
- Field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.  
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Ethiopia Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer (Fixed-Term)
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable.  
  
The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices.

## About the Role

The Senior Tree Expansion Research Officer supports the Ethiopia Trees Program's expansion through desk research, primary data gathering, field verification scoutings, and evidence generation to identify and assess potential expansion opportunities across Ethiopia.

The role synthesizes geographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and stakeholder information to support strategic expansion decisions and operational readiness. The officer will participate in field scouting visits with the expansion team to validate desk research findings and gather additional insights.

## Responsibilities

Data Collection & Research

- Conduct desk research to identify and assess potential program expansion areas across regions, zones, and woredas.
- Collect, analyze, and synthesize agricultural, environmental, demographic, socioeconomic, market, and government data to support expansion planning.
- Review secondary data from government institutions, research organizations, development partners, and other credible sources to generate evidence-based insights.
- Monitor demographic, agricultural, environmental, market, and policy trends to identify opportunities and potential risks for program expansion.
- Develop and maintain databases, trackers, and research documentation to support expansion planning and operational readiness.
- Verify, clean, and analyze research and field data to ensure quality, accuracy, consistency, and usability.
- Support the development and continuous improvement of expansion assessment tools, scoring frameworks, research methodologies, and analytical processes.

Field & Stakeholder Verification of Data

- Participate in field scouting and assessment visits to validate desk research findings and collect additional information.
- Engage with government offices, development partners, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors to verify data, assumptions, and findings.
- Assess key expansion criteria, including agroforestry suitability, water availability, land suitability, market potential, operational feasibility, scalability, accessibility, and implementation risks.
- Identify data gaps and discrepancies and coordinate with relevant stakeholders to obtain and validate additional information.
- Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations.

Reporting & Collaboration

- Prepare clear and evidence-based assessment reports, analytical summaries, and recommendations to support expansion decisions.
- Present research findings and recommendations to relevant teams and stakeholders and contribute to expansion planning discussions.
- Collaborate with the expansion team and relevant technical and operational teams to translate research findings into actionable expansion plans.
- Maintain clear documentation of research findings, field validation results, assumptions, and recommendations to support decision-making and future reference

Reporting, Stakeholder Engagement & Collaboration

- Support engagement with government institutions, community representatives, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders during expansion assessments and field scouting activities.
- Coordinate information gathering, stakeholder consultations, and validation activities to support expansion planning and decision-making.
- Identify collaboration opportunities that strengthen expansion planning, field implementation, and operational readiness.
- Prepare high-quality assessment reports, presentations, briefing materials, and regular progress updates for internal and external stakeholders.
- Document research findings, field observations, lessons learned, stakeholder feedback, and key decisions to support knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.
- Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate research findings and stakeholder insights into actionable recommendations and expansion plans.
- Track assigned activities and maintain accurate and up-to-date documentation related to expansion research, assessments, and planning.
- Perform other research and operational support tasks as assigned to advance the Tree Program’s expansion objectives.
- Support the recruitment of field staff

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

Education

- Bachelor's degree required.
- Candidates with academic backgrounds in Forestry, Agroforestry, Agriculture, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Science, Geography, Rural Development, Watershed Management, or related fields are preferred.

Experience

- 2 years or more of relevant professional experience in forestry, agroforestry, agriculture, natural resource management, landscape restoration, rural development, field innovation, government relations, or related fields.
- Experience conducting research, data collection, expansion assessments, market assessments, or strategic planning.
- Experience working with government institutions, development partners, or community stakeholders.
- Experience supporting field assessments or validation exercises is an advantage.
- Willingness to travel to rural and remote locations for field scouting and stakeholder engagement.

Skills

- Strong analytical, research, and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent data gathering, analysis, and report writing skills.
- Ability to synthesize complex information into practical recommendations for decision-making.
- Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
- Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
- Ability to useMicrosoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
- Experience using digital data collection tools is an advantage.

Languages

- Can communicate in English.
- Fluency in Amharic.
- Proficiency in Afaan Oromo is preferred

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Contract Duration

1 year

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Ethiopia.

## Application Deadline

05 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Mission France - Bénévole Logistique - Ile de France F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

Le Projet Ile de France recherche des : BENEVOLE LOGISTIQUE – Ile de France

**CONTEXTE**

MSF déploie une clinique mobile à la porte de la Villette une fois par semaine (jeudi) pour les populations en situation précaire, notamment migrantes. Le dispositif implique des équipes soignantes bénévoles (médecin, infirmières, assistantes sociales, logisticiens et un agent de sécurité. L’équipe soignante fait des consultations, dispense des médicaments et réfère les patient.es vers des dispositifs de soin permanents. Sur le plan matériel, la clinique mobile est organisée avec un camion aménagé pour les consultations, ainsi que des tentes pour enregistrement et consultations.

**But principal :**  
Assurer la conduite du camion de la clinique mobile le jeudi, participer à l’installation logistique (montage des tentes et mise en place du matériel), soutenir les équipes pendant la durée de la clinique, puis assurer le retour du véhicule au parking.

**Responsabilités :**

- Se rendre au parking situé à proximité de porte de Clignancourt pour récupérer le camion.
- Conduire le camion jusqu’à Porte de la Villette.
- Participer au déchargement du matériel et au montage des tentes.
- Soutenir les équipes logistiques et soignantes pendant la clinique mobile (environ 4 à 5 heures).
- Participer au démontage et au rangement du matériel.
- Assurer le retour du camion au parking en fin de mission.

**Profil recherché**

**Education :** Permis B valide et expérience de conduite de véhicules utilitaires appréciée.

**Compétences :**

- Ponctualité, fiabilité
- Esprit d’équipe
- Sensibilité aux enjeux sociaux et à l’accompagnement de publics en situation de précarité.

**Disponibilité :**

- Jeudis (9h-14h) : engagement régulier à définir selon disponibilités.
- Présence requise sur la durée complète de la clinique mobile (environ 5 heures, hors temps de trajet).
- Engagement minimum souhaité : 2 mois.

**Conditions**

- Mission bénévole, non rémunérée.
- Convention de bénévolat obligatoire.
- Respect de la charte de MSF et des règles de confidentialité.
- Tickets restaurants par journée de bénévolat
- Respect des protocoles MSF

**Encadrement et accompagnement :**

- Intégration et briefings assurés par le logisticien projet et la responsable des activités médicales.
- Référent·e désigné·e pour accompagner le-la bénévole dans sa mission.
- Présence constante d’une équipe MSF sur le terrain

jobs.body:
**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

IRC’s Technical Excellence team is comprised of seven teams which have deep expertise in their respective fields: Education, Economic Wellbeing, Governance, Health, Violence Prevention and Response, MEAL, and Grants & Operations.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning: Global MEAL Practice, Technology for Programs, Regional MEAL Support, and CRRD Data & Analytics.

**Job Overview**

The Software Developer will be part of the METAL team which is responsible for delivering products that support the collection, management and visualization of KPIs relevant to higher-level decision-making for CRRD Programs.

The Software Developer will build and support data tools that drive decision-making across IRC, working with platforms like PowerApps, Power BI, Databricks, and Azure SQL. They will be a skilled contributor to the CRRD Data & Analytics team with strong experience in Microsoft PowerApps and Power Automate.

Specific tasks include data platform development, support, configuration, technical assistance and routing of technical issues, 2nd line help desk support, and participation in setting standards for processes, data quality, data security, and systems configuration.

The Software Developer will report to the Technology Development Lead. They will work closely with other developers, QA, Project Manager and the Program Data Systems Product Manager.

**Major Responsibilities**

- Design, develop, and maintain PowerApps and Power Automate solutions
- Support development and rollout of organization-wide data products in collaboration with METAL and sector experts
- Create technical documentation including system diagrams and implementation manuals
- Implement and maintain data quality processes and development standards
- Ensure compliance with IRC’s data protection, confidentiality, and security policies
- Provide Tier-2 and Tier-3 technical support, including issue routing and resolution
- Collaborate with IT and data engineering teams on systems integration
- Review software requirements and translate them into development tasks
- Contribute to setting and enforcing standards for processes, data quality, and system configurations
- Provide hyper-support during pilot phases of technology rollouts
- Perform other duties as assigned

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Technology Development Lead
- Direct Reports: None
- Management in Partnership: None

**Key Internal Relationships:**

- METAL Product Managers
- METAL QA Analyst
- METAL Project Manager
- IT Data Team

**Desired Experience and Skills**

- At least five years of experience working in technology domain to develop and rollout data platforms for programs – out of which, at least three years of experience developing, implementing, and supporting PowerApps applications for large and complex programs.
- Experience in source code and version control platforms, for example, GitHub, Azure DevOps, or similar.
- Strong in team development processes including pair programming, shadow sessions, code reviews and other strategies to ensure high quality programing.
- Strong code quality assurance practices including unit testing, integration testing, as well as regression testing to ensure quality of the code getting shipped into production.
- Ability to effectively communicate in English both in verbal (i.e., day-to-day discussions, team meetings) and written (requirements and design specifications) form, as well as an overall ability to be clear and concise in all communications.
- Strong analytic curiosity and innovative problem-solving skills using a system thinking approach.
- Demonstrable ability to work both independently and in a dynamic, cross-functional team structure.
- Demonstrable ability to establish and maintain working relationships across all departments and levels of the organization.

**Education:**

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, or related discipline
- Experience with Databricks, Dataverse connectors, APIs, and Microsoft Azure
- Certifications such Microsoft Power Platform Developer are an added advantage

**Compensation:** (US Pay Rate: $85,000 - $95,000/yr; UK Pay Rate: £46,780 - £55,552/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Erasmus Internship - Partnership Development Intern
jobs.body:
**Contract length:** 4–6 months, with a possible paid 6-month extension based on performance and budget availability

**Hours:** flexible, 20-40 hours per week, during CET core working hours (Monday to Friday)

**Location:** Amsterdam or Lyon (to be confirmed) Hybrid arrangement: office-based with some remote flexibility

**Travel:** none, except relocating to Amsterdam or Lyon

**Reporting to**: Grants and Partnerships Coordinator

Erasmus+ supports traineeships (work placements, internships) abroad at any workplace for students currently enrolled in higher education institutions in Program Countries at short-cycle Bachelor and Master level as well as for doctoral candidates. These opportunities are also open to recent graduates.

Erasmus+ traineeships are open to any student enrolled in a higher education institution holding an Erasmus+ Charter for Higher Education.

The traineeship must be relevant for the degree-related learning and personal development needs and, wherever possible, be integrated in the study program.

A traineeship can take place at any organization located anywhere in the world (with the exception of EU institutions, bodies and agencies).

CLEAR Global is an equal-opportunity employer, committed to having a diverse team where individuals of all backgrounds collaborate and learn from one another. We believe we can be most effective with diverse experience and expertise in our team. We recruit on merit, actively seek diverse applicant pools and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, marital or parental status, or sexual orientation, and welcome all types of diversity.

**Background**

CLEAR Global is a US non-profit organization supporting people to get information and be heard, whatever language they speak.

We seek to build real partnerships with organizations that understand the importance of good communication in the right language and format. Our partnership program has been developed to provide NGOs and UN agencies with access to the TWB Platform and the TWB Community of over 200,000 linguists via a comprehensive range of language services.

CLEAR Global’s Language services team oversees the management of the Partnership Program and includes the partnership sales team, the partner success coordinator, the community team, the services and support team, and the operations team.

The majority of partner organizations sign a 12 month partnership agreement that provides access to the services. The level of service and the cost is tied to the level of internal effort required to manage the partnership.

Increasingly we also provide professional services for standalone projects, or as part of a partnership agreement.

CLEAR Global is offering an internship to work as part of this small and dynamic team in the areas of administration, research, outreach, and sales. The candidate will gain valuable experience in a thriving international non-profit organization, learning about everything from not-for-profit humanitarian and development sectors, to business development and income tracking techniques.

**Role**

The Partnership Development Intern will support the Partnership Sales team to carry out tasks related to CLEAR Global’s partnership sales and customer success programs. The role also includes supporting the officers with day-to-day administrative tasks. A big part of the role will entail using CRM (constituent relationship management) database tools, written communications, and web-based research to support CLEAR Global’s partnership goals.

**Responsibilities**

*Fundraising*

- Research new prospective partners which might benefit from our support
- Support collateral, strategy, and implementation of our partnership program for CLEAR Global
- Support relations/communications

*Administration support:*

- Regular data entry into Hubspot
- Support with keeping partners’ account info, as well as outreach records up to date (entering/updating data)
- Monitor partnership requests coming in from different channels
- Support Partner onboarding process - drafting agreements, creating invoices, and sending out outreach communications.
- Support with creating reports

Please note that these roles and responsibilities are approximate and may change over time.

**Qualifications**

The right candidate is an energetic team player who agrees with CLEAR Global’s basic beliefs and values and who can work virtually with team members based throughout the world.

**Requirements**

- Enrolled in or graduated recently from a University degree program (preferably with a degree in the field of languages, communications or marketing);
- Excellent command of English, both oral and written. Knowledge of or interest in other languages is an advantage;
- Previous experience working with non-profit organizations and particularly in the fundraising arena would be a real advantage;
- Familiarity with data entry tools, CRM and cloud computing platforms would be a plus.
- Experience carrying out desktop research, using a range of methods and sources of data
- Must have access to a stable internet connection and a computer.

**About CLEAR Global**

CLEAR Global exists to help people get vital information, and be heard, whatever language they speak. We believe that everyone has the right to give and receive information in a language and format they understand. We work with nonprofit partners and a global community of language professionals to build local language translation capacity, and raise awareness of language barriers. Our network of over 200,000 community members translate millions of words of life-saving and life-changing information a year.

**Core values**

CLEAR Global employees and volunteers are people who believe passionately about the value of this work and take personal responsibility for achieving the mission. CLEAR Global’s mission and organizational spirit embody the core values established in its strategic framework:

- Excellence: As the leading voice for communicating humanitarian information in the right language, CLEAR Global is a leader in the translation industry and in the non-profit sector.
- Integrity: CLEAR Global believes that every person, whether it’s the people who we serve, our volunteers or our staff, has value, deserves respect and has inherent dignity.
- Empowerment: CLEAR Global believes in using language to empower people around the world to control their own development and destiny.
- Innovation: CLEAR Global recognizes and celebrates the power of innovation to address humanitarian and crisis issues around the world.
- Sustainability: CLEAR Global recognizes that meeting our mission necessitates establishment and maintenance of a solid financial and organizational infrastructure.
- Tolerance: Our staff and volunteers are highly knowledgeable and skilled; value each other, our partner and our recipients; create a supportive work environment; and, conduct themselves professionally at all times.

*CLEAR Global may re-advertise the vacancy, cancel the recruitment, or offer an appointment with a modified job description or for a different duration at its discretion.*

jobs.title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Advisor (MHPSS) Technical Advisor
jobs.body:
**Job Title: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Advisor (MHPSS) Technical Advisor**

**Location:** Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq (KRI), with occasional travel to other areas of KRI.

**Type of position:** Employment contract/ Expat or National Contract

**Length of Contract:** 12 months

**Compensation and Benefits:** Competitive salary and benefits commensurate with skills and experience. Local/Expatriate Compensation Package: includes relocation expenses and housing and local transportation allowances.

**About SEED:** SEED is a women-led, local NGO in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, dedicated to creating a thriving society by advancing social protection and human development. We support individuals, empower communities, and strengthen systems to drive lasting change and equal opportunity. With a focus on collaboration, we promote gender equality, protect children, combat human trafficking, and improve mental health and well-being. SEED’s holistic, locally-driven approach integrates transformational services, community development, training and education, and advocacy to create sustainable impact. SEED is committed to creating a just, equitable society where everyone's rights are protected, with healthy families and strong communities, and a future where everyone can thrive.

**Role of the Mental Health and Well-Being Technical Advisor:**

The MHPSS Technical Advisor is responsible for the technical leadership, strategic direction, and operationalization of the community-based psychosocial support and community-based initiatives within their pillar. S/he actively drives the pillar’s progress by aligning strategy and objectives with community-specific needs. Working with program and project managers across SEED, they apply their thematic expertise to lead intervention design and planning, and support implementation of group and community activities. They ensure that all psychosocial support and community development activities are technically sound, culturally appropriate, and effectively designed to meet SEED’s strategic goal of engaging and empowering communities.

Core functions include creating or updating curricula and materials for community and group-based activities; training and equipping staff to deliver the curricula, and providing ongoing technical support to staff; creating robust MEAL systems to review impact and community feedback; and supporting program teams to implement the engagements.

This position will lead the ***Supporting Mental Health and Well-being*** thematic pillar.This pillar aims to strengthen mental health, psychosocial well-being, and resilience by addressing trauma, stress, violence and social fragmentation, and supporting individual, family, and community healing and recovery. Utilizing SEED curricula, this pillar prioritizes psychoeducation, positive coping, and life skills to reduce mental health stigma, restore collective well-being, and facilitate social cohesion and peaceful reintegration.

**Specific Tasks:**

***Technical Leadership, Program Planning and Design, and Innovation (40%)***

- Serve as the technical authority for the thematic pillar, providing technical and programmatic leadership for the design and implementation of all associated curricula and implementation standards.
- Translate SEED’s broad strategic goals and objectives into actionable interventions and engagements.
- Serve as the primary technical advisor for cross-unit initiatives integrating best practices into all organizational programs and strategies.
- Lead the creation of SOPs, policies, and guidance documents regarding PSS implementation, community engagement, and accountability standards for this pillar.
- Collaborate closely with other technical advisors to synchronize strategies, share best practices, and co-design technical tools that drive the unit’s objectives.
- Work closely with program managers to bridge the gap between technical design and operational feasibility/implementation.
- Regularly assess the product portfolio to identify opportunities for new implementations or expansion into new geographic areas.
- Lead the design and development of new tools, curricula, facilitator manuals, and programmatic materials tailored to community needs, ensuring child-friendly, age appropriate, and trauma-informed approaches are maintained across all pertinent interventions.
- Ensure all technical products are culturally sensitive, contextually relevant, and consistent with SEED’s strategic objective.
- Provide data-driven basis for program planning and design through technical reports and briefs that reflect the progress and challenges of the thematic pillar.

***Capacity Building and Technical Supervision (30%)***

- In close collaboration with other Technical Advisors, as well as pertinent colleagues from external departments, lead on ensuring PSS Staff Onboarding Package is updated, relevant and fit for purpose.
- Coordinate with the PSS & Community Development Unit to ensure all PSS staff (coordinators, facilitators, mobilizers and other staff as requested) have been properly onboarded, and refresher support is provided as required.
- Provide technical advice to support program development and implementation to ensure maximum impact and consistency to program/project managers and Program Development and Management Unit.
- Lead or support (as appropriate) the development and revision of PSS Curricula with high quality, through direct provision of training, Training of Trainers, and support to dedicated trainers as appropriate.
- Contribute to the development/refinement of tools and guidance for coaching and technical supervision to PSS staff.
- Provide/support in the provision of regular technical supervision and lead on coaching to technical supervisors, to maintain staff well-being, high quality session delivery, and consistency across the pillar to support PSS staff in the field.

***Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (20%)***

- Support in the review and revision of SEED Standard Indicators aligned with this pillar, including articulating and defining indicators, and identifying/developing appropriate means of verification of their measurement, and support as necessary in results analysis.
- Collaborate closely with MEAL to conduct comprehensive community needs assessments and ensure all findings directly shape program planning and design
- Contribute to/lead on (as appropriate) the design and implementation of monitoring and evaluation (M&E) frameworks and data collection tools to rigorously track the progress, outcomes, and long-term impact of the pillar’s interventions
- Ensure all pillar activities are systematically monitored, documented, evaluated, and reported to maintain high standards for data integrity and technical accountability, ensuring accountability to affected population/program participants at all stages.
- Support the synthesis and analysis of insights with PSS staff to refine programs and strengthen future programs.
- Monitor the effectiveness of training materials in partnership with MEAL using field observations and PSS team facilitation experiences to continuously improve technical resources
- Lead regular technical learning sessions to disseminate compiled results and synthesized data from pillar-level activities to the wider team contributing to organizational knowledge
- Maintain learning and feedback mechanisms to continuously refine technical products based on real-time field data, community shifts, and changes in internally recognized minimum standards
- Support the safe and meaningful participation of women, men, and children program participants at all stages of the program cycle.

***Communication, Coordination and Representation (10%)***

- Produce high-quality reports, policy briefs, presentations, and multimedia content focused on SEED’s work with a specific emphasis on both pillar and community development initiatives
- Support the development of programmatic materials tailored for diverse stakeholders to raise awareness and promote SEED’s mission
- Write and review articles, social media posts, and website content to ensure technical accuracy and alignment with SEED’s strategic goals
- Provide technical input for all promotional materials and ensure all public-facing content adheres to SEED’s Storytelling Policy
- Represent SEED in relevant forums, conferences, and working groups; share insights on interventions and approaches to advocate for the organization’s goals with key stakeholders

**Essential Criteria:**

*Education and Experience*

- Required: Bachelor’s degree in (Clinical, Counseling) Psychology, Social Work (with a mental health focus), or Public Health, or a related social science field with at least 5 years of progressive experience in technical leadership or advisory roles within the MHPSS sector
- Preferred: Master’s degree in Psychology, Clinical Social Work, or Global Mental Health, or a related field with at least 3 years of experience in a technical leadership capacity
- Proven experience in the humanitarian and/or development sector, with a specific technical focus on community-based MHPSS and social cohesion programming
- Demonstrated experience in strategic program design and providing technical supervision to multi-disciplinary teams
- A proven track record of building staff capacity through the design and delivery of training, coaching, and mentorship

*Technical Expertise*

- Deep technical knowledge of MHPSS, trauma-informed care, IASC Guidelines for MHPSS in Emergencies, social norm change, and rights-based programming
- Expert-level experience in curriculum development and creating culturally sensitive tools (SOPs, guidance notes, and training manuals)
- Experience providing technical supervision to MHPSS service providers and PSS facilitators
- Strong background in psychosocial support and community development; experience in social cohesion and social and behavioral change initiatives is an asset
- Proficiency in designing MEAL frameworks, conducting needs assessments, and utilizing data to refine technical interventions

*Context and Skills*

- Experience working in humanitarian and/or development settings is a must; specific experience in the Middle East, particularly Iraq or the Kurdistan Region, is a significant asset
- Exceptional written and verbal English skills are required; proficiency in Kurdish (Sorani) and/or Arabic is highly desirable
- Advanced proficiency in Google Workspace and other digital tools
- Deep commitment to SEED’s mission, values, and ethical standards, including a strong understanding of Do No Harm principles

jobs.title: Directeur.trice des Systèmes d'Information (SI) F/H
jobs.body:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

MSF OCP recherche son/sa prochain·e Directeur·trice des Systèmes d’Information (SI) à horizon novembre 2026.

**Mission**

À la tête du département des systèmes d'information, organisé autour d'une direction adjointe et de plusieurs pôles d'expertise, vous jouez un rôle clé dans la définition et le pilotage de la stratégie SI de l'organisation, couvrant notamment les applications, les infrastructures, les réseaux et les communications, au siège comme sur les terrains. Membre du Comité de direction, vous contribuez aux orientations stratégiques de l'association et accompagnez leur traduction en trajectoires, projets et services numériques répondant aux besoins des équipes et des opérations.

Vous accompagnez notamment la mise en œuvre des ambitions définies dans les orientations stratégiques OCP 2026-2031. En partenariat étroit avec les directions métiers, vous pilotez la transformation numérique de l'organisation et favorisez un usage pertinent de la donnée, des outils numériques, de l'intelligence artificielle et des nouvelles formes de partage des connaissances au service de la décision et de l'action opérationnelle.

Porteur d'une vision fondée sur la qualité de service et l'écoute des utilisateurs, vous accompagnez ces transformations en recherchant un juste équilibre entre innovation, harmonisation, mutualisation, maîtrise des coûts et réduction des vulnérabilités. À ce titre, vos priorités portent notamment sur le renforcement de la cybersécurité et de la maîtrise des risques, la clarification de la gouvernance et de l'architecture des données, l'évolution du patrimoine applicatif ainsi que l'amélioration de la gouvernance des projets. Vous veillez ainsi à la cohérence, à la performance, à la sécurité et à la continuité du système d'information, tout en garantissant des solutions et des modalités d'appui adaptées aux contraintes spécifiques des terrains.

Vous jouez également un rôle majeur dans la structuration et le développement de la filière SI sur les terrains, afin de renforcer durablement les capacités au plus près des opérations.

Au sein des instances internationales du mouvement MSF, vous représentez OCP et participez à la définition de politiques et de solutions communes répondant aux priorités médico-opérationnelles et aux spécificités de l'organisation.

**Responsabilités principales**

Sous la responsabilité hiérarchique de la Directrice générale :

**Définir et piloter la stratégie des systèmes d'information d'OCP**

- Élabore la stratégie SI du siège et des terrains et est garant de leur déclinaison en politiques et feuille de route.
- S’assure de l’atteinte des objectifs définis.
- Participe, avec les autres directions, à la construction de la stratégie d'OCP et en pilote le suivi et la redevabilité.

**Organiser la qualité de service, la gouvernance et l'évolution du système d'information**

- Est garant du pilotage du portefeuille de projets SI en lien étroit avec les directions métiers, du recueil des besoins jusqu'à leur mise en œuvre.
- Définit l'architecture et l'organisation des flux d'information, et arbitre les investissements nécessaires.
- Contribue à la gouvernance des données et à leur qualité, leur accessibilité et leur protection.
- Définit la stratégie d’urbanisation du patrimoine applicatif afin d’en garantir la cohérence avec les besoins métiers et son interopérabilité.
- Est garant des bonnes pratiques de gouvernance des projets et des applications.

**Garantir la sécurité, la continuité et la maîtrise des risques SI**

- S’assure de l’application des politiques de sécurité des systèmes d'information et de protection des données.
- Garantit la disponibilité et la qualité des services SI, adaptés aux contraintes des terrains (faible connectivité, conditions dégradées).
- Organise la continuité et la reprise des services critiques, ainsi que la réponse aux incidents majeurs.

**Contribuer aux dynamiques internationales**

- Représente OCP au sein des plateformes et instances SI internationales du mouvement.
- Contribue à la définition des politiques et stratégies SI internationales de MSF, en veillant à leur cohérence avec les priorités d'OCP.

**Manager et développer le département**

- Fixe les orientations, définit les objectifs et anime les différents pôles du département, y compris sur les terrains, dans une logique matricielle.
- Encadre, conseille et soutient ses collaborateurs ; veille à la qualité de vie au travail et au développement de leurs compétences.
- Pilote les ressources humaines, financières et organisationnelles du département et en assure le suivi budgétaire.
- Définit une stratégie de développement de la filière IT/SI sur les terrains.

**Expérience :**

- Expérience de minimum cinq ans dans un poste similaire, ou d'au moins sept ans en responsabilité des systèmes d'information.
- Expérience confirmée de pilotage stratégique, de conduite de projets et de management d'équipes SI dans une organisation multisite et internationale.
- Connaissance du monde associatif ou humanitaire souhaitable ; expérience d'environnements internationaux et multiculturels appréciée.
- Formation supérieure en informatique (niveau master), école d'ingénieurs ou qualification équivalente.

**Langues :** Français B2 et Anglais C1 indispensable

**Compétences :**

- Vision stratégique et capacité à traduire les orientations de l'organisation en trajectoire SI.
- Maîtrise de la gestion de projets et de portefeuilles multiprojets, ainsi que de la sécurité des systèmes d'information et des infrastructures.
- Bonne connaissance de l'architecture des SI et des systèmes d'entreprise (ERP, CRM, Office 365...).
- Maîtrise des enjeux de gouvernance, de qualité et de protection des données.
- Conduite du changement et transformation numérique.
- Management d’équipes pluridisciplinaires et développement des compétences.
- Gestion budgétaire, allocation des ressources et pilotage de fournisseurs.

**Aptitudes :**

- Leadership fédérateur, orientation service et utilisateurs.
- Qualité d'écoute, pédagogie et capacité à communiquer et à présenter des arbitrages de façon structurée.
- Esprit d'équipe et aptitude à coopérer dans un environnement multiculturel, inclusif et respectueux de la diversité.
- Esprit d'analyse et de synthèse.
- Capacité d’anticipation, sens des priorités et aptitude à identifier et à mettre en œuvre des solutions.
- Sens des responsabilités, capacité de décision, organisation, rigueur et autonomie.

**Valeurs et engagement :**

- Sensibilité réelle au bien-être de son équipe, avec une implication concrète et exigeante dans la prévention des risques psychosociaux (RPS) et le safeguarding, garantissant à ses collaborateurs un environnement de travail sain et sécurisant.

*MSF attend de l'ensemble de ses collaborateurs une adhésion aux valeurs professionnelles et collectives ainsi qu'à la culture associative, afin qu'elle soit portée par tous.*

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Statut :** CDI à temps plein. Poste cadre, basé à Paris avec déplacements à l'étranger à prévoir (fréquence approximative : 4-6 fois par an).

**Rémunération et avantages :** 80,36 K€ brut annuel sur 13 mois. 22 jours de RTT par an. Télétravail selon les règles en vigueur chez MSF (2 j/sem.). Mutuelle prise en charge à 100%. Titres-restaurant de 12€ (prise en charge à 60% par MSF). Prise en charge à 50% de l'abonnement de transport en commun (hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) ou indemnité kilométrique vélo (0,25€ par km, limité à 450€ par an).

**Poste à pourvoir :** Début novembre 2026

**Date limite de dépôt de candidatures :** 28 septembre 2026

jobs.title: Middle School Alliance (MSA) Bilingual Intake Specialist
jobs.body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview**

The Middle School Alliance (MSA) Bilingual Intake Specialist will provide recruitment and intake support, liaise with parents and support afterschool programming at assigned middle school sites. The Specialist will assist with sign in and site programming, family engagement, recruitment and intakes. The Specialist will be on site from 4-7pm Monday through Thursday with 2-3 additional hours some weeks for recruitment and intakes both on site and home visits, as assigned by the MSA Coordinator.

**Major Responsibilities**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

***Site Operation***

- Support MSA Coordinator with students signing in and enforcing program and school rules.
- Assist with snack distribution, dismissal procedures, and site transitions.
- Assist with events, special activities, and school-based initiatives.
- Assist in administering program evaluations.

***Student Recruitment & Family Engagement***

- Support student recruitment and enrollment efforts.
- Support outreach and engagement efforts for students, families, teachers, and school personnel.
- Assist with family communication regarding programming schedules, attendance expectations, transportation updates, and special events.
- Promote inclusive access to OST opportunities and support student participation across diverse student populations.
- Build and maintain positive relationships with youth and families to encourage consistent engagement and participation.
- Support implementation of student and family engagement activities throughout the school year.

***Program Quality & Continuous Improvement***

- Participate in professional development, coaching, training, and quality improvement activities as time allows.
- Support program providers in creating safe, engaging, and youth-centered learning environments.
- Communicate concerns related to quality, consistency, youth engagement, or operational effectiveness to MSA leadership.
- Gather and communicate feedback from youth, families, providers, and school staff to support continuous improvement.

***Relationship Management & Communication***

- Build and maintain collaborative relationships with school administrators, teachers, providers, families, community partners, and youth.
- Represent NextUp and the MSA professionally within school communities and partner spaces.

***Safety, Supervision & Risk Management***

- Assist in ensuring students are properly supervised during transitions, programming, transportation, and dismissal.
- Maintain awareness of site safety concerns and communicate incidents promptly to MSA leadership.

**Job Requirements**

- Bachelor's degree is preferred in education, youth development, nonprofit management, public administration, social work, or a related field \*or equivalent experience.
- Up to 2 years of related experience in youth development, education, after-school programming, or community-based programming.
- Proficient in English and Spanish, both spoken and written.
- Experience working with middle school youth, school communities, or after-school programming strongly preferred.
- Experience with attendance tracking, data systems, and reporting processes preferred.
- This position does not have supervisory responsibility for other staff.

jobs.title: Intensive Case Management Caseworker

This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Intensive Case Management (ICM) Caseworker will address barriers to safety and wellness for especially vulnerable refugees, asylees, and other ORR-eligible populations. The ICM caseworker will be expected to provide strengths-based, client-centered case management to single-headed refugee households; survivors of domestic violence and gender-based violence; older refugees; youth and young adults without parents or permanent guardians; refugees experiencing mental health or psychological difficulties; refugees with physical disabilities or medical conditions; unanticipated refugee arrivals and secondary migrants; and refugees who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender or queer (LGBTQ). They work closely with clients, colleagues, and external parties to develop service plans to meet individual client needs and preferences utilizing a broad range of financial, medical, social, vocational, and other services and resources in accordance with client eligibility and program requirements.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Determine client eligibility for ICM programming and conduct intake assessments, review program expectations, outcomes, and confidentiality with each potential client.
- Develop individualized, SMART Self-sufficiency plans for each client enrolled in the ICM program.
- Evaluate client progress every six months during active program enrollment to determine the client’s progress towards goals and work with the client to identify new needs and actions needed.
- Assist clients in navigating healthcare and social service systems, which may include helping clients apply for benefits and attend and schedule appointments.
- Conduct community outreach and maintain a strong network of service providers that meet client needs. The ICM caseworker may also be expected to maintain a strong relationship with local and state level refugee coordinators and health coordinators to ensure client needs are met.

jobs.title: Employment Specialist
jobs.body:
This position is represented by the OPEIU union and subject to the terms and conditions of a collective bargaining agreement.

**Job Overview:** The Employment Specialist assists refugees and other qualified immigrants to attain self-sufficiency through employment by guiding them through employment preparation, coordinating job placements, and other career advancement services.

jobs.body:

**Seeks**

## Surgeon

## for International Humanitarian Missions

To join our team in International Projects

(Minimum availability of 3 months)

### **\*\*\* Please upload your CV and motivation letter in English \*\*\***

**THIS JOB PROFILE IS IN ENGLISH SINCE THIS IS THE REQUIRED LANGUAGE FOR THE JOB**

**OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION**

Organize and carry out surgery activities, ensure pre and post-operative surgical care, in accordance with **MSF** policies, protocols and universal hygiene standards and in close collaboration with medical staff in the emergency, intensive wards and operation theatre in order to improve patients’ health conditions.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

- Coordinates the implementation of MSF clinical policies, tools, guidelines and protocols ( antibiotic prophylaxis, post-operative pain management, thrombo-prophylaxis, caesarean section, blood transfusion, etc) and recommendations (standard hygiene and sterilization rules, prevention to HIV, TB, Syphilis and Hep B exposure) in order to minimize clinical risks.
- Undertake pre-operative consultations, evaluating the surgical risks with the anaesthetist and/or other medical staff involved, and obtaining the patient’s signed consent to operate.
- Carry out emergency and programmed surgical intervention following MSF protocols and policies including swab counts, ensuring appropriate use of surgical equipment and proper OT registry entry/documentation of all OT intervention.
- Carry out post-operative clinical care and ward rounds collaborating with the anesthetist, the Operating Theatre Nurse and ward staff or other Unit Managers to ensure compliance with MSF protocols and rational use of medicines. Attend OPD, emergency room when required.
- In collaboration with the anaesthetist, carry-out the collection and analysis of quantitative surgical- anaesthesia data, using post-operative observation sheets, routine data collected, patient files, operating department register, patient file, etc to monitor quality. Monthly revue data and analyze clinical trends and comment on adverse events / poor clinical outcome. Support organizing the operating program and with OT staff monitor use of material and equipment and advise on instrument needs and coordinates patient referral.,
- Put in place the emergency disaster response plan of the hospital along with the anesthetist and the medical doctor and /or the responsible nurse and run role hospital practical rehearsals, in order to ensure the continuity of the services under any circumstance
- Knows and helps implement the accidental blood exposure policy.
- Plan, evaluate, and supervise the training of the staff (emergency and the out-patient teams) in order to ensure the amount of knowledge required and to improve people diagnosing, triage, and early detection capabilities.
- Supports other medical teams/wards when needed (i.e. midwifes and obstetric teams in the maternity ward, etc.)

**PROFILE**

**Education and formation**

- **Essential**: General Physician Degree.
- **Essential:** Final Specialization in Surgery (generalist, ortho, gyneco/obs, plastic, war).

**Experience**

- **Essential**: minimum 2 years practicing (after specialization) as Surgeon for a hospital developing multi-purpose activities
- Experience preforming C-section, in orthopedics, plastic surgery (skin graft), and/or can treat trauma
- Desirable work experience with MSF and other NGOs in developing countries

**Languages**

- **Essential:** English (B2 or higher level)
- **Essential**: Spanish (C1 or higher level)
- Knowledge of French will be an asset

**Knowledge**

**Essential** computer literacy (word, excel, internet)

**Competencies**

- People Management and Development
- Commitment to MSF Principles
- Behavioral Flexibility
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Teamwork and Cooperation
- Planning and Organizing
- Cross-cultural Awareness
- Stress Management

**POSITION CONDITIONS**

**Work Venue:** Where the needs of the project require it

**Profits:** Monthly remuneration: in the first 12 months, the bonus approximate gross monthly is USD $1,500. From the second year remuneration increases based on experience (previous and acquired) and the level of responsibility in the field. Private insurance coverage that includes medical coverage and hospital, temporary disability and life insurance. The organization also has an arranged medical evacuation if necessary. The expenses of stay in the land are covered: housing, basic services, cleaning and washing. Other expenses such as transportation, visas, transfer to the country of destination and Displacements in the field will also be covered by MSF. Per diem or monthly per diem: mainly to cover meals and small personal expenses.

**Start:** Depending on the needs of the project

**Duration:** **Minimum 3 months**

**Working day:** Full time

- Planning, supervising and ensuring the implementation of, in close coordination with the HRCo, the associated processes (recruitment, training, briefing, induction, evaluation, potential detection, development and communication) of the project staff in order to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required. Supporting the project line managers in said processes in order to improve staff capabilities, their end results contribution to mission goals and to boost their active participation and **MSF** commitment.
- Advising on set-up and updating the project's organizational chart and job descriptions and assisting the PC, and/or team leaders and supervisors to draw up annual holiday planning and staff shifts in order to forecast HR needs and to ensure HR availability for the project activities
- Ensuring hiring, amendments and contract termination formalities for employees at project level are according to local labour laws. Archiving and updating individual employee files, informing them on their rights and preparing all mandatory tax declarations, in order to ensure legal compliance. In close collaboration with the PC and HRCo, looking for the best options to avoid and/or solve possible labour conflicts in the project
- Supervising/performing payroll procedures, ensuring that all data related to monthly salary calculation of the project national employees are correctly entered in Homere (days off, unpaid leaves, sick leaves, overtime, salary advance, etc.), in order to ensure on time and accurate salary payments. Under supervision of the HRCo, ensuring the indexation process of the national staff salary grids are in order to ensure internal equity, cost-of-living adjustments and the correct application of employment conditions in the project sites
- In close collaboration with the PC and HRCo, implementing the administrative procedures of any Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in force between local partners (e.g. Ministry of Health, etc.) and **MSF**.
- Implementing circuits and workflows (management of cash boxes, transfers, advances, purchase procedures, payment validations, follow up of regular payments, bank reconciliation) in order to anticipate expenses at project level and to optimize cash needs and its security.
- Implementing and supervising transactional procedures and systems in order to ensure transparent accounting practices and full documentary traceability (invoices, receipts, bank statements, etc.), following MSF guidelines and rules, and using the respective software in place. Ensuring and controlling the monthly and yearly accountancy closure and all HR, Administrative and Financial reporting of the Project (Homère and accounting software monthly closure, sitreps, etc.)
- Being responsible for all movements and/or accommodation of staff in the Project.

**PROFILE**

**Education and formation**

**Desirable**, degree in finance, management (business, HR) or administration.

**Experience**

- **Essential**, working experience of at least two years in relevant and similar jobs.
- **Desirable** working experience with MSF or other NGOs, in developing countries.

**Languages**

- **Essential:** English (B2 or higher level)
- **Essential**: Spanish (C1 or higher level)
- **Essential:** French (B2 or higher level)

**Knowledge**

- **Essential** computer literacy (word, excel and internet)
- **Desirable** HR and Financial MSF software (Homère, FFC, SAGA)

**Competencies**

- People Management and Development
- Commitment to MSF Principles
- Behavioral Flexibility
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Teamwork and Cooperation

**POSITION CONDITIONS**

**Work Venue:** Where the needs of the project require it

**Profits:** Monthly remuneration: in the first 12 months, the bonus approximate gross monthly is USD $2,500. From the second year remuneration increases based on experience (previous and acquired) and the level of responsibility in the field. Private insurance coverage that includes medical coverage and hospital, temporary disability and life insurance. The organization also has an arranged medical evacuation if necessary. The expenses of stay in the land are covered: housing, basic services, cleaning and washing. Other expenses such as transportation, visas, transfer to the country of destination and Displacements in the field will also be covered by MSF. jobs.title: Tupande Zone Supervisor - Mtaragon
jobs.body:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## About the Role

As a Zone/Duka Supervisor, you are directly responsible for sales in your retail zone. You will play a key role in understanding the needs of our customers/farmers and help shape the future of businesses across all channels and use technology to connect with customers/farmers. You will develop an execution strategy for your assigned market and work both individually, and with your Sales team and to prospect, qualify, develop, and close new customer/farmer opportunities

## Responsibilities

- Achieve sales, repayment, and impact targets for your zone.
- Manage multiple sales channel performance through the entire business cycle simultaneously, working with cross-functional teams as necessary, and serve as the primary contact for all zonal performance.
- Provide technical support and training to Shop Assistants and Field Agents by setting up and facilitating weekly meetings.
- Define and manage task planning for Duka Assistants and Tupande Agents
- Oversee the management of the tree nursery in the zone with a dotted reporting line to the Tree Advisor
- Oversee and execute inventory ordering, data entry and merchandising.
- Oversee the operation control environment at the Duka
- Actively build your teams through hiring, training and performance management
- Supporting planning and implementation of promotion programs for your zone.
- Assist customers in understanding their needs, articulate key differentiators and typical customer buying journeys, and generally display a passion for our program.
- Support your team to create sales opportunities for customers

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 1+ years of experience in a sales, partner or channel manager role.
- Demonstrated ability to work towards strategic goals consistently.
- Knowledge in Data analysis and inventory management
- Knowledgeable in Google Sheets or MS Excel.
- Work in a team
- Effective strategic and analytical thinking skills.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Mtaragon - Rift Region, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

08 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*
